blocks.text: La CCI France Japon rappelle qu'elle ne certifie en aucune manière les sociétés et n'engage en aucun cas sa responsabilité quant aux actions ou déclarations des entreprises prétendant être certifiées par elle. Toute affirmation en ce sens est faite sans son consentement et n’a aucune valeur officielle. Pour toute vérification, nous vous invitons à contacter directement membership(@)ccifj.or.jp .

title: Adhésion
description: Adhérer à la Chambre de commerce et d’industrie française du Japon, c’est rejoindre une communauté d’affaires de plus de 650 sociétés et 1500 décideurs pour bénéficier de nombreux avantages.

blocks.section: Adhésion
blocks.text: Adhésion

blocks.section: Adhésion
blocks.text: La CCI France Japon a comme principal objectif de faciliter les contacts entre les entreprises membres et entre les membres et d’autres entreprises , afin de leur permettre d’identifier des opportunités de travailler ensemble .

blocks.section: Adhésion
blocks.text: Sa vocation première est d’ animer la communauté d’affaires franco-japonaise, mais également d’accompagner les entreprises françaises ou japonaises dans leur développement international .

blocks.section: Bureau à Fukui
blocks.text: Dans le cadre de son engagement à renforcer les relations économiques entre la France et le Japon, la Chambre de Commerce et d'Industrie Française du Japon (CCIFJ) a inauguré une nouvelle antenne au Centre d'Innovation de Koshino Valley à Fukui. Cette ouverture vise à soutenir les entreprises françaises, internationales et japonaises dans la région. Accessible facilement depuis Tokyo et Osaka, Fukui est une région dynamique qui bénéficie désormais de la ligne Shinkansen Hokuriku. Les membres de la CCIFJ pourront également utiliser le "Fukui Desk" pour leurs activités professionnelles dans cet espace d'incubation moderne.

blocks.section: Bureau à Gunma
blocks.text: Bureau à Gunma

blocks.section: Bureau à Gunma
blocks.text: Dans le cadre de son engagement à renforcer les liens économiques entre la France et le Japon, la Chambre de commerce et d'industrie française du Japon (CCIFJ) a ouvert une antenne à Gunma. Cette région dynamique, située à environ 100 km de Tokyo, joue un rôle clé dans l'industrie, notamment dans l'automobile et la métallurgie, avec des entreprises telles que Michelin, Subaru ou encore Danone. L'antenne vise à intensifier les partenariats économiques, à accompagner les entreprises locales et à favoriser l'expansion des entreprises françaises sur le marché japonais.

title: Business Leaders Forum
description: Véritable lieu d’échanges et de networking, ce Forum est conçu pour les dirigeants de structures françaises ou japonaises qui souhaitent nouer ou développer des partenariats avec des acteurs du monde des affaires en France et au Japon et s’informer sur les évolutions sectorielles et technologique

blocks.section: Business Leaders Forum
blocks.text: Business Leaders Forum

blocks.section: Business Leaders Forum
blocks.text: Depuis 2018, le France Japan Business Leaders Forum est un cycle de 10 conférences de réflexion stratégique. Son objectif est de réunir des experts du secteur lors d'événements gouvernementaux dédiés afin d'échanger sur les tendances, les défis et les opportunités de leur industrie, et de créer une plateforme collaborative pour promouvoir notre lien franco-japonais.

blocks.section: Business Leaders Forum
blocks.text: Ce forum permet d'établir et de développer des partenariats avec des acteurs économiques français et japonais, de s'informer sur les évolutions sectorielles et technologiques, d'échanger sur les enjeux et les opportunités de leur secteur, et d'accroître leur visibilité structurelle, leurs perspectives, leurs concurrents, leurs associations professionnelles et les autorités compétentes en participant à des discussions clés sur de nombreux thèmes.

blocks.section: Business Leaders Forum
blocks.text: Animée par des intervenants impactants, cette édition marque le 9e Business Leader Forum. L'ensemble des webinaires et conférences contribuera à façonner l'avenir du Japon.

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: Details

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: Savencia is a leading international food group specializing in cheese and dairy products . With brands like Caprice des Dieux , Saint Agur , and Bresso , the group combines innovation and tradition to offer high-quality products worldwide . Present in over 120 countries , Savencia is committed to sustainability , taste , and craftsmanship , serving both consumers and culinary professionals.

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: Aux Merveilleux de Fred is a French patisserie known for its delicate meringue-based cakes coated in whipped cream and chocolate shavings. Founded by Frédéric Vaucamps , the brand celebrates artisanal savoir-faire and French tradition . With boutiques across Europe , Asia , and North America , it offers a refined taste of Parisian indulgence around the world.

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: Godiva is a premium Belgian chocolate brand known for its artisanal expertise and rich heritage since 1926 . It offers a wide range of luxury chocolates , truffles , and gourmet treats , blending tradition with innovation . With a strong global presence , Godiva is dedicated to providing indulgent experiences through high-quality ingredients and elegant presentation .

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: Perrier is a French mineral water brand famous for its natural carbonation and distinctive green bottle . Sourced from Vergèze in the south of France, Perrier combines purity , refreshing taste , and a sparkling effervescence . Often associated with elegance and sophistication , Perrier is enjoyed worldwide as a premium sparkling water , both on its own and as a mixer.

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: Moët & Chandon is a prestigious French Champagne house founded in 1743 in the Champagne region of France. Renowned for its exceptional craftsmanship and luxury heritage , it produces some of the world's most celebrated Champagnes. As part of the LVMH Group , Moët & Chandon embodies excellence , elegance , and innovation while preserving centuries of winemaking expertise.

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: Meiji Holdings is a premier Japanese multinational headquartered in Tokyo , specializing in food , dairy , confectionery , nutrition , and pharmaceuticals . Founded in 1916/1917 , its leading subsidiaries include Meiji Co. (food and dairy) and Meiji Seika Pharma (medicine and vaccines). Meiji is known for iconic Japanese brands like Meiji Milk Chocolate , Oishii Gyunyu , and Kinoko no Yama , and it operates globally with sustainable innovation at its core.

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: Ile de France® is a French cheese brand inspired by the iconic ocean liner that first brought French cheese to the U.S. in 1936 . Reflecting French art de vivre , the brand offers a wide range of authentic and innovative cheeses , allowing consumers worldwide to enjoy refined snacks , enhance dishes , or create elegant cheese boards .

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: IWA is a premium Japanese sake brand founded by former Dom Pérignon cellar master Richard Geoffroy . Crafted in Toyama, IWA combines tradition and innovation through a unique blending approach called Assemblage , using different rice types, yeast strains, and brewing techniques. The result is a refined , complex sake that balances richness and purity . IWA redefines sake for a global audience, offering a modern expression of Japan’s iconic beverage .

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: Scapes is a Japanese brand that offers a contemporary reinterpretation of the traditional art of bonsai, combining natural elements with industrial materials such as stainless steel and acrylic. Founded by Shuzo Hamachi , Scapes stands out for its minimalist and conceptual aesthetic, pushing the boundaries between nature and design. Awarded at the 2025 London Design Awards , the brand continues to explore new dialogues between craftsmanship and modernity. At the event, Scapes will present its collaboration with CANON , ALBOS , to be released soon, as well as a collection of bonsai pots created in collaboration with HATAMAN TOUEN Co., Ltd.

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: Nespresso , a brand under the Nestlé Group , specializes in capsule coffee and offers a wide range of premium blends sourced from exceptional coffee - growing regions. Combining innovation , design , and a strong commitment to sustainability , Nespresso delivers a high-end coffee experience both at home and in the workplace . The brand is also actively engaged in capsule recycling and responsible coffee sourcing .

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: French Bloom is a premium French alcohol-free sparkling wine brand that blends French savoir-faire with wellness. Created by Maggie Frerejean-Taittinger and Constance Jablonski , French Bloom uses organic grapes and natural ingredients to craft elegant, festive cuvées without compromise. It offers a refined alternative to traditional champagne, celebrating joy, health, and inclusivity in every glass.

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: Jean-Charles Rochoux is a renowned French master chocolatier known for his unique artisan creations. Based in Paris since 2004, he offers original ganaches , chocolate sculptures , and his famous Saturday Tablet , filled with seasonal fresh fruits. Combining tradition and creativity , he also opened a boutique in Tokyo, sharing his chocolate artistry with a touch of French elegance .

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: Suntory is a leading Japanese beverage company known for its commitment to quality and innovation . For this event, we are pleased to offer two of our signature products: Iyemon Green Tea , a refreshing and authentic Japanese tea, and Premium Boss Black , a rich, unsweetened coffee brewed for bold flavor.

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: Domaine Ricardelle de Lautrec is located in Coursan, Aude , at the crossroads of La Clape, Minervois and Corbières . The Via Domitia , the ancient Roman road linking Rome to Spain, crosses our 50 hectares of vineyards . Once owned by the Toulouse-Lautrec family , the estate and its 19th-century cellars embody a rich heritage. For over 25 years , we have pursued our passion guided by the principles of biodynamic viticulture .

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: KOMA is a furniture atelier founded in 2003 by Shigeki Matsuoka . With the concept of “creating products that embody the beauty of one-of-a-kind works” , the small workshop of about twenty artisans, located in the suburbs of Tokyo, is dedicated to handcrafting furniture that its makers believe represents the very best. These pieces are sold through its directly operated stores in Ogikubo (Suginami Ward) and Aoyama (Minato Ward) .

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: The company has received numerous prestigious design awards from around the world and continues to share the excellence of Japanese craftsmanship on the global stage.

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: CHIE IMAI’s MORRIS is a premium Japanese imo shōchū crafted in Kagoshima from Golden Sengan sweet potatoes and black kōji . Inspired by French elegance and the idea of "drinking perfume," it offers a smooth, floral, and refined flavor at 25% ABV . Awarded Double Gold at the 2023 San Francisco World Spirits Competition and International Spirits Challenge, it’s a sophisticated choice even for those new to shōchū.

title: TV Studio

blocks.section: TV Studio
blocks.text: TV Studio

blocks.section: TV Studio
blocks.text: As part of the annual Business Summit , the TV Studio returns for a new edition co-presented by the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCIFJ) , in partnership with Nikkei and the French Embassy in Japan . This exclusive media platform gives participating companies and guests a unique opportunity to share their vision and insights in a 10-minute interview , reaching a high-level international business audience .

blocks.section: TV Studio
blocks.text: Interviews will be conducted by Régis Arnaud , Editor in Chief of France Japon Eco , a bilingual magazine under the CCIFJ since 2004. Based in Japan since 1995, he is also Japan-based correspondent for Le Figaro and Challenges and contributes regularly to Toyo Keizai . With over 25 years covering the Japanese economy and Franco-Japanese business relations , Régis brings deep expertise and valuable perspective.

blocks.section: TV Studio
blocks.text: Joining him is Yann Rousseau , Tokyo Bureau Chief for Les Échos . Having worked across Asia for nearly two decades —including in Beijing, Hanoi, Phnom Penh, and Paris —he settled in Tokyo in 2011. Yann is widely recognized for his sharp analysis of Japan’s economy and society . He co-authored the investigative book Le Fugitif (2020) with Régis Arnaud, exploring the Carlos Ghosn affair , and frequently comments on Japanese affairs in French-language media and podcasts.

blocks.section: TV Studio
blocks.text: Together, Régis and Yann offer insightful and authoritative interviews . Their extensive experience and credibility make this year’s TV Studio a can’t-miss opportunity for anyone aiming to boost their profile and impact in the international business community .

blocks.section: TV Studio
blocks.text: This year’s TV Studio is designed in collaboration with Koma , known for its refined furniture craftsmanship , and Scapes , which provides elegant bonsai arrangements that bring a touch of Japanese aesthetics to the set creating a sophisticated and harmonious atmosphere befitting this prestigious event.

blocks.section: Guide : Travailler au Japon
blocks.text: D’une manière générale, le marché de l’emploi japonais est conservateur et reste difficilement accessible aux étrangers. Une très bonne maîtrise du japonais est souvent un prérequis pour trouver un travail localement. Ceci est à la fois valable pour les entreprises japonaises mais aussi pour les entreprises étrangères, majoritairement composées de japonais.

blocks.section: Guide : Travailler au Japon
blocks.text: C’est pourquoi, il est important de bien réfléchir à son projet professionnel avant d’envisager son installation au Japon. Afin de vous renseigner au mieux, la CCI France Japon a réalisé un guide complet : Travailler au Japon.

blocks.section: Guide : Travailler au Japon
blocks.text: Vous y trouverez de nombreuses informations sur le marché de l’emploi, les canaux de recherche, et des conseils sur la vie pratique (logement, écoles de langue…).

blocks.section: Guide : Travailler au Japon
blocks.text: Vous pouvez également vous enregistrer sur notre plateforme emploi . Vous y trouverez les offres des entreprises membres de la CCI France Japon.

blocks.section: Guide : Travailler au Japon

blocks.section: Le marché de l'emploi
blocks.text: Le marché de l'emploi

blocks.section: Le marché de l'emploi
blocks.text: Le marché de l’emploi japonais est un marché conservateur, avec un faible taux de turnover. C’est un marché réputé difficile d’accès pour les étrangers dans lequel la main d’œuvre européenne est encore peu représentée. Avec un taux de chômage très faible (-3%), c’est un marché proche du plein emploi. Ce faible taux de chômage est à nuancer par la part que représente les emplois précaires (35% de la population active) dont les deux tiers sont composés de femmes.

blocks.section: Le marché de l'emploi
blocks.text: En 2017, l’Ambassade de France recensait plus de 9000 Français sur le territoire japonais. En prenant en compte, les ressortissants qui ne sont pas inscrits sur les registres consulaires, nous pouvons estimer la population française au Japon à un peu plus de 10 000 personnes.

blocks.section: Le marché de l'emploi
blocks.text: Il n’existe pas de profil type et tout dépend des besoins des entreprises. Néanmoins, nous pouvons observer une tendance générale. En contrat local, les français ayant fait des études supérieures qui ont une bonne maitrise du japonais et qui disposent d’une expertise dans une fonction ou un secteur d’activité sont les plus recherchés. La seule maitrise de la langue japonaise n’est pas toujours suffisante si elle n’est pas doublée d’une expérience valorisable auprès des entreprises.

blocks.section: Le marché de l'emploi
blocks.text: Les métiers dans l’informatique, la recherche et le développement, le recrutement en cabinet, l’enseignement et la restauration sont les branches qui sont souvent les plus susceptibles d’embaucher des étrangers. A condition de parler le japonais, certaines sociétés japonaises peuvent aussi recruter des étrangers pour des postes de « business development » à l’international.

blocks.section: Le marché de l'emploi
blocks.text: Même si cela reste difficile, il n’est pas impossible de trouver un emploi au Japon sans parler le japonais. Certains métiers nécessitent une expertise technique qui est parfois privilégiée à l’utilisation de la langue locale. C’est notamment le cas des ingénieurs IT, des chercheurs R&D ou de certains métiers en finance. D’une manière générale, il s’agit de postes orientés plutôt back office dont l’utilisation de la langue japonaise reste secondaire. A noter également que les cabinets de recrutement peuvent parfois être de bonnes alternatives aux étrangers qui ne trouvent pas de poste dans leur cœur de métier. Le Japon étant un marché relativement fermé aux étrangers, il est d’autant plus indispensable de construire et de bénéficier d’un réseau sur place (souvent par le biais d’associations) pour avoir connaissance d’opportunités via le bouche à oreille.

blocks.section: Le marché de l'emploi
blocks.text: Cela dépend de nombreux facteurs : expérience du candidat, maitrise de la langue locale, intensité de la recherche, distance, force du réseau sur place… Après s’être lancé dans une recherche active, il semble adéquat de faire un premier bilan passé les six premiers mois. Cela permettra de se rendre compte de ses forces, de ses faiblesses, et de revoir éventuellement son positionnement sur le marché de l’emploi.

blocks.section: Le marché de l'emploi
blocks.text: Chaque année, certains cabinets de recrutement (Robert Walters, Michael Page) publient un document répertoriant une moyenne des salaires par branche professionnelle. A titre purement indicatif, il faut compter environ 3 à 4 millions de yen pour un poste d’assistant, 6 à 8 millions de yen pour un manager, 10 millions de yen et plus pour un représentant de filiale d’une équipe d’au moins 5 à 10 personnes. Ces informations doivent être considérées pour les profils étrangers dont le système de rémunération reste fondé sur la compétence et non l’ancienneté. Au Japon, il est possible qu’un assistant avec 20 ans d’expérience puisse gagner 5 à 6 millions de yens, bonus compris.

blocks.section: Les visas
blocks.text: Les visas

blocks.section: Les visas
blocks.text: Il existe de nombreux visas qui permettent de travailler au Japon. Le plus connu est le visa de travail qui regroupe, en réalité, plusieurs visas adaptés à la situation de l’employé (Specialist in Humanities, Skilled Labor…). C’est l’entreprise qui devra sponsoriser l’employé pour l’obtention de son visa. Le « visa étudiant » et le « visa dependant » permettent également d’exercer une activité rémunérée dans la limite de 28h/semaine à condition d’obtenir une dérogation du Bureau de l’Immigration. Le visa étudiant est sponsorisée par une école (université ou école de langues) tandis que le visa dependant est accordé au conjoint marié(e) d’une personne amenée à travailler au Japon. Le visa vacances travail, non renouvelable, est accessible aux moins de 30 ans et permet de travailler au Japon (activité d’appoint) sur une période limitée d’un an.

blocks.section: Les visas
blocks.text: Le site de l’Ambassade du Japon en France référence les différents visas et leurs conditions d’obtention

blocks.section: Les visas
blocks.text: Il est formellement interdit de travailler avec un visa de visiteur temporaire (touriste) de 90 jours. Il est néanmoins possible d’assister à des réunions ou à des rdv à visée professionnelle. A l’expiration de son visa, la pratique consistant à quitter le Japon pour quelques jours avant d’y revenir pour trois mois complémentaires est déconseillée. Les inspecteurs de l’Immigration peuvent parfois juger suspect des va-et-vient trop fréquents.

blocks.section: Les visas
blocks.text: Pour obtenir un visa de travail, il est nécessaire d’avoir un contrat de travail avec une entreprise puisque c’est elle qui entamera les démarches de son obtention auprès du Bureau de l’Immigration. L’entreprise obtiendra, sur un délai variable de 2 à 3 mois, le certificat d’éligibilité (document souvent indispensable) qui vous permettra ensuite d’obtenir votre visa en quelques jours après dépôt de votre dossier au Consulat du Japon en France ou une nouvelle fois au Bureau de l’Immigration pour ceux qui résident au Japon. Il faut donc prévoir environ trois mois avant l’obtention de son visa de travail.

blocks.section: Les visas
blocks.text: Le Bureau de l’Immigration analyse les dossiers au cas par cas, et il n’y a pas de règle stricte quant à la délivrance d’un visa. Nous pouvons, néanmoins, remarquer dans les faits que l’employé doit au moins bénéficier d’une licence (BAC+3), que le contrat de travail ne doit pas être précaire (pas de temps partiel, pas d’activité ponctuelle…), que le salaire doit être raisonnable pour justifier d’un niveau de vie suffisant au Japon (au minimum 200 000 yen) et que la formation et l’expérience de l’employé correspondent au poste pour lequel il effectue sa demande de visa.

blocks.section: Les visas
blocks.text: Il n’est pas aisé d’obtenir un visa de travail avec un métier manuel. Sans licence (BAC+3), il faut avoir entre 3 et 10 ans d’expérience dans son cœur de métier pour postuler sur un visa de type « Skilled Labor ». Outre la problématique du visa, il faut savoir que les diplômes français sont très peu reconnus au Japon et qu’exercer son métier sur le territoire japonais demandera fort probablement des qualifications locales.

blocks.section: Les visas
blocks.text: Plusieurs centres d’immigration existent dans tout le Japon. Pour les résidents de Tokyo, la station de train la plus proche du Bureau de l’immigration est « Shinagawa ». Il faudra ensuite prendre un bus qui vous amènera directement au Bureau.

blocks.section: La langue japonaise
blocks.text: La langue japonaise

blocks.section: La langue japonaise
blocks.text: Le JLPT est un examen de japonais qui s’échelonne sur 5 niveaux (le niveau 1 étant le plus élevé). Contrairement au TOEIC, chaque participant choisit au moment de son inscription le niveau qu’il souhaite passer, puis il obtient un certificat en cas de réussite. L’examiné est libre de choisir le niveau qui lui correspond sans avoir à valider les niveaux inférieurs au préalable. Les épreuves (vocabulaire/grammaire, compréhension de texte et compréhension orale) se présentent sous la forme d’un QCM. Au Japon, il existe deux sessions par an pour passer le test :

blocks.section: La langue japonaise
blocks.text: - le 1er dimanche du mois de juillet

blocks.section: La langue japonaise
blocks.text: - le 1er dimanche du mois de décembre.

blocks.section: La langue japonaise
blocks.text: Plus d’informations sur le site officiel du JLPT : www.jlpt.jp/e/index.html

blocks.section: La langue japonaise
blocks.text: Le JLPT est reconnu comme l’examen officiel de japonais pour les non natifs. Paradoxalement, il est vrai que ce n’est pas un examen qui est toujours très connu des japonais. Néanmoins, les étrangers qui sont au Japon (ou les recruteurs locaux) le reconnaissent quasiment tous. Il est donc vivement conseillé de le passer afin d’améliorer ses chances d’obtenir un emploi. Comme tous les examens de langues, le JLPT permet de valoriser son CV à partir d’un certain niveau. Il peut faciliter l’accès à l’étape de l’entretien, mais ne sera jamais en soi un critère suffisant pour attester du niveau réel de japonais.

blocks.section: La langue japonaise
blocks.text: Conventionnellement, il est considéré que le niveau 2 de l’examen du JLPT est le niveau minimum requis pour travailler en entreprise. Tout dépend ensuite des entreprises et des postes sur lesquels vous souhaitez vous positionner. Un métier dans la communication nécessitera fort probablement un meilleur niveau de japonais qu’un métier dans la recherche. Les niveaux inférieurs de l’examen du JLPT seront tout de même appréciés des recruteurs comme étant un gage d’investissement et d’intérêt envers le Japon et sa langue.

blocks.section: La langue japonaise
blocks.text: En vivant au Japon, il est possible de prendre des cours dans la mairie de son arrondissement. Le prix des cours dans les mairies reste très abordable. Les écoles de langues proposent également des cours adaptés aux étudiants via plusieurs formules (intensif, cours trimestriel à temps partiel…). Elles peuvent sponsoriser des visa d’étudiant (pas de limite d’âge) pour ceux qui souhaitent apprendre le japonais sur une durée supérieure à 3 mois. A l’année, le financement d’une école de langue est plutôt onéreux (environ 5000 à 6000 €).

blocks.section: La langue japonaise
blocks.text: Lorsque l’on est étranger, parler l’anglais parait souvent être une évidence pour les japonais. C’est pourquoi, la maitrise de cette langue n’est pas véritablement considérée comme une valeur ajoutée auprès des recruteurs qui la considèrent souvent comme un prérequis.

blocks.section: La langue japonaise
blocks.text: En dehors du japonais, une maîtrise complète d’une troisième langue (chinois, coréen, portugais…) peut se révéler être un plus sur le marché de l’emploi.

blocks.section: Les canaux de recherche
blocks.text: Les canaux de recherche

blocks.section: Les canaux de recherche
blocks.text: Les trois pistes les plus exploitées pour trouver un emploi au Japon sont :

blocks.section: Les canaux de recherche
blocks.text: 1/ les sites d’emploi (CareerCross, Daijob, Gaijinpot…)

blocks.section: Les canaux de recherche
blocks.text: 2/ les cabinets de recrutement (Michael Page, Robert Walters, JAC…)

blocks.section: Les canaux de recherche
blocks.text: 3/ le réseau (LinkedIn, les associations, les réseaux alumni, les connaissances locales, le bouche à oreille)

blocks.section: Les canaux de recherche
blocks.text: Avant d’envisager une installation au Japon, il est important d’être conscient que le marché de l’emploi local reste à la fois conservateur et difficile d’accès pour les étrangers (barrière de la langue, différences socio-culturelles, forte identité nationale). Une fois sur place, les français les mieux préparés restent ceux qui ont construit un projet professionnel cohérent avec le Japon (échange universitaire, maitrise de la langue, expérience d’au moins 3 à 5 ans, etc…). Si votre projet s’inscrit dans la durée, nous vous invitons à vous investir dans l’apprentissage du Japonais. Même si vous n’atteignez pas un niveau professionnel, apprendre le japonais sera toujours bien perçu par la population locale. Néanmoins, bien qu’il puisse parfois être tentant de s’immerger complètement dans un environnement japonais, nous vous recommandons de rester visible auprès de la communauté francophone. Il est important de ne pas se couper socialement d’un réseau qui peut se révéler être une ressource utile. A cette fin, vous pouvez adhérer à des associations qui vous feront participer à des événements de networking ou participer à des conférences. L’objectif étant de rencontrer de nouvelles personnes, d’apprendre sur l’actualité au Japon et de se faire connaître. Si vous êtes expérimenté mais que vous ne parlez pas le japonais, développer son réseau restera un des meilleurs moyens de trouver un poste au Japon.

blocks.text: Beaucoup de cabinets de recrutement sont présents au Japon et de nombreuses entreprises passent par eux pour recruter leur personnel localement. Ils sont mandatés pour de nombreuses offres et c’est pourquoi il est préférable d’être inscrit dans leur base de données. Ils recherchent essentiellement des profils locaux expérimentés, ou des étrangers avec un bon niveau de langue. Néanmoins, ils peuvent parfois avoir quelques offres plus Junior.

blocks.section: Les canaux de recherche
blocks.text: Il existe plusieurs salons professionnels au Japon et c’est souvent une piste à ne pas négliger dans le cadre de ses recherches. Daijob organise un Job Fair (Go Global Career Fair) composé d’entreprises japonaises et étrangères, environ 4 à 6 fois par an. De nombreux étrangers participent à cet événement gratuit sur inscription. A destination des jeunes diplômés étrangers, Works Japan Global organise une à deux fois par an un forum professionnel intitulé : Job Festa, à Akihabara et à Kyoto. A destination des ingénieurs, notamment avec une spécialité IT, il existe un salon professionnel organisé par @type intitulé : Ingénieur TekiShoku Fair.

blocks.section: Les canaux de recherche
blocks.text: Le VIE est une formule développée et gérée par Business France (anciennement UbiFrance). L’organisme diffuse directement les offres des entreprises sur sa plateforme CiviWeb (https://www.civiweb.com). Pour être éligible, il faut avoir moins de 28 ans et ne pas avoir déjà effectué une mission de même nature. La durée de la mission est souvent d’un an, renouvelable un an. C’est un excellent tremplin pour commencer sa carrière au Japon. En parallèle de Civiweb, la CCIFJ peut parfois diffuser sur son site internet quelques offres de VIE lorsque les entreprises le souhaitent. Néanmoins, toute gestion après le recrutement d’un candidat sera gérée par Business France.

blocks.section: Les canaux de recherche
blocks.text: Il y a essentiellement deux cas de figures. Si vous disposez déjà d’un visa qui vous permette de travailler au Japon, le plus simple reste d’exercer son activité en freelance, puis de remplir annuellement sa feuille d’imposition fiscale japonaise. Vous pouvez vous faire aider d’un cabinet comptable dans vos démarches. Si vous ne possédez pas de visa, ou que vous souhaitez créer une entreprise avec une entité juridique au Japon, il faudra accomplir les démarches pour l’obtention d’un visa « Business Investor ». C’est ce visa qui vous permettra de créer votre structure au Japon, mais son obtention nécessite un capital de départ de 5 millions de yen. Vous retrouverez les différentes entités légales existantes et les démarches à accomplir pour la création de votre entreprise dans le document : S’implanter au Japon.

blocks.section: Les canaux de recherche
blocks.text: Avant de commencer sa recherche, il est important de noter que la formule bien connue du stage en France n’existe pas vraiment au Japon. C’est une pratique méconnue qui ne rentre pas dans le cursus universitaire d’un étudiant japonais. Ceci est à la fois valable pour les entreprises japonaises mais également pour les entreprises françaises, majoritairement composées de japonais. Par conséquent, mieux vaut être averti que les offres de stage sont assez peu nombreuses. La CCI France Japon reçoit environ une dizaine d’offres de stage à l’année. Cela est relativement peu mais s’explique principalement pour les raisons évoquées ci-dessus. Vous trouverez également des offres de stage sur la plateforme Kopra. A toute fin utile, sachez que la CCI France Japon publie également un annuaire des entreprises françaises dans lequel vous trouverez les contacts des entreprises membres.

blocks.section: Les canaux de recherche
blocks.text: La carte de visite est souvent considérée comme un incontournable de la culture japonaise. Les recruteurs ayant toujours votre CV à la main au moment d’un entretien, elle n’est pas indispensable dans le contexte d’un recrutement. Par contre, elle peut se révéler très utile si vous participez à des événements dans lesquels vous êtes amenés à rencontrer beaucoup de monde.

blocks.section: Les canaux de recherche
blocks.text: Trouver un emploi d’appoint au Japon est plus simple qu’un emploi durable. Les secteurs qui recrutent le plus sont : l’enseignement, l’hôtellerie et la restauration. Dans ces secteurs d’activités, le porte à porte et la candidature spontanée sont plus facilement acceptés. Hellowork, organisme public japonais, a un centre dédié aux étrangers et peut vous aider dans vos démarches. Le site Gaijinpot recense aussi de nombreuses annonces de baito. Vous pouvez également trouver des offres d’emploi dans des magazines locaux dédiés au lectorat étranger comme : Metropolis, Weekender…

blocks.section: Les canaux de recherche
blocks.text: Depuis quelques années, de nombreuses écoles de langue sont devenues plus exigeantes et demandent aux candidats d’avoir le diplôme du FLE afin d’enseigner le français. C’est notamment le cas des écoles publiques et de certaines écoles privés. Cependant, certains établissements restent encore ouverts, et il est possible d’enseigner le français à condition de disposer d’une licence ou d’une expérience préalable dans l’enseignement. Les postes disponibles sont souvent à pourvoir en freelance ou à temps partiel et il est plus difficile d’obtenir un poste d’enseignant régulier. Vous pouvez contacter les écoles de langue inscrites dans la brochure « Travailler au Japon » afin de connaître leur éventuel besoin en recrutement.

blocks.section: CV et entretien
blocks.text: CV et entretien

blocks.section: CV et entretien
blocks.text: Pour les entreprises françaises et étrangères, un CV en anglais est souvent suffisant. Sur demande explicite de l’entreprise, et si le candidat parle déjà le japonais, il peut être nécessaire de fournir son CV en japonais. Beaucoup de candidats adoptent alors le format anglo-saxon du CV qu’ils traduisent en japonais. Ce n’est pas un problème, mais sachez qu’il existe aussi au Japon un format standard pré-rempli (Rirekisho et Shokumukeirekisho) que vous pouvez acheter dans les Convenient Stores et qui doit être rempli à la main. Ce CV existe également au format Word ou Excel, et de plus en plus de candidats les rédigent désormais de manière digitale.

blocks.section: CV et entretien
blocks.text: La logique d’un entretien à la française est différent de celui d’un entretien à la japonaise. En France, le candidat part de zéro, le recruteur l’écoute et il gagne des points au fur et à mesure qu’il sait se montrer convaincant. Au Japon, le candidat commence avec « 100 points » et le recruteur décompte les points au fil des erreurs qui sont commises par le candidat. Les premières minutes de l’entretien sont donc capitales et il ne faut en aucun cas négliger son apparence et son attitude. Rester le dos droit, mettre ses mains sur ses genoux, écouter l’interlocuteur avec attention sont des points essentiels pour bien commencer. Après avoir reçu la carte de visite de son interlocuteur avec ses deux mains, on évitera de la ranger brusquement dans sa poche, de la tapoter sur la table, ou d’écrire dessus. On la posera proprement, et face à soi, sur la table. En terme de contenu, les japonais sont souvent curieux et flattés de l’intérêt que vous pouvez porter à leur pays et à leur langue. Ils poseront donc certainement des questions liées à vos motivations sur le Japon. Dans des environnements très japonais, plus que la compétence, ce qui intéresse les recruteurs, c’est de savoir si votre personnalité est compatible avec l’entreprise et l’équipe déjà en place. Il est conseillé de mettre son expérience en perspective et de bien montrer la cohérence entre sa carrière et sa volonté d’intégrer l’entreprise en question.

blocks.section: Logement
blocks.text: Comme pour la France, trouver un appartement au Japon via une agence immobilière est difficile si l’on n’a pas un emploi stable et une personne sur place qui accepte d’être garant. C’est d’ailleurs souvent l’entreprise du salarié qui accepte de porter cette responsabilité. Ce n’est donc pas la solution la plus simple à privilégier lorsque l’on arrive au Japon sans travail. La méthode la plus facile d’accès reste encore celle des Guest House qui accueillent chaque année de nombreux étrangers. Elles proposent des dortoirs, des maisons en colocation ou bien des appartements individuels meublés. Les formalités administratives sont simples et de nombreux employés parlent le français. blocks.section: Quelques aspects culturels
blocks.text: Quelques aspects culturels

blocks.section: Quelques aspects culturels
blocks.text: La culture japonaise est un ensemble vaste et complexe qui est difficilement réductible à quelques lignes. Nous nous attacherons donc à ne décrire qu’un concept clé : Tatemae / Hon’ne (littéralement façade / vrai son), qui se retrouve dans les différentes strates de la société japonaise.

blocks.section: Quelques aspects culturels
blocks.text: Le Tatemae est le comportement de façade qu’adoptent les japonais en société, et qui consiste à toujours rester politiquement très correct afin d’éviter de mettre son interlocuteur dans une situation conflictuelle ou dérangeante. En contrepartie, le Hon’ne renvoie aux véritables pensées subjectives d’une personne que les japonais ne communiquent qu’en cercle restreint (famille, amis très proches). Pour les étrangers, l’objectif n’est pas nécessairement de se comporter comme les japonais. D’une part, parce que les japonais apprécient précisément chez les étrangers le fait d’être différent, et d’autre part, parce qu’ils pardonnent toujours plus à un étranger une impolitesse culturelle qu’à un de leur semblable. Néanmoins, comprendre le Tatemae et le Hon’ne permettra à un étranger de mieux interagir dans la communauté japonaise.

blocks.section: Quelques aspects culturels
blocks.text: Au quotidien, les japonais sont habitués à recevoir une excellente qualité de service, ce qui les rend très exigeants dans leur manière d’appréhender un produit ou un service. Ils sont habitués à être guidés par des instructions claires et précises. Au Japon, il y a des codes et des processus partout et l’anticipation est le maitre mot. Les japonais se sentent souvent déboussolés devant une situation inattendue, ou trop spontanée. A noter également qu’ils ont vraiment le souci de la forme, et qu’ils y accordent presque autant d’importance qu’au fond.

blocks.section: Quelques aspects culturels
blocks.text: De nombreux japonais considèrent leur entreprise comme une seconde famille. Dès l’université, les étudiants ne choisissent pas la fonction qu’ils souhaitent exercer, mais plutôt l’entreprise qu’ils souhaitent intégrer. Ils savent souvent qu’au moment de se faire recruter, ils vont rester de nombreuses années dans la même entreprise. Vierge de toute expérience, ils vont être formés aux valeurs et savoir-faire de leur société en changeant régulièrement de service. Leur salaire sera majoré tous les ans, et avec l’ancienneté, ils auront une vue globale de la société qui les a fait grandir. Indépendamment de leur charge de travail, les japonais investissent beaucoup de temps pour le compte de leur société. Peu d’entre eux acceptent de prendre les 10 jours de congés annuels qui leur sont attribués, puisque s’absenter reviendrait à reporter sa charge de travail sur celle d’un collègue. Les nombreuses heures supplémentaires sont des heures de services rendus à l’entreprise. Travailler n’est donc pas seulement s’épanouir dans ses fonctions et gagner un salaire, mais c’est aussi donner un sens à sa vie.

blocks.section: ABOUT GLOBIS
blocks.text: GLOBIS Corporation is a leading business education and venture capital firm based in Japan. Established in 1992, GLOBIS is best known for operating the GLOBIS University Graduate School of Management, Japan’s largest business school offering MBA programs in both Japanese and English. The company also provides corporate training programs, online learning platforms, and publishes business-related content.

blocks.section: ABOUT GLOBIS
blocks.text: In addition to its educational services, GLOBIS runs a venture capital arm, GLOBIS Capital Partners, which invests in promising startups in Japan and beyond. Through its integrated approach combining education, entrepreneurship, and investment, GLOBIS aims to foster visionary leaders and drive innovation across the world.

blocks.section: Explore Exhibition Booths
blocks.text: At the French-Japanese Business Summit, the Nikkei Hall will host a variety of food, beverage and partner stands . Visitors will have the chance to taste products, discover new flavors, and meet the brands behind them. It’s the perfect place to enjoy, network, and experience French-Japanese gastronomy .

blocks.section: Partners
blocks.text: Partners

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: Details

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: Savencia is a leading international food group specializing in cheese and dairy products . With brands like Caprice des Dieux , Saint Agur , and Bresso , the group combines innovation and tradition to offer high-quality products worldwide . Present in over 120 countries , Savencia is committed to sustainability , taste , and craftsmanship , serving both consumers and culinary professionals.

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: Aux Merveilleux de Fred is a French patisserie known for its delicate meringue-based cakes coated in whipped cream and chocolate shavings. Founded by Frédéric Vaucamps , the brand celebrates artisanal savoir-faire and French tradition . With boutiques across Europe , Asia , and North America , it offers a refined taste of Parisian indulgence around the world.

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: Godiva is a premium Belgian chocolate brand known for its artisanal expertise and rich heritage since 1926 . It offers a wide range of luxury chocolates , truffles , and gourmet treats , blending tradition with innovation . With a strong global presence , Godiva is dedicated to providing indulgent experiences through high-quality ingredients and elegant presentation .

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: Perrier is a French mineral water brand famous for its natural carbonation and distinctive green bottle . Sourced from Vergèze in the south of France, Perrier combines purity , refreshing taste , and a sparkling effervescence . Often associated with elegance and sophistication , Perrier is enjoyed worldwide as a premium sparkling water , both on its own and as a mixer.

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: Meiji Holdings is a premier Japanese multinational headquartered in Tokyo , specializing in food , dairy , confectionery , nutrition , and pharmaceuticals . Founded in 1916/1917 , its leading subsidiaries include Meiji Co. (food and dairy) and Meiji Seika Pharma (medicine and vaccines). Meiji is known for iconic Japanese brands like Meiji Milk Chocolate , Oishii Gyunyu , and Kinoko no Yama , and it operates globally with sustainable innovation at its core.

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: Ile de France® is a French cheese brand inspired by the iconic ocean liner that first brought French cheese to the U.S. in 1936 . Reflecting French art de vivre , the brand offers a wide range of authentic and innovative cheeses , allowing consumers worldwide to enjoy refined snacks , enhance dishes , or create elegant cheese boards .

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: IWA is a premium Japanese sake brand founded by former Dom Pérignon cellar master Richard Geoffroy . Crafted in Toyama, IWA combines tradition and innovation through a unique blending approach called Assemblage , using different rice types, yeast strains, and brewing techniques. The result is a refined , complex sake that balances richness and purity . IWA redefines sake for a global audience, offering a modern expression of Japan’s iconic beverage .

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: Scapes is a Japanese brand that offers a contemporary reinterpretation of the traditional art of bonsai, combining natural elements with industrial materials such as stainless steel and acrylic. Founded by Shuzo Hamachi , Scapes stands out for its minimalist and conceptual aesthetic, pushing the boundaries between nature and design. Awarded at the 2025 London Design Awards , the brand continues to explore new dialogues between craftsmanship and modernity. At the event, Scapes will present its collaboration with CANON , ALBOS , to be released soon, as well as a collection of bonsai pots created in collaboration with HATAMAN TOUEN Co., Ltd.

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: Nespresso , a brand under the Nestlé Group , specializes in capsule coffee and offers a wide range of premium blends sourced from exceptional coffee - growing regions. Combining innovation , design , and a strong commitment to sustainability , Nespresso delivers a high-end coffee experience both at home and in the workplace . The brand is also actively engaged in capsule recycling and responsible coffee sourcing .

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: French Bloom is a premium French alcohol-free sparkling wine brand that blends French savoir-faire with wellness. Created by Maggie Frerejean-Taittinger and Constance Jablonski , French Bloom uses organic grapes and natural ingredients to craft elegant, festive cuvées without compromise. It offers a refined alternative to traditional champagne, celebrating joy, health, and inclusivity in every glass.

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: Jean-Charles Rochoux is a renowned French master chocolatier known for his unique artisan creations. Based in Paris since 2004, he offers original ganaches , chocolate sculptures , and his famous Saturday Tablet , filled with seasonal fresh fruits. Combining tradition and creativity , he also opened a boutique in Tokyo, sharing his chocolate artistry with a touch of French elegance .

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: Suntory is a leading Japanese beverage company known for its commitment to quality and innovation . For this event, we are pleased to offer two of our signature products : Iyemon Green Tea , a refreshing and authentic Japanese tea , and Premium Boss Black , a rich , unsweetened coffee brewed for bold flavor .

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: Domaine Ricardelle de Lautrec is located in Coursan, Aude , at the crossroads of La Clape, Minervois and Corbières . The Via Domitia , the ancient Roman road linking Rome to Spain, crosses our 50 hectares of vineyards . Once owned by the Toulouse-Lautrec family , the estate and its 19th-century cellars embody a rich heritage. For over 25 years , we have pursued our passion guided by the principles of biodynamic viticulture .

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: KOMA is a furniture atelier founded in 2003 by Shigeki Matsuoka . With the concept of “creating products that embody the beauty of one-of-a-kind works” , the small workshop of about twenty artisans, located in the suburbs of Tokyo, is dedicated to handcrafting furniture that its makers believe represents the very best. These pieces are sold through its directly operated stores in Ogikubo (Suginami Ward) and Aoyama (Minato Ward) .

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: The company has received numerous prestigious design awards from around the world and continues to share the excellence of Japanese craftsmanship on the global stage.

blocks.section: Details
blocks.text: CHIE IMAI’s MORRIS is a premium Japanese imo shōchū crafted in Kagoshima from Golden Sengan sweet potatoes and black kōji . Inspired by French elegance and the idea of "drinking perfume," it offers a smooth, floral, and refined flavor at 25% ABV . Awarded Double Gold at the 2023 San Francisco World Spirits Competition and International Spirits Challenge, it’s a sophisticated choice even for those new to shōchū.

title: TV Studio

blocks.section: TV Studio
blocks.text: TV Studio

blocks.section: TV Studio
blocks.text: As part of the annual Business Summit , the TV Studio returns for a new edition co-presented by the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCIFJ) , in partnership with Nikkei and the French Embassy in Japan . This exclusive media platform gives participating companies and guests a unique opportunity to share their vision and insights in a 10-minute interview , reaching a high-level international business audience .

blocks.section: TV Studio
blocks.text: Interviews will be conducted by Régis Arnaud , Editor in Chief of France Japon Eco , a bilingual magazine under the CCIFJ since 2004. Based in Japan since 1995, he is also Japan-based correspondent for Le Figaro and Challenges and contributes regularly to Toyo Keizai . With over 25 years covering the Japanese economy and Franco-Japanese business relations , Régis brings deep expertise and valuable perspective.

blocks.section: TV Studio
blocks.text: Joining him is Yann Rousseau , Tokyo Bureau Chief for Les Échos . Having worked across Asia for nearly two decades —including in Beijing, Hanoi, Phnom Penh, and Paris —he settled in Tokyo in 2011. Yann is widely recognized for his sharp analysis of Japan’s economy and society . He co-authored the investigative book Le Fugitif (2020) with Régis Arnaud, exploring the Carlos Ghosn affair , and frequently comments on Japanese affairs in French-language media and podcasts.

blocks.section: TV Studio
blocks.text: Together, Régis and Yann offer insightful and authoritative interviews . Their extensive experience and credibility make this year’s TV Studio a can’t-miss opportunity for anyone aiming to boost their profile and impact in the international business community .

blocks.section: TV Studio
blocks.text: This year’s TV Studio is designed in collaboration with Koma , known for its refined furniture craftsmanship , and Scapes , which provides elegant bonsai arrangements that bring a touch of Japanese aesthetics to the set creating a sophisticated and harmonious atmosphere befitting this prestigious event.

blocks.section: Specificities of the Japanese Market
blocks.text: Specificities of the Japanese Market

blocks.section: Specificities of the Japanese Market
blocks.text: In Japan, business discussions and decision-making processes are generally gradual and built on relationships of trust. Initial meetings are typically arranged only once a genuine level of interest has been confirmed (on average, 10% of prospects contacted), ensuring a high level of qualification among the contacts met during the mission.

blocks.section: Specificities of the Japanese Market
blocks.text: Between the initial contact and the signing of a contract, business agreements generally require a longer timeframe, often ranging from 1 to 3 years, depending on the industry and the organizational complexity of the companies involved.

blocks.section: Specificities of the Japanese Market
blocks.text: In this context, the objective of this mission is not to secure immediate contracts, but rather to build relationships of trust, validate market interest, and establish a structured sales pipeline designed to support sustainable business development in Japan.

blocks.section: WHY THE HEALTHCARE MARKET IN JAPAN?
blocks.text: WHY THE HEALTHCARE MARKET IN JAPAN?

blocks.section: WHY THE HEALTHCARE MARKET IN JAPAN?
blocks.text: Japan represents one of the most strategic healthcare markets worldwide. Driven by structural demographic trends and strong public funding capacity, it offers long-term visibility for companies operating in the sector.

blocks.section: WHY THE HEALTHCARE MARKET IN JAPAN?
blocks.text: Nearly 30% of the Japanese population is now over 65 years old, and healthcare expenditure accounts for approximately 10–11% of GDP. This demographic shift sustains long-term demand, particularly in high value-added segments.

blocks.section: WHY THE HEALTHCARE MARKET IN JAPAN?
blocks.text: Market opportunities are especially concentrated in:

blocks.section: WHY THE HEALTHCARE MARKET IN JAPAN?
blocks.text: – The silver economy and chronic disease management – Digital health and AI-based diagnostics – Medical devices – Regenerative medicine

blocks.section: WHY THE HEALTHCARE MARKET IN JAPAN?
blocks.text: Japan is a premium ecosystem with a strong focus on innovation. Success in this market requires a clear understanding of regulatory requirements, the establishment of solid local partnerships, and a long-term positioning strategy. In return, the potential lies in high-value, technology-intensive segments.

blocks.section: WHY THE SPACE SECTOR IN JAPAN?
blocks.text: WHY THE SPACE SECTOR IN JAPAN?

blocks.section: WHY THE SPACE SECTOR IN JAPAN?
blocks.text: Japan, the world’s fourth-largest economy and a major space power, plays a significant role in international programs. The country relies in particular on the expertise of Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), which leads the development of next-generation launch vehicles, advanced propulsion technologies, as well as civil and defense satellites.

blocks.section: WHY THE SPACE SECTOR IN JAPAN?
blocks.text: In response to the growing strategic importance of the space sector, the Japanese government has launched a major investment plan, including a space fund of more than USD 6.4 billion over 10 years. This initiative aims to support public and private projects, universities, satellite constellations, and international programs, while strengthening national industrial capabilities.

blocks.section: WHY THE SPACE SECTOR IN JAPAN?
blocks.text: This ambitious strategy positions Japan as a key partner for international companies seeking to expand within the global space industry.

blocks.text: Sport in Asia is currently experiencing significant growth, driven by regional economic momentum and the rapid modernization of sports infrastructure. blocks.section: WHY SPORT IN JAPAN?
blocks.text: The Asian Games illustrate this strong commitment to sport and performance. The event brings together 45 nations, more than 12,000 athletes, and features 41 sports across over 460 medal events.

blocks.text: With an estimated budget of approximately €1 billion, it is the second-largest multi-sport event in the world after the Olympic Games. It represents a unique opportunity to discover the diversity, dynamism, and economic potential of the Asian sports market.

title: Why expanding into Japan?
description: Why expanding into Japan? Discover key figures, trends, business opportunities and the peculiarities of the Japanese market.

blocks.section: Why expanding into Japan?
blocks.text: Why expanding into Japan?

blocks.section: Why expanding into Japan?
blocks.text: CHECK OUR NEWS SECTION

blocks.section: Why expanding into Japan?
blocks.text: Japan: The Third-largest Economy in the World

blocks.section: Why expanding into Japan?
blocks.text: Renowned for its advanced technologies, unique culture, and capacity of resilience, Japan attracts many international companies. It's a country projected towards the future, modern, and yet deeply traditional. Ready to embrace innovations from abroad but less inclined to integrate foreign influences. Its corporate culture, strongly influenced by a diversity of historical and cultural factors, often creates barriers to the establishment of economic partnerships. Nevertheless, in recent years, commercial ties between Japan and other countries have significantly developed.

blocks.section: Why expanding into Japan?
blocks.text: With a GDP of 3.7 trillion euros in 2022 (1.1% growth), Japan emerges as the country with the third largest economy in the world. It is also one of the world's largest importers and serves as the gateway for businesses to enter the North Asian market.

blocks.section: Why expanding into Japan?
blocks.text: As the eleventh most densely populated country in the world, with over 124 million inhabitants within 377,975 square kilometers (329 people per square kilometer), the majority of its population is concentrated in the capital, Tokyo, and other major Japanese cities such as Nagoya, Osaka, Kyoto, Kobe, and Hiroshima.

blocks.section: Why expanding into Japan?
blocks.text: Tokyo: The World's Largest Economic Megalopolis

blocks.section: Why expanding into Japan?
blocks.text: In 2023, the Tokyo metropolitan area has a population of 37 million inhabitants with a very high density (5,000 people per square kilometer). Commercial zones, numerous and diverse, are mainly organized around train stations. They are interconnected by a sophisticated and efficient transportation network. Services, finance, and insurance are the dominant sectors in the Japanese capital.

blocks.section: Why expanding into Japan?
blocks.text: Regional Japan

blocks.section: Why expanding into Japan?
blocks.text: 13 Japanese cities have a population of over one million inhabitants and the country's population is 91% urban. Each region has its own strengths: the north specializes in agri-food industries, woodworking, and paper; the region surrounding Nagoya, Chubu, hosts major automotive and aerospace industrial sites. Osaka is renowned for electronics, and Fukuoka in the south of the country is known for its connections with Asia.

blocks.section: Why expanding into Japan?
blocks.text: Japanese Consumers

blocks.section: Why expanding into Japan?
blocks.text: With an average monthly salary of 2,120 euros in 2022, the Japanese population enjoys one of the highest purchasing powers in the world and a relatively low unemployment rate (2.6% in 2022). Its high standards and strong attraction to novelty and trend set it apart. Japan often serves as a preferred test market for the global launch of new products or services. French, in particular, maintains a high reputation in areas such as cosmetics, luxury goods, gastronomy, and fashion. The Japanese market is also the world's third-largest e-commerce market.

blocks.section: Why expanding into Japan?
blocks.text: Japan, global leader in innovation

blocks.section: Why expanding into Japan?
blocks.text: Japan is the country that allocates the highest proportion of its GDP to R&D (3.4% of GDP compared to 2.2% in France) and is the second-largest filer of patents in the world. The country's R&D accounts for 20% of global R&D. Recognized as a technological leader in B2C, Japan also excels in many B2B sectors. It has 5,328 researchers per million inhabitants (compared to 4,205 in the United States and 4,233 in France).

blocks.section: Why expanding into Japan?
blocks.text: Economic Trends

blocks.section: Why expanding into Japan?
blocks.text: As the third-largest global economic power and a member of ASEAN, Japan is deeply integrated into Asia. In 2022, it is China's second-largest supplier, with 57% of its exports directed towards Asia, a share that has been increasing since the 2000s. Japan's integration into Asian economies is a key factor in the country's current success, benefiting from the growth of emerging Asian countries.

blocks.section: Why expanding into Japan?
blocks.text: The quality of Japanese products, their constant renewal, and the unparalleled focus on customer's experience are strengths that allow certain Japanese conglomerates to remain among the most profitable and powerful groups in the world. Furthermore, Japan has secured mastery of key technologies in many high-tech sectors.

blocks.section: Why expanding into Japan?
blocks.text: According to the Economic Complexity Observatory, Japan has the world's most "complex" economy. This means that it exports a wide variety of highly sophisticated and unique products. The country has maintained the top position in this ranking since the 1990s, thanks to the quantity and quality of its expertise and its strong economic relations. Its major exports include vehicles, integrated circuits, vehicle accessories and components, machinery, and photographic equipment.

blocks.section: Why expanding into Japan?
blocks.text: Demographically, the declining population and increasing life expectancy create new market segments. Seniors receive special attention, whether they are active or retired. This segment of society has high purchasing power and demands specific treatment in terms of leisure, services, and well-being. Japan has thus become a laboratory for new trends that most Western societies will face soon with the aging of their populations.

blocks.section: Why expanding into Japan?
blocks.text: On the financial front, Japan remains a crucial player. With the strength of its external trade, the country holds the world's second-largest foreign exchange reserves (USD 1.265 trillion as of April 2023) and remains one of the major funders globally.

blocks.section: Why expanding into Japan?
blocks.text: In 2011, the Fukushima incident raised questions about the energy mix, particularly the role of nuclear power. Japan still has operational reactors that function very sporadically. Before the incident, nuclear power accounted for 29% of the country's electricity supply, a gap that the country now needs to fill through imports, which weighs on the traditionally surplus trade balance. However, this situation acts as a driving force for energy transition in Japan and has prompted the country to set ambitious targets for renewable energy use.

blocks.section: Why expanding into Japan?
blocks.text: Following the decisions of former Prime Minister Shinzo Abe, Japan embarked on a series of deep reforms known as "Abenomics" since 2013. The government aims to: 1) stimulate domestic demand through massive public spending (EUR 671 billion in 2014), 2) inject liquidity into the economy to encourage lending and investment, and 3) liberalize certain key sectors (such as the pharmaceutical industry and energy).

blocks.section: Why expanding into Japan?
blocks.text: If you want to learn about economic trends by sector, please refer to our sectoral notes (in French).

blocks.section: Why expanding into Japan?
blocks.text: Trade Relations between France and Japan

blocks.section: Why expanding into Japan?
blocks.text: Nearly 10,000 French companies exported a total of 6.5 billion euros to Japan in 2021, a 15.6% increase compared to their level in 2020 (5.6 billion euros).

blocks.section: Why expanding into Japan?
blocks.text: The volume of French exports has not yet returned to the exceptional level of 2019 (7.7 billion euros, partly due to the implementation of the EU-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA) in February 2019); however, it is returning to the average observed during the 2014-2018 period. The trade deficit against France amounted to -2.9 billion euros in 2021.

blocks.section: Why expanding into Japan?
blocks.text: The aerospace sector (1.5 billion euros in 2021, 23% of total exports; +116%) is a significant driver of French exports to Japan.

blocks.section: Why expanding into Japan?
blocks.text: The agri-food sector maintains a good level, and Japan remains our top customer in this segment in Asia. French exports increased by 6% in 2021 (1.23 billion euros, 19% of total exports), close to the record level of 2019 (1.31 billion euros). Half of French agri-food exports to Japan consist of wines and spirits.

blocks.section: Why expanding into Japan?
blocks.text: Luxury products, textiles, clothing, as well as chemicals, perfumes, and cosmetics accounted for over 22% of French exports to Japan in 2021, with respective increases of 7% and 5.3%.

blocks.section: Why expanding into Japan?
blocks.text: Regarding energy, France has a very small market share in this sector in Japan (1%) because it primarily exported nuclear industry-related technologies, which have been stagnant in the archipelago in recent years. The Japanese government is now investing billions of euros in renewable and green energies, mainly hydrogen but also wind, solar, and ammonia.

blocks.section: Why expanding into Japan?
blocks.text: In 2021, Japan is France's 13th largest customer, its 12th largest supplier, and its 2nd largest Asian trading partner after China, for both imports and exports.

blocks.section: Why expanding into Japan?
blocks.text: In 2020, France was the 3rd largest foreign investor in Japan, behind the United States and Singapore. France has 500 companies in Japan, with 69% belonging to the manufacturing sector (Air France, Michelin, Renault, Valeo, Air Liquide, Total, Sanofi Aventis, Danone...) and 31% belonging to the services sector (Axa, BNP Paribas, Société Générale, Crédit Agricole, JCDecaux, Orange...).

title: Hello Tomorrow Japan
description: Hello Tomorrow Japan supports deep tech innovation in Japan, provides assistance to startups, and promotes collaboration.

blocks.section: Hello Tomorrow Japan
blocks.text: Hello Tomorrow Japan

blocks.section: Hello Tomorrow Japan
blocks.text: Since 2017, Hello Tomorrow Japan has been energizing local innovation communities in Japan, marking a significant impact on the country's deep tech landscape.

blocks.section: Hello Tomorrow Japan
blocks.text: Hello Tomorrow Japan is part of the global Hello Tomorrow network, a global network born in France in 2011, which promotes and supports cutting-edge innovations, bridging the gap between ideas and their concrete implementation. Focused on deep tech, Hello Tomorrow helps startup founders generate meaningful change and tackle complex global challenges through collaboration and entrepreneurship.

blocks.section: Hello Tomorrow Japan
blocks.text: Deep tech refers to cutting-edge technologies rooted in scientific discoveries or technical innovations, capable of delivering significant breakthroughs and disrupting various industry sectors.

blocks.section: Hello Tomorrow Japan
blocks.text: Our core mission in Japan is to bridge the gaps in local and global ecosystems by connecting innovators, industry leaders and investment opportunities. Through events and networking, we address the specific needs and interests of Japan's innovation community and facilitate knowledge sharing, idea exchanges and meetings to create meaningful connections and partnerships that foster innovation.

title: BONJOUR FRANCE
description: Bonjour France invites Japanese people to discover the French way of life with exceptional events.

blocks.section: BONJOUR FRANCE
blocks.text: BONJOUR FRANCE

blocks.section: BONJOUR FRANCE
blocks.text: Each year, BONJOUR FRANCE hosts, with its French and Japanese partners, exceptional events that highlight the French " Art de vivre ".

blocks.section: BONJOUR FRANCE
blocks.text: To truly grasp what constitutes the French " Art de vivre " is not an easy task. Living “ à la française” means taking time to have a nice meal, to learn, to dream, to share…

blocks.section: BONJOUR FRANCE
blocks.text: Throughout the year, BONJOUR FRANCE invites the Japanese public to discover the French way of life, by sharing French traditional expertise in a variety of modern and innovative ways.

blocks.section: BONJOUR FRANCE
blocks.text: BONJOUR FRANCE proposes to share unique cultural moments, to discover our gastronomy in an informal manner, to taste new products that cannot be found in Japan and to take part in unique lifestyle events in the mythical department stores and other places.

blocks.section: BONJOUR FRANCE
blocks.text: Find more about BONJOUR FRANCE program on https://bonjourfranceccifj.com/ and come take part in our numerous events to discover the French way of life.

blocks.section: BONJOUR FRANCE
blocks.text: France has dressed up for the occasion, come and meet her!

blocks.section: Entrepreneur
blocks.text: The Entrepreneurship Committee supports current and aspiring entrepreneurs and other business people with entrepreneurial zeal. The committee’s mission is to deliver wisdom, learning, insights, and practical advice for building and expanding business on one’s own terms. Our events are highly interactive, featuring guests who share real experiences of success and failure. They address topics such as rapid business growth, deliberate market disruption, dauntless leadership, capturing market share with panache, disciplined innovation, unfair competitive advantage that is perfectly legal, and other topics of particular interest to entrepreneurs and growth-oriented business people.

title: French Business Awards
description: Organized every year by the French Chamber, the French Business Awards honor excellence and promote success and innovation across all industries. The awards also acknowledge the important social contributions made by organizations through their commitment to community and environment.

blocks.section: French Business Awards
blocks.text: French Business Awards

blocks.section: French Business Awards
blocks.text: The French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan is pleased to present the 2027 edition of the French Business Awards, the awards ceremony that honors companies during our annual New Year’s networking event.

blocks.section: French Business Awards
blocks.text: For this 16th edition , the winners—carefully selected by the jury—will receive an award recognizing their excellence, uniqueness, and commitment in areas ranging from innovation to their dedication to sustainable development.

blocks.section: French Business Awards
blocks.text: An award will also be presented to the company that, during the 2025–2026 period, has distinguished itself through organizational excellence and remarkable results.

blocks.section: French Business Awards
blocks.text: Beyond the awards ceremony, the French Business Awards is above all a convivial and unifying event . Bringing together around 100 guests for a warm and engaging evening, it also offers a great opportunity to expand networks and foster connections within the business community.

blocks.section: French Business Awards
blocks.text: Applications will be closed December 15th 2026.

blocks.section: French Business Awards
blocks.text: The award ceremony will be held on January 28th 2027 in Tokyo.

blocks.section: About the awards :
blocks.text: About the awards :

blocks.section: About the awards :
blocks.text: Any company, whether French or Japanese, operating in Japan may submit an application for one of our awards, with a limit of one application per company. To highlight the diversity of our members and their various fields of activity, we encourage every company to apply in one of the categories.

blocks.section: About the awards :
blocks.text: ※ Depending on the awards, being a member a member of the Chamber, might be mandatory for candidacy.

blocks.text: Company of the Year Award - 2027

blocks.section: Company of the Year Award - 2027
blocks.text: The French Business Awards’ Company of the Year Award recognizes a company or SME that has stood out for its excellence, dynamism, and the quality of its achievements within the 2025–2026 fiscal year.

blocks.section: Company of the Year Award - 2027
blocks.text: This award recognizes an organization which, in every way, demonstrates outstanding performance, innovation, and success, and which fully embodies the values of an inspiring and ambitious company.

blocks.section: Credit Agricole CIB Japan Sustainability Award - 2027
blocks.text: This award recognizes a company or SME doing business with France and/or Japan that has committed to making a tangible contribution to a more sustainable future in Japan by 2025 and/or 2026.

blocks.section: Credit Agricole CIB Japan Sustainability Award - 2027

title: Galas
description: Every year since 1978, the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan is pleased to entertain its members, partners and clients in its exclusive gala evenings. Excellence at every stage: starred dinner, exclusive show and high-value tombola.

blocks.section: Galas
blocks.text: Galas

blocks.section: Galas
blocks.text: Every year since 1978, the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan has had the pleasure to entertain its members, partners and clients with its exclusive gala evenings.

blocks.section: Galas
blocks.text: Those prestigious events are a showcase of the best of France in Japan, gathering almost 800 people in Tokyo, 300 in Kansai, 250 in Fukuoka and 150 in Nagoya, who are Japanese CEOs, politicians, celebrities or journalists.

blocks.section: Galas
blocks.text: The evening revolves around three key moments: first, a French Michelin-starred chef serves a special menu designed for the occasion; then, guests are treated to an exclusive show highlighting a famous aspect of French culture (with prestigious performers such as Julien Clerc, Sylvie Vartan); and finally, a giant raffle gives participants a chance to win numerous prizes from the biggest French brands, including travels to France, luxury accessories and cosmetics.

title: L'Espace@CCIFJ
description: Looking for a unique place to host your next event? CCI France Japon is providing its members with a beautiful 120m² space that reconciles prestige, conviviality and practicality.

blocks.section: L'Espace@CCIFJ
blocks.text: L'Espace@CCIFJ

blocks.section: L'espace@CCIFJ
blocks.text: L'espace@CCIFJ

blocks.section: L'espace@CCIFJ
blocks.text: Looking for a unique place to host your next event? CCI France Japon is providing its members with a beautiful 120m² space that reconciles prestige, conviviality and practicality.

blocks.section: L'espace@CCIFJ
blocks.text: Located on the ground floor of the new premises of CCI France Japon, L’Espace@CCIFJ is designed to host all kind of events: conferences, trainings, industry events, networking, cocktails, product launches, concept store… L’Espace@CCIFJ is way more than a meeting room: it has direct access to the outside, full-height windows and a stylish design. Those unique elements add a ‘French touch’ that will give your events an exclusive twist.

blocks.section: L'espace@CCIFJ
blocks.text: Our event space is ideally situated at a short 2 min walk from the Hanzomon & Ginza lines, 5 min walk from Tokyo station and 10 min walk from the Imperial Palace. It is at the centre of Nihonbashi historical district, a unique mix of culture, commerce and history for more than 400 years in Tokyo. Recent developments have strengthened the position of Nihonbashi as a premium location for high-class business and shopping in Tokyo, a place your clients and collaborators will enjoy discovering, be they Japanese or from abroad.

blocks.section: Testimonies
blocks.text: Testimonies

blocks.section: Testimonies
blocks.text: “ I organized an exhibition in l ’Espace@CCIFJ in mid-January. It's a space with a very convenient access in the center of Nihonbashi and has a very warm atmosphere where we could exhibit many of our different leathers. Many members of the CCI France Japon attended this exhibition which was an opportunity to make them know about our brand and our products. It was a great opportunity, for which I am grateful. “

blocks.section: Testimonies
blocks.text: Toshihiro Tajiri, CEO Kyoto Leather

blocks.section: Testimonies
blocks.text: “ Last January, we organized a press conference and launching party for Perrier water at l’Espace@CCIFJ. For us, it was a natural choice as the location is super convenient, the equipments are perfect, and it offers street level access for the guests, which is unique. The team at the CCIFJ was incredibly supportive and professional. We would highly recommend using l ’ Espace for your next event! ”

blocks.section: Testimonies
blocks.text: Guillaume Calloud, Managing Director Nichifutsu Boeki K.K

blocks.section: Testimonies
blocks.text: “ Last December, Ataway Japan organized a Change Management Seminar inviting a guest speaker from Prosci Canada at l ’ Espace@CCIFJ. There are so many advantages using the place, such as their excellent service, comfortable and well-equipped facility, supportive staff and convenient location. We were very happy to find a place like l ’Espace@CCIFJ , which definitely contributed to the success of the event. … And special thanks to Karim for the wonderful service! ”

blocks.section: Testimonies
blocks.text: Quang Nguyen, Managing Director Ataway Japan K.K

blocks.section: Chizu Sasaki Director of Client Success & Happiness, Dale Carnegie
blocks.text: After graduating from university, Chizu joined a company specializing in educational travel, as a sales rep also provided local support as a tour conductor from consulting sales for study abroad and homestays. Through planning and proposing programs that touch different cultures, she found it rewarding to develop global citizens. She moved her playing field to Temple University's Japan Campus and expand her efforts to develop global citizens, including the recruiting activities such as operation of open campuses, not only for Japanese people but also for students from all over the world. She met Dale Carnegie Training during a training program for Temple University staff, became interested in Dale Carnegie training, and joined the company as a consultant in 2017. She provides learning, awareness, and excitement that she has felt to business professionals in various companies. After that, she obtained a trainer qualification from Dale Carnegie, while concurrently working as a consultant, she conducted training from the customer's point of view from the consultant's point of view. She has studied narration in the past and she is playing a role in Dale Carnegie's podcast. She also has sales manager experience at French company and is well versed in French corporate culture. In her private life, she has a high level of passion for food and drink, and she has acquired a British wine qualification. Born in Sendai City, Miyagi Prefecture.

blocks.text: Ema OKAMOTO Nishijin Okamoto Okamoto Orimono Co., Ltd Executive Managing Director

blocks.section: Ema OKAMOTO Nishijin Okamoto Okamoto Orimono Co., Ltd Executive Managing Director
blocks.text: Originally from the northern region of Sapporo, Ema Okamoto specialized in textile design before joining the century-old workshops of Okamoto Orimono, founded by her husband’s great-grandfather. She began her career as head of design before taking on leadership roles within the company, established in 1909 and specialized in the weaving of luxurious “kinran” silk textiles for temples and shrines across Japan.

blocks.section: Ema OKAMOTO Nishijin Okamoto Okamoto Orimono Co., Ltd Executive Managing Director
blocks.text: Despite the challenges posed by the decline of traditional weaving looms, rising raw material costs, and decreasing domestic demand, Okamoto Orimono continues to refine its techniques and pursue new collaborations in order to connect tradition with the future of weaving. Combining technical mastery and the exceptional quality of silk with the exploration of new patterns inspired by distant cultures and aesthetics, Ema Okamoto now works to bring this weaving art into the worlds of luxury architecture and interior design, both in Japan and internationally.

blocks.text: Currently serving as Director of LVMH Métiers d’Art Japan and Director of Corporate Affairs at LVMH Japan, Emina Morioka joined LVMH in 2011 within the Watches and Jewelry division in Japan, where she led the marketing and communications department for the luxury watch brand TAG Heuer before joining the Group’s headquarters in Paris within the Strategy department.

blocks.section: Emina MORIOKA Director of Public Affairs at LVMH Japan, Director of LVMH Métiers d’Art Japan
blocks.text: In 2022, she was appointed Director of LVMH Métiers d’Art Japan, an entity dedicated to the preservation and development of exceptional craftsmanship and savoir-faire. She is committed to promoting Japan’s outstanding artisanal traditions and manufactures, fostering dialogue between tradition and innovation, and supporting sustainable initiatives that strengthen artisanal ecosystems while ensuring the transmission of unique craftsmanship techniques.
