blocks.section: Hideo Goto President of Schick Japan K.K.
blocks.text: Hideo Goto is Senior Vice President of North Asia and President of Schick Japan K.K. Hideo joined Edgewell in 2022 and built new foundation for the future growth. Hideo successfully turned around Japan business in 2024 and transformed Schick Japan from a shaving to beauty grooming company. Hideo achieved the highest sales and employee engagement in Japan history. In 2025, Hideo expanded his responsibility to lead North Asia region.

blocks.section: Hideo Goto President of Schick Japan K.K.
blocks.text: With more than 20 years of experience in the beauty industry, Hideo has a strong track record of driving results. Hideo has diverse experience in all beauty categories—skincare, makeup, hair care, hair color, fragrances, and shaving—as well as channels—mass B2C, professional B2B2C, luxury, and e-commerce.

blocks.section: Hideo Goto President of Schick Japan K.K.
blocks.text: Prior to Edgewell, Hideo started his career at Johnson & Johnson in 1996, in sales and marketing. In 2005, Hideo joined L’Oréal, where he spent 11 years and turned around several businesses and scaled their growth. Hideo held various leadership positions throughout his tenure, including General Manager in Japan and Taiwan. In 2017, Hideo joined Henkel Beauty Care and turned around businesses while accelerating growth in Japan and South Korea as Country General Manager.

blocks.section: Hideo Goto President of Schick Japan K.K.
blocks.text: Hideo earned an MBA from Thunderbird School of Global Management in 2003 in the U.S., and a Bachelor of Business Administration from Meiji University in 1996.

blocks.section: Hideo Goto President of Schick Japan K.K.

blocks.text: Jérôme Guth is a French Maître d’Armes, specialized in Sabre. He is the current Head Coach of the Japanese fencing Olympic team. He started this position after the 2021 Tokyo Olympics. Since then, his team has broken all sorts of records.

blocks.section: Jérôme GUTH Head Coach of the Japanese fencing Olympic team
blocks.text: Jérôme has the particularity to be in charge of the Women’s & the Men’s programs, that makes him on of the youngest in the World (40) with this kind of responsibility.

blocks.section: Jérôme GUTH Head Coach of the Japanese fencing Olympic team
blocks.text: He is coaching the back-to-back (‘22 & ‘23) individual Women’s Sabre World Champion. She is currently ranked #1 in the world and was Japan’s flag bearer for the 2024 Paris Olympics.

blocks.section: Jérôme GUTH Head Coach of the Japanese fencing Olympic team
blocks.text: The Japanese Sabre team has clinched 45 International medals over the past 3,5 years, which is more than in its entire history. The team qualified for the first time to the Olympics and clinched a bronze medal in Paris 2024.

blocks.section: Jérôme GUTH Head Coach of the Japanese fencing Olympic team
blocks.text: Jérôme is from Strasbourg, France. Before living in Tokyo, he spent 11 years in the USA. He coached at Penn State University and opened a fencing academy in NJ.

blocks.section: Kyle MILLING Head coach of the Gunma Crane Thunde
blocks.text: Kyle Milling is currently the head coach of the Gunma Crane Thunders. A former professional basketball player (in France, Monaco, and Japan), he began his coaching career in France, where he led Hyères-Toulon to a Pro B championship and promotion to Pro A, and later coached the storied Limoges CSP, guiding the team to strong performances in the EuroCup. In 2020, Milling moved to Japan’s B.League, where he first achieved a record number of wins with the Yokohama B-Corsairs. He then took over the Hiroshima Dragonflies and, in just his third season, led the club to its first-ever league championship. For this achievement, he was named B.League Coach of the Year for the 2023–24 season. He holds dual American and French nationality.

title: Mayuko SANO Professor of Cultural Policy at Kyoto University

blocks.section: Mayuko SANO Professor of Cultural Policy at Kyoto University
blocks.text: Mayuko SANO Professor of Cultural Policy at Kyoto University

blocks.section: Mayuko SANO Professor of Cultural Policy at Kyoto University
blocks.text: Professor at the Graduate School of Education of Kyoto University, Mayuko Sano holds an MPhil from the University of Cambridge and a PhD from the University of Tokyo. She began her career at the Japan Foundation and UNESCO before serving as Associate Professor at the Shizuoka University of Art and Culture and at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies, prior to taking up her current position in 2018.

blocks.section: Mayuko SANO Professor of Cultural Policy at Kyoto University
blocks.text: She notably founded the Expo-logy Research Group (2010–), bringing together researchers and specialists from various fields, as well as the New Cultural Policy Project (2019–), both of which she continues to lead. Her major publications include Alcock’s Edo (2003), A Study of Japanese Diplomatic Ceremonies at the End of the Edo Period (2016), and Expo-logy (ed., 2020). She also serves as a board member of the Japan Association for the 2025 World Expo, a member of the evaluation committee for Expo 2025, and an advisor to the Kyoto Cultural Foundation.

She is the owner of the Washington Spirit, OL Lyonnes and London City Lionesses and, in 2024, launched Kynisca, the first global multi-team organization focused on professionalizing women’s football and demonstrating its commercial potential.

blocks.section: Michele Kang President of Olympique Lyonnais
blocks.text: In mid-2025, she expanded her leadership in European football by taking over as president of Olympique Lyonnais to lead its financial restructuring and development. Her broader investments in the ecosystem include IDA Sports and Just Women’s Sports, and philanthropic support for U.S. Soccer through which the Kang Women’s Institute accelerates advancements in the women’s game through science, innovation, and elevated best practices .

blocks.section: Kōtarō NISHIBORI CEO and Director of Hiyoshiya / TCI Laboratory
blocks.text: Originally from Wakayama Prefecture, Kōtarō Nishibori began his career in public service as an interpreter in Canada before joining Hiyoshiya, his wife’s family business, where he became CEO in 2004 and now leads Kyoto’s last remaining traditional Japanese umbrella manufacturer. Guided by the company philosophy that “tradition is a succession of innovations,” upheld over five generations, Kōtarō Nishibori does more than preserve the traditional function of Japanese umbrellas: he actively develops new products and applications by drawing on the unique techniques and structures of these handcrafted umbrellas.

blocks.section: Kōtarō NISHIBORI CEO and Director of Hiyoshiya / TCI Laboratory
blocks.text: Through numerous collaborations with Japanese and international designers, artists, and architects, he has helped promote this craftsmanship in more than 15 countries. Since launching the TCI Laboratory project in 2012, he has also supported the overseas development and market expansion of traditional crafts and SMEs, helping more than 800 companies and artisans grow internationally while continuing his commitment to the transmission of traditional knowledge and expertise.

blocks.text: Pierre VAUVY Director of the General Affairs Department at Okayama Kōgei

blocks.section: Pierre VAUVY Director of the General Affairs Department at Okayama Kōgei
blocks.text: It was first through his passion for Japanese culture and traditional craftsmanship that Pierre Vauvy settled in Japan more than 20 years ago. Through his work at Okayama-Kōgei, he specialized in the technique of Kyo-Yuzen, a hand-dyeing method for kimono fabrics developed in 17th-century Kyoto, where the workshop founded by Takako Okayama in 1968 is still based today.

blocks.section: Pierre VAUVY Director of the General Affairs Department at Okayama Kōgei
blocks.text: Recognized in 1994 by Japan’s Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry as the first woman certified as a traditional craftswoman in the field of Kyo-Yuzen, Takako Okayama developed the dreamlike creations for which Okayama-Kōgei is now renowned both in Japan and internationally, particularly in France. The atelier’s work is distinguished by its soft and subtle color palettes, exemplified by the kimono “YUME,” which today embodies both the brand and the transmission of this textile heritage.

blocks.text: Thomas BERTRAND CEO et fondateur de Ship&Co / Founder and CEO of Ship&co / 株式会社BERTRAND Ship&coの創業者&CEO

blocks.section: Thomas BERTRAND CEO et fondateur de Ship&Co / Founder and CEO of Ship&co / 株式会社BERTRAND Ship&coの創業者&CEO
blocks.text: Entrepreneur français établi à Kyoto depuis 2003, Thomas Bertrand est spécialiste de l’e-commerce et de la logistique. Il est notamment le fondateur de Bento&co, une entreprise qui exporte des articles de cuisine typiquement japonais vers plus de 100 pays, en ciblant à la fois les clients B2B et B2C en ligne et depuis 2012 dans un magasin physique à Kyoto.

blocks.section: Thomas BERTRAND CEO et fondateur de Ship&Co / Founder and CEO of Ship&co / 株式会社BERTRAND Ship&coの創業者&CEO
blocks.text: En parallèle, il fonde Ship&co, la première solution en ligne au Japon qui sert de lien entre les transporteurs et les plateformes e-commerce, en étant connectée aux trois principaux transporteurs du pays : Yamato, Sagawa et JapanPost. De nombreuses autres collaborations avec les transporteurs internationaux tels que FedEx, UPS ou DHL permettent la numérisation du processus d’étiquetage et d’accélérer les envois.

blocks.section: Thomas BERTRAND CEO et fondateur de Ship&Co / Founder and CEO of Ship&co / 株式会社BERTRAND Ship&coの創業者&CEO
blocks.text: A French entrepreneur based in Kyoto since 2003, Thomas Bertrand specializes in e-commerce and logistics. He is notably the founder of Bento&co, a company exporting typically Japanese kitchenware and lifestyle products to more than 100 countries, serving both B2B and B2C customers online as well as through a physical store in Kyoto since 2012.

blocks.section: Thomas BERTRAND CEO et fondateur de Ship&Co / Founder and CEO of Ship&co / 株式会社BERTRAND Ship&coの創業者&CEO
blocks.text: At the same time, he founded Ship&co, the first online solution in Japan designed to connect shipping carriers with e-commerce platforms. The service is integrated with the country’s three main carriers : Yamato, Sagawa, and Japan Post. Additional partnerships with international carriers such as FedEx, UPS, and DHL have further enabled the digitalization of shipping label processes and accelerated international deliveries.

blocks.section: Thomas BERTRAND CEO et fondateur de Ship&Co / Founder and CEO of Ship&co / 株式会社BERTRAND Ship&coの創業者&CEO
blocks.text: 2003年より京都を拠点に活動するフランス人起業家、トマ・ベルトラン氏は、Eコマースおよび物流分野の専門家です。日本ならではのキッチン用品やライフスタイル雑貨を100か国以上へ輸出する「Bento&co」の創業者として知られ、オンラインを通じたBtoB・BtoC向け販売に加え、2012年からは京都に実店舗も展開しています。

blocks.section: Thomas BERTRAND CEO et fondateur de Ship&Co / Founder and CEO of Ship&co / 株式会社BERTRAND Ship&coの創業者&CEO
blocks.text: また、同氏は、日本初となる配送業者とECプラットフォームを連携するオンラインサービス「Ship&co」を創設しました。このサービスは、日本国内の主要配送会社であるヤマト運輸、佐川急便、日本郵便の3社と連携しています。さらに、FedEx、UPS、DHLなど海外配送業者との提携を通じて、配送ラベル作成のデジタル化や国際発送の効率化にも貢献しています。

blocks.section: Toma YAMAZOE Political figure and former mayor of Yosano
blocks.text: After studying architecture at the École Nationale Supérieure d’Architecture de Paris-Malaquais, Toma Yamazoe pursued further studies in metaphysics under Professor Frédéric Nef at the École des Hautes Études en Sciences Sociales (EHESS). During his time in France, he also worked as an interpreter for exhibitions in Paris and Brussels dedicated to the silk craftsmanship of the Tango region, particularly chirimen textiles.

blocks.section: Toma YAMAZOE Political figure and former mayor of Yosano
blocks.text: Upon returning to Japan in 2009, he joined the Ozaki Yukio Memorial Foundation, dedicated to the promotion of democracy, and participated in its Gadō-juku program before being elected with the highest number of votes to the Yosano Town Council in 2010. In 2014, at the age of 32, he was appointed Mayor of Yosano, becoming the youngest mayor in Japan; a position he held for 12 years across three consecutive terms. He also served as the second president of the National Association of Young Mayors of Towns and Villages in Japan.

blocks.section: BONJOUR FRANCE
blocks.text: BONJOUR FRANCE is an initiative created by the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan ( CCI France Japon ) in 2015. Its goal is to promote France through a series of events aimed at the general public, sponsored by the French Embassy.

blocks.section: BONJOUR FRANCE
blocks.text: BONJOUR FRANCE 's mission is to showcase French brands and products in Japan by organizing exceptional events centered around gastronomy and the art of living (Art de vivre).

blocks.section: BONJOUR FRANCE
blocks.text: OUR OBJECTIVE • To present French brands to the Japanese public in a modern, accessible, diverse, and chic way. • To provide a platform for our partners to communicate their “Frenchness.”

blocks.section: BONJOUR FRANCE
blocks.text: OUR ROLE • To bring together French companies around the BONJOUR FRANCE concept by offering them useful promotional tools.

blocks.section: BONJOUR FRANCE
blocks.text: • To organize and coordinate French promotional events in Japan under the " BONJOUR FRANCE " label in cooperation with our partners.

blocks.section: BONJOUR FRANCE
blocks.text: • To develop a BONJOUR FRANCE communication strategy that will benefit partner brands.

blocks.section: BONJOUR FRANCE
blocks.text: • To offer partner companies opportunities to communicate their "Frenchness" from different angles.

blocks.section: BONJOUR FRANCE
blocks.text: • To present products and expertise to a wider audience in Japan by organizing trade events.

blocks.section: BONJOUR FRANCE
blocks.text: OUR TARGET • Lovers of France , strongly interested in French culture and lifestyle, with a high level of cultural exploration and purchasing power.

title: 2022 French Japanese Business Summit
description: The French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCI France Japon) organizes, together with the French Embassy in Japan, for the fifth consecutive year, a major summit dedicated to the French-Japanese business community.

blocks.text: Japan as a model for the future “What learnings can be relevant for the world? “

The French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCI France Japon) organizes, together with the French Embassy in Japan , for the fifth consecutive year, a major summit dedicated to the French-Japanese business community.
The French-Japanese Business Summit will be held on November 29th 2022, from 10:30 to 19:30 (door open at 10:00), at the Nikkei Hall in Tokyo on the following theme :
Japan as a model for the future “What learnings can be relevant for the world ?“

After the most intense crisis the world has faced since 2008, it is time for institutions and countries to adapt and reform again in light of the underlying issues the world is facing that the covid crisis has highlighted. As Japan strives toward a new form of capitalism that is more conscious of these new issues, there is much to learn from the its industrial model’s strengths and from how it is trying to overcome its shortcomings. By focusing on how Japan can concentrate on its core values as a nation of innovation and technology but also a nation of creativity and culture, we can start to grasp what the rest of the world can learn from this model to move towards a more sustainable future that respects both the planet and its workers.

To attempt address these issues, the 2022 French-Japanese Business Summit will gather top-level international speakers from diverse backgrounds – from institutions, citizens and businesses to social sciences, art and architecture – to share their visions, their strategies, and the opportunities they foresee.
For more information, please visit the special site below!

title: 2026 Japan Salary Survey Results: What’s Really Driving Hiring, Retention, and Change?
description: Gain 2026 hiring insights with Dr. David Sweet: salary trends, motivators, AI impact, and tips for thriving in Japan’s evolving talent market.

blocks.text: Gain 2026 hiring insights with Dr. David Sweet: salary trends, motivators, AI impact, and tips for thriving in Japan’s evolving talent market.
HR BREAKFAST 2026 JAPAN SALARY SURVEY RESULTS: WHAT'S REALLY DRIVING HIRING, RETENTION AND CHANGE?
Date : October 8, 2025 (Wed) | Time : 9 AM - 11 AM
EVENT OVERVIEW

In this session, Dr. David Sweet, Managing Director of FocusCore Japan, will present highlights from the 2026 Salary Survey offering essential insights for leaders navigating Japan’s uniquely complex and shifting talent market.

Over the past year, Japan’s labor landscape has continued to evolve rapidly. While foreign firms face pressure from global market shifts, many are doubling down in Japan, capitalizing on the weak yen and stable workforce. But salary expectations, working styles, and employee values have changed—and companies must adapt.
This talk will cover:
Current compensation trends
Salary and bonus shifts
Team growth and restructuring trends
Top motivators
What professionals value most (spoiler: it’s not money)
How AI is expected to reshape different functions
Upskilling & career investment trends
Q&A
This session will be interactive and conclude with a few recommendations for companies navigating Japan’s complex hiring landscape in 2026.
GUEST-SPEAKER
Dr. David Sweet – Expert in Recruitment, Leadership, and Strategy

For the past 30 years, Dr. Sweet has specialized in HR and executive development, recruiting, and leadership development for top-tier companies across Asia. He is the Founder and CEO of FocusCore Group, a leading executive search consultancy, where he helps businesses identify and secure top talent.

He is also the author of six books、 including Sweet Sales , Sweet Success , and Recruit! Becoming the Top-Biller , and has been featured in Facebook & LinkedIn 対応履歴書いらずのソーシャルメディア転職術 for his expertise in social networking for recruitment.

Beyond recruitment, he holds a Ph.D. in Leadership Development and an M.A. in Communications from Regis University in Denver, Colorado. As a certified ICF executive coach, he empowers leaders worldwide to enhance their hiring practices and leadership strategies.
When he’s not consulting or coaching, he pursues his passions for music and marathon running, bringing the same dedication and energy to the stage and the track as he does to the boardroom.

title: A rendez-vous with Jean RENO : Presented by BONJOUR FRANCE
description: Want to meet a cinema icon? BONJOUR FRANCE invites you to a special encounter with Jean RENO!

blocks.text: Want to meet a cinema icon? BONJOUR FRANCE invites you to a special encounter with Jean RENO!
BONJOUR FRANCE is pleased to announce that L'Espace@CCIFJ will open its doors on Monday, April 20 at 6:00 PM for a Talk-Show event in the presence of the iconic film star Jean RENO !

Jean RENO, a major figure in French and international cinema, will offer you an exclusive Talk-Show centered around the theme of the play he is performing solo in Japan, entitled “Rakuda.” This exchange will be hosted by presenter, journalist, and sports commentator Florent DABADIE. At the end of this private Talk-Show, you will have the pleasure of enjoying a cocktail .

As the Talk-Show and the play are part of a joint program, your participation in the Talk-Show also includes the distribution of tickets to attend the play “Rakuda,” on May 13, 15, 20, or 22 from 7:00 PM.

This event is a unique opportunity to learn more about the renowned actor and his recent activities. If you are interested in his work and in the world of cinema, don’t miss this exclusive event, limited to only 100 guests !
BONJOUR FRANCE's Press Release Press Accreditation Application Form

blocks.section: Special guest

blocks.section: Special guest
blocks.text: Jean RENO

blocks.section: Special guest
blocks.text: Jean Reno, a celebrated French actor renowned for his commanding presence and remarkable range, was born in Casablanca to Spanish parents and raised in France. He began his career as a theater actor before attaining international fame through his long-standing collaboration with director Luc Besson. Notable films from this partnership include Léon: The Professional, Nikita, and The Big Blue. Reno has successfully bridged French cinema and Hollywood, appearing in a diverse range of films, including action, drama and comedy, movies like Wasabi, Mission Impossible, Ronin, Godzilla, The Pink Panther, … His deep voice, strong physicality, and ability to convey quiet emotion have established him as one of international’s most recognizable and respected screen actors. Recently, he authored a novel titled “Emma", which has been translated into 16 languages, including most recently, Japanese. Throughout his travels, Reno has always prioritized giving back to his communities and actively works with various non-profit organizations. One such organization in Japan is called “Nobel Kids’ Goodwill Ambassador” and “United World Schools”.

blocks.section: « Rakuda », interpreted by Jean RENO
blocks.text: « Rakuda », interpreted by Jean RENO

blocks.section: « Rakuda », interpreted by Jean RENO
blocks.text: The renowned actor Jean Reno, who captivated audiences worldwide with the film Léon . Behind this success lies a previously untold truth—now brought to the stage as a work of theatrical art. A world premiere.

blocks.section: « Rakuda », interpreted by Jean RENO
blocks.text: Written by: Jean RENO Directed by: Ladislas CHOLLAT Piano: Pablo LANTY Starring: Jean RENO

blocks.section: « Rakuda », interpreted by Jean RENO
blocks.text: Message from Jean Reno “ Traveling is a dance of souls and a quest for the self. Since my youth, I’ve wandered the world’s tapestry. Born to Spanish roots, nurtured by French embrace, I wed an English muse and now call the USA my home. I dream of crafting a stage show, a “voyage” weaving the tale of my life’s journey. The stage will be a canvas of stories, songs and images, guiding the audience through a shared odyssey. Life, in its singular beauty, holds steps both unique and universal, where both sorrows and joys are common to all people.”

title: AEON France Fair - BONJOUR FRANCE 2025
description: Discover the collaboration between BONJOUR FRANCE and AEON from April 29th to May 4th at AEON stores across Japan and at AEON Lake Town!

blocks.text: Discover the collaboration between BONJOUR FRANCE and AEON from April 29th to May 4th at AEON stores across Japan and at AEON Lake Town!
Would you like to discover the "French Art de vivre" ? Travel through your five senses? We present you AEON FRANCE FAIR - BONJOUR FRANCE 2025 !

This large-scale event will take place from Tuesday, April 29th to Sunday, May 4th in AEON stores, convenience stores, and supermarkets nationwide. And all of this will be in parallele with the Osaka World Expo, during which France will have its own pavilion! Numerous activities are also planned at AEON Lake Town in Koshigaya, Saitama such as: opening ceremony, talk shows, and a BONJOUR FRANCE market with exhibitors specially brought in from France for the occasion!

This will be the perfect opportunity to discover or rediscover French craftsmanship and the Art de vivre through high-quality products. AEON Lake Town in Koshigaya, Saitama, the largest shopping center in Japan, will offer, in addition to the opening ceremony, a variety of activities: talk shows, a BONJOUR FRANCE market, and other surprises…
Press release Inviation to the press

"On the occasion of 'BONJOUR FRANCE,' the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan and its partners invite you to discover or rediscover the French Art of Living, the excellence, the richness, and the variety of French products and know-how. Through gourmet encounters and discoveries, the key moments of this campaign throughout 2025 will be opportunities to further strengthen the long-standing friendship that unites our two countries." - S.E.M. Philippe SETTON, Ambassador of France in Japan.

blocks.section: Chefs
blocks.text: Blanche Loiseau, chef at Loiseau de France, is the daughter of renown chef Bernard Loiseau. She studied at the Paul Bocuse Institute before working in gastronomical establishments in France and abroad. In 2019, she went to Japan to study kaiseki cuisine for a year in Aoyagi restaurant, Tokyo, before going back to France in 2021 to work at the Relais Bernard Loiseau In 2023, she opened the Loiseau du Temps restaurant in Besançon, France with the Bernard Loiseau group, before opening Loiseau de France in Tokyo in June 2024.

blocks.section: Chefs
blocks.text: Born in Paris, he began studying the culinary arts at an early age. After working in a number of luxury hotels and restaurants, he decided to take on the challenge of pursuing his career... In Japan! In Tokyo, he created the Parisian bistro concept and opened three Parisian bistros all called “LE PETIT TONNEAU”. In 2022, he became president of the “Culinary Academy of France Japan delegation” (ACPFJ), and in 2024 he was named Officier of l'Ordre de Mérite Agricole (French government Ministry of Agriculture).

blocks.section: Chefs
blocks.text: Dominique CORBY

blocks.section: Chefs
blocks.text: Born in Paris in 1965, he developed a strong interest in the culinary arts from a young age. Following this passion, he began his culinary career at the age of 15. In 1994, he continued his career in Japan, and even became the director of Le Cordon Bleu Japan. He also opened several restaurants in the Tokyo area in order to share important values, such as introducing French-Japanese cuisine to the rest of the world. But his achievements do not stop there. Among the many titles he holds, he was named Chevalier of the Order of Agricultural Merit in France in 2007, became a member of the Japanese branch of the French Culinary Academy’s secretariat in 2010, and was appointed ambassador for a champagne house in 2018. He is also committed to helping the less fortunate through the creation of the association “Lumière et Espoir pour le Japon.”

blocks.section: Chefs
blocks.text: Born in Tokyo to a Japanese mother and a French father, himself the son of one of the pioneers of French gastronomy in Japan, André Pachon, Patric Pachon belongs to a family lineage deeply rooted in the culinary sphere for over 56 years.

blocks.section: Chefs
blocks.text: After completing his studies at the Lycée Français International de Tokyo, he pursued hospitality training in Carcassonne. He further enriched his experience by working in prestigious establishments in France, as at the restaurant Le Tastevin in Maisons-Laffitte, before gaining unique experience at the Palais de l’Élysée and refining his expertise at the Hôtel de Crillon in Paris.

blocks.section: Chefs
blocks.text: Upon returning to Tokyo, he joined his father alongside his brother Thierry to take over and develop the family establishments, Restaurant Pachon, Le Petit Bedon, and Comptoir Occitan. Deeply attached to his Occitan roots, he is committed to promoting the region through his cuisine and a carefully curated selection of wines.

blocks.section: Chefs
blocks.text: In 2024, he was crowned World Champion of Cassoulet de Toulouse in Tokyo, becoming a true ambassador of this iconic specialty and its terroir.

blocks.section: Chefs
blocks.text: Highly active beyond his establishments, he regularly serves on prestigious juries such as the Coupe Georges Baptiste and the Japan Cheese Contest. He also frequently appears in Japanese media and television programs.

blocks.section: Chefs
blocks.text: He is a member of the Académie Culinaire de France and the Académie Universelle du Cassoulet.

blocks.section: Chefs
blocks.text: Fanny Fernandes

blocks.section: Chefs
blocks.text: Fanny Fernandes is a French chef from the south of France. She grew up in an environment deeply rooted in culinary traditions and family values, influenced by both of her parents, particularly her mother, who is from Occitanie and worked in the restaurant industry. Within her family, food always played a central role, with long meals shared together, conversations around recipes, and a strong culture of gathering around the table. She moved to Japan in 2010 and immediately dedicated herself to cooking, with the aim of sharing a cuisine that is warm, family-oriented, sincere, and accessible. In 2021, she opened Cocotte Cuisine in Jiyugaoka, Tokyo — a bistro and delicatessen inspired by her roots — where she offers authentic and approachable dishes from the south of France and the Mediterranean.

title: AI in the Corporate World: Practical Insights and Legal Boundaries
description: Explore how AI is reshaping business, from generative trends to real cases, and learn how leaders can innovate responsibly and manage emerging risks.

blocks.text: Explore how AI is reshaping business, from generative trends to real cases, and learn how leaders can innovate responsibly and manage emerging risks.
HR BREAKFAST AI IN THE CORPORATE WORLD: PRACTICAL INSIGHTS & LEGAL BOUNDARIES
Date : November 25, 2025 (Tue) | Time : 9:00AM - 11:00AM

Join us for an insightful session exploring how Artificial Intelligence is transforming the corporate landscape. From key generative AI trends to real-world applications across industries, our speakers will share practical perspectives on how organizations and leaders can navigate this ongoing transformation effectively
The discussion will also address how companies can govern the use of AI responsibly, balancing innovation with compliance while managing legal and ethical risks.
GUEST-SPEAKERS

Sylvain PIERRE (Moderator) Founder & CEO, Le Wagon Tokyo Sylvain Pierre left France for Vietnam in 2006 to co-found Officience, a French business process outsourcing company, with two other associates. After growing the company to 300 people, he decided to change its management model in 2014 to embrace a flatter, more open structure. He gave a TED talk about this in 2015 in Paris. In 2016, he moved to Japan to launch the Tokyo franchise Le Wagon, a coding bootcamp for entrepreneurs and creative people. In seven years, they grew the local community to over 8,000 members, expanded to Kyoto (October 2018), launched a new Data Science program, and have trained 800 aspiring developers and entrepreneurs. Sylvain is a business books and TED talks enthusiast and a fan of Seth Godin, Clay Shirky, and Frédéric Laloux. Curious about the latest business and social trends, he regularly shares his opinions on innovation, globalization and organizational transformation on his blog and on X (formerly Twitter).

Julien GUILLE (Speaker) Head of Digital Acceleration at Nissan Julien leads AI-driven software acceleration at Nissan, helping the company transform how it delivers digital products. Building on years of experience driving digital transformation and leading digital promotion initiatives, he also contributes to Nissan’s broader AI strategy and operating model.

Clarisse KNAËBEL (Speaker) Privacy and AI Governance Consultant Clarisse is an EU-qualified lawyer specializing in data protection, with international experience across Europe, Asia, and the United States. Her previous experience includes serving as DPO at Contentsquare and as Legal Counsel at the French Data Protection Authority (CNIL). She now operates independently in Japan, advising global French and Japanese organizations on data protection and AI compliance.

title: Breakfast Talk: Inside Korea’s strategy: economy, innovation and soft power
description: The CCI France Japon is pleased to announce the upcoming special event to be held on Wednesday, 18 of November.

blocks.text: The CCI France Japon is pleased to announce the upcoming special event to be held on Wednesday, 18 of November.
How did South Korea transform itself into a global economic and cultural powerhouse?
Over the past decades, South Korea has undergone a remarkable economic transformation , emerging as a major global player and expanding its influence far beyond its borders.

This conference will explore the key drivers behind South Korea’s rise, from the foundations of its economic development and its strategic investments in technology to the growing role of culture and soft power in shaping the country’s international influence.
The discussion will also look ahead, examining the opportunities and challenges that will shape South Korea’s future in an competitive and interconnected global environment.
Join us on November 18th for an insightful discussion on the forces behind South Korea’s transformation and its evolving position on the global stage.

blocks.text: BUILDING TRUST TO AVOID CONFLICT OR BURNOUT

blocks.section: BUILDING TRUST TO AVOID CONFLICT OR BURNOUT
blocks.text: DATE: October 29, 2026 (Thu) | Time: 9AM - 12PM

blocks.section: BUILDING TRUST TO AVOID CONFLICT OR BURNOUT
blocks.text: Many workplace conflicts and cases of burnout are not caused by a lack of skill or motivation, but by a lack of trust. In this course, managers learn how to build trust through everyday interactions and address issues before they escalate.

blocks.section: BUILDING TRUST TO AVOID CONFLICT OR BURNOUT
blocks.text: The program is grounded in the timeless principles found in How to Win Friends and Influence People and How to Stop Worrying and Start Living. These Dale Carnegie principles, practiced worldwide for over 100 years, provide proven guidance for building relationships and managing emotions in today’s workplace.

blocks.section: BUILDING TRUST TO AVOID CONFLICT OR BURNOUT
blocks.text: By strengthening trust as the foundation of leadership, managers can prevent unnecessary conflict, protect their team’s energy, and create an environment that supports sustainable performance.

blocks.section: TRAINER
blocks.text: Chizu SASAKI, Dale Carnegie

blocks.section: TRAINER
blocks.text: After graduating from university, Chizu began her career at a travel agency, where she was involved in planning and proposing educational programs aimed at developing global talent. Through consulting sales work with clients from diverse cultural backgrounds, she developed a strong appreciation for the importance of cultivating internationally minded professionals.

blocks.section: TRAINER
blocks.text: She later joined a U.S. higher education institution, where she was responsible for public relations and educational outreach to promote global learning among students from around the world. During this time, she encountered Dale Carnegie Training through an internal staff development program and deeply resonated with its values and practical approach.

blocks.section: TRAINER
blocks.text: Since joining Dale Carnegie in 2017, Chizu has been designing and delivering customized corporate training programs tailored to clients’ specific needs. Her work focuses on supporting the growth of business professionals and driving organizational development.

blocks.section: TRAINER
blocks.text: In 2024, she was honored with the Wow Trainer award, a prestigious global recognition from Dale Carnegie & Associates. She also hosts the podcast Business Mastery, which ranked No.1 in the management category and continues to receive strong acclaim.

title: Economic Intelligence: A Strategic Tool to protect, anticipate and decide, in an Era of Geopolitical and Trade Instability

blocks.text: In an increasingly complex business environment, Economic Intelligence (EI) has become a strategic asset for organisations looking to anticipate change, identify emerging risks and seize new opportunities in order to stay competitive.
Artificial intelligence is reshaping the way information is gathered, analysed and leveraged, opening up new possibilities while raising important questions and challenges.

During this exclusive seminar, Jacques Beltran, Deputy CEO of ADIT, a leading European firm in strategic intelligence and international support, will explore the evolving relationship between economic intelligence and AI.

He will share insights into how these tools can help organisations anticipate risks, uncover opportunities and make more informed strategic decisions amid a rapidly changing geopolitical and business landscape.
Join us for an insightful discussion and an opportunity to exchange with fellow business professionals on the importance of economic intelligence in a rapidly changing world!

blocks.section: Vous préparez votre départ pour le Japon ou venez d’y arriver ?
blocks.text: Deux heures ne suffisent évidemment pas pour connaître toute la culture japonaise. Elles peuvent en revanche changer le regard avec lequel on aborde ses premières semaines au Japon.

blocks.section: Vous préparez votre départ pour le Japon ou venez d’y arriver ?
blocks.text: Cette formation en ligne propose les repères interculturels essentiels pour mieux comprendre ce que l’on observe, éviter certaines interprétations trop rapides et adopter, dès le départ, les bons réflexes dans son environnement professionnel japonais.

blocks.section: Vous préparez votre départ pour le Japon ou venez d’y arriver ?
blocks.text: Conçue comme une première boussole interculturelle , elle permet de mettre du sens derrière des comportements qui peuvent surprendre : importance du groupe, communication implicite, silence, consensus, rapport au temps, à la hiérarchie ou encore aux règles et aux processus.

blocks.section: Vous préparez votre départ pour le Japon ou venez d’y arriver ?
blocks.text: L’objectif n’est pas d’apprendre « comment sont les Japonais », mais de changer de grille de lecture pour aborder le Japon avec davantage de justesse, de curiosité et de confiance.

blocks.text: ou qui commencent à travailler régulièrement avec des collègues ou partenaires japonais et souhaitent acquérir rapidement quelques clés de compréhension.

blocks.section: À qui s’adresse cette formation ?
blocks.text: La formation est accessible aussi bien depuis la France que depuis le Japon , avec des horaires pensés pour permettre la participation depuis les deux pays.

description: Save the date: CEO Lunch with Michele Kang, President of Olympique Lyonnais

blocks.text: Save the date: CEO Lunch with Michele Kang, President of Olympique Lyonnais
The French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan is delighted to announce an upcoming CEO Networking Lunch with Michele Kang , President of Olympique Lyonnais , on October 23rd .
As pioneering businesswoman, investor and philanthropist, Michele Kang is dedicated to advancing women’s sports worldwide .

She is the owner of the Washington Spirit, OL Lyonnes and London City Lionesses , and in 2024, she founded Kynisca, the first global multi-team organization dedicated to professionalizing women’s football and demonstrating its commercial potential.

In mid-2025, she took over as President of Olympique Lyonnais , where she is leading the club’s financial restructuring and development. Her investments and philanthropic initiatives also extend across the women’s sports ecosystem, including IDA Sports and Just Women’s Sports.
Join us for this exceptional opportunity to meet and exchange with Mrs. Kang and hear from one of the leading figures shaping the future of women’s sports and football .

title: Conversation with Hideo Goto, President of Schick Japan (Edgewell Personal Care)
description: What does it really take to turn a business around — and make the results last? Join us for a candid conversation with Hideo Goto.

blocks.text: What does it really take to turn a business around — and make the results last? Join us for a candid conversation with Hideo Goto.

What does it actually take to turn a business around — not once, but five times? How do you rebuild a company’s culture while restructuring it at the same time? And what changes when the turnaround succeeds — how do you sustain results instead of just achieving them?

If you’d like answers to these questions and more, join us for an in-depth conversation with Hideo Goto , President of Schick Japan and business book author. Hideo has led five corporate turnarounds across his career — at L’Oréal, Henkel, and now Schick Japan — turning sales from decline to double-digit growth and lifting employee engagement to the point of earning the company’s first-ever Great Place to Work certification. He recently distilled this into a five-step transformation recipe, the subject of his new book, available in Japanese and English.

Steven Bleistein, Relansa CEO and Entrepreneur Committee President, will open the discussion and ensure ample time for audience questions. No slides. No speeches. No presentations. Just a candid, provocative conversation.

title: Decoding the Gaishikei Finance Function
description: Survey findings on AI adoption, succession planning, business partnering, and operational pain points - with a panel of Tokyo finance leaders

blocks.text: Survey findings on AI adoption, succession planning, business partnering, and operational pain points - with a panel of Tokyo finance leaders
Meaningful benchmarking of the finance function in foreign companies in Japan has long been a challenge, with most available research focused solely on the Nikkei market.

To help bridge this information gap, FocusCore Group conducted a dedicated survey and built a valuable dataset specifically designed to reflect the unique operational realities of finance teams in foreign companies operating in Japan.
Join us for an exclusive presentation of the survey findings, followed by a panel discussion and Q&A featuring finance leaders based in Tokyo.
Key topics include:
Future-proofing the finance function
AI in Finance
Succession planning and talent management
Finance business partnering
Current operational pain points in the finance function
Retirement policies
Average tenure
This session will provide practical insights, benchmarking data, and an opportunity to discuss the evolving role of finance leadership in Japan.

title: DIGITAL SOLUTIONS FOR SUSTAINABILITY AND RESILIENCE WEBINAR
description: Business Leaders Forum 2021

blocks.text: Business Leaders Forum 2021

The French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCI France-Japon) is organizing a Webinar on “Digital solutions for sustainability and resilience” on Thursday, July 8th 2021 , from 17:00 to 18:30 (JST).

The Covid-19 crisis has accelerated digital transformation in all industries . Some businesses have experienced a major growth during the pandemic (food delivery service, online retail, virtual healthcare, video communications…) while others have decided to adapt or change their business models in order to meet the new growing demand. Digital tools and solutions have played a crucial role in overcoming the crisis and in moving towards a more sustainable and resilient future . This event will help start build visions for 2050 , which is the main topic of the French-Japanese Business Summit that will take place on November 9th .
In this webinar, concrete and practical examples of digital transformations and solutions developed by companies in different sectors will be presented:
Overview of digitalization trends in Japan
The role of digital technology to help businesses in their sustainability strategies
The role of digital twins for Smart Cities operation and management
Importance of digitalization for decarbonization and resiliency of Japan’s electricity
Join this event, designed to help business leaders and policy makers lead change and navigate future developments, to get forward-thinking and integrated perspective.

blocks.section: Program
blocks.text: The main building of Meiji Kinenkan, designated a Tangible Cultural Property by the Tokyo Metropolitan Government, is an exceptional testament to the palace architecture of the Meiji era. The only surviving remains of its kind to have been preserved to this day, it possesses considerable historical value and symbolizes Japan’s journey toward modernity.

blocks.section: Program
blocks.text: Its history dates back to October 1881 (Meiji 14), when the Gokaishokujō, or “Banquet Hall,” was completed on the site of the present-day Akasaka Palace, which at the time served as a temporary imperial residence.

blocks.section: Program
blocks.text: This hall hosted diplomatic receptions at which Emperor Meiji and Empress Shōken received members of foreign royal families as well as dignitaries from around the world. It also served as the imperial dining hall and was used on numerous occasions for banquets and official meals.

blocks.section: Program
blocks.text: In 1888 (Meiji 21), the building was also the setting for a decisive event in Japan’s constitutional history: in the presence of Emperor Meiji, the Privy Council held sessions there devoted to examining the draft Constitution of the Empire of Japan. This place is therefore closely linked to the birth of Japan as a modern constitutional state.

blocks.section: Program
blocks.text: The building also bears witness to Empress Shōken’s determination to promote the modernization of the country and the adoption of Western clothing. In August 1886 (Meiji 19), the Empress herself wore a Western-style dress and received foreign guests at this location for the first time in such attire.

blocks.section: Program
blocks.text: Through this initiative, she notably wished to encourage the development of domestic industries through the Westernization of clothing. Her resolve, summed up in these words: “If it can serve the country, I will do anything,” inspired women of the upper classes and contributed to the spread of Western fashion in Japan.

blocks.section: Program
blocks.text: This change in clothing also had consequences for the interior design of the hall. In order to meet the requirements of diplomatic receptions and facilitate the wearing of Western-style dresses, the floor, initially covered with carpets, was subsequently renovated and fitted with geometrically patterned parquet flooring, made using the Japanese yosegi-bari technique.

blocks.section: Program
blocks.text: Subsequently, the building was bestowed upon Itō Hirobumi, a major figure in the drafting of the Constitution. In 1918 (Taishō 7), it was relocated to its present location in a section of the outer gardens of Meiji Jingu Shrine and was given the name Kempō Kinenkan, or “Constitution Memorial Hall.”

blocks.section: Program
blocks.text: After hosting numerous events of national and social importance, it opened its doors on November 1, 1947 (Shōwa 22), under the name Meiji Kinenkan, as a reception venue for Meiji Jingu. In 2020 (Reiwa 2), its main building was officially designated a Tangible Cultural Property by the Tokyo Metropolitan Government.

blocks.section: Program
blocks.text: Emperor Meiji laid the foundations of modern Japan, while Empress Shōken devoted her efforts to the development of culture, women’s education, and charitable activities. Her humanitarian commitment is notably embodied in the Empress Shōken Fund, established in support of the activities of the Red Cross and considered the oldest international humanitarian fund of its kind in the world.

blocks.section: Program
blocks.text: Even today, the main building of Meiji Kinenkan perpetuates the memory of Emperor Meiji and Empress Shōken. It continues to convey to present generations the spirit of their era, their commitment to serving the country, and the momentum that accompanied the birth of modern Japan.

blocks.section: Partners presentation
blocks.text: Partners presentation

blocks.section: Partners presentation
blocks.text: ★ Chef Philippe MILLE Main Awards: Bronze Medal at the Bocuse d'Or (2009), MOF (2011)

blocks.section: Partners presentation
blocks.text: Originally from Brittany, this talented chef was awarded the prestigious title of Meilleur Ouvrier de France (MOF) in 2011, at the early age of 38 years old. He honed his skills in renowned Parisian establishments such as "Le Cantine des Troisgros" and "Le Bristol". In 2009, he became executive chef at the prestigious hotel "Domaine Les Crayères" in the Champagne region, where he earned a Michelin star, followed by a second in 2012. In 2024, he opened his own restaurant, "ARBANE", in the city of Reims. Combining a deep respect for French culinary tradition with an elegant focus on showcasing ingredients, he quickly established himself as a leading figure in the culinary sphere. He also serves as a brand ambassador for the Champagne house Lanson, passionately exploring food and champagne pairings.

blocks.section: Partners presentation
blocks.text: ★ Lanson – Concept Rooted in tradition, yet driven by innovation.

blocks.section: Partners presentation
blocks.text: Lanson’s distinctive style is defined by an unmatched freshness, where vibrant acidity and pure fruit expression come together in perfect harmony. The secret behind this freshness? A deliberate choice to break from convention: the House forgoes malolactic fermentation, a common practice in Champagne, in order to preserve the lively acidity and pure character of the fruit. This elegance and precision of flavor enhance gastronomic pairings. It is the combination of unwavering dedication to quality and the exceptional craftsmanship of its artisans that defines the Lanson signature. Carefully selected grapes, generous use of reserve wines, extended aging, and this unique non-malolactic philosophy form the foundation of a timeless Champagne, continually loved and sought after.

blocks.section: Partners presentation
blocks.text: La Brasserie Paul Bocuse

blocks.section: Partners presentation
blocks.text: The culinary concept is centered around “Tradition and Modernity.” Chef Keita SUZUKI recreates classic French cuisine by respecting traditional cooking methods while adding his own sense of aesthetics to bring a modern expression. He also places great importance on fresh vegetables and fish sourced directly from local regions, constantly ensuring the delivery of delicious seasonal flavors. Fully enjoy the charm of a brasserie true to authentic French style.

In 2005, joins the NHK French tv program as a regular music navigator, the next year he composed the opening and ending music for the same tv program. Throughout Japan, he played with numerous artists such as Clementine, Ice Saranyu, Aoki Karen, Patrick Nugier, Dominique CHAGNON to name a few. He's also part of different creative musical projects such as TGA (tokyo groove alliance), Instinct, Tatopani and Kazairo (風色).

blocks.section: Artists
blocks.text: Robin DUPUY

blocks.section: Artists
blocks.text: Robin DUPUY is a cellist and composer born in Strasbourg. After studying classical music in Paris, notably with Henri DEMARQUETTE, he explored pop, jazz, and Indian music in search of new sonic expressions. Now inspired by the natural beauty of the Japanese mountains that surround him, he offers an experimental journey through sound and harmonics. Living in Japan since 2004, he has collaborated with a wide range of artists including: Ryuichi Sakamoto, Hisaishi Joe, Ai, Eikichi Yazawa, Fujii Fumiya, Masayuki Suzuki, Tamaki Koji, as well as many other famous artists.

blocks.text: Special Guest

blocks.section: Special Guest
blocks.text: Mathilde BOULACHIN

blocks.section: Special Guest
blocks.text: Originally from Champagne, Mathilde is a recognized entrepreneur and industry expert who developed the first true wine-taste beverage in France. As a wine enthusiast, the idea of de-alcoholized wine while preserving its characteristics came to her after several years without consuming it, following multiple pregnancies.

blocks.section: Special Guest
blocks.text: She went on to found her own company and create Pierre Zéro, a de-alcoholized wine brand designed for all wine lovers. She is now one of the pioneers in this sector, with a strong focus on innovation and inclusivity.

blocks.section: Presentation of our partners
blocks.text: Presentation of our partners

blocks.section: Presentation of our partners
blocks.text: Pierre Zéro

blocks.section: Presentation of our partners
blocks.text: “Choosing a wine-taste beverage as one would choose a wine.”

blocks.section: Presentation of our partners
blocks.text: “Pierre Zéro” is an iconic de-alcoholized wine brand. Preserving all the elegance and character of fine wines, the brand succeeds in recreating a complex aromatic profile while removing the alcohol. It thus offers a new approach to gastronomy, where both wine lovers and non-drinkers can share tasting moments together, on any occasion.

blocks.section: Presentation of our partners
blocks.text: Pierre Zéro Website – Mottox

blocks.section: Presentation of our partners
blocks.text: Olivier ODDOS

blocks.section: Presentation of our partners
blocks.text: Olivier Oddos was born in 1970 in Bordeaux, France. He entered the culinary world at the age of 16 and worked at numerous Michelin-starred restaurants. Even at a young age, he was sometimes chosen as a chef. At the La Tour d’Argent, at that time a 2-starred restaurant, Olivier worked as a second chef. In 2000, at the recommendation of the head chef of La Tour d’Argent, Olivier came to Japan as a cooking instructor for Le Cordon Bleu. After a year working as a technical director and executive chef at the Kobe and Tokyo branches of Le Cordon Bleu, he opened Chez Olivier in Ichigaya in 2009. Olivier considers himself to be both a chef and restaurateur. Thus, to provide the best possible dining experience for everyone, everyday at his restaurant, Olivier is involved not only in the kitchen, but also in the selection of wines and in the service.

blocks.section: Presentation of our partners
blocks.text: Chez Olivier

blocks.section: Presentation of our partners
blocks.text: The restaurant Chez Olivier, which in French means the “House of Olivier,” was opened in 2009 by chef-owner, Olivier Oddos, for guests to enjoy typical French in a relaxed atmosphere. The restaurant uses only the finest ingredients. The vegetables, most of which are organic, come from small growers all over Japan. Because Chef Olivier believes authentic tastes are essential, he is careful to make everything home-made. Nothing is made ahead of time. After an order is placed, Olivier and his staff will prepare the dishes. Olivier wants his guests to taste the flavors of the season, not only on special occasions, but everyday—just as naturally as breathing fresh air. So each day, the dishes at Chez Olivier take full advantage of what the seasons have to offer.

blocks.text: Feedback is not about evaluating performance - it is a powerful way to develop people and unlock their potential. In this course, managers and leaders learn how to deliver constructive feedback that encourages ownership, strengthens trust, and supports continuous growth.

blocks.section: EMPOWERING THROUGH WORDS: MASTERING CONSTRUCTIVE FEEDBACK
blocks.text: The program is grounded in the timeless principles found in How to Win Friends and Influence People and How to Stop Worrying and Start Living. These Dale Carnegie principles, practiced worldwide for over 100 years, are applied directly to feedback conversations in today’s workplace.

blocks.section: EMPOWERING THROUGH WORDS: MASTERING CONSTRUCTIVE FEEDBACK
blocks.text: Through value-centered dialogue and practical approaches, participants learn how to give feedback that builds relationships while driving improvement.

blocks.section: TRAINER
blocks.text: Chizu SASAKI, Dale Carnegie

blocks.section: TRAINER
blocks.text: After graduating from university, Chizu began her career at a travel agency, where she was involved in planning and proposing educational programs aimed at developing global talent. Through consulting sales work with clients from diverse cultural backgrounds, she developed a strong appreciation for the importance of cultivating internationally minded professionals.

blocks.section: TRAINER
blocks.text: She later joined a U.S. higher education institution, where she was responsible for public relations and educational outreach to promote global learning among students from around the world. During this time, she encountered Dale Carnegie Training through an internal staff development program and deeply resonated with its values and practical approach.

blocks.section: TRAINER
blocks.text: Since joining Dale Carnegie in 2017, Chizu has been designing and delivering customized corporate training programs tailored to clients’ specific needs. Her work focuses on supporting the growth of business professionals and driving organizational development.

blocks.section: TRAINER
blocks.text: In 2024, she was honored with the Wow Trainer award, a prestigious global recognition from Dale Carnegie & Associates. She also hosts the podcast Business Mastery, which ranked No.1 in the management category and continues to receive strong acclaim.

title: Energy Conference - Business Leaders Forum 2026
description: Explore the transformations reshaping Japan’s energy system and the local futures taking shape across the country.

blocks.text: Explore the transformations reshaping Japan’s energy system and the local futures taking shape across the country.
Energy Conference 2026

The Chambre de Commerce et d'Industrie Française au Japon is pleased to invite you to the Energy Conference 2026 , taking place on 16 September 2026, from 2:00 to 8:00 PM , at the Espace CCI. This event will bring together key players from the sector to discuss the critical challenges of Japan's energy transition.
Panel 1 — Rising Energy Demand: New Uses and System Flexibility

An exceptional panel featuring speakers from Energy-Pool Japan , EDF and Nissan Motor Co., Ltd , exploring how shifting energy uses are reshaping our systems and the flexibility challenges that come with them.
Panel 2 — Building Local Energy Futures
Engaged voices from Waseda University , Veolia , Naskeo and Fukui Prefecture , giving shape to the energy transitions being built at the local and territorial level.
Fireside Chat — Investment Dynamics in the Energy Private Sector

This exclusive fireside chat will offer the insights of two leading financial institutions in the sector, Crédit Agricole CIB and Natixis , on investment dynamics and the future of private financing in energy.
The day will close with a networking cocktail 🥂

This year, BONJOUR FRANCE is bringing you an even more diverse market: the “ European Marché directed by BONJOUR FRANCE ”, taking place alongside the ANA Windsurfing World Cup Yokosuka-Miura from October 31 to November 3 .

With nearly 38,000 visitors attending the previous edition and 70 athletes from 31 different countries and regions , the Windsurfing World Cup is an international event that brings together a diverse audience from around the world.

For four days, the European Marché will bring a touch of Europe to this exciting sporting event. Brands, creators, and unique products from across Europe will come together to introduce Japanese visitors to the richness and diversity of European craftsmanship, with a special focus on French and European savoir-faire.

Through this new edition, the European Marché also aims to foster cultural exchange between Yokosuka, France, and other European countries, creating a welcoming space to discover and enjoy European gastronomy, craftsmanship, and culture.
Join us for a special weekend by the beach at Tsukuihama!

title: France Japon Eco Event
description: Sports : get ready for Japan’s next growing market

blocks.text: Sports : get ready for Japan’s next growing market

Japan is also a “sports power”. It arrived 3 rd at both last two Olympics in Paris and Tokyo, only behind the United States and China. Japanese skills in baseball, judo, swimming and (of course) sumo are already famous; but it also has become a key country in soccer, rugby, volleyball, basketball – or even fencing.

These performances have created economic activity in an array of sectors: construction, retail, transportation, hospitality, broadcasting among others. According to Japan Sports Agency (JSA), Japan’s sports market is 5 times France’s sports market. Yet sports business is only in its infancy in Japan, offering opportunities to newcomers.

We have assembled a top team of speakers to understand Japan’s sports market. Basketball coach Kyle Milling will come from Gunma, where he runs the Crane Thunders. His last team, Hiroshima’s Dragonflies, clinched their first ever league championship. Japan’s national fencing (sabre) coach Jérôme Guth, whose women team clinched the gold medal at Paris’ Olympics, will join. Veteran sports journalist and writer Florent Dabadie too will be on stage to share his experience and forecasts on the future of sports business in Japan. He will be joined by Abraham Franco, in charge of Sports & Entertainment’s Business Development at leading advertising agency HAKUHODO.
Key players onstage and offstage from the sports and business world will make this night a truly informative, fun event.
Get to the starting line. Join us at the French chamber of commerce on October 27, 5:30 pm.

title: FRENCH JAPANESE BUSINESS SUMMIT 2020

blocks.text: The Chamber of Commerce and Industry France Japon (CCI France Japon) organizes, together with the French Embassy in Japan, for the third consecutive year, a major summit dedicated to the French-Japanese business community.
The French-Japanese Business Summit will be held on November 18 2020, from 10h30 to 19h, at the Nikkei Hall in Tokyo on the theme:
“Growth Opportunities in Africa : Towards New Business Partnerships”

Following the success of the 2018 and 2019 editions, with an average of 700 delegates and 35 speakers per edition, this summit will once again bring together exceptional guests who will give their insights in front of an audience of business and opinion leaders, journalists as well as officials.
This event will be presential and live broadcasted. During this day, plenary sessions and conferences designed to highlight Japanese French and Afrian and African collaboration and expertise.
A networking lunch will be served by Chef-owner of Chez Olivier, Mr. Olivier Oddos, 1 Michelin Star, Tokyo.

Yumiko TANIMURA (Soprano)
Born in Kyoto, she graduated from Kyoto City University of Arts and the Conservatoire National Supérieur de Musique et de Danse de Paris (CNSMDP).

An award winner at numerous international competitions, she is the first Japanese singer to win both the International Lily & Nadia Boulanger Competition and the Lyon International Chamber Music Competition. Her repertoire spans from Baroque music to contemporary works, and she performs throughout Europe and Japan with distinguished conductors while pursuing an active career as a recitalist and educator.
In 2018, she founded Atelier Lyrique Kyoto, promoting musical and cultural exchange between Japan and France.
Tsubasa TATSUNO (Piano)

Born in Kobe, he graduated top of his class from Kyoto City University of Arts before continuing his studies at the Conservatoire National Supérieur de Musique et de Danse de Paris (CNSMDP) and the École Normale de Musique de Paris.
A prizewinner at numerous national and international competitions, he performs widely as a recitalist, concerto soloist, and vocal accompanist in Japan and abroad.
He currently teaches at Tokyo College of Music and serves as vocal accompanist at Kyoto City University of Arts and Osaka College of Music.

Chef Bruno Oger is one of France's leading contemporary chefs and the owner of the two-Michelin-starred La Villa Archange in Le Cannet. A protégé of Georges Blanc, he rose to prominence as Executive Chef of the legendary Hôtel Majestic Cannes, where he earned his first Michelin star in 1997 and a second in 2005. In 2011, just ten months after opening La Villa Archange, he was awarded two Michelin stars. His refined cuisine, inspired by both his native Brittany and the Mediterranean, celebrates seafood, seasonal produce, and aromatic herbs.

For several years, Chef Oger has served as the culinary mentor of Le Lotus, the signature overwater gourmet restaurant at the InterContinental Tahiti Resort & Spa. Working closely with Chef David Philippeau, he contributes to the restaurant's menus, shares his culinary expertise, and regularly trains the brigade, including through exchanges at La Villa Archange. This long-standing collaboration brings together the excellence of French gastronomy and the distinctive flavors of French Polynesia, making Le Lotus one of the region's premier dining destinations.

title: How To Develop A Resilient Mind ?
description: This training uses clinical psychology to help you manage stress and build resilience and adaptability.

blocks.text: This training uses clinical psychology to help you manage stress and build resilience and adaptability.
HOW TO DEVELOP A RESILIENT MIND ?
DATE: July 7, 2025 (Thu) | Time: 13:00-17:00
TRAINING CONTENT

Moderate stress has positive effects, but, when intense stress persists over the long term, it not only negatively impacts our mental and physical health, but also leads to diminished performance, adversely affecting customer satisfaction and hindering business growth. The training program is focusing on Cognitive Training employing clinical psychological theories and has been proven to help you navigate stressors and cultivate self-resilience and adaptability.
Understand stress mechanism and good aspects and negative aspects of stress.
Learn evidence-based methods to raise awareness and nurture a resilient mindset when facing challenges.

Enhance adaptability by fostering healthy thinking habits and open-mindedness to diverse possibilities, putting new ideas into actions, and engage in daily self-reflection thereby establishing a continuous cycle for self-growth.
TARGET AUDIENCE
Anyone who wants to learn practical techniques to cope with stress and build mental resilience.
TRAINING METHOD

Deep-learning approach enriched with psychological theories and hands-on experience which can be applied directly to daily work. Encouraging insights from self-reflection as well as an interactive learning journey. There will be discussions, case studies, and role-plays.
YOUR TRAINER

Makiko Kuramoto, Ph.D., an expert in Organizational psychology, Developmental psychology, and Cultural Psychology, is the Founder and Managing Director of FUMI Consulting. With extensive project management experience in both Japanese and international companies, she offers coaching, training, and consultation services to organizations across various sectors. She also teaches psychology courses at Keio University and Aoyama Gakuin University.

title: How to manage Millennials and GenZ

blocks.text: Context of this program

Around 30% of new grads will quit their job within 3 years. 75% of millennials/Gen Z will prioritise the social impact of a company over the financial conditions offered to them when choosing a job. How they are valued as individuals is extremely important to them, but so is their privacy. Their definition of who to recognise as a superior is different, and should you not satisfy their communication expectations, total withdrawal can be as sudden as it can be absolute.

To us non-millennials/Gen Z individuals navigating the communications with our younger team members can be a source of stress and confusion as their expectations can come across as inconsistent. One is never sure what or when the next « […]harassment » will be coined and what one might be accused of. Non-compliance with requests, incomplete or off topic delivery of requested work, sudden disappearance (resignation) are factors that are not as rare as one would like them to be.
This course provides guidelines to help you understand how and what to communicate to help them maximise their potential, overcome their issues, and deliver the results you need them to deliver.

The Framework will also help you communicate with your younger team members in such a way as to make them feel comfortable and intrinsically motivated to complete the tasks you want to allocate to them.
Who should attend?

If you are managing a team of people under 35, are finding it difficult to communicate with, and intrinsically motivate them, this is the course for you. If you have issues with employee retention, team efficiency, this course will provide you with a framework to overcome the issues and improve your team efficiency.
Training program and objectives
This training has a strong group work and role play component. It is based on the belief you have to think it and experience it to keep it.
The training will be in 2 parts
Part I : About millennials and Gen Z
A working definition of who they are.
A description of their cultural background and, how it differs from hours
Learning how their cultural background impacts their vision of the world and the way they communicate.
Summary
Part II : Communication Framework :
A communication framework for daily conversation.
A delegation framework for assigning tasks in such a way as to keep them motivated and help them succeed.
Buddy plan and PDCA
End : Q&A
About the speaker

Carlo La Porta is the founder and Motivation Architect of Mpowered Sales. He and has been living in Japan for 30 years, mostly as a consultant for both foreign and local consulting firms such as KPMG/Bearingpoint, LowendalMasai and big name clients such as McDonalds Japan, Hitachi/Oclaro, Sakura, Veolia Waters(JP). Early on he came to understand that imposing tasks on client teams or getting their boss to impose tasks upon them is often a guarantee of missed deadlines, low quality work, excuses and team discord. Finding ways to foster intrinsic motivation was crucial to good teamwork and efficient results and it became his passion. Since starting his own company, clients have included both foreign capital and local clients, and to date, all clients have reported at least one of the following: improvements in activity rates (for sales teams), profitability, revenue. Reduction in employee turn over.

blocks.text: Learn to explore unconscious and conscious dynamics in your organization using unconventional tools to understand Boundaries, Authority, Role, & Task.
HR BREAKFAST IMPROVING YOUR LEADERSHIP AND ORGANIZATION'S EFFECTIVENESS A SYSTEMS PSYCHODYNAMICS APPROACH
Date : December 2, 2025 (Tue) | Time : 9:00am - 11:00am

How can we better understand organizational behavior and dynamics by exploring the interplay between conscious and unconscious processes, recognizing that individuals' thoughts, feelings and behaviors are influenced by both their individual psychologies and the larger organizational system ?

This HR Committee will encourage participants to actively testify and emulate the role of an Organizational Role Analysis Consultant, exploring notions such as Boundaries, Authority, Role and Task, in order to better understand the dynamics at play within their own organizations.
What You'll Learn ?
How to get a better understanding of the visible and unconscious dynamics at play in your own organization by using unconventional tools and questioning.
Target Audience
CEOs, Team Leaders, CHRO as well as Change Management and Talent Development professionals.

YOUR GUEST SPEAKER

François-Xavier Lienhart became an Executive Coach in 2022, graduating from the INSEAD Coaching Certificate Program after a career of 35 years in the corporate world, including significant CEO positions in large and and small organizations. His practice is based on the Systems-Psychodynamic approach and uses the Person-Role Organization model, incorporating context and culture, with expertise in various coaching tools. He coaches individual executives as well as teams. He is also a certified Hogan Leadership assessor and accredited coach with the EMCC. He has been based in Japan for more than 20 years.

description: Evolution of Logistics and Supply Chain Automation in the Post-Covid Era, by speakers from 5 major specialist companies.

blocks.text: Evolution of Logistics and Supply Chain Automation in the Post-Covid Era, by speakers from 5 major specialist companies.
General Theme: Evolution of Logistics and Supply Chain Automation in the Post-Covid Era.

Covid has deeply changed the way supply chains are organized around the world, revealing weak points and forcing innovation to tackle new issues. In that regard, the industry is undergoing many transformations, and that is why we want to seize this opportunity to make it known to our community through this event, gathering 5 speakers from 5 major companies of the industry: Kuehne+Nagel for the international approach, Air France KLM Cargo for the point of view of the air transporter with Kansai Airports with a complementary insight from the airport perspective, then Nippon Express for the local Japanese viewpoint, and finally Dassault Systems/Accenture to wrap up the subject with a global understanding of the issues at hand.

blocks.section: Special guest
blocks.text: Françoise MORÉCHAND

blocks.section: Special guest
blocks.text: - A Bridge Between Japan and France -

blocks.section: Special guest
blocks.text: Françoise MORÉCHAND is a French lifestyle advisor and essayist, notably known for having served as beauty director at Chanel. She is currently an international advisor to the 21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art, Kanazawa. She is married to French music and film critic Tatsuji Nagataki.

blocks.section: Special guest
blocks.text: Originally destined to become an interpreter in Chinese or Russian, she chose instead to devote herself to Japanese, convinced of Japan’s future potential. She studied at the École des langues orientales de Paris as well as at the Sorbonne, then settled in Japan in 1958 with her first husband. There, she taught French for Japan Airlines, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan, and Ochanomizu University.

blocks.section: Special guest
blocks.text: She gained widespread recognition as the instructor on the NHK television program “French Conversation,” quickly becoming one of the best-known French women in Japan through her many appearances on television, radio, and in the press. After returning to France in 1964, she worked for Christian Dior and Revlon before returning to Japan in 1974 as beauty director of Chanel. She later continued her media activities, introducing French fashion, culture, and history to the Japanese public.

blocks.section: Special guest
blocks.text: A lifestyle producer in Japan, she has also contributed to the creation of kimonos, ceramics, and fashion collections. A true bridge between French and Japanese cultures, she is the author of numerous books and has served as a visiting professor at Kyoritsu Women's University. In France, her book La Gaijin became a bestseller.

blocks.section: Special guest
blocks.text: Elected in 2000 as the Northern Asia representative to the Conseil supérieur des Français de l’étranger, she is also honorary president of the Union des Français de l’étranger du Japon. She was awarded the Légion d’honneur in 2004, the Ordre national du Mérite at the rank of Commander in 2008, the honorary prize of La Renaissance Française in 2019, and the Order of the Rising Sun (Gold Rays with Rosette) in 2020. She currently serves as a Foreign Trade Advisor of France (CCE) and as tourism ambassador for Ishikawa Prefecture.

blocks.section: What is PARIS mag?
blocks.text: What is PARIS mag?

blocks.section: What is PARIS mag?
blocks.text: PARIS mag is a web magazine dedicated to a simple and refined lifestyle, bridging Japan and Paris, initiated by the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan, BONJOUR FRANCE. Through fashion, gastronomy, culture and lifestyle, the magazine shares a modern vision of the Art de Vivre, thoughtfully created for Japanese readers who have a deep affection for France.

blocks.section: What is PARIS mag?
blocks.text: With a community of nearly 50,000 passionate followers across all social media platforms, PARIS mag has become a true meeting point between France and Japan, as well as a space for those who love France, its culture and its craftsmanship.

blocks.section: What is PARIS mag?
blocks.text: BONJOUR FRANCE takes over in the same spirit, with the ambition to go even further and the desire to offer readers a true « Adventure ». Through articles and exclusive content, the media continues to invite its audience to discover France in a new way, with curiosity and pleasure.

blocks.text: From November 14 to 16, experience the French Art de Vivre at the heart of the Windsurfing World Cup Yokosuka Miura!

Following on from last year, Le Marché BONJOUR FRANCE will take place at the Windsurfing World Cup Yokosuka Miura for three days, from November 14 to 16, 2025. The Windsurfing World Cup is a major windsurfing event which welcomes over 40,000 visitors and around a hundred athletes from over 30 countries, many of whom are French.

To celebrate this wonderful event and the special ties between Yokosuka and France, Le Marché BONJOUR FRANCE will showcase brands that embody the French Art de Vivre. The aim is to introduce high-quality products and promote French culture to the Japanese public.
