blocks.section: Overview
blocks.text: Overview

blocks.section: Overview
blocks.text: Psychological safety is not simply about being “nice” or “easy to talk to.” It is a foundation for team performance, growth, and engagement.

blocks.section: Overview
blocks.text: In this course, managers learn how to act as Psychological Safety Champions—leaders who foster trust, encourage open dialogue, and empower team members to speak up, take risks, and learn from mistakes.

blocks.section: Overview
blocks.text: The program is grounded in the timeless principles found in How to Win Friends and Influence People and How to Stop Worrying and Start Living. These Dale Carnegie principles, practiced worldwide for over 100 years, are translated into practical approaches that fit today’s workplace and leadership challenges.

blocks.section: Overview
blocks.text: By creating an environment where people feel safe to contribute and grow, managers can build teams that achieve sustainable results and strong engagement.

blocks.section: Overview
blocks.text: Understand what psychological safety is and why it directly impacts team performance

blocks.section: Overview
blocks.text: Reflect on how a manager’s words, attitudes, and behaviors influence the team

blocks.section: Overview
blocks.text: Learn trust-building communication based on Dale Carnegie principles

blocks.section: Overview
blocks.text: Discover how to create an environment where ideas and concerns can be shared safely

blocks.section: Overview
blocks.text: Identify clear, practical actions that can be applied immediately in the workplace

blocks.section: TRAINER
blocks.text: TRAINER

blocks.section: TRAINER
blocks.text: Chizu SASAKI, Dale Carnegie

blocks.section: TRAINER
blocks.text: After graduating from university, Chizu began her career at a travel agency, where she was involved in planning and proposing educational programs aimed at developing global talent. Through consulting sales work with clients from diverse cultural backgrounds, she developed a strong appreciation for the importance of cultivating internationally minded professionals.

blocks.section: TRAINER
blocks.text: She later joined a U.S. higher education institution, where she was responsible for public relations and educational outreach to promote global learning among students from around the world. During this time, she encountered Dale Carnegie Training through an internal staff development program and deeply resonated with its values and practical approach.

blocks.section: TRAINER
blocks.text: Since joining Dale Carnegie in 2017, Chizu has been designing and delivering customized corporate training programs tailored to clients’ specific needs. Her work focuses on supporting the growth of business professionals and driving organizational development.

blocks.section: TRAINER
blocks.text: In 2024, she was honored with the Wow Trainer award, a prestigious global recognition from Dale Carnegie & Associates. She also hosts the podcast Business Mastery, which ranked No.1 in the management category and continues to receive strong acclaim.

title: Meet & Engage with Romain Millet
description: Connect & exchange and discover Millet Mountain Group with its CEO, Romain Millet

blocks.text: Connect & exchange and discover Millet Mountain Group with its CEO, Romain Millet
Join the CCIFJ for an exclusive afterwork with Romain Millet, CEO of Millet Moutain Group, and discover the story behind one of France’s iconic outdoor brands!

The CCIFJ invites you to an exclusive afterwork at Millet Mountain Group Japan’s offices , bringing together the group’s history, expertise and leadership during Romain Millet’s visit to Japan this November.

Founded in 1921 in Annecy, in the heart of the French Alps, Millet has spent over a century supporting mountaineers and mountain enthusiasts around the world. With roots in the Alps and products tested in the demanding environment of Chamonix, t he brand has built its reputation on technical expertise, innovation and a deep connection with the mountains.

The company also has a unique family story. In 2021, Romain Millet and his uncle, Jean-Pierre Millet, brought Millet back into the family, renewing its entrepreneurial legacy and paving the way for its next chapter.

Millet Mountain Group Japan is being given a high level of autonomy and 80% of the turnover in Japan is generate by products developed by the Japanese team in Japan. The turnover in Japan has doubled over the past 4 years.
During this special evening, Romain Millet and Per Rasmussen, Representative Director and President, will present the group, offering insights into its history, activities and vision.
Join us for an evening of discovery, exchange and networking over drinks and finger food!

title: Craftsmanship: Cross Perspectives France × Japan
description: How are traditional crafts being defined today in the face of new local and international markets, between creativity and economic instability?

blocks.text: How are traditional crafts being defined today in the face of new local and international markets, between creativity and economic instability?
※ Photo by Ryūji Ōnari (Bleu Abysse) ー ryujionari.jp/works/hekisora-bleu-abysse/

This unprecedented gathering in Kansai is jointly organized by two major institutions: the CCI France Japon Kansai office on the one hand is dedicated to fostering economic exchange , and the Institut Français du Kansai on the other is devoted to promoting French culture . Held in the heart of Kyoto, the event invites participants to explore the current transformations of traditional craftsmanship and savoir-faire between France and Japan.
This dialogue, conducted in Japanese by leading experts from the sector through three thematic roundtable discussions, aims to open conversations on several key structural issues:
Digitalization and traditional craftsmanship: a new source for creating value?
Going global: challenges and strategies for accessing high-value markets
The transcreation of cultural resources: the challenge of transforming heritage into new value
Each roundtable will feature at least two speakers and one moderator.

Following these discussions, opportunities for collaboration between French and Japanese stakeholders will continue during a business networking session and terrace cocktail reception reserved for participants.

blocks.text: How are digital technologies transforming traditional crafts, their distribution channels, and their business models ? From online visibility and e-commerce to new communication strategies and the globalization of customer bases, this roundtable discussion will explore the opportunities and limitations of digitalization for traditional craftsmanship. Through the shared perspectives of actors involved in promoting and spreading Japanese craftsmanship, the speakers will examine the new types of value generated by digital technology, at the crossroads of innovation, transmission, and the market.

This roundtable discussion will explore the strategies implemented to access high-value-added markets, including adapting to cultural contexts, preserving traditional skills, brand positioning, and storytelling around craftsmanship. Drawing on concrete experiences between Japan and other countries, the speakers will share their insights on the necessary conditions for sustainable internationalization that remains true to the identity of their craft.

blocks.text: Jean Todt is the United Nations Secretary-General's Special Envoy for Road Safety. He is also Chairman of the Board of Directors of the International Peace Institute, Vice-Chairman of the Paris Brain Institute, Chairman of the Suu Foundation, and a member of the Board of Directors of the Ban Ki-moon Foundation, the FIFA Foundation, and Gaumont. Finally, he is the former president of the International Automobile Federation and served as CEO of Ferrari from 2006 to 2009.

blocks.section: Theme of our special guest, Marc Amblard

blocks.section: Theme of our special guest, Marc Amblard
blocks.text: Autonomous vehicles are no longer a concept for the future. Thousands of robotaxis and autonomous last-mile delivery vehicles are already operating commercially. About a million autonomous rides are consumed weekly, essentially in American and Chinese cities. Numerous partnerships and deployments have been announced for Europe, Japan, and Korea with a variety of stakeholders. Where do we stand and where is the industry going next?

blocks.text: Masahiro Akita is a Senior Analyst covering Japan Autos & Auto Parts sector at Bernstein, a premier global equity research and brokerage firm and a member of the Société Générale Group. He was previously a Senior Consultant at Frontier Management, where he covered the automotive and auto parts sector. Before that, he spent 13 years at Credit Suisse Securities as a Senior Analyst, leading the Japanese automotive sector team and conducting thematic research for the global automotive team. Earlier in his career, he worked for 12 years at Aisin, a major Japanese automotive supplier, where he held key roles in the automotive parts business.

blocks.section: EMPOWERING THROUGH WORDS: MASTERING EFFECTIVE FEEDBACK
blocks.text: Feedback is not about evaluating performance - it is a powerful way to develop people and unlock their potential. In this course, managers and leaders learn how to deliver constructive feedback that encourages ownership, strengthens trust, and supports continuous growth.

blocks.section: EMPOWERING THROUGH WORDS: MASTERING EFFECTIVE FEEDBACK
blocks.text: The program is grounded in the timeless principles found in How to Win Friends and Influence People and How to Stop Worrying and Start Living. These Dale Carnegie principles, practiced worldwide for over 100 years, are applied directly to feedback conversations in today’s workplace.

blocks.section: EMPOWERING THROUGH WORDS: MASTERING EFFECTIVE FEEDBACK
blocks.text: Through value-centered dialogue and practical approaches, participants learn how to give feedback that builds relationships while driving improvement.

blocks.section: TRAINER
blocks.text: Chizu SASAKI, Dale Carnegie

blocks.section: TRAINER
blocks.text: After graduating from university, Chizu began her career at a travel agency, where she was involved in planning and proposing educational programs aimed at developing global talent. Through consulting sales work with clients from diverse cultural backgrounds, she developed a strong appreciation for the importance of cultivating internationally minded professionals.

blocks.section: TRAINER
blocks.text: She later joined a U.S. higher education institution, where she was responsible for public relations and educational outreach to promote global learning among students from around the world. During this time, she encountered Dale Carnegie Training through an internal staff development program and deeply resonated with its values and practical approach.

blocks.section: TRAINER
blocks.text: Since joining Dale Carnegie in 2017, Chizu has been designing and delivering customized corporate training programs tailored to clients’ specific needs. Her work focuses on supporting the growth of business professionals and driving organizational development.

blocks.section: TRAINER
blocks.text: In 2024, she was honored with the Wow Trainer award, a prestigious global recognition from Dale Carnegie & Associates. She also hosts the podcast Business Mastery, which ranked No.1 in the management category and continues to receive strong acclaim.

blocks.text: Discover how AI, automation and connected technologies are transforming retail and redefining the customer experience.
Retail Tech Conference 2026

The French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan is pleased to invite you to the Retail Tech Conference 2026 , taking place on October 15, 2026 , from 2:00 PM to 8:00 PM at Espace CCI . This conference will bring together leading retail industry players to explore the transformations reshaping the sector at the intersection of artificial intelligence, automation, and customer experience.
Panel 1: Beyond the VIP: AI-Driven Hyperpersonalisation in the Luxury Retail Experience

A distinguished panel featuring representatives from Sogo & Seibu Co., Ltd. and Capgemini , exploring how next-generation technologies are transforming operations, clienteling, and customer experience across the retail and luxury sectors.
Panel 2: Future-Proof Warehousing – Automation, Robotics and Resilient Supply Chains
Experts from Exotec Japan and Mujin Japan will share their insights on intelligent warehousing, robotics, and the technologies shaping more resilient and efficient supply chains.
Panel 3: The Connected Store – Enhancing Customer Experience Through Technology

Representatives from Amazon , IKEA , Matterport , VusionGroup K.K. and EY will discuss the innovations driving the connected store, from in-store intelligence to the digital technologies redefining the customer experience.
Keynotes

The conference will also feature keynote addresses from representatives of Amazon , Sogo & Seibu Co., Ltd. , Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) , the Embassy of France in Japan , and VusionGroup K.K. , sharing their perspectives on the trends and innovations shaping the future of retail.

🥂 The day will conclude with a networking cocktail , offering participants the opportunity to connect with senior decision-makers, industry experts, and key stakeholders in a setting designed to foster meaningful exchanges and new business opportunities. Program

blocks.text: Meet Philippe TROUSSIER, a true icon in the history of football in Japan, over a specially curated menu!

On June 26, 2026 , the CCI France Japan opens the doors of L’Espace@CCIFJ from 6:00 PM , on the occasion of the exceptional visit of Philippe TROUSSIER , former head coach of the Japan national football team.
During the soirée, you will enjoy an exclusive Talk-Show with Philippe TROUSSIER, hosted by Florent DABADIE , presenter, journalist, and sports commentator, who will moderate the discussion.

Through this Talk-Show, several topics will be explored, including the FIFA World Cup, analyses of the Japanese national team’s matches and prospects for the final stage of the tournament, as well as the story behind the wine “FLAT3”, created by Philippe TROUSSIER.

The talk will be followed by a refined and convivial cocktail reception , featuring culinary creations specially designed for the event by Chef Dominique CORBY , offering a unique and gourmet experience. The soirée will also feature “FLAT3” wine as well as Dassai sake , a unique opportunity to taste Philippe TROUSSIER’s wine!
For all enthusiasts of sport, football, and the ties that unite France and Japan, this is a must-attend event, limited to 100 participants to ensure a truly intimate experience!
Doors open: 6:00 PM

blocks.section: Philippe TROUSSIER's wine "FLAT3"
blocks.text: Philippe TROUSSIER's wine "FLAT3"

blocks.section: Philippe TROUSSIER's wine "FLAT3"
blocks.text: Passion is not a word. It is a way of life itself.

blocks.section: Philippe TROUSSIER's wine "FLAT3"
blocks.text: He didn't choose the wine; he was guided by the wine. On the pitch, we have always strived for the optimal balance between defense and offense. That remains true even in the fields. Strength and lightness. Structure and flexibility. Bringing all opposing forces into a single balance. A vintage represents a single season. And within a single bottle lies an unpredictable ending.

blocks.section: Philippe TROUSSIER's wine "FLAT3"
blocks.text: It begins with passion, connects through trust, and leads to harmony.

blocks.section: Philippe TROUSSIER's wine "FLAT3"
blocks.text: The football tactic "flat three" originated in France, but it was in Japan that it truly gained meaning. It is a memory, a transformation, a shared story. This wine is not just about terroir; it's about the connection itself. "FLAT3" is now thriving in a new field: wine. FLAT 3 by KANTOKU Saint-Émilion Grand Cru. A wine that embodies passion and harmony, a symphony of people and land.

blocks.section: Special Guest
blocks.text: Special Guest

blocks.section: Special Guest
blocks.text: Philippe TROUSSIER

blocks.section: Special Guest
blocks.text: After a career as a professional soccer player, Philippe TROUSSIER began coaching in the late 1980s. His coaching career took a major shift when he became coach of several African national teams, including Burkina Faso and Côte d'Ivoire. However, it was in Japan that he truly gained popularity. In 1998, he became the Japan's soccer national team coach. Under his tutelage, the Japanese reached the 2002 World Cup, a major achievement for the country. Philippe TROUSSIER put together a highly disciplined team, and as a result is highly respected in Japan for his role in the rise of Japanese soccer on the international stage. More recently, he has decided to move into the world of viticulture. He has even started producing his own wines in the south of France.

blocks.section: Moderator
blocks.text: Moderator

blocks.section: Moderator
blocks.text: Florent DABADIE

blocks.section: Moderator
blocks.text: Born in Paris in 1974, and graduate of Langues’O, he worked as an editorial assistant for the film magazine Première Japon between 1998 and 2003. At the same time, he interpreted for the French coach of the Japanese national soccer team until the 2002 World Cup. In 2004, he became sports news host for Fuji national television and the WOWOW channel. Later, in 2014, he set up his own production and consultancy company for sports and cultural events.

blocks.section: Chef
blocks.text: Chef

blocks.section: Chef
blocks.text: Dominique CORBY

blocks.section: Chef
blocks.text: Born in Paris in 1965, he developed a strong interest in the culinary arts from a young age. Following this passion, he began his culinary career at the age of 15. In 1994, he continued his career in Japan, and even became the director of Le Cordon Bleu Japan. He also opened several restaurants in the Tokyo area in order to share important values, such as introducing French-Japanese cuisine to the rest of the world. But his achievements do not stop there. Among the many titles he holds, he was named Chevalier of the Order of Agricultural Merit in France in 2007, became a member of the Japanese branch of the French Culinary Academy’s secretariat in 2010, and was appointed ambassador for a champagne house in 2018. He is also committed to helping the less fortunate through the creation of the association “Lumière et Espoir pour le Japon.”

blocks.text: DATE: July 21, 2026 (Tue) | Time: 10 AM - 5PM

blocks.section: TRAINING CONTENT
blocks.text: TRAINING CONTENT

blocks.section: TRAINING CONTENT
blocks.text: In today’s fast-moving organisations, leaders and managers are increasingly expected to present ideas clearly, confidently, and credibly to large and diverse audiences, whether in townhalls, departmental briefings, project updates, or cross-functional meetings.

blocks.section: TRAINING CONTENT
blocks.text: This 1-day immersive program equips participants with the practical skills to present with impact, clarity, and confidence, combining strong message structuring with engaging delivery and purposeful storytelling. The focus is not on “performing”, but on being understood, trusted, and influential when it matters most.

blocks.section: KEY TRAINING OUTCOMES
blocks.text: KEY TRAINING OUTCOMES

blocks.section: KEY TRAINING OUTCOMES
blocks.text: By the end of this program, participants will be able to:

blocks.section: KEY TRAINING OUTCOMES
blocks.text: Present with Confidence, Impact, and Credibility Communicate ideas with clarity and composure when presenting to large or mixed audiences, managing nerves while projecting confidence and professionalism.

blocks.section: KEY TRAINING OUTCOMES
blocks.text: Structure Messages That Are Clear and Memorable Design well-structured presentations that guide audiences logically, highlight key messages, and ensure understanding, even in complex or information-heavy contexts.

blocks.section: KEY TRAINING OUTCOMES
blocks.text: Engage Mass Audiences Through Storytelling Use simple and effective storytelling techniques to bring messages to life, sustain attention, and connect ideas to audience realities and business outcomes.

blocks.section: KEY TRAINING OUTCOMES
blocks.text: Handle Questions and Live Interactions with Control Respond confidently to questions, comments, and spontaneous inputs during presentations, maintaining credibility and control in front of a group.

blocks.section: TARGET AUDIENCE
blocks.text: TARGET AUDIENCE

blocks.section: TARGET AUDIENCE
blocks.text: HR Professionals evaluating or rolling out English presentation skills programs for managers and professionals

blocks.section: TARGET AUDIENCE
blocks.text: People Managers who regularly present to teams, departments, or cross-functional audiences

blocks.section: TARGET AUDIENCE
blocks.text: Executives and Senior Professionals leading townhalls, project briefings, leadership updates, and large-group meetings

blocks.section: TRAINER
blocks.text: TRAINER

blocks.section: TRAINER
blocks.text: Shawn D’COTTA is the Head of Office for Cegos Asia Pacific and a highly sought-after facilitator in communication, presentation skills, and leadership development across the region.

blocks.section: TRAINER
blocks.text: With over 15 years of experience working with multinational organisations, Shawn helps leaders and managers communicate with clarity, confidence, and impact in real business situations, from townhalls and leadership briefings to cross-functional and client-facing presentations. His facilitation style is practical, engaging, and results-driven, blending proven communication frameworks with live practice and personalised feedback.

blocks.section: TRAINER
blocks.text: Shawn has delivered programs across Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Vietnam, and the wider Asia Pacific region for organisations such as Siemens Energy, Lufthansa, Bosch, Samsung, AIA, and various Chambers of Commerce. Participants consistently value his ability to simplify complex ideas, create a safe yet challenging learning environment, and translate skills directly into workplace impact.

blocks.section: TRAINER
blocks.text: He holds multiple professional certifications in training, facilitation, and organisational development, and is recognised for making learning both highly relevant and immediately applicable.

blocks.section: TRAINER
blocks.text: CEGOS ASIA PACIFIC , a global leader in learning and development, empowering professionals across 50+ countries to learn, lead, and make an impact.

blocks.text: The Business Leaders Forum presents the Student Career Forum, connecting young Japanese talents with leading companies!

As part of the CCIFJ Business Summit, the Student Career Forum offers companies direct access to students from leading universities in Tokyo. Organized on December 1st, 2026, at Nikkei Hall, this format has been designed to enable companies to identify, meet, and engage with future talent in a structured, efficient, and high-quality environment.
The forum is primarily aimed at second- and third-year undergraduate students who are seeking internships or exploring their first professional opportunities.
Unlike traditional career fairs, the format emphasizes:
targeted exchanges with relevant profiles
high-quality interactions, beyond simple CV collection
strong alignment with your HR needs and your industry sector
Participating students come from both Japanese and international universities.

In 2025, the following institutions placed their trust in us: University of Tokyo, Waseda University, Keio University, Hitotsubashi University, Sophia University,Meiji University, Rikkyo University, Japan University, Japan Women’s University, HEC Paris, Temple University Japan Campus and more.
Participating companies benefit from:
a dedicated space during the forum
the opportunity to present their organization
access to the CCIFJ Business Summit
Identify and meet talent in Tokyo
Strengthen your employer brand within the Franco-Japanese ecosystem
Access profiles aligned with your recruitment needs
Optimize your presence through a combined experience with the Business Summit

title: Territory and community: Lessons in Leadership from the Maasaï
description: What can we learn from Kenya’s Maasaï and other traditional societies about being more relevant in what we do and who we are?

blocks.text: What can we learn from Kenya’s Maasaï and other traditional societies about being more relevant in what we do and who we are?

blocks.section: HR BREAKFAST TERRITORY AND COMMUNITY LESSONS IN LEADERSHIP FROM THE MAASAÏ
blocks.text: HR BREAKFAST TERRITORY AND COMMUNITY LESSONS IN LEADERSHIP FROM THE MAASAÏ

blocks.section: HR BREAKFAST TERRITORY AND COMMUNITY LESSONS IN LEADERSHIP FROM THE MAASAÏ
blocks.text: Date : October 20, 2026 (Tue) | Time : 9:00am - 11:00am

blocks.section: HR BREAKFAST TERRITORY AND COMMUNITY LESSONS IN LEADERSHIP FROM THE MAASAÏ
blocks.text: Ask a Maasaï chief what matters most in his life and in his role as a leader, and two answers invariably come first: my territory and my community.

blocks.section: HR BREAKFAST TERRITORY AND COMMUNITY LESSONS IN LEADERSHIP FROM THE MAASAÏ
blocks.text: From there arise fundamental questions:

blocks.section: HR BREAKFAST TERRITORY AND COMMUNITY LESSONS IN LEADERSHIP FROM THE MAASAÏ
blocks.text: What does the community need to survive, protect itself and thrive?

blocks.section: HR BREAKFAST TERRITORY AND COMMUNITY LESSONS IN LEADERSHIP FROM THE MAASAÏ
blocks.text: What resources and tools does it need?

blocks.section: HR BREAKFAST TERRITORY AND COMMUNITY LESSONS IN LEADERSHIP FROM THE MAASAÏ
blocks.text: What obstacles will it encounter along its journey?

blocks.section: HR BREAKFAST TERRITORY AND COMMUNITY LESSONS IN LEADERSHIP FROM THE MAASAÏ
blocks.text: How should decisions be made, responsibilities shared and knowledge passed on?

blocks.section: HR BREAKFAST TERRITORY AND COMMUNITY LESSONS IN LEADERSHIP FROM THE MAASAÏ
blocks.text: Drawing on English explorer Anthony Willoughby ’s lifelong experience with traditional societies, and on his recent journey among the Maasaï with Tokyo based Executive Coach François-Xavier Lienhart , we invite you to an interactive and exploratory conversation about what traditional wisdom can teach us about leadership in today’s organizations and, in particular, in modern Japan.

blocks.section: HR BREAKFAST TERRITORY AND COMMUNITY LESSONS IN LEADERSHIP FROM THE MAASAÏ
blocks.text: Together, we will explore some fundamental dimensions of leadership: wisdom, strength and beauty; courage and protection; power and responsibility; decision-making; authority and seniority; symbols and rituals; tradition and modernity; transmission and culture; community and belonging.

blocks.section: HR BREAKFAST TERRITORY AND COMMUNITY LESSONS IN LEADERSHIP FROM THE MAASAÏ
blocks.text: Rather than offering ready-made answers, we shall use these perspectives to question some of our assumptions about leadership and organizational life.

blocks.section: HR BREAKFAST TERRITORY AND COMMUNITY LESSONS IN LEADERSHIP FROM THE MAASAÏ
blocks.text: What makes us relevant as leaders?

blocks.section: HR BREAKFAST TERRITORY AND COMMUNITY LESSONS IN LEADERSHIP FROM THE MAASAÏ
blocks.text: What gives meaning to our actions?

blocks.section: HR BREAKFAST TERRITORY AND COMMUNITY LESSONS IN LEADERSHIP FROM THE MAASAÏ
blocks.text: What do the communities we lead actually need from us?

blocks.section: HR BREAKFAST TERRITORY AND COMMUNITY LESSONS IN LEADERSHIP FROM THE MAASAÏ
blocks.text: And what should we preserve, change or pass on?

blocks.section: Takeaways
blocks.text: Takeaways

blocks.section: Takeaways
blocks.text: Participants will have a unique opportunity to step outside their usual organizational frameworks and reflect on important aspects of their lives as leaders and members of a community. The discussion will encourage reflection on our own behaviours, the meaning of our actions, and the contribution we make to the organizations and communities to which we belong.

blocks.section: Takeaways
blocks.text: IMPORTANT NOTE: This HR Breakfast is not a training session . It is designed to bring together the HR community in Japan, along with professionals interested in the topic, to exchange perspectives and engage in meaningful discussions with the speakers and fellow participants. As this is a community event the presentation is intentionally concise, leaving ample time for questions, interaction, and peer exchange.

blocks.section: GUEST SPEAKERS
blocks.text: François-Xavier LIENHART François-Xavier became an Executive Coach in 2022, graduating from the INSEAD Coaching Certificate Program after a career of 35 years in the corporate world, including significant CEO positions in large and and small organizations. His practice is based on the Systems-Psychodynamic approach and uses the Person-Role Organization model, incorporating context and culture, with expertise in various coaching tools. He coaches individual executives as well as teams. He is also a certified Hogan Leadership assessor and accredited coach with the EMCC. He has been based in Japan for more than 20 years.

blocks.section: GUEST SPEAKERS
blocks.text: Anthony WILLOUGHBY Anthony was raised in Africa, vaguely schooled in the UK and arrived in Japan by boat in 1973, aged 22, at the end of the Trans-Siberian journey. He has now lived and worked in Japan for more than 35 years. Over the past five decades, his work has taken him on journeys and expeditions across Papua New Guinea, East Africa, Mongolia and many other parts of the world. He has spent time learning from Indigenous and traditional communities as well as working with young people, business leaders and organisations in very different environments. Forty years ago, drawing on these expediton experiences, Anthony founded one of Japan’s first outdoor leadership companies, built around journeys, expeditions and learning through experience. The company continues today. His work is now evolving around a question that has emerged from those journeys:

blocks.section: GUEST SPEAKERS
blocks.text: What makes people feel relevant?

blocks.section: GUEST SPEAKERS
blocks.text: What can we learn from the Maasai and other traditional societies about belonging, contribution, responsibility and knowing our place in a community and what might those lessons mean for how we live and work today?

blocks.section: GUEST SPEAKERS
blocks.text: Anthony believes that some of the oldest human instincts, understanding our territory, knowing what is worth protecting and growing, belonging to something larger than ourselves and having something meaningful to contribute may have much to teach us about being relevant in a rapidly changing world.

title: The Daruma Vision Workshop
description: A neuroscience-based workshop using Japanese rituals to help teams shift from doing to being, aligning goals through vision, reflection, and Daruma.

blocks.text: A neuroscience-based workshop using Japanese rituals to help teams shift from doing to being, aligning goals through vision, reflection, and Daruma.
THE DARUMA VISION WORKSHOP
Date: December 3, 2025 (Wed) | Time: 2 PM - 4:30 PM
KEY OBJECTIVES
Get clarity in ‘who you are’ and reinforce commitment to your goals.
Prime you brain for success with science-based approach.
Discover what truly drives your team, and see their potential.
The workshop blends Japanese cultural practices with a neuroscience-based approach to goal achievement.
Participants will engage in guided visualizations, reflective exercises, pair and group conversations with guided prompts, and a Daruma Doll ritual to anchor intentions.

It’s designed to engage leaders and their teams in a powerful team-building experience. Instead of planning every step and forcing more “doing,” you’ll learn to shift at the identity level, or “being”, letting your actions flow naturally.
WORKSHOP STRUCTURE:
Step 1: See The Leader Within Follow a guided visualization to see your success vividly and shift from “maybe” to “inevitable.”
Step 2: Celebrate Like It’s Done Pre-celebrate your wins with others to activate and prime your brain for success.
Step 3: Reverse-engineer Your Success Ask powerful questions to reverse-engineer your success and gain new insights.

Step 4: Anchor Your Intentions Fill in both eyes of the Daruma doll to commit fully to your goals. Step 5: Reflect and Integrate Wrap up with a reflection to absorb key insights and turn them into clear next steps.
Q&A
What is a Daruma?

Meet your power symbol: The DARUMA Doll. A Daruma is a traditional Japanese symbol of perseverance and goal-setting. One eye is typically drawn when setting a goal, the other once it's achieved. But in this workshop, you'll fill in BOTH EYES at once! This bold act will instantly boost your level of commitment. It will also anchor your intention in the present, no more waiting. It’s happening now.

What’s the science behind? This is how it works in simple terms. By visualizing success vividly, you’ll trigger dopamine and activate your brain’s Reticular Activating System (RAS) to spot opportunities aligned with your vision. The more you visualize and pre-celebrate, the stronger your belief and motivation become.
TARGET AUDIENCE
Suited for anyone looking to inspire, align, and empower their teams by starting with inner clarity and presence.
YOUR TRAINER
Lana SUVOROVA

Lana is a Certified Intelligence Coach and fully bilingual facilitator (Japanese, English) with 8 years of corporate experience at Mitsui & Co. and Amazon Japan, and 24 years of living in Japan. She helps leaders in high-pressure, diverse environments lead with heart by bringing more emotional intelligence into the workplace.
Certifications include:
ICF Associate Certified Coach (ACC)
Six Seconds Certified EQ Coach
NLP Master Practitioner
Client experience includes:
Mitsui & Co.,Ltd, Hogan Lovells, CCIFJ, NeuroLeadershio Institute

blocks.section: Guests of honor
blocks.text: Guests of honor

blocks.section: Guests of honor
blocks.text: Kyozo NAGATSUKA - Participation at the cocktail reception from 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM

blocks.section: Guests of honor
blocks.text: Born in Tokyo in 1945. While studying in France, he made his acting debut in the film Chinese in Paris (Les Chinois à Paris). Upon returning to Japan, he began his career in his home country in 1974 with the TBS television series Juhyō.

blocks.section: Guests of honor
blocks.text: In 1992, he played his first leading role in the film Za Chūgaku Kyōshi, for which he received the Best Actor Award at the Mainichi Film Awards. In 1997, his performance in Setouchi Moonlight Serenade earned him the Award of Excellence for Best Actor at the 21st Japan Academy Film Prize.

blocks.section: Guests of honor
blocks.text: In 2024, for his role in the film Teki he won the Best Actor Award at the 37th Tokyo International Film Festival, as well as the Award of Excellence for Best Actor at the 49th Japan Academy Film Prize.

blocks.section: Guests of honor
blocks.text: His notable works include Kin’yōbi no Tsumatachi e, Ai no Arashi, Gyakuten Bengoshi Yabuhara, Atsuhime, Kurara: Hokusai’s Daughter, and All of a Sudden.

blocks.section: Guests of honor
blocks.text: Hironobu TSUJIGUCHI (辻口 博啓) - Participation in the Talk-Show from 3:40 PM to 4:10 PM and the cocktail reception from 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM Will attend the talk show and the cocktail reception

blocks.section: Guests of honor
blocks.text: Renowned pastry chef and chocolatier Hironobu TSUJIGUCHI has represented Japan at some of the world's most prestigious international pastry competitions, including the Coupe du Monde de la Pâtisserie, where he has won numerous awards.

blocks.section: Guests of honor
blocks.text: He is the founder of Mont St. Clair in Jiyūgaoka, Tokyo, and oversees several brands, each with its own unique concept. In 2014, he opened his first overseas boutique, Mont St. Clair Seoul, in South Korea.

blocks.section: Guests of honor
blocks.text: At the prestigious Club des Croqueurs de Chocolat (C.C.C.) chocolate awards, presented annually during the Salon du Chocolat in Paris, his creations received the highest distinction for nine consecutive editions (2013–2018 and 2023–2025). In 2019, marking the competition's 25th anniversary, he received the Best of the Best Award, recognizing him as the finest chocolatier among all those previously honored by the Club des Croqueurs de Chocolat. In 2015, he also won the Gold Award in the Chocolate Bar category at the International Chocolate Awards – World Final.

blocks.section: Guests of honor
blocks.text: Beyond his work as a pastry chef, Hironobu TSUJIGUCHI is actively involved in regional revitalization through sweets, product development and collaborations with companies, consulting, public speaking, and publishing. Widely recognized as one of Japan's leading pioneers in low-sugar desserts, he has developed and supervised numerous low-carb ("locabo") confectionery creations.

blocks.section: Guests of honor
blocks.text: He also serves as Principal of the Super Sweets School in Ishikawa Prefecture and as President of the Japan Sweets Association, where he is dedicated to nurturing the next generation of pastry professionals and promoting Japan's pastry culture. The association administers the Sweets Concierge Certification and advocates the concept of "Sweets-iku," an educational approach that fosters personal development through the art of pastry making.

blocks.section: Guests of honor
blocks.text: In 2015, he served as pastry advisor for Mare, NHK's morning television drama series.

blocks.section: Guests of honor
blocks.text: In January 2019, the documentary LE CHOCOLAT DE H, which follows his creative journey and passion for chocolate, was released. The film was officially selected for screening at the 45th Seattle International Film Festival, held from May 16 to June 9, 2019.

blocks.section: Guests of honor
blocks.text: Tadashi AGI (亜樹直) - Participation in the talk show from 4:20 PM to 4:50 PM and the cocktail reception from 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM

blocks.section: Guests of honor
blocks.text: Tadashi AGI is the shared pen name used by a brother and sister, the writers behind numerous bestselling manga series, including The Drops of God and The Kindaichi Case Files .

blocks.section: Guests of honor
blocks.text: The Drops of God has been translated into French, Korean, Chinese (Taiwan), English, and several other languages, with more than 10 million copies sold worldwide. The series has enjoyed particular acclaim in France. In 2009, it was selected for the Official Selection of the Angoulême International Comics Festival and received the Hall of Fame Award at the Gourmand World Cookbook Awards, often referred to as the "Oscars" of cookbook publishing.

blocks.section: Guests of honor
blocks.text: In 2011, the brother-and-sister duo behind the pen name Tadashi AGI was appointed chevaliers de l'Ordre du Mérite agricole in recognition of their contribution to promoting French wine around the world. In 2018, they were appointed chevaliers de l'Ordre des Arts et des Lettres by the French government. In March 2026, they were promoted to the rank of officiers de l'Ordre du Mérite agricole.

blocks.section: Guests of honor
blocks.text: The live-action adaptation of The Drops of God , starring Tomohisa Yamashita and released in 2023, won the Best Drama Series award at the 52nd International Emmy Awards. The anime adaptation, released in 2025, has also enjoyed great success.

blocks.section: Guests of honor
blocks.text: Shin KIBAYASHI

blocks.section: Guests of honor
blocks.text: After graduating from the School of Political Science and Economics at Waseda University, Shin KIBAYASHI joined Kodansha Ltd. as a manga editor, where he played a key role in developing the stories of hit series such as Shoot! and GTO .

blocks.section: Guests of honor
blocks.text: Since becoming an independent writer, he has written under several pen names and created the original stories for numerous bestselling manga, including The Kindaichi Case Files , The Drops of God , and BLOODY MONDAY . He also conceived the television drama HERO and is the author of the Doctor White novel series (Kadokawa), which was adapted into a television drama in January 2022.

blocks.section: Guests of honor
blocks.text: In 2009, he became the first recipient from Asia to be inducted into the Hall of Fame at the Gourmand World Cookbook Awards, often referred to as the “Academy Awards of food publishing.”

blocks.section: Guests of honor
blocks.text: The French government has awarded him the rank of Officier de l’Ordre du Mérite agricole and Chevalier de l’Ordre des Arts et des Lettres in recognition of his contributions to gastronomy and culture.

blocks.section: Guests of honor
blocks.text: In addition, the French television adaptation of his signature work, The Drops of God , won the International Emmy Award in 2024.

blocks.section: Guests of honor
blocks.text: Yūko KIBAYASHI

blocks.section: Guests of honor
blocks.text: Born in Tokyo, Yūko KIBAYASHI is a manga writer as well as the author of nonfiction books and columns. Her nonfiction works include Akubi Ikkai, 40 En (Shogakukan), Matsumoto Kiyoshi-den: Sugu Yaru-ka o Tsukutta Otoko (Shogakukan), and Kigyōka-tachi no Tōkon: Jidai no Kaze o Yonda Dokusō Business (Nihon Jitsugyō Shuppansha).

blocks.section: Guests of honor
blocks.text: She is also the author of the medical reportage Byōki ni Naru Hito, Naranai Hito, Soshite Naoru Hito (Shogakukan).

blocks.section: Guests of honor
blocks.text: Her other publications include Kami no Shizuku Sakka no Nommelier Nikki , a collection of columns originally published intermittently on Asahi.com (Kodansha), and Kami no Shizuku Wine Shittaka Book (Shufu no Tomo Sha).

blocks.section: Guests of honor
blocks.text: Bebechan - Participation at the cocktail reception from 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM

blocks.section: Guests of honor
blocks.text: Bebechan is a French Youtuber, originally from Nice, living in Japan. His YouTube channel "Bebechan - French in Japan" has over 865 000 subscribers, and he has over one million followers on social media. He shares the charm of Japan and the wonders of Japanese culture through a French lens. Aiming to become a bridge between Japan and France, he is also developing activities focusing on the charms of both countries: in 2023 he published his first book, “French People Don't Say Bonjour.'', and in 2024, he opened a cake shop called “Charles-Henry” in Daikanyama, Tokyo.

title: Waseda Career Forum 2026

blocks.text: Organized by the CCIFJ, the Waseda Career Forum offers companies an excellent opportunity to set up an exhibition booth on the Waseda University campus and fully showcase their corporate appeal to globally-minded students.

Scheduled for Thursday, December 10, 2026, this forum is expected to attract a large number of outstanding bilingual individuals from both Japan and abroad, including Waseda University students and those with a strong interest in foreign-affiliated companies and global careers.
We are currently accepting applications for exhibiting companies.

The forum brings together a wide range of students, from undergraduates to graduate students and recent graduates, whose primary goals include preparing for internships, career development, and active job hunting.
By directly promoting your company's vision and corporate culture, you can resonate deeply with students, thereby ensuring a strong cultural fit.

Every year, Japanese students enrolled in domestic and international universities, as well as bilingual students ready to thrive globally, gather in one place. This year, we aim to further increase the participation of native Japanese students.
We are planning further enhancements to ensure this event serves as a wonderful venue for connecting with exceptional talent.
Past Participating Institutions Include:

Waseda University, Keio University, University of Tokyo, Hitotsubashi University, Sophia University, Ochanomizu University, Rikkyo University, Hosei University, Ibaraki University, Temple University Japan Campus, Shinjuku Japanese Language School (SNG), ISI Language College
A dedicated exhibition booth during the forum
A 10-minute corporate presentation slot to the entire venue (optional for interested companies)
Publication of company profiles in event promotional materials
Due to high demand every year, the number of exhibition booths is limited. Applications are accepted on a first-come, first-served basis, so please reserve your spot early.
Direct access to global talent and outstanding students
Increase corporate awareness and strengthen your employer brand
Access to talent aligned with your recruitment needs

blocks.section: Membership categories:

blocks.section: Membership categories:
blocks.text: Highest membership status for the members wishing to have a significant impact of the French-Japanese business community while showing their investment and support to the CCIFJ . This status grants exclusive services, maximum exposure and personalized solutions.

blocks.section: Membership categories:
blocks.text: Annual membership fee: 650.000 yens

blocks.section: Membership categories:
blocks.text: (From 1 st of January to 31 st of December)

blocks.section: Membership categories:
blocks.text: STATUS BENEFITS

blocks.section: Membership categories:
blocks.text: Start-up membership is an ideal choice for small and young companies that wish to develop their activities, take advantage of the CCI France Japon services and benefit from a dynamic business network and community. This status is reserved for companies with less than 3 years of existence, for the first two years of membership.

blocks.section: Membership categories:
blocks.text: Annual membership fee: 140.000 yens

blocks.section: Membership categories:
blocks.text: (From 1st of January to 31st of December) STATUS BENEFITS

blocks.section: Membership categories:
blocks.text: Dedicated membership status for individual and independent professionals wishing to expand their business network. Individual members can participate in all events organized by the CCI France Japon. This status is reserved to freelancers, micro-structures or retired people.

blocks.section: Membership categories:
blocks.text: Annual membership fee: 80.000 yens

blocks.section: Membership categories:
blocks.text: (From 1st of January to 31st of December)

blocks.section: Membership categories:
blocks.text: BENEFITS STATUS

blocks.section: Membership categories:
blocks.text: Active membership is aimed to companies that are looking to increase their visibility, develop strong partnerships with the French-Japanese business community while being fully involved in all of the activities of the CCI France Japon.

blocks.section: Membership categories:
blocks.text: Annual membership fee: 295.000 yens

blocks.section: Membership categories:
blocks.text: (From 1st of January to 31st of December)

blocks.section: Membership categories:
blocks.text: STATUS BENEFITS

blocks.section: Membership categories:
blocks.text: Regional membership is an ideal choice for companies based in regional areas that do not have a branch in the Tokyo metropolis. CCI France Japon Kansai, Kyushu, Chubu, Gunma, and Fukui support your business and international expansion locally, in coordination with the Tokyo Chamber. This status is reserved for companies that do not have an office or permanent staff in the prefectures of Tokyo, Chiba, Saitama, or Kanagawa.

blocks.section: Membership categories:
blocks.text: Annual membership fee: 150.000 yens

blocks.section: Membership categories:
blocks.text: (From 1st of January to 31st of December)

blocks.section: Membership categories:
blocks.text: STATUS BENEFITS

blocks.section: Membership categories:
blocks.text: This status allows companies and individual persons that are not located in Japan to non-resident be affiliated with CCI France Japon activities.

blocks.section: Membership categories:
blocks.text: Annual membership fee: 550 €

blocks.section: The French Chamber in Fukui
blocks.text: As part of its commitment to strengthening economic ties between France and Japan, the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCIFJ) has opened a new branch at the Koshino Valley Innovation Centre in Fukui. This new addition aims to support French, international, and Japanese companies in the region. Easily accessible from Tokyo and Osaka, Fukui is a dynamic area that now benefits from the Hokuriku Shinkansen line.

blocks.text: The French Chamber in Gunma

blocks.section: The French Chamber in Gunma
blocks.text: As part of its commitment to strengthening economic ties between France and Japan, the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCI France Japon) has opened a branch office in Gunma. This dynamic region, located about 100 km from Tokyo, plays a key role in industries such as automotive and metallurgy, with companies like Michelin, Subaru, and Danone. The branch aims to enhance economic partnerships, support local businesses, and promote the expansion of French companies in the Japanese market.

blocks.section: Honorary committee
blocks.text: The CCI France Japon set up in January 2001 a "Franco-Japanese Strategic Committee". Renamed as "Honorary Committee" in 2007, as part of its rapprochement with the Japanese business community, it aims to strengthen economic and commercial relations between our two countries, dispensing advice and guidance on the development of the Franco-Japanese bilateral relationship. This Committee was relaunched in 2013 at the instigation of Hisataka Nobumoto, Vice-President of the CCI France Japon, with new high-ranking Japanese personalities.

blocks.section: Les données que vous nous communiquez
blocks.text: Pour le formulaire d’inscription à notre newsletter, nous vous demandons votre adresse email afin de pouvoir vous communiquer notre lettre d’information France Japon Express ainsi que votre nom. Les autres champs ne sont pas obligatoires pour la validation du formulaire, vous êtes libre de ne pas les renseigner.

blocks.section: Les données que vous nous communiquez
blocks.text: Concernant l’inscription à un événement, votre nom, prénom et civilité permettent de dresser notre liste d’inscription à l’événement. Votre email nous permet de vous communiquer les différentes informations relatives à l’événement. Par exemple votre confirmation d’inscription, des reminders, un compte rendu de l’événement ou bien encore un questionnaire de satisfaction. Le nom de votre entreprise et votre fonction nous permettent d’en savoir plus sur votre profil et pourquoi vous êtes intéressés par notre événement. De plus il est possible que certains événements ne soit réservé qu’à une catégorie précise de personnes, ou bien adressé à un secteur particulier.

blocks.section: Les données que vous nous communiquez
blocks.text: Pour le formulaire de création de compte à l’espace privé, votre adresse email sera votre identifiant pour accéder à votre espace-privé. En plus de cela, il nous permettra de vous contacter ou de vous envoyer les informations de la Chambre si vous avez manifesté le souhait de les recevoir. En effet, nous vous solliciterons par mail uniquement si vous nous avez donné votre accord. Concernant la civilité, nom et prénom, ces informations nous permettent d’en savoir un peu plus sur vous et de vous préparer des communications personnalisées. Dans le formulaire, ces champs ne sont pas obligatoires pour vous créer un espace privé. Vous êtes donc libres de ne pas les renseigner si vous ne le souhaitez pas.

blocks.section: Les données que nous récoltons à partir de votre parcours sur notre site
blocks.text: Nous récoltons des données relatives à votre parcours sur notre site internet, ces données nous permettent d’optimiser nos contenus et d’améliorer votre expérience utilisateur. Les données récupérées sont toutes anonymes et globales, nous ne récupérons pas d’adresse IP. Elles sont obtenues grâce à des cookies qui sont déposés dans votre navigateur à votre arrivée sur notre site.

blocks.section: Les données que nous récoltons à partir de votre parcours sur notre site
blocks.text: Pour en savoir plus sur les cookies déposés lors d’une visite sur notre site, vous pouvez suivre ce lien.

blocks.section: Les données que nous récoltons à partir de votre parcours sur notre site
blocks.text: Si vous souhaitez supprimer les cookies enregistrés sur votre terminal et paramétrer votre navigateur pour refuser les cookies, vous pouvez le faire via les préférences de votre navigateur internet. Ces options de navigation relatives aux cookies se trouvent habituellement dans les menus « Options », « Outils » ou « Préférences ».

blocks.section: Les données que nous récoltons à partir de votre parcours sur notre site
blocks.text: Veuillez noter que si vous désactivez l’enregistrement de cookies sur votre terminal, certaines parties et fonctionnalités du site internet pourraient ne pas fonctionner correctement.

blocks.section: Les données que nous récoltons à partir de votre parcours sur notre site
blocks.text: Ces données nous permettent d’en savoir plus sur le parcours des utilisateurs sur notre site et nous permet d’améliorer nos contenus et la qualité de service que nous pouvons vous délivrer. Ces données sont complétement anonymisées, c’est-à-dire que nous n’avons aucun moyen de lier une action sur notre site à une personne nomée.

blocks.section: Les données sensibles
blocks.text: Nous ne collectons aucune donnée dite « sensible ». C’est-à-dire des données relatives à l’origine raciale ou ethnique, aux opinions politiques, philosophiques ou religieuses, à l’appartenance syndicale, à la santé ou à l’orientation sexuelle.

blocks.section: Le droit à la rectification
blocks.text: Vous avez le droit d’obtenir la rectification des données à caractère personnel vous concernant si celles si sont inexactes. De plus, vous avez le droit d’obtenir que vos données à caractère personnel incomplètes soient complétées, en nous fournissant une déclaration complémentaire.

blocks.section: Le droit à l’oubli
blocks.text: Le droit à l’oubli

blocks.section: Le droit à l’oubli
blocks.text: À tout moment, vous pouvez exiger de notre part la suppression de vos données à caractère personnel. Votre demande sera traitée dans les meilleurs délais et vos données seront supprimés si leur traitement n’est pas nécessaire aux cas suivants :

blocks.section: Le droit à l’oubli
blocks.text: - Pour respecter une obligation légale qui requiert le traitement prévu par le droit de l'Union ou par le droit de l'État membre auquel le responsable du traitement est soumis, ou pour exécuter une mission d'intérêt public ou relevant de l'exercice de l'autorité publique dont est investi le responsable du traitement ;

blocks.section: Le droit à l’oubli
blocks.text: - À la constatation, à l'exercice ou à la défense de droits en justice.

blocks.section: Le droit à l’oubli
blocks.text: Pour toutes nos communications qui vous sont envoyées par mail, vous avez la possibilité de vous désinscrire de notre liste de diffusion depuis le lien de désabonnement présent dans ces messages.

blocks.section: 2025, année zéro de la nouvelle mobilité
blocks.text: Autonomie, électrification, partage : les trois briques fondatrices de la nouvelle mobilité automobile se mettent en place. Le Japon est bien sûr concerné au premier plan. Certains des meilleurs experts du sujet, japonais et étrangers, hauts fonctionnaires et cadres, intellectuels et amateurs éclairés, se sont réunis le 15 avril à L’Espace de la CCI France Japon pour en discuter à l’occasion de la conférence annuelle Mobility . Ces échanges, passionnants, sont à retrouver dans FJE 182. Pour bien aborder le virage de cette nouvelle ère, lisez-le !

blocks.section: 2025, année zéro de la nouvelle mobilité
blocks.text: Aussi dans FJE 182 : un reportage dans Gunma, le (nouveau) département qui monte au Japon ; une analyse des nouvelles routes de l’industrie touristique ; une autre des progrès spectaculaires du capital-investissement au Japon ; l’histoire inédite d’un rapprochement entre Arcelor et Nippon Steel, ; le retour du festival du cinéma de Yokohama sur le devant de la scène... Enfin, vous saurez tout sur l’actualité de la CCI France Japon et de votre communauté d’affaires.

blocks.section: A vos marques, prêts, Japon !
blocks.text: Le Japon n’est pas seulement une puissance industrielle, culturelle, économique et financière : c’est aussi une puissance sportive . Arrivé troisième aux deux derniers Jeux olympiques, il s’impose dans de plus en plus de disciplines : non seulement base-ball et sumo mais désormais football, rugby, volleyball, basketball, escrime et d’autres.

blocks.section: A vos marques, prêts, Japon !
blocks.text: Ces performances ont d’authentiques retombées. La construction d’infrastructures bat son plein. Les athlètes deviennent des objets de marketing. Les droits de diffusion des compétitions augmentent. Mais le sport au Japon n’est pas encore la locomotive économique qu’elle est devenue dans certains pays. L’hospitalité autour des compétitions en est à ses balbutiements, par exemple. Ces carences font du Japon un marché très prometteur pour des entrants étrangers. C’est pourquoi France Japon Eco fait le point sur le sport au Japon dans sa dernière édition.

blocks.section: A vos marques, prêts, Japon !
blocks.text: Dans ce numéro également : le récit de la fusion Nikon Essilor racontée par Xavier Fontanet, son principal architecte ; un reportage et une analyse de l’ouverture (timide) du Japon à l’armement européen ; un compte-rendu des récents événements les plus marquants de la CCI. Et bien d’autres choses encore !

blocks.section: Automobile : les voies de la mobilité
blocks.text: Autonomie, motorisation, autopartage... sur tous ces thèmes, le Japon suit son propre chemin. Voie d’avenir ou voie sans issue ? Dans France Japon Eco, les principaux acteurs au Japon de cette transformation (Alfonso Albaisa de Nissan, Keisuke Onishi de Navitime, Yoshiaki Aoki de MK Taxi West Japan, et bien d’autres) s’expriment. Ils partagent leurs expériences, comparent la troisième économie du monde aux autres, bref remettent leur rapport d’étape.

blocks.section: Automobile : les voies de la mobilité
blocks.text: À découvrir aussi dans le magazine : le réveil du marché du parfum japonais ; la naissance d’un marché de l’art au Japon ; le redécollage du Salon du Bourget ; l’histoire incroyable de l’amour des Japonais pour la Romanée Conti...

blocks.section: L'automobile numérisée
blocks.text: L’automobile est-elle en train de devenir un « téléphone sur roues » ? L’autonomisation de la conduite, l’électrification de la propulsion, les services à bord transforment nos voitures en ordinateurs roulants. Imaginée par la collaboration d’industries (électronique, automobile, média...), la voiture, symbole de l’émancipation individuelle, est aussi la pièce d’un système de transports « intelligent », où les désirs de l’usager sont exaucés mais aussi devancés. À quoi ressemble le nouveau paysage automobile au Japon ? Les meilleurs experts et praticiens du secteur y répondent dans France Japon Éco.

blocks.section: L'automobile numérisée
blocks.text: Aussi dans France Japon Éco : un reportage sur le jockey Christophe Lemaire, le Français le plus populaire du pays ; une étude de l’« activation » de l’énorme épargne japonaise ; une analyse de la mise en circulation de nouveaux billets de banque ; une autre de l’immigration de travail, à l’aune d’un rapport historique de l’OCDE ; enfin une interview-choc de Kazuhito Yamashita, grand spécialiste du riz japonais.

blocks.section: L'automobile numérisée
blocks.text: France Japon Éco, c’est aussi l’enthousiasmante actualité des entreprises membres, nouvelles et anciennes, de la CCI France Japon, cœur battant de la relation franco-japonaise.

blocks.section: Quelques idées d’avenir
blocks.text: Chaque année, la CCI France Japon réunit chefs d’entreprise et leaders d’opinion dans le cadre de son Business Leaders Forum , offrant une photographie actuelle de l’Archipel : points d’excellence, points faibles, en tout cas opportunités. La variété des sujets traités en novembre 2024 reflète la diversité de l’économie japonaise : innovation, tourisme, énergie, intelligence artificielle... Retrouvez ces « idées d’avenir » dans notre édition 181. Aussi : Taikan Oki, expert mondial de l’eau, nous livre son analyse sur le Japon et cette ressource indispensable. Jean-Marc Peillex, légendaire maire de Saint-Gervais-les-Bains, nous raconte son voyage d’étude dans les montagnes japonaises. Ali Ordoobadi, de Valeo, revient sur 17 ans de carrière au Japon et donne sa vision de l’avenir de l’industrie automobile. Dans France Japon Eco enfin, nous tirons la sonnette d’alarme sur le pitoyable niveau d’anglais pratiqué au Japon, source de frustration pour les Japonais comme pour les étrangers. Enfin, vous saurez tout sur l’actualité de la CCI France Japon et de ses membres, bien sûr.

blocks.section: Ressources humaines : comme vous nous manquez
blocks.text: Les ressources humaines sont devenues la première préoccupation des entreprises au Japon. Du directeur de filiale au plâtrier, de l’informaticien au serveur, tous les postes sont à pourvoir. Le Japon est entraîné dans une spirale de baisse démographique qui siphonne sa population active. L’« armée de réserve » de femmes et de personnes âgées ainsi que la main d’œuvre immigrée ont permis de ralentir ce phénomène depuis dix ans ; pas de l’endiguer, ni de le retourner. Les entreprises doivent désormais « organiser cette pénurie » de main-d’œuvre, qui s’impose progressivement à toutes les économies, proches (Taiwan, la Corée du Sud…) ou lointaine (Italie, France…)

blocks.section: Ressources humaines : comme vous nous manquez
blocks.text: Dans quels secteurs la pénurie est-elle la plus criante ? Comment le Japon s’adapte-t-il ? Pourquoi l’offre de ressources humaines, de moins en moins satisfaisante au vu de la demande, ne se traduit-elle pas par une hausse des salaires ? France Japon Eco répond à ces questions en interrogeant les acteurs de terrain.

blocks.section: Ressources humaines : comme vous nous manquez
blocks.text: Dans FJE 186 encore, nous revenons sur la visite d’Emmanuel Macron au Japon et sur ses conséquences à court et moyen terme. Nous analysons l’autorisation du Japon d’exporter des armes létales, tournant symbolique dans sa politique étrangère et de défense. Nous publions un cahier sur l’avancée (lente) du véhicule autonome, et sa signification pour le marché automobile japonais.

blocks.section: Ressources humaines : comme vous nous manquez
blocks.text: Dans FJE 186 toujours, nous vous présentons ceux qui ont choisi le Japon, que ce soit pour s’y installer (rubrique La relève ), ou pour un voyage d’observation (rubrique Les visiteurs ).

blocks.section: Rêves japonais
blocks.text: Chaque année, le Business Summit de la CCI France Japon est l’occasion de rencontrer quelques-uns des acteurs, étrangers et locaux, de l’économie et de la société japonaise. L’édition 2025 a une fois encore été riche en talents de toutes origines. Robotique, finance, sports, tech… Réformistes ou « gardiens de temple », tout le monde se retrouve au Business Summit. Nous reproduisons quelques-unes de leurs interventions les plus intéressantes.

blocks.section: Rêves japonais
blocks.text: Dans le 184, nous revenons aussi sur la TICAD, sommet Afrique-Japon dans laquelle la France a une place particulière. Nous faisons le point sur les conséquences du yen bas, et vous présentons Shuhei Abe, une des figures de la finance japonaise. La nouvelle génération de décideurs au Japon a aussi toujours sa place – dans la rubrique « La relève ». Nous racontons aussi le geste de Louis Schweitzer, figure-clé de la relation franco-japonaise, avec des anecdotes exclusives. Le Japon n’a pas été une étape mais un fil rouge de sa vie et de sa carrière, comme beaucoup de lecteurs de FJE.

blocks.section: Rêves japonais
blocks.text: Enfin le Japon accueille de plus en plus de chefs d’entreprise, curieux de prospecter davantage ce marché. Ils font très fréquemment escale à la CCI France Japon. Nous avons créé pour eux une nouvelle rubrique, qui renseigne le lecteur sur la place du Japon dans le monde.

blocks.section: Yen, où vas-tu ?
blocks.text: FJE 185 : yen, où vas-tu ?

blocks.section: Yen, où vas-tu ?
blocks.text: Le sujet du yen a toujours occupé une place disproportionnée dans la vie des affaires au Japon. Ses mouvements en yo-yo obligent les entreprises (pour leurs coûts et leurs marges) et les particuliers (pour leurs achats de biens importés, pour leurs voyages à l’étranger…) à des arbitrages constants.

blocks.section: Yen, où vas-tu ?
blocks.text: Mais depuis l’épidémie de COVID, la monnaie japonaise s’est durablement installée à un niveau historiquement bas. France Japon Eco a interrogé chefs d’entreprise et particuliers pour comprendre les effets de cette situation sur leurs activités, et s’il est souhaitable qu’elle cesse.

blocks.section: Yen, où vas-tu ?
blocks.text: Aussi dans FJE : une interview exclusive de l’ambassadrice de France au Japon. Peu de temps après son arrivée, Béatrice le Fraper du Hellen a bien voulu nous recevoir quelques jours avant la visite du Président de la République Emmanuel Macron au Japon. Elle nous explique comment passer, selon son expression, d’un « partenariat d’exception » à un « partenariat exceptionnel », en profitant d’un nouveau coup de projecteur, cette fois politique, sur le Japon.

blocks.section: Yen, où vas-tu ?
blocks.text: Toujours dans FJE : l’interview exclusive de Takuji Aida. L’un des économistes les plus influents du Japon expose la politique économique de la nouvelle Première ministre Sanae Takaichi. Une lecture essentielle pour comprendre la politique économique en train de se dessiner.

blocks.section: Yen, où vas-tu ?
blocks.text: FJE vous explique aussi la réforme prochaine du shopping duty free dans ce maillon essentiel du secteur qu’est le Japon : un quart des ventes mondiales de duty free a lieu ici.

blocks.section: Transformation énergétique : rapport d'étape
blocks.text: Le Japon est sur le point de publier sa nouvelle feuille de route énergétique, qui pavera la voie vers son objectif « zéro CO 2 d’ici 2050, avec une importante étape en 2030. Grâce aux témoignages exclusifs des acteurs de terrain membres de la CCI France Japon et à leurs collaborateurs (entreprises externes, représentants des administrations concernées), FJE vous offre une analyse originale de l’état d’avancement des progrès sur ce dossier majeur, en le comparant notamment avec la situation française.

blocks.section: Transformation énergétique : rapport d'étape
blocks.text: Aussi dans FJE 180 : les dessous de la reprise du réseau aéroportuaire du Kansai par Vinci Airports et son partenaire Orix à l’occasion des trente ans de l’aéroport KIX ; une analyse des défis de l’industrie logistique, si excellente jusqu’ici ; un reportage dans les rayons de Seibu Ikebukuro, grand magasin légendaire en pleine rénovation ; une brève histoire de l’innovation dans l’industrie pharmaceutique japonaise – et ses travers actuels. Enfin une analyse sur l’étrange absence de compte commun parmi la panoplie des services bancaires au Japon. Et l’actualité de la CCI France Japon bien sûr.

title: National Travel Discount - Share your offer
description: Japan launched its new domestic travel subsidy program from Oct. 11 to late December as part of efforts to spur domestic tourism and revive the coronavirus-hit economy.

blocks.section: National Travel Discount - Share your offer
blocks.text: National Travel Discount - Share your offer

blocks.section: National Travel Discount - Share your offer
blocks.text: Japan launched its new domestic travel subsidy program from Oct. 11 to late December as part of efforts to spur domestic tourism and revive the coronavirus-hit economy.

blocks.section: National Travel Discount - Share your offer
blocks.text: The "National Travel Discount" offers a 40% discount on travel costs, up to a maximum of 8,000 yen/person per night for a trip using public transportation (train/subway, bus, airplane, etc.) and 5,000 yen for a trip other than that (without using public transport or accommodation only), with local coupons that can be used at restaurants, souvenir shops, etc. worth 3,000 yen on weekdays and 1,000 yen on weekends.

blocks.section: National Travel Discount - Share your offer
blocks.text: The National Travel Discount program, which is available to Japan residents only, comes in the wake of the "Go To Travel" subsidy program and expands on similar existing programs operating at the prefectural level.

title: 100 days to go to Rugby World Cup France 2023! Japan joins top ranked teams

blocks.text: Companies news

blocks.section: 100 days to go to Rugby World Cup France 2023! Japan joins top ranked teams
blocks.text: 100 days to go to Rugby World Cup France 2023! Japan joins top ranked teams

blocks.section: 100 days to go to Rugby World Cup France 2023! Japan joins top ranked teams
blocks.text: The countdown is on to Rugby World Cup France 2023 with 31 May marking 100 days to go to the start of the tournament on September 8! This will be the 10th Rugby World Cup since the first tournament which was jointly hosted by New Zealand and Australia in 1987. This year also marks a milestone in the history of rugby with 200 years since the birth of the sport in 1823 when William Ellis of “Rugby School” in England first ran with the ball in his hand during a football game.

blocks.section: 100 days to go to Rugby World Cup France 2023! Japan joins top ranked teams
blocks.text: In the past, the Japanese national team suffered a devastating defeat of 145 - 17 at the third Rugby World Cup against the All Blacks, however at the tournament in 2015 the team's tenacious comeback to victory over the mighty South African team prompted head coach Eddie Jones to proclaim "The world has changed”. In addition, the team accomplished its elusive goal of finishing in the top eight at the last tournament in 2019.

blocks.section: 100 days to go to Rugby World Cup France 2023! Japan joins top ranked teams
blocks.text: Japan's national team has been steadily gaining international recognition and has been classified as a "Tier 2" nation, however the international governing body World Rugby (WR) has reorganized the framework of the 10 "Tier 1" nations to create a "High Performance Union" of 11 teams, including Japan. This is indeed very exciting news for Japan.

blocks.section: 100 days to go to Rugby World Cup France 2023! Japan joins top ranked teams
blocks.text: Current candidates for this tournament to keep an eye out for include veterans such as captain Atsushi Sakate and Michael Leitch, as well as youngsters like 22 year old Warner Dearns of New Zealand, who stands at over 2 meters tall and scored a spectacular try against the All Blacks last year. Others include another 22 year old, tough fly-half Seungsin Lee and 24 year old flanker Koji Shimokawa, who’s situational judgment is outstanding. The level of talent continues to grow with each game and expectations are high for the future and further growth of these young players.

blocks.section: 100 days to go to Rugby World Cup France 2023! Japan joins top ranked teams
blocks.text: Will the Japanese team in their cherry blossom jerseys once again show their strength and courage in front of rugby fans around the world? And which country will take home the coveted Webb Ellis Cup? We can’t wait to see what Rugby World Cup has in store for us!

blocks.section: 100 days to go to Rugby World Cup France 2023! Japan joins top ranked teams

title: 12th consecutive monthly decline in consumer spending
description: In Japan, consumer spending fell by 0.5% in February 2024.

blocks.text: Foresight

blocks.section: 12th consecutive monthly decline in consumer spending
blocks.text: 12th consecutive monthly decline in consumer spending

blocks.section: 12th consecutive monthly decline in consumer spending
blocks.text: In Japan, consumer spending fell by 0.5% in February 2024.

blocks.section: 12th consecutive monthly decline in consumer spending
blocks.text: According to a survey published on April 5 by the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications, consumer spending by households of two or more people totaled 279,868 yen, down 0.5% in real terms from the previous year (excluding the effect of price changes), marking the 12th consecutive monthly decline.

title: 2020 French Japanese Business Summit video
description:
Held on November 18th at the Nikkei Hall in Tokyo, the 3rd edition of the French Japanese Business Summit drew almost 550 delegates from Africa, France and Japan.
This year’s theme was: “Growth opportunities in Africa: towards new partnerships”. Delegates heard from an our lineup of panelists and keynote speakers including CEOs, government officials, industry leaders, researchers and professors on the themes that will define the future of economic and business relations between France, Japan and Africa.
During the day, 25 top level speakers from Europe and Japan shared their operational experience in Africa, their challenges (climate change, COVID19), and their vision.
Among the many prestigious speakers: M. Ashwani GUPTA, Director representative executive officer, chief operating officer NISSAN motors, Oussouby SACKO, President of the Kyoto Seika University, OSHIMA Masahiko, Deputy president Head of SMBC, MUTO Megumi Deputy Director, Ogata Sadako research Institute for Peace and Dev. at JICA or Lionel ZINSOU Managing Partner of Southbridge, Former Prime Minister of Benin.  See you on November 9, 2021 for our next French Japanese Business Summit!

title: 45th Gala Dinner of CCI France Japon in Tokyo: A Celebration of French Gastronomy
description:
We are pleased to announce that the 2023 CCI France Japon Tokyo Gala Party will take place on Thursday, November 9th, at 18:00, at the Grand Prince Hotel Shintakanawa.
Every year since 1978, the Tokyo Gala Party celebrates gastronomy, culture, and French art de vivre. This year will be organized in partnership with Paris Region. 
We are pleased to welcome three chefs from Paris this year. Nicolas Beauman from the two-Michelin-starred restaurant "Maison Rostang," Matthias Marc from the one-Michelin-starred restaurant "Substance," and Tom Meyer from "Granite," who has earned one Michelin star and received the MOF (Meilleur Ouvrier de France) title. Coordinated by Eclore group, the three chefs will collaborate to create a special menu exclusively for this one-night event.
The 2023 Tokyo Gala Party will be a unique evening for everyone to remember.
We look forward to seeing you on November 9th, 2023!
