title: Discovering the craftsmanship of Aritaya, an artisan soy sauce brewer.
description: On 22 May 2026, the CCIFJ organised a company visit to Aritaya, a soy sauce brewer located in Gunma Prefecture.

blocks.text: Gunma Event report

blocks.section: Discovering the craftsmanship of Aritaya, an artisan soy sauce brewer.
blocks.text: Discovering the craftsmanship of Aritaya, an artisan soy sauce brewer.

blocks.section: Discovering the craftsmanship of Aritaya, an artisan soy sauce brewer.
blocks.text: On 22 May 2026, the CCIFJ organised a company visit to Aritaya, a soy sauce brewer located in Gunma Prefecture.

blocks.section: Discovering the craftsmanship of Aritaya, an artisan soy sauce brewer.
blocks.text: On 22 May, the Gunma Office held its first event of the year. On this occasion, participants had the opportunity to visit Aritaya, a member company of the CCIFJ located in the city of Annaka.

blocks.section: Discovering the craftsmanship of Aritaya, an artisan soy sauce brewer.
blocks.text: The event began with a tour of Aritaya’s facilities in a warm and friendly atmosphere. Mr Yuasa Kohki, representing the seventh generation of the family business, introduced us to the company’s craftsmanship as well as one of its signature products: a naturally brewed soy sauce matured in the Usui Tunnel. This product perfectly reflects the company’s philosophy of developing unique flavours rooted in the local terroir, shaped by Annaka’s climate and distinctive micro-organisms.

blocks.section: Discovering the craftsmanship of Aritaya, an artisan soy sauce brewer.
blocks.text: The visit continued with a workshop organised by the Annaka Tourism Association, during which participants had the opportunity to press their own soy sauce in an atmosphere filled with curiosity and enthusiasm.

blocks.section: Discovering the craftsmanship of Aritaya, an artisan soy sauce brewer.
blocks.text: The event then concluded with a tasting session featuring dishes specially prepared for the occasion, carefully paired with two soy sauce specialities: firstly, koikuchi, brewed from whole soybeans and fermented in a single stage; secondly, saishikomi, which undergoes a double fermentation process.

blocks.section: Discovering the craftsmanship of Aritaya, an artisan soy sauce brewer.
blocks.text: We would like to extend our sincere thanks to Aritaya for their warm welcome and kindness throughout the day.

blocks.section: Discovering the craftsmanship of Aritaya, an artisan soy sauce brewer.
blocks.text: Many thanks as well to all the participants for their enthusiasm and cheerful spirit.

blocks.section: Discovering the craftsmanship of Aritaya, an artisan soy sauce brewer.
blocks.text: We look forward to seeing you again at future events in Gunma.

title: A Memorable Sake Event in Collaboration with Shimizu Seizaburo and Special Guest Sonia Bichet

blocks.text: Chubu Event report

blocks.section: A Memorable Sake Event in Collaboration with Shimizu Seizaburo and Special Guest Sonia Bichet
blocks.text: A Memorable Sake Event in Collaboration with Shimizu Seizaburo and Special Guest Sonia Bichet

blocks.section: A Memorable Sake Event in Collaboration with Shimizu Seizaburo and Special Guest Sonia Bichet
blocks.text: On Saturday, June 15th, we had the pleasure of hosting an event in collaboration with Shimizu Seizaburo , a renowned sake brewery located in Suzuka, Mie Prefecture . We welcomed a special guest, Sonia Bichet , a MOF ( Meilleur Ouvrier de France ) Fishmonger, known for her exceptional skills at just 29 years old.

blocks.section: Brewery Tour and Sake Tasting
blocks.text: Brewery Tour and Sake Tasting

blocks.section: Brewery Tour and Sake Tasting
blocks.text: The event started with an insightful tour of the brewery, allowing attendees to explore the production and bottling site of the celebrated Zaku sake bottles, notably winning the prestigious Kura Master competition in 2021 , among many other accolades.

blocks.section: Brewery Tour and Sake Tasting
blocks.text: Following the tour, we enjoyed a sake-tasting session, perfectly paired with delicious oysters from Mie provided by the MOF and Shimizu Seizaburo’s local partners. In a traditional toast inspired by the fishermen of Mie, we poured a bit of sake into an oyster shell, raised it to the sky, and said "Kanpai!" before savoring the delicious combination.

blocks.section: Demonstration by Sonia Bichet
blocks.text: Demonstration by Sonia Bichet

blocks.section: Demonstration by Sonia Bichet
blocks.text: The highlight of the event was undoubtedly the demonstration by Sonia Bichet. Participants eagerly gathered around her table, where freshly shucked oysters were served. Throughout the event, Sonia's warmth and enthusiasm were evident as she passionately answered questions and shared her journey.

blocks.section: Demonstration by Sonia Bichet
blocks.text: Sonia has been traveling the world (15 countries) for the past nine months, sharing her passion with younger generations and experiencing different fishing cultures. Despite the exhaustion from her extensive travels, including an incredible immersion with the Ama divers of Toba , Sonia's energy and charm quickly put everyone at ease. She not only showcases her often-stigmatized profession but also highlights the universal and borderless sharing of cuisine, enabling her to share her passion in any country.

blocks.section: Conclusion
blocks.text: Conclusion

blocks.section: Conclusion
blocks.text: I am grateful to Shimizu Seizaburo, Sonia Bichet, and all our participants for making this event unforgettable! Stay tuned for many more enriching events to come!

title: Accor and Bureau Veritas have joined forces to develop a new label
description: The new label is based on sanitary measures to support the return to business in the hospitality and restaurant industry

blocks.text: Companies news

blocks.section: Accor and Bureau Veritas have joined forces to develop a new label
blocks.text: Accor and Bureau Veritas have joined forces to develop a new label

blocks.section: Accor and Bureau Veritas have joined forces to develop a new label
blocks.text: The new label is based on sanitary measures to support the return to business in the hospitality and restaurant industry

blocks.section: Accor and Bureau Veritas have joined forces to develop a new label
blocks.text: Accor and Bureau Veritas, a world-leading provider in testing, inspection and certification, launched a label designed to certify that the appropriate safety standards and cleaning protocols have been achieved to allow businesses to reopen.

blocks.section: Accor and Bureau Veritas have joined forces to develop a new label
blocks.text: The label will cover both accommodation and catering, and will set the sanitary standards applicable to all the Group’s hotels as well as to other chains and independent hotels. The project was carried out in partnership with doctors and epidemiologists, and has been developed in collaboration with Accor owners and trade associations, such as UMIH, GNC, and GNI.

blocks.section: Accor and Bureau Veritas have joined forces to develop a new label
blocks.text: The project will be shared next week within Alliance France Tourisme as well as with the relevant ministries (French Ministries of Tourism, Health and Labor) so that they are actively involved in – and validate – the recommended standards. Concrete proposals will be submitted, in France and subsequently in Europe, to the various governments, relevant ministries and committees for the easing of lockdown measures. Concretely, the output of this effort will be an operational guide made available to all stakeholders in the hospitality industry, enabling them to rigorously apply the health and safety recommendation of authories (WHO, Health Ministry etc), both in guest services spaces and in back office and catering spaces. European customers will be able to check on a dedicated Bureau Veritas website, before they book their next stay whether any hotel or restaurant has been certified or not by Bureau Veritas.

blocks.section: Accor and Bureau Veritas have joined forces to develop a new label
blocks.text: Franck GERVAIS, CEO Europe Accor, said, "Welcoming, protecting and taking care of others is the very DNA of Accor and at the heart of what we do. Today, more than ever, our employees, customers and partners need to be reassured of our ability to offering them the best welcome possible. As the European leader in hospitality, it is our duty to anticipate needs and respond to health and safety requirements by adhering to the highest standards. We are pleased to be pioneering this drive with Bureau Veritas and to extend it to all stakeholders.”

blocks.section: Accor and Bureau Veritas have joined forces to develop a new label
blocks.text: Jacques POMMERAUD, CEO Bureau Veritas Africa & France, added: “For almost 200 years, it has been Bureau Veritas’ mission to shape a world of trust. With this label, today we have the ability to meet the new expectations of our society in terms of health and safety. This label will contribute to the hospitality and restaurant industry reopening with confidence. We are proud to work with Accor, at first in France and subsequently in all European countries. This approach will benefit the entire industry as every company could request to be certified by Bureau Veritas.”

title: Acquisition of USIDE by Sia Partners to reinvent the art of leadership
description:
In the Top 5 in France of strategy and management consulting firms, Sia Partners acquires with Uside the expertise developed over thirty years by Eric Albert and his two partners in supporting managers.
Reinventing the art of leadership, reimagining tomorrow’s ways of working
In the context of the present crisis and subsequent acceleration of corporate transformation, Sia Partners and USIDE believe that executives must reinvent their approach to leadership and management in a way that places human capital at the heart of their organizations.
USIDE is the French standard for management in terms of corporate behavior, having served two thirds of CAC 40 companies. Since its founding in 1990, USIDE has specialized in quality of life at work. Over time, it has developed a broad range of expertise, supporting executives and cultural transformation within organizations and implementing innovative policies for attracting and managing talent. USIDE’s work is based on recognized scientific methodologies, which the firm has developed in accordance with French and international standards. With a team of 70 consultants, led by Eric Albert (Managing Partner and psychiatrist), Laurence Saunder (Managing Partner), and Jean-Luc Emery (Partner and psychiatrist), USIDE generates approximately 10 million euros in annual revenue.
USIDE will remain an autonomous entity, and its three managers will join Sia Partners’ management committee. "Sia Partners and USIDE share the same vision with respect to business transformation—accelerated by the present crisis—and have complementary approaches. Our union is natural: we have known each other for a long time and have already had the opportunity to collaborate on client projects. USIDE’s goal is to draw on Sia Partners' expertise in artificial intelligence and digital and collaborative tools, in order to enhance our databases and behavioral analysis tools. This combination will also allow us to leverage Sia Partners' global network to further USIDE’s development," said Eric Albert, Managing Partner of USIDE.
“Given the intensity of transformations in the aftermath of the crisis, we must, alongside our clients, envision new management codes within organizations, ranging from leadership to employee engagement and quality of life at work. USIDE has a unique ability to enhance the  collective performance of executive committees—a real ‘French touch’ when it comes to management, from which our 500 clients around the world will benefit," adds Matthieu Courtecuisse, founder and CEO of Sia Partners.
Dynamic growth and new offices
With this acquisition, Sia Partners has furthered its development in France, exceeding 1,000 employees (1,900 worldwide). Despite the crisis, the group has continued to grow business, reporting over €170 million in annual revenue in France (€310 million worldwide), reinforcing its position among the top 5 strategy and management consulting firms in the hexagon.
At the group level, despite the uncertainties of the present economic climate, Sia Partners has continued a  dynamic development trajectory characterized by double-digit growth. The group achieved nearly 19% in growth during the 2020 fiscal year (ending June 30), with around 20% in growth expected for the current fiscal year.
In line with Sia Partners’ NEXT-GEN 2023 strategic plan, announced in December 2020, and the group's objective to double in size to 3,000 employees and 500 million euros in revenue by the end of 2023, Sia Partners is opening two new offices in April in its two primary markets, France and the United States, with new locations in Nantes and Los Angeles.

blocks.text: With this acquisition, Sia Partners has furthered its development in France, exceeding 1,000 employees (1,900 worldwide). Despite the crisis, the group has continued to grow business, reporting over €170 million in annual revenue in France (€310 million worldwide), reinforcing its position among the top 5 strategy and management consulting firms in the hexagon.

blocks.section: Acquisition of USIDE by Sia Partners to reinvent the art of leadership
blocks.text: At the group level, despite the uncertainties of the present economic climate, Sia Partners has continued a dynamic development trajectory characterized by double-digit growth. The group achieved nearly 19% in growth during the 2020 fiscal year (ending June 30), with around 20% in growth expected for the current fiscal year.

blocks.section: Acquisition of USIDE by Sia Partners to reinvent the art of leadership
blocks.text: In line with Sia Partners’ NEXT-GEN 2023 strategic plan, announced in December 2020, and the group's objective to double in size to 3,000 employees and 500 million euros in revenue by the end of 2023, Sia Partners is opening two new offices in April in its two primary markets, France and the United States, with new locations in Nantes and Los Angeles.

title: Actes notariés depuis l’étranger
description:
À la suite d’un décret du 3 avril, pendant l’état d’urgence sanitaire, les notaires en France sont habilités à recevoir des actes notariés depuis l’étranger au moyen de la comparution à distance par vidéoconférence. La signature électronique à distance s’applique à tous les actes authentiques, y compris tous les actes solennels (mariages, donations, etc.). Cette méthode évite aux résidents à l’étranger d’avoir à différer des actes importants auxquels ils pouvaient songer.
Il convient de contacter son notaire pour connaître les modalités de mise en œuvre spécifiques à chaque situation.

title: Action against the (re-)entry ban to Japan- Letters to METI
description:
The French Chamber of Commerce in Japan has been working with the EBC to call on the Japanese Government for fair and equal treatment of foreign residents by allowing entry to Japan on the same basis as Japanese nationals.
Last month, several Chambers of commerce, including us, collected data through a survey sent to you, based on the impact of the (re-)entry ban to Japan for your companies. It provided to the EBC (European business council) solid foundation for their discussions with Japanese leaders and attracted a lot of interest from the international media.
– Involve your Japanese business partners or local governments
From their recent talks with the Japanese Government, the EBC understood that it would be most effective to achieve the relaxation of the travel ban if they could obtain a letter from either your large Japanese business partners or local governments (where your investment is located) outlining the hardship caused by the (re-)entry ban.
We need to be able to demonstrate that the travel ban impacts the Japanese economy and puts in jeopardy the health of Japanese companies, Japanese employment, or the proper functioning of local governments' projects.
* The letter should be sent to the METI, with the EBC in copy *
►  Here is an example of letter with the contact names of the people in charge at METI
►  To copy the EBC : Valérie Moschetti - vmoschetti@ebc-jp.com  
They will then be able to follow up and use these complaints for our advocacy work.

title: AeroEdge won the Supplier Performance Award from Safran Aircraft Engines
description:
AeroEdge Co., Ltd, which is located in Ashikaga City, Tochigi, is honored to announce that they have received a 2022 Supplier Performance Award from Safran Aircraft Engines.
They are the first Japanese winner from machining field. Ceremony and party were held on Aug 30th to celebrate their achievement.
Safran Aircraft Engines (Safran AE) is one of the largest aircraft engine manufacturers such as the LEAP engines, and AeroEdge had signed the agreement for long-term supplying of turbine blades made from Titanium Aluminide material.
This year, the Supplier Performance Award was given to only the five companies among all Safran AE’s suppliers in the world, recognized its excellence in all areas relating to support for production deliveries, such as quality and on-time delivery through a year.
They are the first Japanese company who won the award in the field of machining. It was an unexceptional achievement that a young company, only the 7 years has passed since the establishment, won the award. As the result of their commitment to the quality, cost, and delivery, highly regarded their capabilities for technical development and suggestion led to the award.
The ceremony and party were held at COCO FARM&WINERY (located in Ashikaga City, Tochigi) on Aug 30th. Lots of their partners from Safran AE, such as Senior Vice Presidents came from France and participated in the party. The Governor of Tochigi Pref., the Mayor of Ashikaga City, the director of Aircraft Component and Material Industries Office in METI (Japan Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry), the Representative Director and CEO from Peach Aviation Limited, and the Chief Executive Officer from Sendai International Airport. Co., Ltd., are also participated to celebrate their achievement.
“We started this journey in 2013. We were looking for partners who were able to machine this critical material, which is complex and difficult to be machined. When I looked everywhere, one guy in AeroEdge helped us to machine and to deliver this part. Last time I was in your plant in 2016, the plant was not completely finished for mass production because it was the beginning of the plant. It was a big success and I’m very pleased to be with you today, and to have been here in the beginning of the story. I’m quite sure it is not finished and you will be part of new journey we are launching for new engines.” Said Mr. Claude QUILLIEN, Senior Vice President from Safran AE

title: Agility: why having this capability in your organization is so critical
description:
The final HR committee of 2019 was focused on the much talked about topic of organizational agility, the new strategic imperative of the 21st century. Over 20 participants from a wide range of industries and functions came to listen to Ron Stewart, President of Prosci Canada, who divided his presentation in three main parts: “Making a compelling case for agility”, “What are the attributes of agile organization” and “How change management enables agility”.
After a definition of the meaning of agility in a business context, Ron introduced us to the ADKAR model which outlines the 5 steps to follow to be prepared for an organizational change: Awareness, Desire, Knowledge, Ability and Reinforcement. He then explained how to go from the big picture of the change you wish to implement to the detailed actions you need to put in place throughout the organization to make the change successful. Through a series of examples, Ron showed us that any kind of change can impact your employees’ mindset and give an unexpected turn of events to the vision of your initial project, if not anticipated and communicated properly. In one word: be prepared!
CCI France Japon wishes to thank the speakers, participants, president of the HR Committee, Grégory Dancs, and extend its special thanks to Quang Nguyen, Managing Director of Ataway Japan K.K. (CCI France Japon member and the exclusive partner of Prosci in Japan) for the introduction of Ron Stewart and the precious help in preparing this committee.

title: Air France: Boris Darceaux appointed as General Manager for Japan, Korea and New Caledonia
description:
Air France KLM announced the appointment of Boris DARCEAUX as General Manager of Japan, Korea and New Caledonia, effective 1st September 2022.
He will replace Guillaume Glass, who has held the position since September 2019.
Boris Darceaux brings a wealth of sales and marketing experience to Japan proven in the European market where he has contributed to the business performance of Air France KLM. After joining Air France in 1999, he has served several key positions in the organization including Country Manager for Ireland, General Manager for Belgium-Luxembourg and Spain-Portugal. He has most recently held the position of Director Commercial Transformation at the head office where he led projects to reform the business organization and improve operations.
 Commenting on his appointment, Boris Darceaux stated:
"It is an honor to be appointed to this position. Since we started our operations in 1951 for KLM and 1952 for Air France, Japan has been a key market for Air France-KLM. Coming up this year for our Japan network, KLM will be introducing the new Premium Comfort Class, and Air France's scheduled operations from Haneda will resume in September, providing our customers with extra travel comfort and more capacity on direct services between Japan and Europe. I am most certainly convinced that together with our partners, we can support the recovery and sustainable growth of international travel for the Japanese market."

blocks.text: Boris Darceaux brings a wealth of sales and marketing experience to Japan proven in the European market where he has contributed to the business performance of Air France KLM. After joining Air France in 1999, he has served several key positions in the organization including Country Manager for Ireland, General Manager for Belgium-Luxembourg and Spain-Portugal. He has most recently held the position of Director Commercial Transformation at the head office where he led projects to reform the business organization and improve operations.

blocks.section: Air France: Boris Darceaux appointed as General Manager for Japan, Korea and New Caledonia
blocks.text: Commenting on his appointment, Boris Darceaux stated:

blocks.section: Air France: Boris Darceaux appointed as General Manager for Japan, Korea and New Caledonia
blocks.text: "It is an honor to be appointed to this position. Since we started our operations in 1951 for KLM and 1952 for Air France, Japan has been a key market for Air France-KLM. Coming up this year for our Japan network, KLM will be introducing the new Premium Comfort Class, and Air France's scheduled operations from Haneda will resume in September, providing our customers with extra travel comfort and more capacity on direct services between Japan and Europe. I am most certainly convinced that together with our partners, we can support the recovery and sustainable growth of international travel for the Japanese market."

title: Air France celebrates 90 years of elegance
description:
Air France is gearing up to celebrate its 90th anniversary on October 7, 2023, and the airline has big plans to mark this milestone.
To commemorate this occasion, Air France has collaborated with Xavier Ronze, the head of costume design workshops at the Paris Opera ballet, to create a collection of five iconic dresses that embody the airline's legendary history. These dresses will be showcased in an exhibition at the Galeries Lafayette Paris Haussmann from September 28 to October 10, 2023.
Air France, born from the merger of several aviation companies in 1933, has been at the forefront of promoting the French art of travel worldwide, offering nearly 1,000 daily flights to 200 destinations with a fleet of over 240 aircraft. In 2023, Air France is celebrating 90 years of elegance, innovation, and excellence in the world of aviation. The airline has always represented the quintessential French charm and sophistication, offering an exceptional travel experience that embodies the essence of France.
To illustrate and bring to life these 90 years of elegance, Air France is unveiling a collection of five iconic dresses, each representing a different aspect of the airline's history. These dresses symbolize aircraft and technology, uniforms and fashion, iconic posters promoting the airline's vast network, fine dining and tableware, and design and architecture. These dresses are an invitation to explore the various themes that have allowed Air France to continuously set new standards and lead the way in the aviation industry.
Renowned costume designer Xavier Ronze, responsible for the costume design workshops at the Paris Opera Ballet, was tasked with creating these unique dresses. Ronze combined elements from Air France's rich heritage with contemporary pieces to create designs that bridge the gap between history and modernity, embodying the best of both Air France and French expertise.
To showcase this dress collection to the public, Air France has chosen the prestigious Galeries Lafayette in Paris, a renowned fashion destination. The exhibition, which runs from September 28 to October 10, 2023, will feature the dresses in the store's windows, surrounded by vintage Air France memorabilia and modern airline offerings. This display aims to highlight 90 years of in-flight comfort, legendary aircraft, designer uniforms, in-flight dining, and design.
Air France's innovative approach to showcasing its heritage at the heart of Paris allows both French and international visitors to relive their fondest memories of traveling with the airline or become a part of its legendary history.
Inside the store, pop-up shops will offer a range of specially created or reissued items for the anniversary celebration. These include models of old and new aircraft, comfort kits, postcards, luggage tags, notebooks, vintage travel bags, and iconic posters. Additionally, Air France has partnered with luxury French brands like Vanessa Bruno, Delsey, Bernardaud, Brun de Vian-Tiran, and Le Parapluie de Cherbourg to promote French craftsmanship exclusively available at Galeries Lafayette.
For the first time in its history, Air France is also offering visitors the opportunity to purchase original tableware signed by the painter Jean Picart Le Doux, used on board its La Première and Business cabins from 1966 to the 2000s. The proceeds from this sale will be donated to the Air France Foundation, which has been supporting children around the world for 30 years.
As part of the anniversary celebrations, Air France is hosting real fashion shows at Galeries Lafayette Paris Haussmann, allowing visitors to witness 90 years of French elegance. Models will showcase uniforms ranging from the earliest "barman" outfits to couture pieces designed by renowned fashion houses such as Christian Dior, Cristóbal Balenciaga, and Christian Lacroix. These fashion shows provide a unique journey through the different fashion eras that have defined Air France's identity.

title: Air France chooses Michelin as its exclusive tyre supplier as part of an ambitious ten-year partnership
description:
Air France has renewed its trust in Michelin and has selected the French group as the exclusive tyre supplier for its aircraft fleet. The Michelin Group will equip the company's short-, medium- and long-haul aircraft1 with new or retreaded tyres notably produced at the Saint Doulchard plant in Bourges, France.
Air France's aircraft will be equipped with the most modern aircraft tyres, such as Radial Michelin® AIR X tyres incorporating NZG (Near Zero Growth) technology. Designed to guarantee a constant tyre diametre, this technology provides aircraft tyres with greater durability and exceptional resistance.
Pioneers in the field of French aviation and historic partners, Air France and Michelin have always shared a common DNA: innovation at the service of performance and safety.
Between 2010 and 2020, the partnership has enabled Air France to benefit from all the latest technologies developed by Michelin. Over the next ten years, both groups will continue to work together and steer the field of innovation towards a shared ambition, to reduce the carbon footprint. Michelin takes an active part in European research programmes and is working on breakthrough technologies to continue to lighten its tyres and associated systems and to mechanically reduce fuel consumption and CO2 emissions on each flight.
Air France and Michelin will also extend their partnership to digital and other services. Michelin will offer Air France even more ambitious solutions such as its innovative recycling channels, its highperformance ecological resins and its 3D metal and plastic printing expertise. This broadening of the partnership's scope is made possible by Michelin's recent diversification of its areas of activity and knowhow.
These initiatives will help Air France achieve the ambitious sustainable development objectives it has set, including a 50% reduction in its CO2 emissions per passenger/km by 2030.
“More than just a supplier, the Michelin Group is a long-standing partner of Air France. We are delighted to be equipping our aircraft with tyres Made in France and to be extending our collaboration to new fields of innovation. This new agreement paves the way for ambitious projects that will enable us to accelerate the reduction of our environmental footprint, which is one of Air France's priorities.” said Géry Mortreux, EVP Engineering & Maintenance at Air France.
“We are honoured by the trust Air France has placed in us by choosing Michelin as its trusted partner for the next ten years. This commitment naturally includes equipping its entire fleet with highperformance tyres. Guaranteeing a high level of safety in extreme conditions and a large number of landings, Michelin tyres are particularly well suited to new-generation aircraft. Lighter in weight, they also offer significant fuel savings, helping to make aviation even more sustainable. This partnership will also enable us to explore new growth areas for both our groups, beyond the supply of tyres.” said Mauro Sponza, Director of Aeronautical Activities at Michelin.

title: Air France is getting ready to resume services from Haneda Airport
description:
Air France will resume its scheduled flights from Haneda Airport. Departing from Haneda on September 8th, 3 weekly direct flights will be operated throughout the remainder of the summer season serviced by Boeing 787 Dreamliner.
Schedule Haneda-Paris from September 2022: AF279 From 08-sept-22 to 29-oct-22 3/7 Mon, Thu, Sat Tokyo (Haneda) departure 10:25 Paris (CDG) arrival 18:10 AF0272 From 07-sept-22 28-oct-22 3/7 Wed, Fri, Sun Paris (CDG) departure 12:15 Tokyo (Haneda) arrival 08:30 (next day)
 Air France is continuing to optimize its network with efficient and environmentally-friendly aircraft. The Boeing 787 offers operational and environmental benefits with a lower fuel consumption than previous generation aircraft, and a significant reduction in CO2 emissions (around 20%) and noise emissions.
 On board, with windows that are 30% larger than those of previous generation aircraft that invites natural light, more space in the cabins, improved air pressure and humidity levels offers, enhance comfort for the passenger’s travel experience. This aircraft is also equipped with Wi-Fi, allowing customers to stay connected throughout their trip.
 Flight schedules, days of operation and fares are available on their website.
 Operations will be implemented in line with the health measures in force in the different countries or destinations served. Before travelling, Air France invites its customers to check the conditions of entry and the documents required on arrival at their destination.

title: Air France-KLM and HORIBA signed an agreement for the development of Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF)
description:
Air France-KLM and HORIBA signed an agreement to mark a further step to develop the sustainable fuel industry.
HORIBA Ltd. has signed an agreement to join the group’s Corporate SAF Program (Sustainable Aviation Fuel). The Corporate SAF program by Air France- KLM to calls on the business community to play an active role in the future of sustainable travel. This cooperative is an extension of Nabtesco Coporation’s commitment to its CSR goals by choosing to invest in a developing industry ultimately responsible for providing a sustainable option for air transport.
Sustainable fuels for aviation, fundamental levers for reducing CO₂ emissions Air France and KLM have been involved for many years in research and development programs in the field of alternative fuels. In 2011, the two airlines were among the first to operate commercial flights with sustainable fuels, demonstrating that it is possible to use an alternative energy to fossil fuels. The main challenge today is the development of a sustainable industry to which the corporate customers of Air France and KLM can make a concrete contribution.
 Guillaume Glass, General Manager for Japan, Korea and New Caledonia said: “Air France – KLM is leading the path toward decarbonization of air transport. After CO2 reduction via fleet modernization and eco-piloting, and CO2 offset schemes offered to all our customers, we are moving to the next step with our Corporate SAF Program. This new program allows Japanese companies to reduce CO2 emissions by 80% for a part, or all, of their employee’s business trips. I would like to thank HORIBA for their commitment toward sustainable business travel."

title: Air France launches “Ready to Fly”, a pre-travel health document verification service
description:
Since the beginning of the COVID crisis, Air France has been doing everything possible to assist its customers by enabling them to easily check the health documents required by the authorities of their destination country. This information is updated in real time on the airfrance.traveldoc.aero website. With "Ready to Fly", the airline goes one step further by offering its customers the certainty of knowing that they have all the health documents required for their trip before they arrive at the airport. A few days before departure, customers travelling on eligible flights receive an email inviting them to upload their health documents on an Air France online platform. These documents are then checked and if they are complete and correct, a confirmation message is sent to the customer. The boarding passes issued will then be marked "Ready to Fly", enabling them to be processed quickly by Air France teams at the airport on the day of departure. If a document is missing or incomplete, customers receive a notification message inviting them to transfer the missing documents or to present them at the airport on the day of their trip. With "Ready to Fly", Air France ensures its customers enjoy a relaxed start to their journey, knowing that they have all the documents they need to board their flight. This free and optional service also ensures a smoother customer journey through the airport, by eliminating successive checks. Successfully tested since June, "Ready to Fly" will be available as from July 17 on flights from Paris to Corsica and French overseas destinations, before being gradually rolled out over the summer to a growing number of destinations.

title: Air France resumes Haneda service from this summer Starting with 3 weekly flights and increasing to 5 by July
description:
In line with the gradual reopening of French borders and the lifting of certain travel restrictions, this summer season Air France plans to serve close to 200 destinations worldwide.
Haneda is once again reunited with the network, making the comeback from this season as the first resuming flight departed Haneda on Monday, June 21st.
Passengers boarding the AF293 bound for Paris-Charles de Gaulle received a special welcome kit including a facemask envelope.
Air France Japan network for this summer will commence with 9 weekly flights connecting Paris-Charles de Gaulle and its Japan gateways, Haneda, Narita and Osaka, each serviced with 3 weekly flights. From July 7th onwards Haneda will increase frequency to 5 flights, which makes the total number of flights to 11 flights per week.

description: Air France will reinforce its service to Paris with up to 17 weekly flights from Haneda.

blocks.text: Foresight

blocks.section: Air France strengthens its Haneda/Paris route
blocks.text: Air France strengthens its Haneda/Paris route

blocks.section: Air France strengthens its Haneda/Paris route
blocks.text: Air France will reinforce its service to Paris with up to 17 weekly flights from Haneda.

blocks.section: Air France strengthens its Haneda/Paris route
blocks.text: At a press conference on March 22, General Manager of the Japan Branch Boris Darceaux announced the reinforcement of the Air France service between Haneda and Paris for its summer schedule .

blocks.section: Air France strengthens its Haneda/Paris route
blocks.text: Currently more than 14 flights per week (two flights per day) will be increased to a maximum of 17 flights per week (up to three flights per day) from September to October. The Kansai route will also increase from three to five flights per week.

blocks.section: Air France strengthens its Haneda/Paris route
blocks.text: As an official partner of the Paris 2024 Olympic Games , the airline plans to increase the number of its employees, improve its facilities - including the addition of a baggage drop-off point - and increase the number of flights.

blocks.section: Air France strengthens its Haneda/Paris route
blocks.text: Concerned about the environment, the company is actively committed to reducing greenhouse gas emissions , with a target of cutting emissions by 30% by 2030 compared with 2019. To achieve this, it is modernizing its fleets with less polluting models. Air France also offers the possibility of using the train from Paris for connections in France and to Brussels.

description: Find out, in video, the Air France's new commitment to health and safety

blocks.text: COVID-19 • Companies news

blocks.text: Air France: their new commitment to health and safety to ensure you a safe trip

blocks.section: Air France: their new commitment to health and safety to ensure you a safe trip
blocks.text: Find out, in video, the Air France's new commitment to health and safety

blocks.section: Air France: their new commitment to health and safety to ensure you a safe trip
blocks.text: The health and well-being of customers and staff are at the heart of Air France’s concerns. In addition to the strict hygiene procedures routinely applied to its flights, Air France has decided to reinforce its health measures for everyone’s protection at the airport and on board its aircraft. These hygiene measures are implemented throughout the customer journey.

blocks.section: Air France: their new commitment to health and safety to ensure you a safe trip
blocks.text: The wearing of masks will be compulsory on our flights as from 11 May 2020. All customers will have to wear a mask throughout their journey. Customers will be notified of this via all communication channels (email, sms, websites) prior to their departure and will be asked to ensure they possess one or more masks for their trip.

blocks.section: Air France: their new commitment to health and safety to ensure you a safe trip
blocks.text: At the airport, the measures implemented guarantee a travel experience in optimum conditions of health and safety, with the application of physical distancing measures, counters equipped with Plexiglass protection screens, regularly disinfected self-service kiosks, hand sanitizer available throughout the airport and the reorganization of customer channels at check-in and boarding to limit contact

blocks.section: Air France: their new commitment to health and safety to ensure you a safe trip
blocks.text: On board the majority of flights, the current low load factors allow us to respect physical distancing. In cases where this is not possible, requiring all passengers and crew members to wear masks ensures adequate health protection.

blocks.section: Air France: their new commitment to health and safety to ensure you a safe trip
blocks.text: Air France has reinforced aircraft cleaning procedures, notably with the disinfection of all surfaces in contact with customers such as armrests, tables and screens, and the introduction of a specific procedure for disinfecting aircraft by spraying an approved virucidal product.

blocks.section: Air France: their new commitment to health and safety to ensure you a safe trip
blocks.text: The air in the cabin is renewed every 3 minutes. The air recycling system on board Air France aircraft is equipped with HEPA – High Efficiency Particulate Air – filters identical to those used in hospital operating theatres.

blocks.section: Air France: their new commitment to health and safety to ensure you a safe trip
blocks.text: To limit interaction, the in-flight service has been simplified – the meal and beverage service has been completed adapted, and duty-free sales and the newspapers and magazines offer have been temporarily suspended.

title: Air France unveils its new in flight safety video
description:
Air France unveiled its new in flight safety video, an elegant, lively and fast moving showcase of French culture.
Incorporating all the latest regulatory changes in force, this video symbolizes the essence of the Air France brand An invitation to travel for everyone all over the world, where the airline declares its love of France and its lifestyle.
Two flight attendants explain the safety instructions to passengers from all walks of life, travelling together from one iconic landmark to another, places that highlight the best of France, to the tune of lively melodies, inspired by musicals.
In an instant, passengers are transported from the steps of the Opéra Garnier to the gardens of the Palace of Versailles, from the sunny French Riviera to the legendary Hotel Martinez. The stroll continues through the vineyards of Provence, past museums, a fashion show, a typical French café terrace and along the banks of the Seine and its famous booksellers. So many fascinating places just waiting to be discovered and admired.
The safety briefing ends at the top of the sparkling Eiffel Tower, where an Air France crew greets the airline's customers.
In this poetic tribute to the art of French style travel, Air France seeks to capture everyone's attention in order to deliver its safety instructions in a joyful, elegant and colourful video. Six years after the last video was released, this film is adapted to all the various different aircraft and cabin layouts.
Catherine Villar, SVP Customer Experience Air France, said :“With this new video, we are showcasing the best France has to offer in an emotionally engaging way. All our teams here at Air France are ready to welcome our customers and highlight this French lifestyle, which is so dear to us, as soon as they board our flights. We can't wait to reopen the skies, flight after flight, with safety as our absolute and constant priority"
The company developed this film with the creative talent of its new communications agency Aura by Omnicom and in partnership with Atout France, France's tourism development agency. The video was produced by French director and scriptwriter Romain Quirot The music, created especially for the occasion, was written by Ludovic Bource, a French composer who has won a César and an Oscar.

title: Air France/KLM: Reuniting with family and friends during Christmas Holiday
description:
While the world adapts to the reality of COVID 19, customers still need to travel , for instance to go back home to visit family and friends. Air France and KLM acknowledge the needs and do everything possible to reconnect customers worldwide. As your comfort and health remain our top priority, we have adapted our commercial policy to ensure you travel in the best possible condition and put in place the strictest health measures.
Reassurance for new bookings no change fee For customers that want to make a new reservation, but feel uncertain about booking due to COVID 19, Air France and KLM still offer reassurance and flexibility so that you can book with confidence. Giving you the possibility to easily postpone or cancel your trip and request a refundable voucher. You can check Air France or KLM websites for more details.
Special One Way fare to Europe Air France is offering special one way fares to European cities in Economy, Premium Economy and Business class. This special offer is now available and valid for all flights from Japan with a departure until 15 December 2020. Book a one way fare ticket
Health & Safety measures To safeguard your health and safety, Air France and KLM have taken many measures at the airport and on board to bring you safely to where you need to go. Air France commit s to their safety by listing all measures taken under the Air France Protect label. KLM has created a new video to showcase all measures taken by KLM during your journey. Watch KLM Video
What can you do to prepare for your trip? It is important that you travel well prepared during COVID 19. Governments can change the rules and restrictions at any moment, which Air France and KLM closely follow. With the easy Air France TravelDoc and KLM TravelDoc sites, you will know what you need to arrange for a smooth journey What’s available: Customers can perform an antigenic test (result in 2hrs) or RT PCR test (result in 48hrs) at Paris CDG airport. To be tested, customers must have a ticket and must make an appointment on doctolib.fr
Re-entry Japan for foreign nationals From 1st of November it is not needed anymore to request by e mail the “Receipt for Request of Re entry”. Also there are changes to the re entry procedures for short term (7 days) business travelers. Before leaving Japan, please read carefully the re entry information & re entry procedures for short term business travelers from the Japanese authorities. Learn more
Flight schedule update Air France and KLM closely monitor the travel restrictions and are doing everything possible to reconnect customers worldwide. Please check Air France or KLM website for latest network updates.

title: Air Liquide collaborates with Itochu to scale up Japan hydrogen mobility markets
description:
Air Liquide Japan and Itochu Corporation (Itochu) have signed a memorandum of understanding to collaborate on the development of hydrogen mobility markets in Japan.
Air Liquide Japan and Itochu will initially focus on the development of the hydrogen retail infrastructure in Japan, both for passenger vehicles and for the new fleets of commercial vehicles (trucks, busses). The objective is to expand this retail infrastructure and develop a competitive hydrogen supply offer for passenger and commercial end-users, in collaboration with public authorities, allowing a rapid ramp-up of hydrogen mobility in Japan. The two companies will investigate more globally the opportunities to scale up the hydrogen supply chain in support of the Japan Government hydrogen roadmap.
This collaboration will leverage the expertise and technologies of Air Liquide across the hydrogen supply chain and the large footprint of Itochu Group across multiple energy sectors, from fuel retail business to renewable energy production plants.
This collaboration comes after the recent announcement by the Japanese Government of the Green Society plan, to reach carbon neutrality by 2050, in which hydrogen is anticipated to take a key role. Under this plan, the Japanese government will ban the sales of vehicles which completely run on fossil fuels after 2035, pushing for the transportation sector to make a shift toward battery electric and fuel cell electric vehicles.
François Abrial, Member of the Air Liquide Group’s Executive Committee supervising Asia Pacific, said:
“The fight against climate change is at the heart of Air Liquide 's strategy. Hydrogen is projected to play a key role in supporting energy transition and the emergence of a carbon-neutral society. With this collaboration,  we seek  to jointly accelerate the development of Hydrogen mobility markets in Japan, leveraging our complementary technology portfolios and know-how across the entire hydrogen value chain. ”

blocks.text: Alain Li joins Sia Partners as Senior Advisor

blocks.section: Alain Li joins Sia Partners as Senior Advisor
blocks.text: Sia Partners announces the arrival of Alain Li, former CEO of Richemont Asia Pacific, as a new Senior Advisor.

blocks.section: Alain Li joins Sia Partners as Senior Advisor
blocks.text: The relationship with Alain Li and his wealth of experience within the lifestyle industry across the globe will serve as a major asset.

blocks.section: Alain Li joins Sia Partners as Senior Advisor
blocks.text: Before joining Sia Partners, Alain Li served as the Asia-Pacific CEO for the luxury group Richemont, from 2006. Alain was responsible for overseeing the operations and growth of Richemont's luxury brands in the Asia Pacific region. With over 20 years of experience in the luxury goods market, he played a significant role in expanding Richemont's presence in the region and driving its success.

blocks.section: Alain Li joins Sia Partners as Senior Advisor
blocks.text: In addition to his role with Sia Partners, Alain is an Independent Non-Executive Director of Remy Cointreau and has been President of the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Hong Kong since 2022.

blocks.section: Alain Li joins Sia Partners as Senior Advisor
blocks.text: Beyond an obvious focus on the Luxury industry, Alain will also be involved in other domains of the Lifestyle Industry such as Beauty/Cosmetics, Tourism, Food & Beverage and will bring his knowledge of the Asia region.

blocks.section: Alain Li joins Sia Partners as Senior Advisor
blocks.text: " Our revenues within Luxury and Lifestyle brands have tripled in the last two years. Alain will help us to accelerate this traction and share his expertise on various topics such as how to build a data-driven organization in Luxury, how to improve the digital customer journey (activation, personalization, payment, marketplaces), how to be an early adopter of the Web3 ecosystem, how to optimize supply chain and operations, and how to accelerate sustainable roadmaps ." explains Matthieu Courtecuisse, CEO of Sia Partners.

blocks.section: Alain Li joins Sia Partners as Senior Advisor
blocks.text: “ I am delighted to join Sia Partners as a Senior Advisor. I've had the pleasure to collaborate with Sia Partners in the past and was always impressed by their professionalism and expertise .” says Alain Li.

blocks.section: Alain Li joins Sia Partners as Senior Advisor
blocks.text: Sia Partners now has 150 seasoned consultants across the APAC region in four locations (Australia, Japan, Hong Kong, Singapore) and a target to grow by 25% in the coming year.

title: Marketing and Retail Committee
description:
The French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan hosted an engaging event featuring a compelling presentation by Bertrand Stephann, Founder and CEO of Alcmeon, along with Félix Puig, Account Manager at Alcmeon. The focus was on leveraging LINE to drive business growth. This Marketing and Retail Committee event was led by Committee President Philippe Jardin.
Since its launch, LINE has skyrocketed to become Japan's leading platform for monthly active users. The event provided valuable insights on how businesses can harness LINE for conversational retail marketing and customer service strategies. Participants gained a deep understanding of maximizing this platform's potential to enhance their operations and customer engagement.
The session was insightful and captivating, offering a unique opportunity for attendees to ask questions and explore various use cases of LINE in different business scenarios. The event highlighted the growing importance of LINE in the business world and demonstrated how companies can effectively partner with Alcmeon to optimize their customer strategies.

blocks.section: Altavia Japan received "Gold" rating in the 2020 Sustainability Assessments issued by EcoVadis
blocks.text: Altavia is the first international independent group specialized in sales communications for retailers. Founded in 1983 by Chief Executive Officer Raphaël Palti, the group offers tailor-made sales activation solutions to the retailers.

blocks.section: Altavia Japan received "Gold" rating in the 2020 Sustainability Assessments issued by EcoVadis
blocks.text: The "Gold" level is only awarded to the top 5% of all companies surveyed. The Altavia Group has set itself the goal of achieving EcoVadis certification for each of its branches, regardless of the size of the branch office. This is the first branch office in Asia to obtain the certification. By incorporating the latest technology into its production operations, Altavia Japan has achieved a production process that significantly reduces environmental impact and waste while providing a high level of quality. They propose sustainable solutions that challenge the existing sense of values and conventions of production sites. They will continue to focus our efforts on CSR, and make further progress in their ambition to be a company that contributes to the sustainable development of society and is trusted by the public.

blocks.section: Altavia Japan received "Gold" rating in the 2020 Sustainability Assessments issued by EcoVadis
blocks.text: What is the Altavia Group's approach to CSR? The Altavia Group is dedicated to pursuing sustainable growth by providing solutions to diversified social issues such as those surrounding the environment, resources and energy, by providing a range of marketing services using the latest technology. The Group is also a member of the United Nations Global Compact and has been recognized at the Advanced Level since 2018.

title: Altera Consulting Launches Altera Connect: Find and Hire Bilingual Consultant Freelancers in Japan
description:
Altera Consulting Co., Ltd., a leader in digital transformation and consulting services, is thrilled to announce the launch of Altera Connect, an innovative platform designed to bridge the gap between multinational companies and top-tier bilingual consultants in Japan. This service aims to streamline the process of matching businesses with skilled consultants who have both the technical expertise and the cultural fluency needed to succeed in the Japanese market.
Background: Addressing a Critical Need in the Market
The launch of Altera Connect comes in response to a pressing need identified by Altera Consulting through years of industry experience. Japan’s unique business landscape demands not only technical expertise but also cultural and linguistic fluency, which can be challenging for multinational companies to find. Recognizing this gap, Altera Consulting has developed Altera Connect to offer a reliable, efficient solution for sourcing bilingual consultants who can excel in this complex environment.
“Through our extensive work with multinational clients, we realized the critical importance of having consultants who are not only technically proficient but also culturally and linguistically adept. Altera Connect was born out of this necessity to ensure successful project outcomes in Japan,” said Frederic Peyrot, CEO of Altera Consulting.
Altera Connect for Companies: Simplifying the Search for Bilingual Experts
Altera Connect is tailored to meet the unique needs of companies operating in Japan’s dynamic business environment. Multinational corporations often face the challenge of finding consultants who not only possess technical expertise but also have the linguistic and cultural fluency to navigate Japan’s market. Altera Connect addresses this need by offering:
 	Premier Talent Pool: Access to an exclusive selection of bilingual experts in technology, digital transformation, and project management. 	Unmatched Quality and Compatibility: A rigorous four-step vetting process ensures that only the best consultants make it through, guaranteeing high-quality matches. 	Efficient Matching: Personalized assistance from talent managers who match consultants to companies’ specific project needs. 	Adaptive Engagements: Flexible engagement models tailored to companies’ project requirements, desired consultant allocation, and budget. 
“Our platform is designed to provide businesses with the right talent quickly and efficiently, ensuring that projects are executed with precision and cultural sensitivity,” said Frederic, CEO of Altera Consulting.
Altera Connect for Consultants: Unlocking Premier Opportunities
For bilingual consultants, Altera Connect opens doors to exciting projects with leading multinational and domestic companies. The platform streamlines the process of finding relevant and impactful work, allowing consultants to focus on what they do best.
Key benefits for consultants include:
 	Top-Tier Project Access: To access prominent companies on high-impact projects. 	Hassle-Free Engagement: Administrative tasks are handled by Altera Connect, so consultants can concentrate on delivering excellent results. 	Competitive Compensation: Negotiation on behalf of consultants to ensure competitive rates. 	Flexibility: To choose projects that align with their skill, desired rates, interests, and preferred working styles. 	Support and Development: Consultants can access a vast amount of resources and get continuous support from Altera throughout their project delivery. 
“Consultants don’t want to spend time doing sales and finding their next clients; nor do they like negotiating contracts and rates. Altera Connect allows them to focus on what they do best and takes the commercial and admin parts out of their way.” said Frederic, CEO of Altera Consulting.
About Altera Consulting
Altera Consulting is a digital transformation consulting company based in Tokyo, Japan, specializing in helping businesses build and enhance their technology and digital capabilities to improve their business and operations. With a commitment to excellence and innovation, Altera Consulting provides transformation audits and strategy, end-to-end solution implementation and migration, process optimization, data intelligence, ChatGPT training, and agile transformation services.

description: The antique Salon Morikawa in Ashiya kindly hosted a Buffet-Seminar yesterday, gathering about a dozen people around a quality talk and diner.

blocks.section: "Wellness and Nutrition" at the Morikawa Salon
blocks.text: "Wellness and Nutrition" at the Morikawa Salon

blocks.section: "Wellness and Nutrition" at the Morikawa Salon
blocks.text: The antique Salon Morikawa in Ashiya kindly hosted a Buffet-Seminar yesterday, gathering about a dozen people around a quality talk and diner.

blocks.section: "Wellness and Nutrition" at the Morikawa Salon
blocks.text: Yesterday evening, the Morikawa Salon in Ashiya hosted a convivial diner-seminar about "Wellness and Nutrition", with the support of our Chamber's Kansai Desk.

blocks.section: "Wellness and Nutrition" at the Morikawa Salon
blocks.text: In a gorgeous setting made of antique furniture and crockery reenacting an 18th century aristocratic French salon, somewhat ironically decorated with blue-white-red flower arrangements in anticipation for the upcoming Bastille Day on the 14th of July, the Morikawa Clinic did prepare an unforgettable background to host this event.

blocks.section: "Wellness and Nutrition" at the Morikawa Salon
blocks.text: It is in this environment that the short seminar about "Basics of Nutrition and Wellness" was held, presented by the Doctor Morikawa's secretary.

blocks.section: "Wellness and Nutrition" at the Morikawa Salon
blocks.text: However, what everybody was most certainly focusing on was the following Mediterranean healthy (and mostly vegetarian) buffet, designed and prepared especially for the occasion by the French local Cheffe Laurence Anzai, freshly arrived and currently working in the region. To conclude the event, a range of delicious pastries from a local bakery where displayed and served.

blocks.section: "Wellness and Nutrition" at the Morikawa Salon
blocks.text: Although the Morikawa Clinic itself is located in Amagasaki, Ms. Morikawa, a French antique enthusiast, opened this salon on the side in the nice neighborhood of Ashiya, partly to offer to patients the possibility to recover in a relaxing environment after their medical visits. A more spacious and plain version is currently being built right next to the clinic in Amagasaki, and will be available shortly. Another location for a future event perhaps?

blocks.section: "Wellness and Nutrition" at the Morikawa Salon
blocks.text: Thank you very much for coming, and if you find yourself near Ashiya, please feel free to contact the Morikawa family for a special experience at the Salon!

blocks.section: "Wellness and Nutrition" at the Morikawa Salon

blocks.text: Challenges and Opportunities for French and Indo-Pacific Companies

blocks.section: APAC Forum 2024 in New Delhi: Open to Non-CCE Participants
blocks.text: The Asia-Pacific (APAC) Forum 2024, organized by the French Foreign Trade Advisors (CCE), will be held in New Delhi from November 27 to 29. Open to non-CCE participants, this event offers a unique platform for French and Indo-Pacific companies.

blocks.section: APAC Forum 2024 in New Delhi: Open to Non-CCE Participants
blocks.text: The program includes key topics such as geopolitical and defense issues in the Indo-Pacific, French interests in the region, aerospace, space exploration, Asian geoeconomics, consumption trends in India and Asia, future cities, digital and AI's role in energy sustainability, and regional innovations.

blocks.section: APAC Forum 2024 in New Delhi: Open to Non-CCE Participants
blocks.text: Who are the CCEs?

blocks.section: APAC Forum 2024 in New Delhi: Open to Non-CCE Participants
blocks.text: The French Foreign Trade Advisors (CCE) are a network of 4,500 business leaders and international trade experts. Their mission is to assist French companies in their international expansion through four key pillars:

blocks.section: APAC Forum 2024 in New Delhi: Open to Non-CCE Participants
blocks.text: 1. Advising public authorities. 2. Supporting businesses. 3. Training young professionals in international trade. 4. Promoting France's attractiveness.

blocks.section: APAC Forum 2024 in New Delhi: Open to Non-CCE Participants
blocks.text: Present in France and over 150 countries, the CCEs are key players for any company seeking to expand globally.

blocks.section: APAC Forum 2024 in New Delhi: Open to Non-CCE Participants
blocks.text: Why a Regional Forum?

blocks.section: APAC Forum 2024 in New Delhi: Open to Non-CCE Participants
blocks.text: The CCEs regularly organize regional forums to promote knowledge sharing and networking. The APAC Forum is a biennial event, and following the success of the 2023 edition in Vietnam, the 14th edition in India promises invaluable opportunities for business meetings and strategic reflection.

title: An immersive experience to discover Japan's unique business ecosystem.
description:
As part of a visit linked to Expo 2025 in Osaka, a delegation from the Association Progrès du Management (Association for the Progress of Management/APM) — composed of a dozen business leaders from Normandy — took part in a week-long Learning Expedition in Japan, organized by the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan.

The aim of this immersive experience was to discover the Japanese business ecosystem, focusing particularly on management practices, innovation, and industrial excellence. This journey provided participants with the opportunity to engage with key players in Japan’s economic and industrial landscape, gaining valuable insights into leadership, strategy, and the integration of innovation in both business and society.


Tokyo : A Hub of Innovation and Industry

The first four days of the expedition were spent in Tokyo, where participants attended seminars and engaged in a series of industry visits that offered first-hand exposure to cutting-edge developments in various sectors.

 	Day 1 : Seminar at Crédit Agricole’s Tokyo Offices 
The journey began with a full-day seminar hosted at Crédit Agricole’s Tokyo offices, featuring insightful presentations by key figures such as:
- Esther Thiebaut from the Economic Department of the French Embassy in Japan, who provided an overview of the Japanese economic landscape.
- Mehdi Matagne from the Business Development of French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan, who offered a comprehensive outlook on the Japanese market.
- Pierre Mustière CEO and Representative Director of Bouygues Asia, who shared insights into the corporate environment and business culture in Japan.
- François-Xavier Lienhart from Japan Advisory Services, with over 30 years of experience in Japan, shared his professional journey and insights on the local market.

 	Day 2 : Obayashi Corporation's Research Center 
The delegation then visited the Obayashi Corporation’s research center, where they learned about Japan’s cutting-edge construction industry. A highlight was the Grand Ring, a symbol of Expo 2025, built by Obayashi. The visit highlighted how Japan blends technology, tradition, and innovation in its approach to urban development.

 	Day 3 : Mitsubishi Motors and the Future of Mobility 
On the third day, the group visited Mitsubishi Motors, where they were given an overview of the company’s approach to electric vehicles, autonomous driving, and sustainable mobility. Mitsubishi’s strategy was presented as a forward-looking roadmap, balancing environmental responsibility with cutting-edge technological advancements.

 	Day 4 : Nippon Steel's Kashima Works 
The final day in east Japan concluded with a visit to Nippon Steel’s Kashima Works, one of the largest steel production sites in eastern Japan. Participants saw first-hand the scale and sophistication of Japanese industrial technology, including the blast furnace (BF) and basic oxygen furnace (BOF) technologies used in steel production. This visit provided a rare insight into the industrial heart of Japan.


Osaka : A Deep Dive into Innovation and Global Collaboration

After the intensive days in Tokyo, the second part of the journey took place in Osaka, a dynamic hub for industry, innovation, and global business collaboration.

 	Day 5: High-level Meetings at the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry’s Osaka Office 
The day began with a visit to the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan’s Osaka office, where Benoît Rulleau, CEO of Kansai Airports and board member of the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan, discussed his leadership experience in managing one of Japan’s busiest airports. He highlighted the airport’s innovations aimed at improving passenger experience and its strategies for disaster management. The morning continued with Jean-François Rauch, Head of Regional Branches & Activity / Kansai Desk Manager, who gave an overview of the activities and services of the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan outside of Tokyo.

 	Day 6 : Expo 2025 Osaka – A Glimpse into the Future 
The following day was dedicated to exploring Expo 2025 Osaka. Participants were guided through the French Pavilion by Sophie Braincourt, Director of Partnerships for the French Pavilion, where they experienced an immersive presentation showcasing France's cultural, artistic, and technological excellence. The theme of the pavilion, “Hymn to Love”, reflects the values of connection, sustainability, and innovation.
Throughout the day, the group also visited other national pavilions, including those of Japan, Belgium, Italy, and China, to explore each country’s approach to sustainable development, digital transformation, and global collaboration under the central Expo theme: “Designing Future Society for Our Lives”.


A Unique Opportunity to Connect, Learn, and Innovate
This Learning Expedition was not only an educational journey but also a platform for connecting with leading stakeholders in the Japanese business community. The experience has opened new doors for participants, providing them with valuable perspectives on global leadership, strategic innovation, and cross-cultural collaboration.

blocks.text: After the intensive days in Tokyo, the second part of the journey took place in Osaka , a dynamic hub for industry, innovation, and global business collaboration.

blocks.section: An immersive experience to discover Japan's unique business ecosystem.
blocks.text: Day 5: High-level Meetings at the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry’s Osaka Office

blocks.section: An immersive experience to discover Japan's unique business ecosystem.
blocks.text: The day began with a visit to the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan’s Osaka office , where Benoît Rulleau , CEO of Kansai Airports and board member of the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan, discussed his leadership experience in managing one of Japan’s busiest airports. He highlighted the airport’s innovations aimed at improving passenger experience and its strategies for disaster management . The morning continued with Jean-François Rauch , Head of Regional Branches & Activity / Kansai Desk Manager, who gave an overview of the activities and services of the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan outside of Tokyo.

blocks.section: An immersive experience to discover Japan's unique business ecosystem.
blocks.text: Day 6 : Expo 2025 Osaka – A Glimpse into the Future

blocks.section: An immersive experience to discover Japan's unique business ecosystem.
blocks.text: The following day was dedicated to exploring Expo 2025 Osaka . Participants were guided through the French Pavilion by Sophie Braincourt , Director of Partnerships for the French Pavilion, where they experienced an immersive presentation showcasing France's cultural, artistic, and technological excellence. The theme of the pavilion, “Hymn to Love” , reflects the values of connection, sustainability, and innovation.

blocks.section: An immersive experience to discover Japan's unique business ecosystem.
blocks.text: Throughout the day, the group also visited other national pavilions, including those of Japan , Belgium , Italy , and China , to explore each country’s approach to sustainable development , digital transformation , and global collaboration under the central Expo theme: “Designing Future Society for Our Lives” .

blocks.section: An immersive experience to discover Japan's unique business ecosystem.
blocks.text: A Unique Opportunity to Connect, Learn, and Innovate

blocks.section: An immersive experience to discover Japan's unique business ecosystem.
blocks.text: This Learning Expedition was not only an educational journey but also a platform for connecting with leading stakeholders in the Japanese business community. The experience has opened new doors for participants, providing them with valuable perspectives on global leadership , strategic innovation , and cross-cultural collaboration .

title: April: what's changing in Japan
description: Food prices, home delivery services, car-sharing... Everything that is changing in Japan from April.

blocks.text: Foresight

blocks.section: April: what's changing in Japan
blocks.text: April: what's changing in Japan

blocks.section: April: what's changing in Japan
blocks.text: Food prices, home delivery services, car-sharing... Everything that is changing in Japan from April.

blocks.section: April: what's changing in Japan
blocks.text: ​​​​​​ End of carpooling ban

blocks.section: April: what's changing in Japan
blocks.text: The ban on carpooling will be lifted in certain areas (Tokyo, Kanagawa, Aichi, Kyoto) under certain conditions (days and times). Fares will still remain the same as for cabs.

blocks.section: April: what's changing in Japan
blocks.text: Non-governmental organizations will be the main operators in areas where there is a shortage of cabs and other means of transport, with fares varying according to supply and demand.

blocks.section: April: what's changing in Japan
blocks.text: Rising food prices

blocks.section: April: what's changing in Japan
blocks.text: Food prices are set to continue rising in April. According to data from Teikoku Databank, traditionally high prices for raw materials and energy, combined with rising logistics and labor costs, are expected to result in a rapid rise of over 3,000 items in April (mainly processed food products).

blocks.section: April: what's changing in Japan
blocks.text: Coronavirus vaccines to be paid for under certain conditions

blocks.section: April: what's changing in Japan
blocks.text: The reimbursement of drugs and vaccines against the new coronavirus will be reviewed. For example, the Zocova coronavirus vaccine is expected to cost more than 15,000 yen for those benefiting from a 70% health insurance discount.

blocks.section: April: what's changing in Japan
blocks.text: People over 65 will benefit from a “co-payment” of up to 7,000 yen, allowing them to be vaccinated once a year from autumn to winter.

blocks.section: April: what's changing in Japan
blocks.text: Treatment for people under 65 will be considered as “voluntary vaccinations”, and the full amount will have to be paid by each individual in principle.

blocks.section: April: what's changing in Japan
blocks.text: Capping of overtime

blocks.section: April: what's changing in Japan
blocks.text: Following the labor reform law passed in 2018, overtime will be capped in certain sector. These include doctors (960 hours a year - with the exception of doctors and trainees in charge of emergencies and in rural areas), drivers in the transport sector (960 hours a year) as well as construction workers (360 hours a year).

blocks.section: April: what's changing in Japan
blocks.text: Higher prices for medical consultations

blocks.section: April: what's changing in Japan
blocks.text: Fees paid to health care providers will rise by 1.59%, with a further 2.5% increase planned for 2024, the aim being to increase the remuneration of nursing staff.

blocks.section: April: what's changing in Japan
blocks.text: Disability Discrimination Act comes into force

blocks.section: April: what's changing in Japan
blocks.text: Commercial operators and administrative bodies are required to provide accommodation.

title: Cross Chamber Event
description:
The event "Australia and Japan – A Bright Future for Hydrogen" was held on Thursday, October 5, 2023, at L'Espace@CCIFJ. In collaboration with the French-Australian Chamber of Commerce & Industry, this event highlighted the pivotal role of both nations in pioneering the hydrogen economy. 

The event served as a platform for industry leaders from France, Australia, and Japan in the energy and finance sectors to discuss the advantages of the trilateral partnerships and the opportunities available for industrial stakeholders. Key speakers included Yoshihiro Ueno, General Manager of Hydrogen Energy Division at Air Liquide Japan; Bruno Gaussorgues, Group Country Head Japan and Representative Director at Société Générale; and Taku Hasegawa from Kawasaki Heavy Industry, all based in Tokyo. Additionally, live contributions from Sydney featured Kam Ho, Managing Director of Total Eren; Simon Currie, CEO of Energy Estate; and Matthew Walden, a Partner specializing in Energy and Climate Advisory at Deloitte.

Thanks to in depth knowledge of the project, experience, and fluency in Japanese, exchanges are facilitated and encouraged. Maintaining the presence of a Japanese speaking representative in Tokyo on behalf of Banh Vang is a major asset in establishing the trust essential to any business relationship in Japan.

title: Become an exhibitor at EXPAT EXPO TOKYO 2021, the Fair for International Residents in Japan
description:
EXPAT EXPO TOKYO 2021 is only one exhibition for international residents in Japan.
The second edition will be held on November 5th and 6th, with Support of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan.
This expo gives foreign residents and their families the opportunity to meet companies, local governments, and organizations that provide goods and services in English. Also, visitors can enjoy Japanese culture by stage events and workshops, then get luxurious prizes!
More than 2.8 million of foreign nationals are living, working, and studying in Japan (Statistics Bureau, Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications). Although the growth rate is temporarily slowing down due to the COVID-19 spread, the number is likely to increase thanks to efforts by the government and businesses including introduction of “specified skilled worker” visa, recruitment of “highly skilled professionals”, and promotion of diversity. On the other hand, many foreign nationals are facing difficulties in daily lives because of language and cultural barriers. To respond to this situation, the 1st EXPAT EXPO TOKYO was held last year as a matching platform for internationals and local businesses providing foreigner-friendly services, and welcomed a lot of foreign nationals and their families. The two-day event will come back with a five times larger scale under the support of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan, Minato City, Japan National Tourism Organization (JNTO), Japan Association of Tourism Agents, and chambers of commerce in Japan.

Book your stand space
Application for EXPAT EXPO TOKYO 2021 is now open for all businesses aiming at international residents. As an alternative for the shrinking inbound market due to COVID-19, This event will be a unique opportunity to showcase your services and expand your brand recognition in the existing expat market in Japan. The sale will end when all the stand has been sold.
If interested in approaching international residents or HR and GA people in companies that employ foreign nationals, please contact expat_expo@inovent.co.jp

Informations :
 	Date: November 5-6, 2021 (Fri. & Sat.) 	Venue: Tokyo Metropolitan Industrial Trade Center Hamamatsucho-kan 	Contact：expat_expo(@)innovent.co.jp

blocks.section: Bel Japon wins the "Company of the Year" Award at the 2025 French Business Awards Ceremony
blocks.text: Bel Japan , the Japanese subsidiary of Group Bel, has been serving the local market for over 40 years with iconic brands like Kiri, Laughing Cow, and Mini Babybel.
