title: Block Council for Promotion of Foreign Direct Investment in Japan
description:
Block Council is a forum held every year since 2014 by all nine METI Regional Bureaus on a voluntary basis, together with the Investment Facilitation Division of METI and JETRO, and consisting local governments, business associations, financial institutions and companies.
Purpose of “Block Council” :
 	Exchange candid voices, opinions and needs in the regions 	Consider comprehensive collaboration and cooperation in the context of national policies 	Consider innovative projects and ideas that can be launched in the regions 	Encourage the regions to consider using foreign resources for revitalizing the local economies and societies

blocks.section: Breizh Café opens a new location in Strasbourg
blocks.text: Breizh Café continues its development with the opening of a new location in the heart of Strasbourg.

blocks.section: Breizh Café opens a new location in Strasbourg
blocks.text: It all began in 1996 in Tokyo, where Bertrand Larcher opened his first restaurant, offering a unique invitation to explore the connection between Brittany and Japan: respect for ingredients, a love of buckwheat and a constant pursuit of quality. Thirty years later, this vision has grown into a unique ecosystem, from creperies to buckwheat fields, from delicatessens to cider houses, stretching from Cancale to Paris and from Saint-Malo to Tokyo.

blocks.section: Breizh Café opens a new location in Strasbourg
blocks.text: Today, this adventure continues in Strasbourg, with a new location designed as a meeting point between two regions deeply attached to their identity and heritage.

blocks.section: Breizh Café opens a new location in Strasbourg
blocks.text: “Strasbourg is a city of culture with a rich heritage. We imagined this location as a meeting between two regions proud of their identity, brought together through taste, sharing and respect for producers,” says Bertrand Larcher.

blocks.section: Breizh Café opens a new location in Strasbourg
blocks.text: Located at 15 rue Sainte-Barbe , near Strasbourg Cathedral, the new restaurant offers Breizh Café's signature dishes alongside creations inspired by local ingredients.

blocks.section: Breizh Café opens a new location in Strasbourg
blocks.text: The menu features buckwheat galettes as well as recipes specially created for Strasbourg, including Munster cheese, mirabelle plum jam and other Alsatian specialties. Brittany IGP buckwheat and a selection of ciders complete the menu, bringing Breton and Alsatian know-how together.

blocks.section: Breizh Café opens a new location in Strasbourg
blocks.text: With this new opening, Breizh Café continues its development and, in Strasbourg as in Japan, carries on the same philosophy: building bridges between cultures through taste, craftsmanship and respect for ingredients.

title: Bridge on the Shikishima Way－100 Poems by Emperor Meiji－
description:
The author/translator Harold Wright, presently Professor Emeritus at Antioch College,
has studied Japanese poetry and literature under Professor Donald Keene, the famous Japanologist. About 40 years ago, Professor Wright was requested by the then Chief Priest of Meiji Jingu Shrine to translate into English 311 tanka poems of Emperor Meiji and 111 of that of Empress Shoken, his spouse; the Imperial couple known to be excellent poets. Many years have passed, and to the great happy surprise, Meiji Jingu has received lately from the Professor the translations of the “forty-years-old request”.
Today, 100 poems of the Emperor out of these translations are compiled in this book
Together with these translations, Professor Wright has expressed in his article, the chal-lenge and the joy that he experienced in translating the tanka poems, the essential heart of Japanese culture. Also included in this book, a commentary from Professor Nagata Kazuhiro, tanka poet and cell- biologist, explaining the difficulties of translating tanka poems.
The book is totally Japanese-English bilingual. 
We hope that the publication of this book will introduce tanka, the world oldest form of poetry supported by the Imperial Family and people of Japan alike, to many people around the world.
Please enjoy reading the book.
The book is available at major bookstores and Amazon.

title: Broadpeak: a leader in video streaming and digital content technology
description:
Founded in August 2010, Broadpeak established itself in Rennes, a center of excellence and a hub for scientific expertise and innovation. The Brittany-based company, whose founders largely come from Technicolor, has become, in just a few years, a leader in video streaming and digital content technology, serving more than 50 operators worldwide (cable and satellite), as well as television broadcasters.
Broadpeak’s software solutions are recognized for their exceptional flexibility, superior quality of experience for end users, high scalability (capable of handling millions of video streams per day), and optimal security, ensuring strong protection of subscribers’ content.
A successful international expansion
Broadpeak began its international expansion in 2012 with the development and creation of a subsidiary in Singapore. Two years later, the company opened an office in Brazil, followed by the creation of a subsidiary in the United States with a presence in New York and Denver. Momentum accelerated in 2016 with the opening of two offices in South America (Colombia and Peru) and in India.
Recipient of numerous innovation awards, notably from the French Ministry of Higher Education and Research in 2010, Broadpeak was awarded the Innovation Prize in March 2016 as one of the four winning companies at the Oscars of Ille-et-Vilaine, an annual event organized by Bretagne Commerce International.The four award-winning companies were offered a discovery trip to Japan, with the business support department of CCI France Japan in charge of organizing the program of meetings.
A Tokyo presence made possible thanks to the support of CCI France Japan
Jacques Le Mancq, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Broadpeak, traveled to Japan to combine company visits with meetings with Japanese partners.
“High-quality meetings, a very dynamic team, and a highly professional service, these are the key elements to remember about the teams at CCI France Japan. The initial contacts are very promising and point to rapid development growth. After just a few weeks, the meetings are already bearing fruit, with the start of potential partnerships with Japanese telecommunications operators”,  Jacques Le Mancq told us.
In spring 2017, CCI France Japan then supported Broadpeak’s establishment in Tokyo and now hosts two employees in the Chamber’s business center.
“I am extremely satisfied with the content and quality of the work carried out by the business support teams at CCI France Japan. It is a real springboard and a partner of choice for our current and future development in Japan, and this is only the beginning !” declared Jacques Le Mancq, pioneer of the Broadpeak venture.
More information: http://broadpeak.tv/

title: Business Regards croisés - 70 Years of Tefal, 50 Years in Japan
description:
In this new episode of Business - France-Japan Cross Perspectives, we meet Julien Major, Managing Director of Groupe SEB Japan Co., Ltd., on the occasion of Tefal's 70th anniversary. Founded in France in 1956, Tefal has become one of the few foreign household appliance brands to establish a lasting presence in Japan. Julien Major reflects on the keys to the success of a French company in one of the world's most demanding consumer markets.  
After holding positions within Groupe SEB in consumer goods, human resources, and international management, he now leads the group's Japanese subsidiary. Drawing on his international experience, particularly in Japan, he highlights several fundamental values that shape Franco-Japanese business relations, including humility, collaborative work, and the search for consensus. In Japan, major decisions are carefully prepared through a consensus-building process known as nemawashi before being formally approved and publicly announced.
"There is great importance placed on aligning stakeholders before making a decision public."
Japan: A Market Where Quality Allows No Compromise
According to Julien Major, the greatest challenge of the Japanese market lies in its exceptionally high quality standards. Japanese consumers evaluate not only the product itself but every aspect of the customer experience, including the packaging. This pursuit of "zero defects" encourages Groupe SEB Japan Co., Ltd.to systematically adapt its products to local habits rather than simply exporting models designed for other markets. This requires close collaboration between the Japanese teams and the group's international R&D centers to develop products specifically tailored to the expectations of Japanese consumers.
Innovation as the Key to Success
Tefal's strong position in Japan is built above all on innovation. In the early 2000s, Tefal brand Japan introduced electric kettles to a market where water was still predominantly heated on gas stoves. By emphasizing speed, safety, and energy efficiency, the company gradually transformed consumer habits. Today, innovation remains at the heart of the group's strategy. As Japanese homes tend to be more compact than their European counterparts, consumers favor versatile, space-saving, and easy-to-use appliances. This philosophy also led Groupe to enter one of Japan's most symbolic product categories: rice cookers, using infrared cooking technology developed by one of its Chinese subsidiaries.
Decide Slowly, Execute Quickly
Beyond product development, Julien Major also spoke about Japan's management culture. Compared with Europe, decision-making in Japan tends to devote more time to consultation and consensus-building among stakeholders. However, once a direction has been agreed upon, the entire organization shares a common understanding, allowing decisions to be executed quickly and in a coordinated manner. Managers assigned from overseas are expected to be good listeners and willing to reassess their own ways of working. Julien Major believes that, as an expatriate, it is first and foremost the manager's responsibility to adapt to the local environment, rather than expecting the environment to adapt to them.
Made in France, Adapted for Japan
Contrary to common assumptions, a large share of the products sold in Japan continues to be manufactured in France, particularly in Groupe SEB's factories in the Savoie region. This French manufacturing heritage reflects the group's industrial expertise, even though many Japanese consumers are unaware of the brand's French origins. In fact, some even perceive Tefal as a Japanese brand, illustrating just how successfully it has become embedded in the Japanese market.
In a mature market, Groupe SEB Japan Co., Ltd.continues to rely on innovation by creating entirely new product categories rather than simply following existing trends. According to Julien Major, companies willing to take risks and introduce genuine innovations will continue to stand out, even in a market often regarded as conservative.

title: Business Regards croisés – Airstar Japan: When French Lighting Expertise Illuminates the Japanese Events Industry
description:
In this new episode of Business Cross Perspectives, we meet Sébastien Phal, Managing Director of Airstar Japan. Having lived in Japan for many years, he leads the Japanese subsidiary of the world's leading manufacturer of lighting balloons, bringing French technological innovation and creativity to one of the most demanding markets in the world.
"It is a very unique industry and clearly a 100% French expertise."
Founded on a technology developed in Grenoble more than 30 years ago, Airstar has since expanded internationally. In the Asia-Pacific region, its growth has been supported in particular by Partex International, a company based in Singapore since 1993. Beyond its iconic illuminated balloons, Airstar designs lighting, decorative, and spatial solutions for events, exhibitions, and the film industry. Its expertise was notably used during the production of James Cameron's Titanic in the early 1990s.
From Major International Events to Entrepreneurship in Japan: A Demanding Yet Innovation-Friendly Market
Sébastien Phal's journey in Japan began in the wake of the major sporting events that marked the turn of the millennium. Following the Sydney Olympic Games, several major events took place across the Asia-Pacific region, including the America's Cup in New Zealand and the FIFA World Cup in Korea and Japan. Drawn by the region's dynamism, Sébastien Phal decided to settle in Japan. Over several years, he gained firsthand experience of Japanese corporate culture and the local events industry as an employee. It was during this period that he met Airstar's representatives in Asia and helped establish the company's Japanese office.
According to Sébastien Phal, the Japanese market combines high barriers to entry, strong domestic competition, and growing demand for original experiences. While lighting is often approached from a purely functional perspective, the luxury, events, and immersive experience sectors are increasingly seeking more creative solutions. In this context, Airstar Japan differentiates itself through a combination of technology, design, and lighting expertise, delivering projects that include the temporary illumination of historic temples and shrines in Kyoto. Airstar's event engineering capabilities are rapidly evolving toward modern technological solutions. While LED technology now forms the technical foundation of its products, the real added value lies in connectivity and digital tools, enabling remote control of lighting effects, colors, and atmospheres.
From the Olympic Torch to Cinema, Including Titanic
The applications of this technology span an exceptionally wide range of industries. Historically linked to the film sector, the company notably contributed to the production of James Cameron's Titanic in the early 1990s. Today, in Japan, it continues to be involved in other prestigious projects. During the Tokyo Olympic Games, Airstar was selected to illuminate the Olympic torch relay and its convoy, lighting more than 200 meters of roadway within Toyota Group's headquarters complex in Aichi Prefecture. The company has also created scenographic installations for international artists, including the recent Japan concert of singer Bad Bunny. Sébastien Phal also highlights his participation in the Opus project, the final work of composer Ryuichi Sakamoto, for which Airstar's teams developed a dedicated lighting solution to support the film production process.
Although Airstar's expertise extends to film production, construction sites, and emergency response operations, its Japanese subsidiary primarily focuses on the corporate and B2B events market. Luxury brands, fashion companies, and major product launches represent its core business. For these clients, events are above all communication platforms where the creative design of space plays a crucial role, even for highly temporary operations whose effective duration may sometimes last only a few hours.
Next Steps: Meeting Regulatory Challenges and Expanding the Rental Model
The Japanese market presents a significant challenge for foreign technologies due to its stringent certification requirements and technical standards, which are designed to protect the domestic market and favor local solutions. Whether related to electrical standards, safety regulations, or technical compliance, import barriers remain substantial. To overcome these challenges and establish a strong market presence, Airstar Japan has developed a business model centered primarily on equipment rental and temporary installations. The company owns a substantial fleet of equipment that it deploys across approximately one hundred operations each year—effectively launching a new project every two or three days. Sébastien Phal relies on in-house teams capable of managing the entire value chain, from planning and installation to technical programming and dismantling. While decision-making is largely concentrated in Tokyo, Japan's highly efficient logistics network enables the company to operate nationwide, from Hokkaido to Okinawa. 
Looking ahead, several major upcoming events are already expected to serve as significant growth drivers for the company.

blocks.text: Business regards croisés - Andaz Tokyo redefine luxury lifestyle experiences

blocks.section: Business regards croisés - Andaz Tokyo redefine luxury lifestyle experiences
blocks.text: In this new episode of our podcast series Business Regards Croisés , we interviewed Thomas Vidal, General Manager of the Andaz Tokyo Toranomon Hills, one of Tokyo’s most iconic luxury lifestyle hotels. The hotel has established itself as a unique hybrid destination, serving not only as a place to stay but also as a hub for culture and events, where the overall experience is as important as the accommodation itself.

blocks.section: Business regards croisés - Andaz Tokyo redefine luxury lifestyle experiences
blocks.text: A graduate of ESSEC Business School, Thomas Vidal has built most of his career in Asia, particularly in Japan, where he has lived for more than twelve years.

blocks.section: Business regards croisés - Andaz Tokyo redefine luxury lifestyle experiences
blocks.text: “At Tokyo, luxury hospitality has become a playground for experiences”

blocks.section: Business regards croisés - Andaz Tokyo redefine luxury lifestyle experiences
blocks.text: Luxury hospitality as a complete experience

blocks.section: Business regards croisés - Andaz Tokyo redefine luxury lifestyle experiences
blocks.text: Tokyo is now establishing itself as a major destination in the global luxury market, driven by the rebound of international tourism after Covid. Long considered less central than Paris, London, or New York in this segment, the city is now experiencing rapid growth. The market nevertheless remains deeply shaped by a strong local identity, structured around omotenashi and historic hotels with highly codified standards. This specificity forces international hotel groups to adapt their offerings to particularly demanding expectations. After the pandemic, the sector rebounded quickly, notably through the rise of domestic tourism and the staycation phenomenon. In this context, hotels are no longer limited to accommodation alone.

blocks.section: Business regards croisés - Andaz Tokyo redefine luxury lifestyle experiences
blocks.text: Japan: a meticulous and evolving clientele

blocks.section: Business regards croisés - Andaz Tokyo redefine luxury lifestyle experiences
blocks.text: While Japanese guests continue to be defined by extremely high standards and attention to detail, younger generations are rapidly shifting toward more experiential expectations, seeking immersive, modern, and visually appealing stays.

blocks.section: Business regards croisés - Andaz Tokyo redefine luxury lifestyle experiences
blocks.text: Within this culture of extreme attention to detail, certain everyday aspects of hotel life take on particular importance. Slippers are a symbolic example: from the moment guests enter their room, their presence, quality, and comfort directly contribute to the perception of service. This level of precision, sometimes barely noticeable to international guests, can have a real impact on overall satisfaction.

blocks.section: Business regards croisés - Andaz Tokyo redefine luxury lifestyle experiences
blocks.text: “If the slippers are hard to find, and especially if they are not of very good quality, you lose quite a few points in guest satisfaction.”

blocks.section: Business regards croisés - Andaz Tokyo redefine luxury lifestyle experiences
blocks.text: Management and corporate culture in an international environment

blocks.section: Business regards croisés - Andaz Tokyo redefine luxury lifestyle experiences
blocks.text: In such a complex environment, Thomas Vidal insists on one central principle: people make the difference. Management is built around a leadership philosophy focused on taking care of employees. In highly international hotels such as those in Tokyo, managing multicultural teams becomes a daily challenge, yet this diversity fuels creativity, encourages innovation, and strengthens the ability of hotels to cater to an increasingly global clientele.

blocks.section: Business regards croisés - Andaz Tokyo redefine luxury lifestyle experiences
blocks.text: Thomas Vidal’s career reflects the current transformation of luxury hospitality in Japan: a sector undergoing hybridization, where traditional Japanese excellence meets international experience-driven standards. Between the tourism boom, the rise of lifestyle hospitality, and the reinvention of hospitality formats, Tokyo is more than ever establishing itself as a major experimental ground for the world’s leading luxury hotel players.

title: Business Regards Croisés - AXA Japan, Insurance Facing Japan’s New Challenges
description:
In this new episode of Business - Crossed Perspectives France-Japan, we meet Christophe Avenel, President of AXA Japan since April 2026. After several years within the AXA Group and a long experience in Japan, he looks back on the particular place of insurance in the Japanese economy, the evolution of savings behaviours and the transformations to come in the sector. With a life insurance market among the largest in the world, Japan today represents a strategic market for AXA, which has been established there for more than 40 years.
The Japan, a strategic market for AXA
The Japanese insurance market is among the largest in the world, accounting for approximately 300 billion euros for life insurance and 100 billion for non-life insurance. AXA Japan today occupies an important place within the Group, of which it is the first business in Asia. During this episode, Christophe Avenel looks back on the history of AXA’s establishment in Japan and on the integration of Nippon Dantai in the early 2000s, considered a decisive step in the Group’s development among Japanese SMEs.
This long-standing presence also allows AXA to closely observe the evolution of the Japanese economy and the changes affecting companies and households.
From savings to investment
After several decades of deflation and rates close to zero, Japan is entering a new period: inflation, rising interest rates and the development of NISA could gradually change the savings habits of Japanese households, a significant part of whose savings is still held in cash or deposits.
For AXA, this evolution opens up new perspectives, particularly around products combining savings and protection. But it also raises a broader question: how will Japanese people change their relationship with investment after decades of low inflation and very low interest rates?
A new transformation with artificial intelligence
Like the financial sector as a whole, insurance is also facing the rise of artificial intelligence. For AXA Japan, the applications are numerous: customer relations, automation, software development or even employee productivity.
With nearly 9 000 employees in Japan, this transformation also represents a management and organisational challenge. Christophe Avenel discusses the opportunities offered by AI, but also the new risks it is creating, particularly in terms of cybersecurity.
Can technology replace humans?
While some insurance operations can now be fully digitalised, not all situations lend themselves to a relationship based solely on technology. Christophe Avenel therefore looks back on the place that humans must retain in a sector based on trust when it comes to supporting customers during important moments in their lives.
“There will always be moments when people will want to talk to someone. Our role is to make this interaction available at the right time.” 
Between the evolution of savings, rising interest rates, artificial intelligence and the transformation of the ways of interacting with customers, this episode offers a look at the major changes in the insurance sector in Japan and how AXA intends to support them.
AXA JAPAN

title: Business regards croisés - Danone: The HR challenges of foreign companies in Japan
description:
In this new episode of Business – Cross Perspectives, we meet Jean-Renaud Humblot, who joined Danone as HR Director for Japan and South Korea after six years in Australia and New Zealand. Leading human resources in a highly competitive environment, he shares insights into the challenges faced by foreign companies in Japan and the country’s strategic importance for the group.
“Japan is a Danone superstar”
Attracting talent in an ultra-competitive gaishikei market
For gaishikei—foreign companies established in Japan—the job market and talent management are extremely competitive. Indeed, looking for profiles that combine strong expertise with a good command of English immediately limits the pool of candidates. Talent with experience in multinational corporations (MNCs) represents only about 2% of Japan’s workforce. As a result, competition between companies for these profiles is particularly intense.
The loyalty of Japanese employees is often described as legendary. Even in a foreign company like Danone, some employees can reach 15, 20 or even 35 years of tenure. However, in the gaishikei environment, talents tend to have greater mobility as they can leverage competition between companies. Despite this, genuine loyalty remains, especially when employees identify with the company’s culture and values.
Reading between the lines: the intercultural challenge
When faced with communication gaps between French and Japanese professionals, one quickly notices that interactions in Japan tend to be less direct. It is therefore necessary to learn how to read between the lines and understand non-verbal signals. This cultural subtlety can sometimes be surprising.
Jean-Renaud Humblot notably mentions his discovery of taishoku daikō, agencies that handle employee resignations on their behalf.
When such situations occur, questions arise: at what point did dialogue break down? Why did the employee not feel comfortable enough to express their difficulties or discuss resignation internally? For HR teams, this highlights the importance of creating an environment built on trust and open communication.
Gender equality
Regarding gender equality in the workplace, Danone strives to support promotions and reduce pay gaps. Within Danone Japan, no salary gap has been observed between men and women in equivalent positions.
Women represent around 40% of managers, with an even higher proportion at headquarters, although the share is lower in factories. The company also ensures that maternity does not hinder careers. Beyond legal requirements, Danone offers 18 weeks of maternity leave and maintains salary progression during this period in order to preserve pay equality.
Japan’s place in the group’s strategy
The group operates in several segments: specialized nutrition, water, and dairy products. In the dairy segment, Japan is among the most successful markets worldwide. In 2025, Danone recorded its sixth consecutive year of double-digit growth in Japan.

blocks.section: Business regards croisés - Danone: The HR challenges of foreign companies in Japan
blocks.text: The loyalty of Japanese employees is often described as legendary. Even in a foreign company like Danone, some employees can reach 15, 20 or even 35 years of tenure. However, in the gaishikei environment, talents tend to have greater mobility as they can leverage competition between companies. Despite this, genuine loyalty remains, especially when employees identify with the company’s culture and values.

blocks.section: Business regards croisés - Danone: The HR challenges of foreign companies in Japan
blocks.text: Reading between the lines: the intercultural challenge

blocks.section: Business regards croisés - Danone: The HR challenges of foreign companies in Japan
blocks.text: When faced with communication gaps between French and Japanese professionals, one quickly notices that interactions in Japan tend to be less direct. It is therefore necessary to learn how to read between the lines and understand non-verbal signals. This cultural subtlety can sometimes be surprising.

blocks.section: Business regards croisés - Danone: The HR challenges of foreign companies in Japan
blocks.text: Jean-Renaud Humblot notably mentions his discovery of taishoku daikō , agencies that handle employee resignations on their behalf.

blocks.section: Business regards croisés - Danone: The HR challenges of foreign companies in Japan
blocks.text: When such situations occur, questions arise: at what point did dialogue break down? Why did the employee not feel comfortable enough to express their difficulties or discuss resignation internally? For HR teams, this highlights the importance of creating an environment built on trust and open communication.

blocks.section: Business regards croisés - Danone: The HR challenges of foreign companies in Japan
blocks.text: Gender equality

blocks.section: Business regards croisés - Danone: The HR challenges of foreign companies in Japan
blocks.text: Regarding gender equality in the workplace, Danone strives to support promotions and reduce pay gaps. Within Danone Japan, no salary gap has been observed between men and women in equivalent positions.

blocks.section: Business regards croisés - Danone: The HR challenges of foreign companies in Japan
blocks.text: Women represent around 40% of managers, with an even higher proportion at headquarters, although the share is lower in factories. The company also ensures that maternity does not hinder careers. Beyond legal requirements, Danone offers 18 weeks of maternity leave and maintains salary progression during this period in order to preserve pay equality.

blocks.section: Business regards croisés - Danone: The HR challenges of foreign companies in Japan
blocks.text: Japan’s place in the group’s strategy

blocks.section: Business regards croisés - Danone: The HR challenges of foreign companies in Japan
blocks.text: The group operates in several segments: specialized nutrition, water, and dairy products. In the dairy segment, Japan is among the most successful markets worldwide. In 2025, Danone recorded its sixth consecutive year of double-digit growth in Japan.

blocks.section: Business regards croisés - Danone: The HR challenges of foreign companies in Japan

title: Business Regards croisés – MCDecaux is revolutionizing urban advertising in Japan

blocks.text: Interview

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – MCDecaux is revolutionizing urban advertising in Japan
blocks.text: Business Regards croisés – MCDecaux is revolutionizing urban advertising in Japan

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – MCDecaux is revolutionizing urban advertising in Japan
blocks.text: In this new episode of Business Cross Perspectives, we meet Malik Roumane, President & CEO of JCDecaux Japan (MCDecaux). Drawing on a rich career spanning industry, luxury, and B2B, he shares his vision of a unique model that combines innovation, public service, and local adaptation in Japan’s demanding market.

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – MCDecaux is revolutionizing urban advertising in Japan
blocks.text: "Everyone has to benefit from it: the city, the user, and the advertiser."

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – MCDecaux is revolutionizing urban advertising in Japan
blocks.text: Malik Roumane’s career path

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – MCDecaux is revolutionizing urban advertising in Japan
blocks.text: Malik Roumane’s journey in Japan follows a three-stage trajectory. He began in industry, notably with Saint-Gobain, working between France and Japan, where he developed strong expertise in structured and technical environments. He then spent around ten years in the luxury sector with Richemont before transitioning into B2B.

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – MCDecaux is revolutionizing urban advertising in Japan
blocks.text: This third chapter led him to manage various business activities in Japan, culminating in his appointment as head of JCDecaux three and a half years ago. This diversity of experience is now a key asset in the way he leads the company, combining operational excellence, brand sensitivity, and a deep understanding of local dynamics.

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – MCDecaux is revolutionizing urban advertising in Japan
blocks.text: JCDecaux: a unique model serving cities

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – MCDecaux is revolutionizing urban advertising in Japan
blocks.text: Founded in 1964, JCDecaux is built on a simple yet revolutionary idea: financing street furniture through advertising. This model enables cities to benefit from modern, well-maintained, and evolving infrastructure without direct cost to public finances.

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – MCDecaux is revolutionizing urban advertising in Japan
blocks.text: Beyond bus shelters, the offering has significantly expanded over time to include digital services, connectivity, charging solutions, and even initiatives contributing to urban greening. The challenge is no longer just to install infrastructure, but to meet the evolving needs of cities and their residents with a long-term perspective.

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – MCDecaux is revolutionizing urban advertising in Japan
blocks.text: A pioneering presence in Japan

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – MCDecaux is revolutionizing urban advertising in Japan
blocks.text: JCDecaux’s entry into Japan is a textbook case. At the time, advertising in public spaces was not permitted, making the model initially inapplicable. It required extensive engagement with authorities, particularly the MLIT, to demonstrate its benefits.

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – MCDecaux is revolutionizing urban advertising in Japan
blocks.text: The first implementation took place in Yokohama, followed by gradual expansion to other major cities, including Tokyo. A key factor in this success was the creation of a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation, leading to the birth of MCDecaux. This partnership helped legitimize the model and facilitate its adoption within a specific cultural and regulatory context.

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – MCDecaux is revolutionizing urban advertising in Japan
blocks.text: In a Japanese urban environment often perceived as visually saturated, JCDecaux has chosen to prioritize quality over quantity. The company pays close attention to placement, integration, and surroundings to avoid visual pollution.

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – MCDecaux is revolutionizing urban advertising in Japan
blocks.text: This approach helps reposition outdoor advertising as a premium medium, capable of enhancing brands rather than blending into background noise. Major advertisers, particularly in the luxury and automotive sectors, find in it a platform aligned with their image and standards.

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – MCDecaux is revolutionizing urban advertising in Japan
blocks.text: Innovation and Digital

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – MCDecaux is revolutionizing urban advertising in Japan
blocks.text: Technological advancements are opening up new opportunities for the industry. The growth of digital media enables far more agile and targeted delivery of advertising campaigns. Through programmatic buying, advertisers can tailor their messages based on time, location, or external factors such as weather conditions.

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – MCDecaux is revolutionizing urban advertising in Japan
blocks.text: This flexibility creates new ways to engage audiences, while maintaining strong complementarity with traditional formats, which ensure continuous presence and high visibility.

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – MCDecaux is revolutionizing urban advertising in Japan
blocks.text: In Japan, street furniture also plays a vital role in public communication, particularly in the event of natural disasters. Digital displays can be immediately activated by authorities to broadcast alerts, guide the public, and support crisis management. This function further strengthens JCDecaux’s position as an integrated urban player, beyond its advertising role.

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – MCDecaux is revolutionizing urban advertising in Japan
blocks.text: Supporting Japan’s Internationalization

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – MCDecaux is revolutionizing urban advertising in Japan
blocks.text: In a context of demographic decline, Japan is increasingly required to evolve by integrating more international talent. For Malik Roumane, this transformation is both inevitable and an opportunity.

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – MCDecaux is revolutionizing urban advertising in Japan
blocks.text: The goal is to build an environment capable of balancing Japan’s unique characteristics with growing global openness. In the long term, business success will depend on the ability to create hybrid organizations that combine cultures and expertise, while maintaining the right balance within the local context.

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – MCDecaux is revolutionizing urban advertising in Japan

title: Business Regards croisés - PwC: M&A, Tax, ERP, Cybersecurity… What Businesses Need
description:
In this new episode of Business - Regards Croisés France-Japon, we meet Paul Shon, Partner at PwC and Head of the French Desk for Japan & Korea. After several years supporting French companies in Japan, he discusses the changing needs of businesses, the transformation of the Japanese market and the challenges companies face as they develop their activities. ERP, cybersecurity, M&A, tax and foreign investment are among the key topics increasingly shaping the strategies of companies operating in Japan.
The French Desk, a bridge between France and Japan
PwC is now present in nearly 150 countries and employs around 350,000 people worldwide, including approximately 13,000 in Japan. The firm supports companies across a wide range of areas, from audit and tax to management consulting, transactions and mergers and acquisitions. In Japan, PwC works with both Japanese companies and international groups operating in the country.
For French companies, the French Desk plays a particular role by bridging French and Japanese business practices. With nearly 600 French companies established in Japan, this understanding of both environments enables PwC to support companies in their operations and development projects.
ERP and cybersecurity, new challenges for companies
As in many markets, Japanese companies are facing growing needs to transform their information systems. ERP projects, particularly involving solutions such as SAP, account for a significant share of these new demands. PwC supports companies in choosing the right tools, defining their transformation strategy and implementing these systems, projects that can take several years to complete.
Cybersecurity has also become a major concern. Cyberattacks now affect organizations across all sectors and involve senior management, financial and legal teams, as well as risk management functions. For PwC, these transformations therefore require support that goes beyond purely technological issues.
Japan, a market seeking to attract foreign investment
The Japanese government is now seeking to strengthen the country's attractiveness to foreign investors, particularly in strategic sectors such as semiconductors, artificial intelligence, data centers, financial services, biopharma and renewable energy.
This dynamic is creating new opportunities for French companies already operating in Japan. French foreign direct investment in Japan amounts to around €16 billion, while Japanese investment in France stands at approximately €13.5 billion. For PwC, these flows could continue to grow, particularly through mergers and acquisitions.
M&A and tax: supporting companies in a complex environment
Mergers and acquisitions are another important area for PwC Japan. From identifying potential targets to conducting financial, tax and legal due diligence, and then supporting post-acquisition integration, the firm assists companies throughout the process. In French-Japanese transactions, understanding cultural differences is also an important part of the equation.
“It's not just about numbers. It's not just about law or tax. It's about something beyond that. It's about people.”
Tax is another important issue for international groups, particularly when it comes to transfer pricing between different entities within the same group. For French companies operating in Japan, understanding local rules and preparing the necessary documentation can help secure their operations.
Between the transformation of information systems, cybersecurity, investment, M&A and tax, this episode offers an insight into the new needs of companies in Japan and PwC's role in supporting French companies as they develop their activities in the Japanese market.
PwC

title: Business Regards croisés – Tokyo Catering Club : Reinventing Catering in Japan

blocks.text: Interview

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – Tokyo Catering Club : Reinventing Catering in Japan
blocks.text: Business Regards croisés – Tokyo Catering Club : Reinventing Catering in Japan

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – Tokyo Catering Club : Reinventing Catering in Japan
blocks.text: In this new episode of Business – Cross Perspectives , we meet Antréas Garabedian, Co-Founder & CEO of Tokyo Catering Club Co. Ltd. Based in Tokyo for the past two years, he represents a new generation of entrepreneurs choosing Japan as a testing ground, developing a catering model that is flexible, international, and deeply rooted in local realities.

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – Tokyo Catering Club : Reinventing Catering in Japan
blocks.text: “We’re not just here to deliver food. We’re here to create an experience people remember.”

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – Tokyo Catering Club : Reinventing Catering in Japan
blocks.text: From Real Estate in France to Entrepreneurship in Japan: A Leap Guided by Intuition

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – Tokyo Catering Club : Reinventing Catering in Japan
blocks.text: Antréas Garabedian’s journey began in France in the real estate sector, where he led a stable life. Long attracted to Japanese culture and gastronomy, he gradually developed the idea of moving there. After several stays, the plan took shape—only to be put on hold by the global health crisis for nearly three years. When borders reopened, he finally moved to Tokyo with his partner and chose to pursue entrepreneurship. This decision marked a true shift in both geography and career.

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – Tokyo Catering Club : Reinventing Catering in Japan
blocks.text: Establishing a Business in Japan: A Demanding Market Built on Trust

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – Tokyo Catering Club : Reinventing Catering in Japan
blocks.text: The Japanese catering market is defined by high standards, where quality, precision, and reliability are essential. Long-term relationships and trusted networks play a key role. For a foreign company, integration takes time. Tokyo Catering Club had to adapt to local codes, overcome language barriers, and gradually gain access to supplier networks—often through recommendations. At the same time, growing demand from large international companies has created opportunities for providers able to operate in English and meet global standards.

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – Tokyo Catering Club : Reinventing Catering in Japan
blocks.text: A Hybrid Model to Meet International Demand

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – Tokyo Catering Club : Reinventing Catering in Japan
blocks.text: The company goes beyond traditional catering by developing a hybrid approach that combines catering services with event production. It operates across the entire value chain: food, staff, furniture, and logistics. This positioning, still relatively uncommon in Japan—allows it to act as a single point of contact for international clients seeking efficiency. At the same time, Tokyo Catering Club has adapted its original model. Initially designed as an aggregator of producers and artisans, it has evolved into a structure combining in-house production with a network of local partners. This hybridization ensures both consistent quality and the ability to scale quickly.

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – Tokyo Catering Club : Reinventing Catering in Japan
blocks.text: The company can manage events of widely varying sizes, including operations for up to 2,500 people. It also adapts to tight deadlines, extended hours, and complex requirements. Its operations rely on a dedicated kitchen, in-house logistics with its own refrigerated vehicles, and equipment capable of handling large volumes and multiple events simultaneously. This operational control strengthens its ability to deliver reliable, high-quality services under any constraints.

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – Tokyo Catering Club : Reinventing Catering in Japan
blocks.text: Expertise in Under-Served Specific Needs

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – Tokyo Catering Club : Reinventing Catering in Japan
blocks.text: Certain segments of the Japanese catering market remain underdeveloped, particularly when it comes to specific dietary requirements. Tokyo Catering Club has positioned itself to meet needs such as halal-friendly, vegan, and gluten-free options, while also incorporating diverse cultural expectations. This expertise allows the company to work with embassies, Middle Eastern clients, and foreign cultural institutions organizing events in Tokyo. Although this demand remains niche, it represents a strong lever for differentiation and growth.

blocks.section: Business Regards croisés – Tokyo Catering Club : Reinventing Catering in Japan

title: Business Summit: huge success for our 3rd edition
description:
The CCI France Japon ends up its 2020 Business session with its major event: the 3rd edition of the Business Summit, on « Growth Opportunities in Africa, towards New Business Partnership », after a series of successful sectorial events in Hybrid format (Energy, Healthcare, Space, Mobility,…).
The French-Japanese Business Summit has become the essential event for the French and Japanese business community, willing to develop partnerships and shape the future together, in their country and beyond. This conference took a new major step this year, by enlarging its participation worldwide thanks to live broadcasting on top of presentials. Despite the sanitary context, the event attracted more than 550 participants worldwide, all connected towards listening inspiring speakers discuss :
 	Introduction and New approaches in Africa, 	Investments, 	Trends by Geographies and Markets, 	Technology and Innovation, 	Access to care, 	SDG Outlook, 	A modern and Integrated Africa. 
The day opened with 5 prestigious speakers. Armel CAHIERRE, President, French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan, Philippe SETTON, French Ambassador to Japan, YONETANI Koji, Deputy Assistant Minister, Middle Eastern and African Affairs Bureau, MOFA, OCHI Hitoshi Vice Chair, Keidanren / Chair, Committee on Europe (President and CEO , Mitsubishi Chemical Holdings Corporation) and IMAI Toshimitsu, COO for Africa Division, Toyota Tsusho Corporation. All insisted on the importance of partnerships between Japan, France and African countries.
During the day, 25 top level speakers from Europe and Japan shared their operational experience in Africa, their challenges (climate change, COVID19), and their vision.
Among the many prestigious speakers: M. Ashwani GUPTA, Director representative executive officer, chief operating officer NISSAN motors, Oussouby SACKO, President of the Kyoto Seika University, OSHIMA Masahiko, Deputy president Head of SMBC, MUTO Megumi Deputy Director, Ogata Sadako research Institute for Peace and Dev. at JICA or Lionel ZINSOU Managing Partner of Southbridge, Former Prime Minister of Benin.
The lunch by Chef Olivier-owner of Chez Olivier, 1 Michelin star in Tokyo, was a great occasion to network.  
Among the 550 participants, not less than 18 African Embassies delegations,  hundreds of companies, journalists and 11 prestigious Japanese universities representants enjoyed the journey.
Confident after strong attendance numbers and positive feedbacks, the CCI France Japon is giving rendez vous November 9 for its 4th Business Summit. The topic will be decided soon.
Do not hesitate to contact us to be part of next year's journey!

title: Business Summit: huge success for our 5th edition
description:
On November 29th, over 800 participants attended the 5th edition of the French Japanese Business Summit titled “Japan as a model for the future - What learnings can be relevant for the world?”, after a series of successful sectorial conferences held throughout the year (on Energy, Healthcare, Space, Mobility...)
 
Since 2018, the French-Japanese Business Summit has become a flagship event for the French and Japanese business community, aiming to strengthen and highlight partnerships towards the future.
This edition was held in a hybrid format that live-streamed keynotes and plenary discussions featuring over 30 top-level speakers. The participants heard from ISHIBA Shigeru, BAN Shigeru, Christophe WEBER, and many other experts, high level government officials and top-level executives from major companies on the following topics:
 	REWARDS OF TRANSFORMATION 	NEW ENGINES FOR GROWTH 	A NATION OF EXCELLENCY, CREATIVITY & CULTURE 	THE FUTURE OF WORK 	A NATION OF INNOVATION & TECHNOLOGY 
The Opening Ceremony gave off an inspiring start with 4 prestigious speakers: Jérôme CHOUCHAN, President of the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan; MATSUO Takehiko, Director General, Trade Policy Bureau, Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry; Philippe SETTON, French Ambassador to Japan and SATO Yoshio, Chair of Committee on Europe of Keidanren.

They all recalled the undeniable qualities of the Japanese model: diligence in work, sense of service and excellence in execution, refinement and finally the importance of the common good. They also tried to bring their answers to the challenges the country is facing today: the aging population, the energy transition, the work-life balance and the gender parity.

During the day, more than 30 high-level speakers shared their views on the Japanese model and reminded us of the importance of France-Japan collaboration to play a key role in the post-covid world.

Prestigious speakers include:
ISHIBA Shigeru, Member of the House of Representatives, INOUE Kazuyuki, President and Representative Director, Shimizu Corporation, GOTO Takashi, President and Representative Director President and Chief Executive Officer, Seibu Holdings, BAN Shigeru, Architect, SHIGERU BAN ARCHITECTS Professor, Keio University, Christophe WEBER, President and Chief Executive Officer, Takeda Pharmaceutical Company Limited, NODA Yumiko, Chairman & Representative Director, Veolia Japan K.K., NONAKA Ikujiro, Professor Emeritus, Hitotsubashi University, Virginie CAVALLI, President and CEO, Air Liquide Japan G.K and NISHIMURA Motohiko, Executive Officer, Deputy General Manager, Hydrogen Strategy Division, Kawasaki Heavy Industries, Ltd.

The lunch served by Chef-owner of Chez Olivier, Olivier Oddos was a great networking opportunity for speakers and participants.
In 2023, the 6th edition of the Business Summit will be held on November 28th – we hope that you will be part of the discussion! The topic will be announced soon.
Do not hesitate to contact us to be part of next year's journey!
Finally, we would like to express our gratitude again to the following sponsors and partners for their support of this event.

title: Business Summit: huge success for our 6th edition
description:
On November 28th, around 1,000 participants attended the 6th edition of the French Japanese Business Summit titled “Innovation: Racing for a global advantage”, after a series of successful sectorial conferences held throughout the year (on Energy, Healthcare, Space, Mobility...)
Since 2018, the French-Japanese Business Summit has become a flagship event for the French and Japanese business community, aiming to strengthen and highlight partnerships towards the future.
This edition was held in Nikkei Hall in Tokyo and welcomed over 30 top-level speakers. The participants heard from top-level executives from well-known French and Japanese companies, high level government officials and prestigious academics.
The Opening Ceremony gave off an inspiring start with 4 prestigious speakers: Jérôme CHOUCHAN, President of the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan, HIGASHIHARA Toshiaki, Vice Chair, Chair of Committee on Europe, Keidanren, Philippe SETTON, French Ambassador to Japan, and KONO Taro, Minister for Digital Transformation

title: BuyCo: the logistics management platform conquering the Japanese market
description: Découvrez comment la CCI France Japon a accompagné BuyCo dans son expansion au Japon dans les secteurs de la tech et de la logistique.

blocks.text: BuyCo: the logistics management platform conquering the Japanese market

blocks.section: BuyCo: the logistics management platform conquering the Japanese market
blocks.text: In January 2023, the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan supported several French companies in Japan, including BuyCo, as part of a Team France Export prospecting mission during the visit of a French ministerial delegation.

blocks.section: BuyCo: the logistics management platform conquering the Japanese market
blocks.text: Since 2015, BuyCo has been developing a platform to manage and optimize container transportation. This SaaS platform allows logistics chain participants to be centralized and information to be collected, daily operations to be automated, shipments to be tracked in real time, and overall visibility to be provided. The company's platform has been implemented and used by large companies: 4,500 users in more than 70 countries.

blocks.section: BuyCo: the logistics management platform conquering the Japanese market
blocks.text: Thanks to this prospecting mission, BuyCo received confirmation that its offer was also of interest to the Japanese market, which allowed it to secure 3 qualified meetings with major Japanese players specializing in this sector. BuyCo has officially signed a contract with one of these 3 companies and is in the process of finalizing a contract with another, which will be officially signed very soon.

blocks.section: BuyCo: the logistics management platform conquering the Japanese market
blocks.text: "The Japanese market represents a market with very high potential for our transportation software publishing business for importers and exporters. The French Chamber of Commerce in Japan has been able to support us by offering solutions tailored to our needs, particularly in commercial prospecting, which requires knowledge of the Japanese market and its language. Thanks to Team France Export, we were able to achieve our goals more quickly."

title: Caderas Martin in Japan : a new step, true to who we are
description:
For over forty years, we have worked alongside Japanese companies. Today, that relationship enters a new phase : the launch of Caderas Martin Japan in Tokyo.

Over those four decades, our Japanese clients in France showed us what their market expects. They shared their way of working, their standards, and an approach to business relationships unlike any other.
Caderas Martin Japan is the result of that history and of a meeting between Laurent Dantan, Chartered Accountant and President of the Caderas Martin Group, and Mr. Ko Koike, a Japanese CPA. You don’t establish yourself in Japan without those who know it from within. This partnership reflects how we choose to grow: through precise expertise and a strong local foundation.
Our clients in Japan now have a dedicated structure, with their own teams and points of contact, held to the same standards as in France. Deadlines, Japanese regulatory matters, day-to-day support, everything becomes more seamless.
In Paris, our Japan Desk continues to support Japanese companies establishing themselves in France. With Caderas Martin Japan, the circle is complete: one firm, two countries, the same commitment to staying close to our clients.
This presence responds to real needs and to relationships already built. To our Japanese partners and clients, thank you for these forty years of trust. This new company is yours as much as ours.

日本とフランスのあいだで、これからも。
“Between Japan and France, today and tomorrow.”

title: Capgemini to acquire Multibook’s SAP services business in Japan and South East Asia
description:
The acquisition of Multibook’s SAP arm will enable Capgemini to help more clients in Japan and beyond to accelerate their business transformation to the cloud. It supports the Group’s growth ambition in the Asia-Pacific region
 Capgemini announced that it has signed an agreement for the acquisition of Multibook’s SAP global services line. The acquisition will enable Capgemini to further build its SAP capabilities and enrich its client portfolio of business services in Japan and South East Asia. Headquartered in Tokyo, Multibook has developed an 80+ people strong business delivering global SAP rollouts for its clients. Its SAP business operates in Japan and across Asia-Pacific and a subsidiary in the USA. It has established a strong relationship with industry leading brands in Japan and beyond, as part of the global SAP model.  This acquisition will reinforce Capgemini’s partnership with SAP in Japan. As a result of its global delivery model, it will also allow Capgemini to onboard SAP professionals to further serve clients across South East Asia. With small operations in Thailand, this acquisition opens a new chapter for Capgemini in the country, where it will be able to work with clients on rolling out locally their global transformation program.  “By pairing Capgemini’s global expertise with the talent and insight of Multibook’s SAP business, which works exclusively with SAP related technologies in Japan and South East Asia, this acquisition will strengthen our ability to help clients accelerate their transformation to run their entire business in the cloud with the next generation Intelligent SAP Solutions,” said Olaf Pietschner, CEO of Capgemini in Asia-Pacific and the Middle East and member of the Group Executive Committee. “Their extensive expertise and knowledge will further deepen our networks and capabilities to meet the anticipated growth in demand for SAP and cloud services in Japan, Hong Kong, Singapore, the Philippines and Thailand, and we are delighted to welcome them to the team.” Shinichi Tonomura, Deputy CEO for Capgemini in Asia-Pacific and the Middle East said, “The acquisition of Multibook’s SAP specialist business is an illustration of our commitment to expand in Japan and deliver value to our local clients at scale. It will further enhance our local SAP competency, reinforcing the foundation of our growth.”  “Joining Capgemini marks an exciting new step for me and my team and is a recognition of the value we have created with SAP for our clients,” said Tadaaki Murayama, Chief Executive Officer of Multibook, who will join Capgemini as part of the transaction. “Being part of Capgemini, will enable us to offer our clients the appropriate scale to transform globally, as well as new growth and career opportunities for our people.”  The transaction is subject to customary regulatory approvals and conditions precedents and is due to close in the coming weeks.

blocks.section: CCI France Japan expands its presence: Decision to open a local branch in Gunma
blocks.text: The French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan announced that it will open a branch office in Gunma.

blocks.section: CCI France Japan expands its presence: Decision to open a local branch in Gunma
blocks.text: As part of its ongoing commitment to strengthen economic ties between France and Japan, the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCIFJ) announced the opening of a branch office in Gunma on May 9.

blocks.section: CCI France Japan expands its presence: Decision to open a local branch in Gunma
blocks.text: This strategic addition to our network reveals the CCIFJ's growing commitment to supporting French, international and Japanese companies in the region .

blocks.section: CCI France Japan expands its presence: Decision to open a local branch in Gunma
blocks.text: Located 100 km away from Tokyo, Gunma prefecture offers a favorable environment for business and cultural development.

blocks.section: CCI France Japan expands its presence: Decision to open a local branch in Gunma
blocks.text: Gunma has been a pioneer in France-Japan relations , notably in the silk industry with the Tomioka factory. Its economy is rooted in manufacturing, particularly the automotive and metallurgy industries, with renowned companies such as Michelin and Subaru among others. Danone, also member of the CCIFJ, has a major production site in the region.

blocks.section: CCI France Japan expands its presence: Decision to open a local branch in Gunma
blocks.text: The opening of this branch is an important step in the development of economic relations between France and Gunma prefecture. Through its local presence, the CCI France Japon aims to intensify cooperation with the region economic players. CCIFJ is planning to organize regular local events, connect Gunna companies with CCIFJ members and support Gunma companies go overseas … in order to foster mutual economic growth.

As part of its commitment to strengthening economic ties between France and Japan, CCI France Japan has opened a local office in Hokkaido, a strategic region in the north of the country, more specifically located in Sapporo.

The region also stands out for its diversified ecosystem, including biotechnology, information technology, renewable energy industries, as well as semiconductors (chips), supported by a dense network of universities and research centers.

title: CCI France Japon and CNCPI sign a Memorandum of Understanding to strengthen cooperation in economics, innovation, and intellectual property between Japan and France
description:
During a joint event held in Tokyo on Wednesday, June 4, 2025, in the presence of Nicolas Bonnardel, Managing Director of CCI France Japon, and Emmanuel Potdevin, President of the CNCPI, the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCI France Japon) and the CNCPI (National Council of Industrial Property Attorneys) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen and promote economic and trade relations between Japanese and French businesses, focusing on the following key areas:
 	 	Sharing of information, knowledge, and best practices in the fields of intellectual property, innovation, and creativity for the benefit of companies and project leaders 	 	 	Facilitating connections and mentorship between members of both organizations 	 	 	Promoting business partnerships between French and Japanese companies 	 	 	Co-organizing joint events (study tours, workshops, seminars, webinars, and B2B missions) 	 

About CCI France Japon:
The French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCI France Japon) is the leading European Chamber in Japan. Founded in 1918, it brings together a network of over 700 member companies across all sectors, including one-third Japanese firms. CCI France Japon is a member of CCI France International (120 chambers in 95 countries, representing 36,000 companies worldwide) and the European Business Council – European Chamber (22 industry committees).
About CNCPI: The CNCPI, Compagnie Nationale des Conseils en Propriété Industrielle, represents 1,130 Industrial Property Attorneys practicing in France. Their core mission is to support companies in the protection, defense, and enhancement of their intellectual property rights (trademarks, patents, designs, software, personal data, digital law, etc.). The CNCPI advocates for a bold innovation policy backed by intellectual property—an essential tool for innovation—working in close collaboration with political and economic decision-makers and relevant industry networks.
Press contact, CNCPI: Bruno Cammalleri – 06 67 50 89 20 – bruno.cammalleri@cncpi.fr

title: CCI France Japon awarded two prizes at the CCIFI Seminar
description:
CCI France Japon was honored with two awards during the seminar of Presidents and Directors of the network of French Chambers of Commerce and Industry abroad (CCIFI), which brings together 120 chambers worldwide.
? It received the Communication Award and the Best Contribution Award for the launch of its CCIFJ Business Tips video series, designed with the support of artificial intelligence.
This series supports businesses in their development in Japan. CCIFJ Business Tips are short, practical videos that shed light on cultural differences between France and Japan in the professional world. They provide concrete advice to better understand these differences, anticipate them, and integrate them into the day-to-day management of a company in Japan. Aimed at executives, managers, and entrepreneurs, these videos are a simple and effective tool for succeeding in the Franco-Japanese business environment.
➡ About ten videos are already available: see the series on YouTube
? CCI France Japon was also awarded the Best Contribution Award for organizing its Business Summit 2024, held at the prestigious Nikkei Hall. The event brought together internationally renowned speakers and over 900 participants from various sectors for a full day of conferences and networking. Discussions focused on the major transformations shaping the future of France and Japan, and on strategies based on innovation, partnerships, and diversity to strengthen their global influence.
CCI France Japon is very proud of these distinctions and will continue to promote its initiatives and support its members with pride.

blocks.text: CCI France Japon Expands Network with New Branch Office in Fukui's Koshino Valley

blocks.section: CCI France Japon Expands Network with New Branch Office in Fukui's Koshino Valley
blocks.text: The French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan announced that it will open a branch office in Fukui.

blocks.section: CCI France Japon Expands Network with New Branch Office in Fukui's Koshino Valley
blocks.text: As part of its ongoing commitment to strengthening economic ties between France and Japan, the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCIFJ) announced on 28 October the opening of a new branch office at the Koshino Valley Innovation Centre in Fukui. This strategic addition reflects the CCIFJ’s dedication to supporting French, international, and Japanese companies in the region.

blocks.section: CCI France Japon Expands Network with New Branch Office in Fukui's Koshino Valley
blocks.text: Fukui, easily accessible from both Tokyo and Osaka, offers a wealth of attractions, including one of the world’s leading dinosaur museums, a world-renowned temple, and gourmet-rated regional delicacies. In 2020, the Fukui Paris Business Centre will open to promote Fukui crafts in Paris and foster Franco-Japanese relations. The extension of the Hokuriku Shinkansen bullet train line to Fukui this year has made the region less than 3 hours from Tokyo. This connection is expected to significantly boost the economy of Fukui Prefecture, as Kanazawa experienced a threefold increase in visitors following a similar bullet train extension in 2015.

blocks.section: CCI France Japon Expands Network with New Branch Office in Fukui's Koshino Valley
blocks.text: The opening of the Fukui branch is a major step in the development of economic relations between France and Fukui Prefecture. Through its local presence, CCIFJ aims to support companies from both countries expanding and innovating in each other’s markets, fostering stronger business collaboration.

blocks.section: CCI France Japon Expands Network with New Branch Office in Fukui's Koshino Valley
blocks.text: We are also pleased to announce that members of CCI France Japon can now utilize the Fukui Desk at Koshino Valley for their business activities. This space offers access to a state-of-the-art incubation facility designed for startups, entrepreneurs, and companies looking to expand their operations. Koshino Valley provides a wide range of professional equipment and resources that many businesses already rely on.

blocks.section: CCI France Japon Expands Network with New Branch Office in Fukui's Koshino Valley
blocks.text: The opening event was attended by Tatsuji Sugimoto, Governor of Fukui, Otsuka Tomoki, Director General of Fukui Prefecture, Jérôme Chouchan, President of CCI France Japon, Nicolas Bonnardel, General Manager of CCI France Japon and 11 board members from CCI France Japon.

blocks.section: CCI France Japon Expands Network with New Branch Office in Fukui's Koshino Valley
blocks.text: With offices now in Tokyo, Osaka, Nagoya, Fukuoka, Gunma, and Fukui the CCIFJ offers a full range of services to help companies expand their market reach.

blocks.text: 2023: an innovative Chamber in a contrasted environment

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2024: a look back at the event
blocks.text: Jérôme Chouchan began his speech with conviction reminding the Chamber's mission, vision and core values, underlining its unwavering commitment to its members. He then highlighted the main lines of the "Vision 2026" plan, based on a strategic reinforcement of existing activities to better meet the specific expectations of our members. This plan is based on three fundamental pillars: the satisfaction of 800 members by 2026, regional expansion and the development of an innovative communications platform.

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2024: a look back at the event
blocks.text: Jérôme Chouchan then detailed the main activities and successes of 2023, highlighting the Chamber's dynamism and efficiency in achieving its objectives.

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2024: a look back at the event
blocks.text: In conclusion, he expressed his deep gratitude to all members for their loyalty and active participation in the Chamber's activities. He also affirmed his firm commitment to placing member satisfaction at the heart of all the organization's future actions, demonstrating an ongoing commitment to excellence and quality service.

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2024: a look back at the event
blocks.text: Each Director and Committee President then presented their 2023 activities and results.

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2024: a look back at the event
blocks.text: Following the auditors' report, the 2023 financial report and the 2024 budget were approved at the meeting.

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2024: a look back at the event
blocks.text: New Board of Directors

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2024: a look back at the event
blocks.text: The election of the new Board of Directors also took place during the General Meeting.

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2024: a look back at the event
blocks.text: Jérôme Chouchan was re-elected as the President of CCI France Japon for a further two years. We would like to thank him for his commitment. Our thanks also go to the outgoing directors for their dedication. We extend a warm welcome to the new members and wish all those who have been re-elected every success for the future.

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2024: a look back at the event
blocks.text: Medal of honor:

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2024: a look back at the event
blocks.text: The CCI France Japon was also pleased to award the Medal of Honor to Christian Polak for his involvement and loyal service to the CCI in recent years, and for his contribution to Franco-Japanese relations.

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2024: a look back at the event
blocks.text: Conference

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2024: a look back at the event
blocks.text: Chairman of Kewpie Corporation, Mr Amane NAKASHIMA, then took part in the luncheon.

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2024: a look back at the event
blocks.text: He began by looking back at the origins of the Kewpie brand, offering the audience a glimpse of its history and evolution over time.

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2024: a look back at the event
blocks.text: In his speech, Amane Nakashima shared Kewpie's motto and philosophy, stressing the importance of earning customers' trust to ensure the company's long-term sustainability. He insisted that the Kewpie Group continues to follow its founder's doctrine, which advocates action based on moral principles, the pursuit of originality and ingenuity, and concern for the welfare of parents.

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2024: a look back at the event
blocks.text: In addition, Amane Nakashima highlighted the diversification of the brand's activities, mentioning the management of Caves Legrand and the National Azabu supermarket, among others. This diversification testifies to Kewpie's commitment to exploring new opportunities while remaining true to its core values.

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2024: a look back at the event
blocks.text: Mr Philippe Setton, French Ambassador to Japan, closed the Annual General Meeting

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2024: a look back at the event
blocks.text: His speech highlighted the dynamism of the Chamber and the strong French presence in Japan. He noted that France is now the fifth-largest investor country in Japan, testifying to a strong economic relationship between the two nations.

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2024: a look back at the event
blocks.text: The year 2023 was marked by Japan's presidency of the G7, and Philippe Setton expressed his desire to deepen Franco-Japanese relations in 2024. He stressed the importance of upcoming events this year, including the Vivatech trade show in Paris, where Japan will be the country of honor, the Olympic Games in Paris, as well as the Osaka World Expo, where France will have its own pavilion.

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2024: a look back at the event
blocks.text: In his speech, Philippe Setton also emphasized the importance of cooperation between the Chamber of Commerce and the various embassy departments, notably Business France and Atout France.

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2024: a look back at the event
blocks.text: In conclusion, Philippe Setton complimented Christian Polak on the medal he had been awarded, highlighting his commitment and contribution to Franco-Japanese relations.
