blocks.text: Approval of the 2024 Accounts and the 2025 Budget

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2025: a look back at the event
blocks.text: Following the presentation of the auditors' report , the 2024 financial report and the 2025 budget were approved during the assembly. The membership fees were then reviewed, notably highlighting the associate member status , set at 190,000 yen .

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2025: a look back at the event
blocks.text: Conference

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2025: a look back at the event
blocks.text: Mr. Hiromi Yamaji , Group CEO of Japan Exchange Group (JPX) , spoke during the lunch session about the transformation of Japanese companies and the growth of the Japanese market .

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2025: a look back at the event
blocks.text: Market and Corporate Transformation Mr. Yamaji presented the evolution of Japanese companies and the transformation of the stock market , highlighting the initiatives and results of JPX, founded in 2013 and operator of the Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE) .

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2025: a look back at the event
blocks.text: Local Dominance in a Global Market He provided insights into the distribution of the equities and derivatives market by investor type.

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2025: a look back at the event
blocks.text: Ownership of Japanese Stocks:

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2025: a look back at the event
blocks.text: 30% of Japanese stocks are held by foreign investors .

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2025: a look back at the event
blocks.text: 17% by individual investors .

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2025: a look back at the event
blocks.text: 19% by corporations .

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2025: a look back at the event
blocks.text: NISA (Nippon Individual Savings Account) Participation:

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2025: a look back at the event
blocks.text: Between January 2024 and January 2025 , the 10 largest brokers recorded ¥15.3 trillion in purchases through new NISA accounts.

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2025: a look back at the event
blocks.text: 37% (~¥5.7 trillion) of this was invested in domestic individual stocks .

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2025: a look back at the event
blocks.text: By September 2024 , 48.7% of NISA accounts were held by investors under 50 years old .

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2025: a look back at the event
blocks.text: Corporate Governance Reforms

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2025: a look back at the event
blocks.text: Almost all Prime market companies now comply with the requirement of having at least one-third independent directors .

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2025: a look back at the event
blocks.text: Nomination and compensation committees have become the norm.

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2025: a look back at the event
blocks.text: TSE Market Restructuring and Capital Efficiency

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2025: a look back at the event
blocks.text: In April 2022 , the market was restructured into three segments (Prime, Standard, and Growth) to improve performance.

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2025: a look back at the event
blocks.text: The focus was on enhancing PBR (Price-to-Book Ratio) and ROE (Return on Equity) , still below European and U.S. levels.

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2025: a look back at the event
blocks.text: Key Initiatives and Results:

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2025: a look back at the event
blocks.text: March 2023: 91% of Prime market and 49% of Standard market companies published detailed financial information.

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2025: a look back at the event
blocks.text: February 2024: TSE released 29 "best practices" based on feedback from over 100 investors .

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2025: a look back at the event
blocks.text: November 2024: New publication of "best practices" and examples of companies failing to meet investor expectations, following consultations with over 300 investors .

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2025: a look back at the event
blocks.text: January 2025: Companies that had published financial information but had not yet been contacted by institutional investors were invited to express interest in more active engagement .

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2025: a look back at the event
blocks.text: Overall Results of TSE Initiatives:

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2025: a look back at the event
blocks.text: Shareholder returns: Share buybacks have increased nearly sixfold over the past decade, and dividends have doubled .

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2025: a look back at the event
blocks.text: M&A growth: 4,700 M&A deals were recorded in 2024 (+17.1%), totaling ¥19.6 trillion (+8%).

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2025: a look back at the event
blocks.text: Improved English communication: By April 2025 , all Prime market companies will be required to publish financial results simultaneously in Japanese and English.

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2025: a look back at the event
blocks.text: Mr. Yamaji concluded by emphasizing that these reforms aim to attract more foreign investment and strengthen the global competitiveness of Japanese companies .

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2025: a look back at the event
blocks.text: Mr. Raphaël Keller , Minister-Counsellor for Economic Affairs , concluded the General Assembly .

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Meeting 2025: a look back at the event
blocks.text: Mr. Raphaël Keller praised the dynamism of the CCI France Japon, highlighting its key role in strengthening Franco-Japanese economic relations through its member recruitment, events, and regional expansion. He emphasized the importance of cooperation with the Embassy, especially in providing strategic information. He commended France for being the leading European investor in Japan and mentioned Franco-Japanese investment projects. Lastly, he highlighted the significance of Vivatech and the World Expo in Osaka for further developing economic and innovation exchanges, as well as the growing cooperation with La French Tech in Japan.

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Assemby 2026: a look back at the event
blocks.text: The 2026 General Meeting of the CCI France Japon was held on Friday, March 27 at the Park Hyatt Tokyo.

blocks.section: CCI France Japon General Assemby 2026: a look back at the event
blocks.text: During the event, a membership certificate was presented to the new companies in attendance that became members in 2025:

blocks.section: Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France Japon, opened the meeting
blocks.text: Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France Japon, opened the meeting

blocks.section: Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France Japon, opened the meeting
blocks.text: Review of 2025

blocks.section: Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France Japon, opened the meeting
blocks.text: Jérôme Chouchan recalled the mission and vision of the CCI France Japon, as well as its core values.

blocks.section: Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France Japon, opened the meeting
blocks.text: The year 2025 was marked by the success of the Osaka Kansai World Expo and the France Pavilion, which attracted a record number of French delegations. The CCI France Japon played an active role in fostering connections between these delegations and its members.

blocks.section: Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France Japon, opened the meeting
blocks.text: The Chamber reached a historic milestone with more than 719 members, confirming its leading position in Japan and strengthening the momentum of its community.

blocks.section: Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France Japon, opened the meeting
blocks.text: Member satisfaction remained at the heart of its actions, structured around three key areas:

blocks.section: Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France Japon, opened the meeting
blocks.text: a personalized business matching service, with 3,690 connections made in 2025

blocks.section: Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France Japon, opened the meeting
blocks.text: a member visit program to better understand needs and support projects

blocks.section: Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France Japon, opened the meeting
blocks.text: the regular organization of free events, such as Café Croissant and Connect, encouraging exchanges among members

blocks.section: Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France Japon, opened the meeting
blocks.text: The year was also marked by the success of flagship events, further enhancing the visibility and influence of the CCI France Japon:

blocks.section: Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France Japon, opened the meeting
blocks.text: the Business Summit, bringing together top-level decision-makers around Franco-Japanese economic issues

blocks.section: Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France Japon, opened the meeting
blocks.text: the Business Leaders Forums , providing a platform for exchange and strategic reflection among executives

blocks.section: Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France Japon, opened the meeting
blocks.text: the Osaka Kansai World Expo 2025

blocks.section: Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France Japon, opened the meeting
blocks.text: a large-scale French Fair organized with AEON , deployed across 5,000 points of sale throughout Japan, showcasing French products and expertise

blocks.section: Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France Japon, opened the meeting
blocks.text: Regional development also accelerated, with strengthened activities across the Fukuoka, Kansai, Nagoya, Gunma and Fukui offices. The Chamber also offers coworking spaces and meeting rooms through its “Le Booster” business centers in Tokyo, Osaka, Nagoya and Fukui.

blocks.section: Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France Japon, opened the meeting
blocks.text: Finally, major progress was achieved in digitalization with the launch of two digital formats from the CCI France Japon Studio : the interview series “Business Regards croisés” and the podcast “Itinéraires singuliers”.

blocks.section: Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France Japon, opened the meeting
blocks.text: The presentation concluded with the screening of a video summarizing the Chamber’s 2025 activities , highlighting the year’s key moments and achievements.

blocks.section: Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France Japon, opened the meeting
blocks.text: Each director and committee president then presented their 2025 activities and results.

blocks.section: Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France Japon, opened the meeting
blocks.text: ► We invite you to explore the detailed breakdown by activity in our 2025 Activity Report.

blocks.section: Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France Japon, opened the meeting
blocks.text: Following the presentation of the auditors’ report, the 2025 financial statements and the 2026 budget - including the increase in membership fees - were approved at the General Meeting.

blocks.section: Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France Japon, opened the meeting
blocks.text: The new membership fee structure for 2026 has been set as follows: JPY 650,000 for Benefactor Members, JPY 295,000 for Active Members, JPY 210,000 for Associate Members, JPY 140,000 for Startups, JPY 150,000 for Non-Kantô Members, EUR 550 for Non-Resident Members, and JPY 80,000 for Individual Members.

blocks.section: Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France Japon, opened the meeting
blocks.text: The election of the new Executive Board also took place during the General Meeting.

blocks.section: Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France Japon, opened the meeting
blocks.text: Jérôme Chouchan was reappointed as President of the CCI France Japon for an additional two-year term. We thank him for his continued commitment. Our thanks also go to the outgoing board members for their dedication. We warmly welcome the new members and wish those reappointed every success in continuing their mandates.

blocks.section: Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France Japon, opened the meeting
blocks.text: The CCI France Japon also had the pleasure of presenting the Honor Medal to Ichiro Kashitani, Vice Chairman of the Board of Toyota Tsusho Corporation, in recognition of his commitment and dedicated service to the Chamber over the past years, as well as his contribution to Franco-Japanese relations.

blocks.section: Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France Japon, opened the meeting
blocks.text: Takeshi Idezawa, CEO of LY Corporation, speaks about Initiatives for the Age of Generative AI.

blocks.section: Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France Japon, opened the meeting
blocks.text: A leading figure in Japan’s digital landscape and co-founder of the LINE messaging application, Takeshi Idezawa addressed the key challenges linked to the rise of generative artificial intelligence.

blocks.section: Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France Japon, opened the meeting
blocks.text: He emphasized that one of the main challenges today is accelerating companies’ digital transformation, in a context where AI is profoundly reshaping business models. The emergence of tools such as copilots and autonomous agents marks a shift from conversational AI to action-oriented AI capable of interacting with systems and executing complex tasks.

blocks.section: Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France Japon, opened the meeting
blocks.text: According to him, we are entering a new era of connected and strategic AI, where personal agents will be able to handle everyday activities (bookings, negotiations, services), fundamentally transforming interactions between companies and customers.

blocks.section: Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France Japon, opened the meeting
blocks.text: In this context, LY Corporation aims to build a comprehensive AI agent ecosystem integrated across its multiple services. The objective is clear: to evolve from an internet company into an AI agent-driven company, by optimizing user experience and integrating services at a national scale. According to the company, the fastest movers will be the most competitive in the market.

blocks.section: Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France Japon, opened the meeting
blocks.text: Mr. Gilles Bordes, Minister counsellor for economic affairs at the French Embassy in Tokyo, emphasized that Japan is at an important stage in its development, marked by a desire to consolidate its position in Asia and on the global stage. In this context, he highlighted opportunities for cooperation between France and Japan in investment and innovation across strategic sectors, as well as the importance of President Emmanuel Macron’s upcoming visit to deepen bilateral economic relations.

title: CCIFJ and the Japan Institute for Overseas Investment strengthen their cooperation
description:
The French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCIFJ) and the Japan Institute for Overseas Investment (JOI) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) on October 6, 2026, aimed at strengthening their cooperation and fostering investment and economic ties between France and Japan.
The agreement was signed by Jérôme Chouchan, President of CCIFJ, and Kenichiro Hayashi, President of the Japan Institute for Overseas Investment.
Established to contribute to the development of economic relations between Japan and other countries, JOI supports Japanese companies in their international investments, notably through research, analysis and the dissemination of information. For its part, CCIFJ helps Japanese companies and investors better understand the French market, its investment opportunities and its economic environment. The new agreement formalizes the two organizations’ commitment to working more closely together to promote Japanese direct investment in France.
A Practical Partnership Serving Businesses
The cooperation will include regular exchanges of information on France’s investment environment and conditions, as well as on opportunities for cooperation between French and Japanese companies. The two organizations will also be able to share and promote their respective activities and facilitate networking opportunities between their business communities.
The partnership also provides for cooperation in organizing seminars and roundtable discussions designed to provide companies with better information on economic and investment opportunities. JOI may also promote selected information and initiatives from CCIFJ on its website.
Finally, CCIFJ will be able to support JOI’s research activities related to Japanese direct investment in France, notably by providing relevant information and facilitating introductions to key stakeholders.
Building Stronger Bridges Between the French and Japanese Business Ecosystems
Through this MOU, CCIFJ is strengthening its role as a bridge between the French and Japanese business communities. The objective is to facilitate Japanese companies’ access to information about the French market while creating more opportunities for meetings, dialogue and cooperation between businesses from both countries.
This partnership with JOI will therefore create new channels for exchange and help raise awareness among Japanese companies of the opportunities France has to offer.
The MOU has been concluded for an initial period of three years and will subsequently be automatically renewed unless terminated by either party.

title: CEO lunch
description:
On November 13th, CCI France Japon welcomed Mr. Romain Millet from Millet Mountain Group for a CEO networking lunch event. It was an insightful and inspiring session that provided participants with a deep dive into the remarkable journey of Mr. Millet, who showcased his extensive experience particularly excelling in the field of consumer goods.
The talk unfolded Mr. Millet's impressive professional trajectory, including notable roles such as CEO and President of Lafuma Group, President of the La Chameau brand, Managing Director for Cache Cache, CEO of Beaumanoir Group in China, and President of the LVMH Watches Division in the China, Korea, Macau, Hong Kong, and Taiwan region. Since 2020, as the CEO of Millet Mountain Group, Mr. Millet undertook the venture with his uncle Jean Pierre, symbolizing the reconstruction of a century-old family entrepreneurship. This move not only reflects his commitment to revitalizing the business but also showcases his dedication to preserving a rich legacy.
The CEO lunch event left participants inspired by Mr. Millet's leadership journey and strategic insights.

title: Ceremony for the Extension of Danone’s Factory in the City of Tatebayashi
description:
On Thursday 7 May 2026, the CCI France Japan had the honour of attending the extension ceremony of Danone’s factory located in the city of Tatebayashi, in Gunma Prefecture.
This project reflects the Group’s commitment to meeting the growing needs of Japanese consumers in an increasingly stable and flexible manner. Today, the Japanese market represents a key growth market for Danone, driven by sustained demand and strong development potential.
Since its establishment in 2002, the Tatebayashi factory has been responsible for the nationwide production of Danone products and has actively contributed to the local economic vitality of Gunma Prefecture.
As a benefactor member of the CCI France Japan, Danone Japan welcomed several local representatives as well as the CCIFJ on this occasion to celebrate this new stage in the company’s development and to highlight the strong relationships of trust built with its regional and institutional partners.
François-Xavier Lienhart, member of the CCIFJ Board of Directors, then delivered a speech before Danone Chief Executive Officer Rodrigo Lima, alongside the Mayor of Tatebayashi and the Vice Governor of Gunma, extending his wishes for continued prosperity and success in the Group’s future activities.
The ceremony then continued with a convivial moment of discussion and exchange among the guests.

title: Champagne A. Robert : a fruitful prospecting mission
description:
Champagne A. Robert, an estate grown producer, took part in a prospecting mission organized by CCI France Japan in March 2017. Meetings with six prospects over two days went smoothly and proved to be fruitful.
The vineyard, which dates back to 1722, already exports to several countries, particularly in Asia, but Japan represented a special case for Mr. Arnaud Robert.
“The CCI France Japan prospecting mission in the spring was very helpful to us. We deliberately took our time with Japan, as this country, which offers strong qualitative and quantitative potential, requires a certain level of export experience. Feedback from prospects was positive, and the maturity and diversity of operators allow us to reach our objectives. We are considering several follow up visits to Japan as well as participation in Foodex in February 2018”, explains Arnaud Robert, Managing Director of Champagne A. Robert.
Learn more :
https://www.champagne-robert.fr/

blocks.text: This geographic foothold will enable the developer to provide customized business services and participate in the creation of a governance framework for technology. Thanks to a partnership with Microsoft, many Japanese companies are already exploiting OpenA's generative AI technology.

title: Circular Economy Seminar
description:
During the French Presidency of the Council of the European Union, the Embassy of France in Japan (Economic Department) in cooperation with the Delegation of the European Union in Japan, will organize a seminar on June 22nd, 2022 dedicated to circular economy.
This seminar, taking place in Tokyo and broadcasted online via Zoom, will bring together Japanese, French and European institutional and private stakeholders to discuss the latest EU and Japanese policies and experiences regarding circular economy. The seminar will also highlight collaborations and innovative projects from private actors in areas such as new design modes, recycling, reduction and reuse of plastics, by looking at circular economy strategies from different sectors.
This seminar is co-funded by “Rethinking Plastics – Circular Economy Solutions to Marine Litter” project of the European Union and the German Federal Government and by the French Ministry of Ecological Transition and Territorial Cohesion.

Date and time : Wednesday 22nd June 2022 16:00 - 19:00 (JST) / 9:00 – 12:00 (CEST) Modalities : Hybrid format, face-to-face at l’Espace@CCIFJ (Tokyo) and broadcasted on ZOOM Audience : up to 70 participants onsite and 500 online Language : English / Japanese (simultaneous translation)

Agenda (tentative)
15:30 - 16:00 : Doors opening 16:00 - 16:15 : Opening remarks 16:15 - 17:05 : Keynote lectures - The circular economy at the heart of French, European and Japanese policies 17:05 - 17:55 : Short presentations - Good practices and collaborations of the EU/FR/JP private sector on eco-design, recycling and sustainable products 17:55 - 18:05 : Break 18:05 - 18:50 : Round table - Trends and advances in the circular economy in EU and Japan 18:50 - 19:00 : Closing remarks and conclusion

title: Cofrex, Business France and the CCI France Japon sign a partnership agreement surrounding the France Pavilion for Expo Osaka 2025
description:
With the aim of mobilizing the French and Japanese business ecosystems surrounding the France Pavilion for Expo Osaka 2025, Mr. Jacques Maire, General Commissioner of the France Pavilion and Chairman of the Compagnie Française des Expositions (Cofrex), Ms. Marie-Cécile Tardieu, Chief Operating Officer (Investment Division) of Business France and Mr. Jérôme Chouchan, President of the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCI France-Japan) have signed a tripartite partnership agreement to contribute to the dynamic of promoting French representation at this global event bringing together an audience of all ages, on November 9, 2023.
From April 13 to October 13, 2025 in Osaka (Kansai region of Japan), with the theme “Designing the society of the future, imagining our life tomorrow”, broken down into three sub-themes – “Saving lives”, “Empowering lives”, “Connecting lives” – the World Exhibition is an international laboratory of expertise and innovation in harmony with the UN’s Sustainable Development Goals. It stands out as a unique opportunity to promote the expertise and innovations of public and private players nationwide by sharing them with as many people as possible.
By choosing to express its messages through the sub-theme “Empowering lives”, the ambition of the France Pavilion is part of a desire to promote French expertise in all its diversity and boldness. The France Pavilion will enjoy an exceptional location, opposite the Japanese Pavilion and the main entrance, with the tripartite partnership being organized there to include the organization of the “Business Leaders Forum 2025”, a calendar of networking sessions, conferences, welcoming delegations from all nations.
For Jacques Maire, General Commissioner of the France Pavilion and Chairman of Cofrex: “With Business France and the CCI France-Japan, Team-Export France will become a partner of Cofrex for Expo Osaka 2025. The France Pavilion is a platform and event format serving French businesses. It will welcome them for six months under the same ambition, to promote France in the region.”

“I am delighted that through this partnership, Business France can provide its expertise in supporting French businesses, which carry and promote their proficiency throughout the world, thereby contributing to France’s influence. As true standards of our country internationally, French firms proudly display their capacities for innovation and daring, knowing just how to anticipate current and future transformations. This is the whole point of Expo Osaka 2025, which will contribute to further strengthening relations between France and Japan,” said Marie-Cécile Tardieu, Chief Operating Officer (Investment Division) 

Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France-Japan, expressed his enthusiasm about this unique partnership: “The partnership between Business France, Cofrex and our Chamber of Commerce is a real opportunity, a powerful alliance to open the Japanese market to our businesses and to show the strength of French innovation in Japan. The synergies involved will allow the French pavilion to embody the excellence, creativity and expertise of our nation around the central theme of the hymn to love.”

About COFREX
Founded in January 2018, Cofrex SAS, a publicly owned company, is the first permanent structure dedicated to the preparation, organization and implementation of France’s participation in World and International Expos. Its sustainable approach draws on the experience of previous exhibitions for optimal organization, at best cost and with the least impact. It is based on a partnership between public and private players, working around France’s image and attractiveness.
For further information, please visit: www.cofrex.fr
About the France Pavilion at Expo Osaka 2025
The World Expo Osaka 2025 in Japan will be held from April 13 to October 13, 2025 on the theme “Designing the society of the future, imagining our lives of tomorrow”, broken down into three sub-themes: “Saving lives”, “Empowering Lives” and “Connecting Lives”. It will take place on Yumeshima Island, an artificial island located in Osaka Bay comprising a 155-hectare (383-acre) site, the general architecture of which has been entrusted to the architect Sosuke Fujimoto. Together, all the Pavilions will be connected by a “roof ring” 615m in diameter and 2,000m around the circumference, distributed in three macro-zones: Green World, Pavilion World and Water World. More than 150 countries will be represented and 28 million visitors are expected at the event. The France Pavilion, whose ambition is to promote French innovations and expertise, will be located in the “Empowering lives” area, near the Japan Pavilion and the main entrance to the World Exhibition.
For further information, please visit: www.franceosaka2025.fr
About Business France
Business France is the national agency supporting the international development of the French economy, responsible for fostering export growth by French businesses, as well as promoting and facilitating international investment in France. It promotes France’s companies, business image and nationwide attractiveness as an investment location, and also runs the VIE international internship program. Business France has 1,500 personnel, both in France and in 55 countries throughout the world, who work with a network of partners.
Since January 2019, as part of the reform of the state support system for exports, Business France has given private-sector partners responsibility for supporting French SMEs and mid-size companies in the following markets: Belgium, Hungary, Morocco, Norway, the Philippines and Singapore.
For further information, please visit: www.businessfrance.fr @businessfrance
About the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan
The French Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Japan (CCI France-Japan) is one of the leading foreign chambers in Japan, being the oldest, the largest European Chamber in Japan and the third largest in the CCI France International global network.Since 1918, the CCI France-Japan has built a solid business network, bringing together more than 650 members of all nationalities. Including branches and business centers in Tokyo, Osaka, Nagoya and Fukuoka, the CCI France-Japan positions itself as the international platform promoting fruitful relationships between its members and developing business opportunities between France and Japan.
With 800 existing member businesses, our ambition is to become the benchmark international business community in Japan by 2026, thanks to regional expansion, our customized activities and services, as well as the establishment of an interactive communication platform.
For further information on the activities of the CCI France-Japan, please visit: https://www.ccifj.or.jp/services-aux-entreprises/implantation-et-business-center.html

title: Welcoming 2026 Together With CCIFJ Kyushu
description:
On Friday, February 20, 2026, CCIFJ Kyushu held its first event of the year: the New Year’s Party, hosted at Hotel JAL City Fukuoka.
The evening brought together a diverse group of professionals. We were pleased to welcome long-standing member companies such as JUST.WILL, TWOBLOOM, and WASOMI, who continue to show loyal support for CCIFJ Kyushu events. Representatives from Bourbon and the French restaurant La Rochelle were also in attendance.
The event coincided with a visit to Fukuoka by the Managing Director. This provided a valuable opportunity to strengthen ties and reaffirm our commitment to members across all regions, highlighting our goal of building local communities that remain connected on a national scale.
Following a traditional introductory round where guests presented their activities, participants enjoyed a seasonal menu featuring local specialties such as grilled yellowtail and roasted Itoshima pork. The varied selection and open bar encouraged fluid conversation, allowing guests to get to know one another in a relaxed atmosphere.
The dinner proved highly conducive to networking. Business cards were exchanged throughout the evening, particularly as dessert was served. It was a warm occasion that concluded with a shared desire to reconnect soon, despite many guests wishing to extend the evening further.
The gathering also served as a platform to announce the upcoming Kyushu office program, most notably the Fukuoka Gala, which will take place on Monday, May 18, at the Solaria Hotel starting from 6:15 PM.
We would like to thank all participants for their ongoing contribution to our local community, as well as the staff at Hotel JAL City for their hospitality—a wonderful way to begin the year together.

title: Cheese Concours organized by MOF Museum Nagoya in Ogaki
description:
From February 26 to 28, 2026, the city of Ogaki hosted for the first time a major gastronomic and cultural event with a cheese competition organized by the MOF Museum Nagoya, supported by the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCIFJ) and the City of Ogaki. The event forms part of the initiatives leading up to the official opening of the Musée des Meilleurs Ouvriers de France (MOF) in Ogaki, scheduled for April 1, 2026.
Held in the unique setting of a former school repurposed for the occasion, the event brought together professionals, artisans, institutional partners, and members of the public to celebrate craftsmanship and promote Franco-Japanese cultural exchange.

blocks.text: Chubu Event report

blocks.section: Cheese Concours organized by MOF Museum Nagoya in Ogaki
blocks.text: Cheese Concours organized by MOF Museum Nagoya in Ogaki

blocks.section: Cheese Concours organized by MOF Museum Nagoya in Ogaki
blocks.text: From February 26 to 28, 2026, the city of Ogaki hosted for the first time a major gastronomic and cultural event with a cheese competition organized by the MOF Museum Nagoya , supported by the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCIFJ) and the City of Ogaki. The event forms part of the initiatives leading up to the official opening of the Musée des Meilleurs Ouvriers de France (MOF) in Ogaki, scheduled for April 1, 2026.

blocks.section: Cheese Concours organized by MOF Museum Nagoya in Ogaki
blocks.text: Held in the unique setting of a former school repurposed for the occasion, the event brought together professionals, artisans, institutional partners, and members of the public to celebrate craftsmanship and promote Franco-Japanese cultural exchange.

blocks.section: A Competition Combining Artistic Creativity and Gastronomic Excellence
blocks.text: A Competition Combining Artistic Creativity and Gastronomic Excellence

blocks.section: A Competition Combining Artistic Creativity and Gastronomic Excellence
blocks.text: At the heart of the three-day program was a cheese competition inviting participants to create artistic and culinary works highlighting cheese in innovative ways. Contestants designed original constructions including sculptures and cheese pyramids showcasing both creativity and technical skill.

blocks.section: A Competition Combining Artistic Creativity and Gastronomic Excellence
blocks.text: A distinctive feature of this edition was the use of both French and Japanese cheeses, illustrating the growing dialogue between the cheesemaking traditions of the two countries as well as the rising quality of Japanese local production. The creations were evaluated by a jury based on two complementary criteria: visual aesthetics and taste quality, emphasizing the balance between artistic expression and gastronomic excellence.

blocks.section: Exceptional Demonstrations by Meilleurs Ouvriers de France
blocks.text: Exceptional Demonstrations by Meilleurs Ouvriers de France

blocks.section: Exceptional Demonstrations by Meilleurs Ouvriers de France
blocks.text: Among the highlights of the event were live demonstrations conducted by Meilleurs Ouvriers de France who traveled from France, including Dominique Bouchait , Meilleur Ouvrier de France cheesemonger and Christian Vabret , Meilleur Ouvrier de France baker. In front of an engaged audience, the artisans created impressive Eiffel Towers made entirely of cheese, demonstrating the precision, creativity, and expertise associated with the prestigious MOF title.

blocks.section: A Complete Gastronomic Experience
blocks.text: A Complete Gastronomic Experience

blocks.section: A Complete Gastronomic Experience
blocks.text: Beyond the competition itself, the event offered a rich culinary experience. Alongside cheese tastings, visitors enjoyed a variety of cheese-based dishes, including cheesecakes, as well as a wide selection of fruits carefully chosen to complement the flavors and enhance the tasting experience.

blocks.section: A Complete Gastronomic Experience
blocks.text: Following the award ceremony honoring the winning creations, visitors were invited to participate in a collective tasting of the cheese structures prepared during the competition, reinforcing the spirit of sharing and conviviality that characterized the three-day event.

blocks.section: A Complete Gastronomic Experience
blocks.text: The guests enjoyed a stunning buffet and thoroughly enjoyed the cheese like the vice-mayor of Ogaki, Mr Toyoda who joined us on this beautiful evening.

blocks.section: An Immersion in French Culture
blocks.text: An Immersion in French Culture

blocks.section: An Immersion in French Culture
blocks.text: The event also featured a broader cultural dimension, with activities celebrating French lifestyle and traditions. Petanque tournaments organized near the venue contributed to a friendly and accessible atmosphere, encouraging interaction between Japanese and French participants and visitors.

blocks.section: A Prelude to the Opening of the MOF Museum in Ogaki
blocks.text: A Prelude to the Opening of the MOF Museum in Ogaki

blocks.section: A Prelude to the Opening of the MOF Museum in Ogaki
blocks.text: This competition represents an important milestone ahead of the opening of the Musée des Meilleurs Ouvriers de France in Ogaki on April 1, 2026. Supported by the CCIFJ and the City of Ogaki, the future museum aims to become a reference venue for promoting French artisanal excellence in Japan and a lasting symbol of Franco-Japanese cultural cooperation.

blocks.section: Acknowledgments
blocks.text: Acknowledgments

blocks.section: Acknowledgments
blocks.text: The organizers would like to express their sincere gratitude to all institutional and private partners, the participating Meilleurs Ouvriers de France, the competition candidates, and the many visitors who contributed to the success of this event. Their commitment and enthusiasm helped make these three days a meaningful moment of exchange, fully reflecting the richness of cultural and gastronomic ties between France and Japan.

blocks.section: Acknowledgments
blocks.text: We also extend our heartfelt wishes for the success of the future Musée des Meilleurs Ouvriers de France in Ogaki, whose upcoming opening marks an important step in promoting artisanal excellence and strengthening Franco-Japanese cultural relation

title: An Overview of Factory Automation in Japan by Stäubli
description: For the 6th edition of our Kansai Sectoral Gatherings, we visited Stäubli's showroom in Umeda, talking Factory Automation among a throng of robots.

blocks.text: Kansai Event report

blocks.section: An Overview of Factory Automation in Japan by Stäubli
blocks.text: An Overview of Factory Automation in Japan by Stäubli

blocks.section: An Overview of Factory Automation in Japan by Stäubli
blocks.text: For the 6th edition of our Kansai Sectoral Gatherings, we visited Stäubli's showroom in Umeda, talking Factory Automation among a throng of robots.

blocks.section: An Overview of Factory Automation in Japan by Stäubli
blocks.text: Yesterday, we held our sixth edition of this year’s sectoral gatherings at Stäubli ’s showroom, right next to Umeda. Stäubli’s team had prepared a stunning presentation that was giving a broad overview of the situation of Factory Automation in Japan.

blocks.section: An Overview of Factory Automation in Japan by Stäubli
blocks.text: Stäubli is a Switzerland-based company that has 130 years of experience in automation, starting with weaving machines and working its way through specialized connectors and robots, thanks to a mix of innovation and acquisition . They now have expertise in 20 different industrial segments , which gives them a diverse vision of the issues arising in the industry.

blocks.section: An Overview of Factory Automation in Japan by Stäubli
blocks.text: The assessment regarding Japan is actually quite gloomy , and we could only make rather negative observations: despite a rapidly aging population that would require the society to replace the decreasing workforce with automated solutions whenever it can, automation in Japan is actually lagging behind and moving at a slow pace. We drew the same conclusions earlier this year regarding the related subject of digital transformation . As a result, Japan’s productivity is taking a worrying dip , with people working long hours to produce less than other countries with better work-life balance. At the same time, Japan’s industry is lacking the innovation necessary to compete internationally. It was observed that the comfort offered by Japanese society tends to make people afraid to take risks and try new solutions. As a consequence, Japan often waits for others to develop and try new solutions before adopting them, which means that the Japanese industry does not offer solutions that would stand out on the market. Despite the current depreciation of the yen and Japan's manufacturing capacity, we can only notice that exports are low . Finally, you would think that introducing robots in the production lines would be perceived as labor cost reduction, but high-end robots and their inclusion itself are actually very expensive and require a lot of investments that many companies are not willing to make. Then, introducing robots in a production line also means more qualified employees , because it takes much more skills and knowledge to program, repair or maintain a robot than to just perform the task taken up by it.

blocks.section: An Overview of Factory Automation in Japan by Stäubli
blocks.text: As Stäubli’s speakers pointed out however, factory automation could bring many positive improvements to Japan’s economy. First of all, robots can perform better, more precise tasks than humans , and with a much lower rate of mistakes . As such, introducing more robots could allow Japan to shine once more in the field of very high-end technological products, singling itself out from its local competitors in the manufacturing industry. Obviously, automation would also be an answer to the aging population and the dire necessity to increase production drastically to keep up the pace and provide enough revenue for the elderly.

blocks.section: An Overview of Factory Automation in Japan by Stäubli
blocks.text: The bottom line of this overview was that Japan in general and Kansai in particular are a manufacturing country/region. It has the potential to become a truly productive place for high-end products and take the lead again in specific fields. However, it needs to face and address its issues without any delay if it does not want to fall behind beyond any hope of recovery. In this matter, foreign companies established in Japan are more than willing to help and bring their insight. As was pointed out, Japan already showed its incredible capacity to transform in a blink by relying on foreign expertise during the Meiji era. It might be time for another magic trick of the same kind.

blocks.section: An Overview of Factory Automation in Japan by Stäubli
blocks.text: In conclusion, all the attendees agreed that the matter is vast and that we could only scratch it that evening. We parted while already making plans for a greater event on the subject, so keep an eye out for our upcoming “Factory Automation Business Summit” sometime next year, and of course do not miss the Smart Manufacturing Summit in March 2024!

title: Conserverie PAPILLON MARMUS : Occitanie on your plate
description: The company took part in a collective mission in May 2018 with the support of the Occitanie Region, a strategy that proved successful.

blocks.text: Sectors & markets

blocks.section: Conserverie PAPILLON MARMUS : Occitanie on your plate
blocks.text: Conserverie PAPILLON MARMUS : Occitanie on your plate

blocks.section: Conserverie PAPILLON MARMUS : Occitanie on your plate
blocks.text: The company took part in a collective mission in May 2018 with the support of the Occitanie Region, a strategy that proved successful.

blocks.section: Conserverie PAPILLON MARMUS : Occitanie on your plate
blocks.text: Founded in 1955, Conserverie PAPILLON MARMUS took part in a collective mission of companies from the Occitanie region from May 28 to 30, 2018, with the aim of exporting its premium quality terrines and pâtés made in Aveyron from French meat.

blocks.section: Conserverie PAPILLON MARMUS : Occitanie on your plate
blocks.text: Following a comprehensive program of visits to various agri food retail outlets, Alexandre Marmus benefited from personalized B2B meetings with seven prospects selected by our team. All of them expressed interest, but it was with the importer YAKURYO KAIHATSU, specializing in organic products, that the collaboration proved to be the most fruitful.

blocks.section: Conserverie PAPILLON MARMUS : Occitanie on your plate
blocks.text: “ As soon as we returned, daily correspondence was established ,” explains Alexandre Marmus. “ We quickly appreciated the curiosity of the Japanese, as well as their very constructive and distinctive approach to our products. Having already had a first experience in Japan in the past, we paid particular attention to nurturing the relationship with our future partner. Fast responses combined with a high level of detail allowed us to overcome the distance. In three months, we built a very respectful relationship that facilitated all the steps required for the success of the project .”

blocks.section: Conserverie PAPILLON MARMUS : Occitanie on your plate
blocks.text: At the end of September, after several test shipments including sampling, selection of the carrier, and validation of customs procedures, a pallet of 5,000 terrines under the MAISON PAPILLON brand set sail for the Land of the Rising Sun. YAKURYO KAIHATSU carefully selected five organic duck recipes, which were presented at the French Fair of the MITSUKOSHI department store in Nihonbashi. Thanks to this dynamic partnership, the family owned company has thus embarked on a new chapter in the gourmet showcases of Tokyo.

blocks.section: Conserverie PAPILLON MARMUS : Occitanie on your plate
blocks.text: Alexandre Marmus shares with us, “ We are very proud to offer our know how in Japan, as it represents recognition of our standards and our philosophy of conduct .” These initial sales have already fully covered the investment made and open up numerous export opportunities to other Asian countries, which recognize the unwavering reputation for quality of products sold in Japan.

blocks.text: Constantin is an independent network for audit, tax and advisory services with a unique operating model over the world.

blocks.section: CONSTANTIN JAPAN
blocks.text: For more than 50 years, the firm has stood for quality, precision and integrity in assisting European and North-American groups with all aspects of their financial reporting, cross-border operations, and growth opportunities.

blocks.section: CONSTANTIN JAPAN
blocks.text: The firm is built on the principle of adopting an integrated approach to guarantee responsiveness and consistent quality of service to enterprises of all sizes with international operations. Unlike global networks of firm members, they focus on close interdisciplinary and cross-border collaboration of integrated teams inside one single organization.

blocks.section: CONSTANTIN JAPAN
blocks.text: With offices located in 8 different countries across the Asia-Pacific, they are able to serve transnational organizations as a one-stop-shop. They work seamlessly thanks to a structure that allows them to coordinate the liaison and the group consolidation with the headquarters on a regional basis.

blocks.section: CONSTANTIN JAPAN
blocks.text: In Asia-Pacific, they combine the ability to ensure high quality practices with the understanding of local regulatory frameworks to adapt to the particular context of expanding across dynamic markets and fast changing environments.

title: Recap Event - Entrepreneur Committee
description:
The French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan hosted an entrepreneur committee featuring Rodrigo Lima, Danone Japan President. He captivated the audience by sharing his journey from Brazil to Australia, detailing how he discovered Japan, and the innovative strategies he employed to develop Danone brand.
Under the guidance of Mr. Steven Bleistein, the discussion attracted over 50 participants and was rich in storytelling and valuable advice for the future of companies in Japan. The Q&A session offered participants the chance to delve deeper into the Danone Japan brand's development and the challenges encountered across different countries.

title: Entrepreneur Committee
description:
On December 9th, the French Chamber of Commerce had the pleasure of hosting Makiko Ono, President and CEO of Suntory Beverage & Food Limited, for an insightful Entrepreneur Committee event by Steven Bleistein.
The event drew over 60 participants, providing ample opportunities for networking and engaging discussions during the Q&A sessions.
We delved into Makiko Ono’s journey, exploring her motivations, goals, and achievements. As the first female CEO of Suntory, she has successfully led the company in securing major partnerships with leading brands. Her insights on leadership and innovation were both inspiring and insightful.
The event also offered a platform for participants to connect and exchange ideas, fostering collaboration and support within the community.

blocks.text: To help you to adjust your travel plans in light of the ongoing health crisis, we have put in place exceptional measures throughout our network.

blocks.section: YOU ARE ABROAD AND WISH TO RETURN TO EUROPE

blocks.section: YOU ARE ABROAD AND WISH TO RETURN TO EUROPE
blocks.text: We offer special fares for French and European citizens and residents who wish to return to Europe.

blocks.section: YOU ARE ABROAD AND WISH TO RETURN TO EUROPE
blocks.text: If you have a ticket for a flight operated by Air France , we recommend to anticipate your return to Europe as soon as possible, by changing your booking online in the "My Bookings" section of our website or mobile application. You can also contact your sales agent.

blocks.section: YOU ARE ABROAD AND WISH TO RETURN TO EUROPE
blocks.text: If you wish, you can buy a new ticket at a special fare. You can then cancel your initial flight and obtain a credit valid for 1 year on all Air France, KLM, Delta Air Lines and Virgin Atlantic flights.

blocks.section: YOU ARE ABROAD AND WISH TO RETURN TO EUROPE
blocks.text: If you do not have a ticket for a flight operated by Air France , you can purchase a ticket on our website or from an Air France sales outlet and benefit from our special fares.

blocks.section: YOU ARE ABROAD AND WISH TO RETURN TO EUROPE
blocks.text: Please note that only nationals and residents of the European Union, the Schengen area and United Kingdom, and their family members, are allowed to travel to France.

blocks.section: YOU ARE ABROAD AND WISH TO RETURN TO EUROPE
blocks.text: This one way special fare is available for the travel period until June 15th, 2020.

blocks.section: YOU ARE ABROAD AND WISH TO RETURN TO EUROPE

blocks.section: YOU WANT TO POSTPONE YOUR TRIP
blocks.text: YOU WANT TO POSTPONE YOUR TRIP

blocks.section: YOU WANT TO POSTPONE YOUR TRIP
blocks.text: If you have purchased a ticket for a flight departing before 3 July 2020 , you can postpone your departure date without change fees, subject to the availability in the same travel cabin. Any changes to your flight must be made before its scheduled departure. Your new trip must begin no later than 30 November 2020 included.

blocks.section: YOU WANT TO POSTPONE YOUR TRIP
blocks.text: If you wish to travel on or after 1 December 2020 , you can also postpone your departure date without any change fee. It the fare type mentioned in your ticket is not available, you may need to pay the fare difference. Save time by changing your booking online in the "My Bookings" section of our website or mobile application. You can also contact your sales agent. Postpone my trip

blocks.section: YOU WANT TO POSTPONE YOUR TRIP
blocks.text: *Except for group rates and allotments.

blocks.section: YOU WANT TO CANCEL YOUR TRIP
blocks.text: YOU WANT TO CANCEL YOUR TRIP

blocks.section: YOU WANT TO CANCEL YOUR TRIP
blocks.text: If you have purchased a ticket at a travel agency for a flight departing before 3 July 2020 and you no longer wish to travel, please contact them for further information. If you purchased a ticket directly from our website or at an Air France agency for a flight departing before 3 July 2020 and you no longer wish to travel , you can request a travel voucher from the "My Bookings" section of our website or mobile application. This non-refundable voucher is valid for 1 year on all Air France, KLM, Delta Air Lines and Virgin Atlantic flights and Kenya Airways flights. REQUEST A TRAVEL VOUCHER IN "MY BOOKINGS"

blocks.section: YOU WANT TO PLAN A TRIP
blocks.text: Book with confidence. For any booking made before 31 March 2020, you have until 30 September 2020 to postpone your departure date without change fees, subject to availability of the same fare. Your new trip must begin no later than 30 November 2020. Before making any travel arrangements, please contact the relevant national authorities to check entry and stay requirements in your destination and transit countries. Travel restrictions are already in force for many nationalities or for travelers who have recently visited certain countries. These restrictions may change at very short notice. Please be advised that you should make your own arrangements (such as accommodation or alternative travel options) to mitigate the risk.

blocks.section: [Translate to Anglais:] Smile Food Project, une initiative gastronomique solidaire
blocks.text: Afin de soutenir les professionnels de la santé qui se trouvent en première ligne du combat contre le nouveau coronavirus, des entreprises gérant des restaurants ainsi que des groupes menant des activités évoluant autour du thème de la durabilité alimentaire ont monté, sous l’égide d’une collaboration avec Gurunavi, Inc., « Smile Food Project ».

blocks.section: [Translate to Anglais:] Smile Food Project, une initiative gastronomique solidaire
blocks.text: Cette opération permet de livrer aux équipes médicales des plats cuisinés conçus par les plus grands chefs.

blocks.section: [Translate to Anglais:] Smile Food Project, une initiative gastronomique solidaire
blocks.text: La participation de Shinsuke Ishii, le chef et propriétaire du restaurant français Sincere, Fumio Yonezawa, le chef du restaurant de grillades The Burn, ainsi que de nombreux autres chefs est prévue. Les plats livrés seront essentiellement à base de légumes et réalisés en conformité avec un contrôle d’hygiène rigoureux.

blocks.section: [Translate to Anglais:] Smile Food Project, une initiative gastronomique solidaire
blocks.text: L’initiative se concentrera dans un premier temps sur la livraison de repas dans la région métropolitaine de Tokyo, mais le projet envisage également d’en livrer dans d’autres préfectures.

blocks.section: [Translate to Anglais:] Smile Food Project, une initiative gastronomique solidaire
blocks.text: Actuellement, Smile Food Project est à la recherche d’entreprises partenaires partageant les valeurs du projet et prêtes à lui apporter leur soutien.

blocks.section: La Fondation NRHK se lance dans la production de masques
blocks.text: La fondation NRHK a stoppé toutes ses activités liées aux heritages japonais afin de mettre à contribution ses imprimantes 3D dans la production de masques faciaux à l'attention des personnels soignants en contact avec le COIVD-19. Cet acte de volontariat permet de produire 120 masques par jour, afin d’aider au mieux les hôpitaux des zones les plus touchées du Kansai. Si vous souhaitez aider par une donation à la fondation ou si vous êtes en relation avec des services sanitaires en contact avec le COVID-19: contactez le consulat de France ou la NRHK (contact@nrhk.or.jp).

blocks.section: Thuasne lance une production de masques réutilisables
blocks.text: Thuasne lance une production de masques réutilisables

blocks.section: Thuasne lance une production de masques réutilisables
blocks.text: Avec le développement rapide de l’épidémie de coronavirus, Thuasne a décidé de mobiliser une partie de son outil industriel pour la fabrication de masques réutilisables. En tant que fabricant de dispositifs médicaux spécialisés dans les orthèses, le groupe s’est appuyé sur des matières textiles et des procédés de fabrication déjà maitrisés au sein de l’entreprise pour mettre en place un plan de développement intense et rapide. Les matières premières proviennent de pays européens, déjà en stock ou faciles à approvisionner. Ces masques répondent au guide d’exigences pour les masques barrières (AFNOR SPEC S76-001) publié ce vendredi 27 mars 2020 et tous leurs composants sont certifiés Reach ou OEKO-TEX®. Ils sont filtrants, respirants et sont produits à Saint-Etienne sur un site certifié ISO 9001-13485 (juin 2019).

blocks.section: Thuasne lance une production de masques réutilisables
blocks.text: Issus de la technologie du tissage, ces masques barrières sont destinés à l’usage de personnes saines ne présentant pas de symptôme clinique d’infection virale et n’étant pas en contact avec des personnes présentant de tels symptômes. Ils sont lavables 30 fois à 60°avec un séchage à l’air libre.

blocks.section: Thuasne lance une production de masques réutilisables
blocks.text: « Thuasne a voulu s’assurer que l’ensemble des tests soient réalisés avant toute communication et nous sommes en contact permanent avec les autorités compétentes dans le cadre du plan de protection des personnes. » a déclaré Elizabeth Ducottet, Président Directeur Général du Groupe. « Cette réponse est solide », ajoute t-elle « car notre outil industriel fait l’objet d’une politique d’investissement constante et notre personnel a répondu présent. Nous avons mis en place toutes les mesures nécessaires pour assurer leur protection et nous sommes fiers de leur engagement à nos côtés dans cette démarche de solidarité. En tant qu’industriel de la santé, nous nous devions de répondre présent ! »

blocks.text: Dons de masques, de pneus pour les véhicules d’urgence ou encore fabrication de masques type FFP2 lancée de manière industrielle, le groupe participe à l’effort collectif contre la pandémie.

blocks.section: Michelin utilise ses imprimantes 3D pour fabriquer masques et respirateurs
blocks.text: Grâce à la technique d’impression 3D, le groupe est parvenu en partenariat avec le CEA ( Commissariat à l'énergie atomique) et d’autres entreprises un masque imprimé en 3D plastique réutilisable équipé d’un filtre interchangeable en partenariat avec le CEA ( Commissariat à l'énergie atomique). Après homologation, Michelin espère pouvoir livrer les premiers masques 3D sous dizaine.

blocks.section: Michelin utilise ses imprimantes 3D pour fabriquer masques et respirateurs

title: Covid-19 : Point de situation au 10 avril 2020
description: Source : DG Trésor - Ministère de l'économie et des finances

blocks.text: COVID-19

blocks.section: Covid-19 : Point de situation au 10 avril 2020
blocks.text: Covid-19 : Point de situation au 10 avril 2020

blocks.section: Covid-19 : Point de situation au 10 avril 2020
blocks.text: Source : DG Trésor - Ministère de l'économie et des finances

blocks.section: Covid-19 : Point de situation au 10 avril 2020
blocks.text: L’épidémie de Covid-19 a un impact déjà fort sur les économies asiatiques, y compris celle du Japon. Le gouvernement japonais tente de prendre des mesures pour contrer les conséquences graves qui pourraient apparaître à la fois sur le court et long terme. À mesure que l’épidémie se poursuit dans le monde, les plans de soutien économique nippons se multiplient, accompagnés par des mesures financières.

blocks.section: Covid-19 : Point de situation au 10 avril 2020
blocks.text: Pour rappel, l’épidémie de Covid-19 touche l’économie japonaise par au moins cinq canaux :

blocks.section: Covid-19 : Point de situation au 10 avril 2020
blocks.text: Une baisse du flux touristique : forte décélération du tourisme chinois depuis fin janvier (pour mémoire, les touristes en provenance de Chine ont représenté 30% des touristes étrangers en 2019 et 40% des recettes touristiques) ; le nombre de visiteurs étrangers au Japon, toutes nationalités confondues, a chuté de 58% en février. Il s’agit de la plus forte baisse enregistrée depuis la catastrophe de Fukushima en 2011.

blocks.section: Covid-19 : Point de situation au 10 avril 2020
blocks.text: Un risque croissant de rupture dans les chaînes d’approvisionnement, en particulier dans l’automobile ou la métallurgie. La Chine a vu ses exportations se replier de 17,2% sur les deux premiers mois de l’année 2020. En conséquence les importations japonaises en provenance de Chine ont connu une chute historique de 47% en février 2020.

blocks.section: Covid-19 : Point de situation au 10 avril 2020
blocks.text: Une baisse des exportations vers la Chine, qui représentaient 19% des exportations nippones en 2019 et 2,7% du PIB du pays. Déjà en retrait sur 2019 (-7,7% par rapport à 2018), sur fond de ralentissement de la croissance chinoise, les exportations du Japon ont diminué en rythme annuel de 1% en février 2020. Il s’agit du 15 ème mois de baisse consécutive.

blocks.section: Covid-19 : Point de situation au 10 avril 2020
blocks.text: Un recul de la confiance des ménages japonais qui pourrait affecter la consommation privée (56% du PIB nippon). Particulièrement résiliente sur les trois premiers trimestres 2019, celle-ci a fortement baissé sur le 4 ème trimestre, à la suite de l’augmentation de la TVA en octobre 2019.

blocks.section: Covid-19 : Point de situation au 10 avril 2020
blocks.text: Un risque de ralentissement de l’activité économique mondiale , avec un impact économique du Covid-19 vraisemblablement supérieur à celui du SRAS (l’économie chinoise pesant 17% du PIB mondial en 2019 contre 6% en 2002).

blocks.section: Premier plan économique nippon – 14 février 2020
blocks.text: Premier plan économique nippon – 14 février 2020

blocks.section: Premier plan économique nippon – 14 février 2020
blocks.text: Le premier plan d’appui économique, approuvé le 14 février, s’est élevé à 15,3 milliards ¥ (128 millions €) et a visé les entreprises et personnes touchées par le coronavirus. Pour se financer, l’Etat japonais a utilisé les réserves budgétaires de l’exercice 2019/20. Site du Kantei (en japonais)

blocks.section: Premier plan économique nippon – 14 février 2020
blocks.text: Principales mesures budgétaires actées :

blocks.section: Premier plan économique nippon – 14 février 2020
blocks.text: 3 milliards ¥ destinés à la prise en charge des Japonais rapatriés de Chine et aux passagers du paquebot de croisière stationné à Yokohama ;

blocks.section: Premier plan économique nippon – 14 février 2020
blocks.text: 6,5 milliards ¥ pour permettre un renforcement du contrôle des infections domestiques (entre autres 3,6 milliards pour le renforcement du système d'inspection; 1 milliard pour la recherche et le développement de kits de test, de médicaments antiviraux et de vaccins; enfin une aide à la production de masques de 450 millions de yens);

blocks.section: Premier plan économique nippon – 14 février 2020
blocks.text: 3,4 milliards ¥ pour le renforcement des contrôles aux frontières

blocks.section: Premier plan économique nippon – 14 février 2020
blocks.text: 600 millions ¥ : réponse d'urgence aux industries touchées (notamment par la mise en place d'allocations pour le maintien de l'emploi dans les secteurs les plus touchés : 100 millions de yens)

blocks.section: Premier plan économique nippon – 14 février 2020
blocks.text: Enfin, 1,8 milliard ¥ pour un renforcement de la coopération internationale (en Asie et dans les régions du monde les plus touchées)

blocks.section: Premier plan économique nippon – 14 février 2020
blocks.text: Ces mesures budgétaires ont été complétées par des mesures financières : déblocage de prêts et garanties jusqu’à 500 milliards ¥ (4 milliards €) via l’agence financière publique Japan Finance Corporation :

blocks.section: Premier plan économique nippon – 14 février 2020
blocks.text: pour les établissements confrontés à un problème de trésorerie momentané du fait de la survenance du virus, plus particulièrement dans les secteurs du tourisme, de l’hôtellerie et de la restauration (prêts de 10 millions ¥ à 30 millions ¥ pour l’hôtellerie) ;

blocks.section: Premier plan économique nippon – 14 février 2020
blocks.text: pour les PME confrontées à une aggravation momentanée de leur courant d'affaires du fait de la survenance du virus : prêt de 48 millions ¥ maximum pour les microentreprises - prêt de 720 millions ¥ maximum pour les PME.

blocks.section: Deuxième plan d’urgence économique – 10 mars 2020
blocks.text: Deuxième plan d’urgence économique – 10 mars 2020

blocks.section: Deuxième plan d’urgence économique – 10 mars 2020
blocks.text: Annoncé le 10 mars 2020 par le Premier ministre japonais, le deuxième plan d’urgence s’élève à 3,6 milliards €, financé par le fonds de réserves budgétaires de l’exercice fiscal 2019/20, et complété par des mesures financières de plus de 13,4 milliards € . C’est la première fois que le fonds de réserve est utilisé pour lutter contre une épidémie : cette enveloppe est habituellement allouée aux seules mesures exceptionnelles liées aux catastrophes naturelles.

blocks.section: Deuxième plan d’urgence économique – 10 mars 2020
blocks.text: I. Des mesures fiscales pour un total de 430,8 milliards ¥ (3,6 milliards €), englobant :

blocks.section: Deuxième plan d’urgence économique – 10 mars 2020
blocks.text: 1. Un soutien à l’offre médicale et des mesures de prévention de la propagation (48,6 milliards ¥, 404 millions €)

blocks.section: Deuxième plan d’urgence économique – 10 mars 2020
blocks.text: Production et livraison de masques au grand public ainsi qu’aux établissements de santé et de soins (18,3 milliards ¥) ;

blocks.section: Deuxième plan d’urgence économique – 10 mars 2020
blocks.text: Renforcement des capacités de dépistage et d’accueil ; un soutien à la recherche de vaccins (13,3 milliards ¥) ;

blocks.section: Deuxième plan d’urgence économique – 10 mars 2020
blocks.text: Prise en charge des tests par l’assurance maladie ;

blocks.section: Deuxième plan d’urgence économique – 10 mars 2020
blocks.text: Communication publique multi-langues.

blocks.section: Deuxième plan d’urgence économique – 10 mars 2020
blocks.text: 2. Une aide aux familles touchées par la fermeture des écoles (246,3 milliards ¥, 2,07 milliards €)

blocks.section: Deuxième plan d’urgence économique – 10 mars 2020
blocks.text: L’essentiel (63%) consiste en une allocation journalière aux parents absents de leur travail (8 330 ¥ par jour et par personne pour les salariés réguliers et non réguliers (70€) et 4 100 ¥ par jour pour les personnes travaillant à leurs compte) ;

blocks.section: Deuxième plan d’urgence économique – 10 mars 2020
blocks.text: Mise à disposition de prêts d’urgence à faible montant sans intérêts (20,7 milliards ¥) ;

blocks.section: Deuxième plan d’urgence économique – 10 mars 2020
blocks.text: Soutien lié aux fermetures de cantine (remboursement de frais aux familles et soutien aux professionnels – 21,2 milliards ¥) ;

blocks.section: Deuxième plan d’urgence économique – 10 mars 2020
blocks.text: Promotion du télétravail.

blocks.section: Deuxième plan d’urgence économique – 10 mars 2020
blocks.text: 3. Un soutien aux entreprises touchées par une baisse d’activité et des mesures pour l’emploi (119,2 milliards ¥, 1 milliard €)

blocks.section: Deuxième plan d’urgence économique – 10 mars 2020
blocks.text: Prise en charge des intérêts des emprunts (78 milliards ¥) ;

blocks.section: Deuxième plan d’urgence économique – 10 mars 2020
blocks.text: Élargissement et rétroactivité du dispositif d’allocations pour le maintien de l’emploi (37,4 milliards ¥) ;

blocks.section: Deuxième plan d’urgence économique – 10 mars 2020
blocks.text: Mesures supplémentaires de soutien pour le secteur du tourisme.

blocks.section: Deuxième plan d’urgence économique – 10 mars 2020
blocks.text: 4. Des mesures d’urgence (16,7 milliards ¥ dont 92% de contribution à l’OMS – 144 millions €)

blocks.section: Deuxième plan d’urgence économique – 10 mars 2020
blocks.text: Dispositifs législatifs spéciaux, allègement des mesures administratives, soutien fiscal aux collectivités locales.

blocks.section: Deuxième plan d’urgence économique – 10 mars 2020
blocks.text: II. Des mesures financières pour un total de 1 600 milliards de yens (13,4 milliards €) :

blocks.section: Deuxième plan d’urgence économique – 10 mars 2020
blocks.text: Prêts à taux réduits (606 milliards ¥) à destination des PME ;

blocks.section: Deuxième plan d’urgence économique – 10 mars 2020
blocks.text: Nouvelles lignes de prêts (543 milliards ¥) ;

blocks.section: Deuxième plan d’urgence économique – 10 mars 2020
blocks.text: Aides et subventions de la Banque de Développement du Japon (204 milliards ¥) pour les grandes entreprises et les PME qui relocalisent leur production au Japon ;

blocks.section: Deuxième plan d’urgence économique – 10 mars 2020
blocks.text: Soutien financier de la part de JBIC (250 milliards ¥) pour les entreprises japonaises opérant à l’international.

blocks.section: Un 3 ème plan économique massif – 7 avril 2020
blocks.text: Un 3 ème plan économique massif – 7 avril 2020

blocks.section: Un 3 ème plan économique massif – 7 avril 2020
blocks.text: Annonce d’un vaste plan d’urgence économique (près de 1000 Mds USD) en parallèle de la déclaration de l’état d’urgence par le gouvernement Abe.

blocks.section: Un 3 ème plan économique massif – 7 avril 2020
blocks.text: Annonce le 7 avril 2020 d’un 3 ème plan d’urgence d’une valeur historique de 785 Mds USD dont 34% de mesures budgétaires et 66% de mesures financières.

blocks.section: Un 3 ème plan économique massif – 7 avril 2020
blocks.text: 1. Soutien à l'emploi et à la poursuite de l'activité (80 trillions ¥ soit 727 Mds d’USD, dont 200 de mesures budgétaires et 527 de mesures financières).

blocks.section: Un 3 ème plan économique massif – 7 avril 2020
blocks.text: Le dispositif de soutien aux entreprises comprend (i) des m esures de soutien à l’emploi par le relèvement du ratio de prise en charge par l’Etat du chômage technique, dès lors que l’entreprise s’engage à ne pas licencier et l’élargissement du dispositif d’ajustement de l’emploi aux travailleurs non-réguliers (ii) des mesures de soutien à la trésorerie avec octroi de prêts sans intérêt et sans caution et lignes de financement d’urgence pour le transport aérien (iii) des m esures pour la poursuite des activités des PME et des auto entrepreneurs ( freelance) via des allocations pour les entrepreneurs ayant subi une baisse de 50% des revenus et moratoire pour le versement des cotisations de sécurité sociale (iv) enfin une série de mesures fiscales (exemptions, crédit d’impôt et moratoire détaillés en annexe).

blocks.section: Un 3 ème plan économique massif – 7 avril 2020
blocks.text: Le dispositif de soutien aux ménages se concentre sur les particuliers subissant une baisse de revenus, par le versement, sous conditions, d'une allocation de 300 000 ¥ par foyer (environ 2 500€), un relèvement de 10 000 ¥ (80€) de l’allocation par enfant et une exemption du paiement des cotisations maladie et retraite. 13 millions de foyers pourraient bénéficier de de dispositif pour un montant de 4 trillions ¥.

blocks.section: Un 3 ème plan économique massif – 7 avril 2020
blocks.text: 2. Mesures pour renforcer la résilience du tissu économique ( 15 trillions ¥ soit 142,7 Mds USD, dont 92,7 de mesures budgétaires et 50 d’aides financières) : Ce pilier vise à promouvoir une moindre dépendance de l’économie au découpage mondial des chaînes de valeur et donc aux importations. Le Gouvernement n’en rappelle pas moins son rejet du protectionnisme et son soutien aux accords de libre-échange mais promeut la relocalisation sur le territoire des entreprises, afin de renforcer l’indépendance du pays. Ce chapitre rappelle fondamentalement la stratégie habituelle de nécessaire transformation numérique de la société et d’accroissement des investissements publics destinées à la prévention des catastrophes naturelles.

blocks.section: Un 3 ème plan économique massif – 7 avril 2020
blocks.text: 3. Mesures visant à promouvoir la consommation dans les secteurs les plus touchés (tourisme, hébergement, services de restauration, agriculture), comptant pour 8 trillions ¥ (soit 77,3 Mds USD, dont 30 Mds de mesures budgétaires et 47,3 Mds de mesures financières). Le gouvernement compte distribuer des coupons et/ou bons d’achats aux ménages.

blocks.section: Un 3 ème plan économique massif – 7 avril 2020
blocks.text: 4. Mesures sanitaires (mesure budgétaire de 2 500 Mds ¥ soit 22,7 Mds USD) : l’objectif est d’augmenter les capacités du système de santé japonais, de consolider l’offre médicale, de soutenir la recherche de vaccins et d’augmenter la production du traitement japonais « Avigan » pour exportation à l’étranger.

blocks.section: Un 3 ème plan économique massif – 7 avril 2020
blocks.text: 5. Préparations de l'avenir : un fonds de réserve de long terme (1,5 trillion ¥ soit 13,6 Mds USD) est constitué pour soutenir l'économie dans l'éventualité de nouvelles vagues infectieuses dans le pays.

blocks.section: Un 3 ème plan économique massif – 7 avril 2020
blocks.text: Pour plus d'informations, lire l'article dédié au troisième plan d'urgence économique.

blocks.text: COVID-19

blocks.section: COVID-19 : Téléchargement des attestations de déplacement international dérogatoires
blocks.text: COVID-19 : Téléchargement des attestations de déplacement international dérogatoires

blocks.section: COVID-19 : Téléchargement des attestations de déplacement international dérogatoires
blocks.text: Source : Ambassade de France au Japon Mise à jour : 7 avril 2020

blocks.section: COVID-19 : Téléchargement des attestations de déplacement international dérogatoires
blocks.text: Vous rentrez ou vous transitez par la France ? Vous devez désormais vous munir d’une attestation de déplacement international dérogatoire vers la France métropolitaine et l’Outre-Mer à présenter à votre compagnie aérienne et aux contrôles aux frontières avec les pièces justificatives requises.

blocks.section: COVID-19 : Téléchargement des attestations de déplacement international dérogatoires
blocks.text: Cette attestation est exigée pour une entrée ou un transit sur le territoire français depuis le lundi 6 avril 2020 à 18h (heure de Paris).

blocks.section: COVID-19 : Téléchargement des attestations de déplacement international dérogatoires
blocks.text: Accompagnée des pièces justificatives démontrant le statut invoqué, elle sera à présenter aux compagnies de transport, avant l’utilisation du titre de transport, par les passagers qui souhaitent voyager à destination du territoire français. Elle devra aussi être présentée aux autorités en charge du contrôle aux frontières, cela pour tout type de frontières :

blocks.section: COVID-19 : Téléchargement des attestations de déplacement international dérogatoires
blocks.text: aux frontières extérieures de la France (liaisons aériennes, maritimes, terrestres, dont les liaisons ferroviaires) ;

blocks.section: COVID-19 : Téléchargement des attestations de déplacement international dérogatoires
blocks.text: aux frontières intérieures de la France.

blocks.section: COVID19 - 3e plan d’urgence économique historique de près de 1000 Mds USD
blocks.text: Au fur et à mesure de l’avancée de l’épidémie, ce ne sont plus seulement les secteurs du tourisme, de la vente, de l’événementiel et du transport aérien qui sont touchés, mais l’ensemble de l’économie qui entrerait en récession. La décision, prise le 7 avril, de déclarer l’état d’urgence et de limiter les déplacements de la population - confinement léger et volontaire « à la japonaise » – exercera un impact négatif supplémentaire sur le 2ème trimestre. Nomura a révisé de -0,2% à -4,8% la croissance japonaise en 2020 tandis que BNP Paribas a évalué l’impact d’un confinement d’un mois à Tokyo à -0,7 point de PIB annuel.

blocks.section: 1. Un plan gonflé par d'anciennes mesures mais une somme tout de même historique
blocks.text: 1. Un plan gonflé par d'anciennes mesures mais une somme tout de même historique

blocks.section: 1. Un plan gonflé par d'anciennes mesures mais une somme tout de même historique
blocks.text: * Ce nouveau plan de 108 trillions ¥ (983 Mds US$) est le plus vaste décidé depuis la crise des subprimes de 2008 (58,8 trillions ¥) et représente plus de 20% du PIB nippon.

blocks.section: 1. Un plan gonflé par d'anciennes mesures mais une somme tout de même historique
blocks.text: Avec 359 milliards USD d’aides budgétaires (36% de l’ensemble), dont 265 milliards USD d’appui nouveau , le plan d’ensemble s’articule autour de 5 piliers : 74% des aides sont dirigés vers le maintien de l’emploi et la poursuite de l’activité, 15% vers la reconstruction d’un tissu économique plus résilient, 8% pour la reprise de l’activité, 2% en faveur de mesures destinées à prévenir la propagation de l’infection, 1% pour alimenter un fonds de réserve.

blocks.section: 1. Un plan gonflé par d'anciennes mesures mais une somme tout de même historique
blocks.text: L’enveloppe purement budgétaire de plan (265 milliards USD) apparaît facialement colossale : presque 6 fois l’appui budgétaire décidé récemment par la France ; 28% du budget de l’Etat, validé le 27 février - avant le 3ème plan d’urgence – à 102 658 Mds ¥ soit 933 milliards USD, 5 fois le budget annuel de la défense ou celui de l’éducation ; supérieur aux seules recettes annuelles de TVA du pays (200 milliards US$). Au regard des moyens déployés, la consolidation fiscale visée par le Gouvernement Abe (excédent primaire en 2025) semble plus que jamais hypothétique.

blocks.section: 1. Un plan gonflé par d'anciennes mesures mais une somme tout de même historique
blocks.text: Le Ministre des Finances a d’ailleurs annoncé des émissions prochaines d’obligations souveraines pour 16 000 milliards ¥ (145 milliards USD) qui pèseront sur le niveau de la dette publique (proche de 250% du PIB). Ces émissions permettront le financement du 1er budget additionnel pour l’année fiscale 2020/2021, soumis à la Diète dans les prochaines semaines : 16,8 trillions ¥ – 152 Mds USD sur les 359 Mds USD d’aides budgétaires, ce qui correspond à un déblocage immédiat de 42% de l’enveloppe budgétaire globale.

blocks.section: 2. Cinq pilliers : une attention particulière portée aux entreprises et aux ménages les plus touchés
blocks.text: des mesures de soutien à la trésorerie avec octroi de prêts sans intérêt et sans caution et lignes de financement d’urgence pour le transport aérien
