blocks.text: des mesures pour la poursuite des activités des PME et des auto entrepreneurs ( freelance) via des allocations pour les entrepreneurs ayant subi une baisse de 50% des revenus et moratoire pour le versement des cotisations de sécurité sociale

blocks.section: 2. Cinq pilliers : une attention particulière portée aux entreprises et aux ménages les plus touchés
blocks.text: enfin une série de mesures fiscales (exemptions, crédit d’impôt et moratoire détaillés en annexe).

blocks.section: 2. Cinq pilliers : une attention particulière portée aux entreprises et aux ménages les plus touchés
blocks.text: Le dispositif de soutien aux ménages se concentre sur les particuliers subissant une baisse de revenus, par le versement, sous conditions, d'une allocation de 300 000 ¥ par foyer (environ 2500€), un relèvement de 10 000 ¥ (80€) de l’allocation par enfant et une exemption du paiement des cotisations maladie et retraite. 13 millions de foyers pourraient bénéficier de de dispositif pour un montant de 4 trillions ¥.

blocks.section: 2. Cinq pilliers : une attention particulière portée aux entreprises et aux ménages les plus touchés
blocks.text: * Mesures pour renforcer la résilience du tissu économique (15 trillions ¥ soit 142,7 Mds USD, dont 92,7 de mesures budgétaires et 50 d’aides financières) : ce pilier vise à promouvoir une moindre dépendance de l’économie au découpage mondial des chaînes de valeur et donc aux importations. Le Gouvernement n’en rappelle pas moins son rejet du protectionnisme et son soutien aux accords de libre-échange mais promeut la relocalisation sur le territoire des entreprises, afin de renforcer l’indépendance du pays. Ce chapitre rappelle fondamentalement la stratégie habituelle de nécessaire transformation numérique de la société et d’accroissement des investissements publics destinées à la prévention des catastrophes naturelles.

blocks.section: 2. Cinq pilliers : une attention particulière portée aux entreprises et aux ménages les plus touchés
blocks.text: * Mesures visant à promouvoir la consommation dans les secteurs les plus touchés (tourisme, hébergement, services de restauration, agriculture) : ces mesures comptent pour 8 trillions ¥ (soit 77,3 Mds USD, dont 30 Mds de mesures budgétaires et 47,3 Mds de mesures financières). Le gouvernement compte distribuer des coupons et/ou bons d’achats aux ménages.

blocks.section: 2. Cinq pilliers : une attention particulière portée aux entreprises et aux ménages les plus touchés
blocks.text: * Mesures sanitaires (mesure budgétaire de 2 500 Mds ¥ soit 22,7 Mds USD) : l’objectif est d’augmenter les capacités du système de santé japonais, de consolider l’offre médicale, de soutenir la recherche de vaccins et d’augmenter la production du traitement japonais « Avigan » pour exportation à l’étranger.

blocks.section: 2. Cinq pilliers : une attention particulière portée aux entreprises et aux ménages les plus touchés
blocks.text: * Préparations de l'avenir : un fonds de réserve de long terme (1,5 trillion ¥ soit 13,6 Mds USD) est constitué pour soutenir l'économie dans l'éventualité de nouvelles vagues infectieuses dans le pays.

title: Crêpes party in Kansai for Candlemas
description: Today is Candlemas, a traditional Christian feast day, which most people in France associate with eating crêpes.

blocks.text: Kansai Event report

blocks.section: Crêpes party in Kansai for Candlemas
blocks.text: Crêpes party in Kansai for Candlemas

blocks.section: Crêpes party in Kansai for Candlemas
blocks.text: Today is Candlemas, a traditional Christian feast day, which most people in France associate with eating crêpes.

blocks.section: Crêpes party in Kansai for Candlemas
blocks.text: It is customary in France to eat crêpes with your family and/or friends for Candlemas , so it is very naturally that we organized a crêpes party at the office yesterday, February 1.

blocks.section: Crêpes party in Kansai for Candlemas
blocks.text: It is always a good occasion to gather people for a warm evening among our residents in Dojima Avanza . This year however, it was all the more special thanks to the generous sponsorship of two partners : Nichifutsu Shōji from Kobe and Yamasan from Kyoto.

blocks.section: Crêpes party in Kansai for Candlemas
blocks.text: Nichifutsu Shōji is a company specialized in supplying many high-quality base ingredients from France for restaurants and hotels (like doughs or chocolate). They also happen to have a retail grocery store Bon App' in Sannomiya, where you can find many goods usually impossible to source in Japan, like high quality jams with rare flavors.

blocks.section: Crêpes party in Kansai for Candlemas
blocks.text: On this special occasion, we were lucky enough to have special jams that are usually not actually available, but that we were authorized to use in our crêpes : rhubarbe, pêche de vigne and Framboise (raspberries)/chocolate. The taste is strong and brings you right back to those childhood memories the way the proverbial madeleine of Proust does.

blocks.section: Crêpes party in Kansai for Candlemas
blocks.text: Then there was Yamasan , a company in Uji, Kyoto that specialized in traditional, highly-concentrated and high-quality matcha tea. They provided a wide array of products, among which we used the matcha powder designed for baking, which we could mix in the dough to make a matcha flavored version of our usual crêpes.

blocks.section: Crêpes party in Kansai for Candlemas
blocks.text: In addition, there was a matcha chocolate that we could make into a ganache to fill the crêpes, and we were also given a sakura powder (not sweetened) that would give a nice sakura taste and color to the whip cream and ganache we mixed with seasonal strawberries.

blocks.section: Crêpes party in Kansai for Candlemas
blocks.text: To conclude, this was definitely a nice culinary experience that allowed us once more to discover or rediscover all that Kansai has to offer in terms of nice tastes and products. We do hope to organize even more convivial gatherings like this one throughout the year, and we are looking forward to your participation!

title: Cross Perspectives – Le Wagon Tokyo: Shaping Tomorrow’s Tech Talent in the Heart of Japan
description:
In this new episode of our Business series Cross Perspectives, we meet Le Wagon Tokyo, the Japanese campus of the renowned French coding bootcamp. Established in 2017, Le Wagon has trained more than 1,100 students in nearly nine years, becoming a key reference for those seeking a career change into tech in Japan.
« Before launching the campus, I met almost 200 people between 2013 and 2016. That network changed everything: I never felt like I was building a company in Japan, but rather within an international micro-ecosystem. » 
 An international journey turned entrepreneurial engine Before moving to Japan, Pierre spent ten years in Vietnam, where he helped build and scale a web-outsourcing company from 5 to 300 employees. Frequent business trips to meet Japanese clients gradually sparked his interest in the country. In 2016, he decided to take the leap and relocate to Japan to open a representative office, eventually meeting a future co-founder and launching Le Wagon Tokyo. It marked the start of a new entrepreneurial chapter, this time fully his own, in a country he was still learning to navigate.
 Starting a business in Japan: simple administration, complex banking Contrary to common perceptions, setting up a company in Japan was not the hardest part. “Incorporating the company took us about one month,” Pierre recalls. The real hurdles came afterward: securing a corporate bank account, dealing with local administrative nuances, and understanding the visa system. Yet, the strong network built over several years helped bypass many obstacles and accelerate the creation of the campus.
 Le Wagon Tokyo: training, reskilling, and empowering new tech professionals Le Wagon offers two intensive programs, Web Development and Data Science, available in full-time or part-time formats. The main audience: individuals seeking a complete career shift. “Around 60 to 70% of our students come for a full professional reconversion,” he explains. Courses are delivered entirely in English and designed to be highly structured, constantly updated, and accessible to both international and Japanese learners looking to upgrade their skills or enter the fast-growing tech industry.
 Official recognition and a unique role in the Japanese market For the past three years, Le Wagon Tokyo has been certified by Hello Work, Japan’s public employment agency, which subsidizes 50 to 70% of tuition fees. An exceptional recognition for a foreign institution. Authorities thoroughly reviewed each module of the curriculum before granting approval. Today, the Tokyo campus ranks among the top five of Le Wagon’s global network, alongside Paris, London, Berlin, and Rio.

title: Young Professionals committee event
description:
On Friday, October 6, 2023, a seminar titled "Customer Engagement through LINE – Luxury Retail Use Cases" was held at L'Espace@CCIFJ. The primary objective of this seminar was to exchange insights and experiences related to Client Development practices, with a specific focus on leveraging LINE as a communication channel in Japan.
The key speaker for the event was Thomas Prunel, the IT Digital Director at LVMH KK. Mr. Prunel brought his expertise and insights to the forefront, shedding light on the innovative strategies and approaches used in luxury retail for customer engagement through LINE.
Attendees left the seminar with a deeper understanding of how technology and digital platforms can be harnessed to elevate customer engagement in the luxury retail industry.

title: Cyber Security Incident Response Plan: Protecting your business in the digital world
description:
In our ever-evolving digital landscape, the threat of cyber-attacks looms large over businesses of all sizes.
Recognising the gravity of this situation, the CCIFJ has worked diligently to compile a comprehensive document entitled "Cyber Security Incident Response Plan", tailored specifically for our esteemed members. This guide is designed to equip you with proactive measures to mitigate damage and protect your business in the event of a cyber security breach.
You will find:  - Things you should never do: Before delving into the proactive measures, it's important to highlight the actions that must be avoided at all costs during a cybersecurity incident.  - 5 steps to take in the event of a malware infection: In the unfortunate event of a malware infection, quick and decisive action is paramount.   - A list of vendors offering prevention and solutions: To further strengthen your cybersecurity posture, we have compiled a list of CCIFJ corporate members that offer cutting-edge prevention solutions and assistance in minimising damage in the event of a cyber-attack.   Stay vigilant, stay safe.   READ THE DOCUMENT


Would you like to add your company to this list or provide additional information? Please contact t.funabashi@ccifj.or.jp 
This document is subject to change without notice.

title: Decline in the ratio of job vacancies to job applications
description: The ratio between job supply and demand fell in fiscal 2023, the first time in three years.

blocks.text: Foresight

blocks.section: Decline in the ratio of job vacancies to job applications
blocks.text: Decline in the ratio of job vacancies to job applications

blocks.section: Decline in the ratio of job vacancies to job applications
blocks.text: The ratio between job supply and demand fell in fiscal 2023, the first time in three years.

blocks.section: Decline in the ratio of job vacancies to job applications
blocks.text: With many industries facing severe labor shortages , the ratio of job offers to job demands declined in fiscal 2022.

blocks.section: Decline in the ratio of job vacancies to job applications
blocks.text: According to a report published by the Ministry of Labor on April 30, the ratio averaged 1.29 for the year ending March: a drop of 0.02 points compared to fiscal 2022. This ratio means that there are 129 vacancies for every 100 applicants.

blocks.section: Decline in the ratio of job vacancies to job applications
blocks.text: The average number of jobseekers rose by 0.1% compared to FY2022, reaching 1.92 million per month, while the average number of active job offers fell by 1.6% to around 2.47 million.

blocks.section: Decline in the ratio of job vacancies to job applications
blocks.text: Masahiko Yamada, Director General of the Ministry of Labor's Employment Security Bureau, explained this phenomenon by companies’ investments in labor-saving technologies .

blocks.section: Decline in the ratio of job vacancies to job applications
blocks.text: Rising material prices may also be behind the decline in this ratio, particularly in the manufacturing and construction sectors.

blocks.section: Decline in the ratio of job vacancies to job applications
blocks.text: Unemployment averaged 2.6% in fiscal 2023, unchanged from the previous year.

title: Discover the experience sharing of Benjamin Costa, Japan Director of La Maison du Chocolat.
description:
A business leader with extensive experience bridging French and Japanese cultures answers our questions.

Mr Costa has been the Japan Director of La Maison du Chocolat for three and a half years. La Maison du Chocolat is a French high end chocolate company established in Japan since 1998.
He chose to take on this challenge in order to contribute to the development of a French company in Japan, while benefiting from a certain level of operational freedom, allowing better adaptation to the specificities of the Japanese market.
Today, the brand relies on a team of over one hundred employees and operates ten boutiques located in major cities across Japan. While online sales and corporate gifting also play an important role, the company’s core business remains its retail stores, in a country where the sense of service is truly a way of life.

Key development insights for a retail company in Japan
The brand, now very popular in Japan, has successfully adapted to local consumption habits. However, competition in this market is intense, and it is essential to constantly identify new trends in order to remain attractive, particularly to younger consumers. Launching a new collection every season is essential, but it is not sufficient on its own. To expand the customer base, an evolving and flexible marketing strategy is also required.
More generally, the retail sector is highly trend driven.
At the head of the company, Mr Costa works with an entirely Japanese team. From his arrival, he sought to involve his employees more closely in decision making, not only in how objectives should be implemented, but also in defining the best way to achieve them.
The working culture in Japan, as well as consumer expectations, differ significantly from those in other markets. As a result, relying on the skills and perspective of Japanese team members is essential to successfully develop the business.
From a management perspective, it is important to show employees that their opinions matter and to support them in bringing their ideas forward. They must be encouraged to propose new initiatives, which is not always easy in a country that values stability and tends to avoid risks associated with change. Progress must be gradual, and it is through a series of small wins that change takes hold, allowing what was once considered “not possible” to become possible.
Mr Costa explained that he began with quick wins, such as obtaining approval from headquarters to change the color of a packaging box that had long been considered untouchable. This helped demonstrate that parts of the product range could be adjusted when supported by strong arguments. Thanks to these small successes, his teams gradually began to put forward new ideas.
Decision making : 
In Japan, decision making to validate a project can take up to ten times longer, as Japanese stakeholders need to review and approve every detail, sometimes repeatedly, before moving forward.
To keep discussions progressing and avoid endless intermediate meetings, Mr Costa summarizes the key decision points by email. This approach helps streamline exchanges and ensures that only the most essential meetings are held.
He also seeks to optimize collaboration by confirming, at the end of each meeting, that the next steps are clearly understood and that timelines are fully aligned. The objective is not to move as quickly as in France, but rather to reduce project and planning cycles as much as possible, from discussion and validation through to implementation.
Future challenges :
Regardless of the sector, it is important to note that the Japanese have a highly developed sense of service but a commercial mindset that is quite different from ours, if not relatively underdeveloped. In retail, it is still common to see many sales staff in stores, but this does not necessarily mean greater efficiency, often due to a lack of training. However, with the challenges of an aging population and low birth rates, mindsets will need to evolve by drawing inspiration from practices abroad, with the aim of optimizing workforce size. Training will therefore become a key issue in the future, in order to manage increasingly lean teams.

Retail in the agri food sector : logistics and distribution channels
The brand’s chocolates are produced in France, where the core know how is located. However, there is also a pastry workshop in Tokyo, notably for the production of éclairs. The company has chosen to import its products directly and relies on a freight forwarder to handle all customs procedures, which are undoubtedly among the strictest in the world.
The brand is present in major department stores such as Hankyu, Newoman, Matsuya and Takashimaya, the Japanese equivalents of Galeries Lafayette in France. These venues remain a safe and effective channel for the development of luxury brands, as they enhance brand image and offer strong customer traffic, but competition is extremely intense.
In the agri food retail sector, having a physical presence is essential. Visual appeal matters, and tasting and product presentation also play a crucial role.
It is important to keep in mind that some importers look for brands to create a short term buzz, and that one year later their commercial efforts may shift in favor of a new product. As a result, it is often necessary to have a local representative to support the importer when choosing this distribution channel.
As for e commerce, it remains a limited channel for the agri food sector, accounting for only 3 percent of turnover in this segment, even though Japan is the fourth largest e-commerce market in the world.
With this channel, it is essential to ensure strong logistics services. For example, Yamato is a reliable partner for delivery.
E-commerce alone does not work, but it remains an interesting growth driver when used as a complement. It must be supported by strong commercial actions such as advertising, product demonstrations, tastings, pop up stores and physical boutiques.

To sum up, Mr Costa has given us valuable insights into how a French retail company operates in Japan. His experience was highly enriching, and we hope it will be just as insightful for all readers of this article.
Of course, there are countless experiences to share. Our Business Services team supports and advises companies throughout their entire development in Japan.
Feel free to contact us to discuss your project : business@ccifj.or.jp

blocks.text: A survey carried out by the Japanese company Mynavi revealed that over 90% of foreign workers currently interviewed in Japan wished to continue working there after the expiry of their current visa.

blocks.section: Despite the yen's weakness, is Japan still an attractive country for foreign workers?
blocks.text: Although this figure is high, it represents a drop compared to the company's survey conducted in 2022. In fact, 5.7% of those surveyed said they did not want to continue working in Japan.

blocks.section: Despite the yen's weakness, is Japan still an attractive country for foreign workers?
blocks.text: The main reason for this is the depreciation of the yen (40% of respondents), which has reduced the income of foreign workers once converted into their home currency.

blocks.section: Despite the yen's weakness, is Japan still an attractive country for foreign workers?
blocks.text: Poor working conditions, with long hours of overtime and poor economic prospects, are also a factor in Japan's attractiveness to foreign workers.

blocks.section: Despite the yen's weakness, is Japan still an attractive country for foreign workers?
blocks.text: “Japan's declining attractiveness to foreign talent is becoming a reality,” said Motoki Yuzuriha, President of Mynavi Global. For him, “companies need to improve wages and other benefits and, at the same time, create workplaces where foreign and Japanese workers can work well together.”

title: Marketing & Retail Committee - Event Recap
description:

The event featured Mr. Malik ROUMANE, President and Representative Director of MCDecaux Japan K.K., who spoke on "Developing a Media in Japan: The Story of a Worldwide Out of Home Advertising Leader."

title: DEVIALET opens its first boutique in Tokyo, at NEWoMan Takanawa
description:
September 12 marked a new milestone for the French house of acoustic innovation. DEVIALET has inaugurated its boutique inside the brand-new NEWoMan Takanawa shopping complex. Located in the North Wing, this new address is the brand’s first standalone store in the Japanese capital.
After captivating enthusiasts in prestigious locations such as GINZA SIX and Isetan Shinjuku, the brand is now strengthening its presence in Tokyo with a space entirely dedicated to its universe.
The boutique offers a wide selection of DEVIALET’s signature products and invites visitors to discover the brand’s excellence in sound within an elegant, immersive setting designed for the ultimate listening experience.
Conveniently accessible from JR Takanawa Gateway Station, the boutique is located at the North Wing entrance of the shopping complex, near the Nicolai Bergmann store.
DEVIALET NEWoMan Takanawa is now open, welcoming music lovers and audio design enthusiasts. The team looks forward to hosting you and sharing the DEVIALET experience.

title: Discover the beauty of Japanese tradition with Bonjour Matsue
description: Matsue City organized a workshop focused on Japanese confectionery and matcha preparation.

blocks.section: Discover the beauty of Japanese tradition with Bonjour Matsue
blocks.text: Discover the beauty of Japanese tradition with Bonjour Matsue

blocks.section: Discover the beauty of Japanese tradition with Bonjour Matsue
blocks.text: Matsue City organized a workshop focused on Japanese confectionery and matcha preparation.

blocks.section: Discover the beauty of Japanese tradition with Bonjour Matsue
blocks.text: ※This is an event organized by Matsue-city. As spring graces Matsue Castle with an enchanting display of cherry blossoms in full bloom, we invite you to partake in a truly inspiring experience—a Japanese confectionery-making workshop that promises to delight your senses. Dive into the essence of Japanese culture as you create your own Matcha, and savor the satisfaction of enjoying the very tea you have crafted with your own hands. In Matsue, tea is a big part of daily life. Even though the Japanese tea ceremony is often perceived as a formal and codified activity, the local tea culture is simple and open to everyone. People usually drink tea twice a day during the dedicated « tea time » (around 10 am and 3 pm). In the local supermarket, it is not unusual to find some high-quality matcha and Japanese traditional sweets (wagashi) that are used as a side dish to balance the tea’s bitterness. The daily ritual unfolds simply: boil the water, pour it into a bowl, stir the matcha, and savor it while relaxing. A key figure in this tradition is Harusato Matsudaira, known as Fumaï, the 7th lord of Matsue during the Edo period. He promoted tea ceremonies as an art of hospitality, making them welcoming and accessible. His influence led to the annual "Matsue Castle Grand Tea Ceremony," one of Japan's significant tea festivals. Matsue is also known for its wagashi artisans, alongside Kyoto and Kanazawa. Visitors can discover how they are made in one of the many historic shops of the castle town. We invite you to stop by Matsue and enjoy tea just like Fumaï envisioned: open to everyone, simple, and a perfect way to unwind. Contact: Bonjour Matsue Event Management Office(Naccy Corporation) Mail: bonjourmatsue(@)naccy.jp

blocks.text: This interview features Bertrand Stephann, founder and CEO of Alcméon, a SaaS (Software as a Service) platform dedicated to professional messaging. It is aimed primarily at large enterprises wishing to optimize their customer interactions via messaging applications such as WhatsApp and Line.

blocks.text: ▶️ 11 minutes ? Language : french - available subtitles : french, english and japanese

blocks.section: Discover the key to successful customer relations with Bertrand Stephann, founder and CEO of Alcméon!
blocks.text: Topics: retail, LINE, customer relations, conversational marketing, digital strategy, SaaS, sales optimization, customer engagement.

blocks.section: Discover the key to successful customer relations with Bertrand Stephann, founder and CEO of Alcméon!
blocks.text: Bertrand Stephann's background:

blocks.section: Discover the key to successful customer relations with Bertrand Stephann, founder and CEO of Alcméon!
blocks.text: In the interview, Mr.Stephann looks back on his career path, which was marked by over 25 years in the digital industry, with management positions at Allociné and AuFéminin, before turning to creating software to improve customer relations. He explains that the idea for Alcméon arose from an observation: online advertising can confuse users, and brands need tools to offer their customers helpful, fluid responses.

blocks.section: Discover the key to successful customer relations with Bertrand Stephann, founder and CEO of Alcméon!
blocks.text: The importance of the Line application:

blocks.section: Discover the key to successful customer relations with Bertrand Stephann, founder and CEO of Alcméon!
blocks.text: A large part of the interview is devoted to using Line, a must-have messaging app in Japan, which counts 78% of the Japanese population as active users. Mr.Stephann describes Line as a “super app” that enables communication, payment, or ordering of services, making it essential for brands wishing to establish themselves in Japan. He shares concrete examples of success, including Christian Dior Couture, which uses Alcméon to manage its customer interactions on Line in Japan.

blocks.section: Discover the key to successful customer relations with Bertrand Stephann, founder and CEO of Alcméon!
blocks.text: The challenges of personalisation:

blocks.section: Discover the key to successful customer relations with Bertrand Stephann, founder and CEO of Alcméon!
blocks.text: Finally, the interview explores the challenges of personalising customer experiences and the strategies companies must adopt, particularly in Japan. Stephann recommends starting with simple use cases and adapting to the Japanese market’s particularities, where customer service expectations are extremely high. He stresses the importance of providing smooth, efficient customer journeys to guarantee optimum satisfaction.

blocks.section: Discover the key to successful customer relations with Bertrand Stephann, founder and CEO of Alcméon!
blocks.text: Conclusion :

blocks.section: Discover the key to successful customer relations with Bertrand Stephann, founder and CEO of Alcméon!
blocks.text: Mr. Stephann emphasises the two pillars of good customer service: responsiveness and attention to detail, essential for building customer loyalty and differentiation in a highly competitive digital environment.

blocks.section: Discovering Tokyo’s Financial Landscape: A Learning Expedition with ESCP
blocks.text: The CCIFJ, in partnership with ESCP, organized a Learning Expedition for students of the Executive Master in Strategic Finance.

blocks.section: Discovering Tokyo’s Financial Landscape: A Learning Expedition with ESCP
blocks.text: Understanding Japan’s financial ecosystem requires to discover all different kinds of actors. It calls for direct exposure to the institutions that structure the market, the companies that innovate within it, and the legal and regulatory frameworks that ensure its stability. This was precisely the ambition of the Learning Expedition to Japan jointly organized by the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan and ESCP Business School for participants of the Executive Master in Strategic Finance.

blocks.section: Discovering Tokyo’s Financial Landscape: A Learning Expedition with ESCP
blocks.text: Over the course of an intensive week in Tokyo, executives and finance professionals were immersed in Japan’s financial architecture, guided by a carefully designed learning journey that connected macroeconomics, banking, fintech, regulation, law, ESG and M&A. The objective was not only to observe Japan’s financial system, but to understand how its different components interact and support one of the world’s most advanced economies.

blocks.section: Discovering Tokyo’s Financial Landscape: A Learning Expedition with ESCP
blocks.text: Day 1 – Foundations: Japan’s Economy and Financial Innovation

blocks.section: Discovering Tokyo’s Financial Landscape: A Learning Expedition with ESCP
blocks.text: The Learning Expedition began in Tokyo with a comprehensive introduction to Japan’s economic, legal, and financial environment. Participants gained a 360° view of Japan’s macroeconomic landscape, business practices, taxation, and legal frameworks through sessions with:

blocks.section: Discovering Tokyo’s Financial Landscape: A Learning Expedition with ESCP
blocks.text: Arthur Sogno-Pèes from the Regional Economic Service of the French Embassy in Japan, offered a comprehensive overview of Japan’s economic landscape.

blocks.section: Discovering Tokyo’s Financial Landscape: A Learning Expedition with ESCP
blocks.text: Emilie Teruel-Esclattier, Head of Business Development at the French Chamber of Commerce in Japan, led an interactive session on intercultural communication, highlighting the practical realities of doing business in Japan.

blocks.section: Discovering Tokyo’s Financial Landscape: A Learning Expedition with ESCP
blocks.text: Miyako Ikuta, attorney-at-law at Kitahama Partners, provided an introduction to the Japanese legal framework, highlighting key differences and similarities with French law.

blocks.section: Discovering Tokyo’s Financial Landscape: A Learning Expedition with ESCP
blocks.text: Matthew Denver, Senior Manager in taxatation at EY Japan, presented insights into taxation practices in Japan.

blocks.section: Discovering Tokyo’s Financial Landscape: A Learning Expedition with ESCP
blocks.text: In the afternoon, the group met Kazuhiro Nakano, President of Famima Digital One, a subsidiary of the FamilyMart Group, to learn about FamiPay, the company’s mobile payment and digital financial services platform. The session highlighted how traditional retail companies in Japan are leveraging trust, data, and scale to drive fintech innovation, demonstrating the integration of established business models with cutting-edge financial solutions.

blocks.section: Discovering Tokyo’s Financial Landscape: A Learning Expedition with ESCP
blocks.text: Day 2 – Banks as Strategic Pillars of the Economy

blocks.section: Discovering Tokyo’s Financial Landscape: A Learning Expedition with ESCP
blocks.text: The second day focused on Japan’s banking sector and its pivotal role in economic development. The day began with a session at Crédit Agricole Corporate & Investment Bank Japan , where participants gained insights into how an international bank operates within the Japanese market. Sylvain Legros, Head of Corporate Planning, and Nicolas Sauvage, President of Crédit Agricole Life Insurance Japan, discussed the bank’s overall strategy and its approach to life insurance in Japan. Nobuaki Moroi, Head of Aircraft Finance, and Tamami Kodemura, Head of Export Finance, shared their expertise on financing solutions for global trade and aircraft, while Mohamed-Cherif Lafram, Deputy CFO of CA Life Insurance Japan, addressed the challenges and opportunities arising from Japan’s ageing society. Daisaku Chabata, Head of Sustainable & Investment Banking, highlighted ESG initiatives and the integration of sustainable finance into corporate strategy.

blocks.section: Discovering Tokyo’s Financial Landscape: A Learning Expedition with ESCP
blocks.text: A working lunch at Conrad Tokyo allowed participants to continue the discussions with the CACIB team, providing practical insights into the intersection of finance, regulation, and strategic decision-making in the Japanese context.

blocks.section: Discovering Tokyo’s Financial Landscape: A Learning Expedition with ESCP
blocks.text: The day concluded with a session at SBI Shinsei Bank , a leading Japanese bank, where participants explored the Group’s approach to international expansion, structured financial solutions, and ESG initiatives. Yasuhiro Fujiki, General Manager of the Group’s International Business Division and Head of Group Corporate Planning, shared insights on the bank’s global strategy and international operations while Yuko Nagasawa, Head of Group Structured Solutions and Head of Group Corporate Planning, discussed how the bank develops tailored financial solutions to support corporate growth and investment.

blocks.section: Discovering Tokyo’s Financial Landscape: A Learning Expedition with ESCP
blocks.text: These exchanges highlighted how Japanese banks serve as strategic partners for long-term industrial, demographic, and sustainable development, emphasizing growth and resilience over short-term performance.

blocks.section: Discovering Tokyo’s Financial Landscape: A Learning Expedition with ESCP
blocks.text: Day 3 – Legal and Regulatory Foundations

blocks.section: Discovering Tokyo’s Financial Landscape: A Learning Expedition with ESCP
blocks.text: The third day was dedicated to the legal and regulatory frameworks that underpin Japan’s financial system. The morning session with Hiroyuki Kanae and Kenji Hirooka, attorneys at Anderson Mori & Tomotsune , provided participants with an in-depth view of Japan’s M&A market, including hostile takeovers, corporate governance, and the legal nuances that influence cross-border transactions.

blocks.section: Discovering Tokyo’s Financial Landscape: A Learning Expedition with ESCP
blocks.text: In the afternoon, the group met with Laurent Dubois, attorney at TMI Associates , for a discussion on the key differences between French and Japanese corporate and finance law. The session also explored practical implications for international business, including structuring cross-border deals, navigating regulatory compliance, and understanding how legal frameworks shape strategic decision-making in Japan’s corporate environment.

blocks.section: Discovering Tokyo’s Financial Landscape: A Learning Expedition with ESCP
blocks.text: Day 4 – Governance, Regulation, and Market Infrastructure

blocks.section: Discovering Tokyo’s Financial Landscape: A Learning Expedition with ESCP
blocks.text: The fourth day focused on the institutions that uphold transparency and stability in Japan’s financial markets. Participants visited the Tokyo Stock Exchange to understand its role as the central hub of the country’s capital markets. They then met with Takashi Somekawa from the Financial Services Agency (JFSA) , who, together with Taisuke Jingu, provided an in-depth overview of the FSA’s regulatory activities, including its work in financial markets and private equity, and discussed the agency’s role in supporting the development of these markets in Japan. The day concluded with a visit to the Bank of Japan , where participants enjoyed a guided tour of the historic institution.

blocks.section: Discovering Tokyo’s Financial Landscape: A Learning Expedition with ESCP
blocks.text: Day 5 – M&A, Succession, and the Future of Japanese Finance

blocks.section: Discovering Tokyo’s Financial Landscape: A Learning Expedition with ESCP
blocks.text: The Learning Expedition concluded with a comprehensive look at Japan’s evolving M&A landscape and the critical role played by advisory firms in facilitating transactions. Participants attended a session led by Kazuhiro Ishikawa, Representative Director of HC Financial Advisors , one of Japan’s leading M&A advisory firms. He provided a practical perspective on how demographic shifts, such as an aging population and business succession challenges, are reshaping deal flow, generating both complex challenges and new opportunities for domestic investors. The session highlighted the strategic importance of advisory expertise in navigating Japan’s unique corporate and regulatory environment, offering participants valuable insights into the mechanisms behind cross-border and domestic mergers and acquisitions.

blocks.section: Discovering Tokyo’s Financial Landscape: A Learning Expedition with ESCP
blocks.text: Conclusion : A Strategic Learning Journey

blocks.section: Discovering Tokyo’s Financial Landscape: A Learning Expedition with ESCP
blocks.text: This Learning Expedition provided participants with an integrated understanding of Japan’s financial ecosystem, spanning regulators, financial institutions, legal frameworks, fintechs, advisory firms, and market infrastructure. More than a series of visits, it was conceived as a coherent, immersive journey aligned with ESCP Business School’s Executive Master in Strategic Finance.

blocks.section: Discovering Tokyo’s Financial Landscape: A Learning Expedition with ESCP
blocks.text: The French Chamber of Commerce in Japan is proud to act as a key facilitator between France and Japan, connecting executive education programs with leading companies, financial institutions, and business leaders. Through this expedition, participants gained both technical knowledge and a nuanced understanding of how Japan’s financial system functions within one of the world’s largest economies.

title: EBC: 2024 White Paper launch event
description:
The EBC will launch its 2024 White Paper on 29 February at the EU Delegation.
The White Paper, the cornerstone product of the EBC, is a meticulous compilation of the challenges faced by its members. It is regularly updated and available on the EBC website, ensuring that stakeholders are kept abreast of the latest developments.
 The event promises valuable insights from five distinguished industry representatives Legal services, Pharmaceutical Industries, Food & Agriculture, Sustainability and Materials. This is a unique opportunity to hear first-hand from experts not only about the challenges facing European industry in Japan, but also about the recommendations proposed to address these issues. The White Paper serves as a powerful advocacy tool to influence improvements in the Japanese regulatory framework.  
Interesting in joining the EBC Committees:
The European Business Council (EBC) has 22 committees devoted to improving the business environment for European companies in different sectors.
By becoming a member of a committee, you will be able to:
 	Discuss regulatory developments and issues of common concern; 	Visit Japanese government officials, write position papers and engage in media campaigns, when necessary; 	Provide briefings on the current state of your specific business sector for visiting European Commission officials and various European industry representatives; 	Give presentations to governmental bodies and political parties upon request; 	Contribute one chapter to the annual White Paper; 	Exchange sector-specific information; 
and many other opportunities!
To register, please email: ebc@ebc-jp.com

title: EBC Flash Survey on the Impact of the entry ban on European companies and their Japanese partners
description:
The entry restrictions imposed by the Japanese government on foreign non-residents since January 2021 seem to have negative economic impacts on foreign and Japanese businesses and the economy in Japan.
The EBC has been actively advocating this issue through various meetings with the Japanese authorities and by publishing on May 28 a joint statement with the ACCJ, the ANZCCJ and the CCCJ.
To better evaluate the impact of the entry restrictions on European businesses and use the results for advocacy purposes, the EBC is launching a flash survey for members of the various national European Chambers. The more companies that take part in the survey, the more representative the results become, hence more useful. We therefore hope for your cooperation and support.
Fill out the survey
 From Tuesday June 15 to July 15.

title: EBC - Results of the Flash Survey on the impact of the entry ban on European and American companies and their Japanese partners
description:
The objective of this survey is to better understand the current situation among European and American companies operating in Japan confronted by the entry restrictions due to the COVID-19 crisis and to highlight the direct impact on their economic activity as well as on their Japanese partners.
This survey was designed by the European Business Council in Japan (EBC) and sent to the 15 European National Chambers of Commerce in Japan, who circulated it among their members between June 15 and July 7. The American Chamber of Commerce in Japan (ACCJ) also circulated the survey among its Commercial Membership Representative Members from June 17 to June 25.
325 European and American companies, with headquarters based in 19 European countries, Japan, and the United States, responded. The data was collected anonymously.

Since May 2020, and except for a short period between 1 October 2020 and 7 January 2021, it has been very difficult if not almost impossible for foreign new expatriates or experts to enter Japan. As a result, many respondents report that they lack key personnel and specialists from abroad and current projects have been suspended or new projects cannot be developed, leading to production delays and the cancellation of foreign direct investments into Japan. Companies’ Japanese clients and partners have also been financially impacted.
• 68% of the surveyed foreign companies say that the impact of the entry restrictions on their Japanese customers or partners is significant.
• 12% of respondents estimated that the financial impact on their company’s customers and partners could be over ¥500 million, and 18% of respondents estimated the impact could be between ¥10 million - ¥50 million.
• 71% of respondents say their business plans involve the use of overseas specialists, most of whom have been unable to enter Japan.

title: EBC Survey on Japan’s New Foreigners’ Policy
description:
The European Business Council in Japan (EBC) has launched a survey regarding Japan’s new Foreigners’ Policy.
Several European National chambers of commerce have recently informed the EBC that some of their member companies are becoming increasingly concerned about potential difficulties arising from recent changes in Japan’s visa and immigration policies.
In order to conduct effective advocacy with the Japanese government, the EBC would like to better assess the impact of these changes on European businesses operating in Japan and identify the main issues and concerns faced by companies.
We would therefore greatly appreciate your participation in this survey, available at the following link:
https://www.surveymonkey.com/r/2DPM3R8

title: EBC welcomes Nikolaus Boltze as its next President
description:
The European Business Council in Japan (EBC) has announced the appointment of Nikolaus Boltze as its next President, following the completion of its presidential election process on 12 November. 
His appointment will take effect in January 2026.
Currently serving as Country Representative for thyssenkrupp AG in Japan, Nikolaus brings extensive leadership experience and a strong understanding of Europe-Japan business relations. Within the EBC, he has been actively involved in several committees, notably as Chair of the Aeronautics, Space, Defence & Security Committee.
He has also served as President of the EU-Japan Centre for Industrial Cooperation and represents his company on the European side of the EU-Japan Business Round Table, contributing to high-level policy discussions with Japanese and European authorities.
With his background in corporate leadership and cross-border cooperation, Nikolaus Boltze is well positioned to lead the EBC’s strategic direction from January 2026, succeeding Laurent Depus, whose dedicated leadership continues until 31 December 2025.

title: EIFJ Tokyo: a bilingual school of excellence, 123 students from nursery to middle school - tuition fees discounts for all its members
description:
At the French-Japanese International School of Tokyo, we educate students to become creative and ethical citizens through an official, comprehensive & bilingual curriculum in classes of excellence. We teach all students to think objectively & behave responsibly, to shape their own views and respect others, to determine their aims in life and be successful.
The French-Japanese International School of Tokyo (established in 2019), is a primary (2019), secondary school (2022), and a French International nursery, with a total capacity of 250 places, supported by the Tokyo Metropolitan Government. A forthcoming mission by the AEFE (Agency for French Education Abroad - French Ministry) could result in support towards accreditation if the conditions are met.
Because at EIFJ, a school founded by parents, where all the parents' voices count (represented by their delegates in the School Council), we believe that it is essential that no French or French-Japanese student should leave the French education system, in a difficult economic context. We are therefore proposing as well a special offer (valid until 31 July 2023) for French and French-Japanese families: first enrolment fee and annual fund waived. Further exemptions and discounts are also available for students demonstrating excellent academic results, and for siblings. title: Eighty Days Japan
description:
Eighty Days is an accredited Yunus Social Business Company and Tokyo-based DMC founded in 2016. We aim to bolster the local economies of rural areas, protect and rejuvenate traditional cultures that are in danger of being lost, and bring overseas visitors to parts of Japan that we believe deserve more attention and appreciation than they’re currently receiving. We specialize in providing high-end FIT, MICE, and group tours, where we aim to connect adventurous visitors with local people eager to share their passion for their areas.  Our services:
- Custom tours and experiences - we cover a wide range of customers from FIT to MICE and educational tours, as well as cover all 47 prefectures in Japan. - Tour Guides - we provide local and experienced tour guides across the country. - Reservations and Logistical Services - we provide assistance with reservations for accommodation, transfers, and other bookings. - We offer unique Online Live Experiences - Immersive introductions to local areas and cultural activities in Japan through online live seminars

title: Election of Laurent Depus as President of the EBC
description:
The European Business Council (EBC) has announced the election of Laurent Depus as a new President. Laurent Depus officially assumed his role on January 1, 2024, succeeding the former President, Michael Mroczek.
Laurent Depus, a seasoned professional with 36 years of experience in Japan's financial sector, brings a wealth of knowledge and expertise to the role. As a Belgian national, he has held key positions in senior management across Anglo-Saxon, European, and domestic companies. His extensive background includes years of regulatory relationship management and advocacy with Japan's financial authorities and administrations.
Notably, Laurent serves as an ambassador for FinCity.Tokyo and holds a position on the Board of SMBC Trust Bank. He remains actively engaged with foreign financial stakeholders, demonstrating his commitment to fostering strong international ties. Additionally, Laurent collaborates closely with the International Bankers Association (IBA), further contributing to the global financial dialogue.
The EBC extends its sincere gratitude to Michael Mroczek for his exceptional leadership during the past five years. His fundamental contributions have played a pivotal role in advancing the mission and goals of the EBC.

title: France Japon Eco
description:
The French Chamber of Commerce in Tokyo hosted a Jolt Capital lead insightful conference that delved into the rapidly evolving world of growth deeptech investment. With a remarkable turnout of industry professionals, entrepreneurs, and investors, the event underscored Jolt Capital's commitment to nurturing cutting-edge technologies beyond the transient trends that often plague the investment landscape.
The night featured an engaging discussion led by Jolt Capital’s founder, Jean Schmitt, who shared insights into the firm’s innovative approach to investment, highlighting its successful portfolio that includes companies like Heptagon and NILT. Schmitt emphasized the importance of focusing on the fundamental strengths of technologies and the capabilities of the companies at their scaling stage, a philosophy that has positioned Jolt as a leading player in the European deeptech scene.
We would like to extend our heartfelt thanks to the speakers. Your insights and expertise made a significant impact and inspired all attendees.

title: In July 2026, the Orchestre national d'Île-de-France goes to Japan on an exceptional tour
description:
From 1 to 18 July 2026, the Orchestre national d'Île-de-France will travel for its first tour in Japan:
10 concerts in some of the country’s most prestigious venues, and 2 return concerts in Paris (Philharmonie de Paris and La Seine Musicale);8 cities visited: Osaka, Takamatsu, Fukuoka, Tokyo, Sapporo, Nagoya, Hamamatsu, Musashino;More than 20,000 spectators expected.
This international tour, dedicated to artistic dialogue between France and Japan, will celebrate friendship and cultural exchange between the two countries.
The Orchestra is seeking partners to support this Japanese adventure.
Supporting this exceptional project offers companies the opportunity to associate their image with an artistic journey combining visibility, commitment and influence:
A strong lever for image, influence and business opportunities;A prestigious partnership with an orchestra of excellence;A meaningful commitment in support of artistic creation and cultural cooperation;Enhanced visibility to develop business relationships;Attractive tax benefits and exclusive partner privileges.
Join the adventure and become a partner of the Orchestre national d'Île-de-France tour in Japan.
Information and contact: audrey.chauvelot@orchestre-ile.com
----

title: End-of-Year Dinner of the Kansai Desk at Heian Jingu
description: What better setting than the stunning Heian Jingu to celebrate the end of the year and bring together the members of the Kansai office of the CCIFJ?

blocks.text: Kansai Event report

blocks.section: End-of-Year Dinner of the Kansai Desk at Heian Jingu
blocks.text: End-of-Year Dinner of the Kansai Desk at Heian Jingu

blocks.section: End-of-Year Dinner of the Kansai Desk at Heian Jingu
blocks.text: What better setting than the stunning Heian Jingu to celebrate the end of the year and bring together the members of the Kansai office of the CCIFJ?

blocks.section: End-of-Year Dinner of the Kansai Desk at Heian Jingu
blocks.text: On the evening of Thursday, December 5th, we shared a gourmet dinner in the heart of Kyoto, in the banquet hall adjacent to the private gardens of the famous Heian Jingu temple.

blocks.section: End-of-Year Dinner of the Kansai Desk at Heian Jingu
blocks.text: A special moment to close a year full of events for the Chamber, with a refined menu crafted by Chef Ishii Shu , blending Japanese and French cuisine.

blocks.section: End-of-Year Dinner of the Kansai Desk at Heian Jingu
blocks.text: During the meal, our guests enjoyed a beautiful view of the Heian Jingu gardens, with the vibrant colors of the autumn momiji. They savored dishes such as sushis with Pacific saury, dengaku, and perfectly roasted Wagyu steak, among others.

blocks.section: End-of-Year Dinner of the Kansai Desk at Heian Jingu
blocks.text: Our partner, Shimizu Seisaburo Shoten , was also highlighted during a raffle, where some of their finest bottles of Japanese sake were given as prizes.

blocks.section: End-of-Year Dinner of the Kansai Desk at Heian Jingu
blocks.text: We would like to warmly thank Sandrine Mouchet , Consul General of France, as well as Benoit Rulleau , Board Member of the CCIFJ, and Seiichiro Hayashi , Ambassador of the Chamber in Kansai, for their presence at this event.

blocks.section: End-of-Year Dinner of the Kansai Desk at Heian Jingu
blocks.text: We were also honored to welcome Christophe Lemaire , renowned French jockey and founder of CL by C. Lemaire (CL by C.ルメール), to this event.

blocks.section: End-of-Year Dinner of the Kansai Desk at Heian Jingu
blocks.text: Finally, a big thank you to the team at our partner VMG , responsible for managing the Heian Jingu Event Hall , for their exceptional hospitality, without which this event would not have been possible.

blocks.section: End-of-Year Dinner of the Kansai Desk at Heian Jingu
blocks.text: The Kansai office of the Chamber wishes you all a wonderful holiday season and looks forward to seeing you in 2025 at our upcoming events!

blocks.text: With races in USA, Germany, Italy, Wales and Japan, Grinduro is well known globally among gravel cycling enthusiasts as an event which combines a challenging endurance gravel ride with a weekend long festival featuring great food, art, and high-quality music.

title: Joint Chamber Event - EU Cocktail 2024 - Event Recap
description:
Building on the tremendous success of last year’s event, the European Cocktail 2024 is set to be an exceptional evening. The European Cocktail has firmly established itself as the must-attend event of the year, offering unparalleled opportunities for networking and collaboration. We look forward to welcoming you to another memorable evening in 2024!

title: EU-Japan Sustainable Solutions Matchmaking at Kawasaki Eco-Tech Fair 2024
description:
The EU-Japan Centre for Industrial Cooperation, Kawasaki City and UNIDO ITPO Tokyo are co-organising an exclusive matchmaking event at the Kawasaki International Eco-Tech Fair from 13 to 15 November 2024. 
EU participants will be able to meet Japanese companies and representatives from the Philippines (Cebu) and Cambodia to discuss EU-Japan joint projects in the Philippines and Cambodia.
A call for applications is open for EU companies and their subsidiaries in Japan and Southeast Asia developing sustainable solutions related to energy, the circular economy, waste and resource management or doing consulting and project management in Southeast Asia.
The deadline for applications is 8 October 2024 at midnight (Tokyo time)

title: European industry in Japan heavily affected by the (re-)entry ban on non-Japanese citizens
description:
The European Business Council in Japan (EBC), in cooperation with the various national European Chambers in Japan, has carried out a survey to understand the current situation of European companies in Japan.
The result is clear. According to the answers, 85% of European companies are negatively affected by the ban. Mainly affected is the ability to successfully carry out new or existing projects due to management and/or specialists not being able to (re-)enter Japan. 44% of responders expect a loss in revenue solely due to the (re-)entry ban.
Furthermore, the management of European subsidiaries in Japan cannot travel to the headquarters in Europe causing disruptions to the governance of the companies. Moreover, according to the survey, companies are suffering as leadership and expert positions cannot be filled as non-Japanese personnel cannot enter Japan despite having the proper visas.
In addition, 65% of companies that use Japan as a regional headquarter express problems with management not being able to visit subsidiaries in other countries, eg. South Korea, Taiwan and the Philippines. Unfortunately, the current situation is in direct opposition to Japan’s wish for more foreign companies to use Japan as their regional hub.
Michael Mroczek, the EBC President, said at a press conference that despite the good start of the EU-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement, we are now at risk of losing the momentum due to the (re-)entry ban.
Further, the EBC has been approached by various European companies concerned that the current travel restrictions are unfairly interfering in proper management of European investments in Japan. This is of concern as under various treaties, such as the Free Trade Agreement between Japan and Switzerland and the Energy Charter Treaty, claims may be filed directly against the Government of Japan when fair and equitable treatment is denied to foreign investors.
Furthermore, the (re-)entry ban of permanent and long-term residents may be in breach Article 12 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, which clearly states that “[n]o one shall be arbitrarily deprived of the right to enter his own country.”
The EBC again reiterates its requests for Japan to extend the same treatment to non-Japanese residents as is offered to Japanese nationals. This means that Europeans residents, together with other nationals, shall be able to leave and come back to Japan. This is possible in all other G7 countries, except for Japan.
► Survey on the impact of the (re-)entry ban to Japan on European businesses (detail)

blocks.text: On June 26, 2026 , CCI France Japon had the pleasure of welcoming 110 participants to L’Espace@CCIFJ for an exceptional evening featuring Philippe TROUSSIER , former head coach of the Japan national football team, and Florent DABADIE , presenter, journalist, and sports commentator.

blocks.section: Event Report – Soirée BONJOUR FRANCE with Philippe Troussier x Florent Dabadie, featuring the cuisine of Dominique Corby
blocks.text: Organized as part of the BONJOUR FRANCE initiative, the event offered participants a unique opportunity to learn more about Philippe TROUSSIER's career and expertise. The soirée opened with welcoming remarks by Bernard DELMAS , Administrator of CCI France Japon, while Mayu HANDA , Director of BONJOUR FRANCE, served as MC throughout the event.

blocks.section: Event Report – Soirée BONJOUR FRANCE with Philippe Troussier x Florent Dabadie, featuring the cuisine of Dominique Corby
blocks.text: Moderated by Florent DABADIE, the Talk-Show covered a wide range of topics, including the FIFA World Cup, analyses of the Japan–Sweden and Japan–Brazil matches, as well as memorable anecdotes from Philippe TROUSSIER's coaching career. The discussion also explored his wine project, "FLAT3", before concluding with an interactive Q&A session that gave participants the opportunity to engage directly with the speakers.

blocks.section: Event Report – Soirée BONJOUR FRANCE with Philippe Troussier x Florent Dabadie, featuring the cuisine of Dominique Corby
blocks.text: Following the Talk-Show, guests enjoyed a cocktail reception specially created for the occasion by Chef Dominique CORBY. The reception provided a warm and convivial setting for further discussions while guests enjoyed "FLAT3" wine, DASSAI sake, Maison Kayser bread, and Oliviers&Co olive oil.

blocks.section: Event Report – Soirée BONJOUR FRANCE with Philippe Troussier x Florent Dabadie, featuring the cuisine of Dominique Corby
blocks.text: CCI France Japon and BONJOUR FRANCE would like to extend their sincere thanks to Philippe TROUSSIER, Florent DABADIE, Chef Dominique CORBY, our sponsors, and all participants for contributing to the success of this memorable soirée.

title: Event recap: At the heart of French–Japanese cooperation in Gunma
description: On December 3rd, the CCIFJ Gunma Desk had the pleasure of hosting a new event focused on French–Japanese cooperation.

blocks.text: Event report

blocks.section: Event recap: At the heart of French–Japanese cooperation in Gunma
blocks.text: Event recap: At the heart of French–Japanese cooperation in Gunma

blocks.section: Event recap: At the heart of French–Japanese cooperation in Gunma
blocks.text: On December 3rd, the CCIFJ Gunma Desk had the pleasure of hosting a new event focused on French–Japanese cooperation.

blocks.section: Event recap: At the heart of French–Japanese cooperation in Gunma
blocks.text: On Wednesday, December 3rd, the Gunma Desk of the CCI France-Japan (CCIFJ) had the pleasure of hosting a new event dedicated to strengthening Franco-Japanese cooperation, bringing together around twenty participants.

blocks.section: Event recap: At the heart of French–Japanese cooperation in Gunma
blocks.text: The event, “Envisioning Gunma’s Future through Franco-Japanese Economic Cooperations” took place in Netsugen , on the 32nd floor of the Gunma Prefectural Office in Maebashi.

blocks.section: Event recap: At the heart of French–Japanese cooperation in Gunma
blocks.text: The first part of the event featured a seminar led by the Fondation France-Japon (FFJ), an academic foundation affiliated with EHESS (School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences) and conducting research on France and Japan in the field of social sciences. Sébastien Lechevalier , President of the FFJ, introduced several development perspectives for Gunma based on the foundation’s research, focusing on three key themes: population aging, innovation, and regional development.

blocks.section: Event recap: At the heart of French–Japanese cooperation in Gunma
blocks.text: His presentation was followed by remarks from Bernard Delmas , Honorary Chairman of the CCIFJ and co-chair of the “FFJ Circle”. Drawing on his experience at Michelin in both Auvergne and Gunma, he provided insightful comparisons between the two regions and highlighted their similarities. He also introduced a concrete example of Franco-Japanese cooperation: the Michelin Cities International Network , to which Clermont-Ferrand and Maebashi both belong.

blocks.section: Event recap: At the heart of French–Japanese cooperation in Gunma
blocks.text: Mayuko Yamamoto , in charge of international relations at the FFJ, then shared her perspective as a Japanese researcher in France. She emphasized that regional areas such as Gunma often serve as fertile ground for innovation, with peripheral territories offering unique conditions for new initiatives.

blocks.section: Event recap: At the heart of French–Japanese cooperation in Gunma
blocks.text: To conclude, the speakers highlighted how international cooperation, particularly Franco-Japanese collaboration, can offer valuable opportunities for Gunma’s future. Beyond existing initiatives such as those led by the CCIFJ or the Franco-Japanese Association of Gunma , further potential lies in partnerships with French regions, cities, and universities.

blocks.section: Event recap: At the heart of French–Japanese cooperation in Gunma
blocks.text: In the second half of the event, participants enjoyed a convivial networking session over French wine and specialties.

blocks.section: Event recap: At the heart of French–Japanese cooperation in Gunma
blocks.text: We would like to express our sincere gratitude to the Gunma Prefectural Government for its support.

blocks.section: Event recap: At the heart of French–Japanese cooperation in Gunma
blocks.text: We look forward to welcoming you again soon for upcoming events in Gunma!

title: Event recap : Discovering “BVLGARI KALEIDOS”
description:
On Tuesday, 14 October, we had the pleasure to co-organize a private viewing of the exhibition “BVLGARI KALEIDOS: Colors, Cultures and Crafts” at The National Art Center, Tokyo.
We extend our heartfelt thanks to Mr Denis Coan, managing director of Bvlgari Japan, for kindly guiding us through this magnificent exhibition. Presented in Japan for the first time in ten years and marking Bvlgari’s largest exhibition in the country, BVLGARI KALEIDOS offers an inspiring exploration of nearly 350 masterpieces — from iconic jewellery to contemporary art.
The exhibition is open to the public until December 15, 2025, offering visitors a rare opportunity to experience the timeless elegance and creative spirit of Bvlgari.

title: Event Recap: European Joint Chamber Networking Party 2026.
description:
Held on October 19, the European Joint Chamber Networking Party 2026 brought together more than 300 guests for an exceptional night. Gathering members of the European and Japanese business communities, it was a great opportunity to make new connections and exchange ideas with professionals from different industries. 

A big thank you to our host, The Mandarin Oriental, Tokyo (マンダリン   オリエンタル 東京), for welcoming us in such a wonderful setting. 

We would also like to extend our warmest thanks to the 17 chambers that took part in this event:
Austrian Business Council (ABC)
Belgian-Luxembourg Chamber of Commerce in Japan (BLCCJ)
BCCJ – The British Chamber of Commerce in Japan
Danish Chamber of Commerce in Japan (DCCJ)
Finnish Chamber of Commerce in Japan (FCCJ)
European Business Council in Japan (EBC)
German Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (AHK Japan)
Greek Chamber of Commerce in Japan
Icelandic Chamber of Commerce in Japan (ISCCJ)
IJCC – Ireland Japan Chamber of Commerce
Italian Chamber of Commerce in Japan
Netherlands Chamber of Commerce in Japan (NCCJ)
Norwegian Chamber of Commerce in Japan (NCCJ)
Spanish Chamber of Commerce in Japan (SpCCJ)
Swedish Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan
Swiss Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (SCCJ)
Tokyo and Japan Chamber of Commerce and Industry

We are also grateful to Baron Philippe de Rothschild for their generous support and for accompanying the evening with their exceptional wines, which added a touch of elegance and conviviality to the night.

Because of the commitment of all our partners and guests, the bonds between Europe and Japan are highlighted during this joint event. We look forward to continuing to build bridges between our business communities, and to welcoming you again at the next edition!

Many thanks to : Baron Philippe de Rothschild, LIFE.14, Mandarin Oriental Tokyo マンダリン   オリエンタル 東京.

title: Event recap - Exclusive networking event with French companies from MEDEF International, Business France and French Tech
description:
On March 31, 2026, the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan had the pleasure of hosting a special networking event at L’Espace with 120 participants, in partnership with MEDEF International, Business France and La French Tech.
As part of the French Presidential visit to Japan, this event gathered a high-level delegation, highlighting the strong momentum of France-Japan economic relations.
 Opening remarks were delivered by:
Mr Jérome Chouchan (President of CCIFJ)Mr Frédéric Sanchez (Chairman of MEDEF International)Mr Louis Margueritte (Chief Executive Officer of Business France)Ms Julie Huguet (Director of Mission French Tech)Mr Dominique Restino (President of CCI Paris Ile de France)Mr Patrick Martin (Chairman of MEDEF)
We were also honored by the presence of Mr. Roland Lescure, Minister for the Economy, Finance and Industrial and Energy Sovereignty.
High level Executives have been also attended such as Mr. Bernard Fontana, Chairman of EDF, Mr. Jérôme Stubler, CEO of Equans and Mr. Christophe Maquet, Board Member of Veolia.
This event offered high-quality exchanges and valuable networking opportunities, fostering new connections and future collaborations between French and Japanese business communities.
Thank you to all participants for your presence and engagement.
Let’s continue to strengthen the France-Japan business momentum.

Photos : Life.14

title: FBA 2024/Shinnenkai Networking
description:
The CCI France Japon held the 13th edition of its French Business Award on Thursday, January 25th, 2024 at Grand Hyatt Tokyo.
This year, 20 companies of various industries and sectors were in competition for 6 awards, which showcase and reward the efforts and successes of companies in Japan.
The CCI France Japon is pleased to announce the results of this competition. The 2024 laureates are:
 	Kansai Airports (“Company of the Year” Award), 	Acrelec Japan (“Product or Service of the Year” Award), 	Emulsion Flow Technologies Ltd. (“French Tech Tokyo” Award),  	Asuene (“Sustainability Award”),  	Telmont  (“Special Jury Award”) 	Valeo Japan Co., Ltd. ("Innovation Award") 
The jury was composed of the Chairman of the CCI France Japon, and French and Japanese business leaders.
They selected among the nominees the most dynamic, innovative, and performing companies with grounded success in the Japanese market.
All 20 companies were a testimony of the diversity, strength, and polyvalence of French and Japanese businesses.
Highly diverse industries were showcased this year.

title: Event recap: Leadership lessons with Hogan Assessments
description: The CCIFJ welcomed Hogan Assessments on October 29, 2025, for an exploration of leadership styles between France and Japan.

blocks.text: Event report • The Chamber

blocks.section: Event recap: Leadership lessons with Hogan Assessments
blocks.text: Event recap: Leadership lessons with Hogan Assessments

blocks.section: Event recap: Leadership lessons with Hogan Assessments
blocks.text: The CCIFJ welcomed Hogan Assessments on October 29, 2025, for an exploration of leadership styles between France and Japan.

blocks.section: Event recap: Leadership lessons with Hogan Assessments
blocks.text: On October 29, 2025 , at the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCIFJ) , Hogan Assessments led an insightful presentation in Tokyo on the theme:

blocks.section: Event recap: Leadership lessons with Hogan Assessments
blocks.text: “Bridging Perspectives: Leadership Lessons Between France and Japan” , featuring Dr. Ryne Sherman , Chief Science Officer.

blocks.section: Event recap: Leadership lessons with Hogan Assessments
blocks.text: During the event, Hogan shared key insights from its extensive database, comparing the personalities and leadership styles of Japanese and French executives. While these two cultures approach leadership differently, the results revealed surprising points of convergence in values, decision-making, and teamwork.

blocks.section: Event recap: Leadership lessons with Hogan Assessments
blocks.text: The session offered to 40 professionals; HR, business leaders, and international decision-makers a fresh, data-driven perspective on the essentials of effective cross-cultural leadership.

blocks.section: Event recap: Leadership lessons with Hogan Assessments
blocks.text: Rather than a formal lecture, the goal was to stimulate reflection and dialogue . Following the presentation, participants continued the conversation during a networking cocktail .

blocks.section: Event recap: Leadership lessons with Hogan Assessments
blocks.text: Anne-Marie Paiement , Regional Manager at Hogan Assessments:

blocks.section: Event recap: Leadership lessons with Hogan Assessments
blocks.text: “We were delighted to collaborate with the CCI France Japan for this event dedicated to intercultural leadership. This gathering fostered rich and constructive exchanges among professionals from diverse backgrounds, highlighting the importance of understanding and valuing different managerial approaches in a globalized world.”

blocks.section: Event recap: Leadership lessons with Hogan Assessments
blocks.text: About Hogan Assessments

blocks.section: Event recap: Leadership lessons with Hogan Assessments
blocks.text: A pioneer and global leader in applied personality science for the business world, Hogan Assessments helps organizations select the right talent, develop employees, build effective leaders, and achieve measurable results in 56 countries and 47 languages.

blocks.section: Event recap: Leadership lessons with Hogan Assessments
blocks.text: With over 40 years of scientifically validated research , Hogan was the first company to measure personality in a professional context and remains a worldwide reference today.

blocks.section: Event recap: Leadership lessons with Hogan Assessments
blocks.text: Dr. Ryne Sherman , as Chief Science Officer at Hogan Assessments, oversees the company’s key data science activities, including talent analytics, product innovation, business intelligence, and research archive management . A recognized expert in personality psychology, workplace performance, and modern assessment methods (including AI-based tools), he has taught psychology at Texas Tech University and Florida Atlantic University , where he received numerous honors. Author of over 50 scientific publications, he also co-hosts the podcast Science of Personality and regularly speaks on personality, leadership, and professional assessment topics. For more information : https://www.hoganassessments.com/

blocks.section: Event recap: Leadership lessons with Hogan Assessments
blocks.text: Acknowledgements :

blocks.section: Event recap: Leadership lessons with Hogan Assessments
blocks.text: A heartfelt thank you to Hogan Assessments and Anne-Marie Paiement for making this event possible, as well as to Krista Pederson and Ryne Sherman for their inspiring presentations.

blocks.section: Event recap: Leadership lessons with Hogan Assessments
blocks.text: Finally, warm thanks to everyone who joined us. We look forward to welcoming you to future CCIFJ events to continue these valuable and enriching exchanges of ideas.

title: Event recap : Wagashi workshop
description: On Sunday, July 13th, the Chubu Desk of the CCIFJ had the pleasure of welcoming around ten participants to attend a demonstration by Mr. Nobuharu Okamoto, master wagashi artisan from Kotoyo confectionery house.

blocks.text: Chubu Events

blocks.section: Event recap : Wagashi workshop
blocks.text: Event recap : Wagashi workshop

blocks.section: Event recap : Wagashi workshop
blocks.text: On Sunday, July 13th, the Chubu Desk of the CCIFJ had the pleasure of welcoming around ten participants to attend a demonstration by Mr. Nobuharu Okamoto, master wagashi artisan from Kotoyo confectionery house.

blocks.section: Event recap : Wagashi workshop
blocks.text: Globally recognized for his expertise, Mr. Okamoto regularly travels the world to share the delicate art of wagashi, a tradition that has been passed down in his family for over 100 years.

blocks.section: Event recap : Wagashi workshop
blocks.text: On this exclusive small-scale event, around ten participants including several long-time members of the French community in Nagoya, as well as Japanese guests curious to discover this traditional practice gathered in a warm and friendly atmosphere.

blocks.section: Event recap : Wagashi workshop
blocks.text: After a live demonstration with commentary on several of his confectionery techniques, Mr. Okamoto surprised the participants by crafting a wagashi blindfolded, a striking display of the precision and mastery he has developed over the years.

blocks.section: Event recap : Wagashi workshop
blocks.text: This was followed by a hands-on workshop, during which each participant had the opportunity to try their hand at making wagashi, guided step by step by the master.

blocks.section: Event recap : Wagashi workshop
blocks.text: The workshop concluded on a sweet note, with a tasting of the pastries created by the participants with a serving of matcha tea, in an warm and lively atmosphere.

blocks.section: Event recap : Wagashi workshop
blocks.text: The CCIFJ Nagoya extends its sincere thanks to Mr. Okamoto for his generosity and dedication, as well as to all participants for their presence and enthusiasm.

blocks.section: Event recap : Wagashi workshop
blocks.text: We also wish to thank Julie Baud (@tonarinojuri), a tour guide based in Nagoya and actively involved in promoting traditional Japanese arts, for honoring us with her presence on this occasion.

blocks.section: Event recap : Wagashi workshop
blocks.text: We look forward to seeing you at our upcoming events in Nagoya!

title: Event Recap | What Will Companies Value in the AI Era? Redefining Women's Empowerment, Leadership, and Ways of Working
description:
On July 13th, the CCI France Japon, Women in Business Committee hosted an engaging panel discussion on one of the most timely questions facing the business world today: how AI is reshaping the way organisations define value, leadership, and career development — and what this means for women in business.
Moderated by Aiko Katoh, Founder and CEO of coichigo KK, the panel featured Kuniko Milhous (Dassault Systèmes), Aiko Shimizu (Microsoft), and Rebecca Takada (Outfoxr) for a rich and thought-provoking exchange covering the opportunities and challenges the AI era presents. The session was followed by a networking cocktail, allowing participants to continue the conversation in a convivial setting.
We extend our sincere thanks to all panelists for the quality of their contributions, and look forward to welcoming you at our next Women in Business Committee event.
