blocks.section: Baccarat's Master-Class at the Fukuoka Chamber of Commerce: Branding of a Centuries Old Luxury Brand
blocks.text: Fukuoka's CCI hosted yesterday Mr. Yoshikazu Yann GAHIER's conference on Baccarat Pacific's branding strategies, co-organized by the CCIFJ.

blocks.section: Baccarat's Master-Class at the Fukuoka Chamber of Commerce: Branding of a Centuries Old Luxury Brand
blocks.text: Yesterday, July 26, 2023 in Fukuoka, it was a little over 70 participants who had the opportunity to attend the presentation of a centuries-old French company: Baccarat.

blocks.section: Baccarat's Master-Class at the Fukuoka Chamber of Commerce: Branding of a Centuries Old Luxury Brand
blocks.text: The event started with a Japanese presentation of the CCIFJ's activities by the West Japan area manager. Then Mr. Yoshikazu Yann Gahier, President of Baccarat Pacific, who is also a member of the Chamber's Board of Administrators, opened his speech with a historical retrospective of the company. An attentive audience learned a lot about the history of the "cristal of kings", which is synonym of luxury and elegance since 1764. We also learned that the company accounts for 15 Meilleurs Ouvriers de France (MOF, Best Craftsmen of France, a high distinction) among its qualified makers.

blocks.section: Baccarat's Master-Class at the Fukuoka Chamber of Commerce: Branding of a Centuries Old Luxury Brand
blocks.text: The speech began with a few words in French to surprise the Japanese attendees and get their attention. Then, Mr. Gahier did a brilliant Japanese presentation of the strategies developed by Baccarat over the past 40 years in the country to bring the brand from a status of near unawareness to one of the main references of French luxury.

blocks.section: Baccarat's Master-Class at the Fukuoka Chamber of Commerce: Branding of a Centuries Old Luxury Brand
blocks.text: Japanese culture gives a prominent role to the exchange of gifts, and that was an obvious angle that Baccarat worked hard, but it is also thanks to many innovative ideas that the company could think out of the box and stand out, for instance by developing a counter-intuitive "casual baccarat" image, items that you can drink from everyday at home. Beyond the signature crystal glass, other collections have been put in the spotlight, like chandeliers and ornaments. Some products inspired by mangas are also designed for younger people, such as « Doraemon » ornament or « Jojo’s bizarre Adventure » engraved pieces. This conference was the occasion for Yann Gahier to show a dynamic company full of ideas, which demonstrated its agility during the Covid-19 epidemic by adapting its marketing strategy to the new conditions of everyday life.

blocks.section: Baccarat's Master-Class at the Fukuoka Chamber of Commerce: Branding of a Centuries Old Luxury Brand
blocks.text: Finally, each participant went home with two tickets for a free drink at one of the three B bars that can be found in Tokyo or Osaka. There, high-end cocktails can be ordered, enhancing the company's high standards. Those bars are particularly convenient to discover Baccarat's many models of glasses and ornamental products.

blocks.section: Baccarat's Master-Class at the Fukuoka Chamber of Commerce: Branding of a Centuries Old Luxury Brand
blocks.text: The Q&A session following the conference also allowed the participants to share opinions with Mr. Gahier, ask burning questions about the subject and get insights about personal ideas. For those who did not dare or did not have time to talk in public, a short networking moment concluded the event, allowing everyone to raise a few last issues directly with the speaker. That alone showed how sincere the interest from the audience was. The event finally ended with a private dinner shared with the Fukuoka CCI's delegation going to France at the end of August this year on a business trip.

title: Event Report: "From Tokyo to the World; Birth of a New J-Beauty Brand"
description:
We are delighted to share the highlights of our recent event, "From Tokyo to the World; Birth of a New J-Beauty Brand," which took place on May 17th. The event featured an insightful session with the co-founders of DAMDAM, Giselle Go and Philippe Terrien, as they shared their inspiring journey of building a global J-beauty brand.
During the event, attendees had the opportunity to learn about DAMDAM's remarkable progression from concept to a successful launch. Giselle and Philippe shared their creative process, shedding light on the challenges they encountered and overcame along the way. The audience gained valuable insights into the strategies employed by DAMDAM to establish their unique position in the competitive beauty industry.
One of the key highlights of the event was the discussion on DAMDAM's effective use of digital tools. Giselle and Philippe shared their innovative digital marketing strategies and how they harnessed technology to propel their brand forward. Attendees were inspired by the power of digital platforms in reaching a global audience and enhancing brand visibility.
Moreover, DAMDAM's co-founders provided valuable insights into their international expansion efforts. They shared their experiences of entering new markets beyond Tokyo, adapting their products to suit diverse consumer preferences, and building strong relationships with international partners. Their journey from Tokyo to the world served as an inspiration to all aspiring entrepreneurs in the beauty industry.
We would like to express our gratitude to Giselle Go and Philippe Terrien for their engaging session, as well as to all the attendees who made the event a success. Their presence and participation contributed to an enriching and insightful discussion.
Stay tuned for more upcoming events as we continue to bring you inspiring stories and valuable industry insights.

title: Event report: Gala Fukuoka 2024
description:
The Gala Party Fukuoka 2024 was held at Solaria Nishitetsu Hotel Fukuoka on Wednesday, 12 June 2024.
Gala Party Fukuoka is held annually under the support of Fukuoka's sister city, Bordeaux.
This year, Michelin-starred chef Mathieu Martin came to Japan to supervise a special one-night-only dinner. The 220 people in attendance enjoyed the chef's full-course meal, while savouring the excellent wines specially chosen by the Bordeaux Wine Commission (CIVB).
Dinner was followed by a special stage performance by ballet dancers from Ballet Blanc Art and Dan Emoto from the Tokyo Ballet, and concluded by a grand raffle with a collection of magnificent prizes. 
We would like to thank the following partners for their great cooperation in organizing the event・Bordeaux city ・Le Conseil Interprofessionnel du Vin de Bordeaux (CIVB)・Clarins

title: Event Report
description:
Gontran Cherrier, the fourth-generation baker, recently visited Japan, where he shared his culinary expertise. Graduating from the prestigious Ferrandi Culinary School and Les Grands Moulin de Paris as a Master Baker, Gontran honed his skills at esteemed establishments like the three Michelin-starred restaurant L’Arpège with Alain Passard and Lucas Carton with Alain Senderens.
During his visit, Gontran showcased his mastery as a pastry chef, chocolate maker, and, above all, a master baker. His travels have influenced his creations, leading him to establish training programs and production centers in Russia and Romania.
Gontran Cherrier's repertoire in Japan included a wide range of classic French bakery delights, from Viennoiserie (Danish pastries) to artisan bread, pastries, sandwiches, and a variety of beverages.
His visit to Japan provided a unique opportunity for culinary enthusiasts to experience his creations firsthand and learn from his rich culinary journey.

blocks.text: On April 4th, a limited number of 400 guests — including participants, invitees, sponsors, partners, members of the press, and VIPs — gathered at the Residence of the French Ambassador to Japan for the Opening Ceremony celebrating the 10th Anniversary of BONJOUR FRANCE 2025.

blocks.section: Event report of the Opening Ceremony – Opening Ceremony of BONJOUR FRANCE 2025’s 10th Anniversary
blocks.text: The ceremony began in grand fashion with the arrival of several distinguished guests:

blocks.section: Event report of the Opening Ceremony – Opening Ceremony of BONJOUR FRANCE 2025’s 10th Anniversary
blocks.text: - Ms. Christel TAKIGAWA, TV presenter, Knight of the Order of Arts and Letters and the National Order of Merit for her contributions to Franco-Japanese relations.

blocks.section: Event report of the Opening Ceremony – Opening Ceremony of BONJOUR FRANCE 2025’s 10th Anniversary
blocks.text: - Ms. Saila KUNIKIDA, a Japanese-Italian creative director, model, and executive producer with a multicultural background between Paris, Tokyo, and Berlin.

blocks.section: Event report of the Opening Ceremony – Opening Ceremony of BONJOUR FRANCE 2025’s 10th Anniversary
blocks.text: - Mr. Bebechan, a well-known YouTuber in Japan, whose channel "Bebechan – Français au Japon" has over 783k subscribers.

blocks.section: Event report of the Opening Ceremony – Opening Ceremony of BONJOUR FRANCE 2025’s 10th Anniversary
blocks.text: - Mr. Florent DABADIE, interpreter and sports news presenter.

blocks.section: Event report of the Opening Ceremony – Opening Ceremony of BONJOUR FRANCE 2025’s 10th Anniversary
blocks.text: - Mr. Yoshihiro HAMAGUCHI, General Merchandise Manager at AEON RETAIL Co., Ltd.

blocks.section: Event report of the Opening Ceremony – Opening Ceremony of BONJOUR FRANCE 2025’s 10th Anniversary
blocks.text: They were joined by H.E. Mr. Philippe SETTON, French Ambassador in Japan, and Mr. Jérôme CHOUCHAN, President of the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCI France Japon), who each delivered a speech before proceeding with a symbolic ribbon-cutting to mark BONJOUR FRANCE’s 10th anniversary.

blocks.section: Event report of the Opening Ceremony – Opening Ceremony of BONJOUR FRANCE 2025’s 10th Anniversary
blocks.text: Following this solemn moment, the choir “Les Alouettes” gave a singing performance. The stage of the French Ambassador’s Residence then welcomed Mr. Philippe TROUSSIER, former football coach and former manager of the Japanese national team during the 2002 FIFA World Cup.

blocks.text: Next, the Confrérie du Sabre d’Or performed a champagne sabering ceremony, followed by a toast led by Mr. Bernard Delmas, board member of the CCI France Japon. blocks.text: Throughout the evening, guests enjoyed various aspects of French culture — from gastronomy to everyday lifestyle — including a special car exhibition by Nissan Motor Corporation. Musical performances by Mr. Philippe MARCHAND, pianist and singer, accompanied by Ms. Yukari, also graced this exceptional evening.

description: Throwback to the BONJOUR FRANCE Opening Ceremony held on May 17th, 2024.

blocks.text: Event report

blocks.section: Event Report: Opening Ceremony – Soirée BONJOUR FRANCE 2024
blocks.text: Event Report: Opening Ceremony – Soirée BONJOUR FRANCE 2024

blocks.section: Event Report: Opening Ceremony – Soirée BONJOUR FRANCE 2024
blocks.text: Throwback to the BONJOUR FRANCE Opening Ceremony held on May 17th, 2024.

blocks.section: Event Report: Opening Ceremony – Soirée BONJOUR FRANCE 2024
blocks.text: On May 17 th , 2024, the BONJOUR FRANCE Opening Ceremony, which took place at the French Ambassador’s Residence in Japan, gathered 630 people, participants, guests, sponsors, partners and CCIFJ staff members alike.

blocks.section: Event Report: Opening Ceremony – Soirée BONJOUR FRANCE 2024
blocks.text: The Ceremony started with the arrival of esteemed guests:

blocks.section: Event Report: Opening Ceremony – Soirée BONJOUR FRANCE 2024
blocks.text: Mrs. TAKIGAWA Christel, freelance announcer, who was awarded the title of knight of the Ordre des Arts et des Lettres and the Ordre national du Mérite by the French government for her contribution to the long-lasting relationship between France and Japan.

blocks.section: Event Report: Opening Ceremony – Soirée BONJOUR FRANCE 2024
blocks.text: Cocomi, flutist and model, whose 2 nd album titled “Mélancolie” compiles reinterpretations of famous classical French artists.

blocks.section: Event Report: Opening Ceremony – Soirée BONJOUR FRANCE 2024
blocks.text: Ms. Klara BLANC, French influencer and model in Japan, who promotes the Parisian lifestyle to her hundreds of thousands of followers.

blocks.section: Event Report: Opening Ceremony – Soirée BONJOUR FRANCE 2024
blocks.text: Ms Clara BODIN, French model, actress, entrepreneur and MC, who has contributed to the success of BONJOUR FRANCE since 2015.

blocks.section: Event Report: Opening Ceremony – Soirée BONJOUR FRANCE 2024
blocks.text: And Mr. KASHITANI Ichiro, President of Toyota Tsusho and 3 rd vice president of the CCI France Japon.

blocks.section: Event Report: Opening Ceremony – Soirée BONJOUR FRANCE 2024
blocks.text: Our guests joined His Excellency Philippe SETTON, Ambassador of France to Japan, and Mr. Jérôme CHOUCHAN, President of the CCI France Japon. After speeches by Mr. SETTON and Mr. CHOUCHAN, the 2024 BONJOUR FRANCE season was officially inaugurated through a traditional ribbon cutting ceremony, followed by a flute performance by Cocomi.

blocks.section: Event Report: Opening Ceremony – Soirée BONJOUR FRANCE 2024
blocks.text: The Confrérie du Sabre d’Or performed a champagne sabrage before its ambassador Mr. Bernard ANQUETIL, made a speech and gathered everyone present to raise a toast to the evening. The Ceremony ended with a speech by Mr. KOHARI Yukitaka, director of the Bernard Buffet museum, after which the cocktail party started.

blocks.section: Event Report: Opening Ceremony – Soirée BONJOUR FRANCE 2024
blocks.text: Guests were able to enjoy several sides of the French culture throughout the evening, from gastronomy to lifestyle, thanks to remarkable exhibitions such as the paintings of the Bernard Buffet Museum or the Toyota Motor Corporation sportscars. Several happenings gave the evening an enjoyable rhythm: the cooking performances by chef Bernard ANQUETIL, and the musical performances of singer pianist Philippe MARCHAND and pianist NINOMIYA Yukiko. The opening ceremony ended with a wonderful prize raffle in collaboration with our sponsors.

blocks.section: Event Report: Opening Ceremony – Soirée BONJOUR FRANCE 2024
blocks.text: This evening was a resounding success to our guests and our collaborators, and hints towards a very eventful year for BONJOUR FRANCE. We would like to give our special thanks to the French Ambassy for their patronage. Special thanks to Toyota Motor Corporation, as well as all of our sponsors and partners, for their precious collaboration.

title: Exchange Rate Survey Report
description:
Amidst the current economic situation, where the Japanese Yen is steadily depreciating, the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCIFJ) conducted a survey with 69 of its members. The survey aimed to understand how this currency decline directly affects their businesses.
The survey covered various questions about the general economic impact and individual business experiences. It highlighted how the weakening yen is affecting member companies differently. Participants also shared their views on where they believe the yen's exchange rate might head in the near future, along with testimonies on reasons for the yen's ongoing depreciation.
These findings provide a clearer picture of how businesses are managing currency fluctuations and offer insights into potential developments in the currency markets.  Explore the detailed report

blocks.section: Exclusive Jewelry Exhibition by Shanu Agarwal
blocks.text: This jewelry exhibition will feature Shanu’s latest designs, showcasing a range of exclusive, handcrafted pieces that embody her artistic vision. Known for her perfectionism, Shanu personally selects the finest gemstones for each creation and dedicates hours to perfecting every detail, ensuring that her jewelry radiates elegance, luxury, and empowerment.

blocks.section: Exclusive Jewelry Exhibition by Shanu Agarwal
blocks.text: Why Attend?

blocks.section: Exclusive Jewelry Exhibition by Shanu Agarwal
blocks.text: This exclusive event offers a chance to meet Shanu Agarwal in person, hear about her journey as a designer, and experience firsthand the meticulous craftsmanship that goes into each piece. Attendees will also gain insight into the creative process behind her jewelry and learn how Shanu transforms raw gemstones into wearable art.

blocks.section: Exclusive Jewelry Exhibition by Shanu Agarwal
blocks.text: We look forward to welcoming you to this exclusive event!

blocks.section: Exclusive Jewelry Exhibition by Shanu Agarwal
blocks.text: About Shanu Agarwal:

blocks.section: Exclusive Jewelry Exhibition by Shanu Agarwal
blocks.text: Born and raised in Mumbai, India, Shanu Agarwal has been passionate about creative design from a young age. After completing her fashion design studies at a prestigious university in Mumbai, Shanu began designing for her father’s boutique. This early experience allowed her to see her designs come to life as magnificent jewelry pieces, further sparking her passion for the craft.

blocks.section: Exclusive Jewelry Exhibition by Shanu Agarwal
blocks.text: In 1995, Shanu moved to Japan after her marriage, where she has continued to build her career as a jewelry designer. Over the years, her unique designs have gained recognition and admiration in high-end stores, both in Japan and internationally.

blocks.section: Exclusive Jewelry Exhibition by Shanu Agarwal
blocks.text: Shanu believes that jewelry has the power to instill confidence, empowerment, and a sense of invincibility in women. “When a woman adorns a unique piece of diamond jewelry, it empowers her and makes her unstoppable,” she says. This belief drives her to create exquisite pieces using the finest diamonds and precious stones, with each piece carefully curated to reflect her vision of beauty and empowerment.

title: Exhibition TENNIS LEGENDS starts on october
description:
Tokyu Corporation, Den-en Tennis Club and CCIFJ are pleased to present a solo exhibition by
French photographer GOVIN SOREL.

blocks.section: Exhibition TENNIS LEGENDS starts on october
blocks.text: Exhibition TENNIS LEGENDS starts on october

blocks.section: Exhibition TENNIS LEGENDS starts on october
blocks.text: Tokyu Corporation, Den-en Tennis Club and CCIFJ are pleased to present a solo exhibition by French photographer GOVIN SOREL.

blocks.section: Exhibition TENNIS LEGENDS starts on october
blocks.text: To mark the 90th anniversary of the Den-en Tennis Club, the artist GOVIN SOREL is exhibiting twelve unpublished photographs featuring portraits of the great players who have marked the history of tennis, including the ‘sworn enemies’ Björn Borg and John Mc Enroe in a single shot. But also, both finalists of the 1983 tournament; Yannick Noah from France and Mats Wilander from Sweden. This exhibition will be held from October 1-31, 2024 at the Denen Tennis Club, one of the most famous tennis clubs in Japan's tennis history!

blocks.section: Exhibition TENNIS LEGENDS starts on october
blocks.text: Focusing on Rolland Garros' 1995 Legends Trophy, the exhibition photographs capture not just individual beauty but also embody the collective story. Without the pressure of the professional circuit, all the players gathered after the matches at the Villa Barclay near the Champs Élysées to celebrate their meeting again.

blocks.section: Exhibition TENNIS LEGENDS starts on october
blocks.text: GOVIN SOREL's fascination with the notion of identity, and with his work, is now at the heart of this exhibition. The twelve portraits, staged in a theatrical and poetic manner, bear witness to a collective identity. As such, each of these twelve black and white portraits calls for a cross-representation between the man and the sportsman, substituting their athletic past with an object.

blocks.section: Exhibition TENNIS LEGENDS starts on october
blocks.text: This approach, which puts the sportsman, his mischief and sometimes his skill, under the microscope, leads to deep down to tennis' essence. What excites in competition, beyond the intense stakes, if not the athlete, is his personality, his otherness.

blocks.section: Exhibition TENNIS LEGENDS starts on october
blocks.text: That through which a sport brings to the highest what it is, the alliance of strength and grace. All the shots were taken with a Polaroid 4x5 sheet film, as a one-shot, to leave them free to strike their pose, without any direction, blurring all boundaries between professional and private life.

blocks.section: Exhibition TENNIS LEGENDS starts on october
blocks.text: GOVIN SOREL is a renowned photographer who knows how to immortalize athletes and men, the space and the light that all great portraitists achieve. While the players he photographs are looking for the perfect gesture, GOVIN SOREL seeks to freeze the movement of the players' bodies. GOVIN SOREL considers this same movement to be ‘the expression of life’ and admits to having been influenced by humanist photographers such as Henri Cartier-Bresson.

blocks.section: Exhibition TENNIS LEGENDS starts on october
blocks.text: From Mansour Bahrani to Yannick Noah, from McEnroe to Stan Smith, he has a talent for capturing such moments of pure harmony. Each of them has renounced their own image to convey a glimpse of their personality, with humor, elegance and simplicity.

blocks.section: Exhibition TENNIS LEGENDS starts on october

title: EXPAT EXPO TOKYO 2022：Festival for international residents in Japan, on 25th & 26th November
description:
"The 3rd EXPAT EXPO TOKYO 2022", the only exhibition for foreigners living in Japan will be held on November 25th (Fri) and 26th (Sat) at the Tokyo Metropolitan Industrial Trade Center Hamamatsucho-kan, with the support of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Minato city, the Japan National Tourism Organization, and France and other countries chamber of commerce and Industry in Japan.
We have large numbers of exhibitors such as International Schools, Japanese Schools, Real Estate, Healthcare, Investment Consultation, Disaster Prevention Information, life support services such as consultation centers, there are also Japan products that can be used for personal use and gifts.
The following three projects will be also held from this time.
・EXPAT TRAVEL FAIR
Great chance to meet Municipality tourism association, travel agency, hotels etc..  You can communicate in English with them.
・WORLD FOOD FAIR
About 10 embassies introduce the food culture of each country as well as Japan. You can taste for free.
・International Flea Market
The first flea market for international families by international families. The main purpose is to hold this event is to be used as a place for international exchange and SDGs education for children.
　
As previous years , there will be performance, experience-based activity, and games to enjoy Japan culture. Also, seminars on various themes and presentations by foreign embassies will be added this time.
Please come with your family and friends. Or if you are in corporate management, human resources, or general affairs, please come to the venue as a place to compare and examine corporate services.
When you visit to the event, please come with an invitation ticket or do pre-registering for the visit from the website.
※If you do pre-registering, the reception on the day will be much smoother. It will be free admission.
　WEB：　https://expat-expo.jp/ 　Invitation ticket：　https://www.expat-expo.jp/inv2022/
In addition, "International Job Fair Tokyo 2022", a job fair for foreigners living in Japan will also be held at the same venue.
If you are looking for employment or career change opportunities, or if you are a company who wants to do recruitment, please stop by here as well.
We are looking forward to see you at the event.

Information :
◆Date: November 25th & 26th, 2022
◆Venue: Tokyo Metropolitan Industrial Trade Center Hamamatsucho-Kan
◆Contact：expat@innovent.co.jp

title: Exploring Japan’s Leather Industry in Himeji
description: An Immersive Visit to a Traditional Japanese Tannery in the Heart of Hyōgo Prefecture

blocks.text: Kansai Event report

blocks.section: Exploring Japan’s Leather Industry in Himeji
blocks.text: Exploring Japan’s Leather Industry in Himeji

blocks.section: Exploring Japan’s Leather Industry in Himeji
blocks.text: An Immersive Visit to a Traditional Japanese Tannery in the Heart of Hyōgo Prefecture

blocks.section: Exploring Japan’s Leather Industry in Himeji
blocks.text: Not everyone has the chance to step inside a tannery, especially one that preserves an ancestral craft dating back over 1,000 years: the production of Himeji white leather .

blocks.section: Exploring Japan’s Leather Industry in Himeji
blocks.text: On April 8, we had the privilege of offering an exclusive behind-the-scenes experience to around fifteen lucky participants at the Sanyo Leather tannery. This unique opportunity was made possible thanks to Mr. Emmanuel Marchat , Board Member of the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCIFJ) and Managing Director of Stahl Japan .

blocks.section: Exploring Japan’s Leather Industry in Himeji
blocks.text: Stahl is a global leader in the production of chemical agents used notably in leather processing. Long considered a polluting industry, leather manufacturing has undergone a significant transformation in recent decades, thanks in part to the growing use of water-based , more environmentally friendly solutions, many developed by Stahl. Sanyo Leather is in fact the second tannery in Japan to have received the LWG environmental certification .

blocks.section: Understanding the Leather-Making Process
blocks.text: Understanding the Leather-Making Process

blocks.section: Understanding the Leather-Making Process
blocks.text: The day began with a seminar presented by Mr. Marchat, who gave a detailed overview of the leather production process:

blocks.section: Understanding the Leather-Making Process
blocks.text: Cleaning : Soaking in lime and acid baths to remove impurities, soften, and prepare the hides

blocks.section: Understanding the Leather-Making Process
blocks.text: Tanning : Using tannin or chrome, this step gives leather its key properties and durability

blocks.section: Understanding the Leather-Making Process
blocks.text: Dyeing : The leather is refined, dyed, and stretched

blocks.section: Understanding the Leather-Making Process
blocks.text: Drying : A crucial step to stabilize the material

blocks.section: Understanding the Leather-Making Process
blocks.text: Finishing : Sanding, polishing, painting (which affects only the surface, unlike dye which penetrates the entire thickness), ironing, and embossing (which gives the leather its final texture)

blocks.section: Understanding the Leather-Making Process
blocks.text: We then had the opportunity to tour the tannery and observe each of these steps firsthand. Sanyo Leather stands out as one of the few tanneries in Japan to still manage the entire production process in-house—from receiving the raw hides to finishing the leather.

blocks.section: Understanding the Leather-Making Process
blocks.text: Mr. Marchat also emphasized a little-known fact: leather production is a circular activity that adds value to a by-product of the food industry. Indeed, the hides used come almost exclusively from meat consumption.

blocks.section: A Moment of Conviviality
blocks.text: A Moment of Conviviality

blocks.section: A Moment of Conviviality
blocks.text: The day continued with a relaxed lunch in Himeji Castle Park under the blooming cherry blossoms—a chance for participants to share their impressions and strengthen professional ties in an informal setting.

blocks.section: A Moment of Conviviality
blocks.text: To round off the experience, part of the group enjoyed a self-guided tour of Himeji Castle, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, adding a cultural touch to an already rich and engaging day.

blocks.section: A Moment of Conviviality
blocks.text: A heartfelt thank you to all participants for their presence and interest, and to Mr. Emmanuel Marchat for his commitment and invaluable insights.

blocks.section: A Moment of Conviviality
blocks.text: We look forward to welcoming you to our upcoming events at the heart of the Kansai economic network!

title: Expo 2025 Osaka, Kansai, Japan: Mazars to Sponsor the France Pavilion

blocks.text: Companies news

blocks.section: Expo 2025 Osaka, Kansai, Japan: Mazars to Sponsor the France Pavilion
blocks.text: Expo 2025 Osaka, Kansai, Japan: Mazars to Sponsor the France Pavilion

blocks.section: Expo 2025 Osaka, Kansai, Japan: Mazars to Sponsor the France Pavilion
blocks.text: 25 April 2023 - Mazars, the international audit, tax and advisory firm, has signed on to sponsor the France Pavilion for Expo 2025 Osaka, Kansai, Japan (“the Expo”), which will be held from 13 April through 13 November 2025.

blocks.section: Expo 2025 Osaka, Kansai, Japan: Mazars to Sponsor the France Pavilion
blocks.text: Based on an agreement signed with La Compagnie Française des Expositions (COFREX), who is organising and implementing France’s participation in the Expo, Mazars will provide support to France as a sponsor. Mazars provides COFREX with expertise to support overseas investment in Japan and will form an expert team to handle the specific needs of COFREX for this event in relation to international mobility, tax and other compliance matters. Under the theme of “Designing Future Society for Our Lives” the Expo will be held in Japan, where Mazars has worked for over 30 years. Since 1992, Mazars in Japan has played a key role in providing services to foreign investors and Japanese companies, especially those with overseas operations. Today, it is recognized as a top professional service firm in Japan. As one integrated team, Mazars in Japan will support COFREX in all aspects of accounting, finance, HR management, regulations, and tax matters, working closely with Mazars in France to fulfill the crucial mission to ensure a success of the France Pavilion at the Expo. Olivier Lenel, CEO & Chairman of the Management Board of Mazars in France, commented: “I am very proud to contribute to a major event that will be held in Japan. We will take this opportunity to reaffirm our responsibility to contribute to the public good and exert our international partnership for COFREX and the Japan-France friendship.” Jean-Francois Salzmann, Mazars in Japan Managing Partner, said: “The theme of the Expo 2025 essentially matches Mazars’s commitment to sustainable reform. We are delighted to participate in the Expo in Japan and are determined to dedicate all our efforts for the success.” Jacques Maire, COFREX Chair and General Commissioner of the France Pavilion at the Expo, commented: “The partnership with the Mazars Group, the new sponsor of the French Pavilion, will bring us many benefits. Full access to its expertise is a great opportunity to ensure, in the very specific Japanese context, a very professional deployment of all the activities of the Pavilion: construction, management and commercial activities. It is a key contribution to the radiance of the Pavilion in Osaka 2025.”

title: EY European Attractiveness Survey 2023
description:
France continues to maintain its position as the leading European country in attracting foreign investment, with nearly 1,260 projects registered in 2022, marking the fourth consecutive year of this achievement. This remarkable feat sets a historic record and comes as encouraging news just before the sixth edition of the Choose France summit. This exclusive event, scheduled for 15th May, is specifically designed for top executives from major foreign companies and will take place at the prestigious Château de Versailles, following an invitation extended by the President of the French Republic.
France is the most attractive country in Europe in 2022
France maintains its position as the most attractive country in Europe in 2022, according to a survey conducted by EY. Despite the challenging geopolitical, economic, and social environment, France has even extended its lead over its traditional competitors, the UK and Germany.
The survey revealed that France recorded 1,259 announced implementations or expansions in 2022, representing a 3% increase compared to the previous year. This achievement marks the fourth consecutive year that France has topped the European ranking. EY attributes this ongoing success to the continued positive momentum that started in 2017, despite economic challenges stemming from geopolitical crises.
EY's findings indicate that the desire to invest in France remains strong, with 61% of surveyed companies having immediate investment plans in the country for 2023. Decision-makers closely scrutinize France's economic, social, and energy landscape, anticipating potential changes in the short term that could impact future results.

An upturn for all French regions
A positive trend can be observed in all regions of France, with each region benefiting from its attractive status. The Ile-de-France region, with 326 projects in 2022, has secured the top spot in the ranking of the most attractive regions in Europe, surpassing Greater London (299 projects in 2022) for the first time in the history of the EY survey.
After the capital, three other regions have passed the milestone of 100 implementation projects: Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes, Hauts-de-France and Nouvelle-Aquitaine. In particular, EY highlights that almost half of the projects affect rural areas or medium-sized towns with fewer than 200,000 inhabitants. This underscores the importance of France's attractiveness, which extends to all its territories, including the Ile-de-France and the regions, major metropolitan areas and more remote areas far from major urban centres.
EY concludes that this widespread attractiveness throughout the country represents a significant opportunity for France to showcase its attractiveness in different regions and territories, regardless of their proximity to major urban centres.

title: Facing rising prices, more and more Japanese are opting for the suburbs
description: As property prices continue to soar in Japan, almost 17,000 people have left Tokyo to settle in the suburbs.

blocks.text: Foresight

blocks.section: Facing rising prices, more and more Japanese are opting for the suburbs
blocks.text: Facing rising prices, more and more Japanese are opting for the suburbs

blocks.section: Facing rising prices, more and more Japanese are opting for the suburbs
blocks.text: As property prices continue to soar in Japan, almost 17,000 people have left Tokyo to settle in the suburbs.

blocks.section: Facing rising prices, more and more Japanese are opting for the suburbs
blocks.text: The “ datsu tokyo ” movement (脱・東京) is gaining momentum in the Japanese capital due to rising property prices. Last year, almost 17,000 people left Tokyo for outlying prefectures.

blocks.section: Facing rising prices, more and more Japanese are opting for the suburbs
blocks.text: Published by the Ministry of the Interior, a report shows how the prefectures of Tokyo, Kanagawa, Saitama and Chiba are experiencing an over-migration of 20-year-olds to Tokyo. However, people in their thirties and forties, the generation that raises children, prefer to emigrate to outlying regions.

blocks.section: Facing rising prices, more and more Japanese are opting for the suburbs
blocks.text: With rising rental prices, the generation raising children is struggling to find housing in Tokyo: a report published by the Cabinet Office indicates a shift “to suburbs of the Tokyo metropolitan area, where housing prices are lower.”

blocks.section: Facing rising prices, more and more Japanese are opting for the suburbs
blocks.text: The same report stresses the need to “guarantee housing for the generation raising children by promoting supply-side measures, such as increasing the supply of public housing.”

blocks.section: Facing rising prices, more and more Japanese are opting for the suburbs
blocks.text: The lack of affordable housing is therefore yet another obstacle for families, in a country characterized by a falling birth rate and an aging population.

blocks.section: Gala payments お支払い
blocks.text: Gala payments お支払い

blocks.section: Gala payments お支払い
blocks.text: We unfortunately cannot hand the receipt at the venue. If you wish to receive a receipt either by post or by email, please send a note to gala(@)ccifj.or.jp .

blocks.section: Gala payments お支払い
blocks.text: イベント当日に領収証のお渡しは行っておりません。ご希望の場合は gala(@)ccifj.or.jp までお問い合わせください。イベント後に原本を郵送もしくはメールにてデータをお送りいたします。

blocks.section: Gala payments お支払い
blocks.text: We will send you an invoice for the participation fee by mail, and we kindly request that you make the payment to the designated bank account. Please note that it may take a few weeks for the invoice to be delivered after your application is confirmed. Additionally, please note that on-site payments at the venue on the day of the event are not accepted, so we kindly ask you to make the payment in advance.

blocks.section: Gala payments お支払い
blocks.text: 参加費は請求書を郵送でお送りしますので、記載されている銀行口座へお振込みをお願いいたします。尚、請求書のお届けにはお申込みの確定から数週間かかる可能性がございます。尚、当日現地会場でのお支払いは対応しておりませんので、必ず事前にお支払いいただきますよう、お願い申し上げます。

blocks.section: Applications お申し込み
blocks.text: Applications お申し込み

blocks.section: Applications お申し込み
blocks.text: We have set prices for both members and non-members of the French Chamber of Commerce in Japan.

blocks.section: Applications お申し込み
blocks.text: 在日フランス商工会議所会員価格と非会員価格を設定しています。

blocks.section: Applications お申し込み
blocks.text: Reservations are possible for one person and above. The number of people per table is set at 10, so if you make a reservation with fewer than 10 people, you will be seated with another small group. Please note that the seating arrangements will be determined by CCIFJ. If you wish to be seated with specific individuals, please try to make the reservation together (such as having one representative fill out the reservation form) or indicate your request in the comments section of the form.

blocks.section: Applications お申し込み
blocks.text: 予約は１名から可能です。1テーブルの人数は10名となっていますので、10名以下の人数で予約される場合は他の少人数グループと相席になります。尚、組み合わせはガラ・パーティー運営によって決定されますのであらかじめご了承ください。同席をされたい方がいる場合は、なるべく予約を纏めて行っていただくか（代表1名が予約フォームを記入するなど）、フォーム内にコメントをご記載ください。

blocks.section: Applications お申し込み
blocks.text: Once you submit the application form, you will receive a confirmation email from the organizers within a few days, which will finalize your application. Subsequently, we will send you an invoice for the participation fee within a few weeks, and finally, we will send the invitations cards.

blocks.section: Applications お申し込み
blocks.text: お申込みフォームを送信されましたら、運営より確定のメールを数日内にお送りし、申し込みの確定となります。その後、数週間内に参加費の請求書をお届けし、最後に招待状をメールでお届けいたします。

blocks.section: Applications お申し込み
blocks.text: If you have dietary restrictions, such as food allergies, or cannot consume alcohol, please indicate them in advance on the application form or inform us as soon as possible.

blocks.section: Applications お申し込み
blocks.text: 食物アレルギーやアルコール不可などの食事制限がある場合は、申し込みフォーム内であらかじめ回答いただくか、確認でき次第すぐにご連絡ください。

blocks.section: Applications お申し込み
blocks.text: Please check the gala party website for the respective application deadlines. Please note that depending on the progress, we may close the application earlier than planned, so we recommend completing your application as soon as possible.

blocks.section: Dress Code ドレスコード
blocks.text: 当日は、夜会服（例：タキシード、ダークスーツ、イブニングドレス、訪問着）でご参加いただきますようお願いいたします。

blocks.section: Dress Code ドレスコード
blocks.text: We kindly request that you attend the event in formal attire (tuxedo, dark suit, evening dress, or formal kimono).

blocks.section: Dress Code ドレスコード
blocks.text: There are no reserved spaces for changing clothes within the hotel premises. Therefore, please come to the banquet hall after having already changed into your attire. Thank you for your understanding.

blocks.section: Dress Code ドレスコード
blocks.text: 着替え用としてホテル館内に予約しているスペースはありませんので、あらかじめお召し替えを済ませてから宴会場までお越しいただきますよう、よろしくお願いいたします。

blocks.section: Invitation 招待状
blocks.text: Invitation 招待状

blocks.section: Invitation 招待状
blocks.text: We will send an invitation via email approximately one week before the event. You can either bring a printed copy or show it on your smartphone for admission. In case you do not have the invitation with you, it is possible to check-in with your name; however, it may take more time than with the invitation.

blocks.section: Invitation 招待状
blocks.text: 1週間前を目途にデータの招待状をメールにてお送りします。こちらは当日印刷したものをお持ちいただいても、スマートフォン等で提示いただく形でも受付可能です。万が一招待状をお持ちでない場合もお名前で受付可能ですが、招待状をお持ちの場合よりも時間がかかりますのであらかじめご了承ください。

blocks.section: Raffles 大抽選会
blocks.text: Raffles 大抽選会

blocks.section: Raffles 大抽選会
blocks.text: Raffle tickets will be available for purchase on-site at 1,000 yen each, payable in cash. Please note that some parties may also offer pre-sale tickets.

blocks.section: Raffles 大抽選会
blocks.text: 当日会場にて販売を行っております。 ガラ・パーティー福岡の抽選券は1枚￥1,000、現金でご購入いただけます。尚、前売り券の販売を実施する場合がございます。

blocks.section: Changes After Application お申し込み後の変更について
blocks.text: Changes After Application お申し込み後の変更について

blocks.section: Changes After Application お申し込み後の変更について
blocks.text: On the day of the event, participant names will be registered in the reception system, and name tags will be placed at each seat in the banquet room. Please note that changes to participant names or any modification of the reservations after May 9, 2025 at noon will be charged 5,000 yens. Please inform the Gala Party organizers ( gala(@)ccifj.or.jp ) as soon as possible.

blocks.section: Changes After Application お申し込み後の変更について
blocks.text: イベント当日は、受付システムに参加者名が登録され、宴会場では各席に名札が設置されます。2025年5月9日（金）正午以降のお申込み内容変更（参加者名・人数の変更、食事リクエストの追加等）については1件につき￥5,000（税込）の手数料を頂戴いたしますので、何卒ご理解の程どうぞよろしくお願い申し上げます。尚、事故や急病等でやむを得ず欠席が発生する場合は、なるべく早めにガラ・パーティー運営（ gala(@)ccifj.or.jp ）までお知らせください。

blocks.section: Changes After Application お申し込み後の変更について
blocks.text: For cancellations made after the cancellation fee deadline (approximately 1 month before the event), the full cost of the seat will be charged. If you are unable to attend the event due to unavoidable circumstances, we recommend considering a replacement participant, if possible.

blocks.section: Changes After Application お申し込み後の変更について
blocks.text: キャンセル料発生期日（目安：イベント1か月前）以降の予約取り消しについては、お席の代金を100％請求させていただきますのであらかじめご了承ください。尚、やむを得ず欠席が発生する場合はなるべく参加者の差し替えをご検討いただくことをお勧めします。

blocks.section: Others その他
blocks.text: The Gala Party consists of three parts: the dinner, the show, and the raffle. Registration starts at 6:15 PM, Opening ceremony at 7:00 PM, Closing at 9:30 PM.

blocks.section: Others その他
blocks.text: ガラ・パーティーはディナー、エンターテインメント、大抽選会の3部構成です。

blocks.section: Others その他
blocks.text: ※18時15分受付開始、19時00分開会、21時30分閉会

blocks.text: 事前の参加者リストの開示は行っておりませんのであらかじめご了承ください。

blocks.section: Others その他
blocks.text: ガラパーティーに関するお問い合わせは、 gala(@)ccifj.or.jp までお願いします。数日以内にご返信させていただきます。

blocks.section: Others その他

description: The famous grocery store on rue de la Madeleine in Paris has been acquired by the Breton Galapagos group.

blocks.text: Fauchon grocery announced buyout by Galapagos group

blocks.section: Fauchon grocery announced buyout by Galapagos group
blocks.text: The famous grocery store on rue de la Madeleine in Paris has been acquired by the Breton Galapagos group.

blocks.section: Fauchon grocery announced buyout by Galapagos group
blocks.text: Fauchon has been acquired by Galapagos, headed by Jérôme Tacquard .

blocks.section: Fauchon grocery announced buyout by Galapagos group
blocks.text: “There is a lot in common between the two entities, a sharing of values and an anchoring in French haute gastronomy,” he explains in an interview with the newspaper Ouest France .

blocks.section: Fauchon grocery announced buyout by Galapagos group
blocks.text: The Fauchon grocery store is known as the emblem of Place Madeleine in Paris , but also for its stores all over the world. However, the brand has been weakened by the health crisis.

blocks.section: Fauchon grocery announced buyout by Galapagos group
blocks.text: The Galapagos group is famous for its Biscuits roses de chez Fossier, Gavottes (crêpes dentelles) and Traou Mad (cookies), and also owns Mademoiselle de Margaux and Moulin du Pivert (organic cookies). It generates annual sales of close to 125 million euros.

blocks.section: Fauchon grocery announced buyout by Galapagos group
blocks.text: This acquisition will strengthen Galapagos’ international presence : Fauchon is present in over 15 countries with more than 80 points of sale, and also runs two 5-star hotels (Paris and Kyoto).

blocks.section: Fauchon grocery announced buyout by Galapagos group
blocks.text: “We already generate 20% of our sales internationally, and the arrival of Fauchon in the family group, with its strong synergies, will enable us to pursue this development and continue to promote France and its gourmet products,” commented Jérome Tacquard .

title: Félix Portier, CCIFJ Ambassador for Hokkaido
description:
As General Manager of NASKEO Kankyo KK, the Japanese subsidiary of the Keon Group, Félix Portier works from Sapporo to develop anaerobic digestion solutions tailored to the needs of farms and wastewater treatment plants. With nearly ten years of experience in Hokkaido, he now draws on his local knowledge to strengthen ties between French and Japanese companies.
A career between France and Japan
After studying Japanese at Toulouse II - Jean Jaurès University, including a year as an exchange student at the University of the Ryukyus in Okinawa, Félix Portier obtained his master’s degree in 2015. He subsequently worked in a variety of fields, from translation and interpreting to manual work, before joining NASKEO in 2017 through the French International Internship Programme (V.I.E.) as a site coordinator on an anaerobic digestion project in Hokkaido. He later moved into business development before becoming Managing Director of NASKEO Kankyo KK in August 2025, following the acquisition of stakes in the company by two Hokkaido-based groups.
Anaerobic digestion in support of the energy transition
Based in Sapporo, he oversees the deployment of Biolectric® micro-anaerobic digestion units, which enable livestock farms to convert their organic waste into renewable energy. Operating at the intersection of agriculture and the energy transition, this business allows him to build close relationships with local stakeholders. In January 2026, NASKEO Kankyo notably received the Jury’s Special Award at the French Business Awards (FBA), organized by the CCIFJ, and won the Hokkaido GX New Energy Award.
Strengthening ties between France and Hokkaido
As the CCIFJ Ambassador for Hokkaido, Félix Portier aims to raise awareness among French companies of the region's economic potential, particularly in agriculture, agri-food and renewable energy, as well as logistics, automation and tourism. His priorities are to increase the Chamber's visibility across the island, develop relationships with local economic and institutional stakeholders, and foster exchanges between French and Japanese companies through events, business meetings and visits by French delegations.
One of NASKEO Kankyo's ongoing projects involves installing two Biolectric® units at a dairy farm with 700 cows in northern Hokkaido, with commissioning scheduled for summer 2027. This project illustrates the opportunities for cooperation between French expertise and Japanese partners, as well as Félix Portier's ambition to contribute to the long-term development of economic ties between France and Hokkaido.
Contact:
Félix Portierfelix.portier@naskeo.com

His priorities are to increase the Chamber's visibility across the island, develop relationships with local economic and institutional stakeholders, and foster exchanges between French and Japanese companies through events, business meetings and visits by French delegations.

blocks.section: Félix Portier, CCIFJ Ambassador for Hokkaido
blocks.text: One of NASKEO Kankyo's ongoing projects involves installing two Biolectric® units at a dairy farm with 700 cows in northern Hokkaido, with commissioning scheduled for summer 2027. This project illustrates the opportunities for cooperation between French expertise and Japanese partners, as well as Félix Portier's ambition to contribute to the long-term development of economic ties between France and Hokkaido.

blocks.section: First edition of the Food & Beverage Forum by the Kansai Desk
blocks.text: Promouvoir l'excellence des produits français auprès des professionnels du monde hôtelier du Kansai lors de notre premier Forum Food & Beverage.

blocks.section: First edition of the Food & Beverage Forum by the Kansai Desk
blocks.text: Notre événement s’est tenu ce mardi dans la lumineuse salle " Daidokoro ", une cuisine communale flambante neuve au 8e étage du bâtiment " Question ", idéalement situé en face de l’hôtel de ville en plein cœur de Kyoto et facilement accessible. Il s’agissait du premier forum Food & Beverage organisé au Kansai par notre Chambre : une demande de longue date de plusieurs membres et partenaires locaux, soucieux de faire le lien entre les importateurs locaux de produits français et les professionnels de l’hôtellerie et de la restauration .

blocks.section: First edition of the Food & Beverage Forum by the Kansai Desk
blocks.text: Objectif : faciliter la collaboration entre ces acteurs clés, en créant un cadre propice à l’échange, la dégustation et l’exploration de nouveaux partenariats commerciaux .

blocks.section: First edition of the Food & Beverage Forum by the Kansai Desk
blocks.text: Les visiteurs ont pu déguster des produits emblématiques présentés par nos exposants partenaires, au nombre desquels on pouvait compter :

blocks.section: First edition of the Food & Beverage Forum by the Kansai Desk
blocks.text: Les vins, spiritueux et champagnes (y compris sans alcool) d’ AOC France

blocks.section: First edition of the Food & Beverage Forum by the Kansai Desk
blocks.text: Les confiseries traditionelles (comme les célèbres “ Bêtises de Cambrai ”) proposées par l’ Auberge du Tanuki noir

blocks.section: First edition of the Food & Beverage Forum by the Kansai Desk
blocks.text: Les bières pressions artisanales de la Brasserie Licorne

blocks.section: First edition of the Food & Beverage Forum by the Kansai Desk
blocks.text: Une sélection de vins de choix importés par Émotions .

blocks.section: First edition of the Food & Beverage Forum by the Kansai Desk
blocks.text: Des fromages sélectionnés par le MOF Mons et importés par les Fromages de Mythese à Kyoto,

blocks.section: First edition of the Food & Beverage Forum by the Kansai Desk
blocks.text: Une série de vins et boissons pétillantes sans alcool présentées par Mottox

blocks.section: First edition of the Food & Beverage Forum by the Kansai Desk
blocks.text: Les chocolats fins et purées de fruits à destination des pâtissiers de Nichifutsu Shoji

blocks.section: First edition of the Food & Beverage Forum by the Kansai Desk
blocks.text: Enfin, Rougié Sarlat a conquis les amateurs de gastronomie avec son foie gras de qualité unique.

blocks.section: First edition of the Food & Beverage Forum by the Kansai Desk
blocks.text: Nous avons aussi eu le privilège d'accueillir Monsieur Katsume Yasushi , député de la première circonscription de Kyoto à la Chambre des représentants, et grand amateur de produits français. Il était pour l’occasion invité par notre ambassadeur de la CCIFJ à Kyoto, Monsieur Hayashi , qui nous a également gratifiés de sa présence et de son aide tout au long de la journée.

blocks.section: First edition of the Food & Beverage Forum by the Kansai Desk
blocks.text: L’événement a également été ponctuée par l’intervention de l’entreprise Label Bank , qui nous a partagé son expertise sur le sujet du marché des importations de produits alimentaires et de boissons au Japon, en fournissant des informations précieuses sur les exigences réglementaires en matière d'étiquetage , un sujet d’importance pour les professionnels présents.

blocks.section: First edition of the Food & Beverage Forum by the Kansai Desk
blocks.text: Les discussions animées qui ont suivi ont montré l’intérêt croissant pour ces échanges , et ont permis d’élargir les opportunités de tous les participants.

blocks.section: First edition of the Food & Beverage Forum by the Kansai Desk
blocks.text: Nous tenons à remercier chaleureusement nos huit exposants ainsi que tous les visiteurs qui se sont déplacés jusqu’à nous. Fort de ce premier forum Food & Beverage, nous espérons pouvoir organiser une nouvelle édition, en réunissant encore davantage de participants et en continuant à promouvoir l’excellence des produits français dans la région du Kansai.

title: For its 100th anniversary, Gucci opens a pop-up exhibition in a historical Kyoto Machiya
description:
For its 100th anniversary, a Kyoto Machiya (Japanese townhouse) has been transformed into the Gucci Bamboo House – in honor of the brand’s iconic bag.
The pop-up is in celebration of the brand’s 100th anniversary and highlights the latest collection titled ‘Aria’ by creative director Alessandro Michele.
As Gucci frequently draws inspiration from the past to create new and innovative pieces, Kyoto – revered for its deeply rooted traditions – was a fitting destination to showcase the new collection.
Installations include the brand’s bags with classic bamboo handles while also showing the craftsmanship behind the process.
The library is especially eye-catching with flower-print wallpaper, Gucci chairs and curated bookshelves reminiscent of the Gucci Garden Bookstore in Florence, Italy. Other details, like the shoji paper panels with Gucci monogram, are far more subtle. There is also a salon displaying the reissued Gucci Diana bag.
As a nod to the brand’s latest series of handbags – a revival of the bamboo-handled purses Gucci first released in 1947 – the house is now monikered as the Gucci Bamboo House. This theme is consistent throughout the machiya, which is not only decorated with bamboo furnishings and installations but also boasts a lush bamboo grove in its private Japanese garden.
The Gucci Bamboo House is now open through August 15. Admission is free, but visitors must make reservations in advance. 
More information

title: Looking Back at the 2026 France–Japan Economic Forum in Fukuoka, Kyushu Desk
description: Mr. Bernard Delmas's exceptional intervention sparked fruitful discussions and valuable exchanges among participants.

blocks.text: Kyushu Event report

blocks.section: Looking Back at the 2026 France–Japan Economic Forum in Fukuoka, Kyushu Desk
blocks.text: Looking Back at the 2026 France–Japan Economic Forum in Fukuoka, Kyushu Desk

blocks.section: Looking Back at the 2026 France–Japan Economic Forum in Fukuoka, Kyushu Desk
blocks.text: Mr. Bernard Delmas's exceptional intervention sparked fruitful discussions and valuable exchanges among participants.

blocks.section: Looking Back at the 2026 France–Japan Economic Forum in Fukuoka, Kyushu Desk
blocks.text: On May 28, the CCIFJ 2026 Economic Forum in Fukuoka provided an opportunity for rich discussions and valuable exchanges during an exceptional presentation by Bernard Delmas . This edition brought together around sixty participants around the theme: “Supporting Companies Beyond Borders: Global Leadership Through the Experiences of Michelin and Nissan .”

blocks.section: Looking Back at the 2026 France–Japan Economic Forum in Fukuoka, Kyushu Desk
blocks.text: Following a brief presentation of the Chamber’s activities by our Director of Regional Offices, we had the privilege of welcoming Bernard Delmas, former executive of Michelin and Nissan Motor Corporation, who generously shared his experience and insights during a particularly engaging and thought-provoking presentation.

blocks.section: Looking Back at the 2026 France–Japan Economic Forum in Fukuoka, Kyushu Desk
blocks.text: Having arrived in Japan in the 1980s, Bernard Delmas has witnessed firsthand the profound transformations the country has undergone over the past four decades. Drawing on this unique perspective, he highlighted how international leadership relies on a delicate balance between global vision, local adaptation, and intercultural openness. These challenges remain more relevant than ever for companies seeking to expand and thrive internationally.

blocks.section: Looking Back at the 2026 France–Japan Economic Forum in Fukuoka, Kyushu Desk
blocks.text: A question-and-answer session followed, allowing participants to further explore the topics raised during the presentation and gain additional insights into the many questions and concerns facing businesses today. Attendees enthusiastically took advantage of this opportunity to engage directly with the speaker.

blocks.section: Looking Back at the 2026 France–Japan Economic Forum in Fukuoka, Kyushu Desk
blocks.text: Participants highly appreciated the quality of the discussions and continued their conversations during the networking session that followed. This convivial moment, accompanied by coffee and a selection of French pastries that were particularly enjoyed by guests, helped extend the exchanges in a warm and lively atmosphere. The forum concluded at 5:30 p.m., although many participants were still engaged in conversation, already looking forward to future opportunities to meet again.

blocks.section: Looking Back at the 2026 France–Japan Economic Forum in Fukuoka, Kyushu Desk
blocks.text: We would like to extend our warmest thanks to the Fukuoka Chamber of Commerce and Industry (FCCI), with whom we co-organized this forum. Our sincere gratitude also goes to the City of Fukuoka and the Institut français du Kyushu for their valuable support in making this event possible.

blocks.section: Looking Back at the 2026 France–Japan Economic Forum in Fukuoka, Kyushu Desk
blocks.text: Finally, we would like to thank all participants for their attendance and for the quality of the exchanges throughout the afternoon.

blocks.text: AI, Defense & Industrial Sovereignty

blocks.section: France–Japan Strategic Tech Forum 2026: A Key Event for Franco-Japanese Innovation
blocks.text: On September 24, 2026 , Tokyo will host the France–Japan Strategic Tech Forum 2026 , organized by La French Tech Tokyo in partnership with Alta Ares and Scrum Ventures . The event will bring together more than 150 stakeholders from the French and Japanese tech ecosystems to address issues at the heart of today’s strategic agenda: AI, defense, deeptech and industrial sovereignty .

blocks.section: France–Japan Strategic Tech Forum 2026: A Key Event for Franco-Japanese Innovation
blocks.text: Through keynotes, panel discussions and networking sessions, the forum aims to foster collaboration between startups, corporations, investors and public-sector stakeholders from France and Japan. Discussions will notably explore emerging trends in technological and industrial sovereignty, the role of AI in strategic sectors, and opportunities for stronger cooperation between the two countries.

blocks.section: France–Japan Strategic Tech Forum 2026: A Key Event for Franco-Japanese Innovation
blocks.text: The forum is designed for innovative startups, VC and CVC investors, French companies operating in Japan, as well as Japanese corporations looking to strengthen their ties with the French Tech ecosystem.

blocks.section: A Sponsorship Opportunity for CCIFJ Member Companies
blocks.text: For companies with an interest in AI, cybersecurity, defense, deeptech or industrial innovation , the forum also offers a valuable opportunity to become a partner of the event.

blocks.section: A Sponsorship Opportunity for CCIFJ Member Companies
blocks.text: Partners will benefit from increased visibility among a highly qualified audience of business leaders, investors, entrepreneurs and public-sector stakeholders from both France and Japan. Depending on the partnership level, opportunities include speaking or panel participation, enhanced brand visibility, curated introductions and privileged access to participants.

blocks.section: A Sponsorship Opportunity for CCIFJ Member Companies
blocks.text: Beyond visibility, sponsorship offers an opportunity to build strategic relationships with innovative startups, investors and corporate partners across the French and Japanese ecosystems.

title: Free Online Event Digital Beaujolais Night: "Cheers! Let's travel around Beaujolais!"
description:
Friday, November 18 Free Online Event Digital Beaujolais Night - Cheers! Let's travel around Beaujolais! Sponsored by Inter Beaujolais  November 17th is the day Beaujolais Nouveau is finally released!
To celebrate, Inter Beaujolais will hold a free online event "Digital Beaujolais Night!" on Friday, November 18. Connecting to the Beaujolais region of France, three producers will talk live about this year's Beaujolais Nouveau and the trends in Beaujolais wine production. In the second part, Yuya Kondo, chef-sommelier at Ginza L'écrin, and Sakura Akimoto, owner-chef of Morceau, will be invited as guests to introduce Beaujolais wine and food pairings.

title: Free Webinar: Dr. Jacques Attali, "Intelligence of Europe"; Interpreting Cities, People and the World in the So-Called "With-Corona" Era
description:
Purpose of the symposium
In 2020, the global spread of the novel coronavirus COVID-19 has significantly affected our society and economy.
Looking back at the history since the Industrial Revolution, the period of industrialization and mass production and consumption has been premised on a shift of population from rural to urban areas; in other words "sparse population" to "dense population." Every business activity in recent years, from office buildings and retail facilities to restaurants, is based on "volume" associated with "dense crowds."
That assumption has collapsed due to the fear of the novel coronavirus COVID-19.
It is no exaggeration to say that this is an event that will remain in the history of humanity, as we started calling it "BC/AC" (Before Corona/After Corona) to mark the end/beginning of the history. Since it takes a certain amount of time to develop a vaccine, it is inevitable to coexist with COVID-19.
Even if we manage to overcome COVID-19, the battle between humans and infectious diseases will still continue, given that there are a large number of unexpected infectious diseases in the nature.
How will our society and economy, and the world change in the era of "With-Corona"? In these days, in which national particularism can make a profit, how can humankind deal with global issues such as infectious diseases and global warming?
At this symposium, we would like to examine the answers to that questions together with the French thinker and economist, Dr. Jacques Attali, who is also referred to as "Intelligence of Europe." Then, we will discuss with experts including Dr. Attali, Prof. Kazunari Uchida, Prof. Kengo Kuma and Prof. Seiichiro Yonekura, about the community development and working style in the With-Corona era as well as the possibility of sustainable development goals (SDGs) and public-private partnership (PPP).

Information
Time & Date: 4:45pm to 7:00pm on Monday 28th of September 2020 (JST)
Venue: Online Webinar via Zoom
Languages: French, Japanese
Fee: Free
Apply: http://ptix.at/iN7uQ8

Panelists
Dr. Jacques Attali,
Prof. Kazunari Uchida, Professor at Waseda Business School (Graduate School of Business and Finance)
Prof. Kengo Kuma, Architect, Special Professor and Professor Emeritus at the University of Tokyo
Prof. Seiichiro Yonekura, Professor at Hitotsubashi University Institute of Innovation Research, Professor at Hosei University Business school of Innovation Management

Moderator
Mr. Kimikazu Uemura, Director of CPDS, FEF and OPPS

Program
1.    Opening remark (4:45pm -) : Mr. Kuniaki Hanamura, Chairperson of CPDS
2.    Guest speech (4:47pm -): Mr. Hiroto Izumi, Special Advisor to the Prime Minister
3.    Introduction of the organizers (4:50pm -)
4.    Keynote speech (5:00pm -): Dr. Jacques Attali, French economist and thinker, former president of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development
5.    Panel discussion (6:00pm -)
6.    Closing remark (6:55pm -): Mr. Takeshi Maeda, Chairperson of FEF

Organizers
 	Construction Project Delivery System Council (CPDS) 	Future Environment Forum (FEF) 	Organization for PPP Promotion Support (OPPS) 

Sponsors
 	 Japanese government (MLIT and MEXT) 	 Japanese government agencies (JICA, UR) 	 Nikkei Inc., Nikkei Business Publications, Inc., 	United Nations Centre for Regional Development (UNCRD)

blocks.text: Under the patronage of the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan, BONJOUR FRANCE has been organizing events to promote the French art of living since 2015.

title: French artist Marion Flament returns to Japan with her first major solo exhibition
description:
Starting December 4, 2025, the Esther Okada Art Gallery in Yoyogi will present Nothing Seems Certain, the first major solo exhibition in Japan by Marion FLAMENT, a 36-year-old French artist renowned for her bold glass creations and striking play of light. The exhibition will run until December 21, 2025.
Her art explores the poetics of the ephemeral and light as a language, revealing the memory of materials and the traces left by time. Between matter, elements, and duration, her work acts as a sensitive revealer, inviting viewers to change their perception of the world.
In Nothing Seems Certain, Marion Flament seeks to materialize impermanence, fragility, and transformation. Her compositions, often minimalist, balance between the organic and the geometric, between chaos and control. More than a visual demonstration, her work offers an emotional and sensory experience, where texture, color, and light interact in subtle harmony.
Her creations invite us to slow down and observe, to rediscover the beauty of details and the hidden richness within the simplicity of matter. Through this approach, Marion Flament offers a poetic counterpoint to the frenetic pace of the modern world – an art of contemplation and resonance.
Born in 1989 in Reims, Marion Flament lives and works in Paris. A graduate of the École Boulle and the École nationale supérieure des arts décoratifs de Paris (EnsAD), she is a laureate of the Hermès Glass Academy, the Artists’ Foundation, ADAGP, and CNAP. Her work has been showcased in numerous international art residencies and exhibited in Milan, Munich, Hong Kong, Tokyo, and Singapore, confirming her place on the global contemporary art scene.
More information: www.zulaarts.com

blocks.section: French bistro "Loiseau de France" settles in Tokyo
blocks.text: Reflecting the vision of legendary French chef Bernard Loiseau, the Loiseau de France Bistro will open its doors in Tokyo on Sunday, June 2, 2024.

blocks.section: French bistro "Loiseau de France" settles in Tokyo
blocks.text: Bérangère Loiseau, CEO of the Bernard Loiseau Group, is delighted to have fulfilled Bernard Loiseau's ambition to return to the cosmopolitan city of Tokyo after three decades of hard work.

blocks.section: French bistro "Loiseau de France" settles in Tokyo
blocks.text: On Sunday, June 2, 2024, Tokyo will welcome the opening of Loiseau de France, a new gastronomic adventure inspired by the vision of the renowned French chef Bernard Loiseau. For Bérangère Loiseau, CEO of the group of the same name, this opening is an emotional achievement and a tribute to her father, thirty years after Bernard Loiseau enchanted Japan with his cuisine.

blocks.section: French bistro "Loiseau de France" settles in Tokyo
blocks.text: The Loiseau family's ties with Japan go back to the years 1992-1995, when Bernard Loiseau opened a replica of his restaurant "La Côte d'Or" on Rokko Island, Kobe. His cuisine, based on the purity of flavors and simplicity (low fat, low sugar and sauces deglazed with water), immediately captivated Japanese palates.

blocks.section: French bistro "Loiseau de France" settles in Tokyo
blocks.text: Loiseau de France will be located at the Institut Français du Japon (IFJ) in Tokyo, a vibrant cultural center managed by the French Embassy and dedicated to promoting the French language and culture. The IFJ, which will be transformed into a "French village" by architect Sou Fujimoto in 2021, surrounded by a lush garden, is the perfect setting for this new bistro.

blocks.section: French bistro "Loiseau de France" settles in Tokyo
blocks.text: The restaurant will have three distinct spaces: - A 63-seat bistro dining room. - A snack area with 20 seats and a terrace. - A boutique dedicated to 100% Made in France products.

blocks.section: French bistro "Loiseau de France" settles in Tokyo
blocks.text: Blanche Loiseau, after a year of immersion in Japanese culinary culture and an enriching experience as a chef at "Loiseau du Temps" in Besançon, returns to Japan to lead Loiseau de France. She is joined by chef Hiroshi Yamaguchi, a former apprentice of Bernard Loiseau, and an international team of eight.

blocks.section: French bistro "Loiseau de France" settles in Tokyo
blocks.text: The restaurant's décor reflects the elegance of Loiseau's bistros, with fine materials, an oak wine cellar with a refined selection of wines, and a dessert cart. Belle Époque influences are evident in the fabrics and decorative elements, with a Raoul Dufy painting reimagined as Japanese panels dominating the space.

blocks.section: French bistro "Loiseau de France" settles in Tokyo
blocks.text: The bistro's menu is a true invitation to discover the terroirs of France through iconic dishes: poached eggs in red wine sauce, beef bourguignon Bernard Loiseau style, fish quenelle with Nantua sauce, and marinated mackerel fillet. A classic dessert, the Opéra, represents Paris in all its splendor. The culinary journey continues with a carefully curated selection of wines from French vineyards.

blocks.section: French bistro "Loiseau de France" settles in Tokyo
blocks.text: Behind a canvas of art, a music stage will allow the restaurant to host various events, reinforcing its role as an "embassy of French terroirs".

blocks.section: French bistro "Loiseau de France" settles in Tokyo
blocks.text: Address: Institut Français du Japon - Tokyo 1F, 15 Ichigaya-Funakawara-cho, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo 162-0826, Japan Instagram: @loiseaudefrance

title: French Business Awards / Shinnenkai 2025
description:
The French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan hosted the French Business Awards ceremony / Shinnenkai at Grand Hyatt Tokyo on January 30th, in presence of his Excellency, Mr Setton, Ambassador of France to Japan. This event, attended by over 135 participants, provided an exceptional opportunity for networking.

With 20 candidates and 8 awarded prizes, we are delighted to announce our CCI France Japon 2025 laureates:
 	Bel Japan (“Company of the Year” Award) 	Brose Japan (“Product or Service of the Year” Award) 	Stahl Japan (“Credit Agricole CIB Japan Sustainability Award”) 	Sagri Co Ltd. (“French Tech Tokyo” Award) 	EXOTEC Nihon (“Special Jury Award”) 	YUASA SOY SAUCE (“Coup de Coeur”) 	FACIL'iti (“Best Local Expansion Award”) 	JUST.WILL (“Innovation Award”) 

The jury, consisting of the Vice President of CCI France Japon and prominent French and Japanese business leaders, meticulously evaluated the nominees to select the most dynamic, innovative, and high-performing companies thriving in their categories and market. Their selections exemplify the diversity and strength of French and Japanese enterprises.

We extend our thanks to our sponsors, EY, Credit Agricole CIB, and Hotel de l'Alpage, whose support made this event possible.
A special thank you to our partners Baron Philippe de Rothschild and Life.14 for their continuous support.
Finally, we express our gratitude to Grand Hyatt Tokyo for their exceptional hosting and cooperation in making this event a success.

title: French Excellence in Japan: 30 MOFs at the French Pavilion
description:
From Friday, September 26 to Sunday, September 28, the France Pavilion hosted an exceptional event: for the very first time, 30 “Meilleurs Ouvriers de France” (MOF), representing a wide range of professions, gathered in Japan to share and showcase their French craftsmanship with both Japanese and international audiences.
With the official support of the city of Ogaki, located in Gifu Prefecture, and with the participation of the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCIFJ) as an official partner, the 30 MOF in attendance shared their passion and expertise with as many people as possible. They also expressed their desire to build strong ties with Japan through craftsmanship, culture, and savoir-faire.

blocks.section: French Excellence in Japan: 30 MOFs at the French Pavilion
blocks.text: With the official support of the city of Ogaki , located in Gifu Prefecture , and with the participation of the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCIFJ) as an official partner, the 30 MOF in attendance shared their passion and expertise with as many people as possible. They also expressed their desire to build strong ties with Japan through craftsmanship, culture, and savoir-faire.

blocks.section: French Excellence in Japan: 30 MOFs at the French Pavilion
blocks.text: This public event highlighted the vital role of craftsmanship and traditional expertise as a natural bridge between France and Japan . For many years, our two countries have shared a mutual admiration for the transmission of tradition and excellence in creation . The presence of the MOF underscored this affinity, illustrating how craftsmanship stands at the crossroads of culture, industry, and commerce .

blocks.section: French Excellence in Japan: 30 MOFs at the French Pavilion
blocks.text: This first edition paves the way for future prospects. Indeed, for such an event to take place again, the support of partners and sponsors is essential. Only under these conditions can France and Japan continue to build lasting connections around the excellence of craftsmanship .

title: French Japanese Business Summit 2020: Registration is open!
description:
The Chamber of Commerce and Industry France Japon (CCI France Japon) organizes, together with the French Embassy in Japan, for the third consecutive year, a major summit dedicated to the French-Japanese business community.
The French-Japanese Business Summit will be held on November 18 2020, from 10h30 to 19h, at the Nikkei Hall  in Tokyo on the theme:
“Growth Opportunities in Africa : Towards New Business Partnerships”
Following the success of the 2018 and 2019 editions, with an average of 700 delegates and 35 speakers per edition, this summit will once again bring together exceptional guests who will give their insights in front of an audience of business and opinion leaders, journalists as well as officials.
This event will be presential and live broadcasted. During this day, plenary sessions and conferences designed to highlight excellence & partnerships between African countries, Japan and France, and to strengthen economic and commercial relations, will be held.
A networking lunch will be served by Chef-owner of Chez Olivier, Mr. Olivier Oddos, 1 Michelin Star, Tokyo.

blocks.section: French Japanese Business Summit 2022: Registrations open!
blocks.text: Japan as a model for the future “What learnings can be relevant for the world? “

blocks.section: French Japanese Business Summit 2022: Registrations open!
blocks.text: After the most intense crisis the world has faced since 2008, it is time for institutions and countries to adapt and reform again in light of the underlying issues the world is facing that the covid crisis has highlighted. As Japan strives toward a new form of capitalism that is more conscious of these new issues, there is much to learn from the its industrial model’s strengths and from how it is trying to overcome its shortcomings. By focusing on how Japan can concentrate on its core values as a nation of innovation and technology but also a nation of creativity and culture, we can start to grasp what the rest of the world can learn from this model to move towards a more sustainable future that respects both the planet and its workers.

blocks.section: French Japanese Business Summit 2022: Registrations open!
blocks.text: To attempt address these issues, the 2022 French-Japanese Business Summit will gather top-level international speakers from diverse backgrounds – from institutions, citizens and businesses to social sciences, art and architecture – to share their visions, their strategies, and the opportunities they foresee.

title: ​​​​​​​French Japanese Business Summit 2024: Registrations are open!
description:
The French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCI France Japon), under the patronage of the French Embassy to Japan and in partnership with Nikkei, organizes for the 7th consecutive year a great summit dedicated to the French and Japanese business communities.
The French Japanese Business Summit will be held on December 3rd, 2024, at the Tokyo Nikkei Hall, on the theme: “Inventing a Better Future in a Changing World”.
The world is undergoing unprecedented change and uncertainty. Complex and interconnected problems, such as climate change, pandemics, inequality, cyberattacks, and social unrest, challenge the world. These problems demand innovative and collaborative solutions that can harness the power of technology, creativity, and human potential. As business leaders and responsible citizens, we have the unique opportunity and the responsibility to shape the future of our industries, communities, and society in this changing world. We can leverage our resources, expertise, and influence to create positive impact and value for all stakeholders. We can also inspire and empower others to join us in our vision and mission.
During this 2024’s edition of Business Summit, international speakers and participants from diverse backgrounds will convene at Nikkei Hall for a full-day of conferences and networking opportunities. Experts will share their insights on the upcoming transformations for both France and Japan, the strategies driving their global influence, and how they can effectively contribute to a better future.
SELECTED SPEAKERS 
•             Makoto Takashima, Chair of Committee on Europe, Keidanren, Chairman of the Board, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation
•             Inge Kerkloh-Devif, Senior Executive Director, Innovation & Entrepreneurship Institute HEC Paris
•             Franck Leroy, President, Regional Government of Region Grand Est
•             Joji Tagawa, Senior Vice President and Chief Sustainability Officer, Nissan Motor Corporation
•             Teruo Fujii, President, University of Tokyo
•             Philippe Larretche, Decarbonization Director (Strategy and Innovation), Veolia Group
•             François Tardif, Executive Vice President, FORVIA Asia Faurecia Clarion Electronics
•             Taro Fujie, President & CEO, Ajinomoto Co., Inc.
•             Kathy Matsui, General Partner, Mpower Partners
•             Yoshimitsu Kaji, Chairman and CSDO, Cinnamon AI
•             Philippe Godbout, President, Dassault Systèmes Japan
•             Cecile Beliot-Zind, Chief Executive Officer, BEL

And many more !
