blocks.text: On October 15, CCI France Japon, in partnership with Fukui Prefectural Government, organized the “Fukui Prefecture × CCI France Japon Aerospace Business Matching Event” at Todofuken Kaikan in Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo.

blocks.section: Fukui×CCI France Japon Aerospace Business Matching Event
blocks.text: Fukui Prefecture is one of Japan’s leading manufacturing regions and has been expanding its presence in the aerospace sector by leveraging its advanced precision-processing technologies.

blocks.section: Fukui×CCI France Japon Aerospace Business Matching Event
blocks.text: The event brought together Fukui-based companies with specialized expertise and a strong interest in entering the French aerospace industry, as well as French-affiliated companies from the CCI France Japon network.

blocks.section: Fukui×CCI France Japon Aerospace Business Matching Event
blocks.text: As a first step toward future collaboration, participants engaged in one-to-one business meetings throughout the day. In a friendly and constructive atmosphere, companies exchanged ideas, explored potential partnerships, and built valuable new connections.

blocks.section: Fukui×CCI France Japon Aerospace Business Matching Event
blocks.text: We would like to thank all participating companies for their active engagement and look forward to seeing these discussions develop into future business opportunities.

title: G7 CCIs meeting in Osaka ahead of Expo Osaka Kansai 2025
description: On October 8, in the run-up to World Expo 2025, the heads of the Osaka CCI and G7 countries met in the host city.

blocks.text: Kansai Event report

blocks.section: G7 CCIs meeting in Osaka ahead of Expo Osaka Kansai 2025
blocks.text: G7 CCIs meeting in Osaka ahead of Expo Osaka Kansai 2025

blocks.section: G7 CCIs meeting in Osaka ahead of Expo Osaka Kansai 2025
blocks.text: On October 8, in the run-up to World Expo 2025, the heads of the Osaka CCI and G7 countries met in the host city.

blocks.section: G7 CCIs meeting in Osaka ahead of Expo Osaka Kansai 2025
blocks.text: The day was structured around two highlights: a roundtable discussion in the morning, attended by 25 people, and a networking event for members and chamber representatives in the evening. Nearly 130 people attended this event. The backdrop to the meeting was World Expo 2025 and the growing role of chambers of commerce in promoting the Kansai region as a key economic partner.

blocks.section: G7 CCIs meeting in Osaka ahead of Expo Osaka Kansai 2025
blocks.text: Mr. Shingo Torii, President of the Osaka Chamber of Commerce and Industry opened the day’s discussions, accompanied by 10 representatives from the Osaka CCI.

blocks.section: G7 CCIs meeting in Osaka ahead of Expo Osaka Kansai 2025
blocks.text: All the chambers of commerce of the G7 countries took part in the discussions:

blocks.section: G7 CCIs meeting in Osaka ahead of Expo Osaka Kansai 2025
blocks.text: The ACCJ (American Chamber of Commerce) was represented by its President, Mr.Victor Osumi, Managing Director and President Japan of Delta Air Lines, its Vice-President Kansai Mr. Jiro Kawakami, Chief Of Staff at MGM Resorts Japan LLC, as well as its Governor of Kansai, Ms. Simone Thomsen, President of Eli Lilly Japan K. K.

blocks.section: G7 CCIs meeting in Osaka ahead of Expo Osaka Kansai 2025
blocks.text: The AHK (German CCI) was represented by its CEO, Mr. Marcus Schürmann, and Ms. Ying Chen, President and Representative Director of Bayer Yakuhin Ltd.

blocks.section: G7 CCIs meeting in Osaka ahead of Expo Osaka Kansai 2025
blocks.text: The BCCJ (British CC) was represented by its President, Mr. Richard Lyle (VP Trade & FDI, Intralink), and its Executive Director Sarah Backley.

blocks.section: G7 CCIs meeting in Osaka ahead of Expo Osaka Kansai 2025
blocks.text: The CCCJ (Canadian CC) was represented by its President Mr. Marc Bolduc (Country Director, Intralox Japan), and its Executive Director Ms. Noriko Ishida.

blocks.section: G7 CCIs meeting in Osaka ahead of Expo Osaka Kansai 2025
blocks.text: The CCIFJ was represented by Benoit Rulleau, Director of the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan, and Co-CEO of Kansai Airports, and by Mr. Nicolas Bonnardel, General Manager of the CCIFJ.

blocks.section: G7 CCIs meeting in Osaka ahead of Expo Osaka Kansai 2025
blocks.text: The EBC (European Business Council) was represented by its Executive Director (COO), Valérie Moschetti.

blocks.section: G7 CCIs meeting in Osaka ahead of Expo Osaka Kansai 2025
blocks.text: The ICCJ was represented by its president, Mr. Takaaki Komatani, CEO of Itochu Fashion System, eand its General Manager, Mr. Davide Fantoni.

blocks.section: G7 CCIs meeting in Osaka ahead of Expo Osaka Kansai 2025
blocks.text: The general theme of the World Expo is "Designing Future Society for our Lives," and its holding in Osaka is already having an impact on the city and on relations between G7 members.

blocks.section: G7 CCIs meeting in Osaka ahead of Expo Osaka Kansai 2025
blocks.text: Indeed, during the roundtable, participants agreed to strengthen cooperation among chambers of commerce and to use the Expo as an opportunity to deepen their regional trade exchanges and activities. For this purpose, private visits for business delegations from the various countries are being considered.

blocks.section: G7 CCIs meeting in Osaka ahead of Expo Osaka Kansai 2025
blocks.text: The roundtable began with a brief introduction from each of the G7 chambers: Benoit Rulleau presented the CCIFJ, emphasizing its strong connection to the Kansai region, whose offices in Osaka organized 25 events in 2023.

blocks.section: G7 CCIs meeting in Osaka ahead of Expo Osaka Kansai 2025
blocks.text: He also highlighted the importance of supporting the establishment of an international school to enhance the city’s attractiveness to foreign companies. According to him, this potential establishment relies not only on the support of local authorities but also on that of the private sector, where chambers of commerce can have a significant influence.

blocks.section: G7 CCIs meeting in Osaka ahead of Expo Osaka Kansai 2025
blocks.text: In addition to the organization of the event itself, this morning's session was also intended to raise the question of the Expo's legacy beyond the year 2025, in particular its contribution to the city of Osaka, its businesses and, more broadly, the Kansai region.

blocks.section: G7 CCIs meeting in Osaka ahead of Expo Osaka Kansai 2025
blocks.text: Representatives of the Osaka Chamber then presented, by committee, the various Expo-related initiatives aimed at increasing the attractiveness or stimulating the activity of the Osaka region during 2025 and beyond.

blocks.section: G7 CCIs meeting in Osaka ahead of Expo Osaka Kansai 2025
blocks.text: This morning's discussions have a significant impact on Kansai and Japan as a whole, and their location in Osaka lends a true national importance, underscored by NHK's dedicated article on the G7 Chambers of Commerce meeting.

blocks.section: G7 CCIs meeting in Osaka ahead of Expo Osaka Kansai 2025
blocks.text: The representatives of the chambers of commerce and industry then continued their discussions at a more informal reception, attended by representatives of the city and prefecture of Osaka, such as Keiji Okamoto, General Director of the Economic Strategy Department of the City of Osaka.

blocks.section: G7 CCIs meeting in Osaka ahead of Expo Osaka Kansai 2025
blocks.text: The evening was reserved for networking between members and representatives of the various Chambers. This event, was organized on the ground mainly by the American and French Chambers - the only Chambers with branches in the region - and coordinated with the support from Tokyo of the British and Canadian Chambers. The discussions began with a presentation of the various representatives of the seven Chambers who honored us with their presence.

blocks.section: G7 CCIs meeting in Osaka ahead of Expo Osaka Kansai 2025
blocks.text: The evening continued with a buffet during which chamber members and representatives were able to exchange ideas, meet new people, and imagine together the Kansai of tomorrow.

blocks.section: G7 CCIs meeting in Osaka ahead of Expo Osaka Kansai 2025
blocks.text: The remarkable diversity of the people present that evening helped to introduce new faces and forge previously non-existent links:

blocks.section: G7 CCIs meeting in Osaka ahead of Expo Osaka Kansai 2025
blocks.text: This event signals an exciting series of exchanges to come, with 2025 set to be a year full of collaborations between chambers of commerce and countries all around the world!

title: Gala Party in Fukuoka : Mathieu Martin shares his Culinary Adventure
description: Fukuoka, Japan - In culinary world, every travel is an opportunity to discover new flavors and to share unique moments.

blocks.text: Kyushu

blocks.section: Gala Party in Fukuoka : Mathieu Martin shares his Culinary Adventure
blocks.text: Gala Party in Fukuoka : Mathieu Martin shares his Culinary Adventure

blocks.section: Gala Party in Fukuoka : Mathieu Martin shares his Culinary Adventure
blocks.text: Fukuoka, Japan - In culinary world, every travel is an opportunity to discover new flavors and to share unique moments.

blocks.section: Gala Party in Fukuoka : Mathieu Martin shares his Culinary Adventure
blocks.text: Arrived on 9th of June, Mathieu Martin has soon plunged into the vibrante atomosphere of Fukuoka. His first day in the town has started with his walking in the Ohori Park , followed by an immersion into the dynamic areas of Daimyo and Tenjin . The highlight of the day was without doubt the tasting of a traditionnal tonkatsu ramen at a bustling yatai in Nakatsu , offering him a fisrt taste of the richness of the local cuisine.

blocks.section: Gala Party in Fukuoka : Mathieu Martin shares his Culinary Adventure
blocks.text: The morning of 10th June was devoted to the meetings with local producters, guided by Fukuoka town hall. Mathieu began his day by visiting a renowend Wagyu beef breeder, devolving into the subtlety of the breeding of this world-renowned beef.

blocks.section: Gala Party in Fukuoka : Mathieu Martin shares his Culinary Adventure
blocks.text: He then had the unique opportunity to discover edible chrysanthemums ( shungiku ), thanks to a passionate grower, underlining the importance of local agricultural culture in regional cuisine.

blocks.section: Gala Party in Fukuoka : Mathieu Martin shares his Culinary Adventure
blocks.text: Between two explorations, Mathieu also had the pleasure to try the famous mentai furansu , a local speciality that surprised him with its taste. His day ended at Solaria Nishitetsu Hotel , where he shared his expertise with local chefs, while tasting their own innovative creations. Inspired by his morning discoveries, he ended his day with a Wagyu barbecue, celebrating the perfection of the local beef.

blocks.section: Gala Party in Fukuoka : Mathieu Martin shares his Culinary Adventure
blocks.text: Tuesday 11 June was a day dedicated to perfecting details of the dishes in the kitchen. Mathieu Martin worked closely with the team at the Solaria Nishitetsu Hotel to ensure that every dish for the gala the following evening was a true work of culinary art.

blocks.section: Gala Party in Fukuoka : Mathieu Martin shares his Culinary Adventure
blocks.text: Finally, on Wednesday 12 June, on the day of the long-awaited gala, Mathieu Martin and his team shone. Despite the palpable stress before the start of the service, the chef was able to appease the spirits of the team sharing a traditional comforting dish with them. Together, they offered a sumptuous feast that won over the guests, marking the end of an unforgettable experience in Fukuoka. The stress had eased when he went into the hall, with the guests showering him with compliments. Finally, whether on stage or at the end of the event in the kitchen, the farewells were full of emotion, marking both the chef and the Solaria Nishitetsu Hôtel team.

blocks.section: Gala Party in Fukuoka : Mathieu Martin shares his Culinary Adventure
blocks.text: For Mathieu Martin, this stay in Fukuoka will remain engraved in his memory as an enriching experience on both a culinary and personal level. Through every meeting, every tasting and every moment shared in the kitchen, he has been able to capture the very essence of Japanese gastronomy and strengthen the bonds between the cultures through a passion for cuisine.

blocks.section: Gala Party in Fukuoka : Mathieu Martin shares his Culinary Adventure
blocks.text: Gourmets can expect to see the influences of this adventure in Mathieu Martin's future creations, as he continues to push the boundaries of culinary creativity around the world.

title: GEODIS becomes Official Freight Carrier of Rugby World Cup France 2023

blocks.text: Companies news

blocks.section: GEODIS becomes Official Freight Carrier of Rugby World Cup France 2023
blocks.text: GEODIS becomes Official Freight Carrier of Rugby World Cup France 2023

blocks.section: GEODIS becomes Official Freight Carrier of Rugby World Cup France 2023
blocks.text: The France 2023 Organising Committee has announced that GEODIS, a global leading transport and logistics provider, has been appointed as Official Freight Carrier of the tournament. GEODIS has therefore committed to provide bespoke logistics services with the target of having the lowest possible impact on the environment.

blocks.section: GEODIS becomes Official Freight Carrier of Rugby World Cup France 2023
blocks.text: Drawing on its expertise, worldwide capabilities and infrastructure, GEODIS will be responsible for ensuring the efficient management of approximately 80 tons of equipment for the 20 participating nations. It will also meet the logistical needs of the thousands of volunteers involved throughout the tournament. GEODIS will be fully dedicated to the seamless delivery of this major international sporting event, across nine stadiums in 10 French host cities.

blocks.section: GEODIS becomes Official Freight Carrier of Rugby World Cup France 2023
blocks.text: In accordance with the Group's ambition to continuously reduce its CO 2 emissions by 2030, GEODIS will use low-carbon vehicles to achieve its mission. GEODIS is already committed to deploying such fleets in roughly 40 French cities between now and 2024.

blocks.section: GEODIS becomes Official Freight Carrier of Rugby World Cup France 2023
blocks.text: Claude Atcher, France 2023 CEO, said: “From the start of the France 2023 project, we made our responsibility clear: to organise an event capable of minimising its impact on the environment, notably through the help of its partners. We are happy to share this ambition with GEODIS, a company that is both experienced in delivering international sporting events and committed to tackling environmental issues within its industry. We will work together to make Rugby World Cup 2023 a sustainable event, aligned with societal challenges of today and tomorrow.”

blocks.section: GEODIS becomes Official Freight Carrier of Rugby World Cup France 2023
blocks.text: Marie-Christine Lombard, GEODIS CEO, said: “I am proud that GEODIS has been entrusted with the critical mission of being the Official Freight Carrier of Rugby World Cup France 2023. Team spirit, integrity, passion, discipline and respect are all values that characterise this sport and that we share at GEODIS. As the CEO of a French-rooted yet truly international group, I am excited for our teams to play a part in an event that brings so many people together and that gives France the opportunity to shine at an international level."

blocks.section: GEODIS becomes Official Freight Carrier of Rugby World Cup France 2023

title: GIFAS and Aeromart: Strengthening aerospace industries ties between Europe and Japan
description:
On September 26, 2023, the CCIFJ organized a private meeting in Nagoya for GIFAS, the French Aerospace Industry Association, as an introduction to the Aeromart Nagoya. It was also the occasion to meet Sylvain Four, Director for European and International Affairs for GIFAS in France, who was with us for the occasion. The meeting took place at the Nagoya Chamber of Commerce and Industry, which was kind enough to provide one of its conference halls as part of our on-going collaboration with them.
GIFAS is the French Aerospace Industry Association, bringing together over 400 companies specializing in the design, development, production, marketing and maintenance of all civil and military aerospace programs and equipment, as well as organizations from the French administration. They also organize the Paris Air Show, the world's largest air show, held every two years in Paris.
We had an insightful meeting, where each participant discussed the possibilities to develop better relations with Japanese aerospace actors. The session began with several in depth presentations of the current situation, after which the discussion focused on solutions to involve Japanese companies and administrations further, particularly through the organization of more impactful events.

blocks.text: The meeting was followed by a cocktail reception at the CCIFJ Business Center in Nagoya, a golden opportunity for CCIFJ Chūbu and Kansai members of the sector to exchange business cards with French aerospace public and private representatives , but also a more relaxed environment for friendly discussions and more informal information exchanges.

blocks.text: Participants in this event included representatives from the following entities: Airbus Defense and Space, Air Liquide, Daher, Fives Group, Safran, Thales, as well as the Directorate General for Civil Aviation (subordinate to the Ministry of Ecology, Sustainable Development and Energy), the French Embassy in Japan and Business France.

title: Gontran Cherrier opens 2nd store in Japan on October 4th, located in Shinjuku, and starts an opening campaign!
description:
Meitetsu Kyosho Corporation (Head office: Nakamura-ku, Nagoya; Representative Director: Masahiro Kobayashi) will open its second bakery in Japan, the Gontran Cherrier Shinjuku store, on October 4th, 2022. The new bakery will be located in the Shinjuku Odakyu Department Store (Shinjuku West Exit Halc 1F), which will be reopening on the same day. The bakery’s opening campaign will start at the same time.

Following the opening of its first store at Aoyama in July 2021, this new Shinjuku store will specialize in takeout under the concept of “Mr. Gontran Cherrier's small store” (Le petit magasin de M. Gontran Cherrier). This new store will offer quality and freshly made breads, such as its’ signature croissant, to passersby in the station.
 Detail of the campaign
The coupons are available at Gontran Cherrier’s Aoyama & Shinjuku store will be distributed as following:  【About the coupon】
１．Period of distribution ：From October 4th, 2022 to October 10th, 2022
２．Distribution store ： Gontran Cherrier Aoyama & Shinjuku
３．Distribution target ： Customers making purchases at the Shinjuku and Aoyama Gontran Cherrier’s stores (the first 150 customers each day)
※An original eco bag will come with the coupon if the total amount is more than 2000 yen.
４．Contents of coupon ：In exchange for the coupon, we offer either an kouign-amann, a croissant or a pain au chocolat and a cup of coffee (hot or cold) from October 15th, 2022  to January 31st, 2023

 About Gontran Cherrier Shinjuku store
 	Address：Odakyu Shinjuku 1st Floor　1-5-1, Nishi-Shinjuku, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo 160-0023 	Surface：31.13 ㎡ 	Business style：Bakery with drinks to go ※No eat-in space available 	Opening day：October 4th, 10am　※ Simultaneously with the reopening of Odakyu Shinjuku 	Time table：7:30am - 8:30pm（until 8pm on Sundays and holidays） 	Close：New Year Holiday season 	WEB site：http://gontrancherrier.jp/ 	Instagram：https://www.instagram.com/gontrancherrierjp/ 


 Biography of Gontran Cherrier
A 4th generation baker from Normandy, France. After graduating from a culinary school, he worked at the 3 stars restaurants L'arpège and Lucas Carton in Paris, before opening his own bakery.
With a desire to bring real bread around the world, he has opened his own bakery, Gontran Cherrier, in several countries. After temporarily withdrawing from the Japanese market in 2017, he re-launched a bakery in Aoyama, Tokyo in 2021 with Meitetsu Kyosho as a partner.  
Opening his first store in Montmartre, Paris（2010）
Selected as one of the 10 best bakeries in Japan（2014）
Host of the TV program The Best Bakery In France（2013-2016）     
4th prize for the best baguette in Paris（2017）
Selected one of the top 10 croissants in Paris by Vogue（2019）
Re-launching of Gontran Cherrier’s bakery in Aoyama, Tokyo（2021） ※ Author of 9 books. Currently operating about 60 stores in more than 10 countries.  

Public Relations Office, Meitetsu Kyosho Corporation TEL: 052-582-1011to Mawaki, Shibata

title: Good start for the First Kansai Business Summit!
description: The Evolution of Supply Chains after the Covid pandemic: a rich subject for our first Kansai Business Summit, with over 50 people in attendance.

blocks.text: Kansai Event report Supply chain

blocks.section: Good start for the First Kansai Business Summit!
blocks.text: Good start for the First Kansai Business Summit!

blocks.section: Good start for the First Kansai Business Summit!
blocks.text: The Evolution of Supply Chains after the Covid pandemic: a rich subject for our first Kansai Business Summit, with over 50 people in attendance.

blocks.section: Good start for the First Kansai Business Summit!
blocks.text: One year in the planning, but finally! On October 4 , 2023, our very own Kansai Business Summit was held in a conference room with a great (and rather fitting) view over the harbor district, on the 29th floor of the Kansai Economic Federation building in Nakanoshima .

blocks.section: Good start for the First Kansai Business Summit!
blocks.text: This event was put together thanks to the sponsorships of Dassault Systems (main) and Kuehne+Nagel (secondary). Our co-organizer, the KanKeiRen (Kansai Economic Federation), also played a crucial role in providing and preparing the conference room, in order to accommodate the crowd of over 50 participants who had registered. It is to be noted that many people from the ACCJ (American Chamber of Commerce) in Kansai were also present, thanks to this partner’s undying involvement at our side.

blocks.section: Good start for the First Kansai Business Summit!
blocks.text: The event started at 3 pm. After a short introduction by the CCIFJ, it was Mr. Takeshi Inoue (井上 剛志), Director of International Affairs at the KanKeiRen, who opened the event in earnest with a vibrant homage to international collaborations. The keynote speech was then delivered by Mr Shinichirō Kohno , Managing Director, Industry X Engineering & Manufacturing Lead at Accenture , to introduce the theme at hand: Evolution of Logistics and Supply Chain Automation in the Post-Covid Era .

blocks.section: Good start for the First Kansai Business Summit!
blocks.text: To better cover it, our five speakers explored it through each of their own specialties: Ms. Misuzu Maruyama (丸山 美鈴), General Manager Sales and Marketing at Kuehne+Nagel focused on sea transport and international aspects . Mr. Kazuto Tada (多田 和人), Manager, Customer Service Japan & Korea at Air France KLM Cargo focused on air transport . Mr. Hayato Shingu (新宮 早人), General Manager, Head of Aero Commercial Department at Kansai Airports developed the infrastructural point of view with an insight on the logistics environment at an airport. Then Mr. Yoshihiro Maruyama (丸山 義弘), Osaka Branch General Manager at Nippon Express , covered the ground transportation and warehouse management aspects. To conclude, Mr. Kohno from Accenture brought the whole theme together with a severe analysis of Japan’s falling behind on digitalization and the necessity to consider “ hyper-automation ” to optimize the whole chain, with a shift from a vertical organization to a fully automated network, in order to increase flexibility and adaptability.

blocks.section: Good start for the First Kansai Business Summit!
blocks.text: A Q&A was supposed to take place after the conference, but due to some oversights in time-management, the speeches were longer than expected and that part had to be cut in order to save enough time for people to network in the end.

blocks.section: Good start for the First Kansai Business Summit!
blocks.text: For those who want to learn more and can read Japanese (or have a good translator), the Daily Cargo published a full report of the event on page 11 of their n°13159 (October 10).

blocks.section: Good start for the First Kansai Business Summit!
blocks.text: That networking session finally allowed all participants to get to know each other and to exchange freely around a few tables filled with French delicacies, such as pâté en croûte, rillettes and quiches.

blocks.section: Good start for the First Kansai Business Summit!
blocks.text: On the drinks side, our member Jupiter international was kind enough to provide an abundance of Perrier bottles, after already supplying an equal amount of Contrex bottles for the conference.

blocks.section: Good start for the First Kansai Business Summit!
blocks.text: The company Focus from Nagano also provided an impressive draft beer machine, which delivered a quality craft beer imported straight from Europe. It was particularly appreciated by some of our German friends.

blocks.section: Good start for the First Kansai Business Summit!
blocks.text: Draft beer "Licorne" by Focus

blocks.section: Good start for the First Kansai Business Summit!
blocks.text: This was our first edition, and there sure is some room for improvement, but all parts involved did an incredible job to make this event worthy. We are very much looking forward to collaborating again next year!

title: Government calls for “25,000 foreign drivers” in the automotive sector
description: Due to the aging population, the Japanese government is now opening up the automotive sector to foreign labor.

blocks.text: Foresight

blocks.section: Government calls for “25,000 foreign drivers” in the automotive sector
blocks.text: Government calls for “25,000 foreign drivers” in the automotive sector

blocks.section: Government calls for “25,000 foreign drivers” in the automotive sector
blocks.text: Due to the aging population, the Japanese government is now opening up the automotive sector to foreign labor.

blocks.section: Government calls for “25,000 foreign drivers” in the automotive sector
blocks.text: Faced with labor shortages and a reduction in overtime for truck drivers , the Japanese government relaxed the conditions for accepting foreign workers on March 29.

blocks.section: Government calls for “25,000 foreign drivers” in the automotive sector
blocks.text: The “2024 problem” refers to the reduction of overtime for truck drivers, which could lead to a shortage of personnel in the transport and logistics sectors. The government is therefore seeking to alleviate this shortage by bringing in foreign drivers.

blocks.section: Government calls for “25,000 foreign drivers” in the automotive sector
blocks.text: Over the next five years, the motor transport industry as a whole (including buses and cabs) will accept up to 24,500 foreign drivers . However, this may not be enough, as the transport sector will be short of almost 200,000 drivers - efforts to find drivers domestically will also remain paramount.

blocks.section: Government calls for “25,000 foreign drivers” in the automotive sector
blocks.text: Despite these coming shortages, the number of foreign nationals is fixed every five years under the existence of a specified skills system, which came into being in 2019.

blocks.section: Government calls for “25,000 foreign drivers” in the automotive sector
blocks.text: This is divided into two categories: specific skills number 1, which require a “considerable degree of knowledge or experience” and a period of residence not exceeding five years; and specific skills number 2, which require “qualified skills” based on years of professional experience.

blocks.section: Government calls for “25,000 foreign drivers” in the automotive sector
blocks.text: The recruitment of truck drivers falls into the first category.

title: Great success for the 4 Chambers Spring Meet & Greet in Kobe!
description: Resounding success for the Spring Meet & Greet: 4 Chambers of Commerce and nearly 150 participants, including 30 from the French Chamber!

blocks.text: Kansai Event report

blocks.section: Great success for the 4 Chambers Spring Meet & Greet in Kobe!
blocks.text: Great success for the 4 Chambers Spring Meet & Greet in Kobe!

blocks.section: Great success for the 4 Chambers Spring Meet & Greet in Kobe!
blocks.text: Resounding success for the Spring Meet & Greet: 4 Chambers of Commerce and nearly 150 participants, including 30 from the French Chamber!

blocks.section: Great success for the 4 Chambers Spring Meet & Greet in Kobe!
blocks.text: After having successfully organized the previous Spring Meet & Greet alongside the American Chamber of Commerce in Japan (ACCJ) , and the Kobe Chamber of Commerce and Industry (KCCI) , we were pleased to add the German Chamber of Commerce in Japan (AHK) to this fruitful collaboration.

blocks.section: Great success for the 4 Chambers Spring Meet & Greet in Kobe!
blocks.text: The most enthusiastic ones came from 6pm, and 30 minutes after we started welcoming our guests to the sumptuous 4th floor of the Kobe Oriental Hotel . The setting immediately captivated all the participants.

blocks.section: Great success for the 4 Chambers Spring Meet & Greet in Kobe!
blocks.text: The event was a resounding success , far surpassing the attendance of the previous year with nearly 150 participants in this edition (70 for the ACCJ, 33 for the KCCI, 30 for the CCIFJ, and 16 for the AHK), compared to around a hundred in 2023. This figure could not have been exceeded solely due to space limitations, and unfortunately, we even had to turn down several late registrations. This turnout reflects the enthusiasm that this international Meet & Greet format generates within our communities , definitively burying the dark hours of COVID.

blocks.section: Great success for the 4 Chambers Spring Meet & Greet in Kobe!
blocks.text: Rain stopped luckily at the beginning of the evening, giving us the opportunity to fully enjoy the outdoor space adjacent to the reception hall.

blocks.section: Great success for the 4 Chambers Spring Meet & Greet in Kobe!
blocks.text: The evening kicked off with inspiring speeches from several personalities representing each of the Chambers, namely: - Mr. Jiro KAWAKAMI , Vice President of the Kansai Chapter of the ACCJ and Vice President/Chief of Staff at MGM Resorts Japan LLC; - Mr. Benoit RULLEAU , Board Member of the CCIFJ and Representative Director/Co-General Manager of Kansai Airport ; - Ms. Kimiko ITO , Vice President of the KCCI and Representative Director of Tashima & Co., Ltd. ; - Mr. Felix VON HELDEN , Head of Member Relations Department at the AHK.

blocks.section: Great success for the 4 Chambers Spring Meet & Greet in Kobe!
blocks.text: Their speeches emphasized the crucial importance of international solidarity , especially in the current geopolitical context.

blocks.section: Great success for the 4 Chambers Spring Meet & Greet in Kobe!
blocks.text: Among our distinguished guests, we had the honor of also welcoming the presence of Mr. Jason CUBAS , Consul General of the United States of America , who graciously concluded the speeches by presiding over the traditional Kampai .

blocks.section: Great success for the 4 Chambers Spring Meet & Greet in Kobe!
blocks.text: The party truly began with the networking "Meet & Greet" ! In between visits to the buffet, exchanging business cards multiplied, discussions flowed freely, and everyone had the opportunity to reconnect with old contacts or meet new ones .

blocks.section: Great success for the 4 Chambers Spring Meet & Greet in Kobe!
blocks.text: We know that two hours are not enough to truly get around to all the guests, but that is the game . The conversations were so lively that, as always, it was difficult to bring them to an end, and it was the hotel staff who finally had to push us towards the exit.

blocks.section: Great success for the 4 Chambers Spring Meet & Greet in Kobe!
blocks.text: We are extremely proud of the success of this edition, and we hope you enjoyed it as much as we did. See you next year for an even more ambitious Spring Meet & Greet?

blocks.section: Ground breaking ceremony for the France Pavilion at Expo 2025
blocks.text: The groundbreaking ceremony took place in the presence of Minister Franck Riester on Yumeshima Island on Tuesday, April 23, 2024.

blocks.section: Ground breaking ceremony for the France Pavilion at Expo 2025
blocks.text: Less than a year before the Osaka 2025 World Expo , a decisive milestone has been reached with the start of construction on the French Pavilion . This symbolic moment, taking place on Yumeshima Island , was marked by the inaugural act of Mr. Franck RIESTER , Minister Delegate in charge of Foreign Trade, Attractiveness, Francophonie, and French Nationals Abroad.

blocks.section: Ground breaking ceremony for the France Pavilion at Expo 2025
blocks.text: The ceremony began at 10 am with speeches by Mr. Jacques MAIRE , President of Cofrex and Commissioner General of the France Pavilion, followed by Mr. Hideyuki YOKOYAMA (横山 英幸), Mayor of Osaka , Mr. Ono HEIHACHIRŌ (小野 平八郎), and finally Mr. Franck RIESTER.

blocks.section: Ground breaking ceremony for the France Pavilion at Expo 2025
blocks.text: The construction kickoff, symbolized by the traditional "Sei… no! Hei hei hei!", marked the official start of the France Pavilion Expo 2025 project.

blocks.section: Ground breaking ceremony for the France Pavilion at Expo 2025
blocks.text: From left to right: Mr. Thomas Coldefy, architect; Mr. Philippe Setton, Ambassador of France to Japan; Mr. Ono Heihachiro, Deputy Secretary General of the Japan Association for the 2025 World Expo; Mr. Franck Riester, Minister Delegate in charge of Foreign Trade, Attractiveness, Francophonie, and French Nationals Abroad; Mr. Yokoyama Hideyuki, Mayor of Osaka; Mr. Jacques Maire, Commissioner General of the French section at Expo 2025 Osaka Kansai; Mr. Tsutomu Himeno, Representative of the Government and Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary for Kansai, Ministry of Foreign Affairs; Mr. Giuseppe Chiaranda, President of Rimond.

blocks.section: Ground breaking ceremony for the France Pavilion at Expo 2025
blocks.text: Following this event, Mr. Thomas COLDEFY , architect and co-founder of Coldefy & Associés Architectes Urbanistes , Mr. Maire, and Mr. Franck Riester answered media questions during a Q&A session.

blocks.section: Ground breaking ceremony for the France Pavilion at Expo 2025
blocks.text: This event brought together a significant number of leading political and economic figures, including Mr. Seiji YASUBUCHI (安渕 聖司), Representative Director of Axa Japan ; Mr. Kazushige SAKIYAMA (崎山 一茂), Vice President of Bureau Veritas ; Ms. Celine TAKIZAWA (滝澤 セリーヌ) of Mazars ; Mr. Malik ROUMANE , President of MCDecaux ; and Mr. Philippe SETTON , France Ambassador .

blocks.section: Ground breaking ceremony for the France Pavilion at Expo 2025
blocks.text: Among the notable attendees, the presence of Mr. Norbert LEURET , Vice President of the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan and President of LVMH Japan , as a Gold partner of the Pavilion, underscores the company's commitment to this major international event.

title: Grunberger Diamonds, the resilience of diamonds
description:
Company Presentation Grunberger Diamonds is a fourth-generation diamond manufacturer from Antwerp, specialized in Ideal Cut diamonds with Hearts and Arrows.
Known in the diamond trade as having the best cut melee diamond in the world, they offer their “Grunberger Precison Cut”™️ in many different sizes and qualities. The fire and brightness of each of their stones is something you can see and experience for yourself: seeing is believing! All our diamonds are certified conflict free and are fully traceable.
In the past couple years, Grunberger Diamonds Japan has also been involved in developing jewelry for other companies and recently by creating its own brand: Grunberger Jewels. GJ offers high end engagement and wedding bands as well as custom made designs.
With their inhouse designer they can create original and unique jewelry pieces adapting ourselves to all of their customers’ needs.

title: Harnessing Renewable Energy in the Food & Beverage Industry: A Recap of the Latest TotalEnergies Webinar
description:
TotalEnergies ENEOS recently hosted the webinar “Harnessing Renewable Energy in the Food & Beverage Industry”, which attracted more than 70 attendees. The event focused on the challenges faced by the F&B and FMCG industries in decarbonizing their operations and adopting more sustainable energy solutions.
Their expert speakers shared valuable insights, covering key topics such as: - ? How green electricity can significantly reduce emissions in the F&B sector - ? The business benefits of adopting sustainable energy solutions - ? TotalEnergies' expertise across the energy value chain, offering tailored solutions for the sector  A special thank you to Raditya Pramudiantoro from Danone, who shared the company’s inspiring efforts in decarbonizing their operations in Indonesia, and to Sharon Goh and Rachel Sarah-Ann Toh for their expert analysis of the challenges and opportunities that lie ahead for the F&B industry on its path to achieving Net Zero.  If you missed the event, don't worry! You can still access the full discussion on-demand
To explore how TotalEnergies ENEOS can help your company decarbonize, feel free to contact them directly for more information.
You can find more information on their Linkedin Page.

title: Health, Well-being, and Nutrition at the Morikawa Salon 2025
description: The Morikawa Salon welcomed a small group of guests on Thursday evening for an intimate and elegant gathering dedicated to well-being. Inspired bu the charm of 18th century salons, the event offered a unique opportunity to re-discover the services of the Morikawa Clinic while enjoying a refined moment of French-style relaxation.

blocks.text: Kansai Event report

blocks.section: Health, Well-being, and Nutrition at the Morikawa Salon 2025
blocks.text: Health, Well-being, and Nutrition at the Morikawa Salon 2025

blocks.section: Health, Well-being, and Nutrition at the Morikawa Salon 2025
blocks.text: The Morikawa Salon welcomed a small group of guests on Thursday evening for an intimate and elegant gathering dedicated to well-being. Inspired bu the charm of 18th century salons, the event offered a unique opportunity to re-discover the services of the Morikawa Clinic while enjoying a refined moment of French-style relaxation.

blocks.section: Health, Well-being, and Nutrition at the Morikawa Salon 2025
blocks.text: Morikawa Clinic, founder of the Medical Corporation Koujinkai group , has for several years embraced a holistic approach to well-being, combining medical care, nutritional guidance, and personalized support. The evening highlighted this philosophy in a spirit of warmth, sharing and conviviality.

blocks.section: Health, Well-being, and Nutrition at the Morikawa Salon 2025
blocks.text: The event was opened by the CCIFJ , who welcomed the guests. The floor was then given to Ms. Morikawa and Mr. Yasuhara , who both spoke on topics related to health, lifestyle, and nutrition. As in previous years, their talks were marked by clarity, kindness, and practical insight. Mr. Yasuhara in particular emphasized the importance of prevention and anticipation in maintaining daily health. Adopting healthy eating habits, staying active, and being mindful of one's lifestyle can significantly reduce the need for more intensive medical treatments. As the saying goes: prevention is better than cure.

blocks.section: Health, Well-being, and Nutrition at the Morikawa Salon 2025
blocks.text: The discussions were engaging, and the guests very mindful, showing genuine interest in the accessible and actionable advice shared throughout the evening.

blocks.section: Health, Well-being, and Nutrition at the Morikawa Salon 2025
blocks.text: The evening continued around a warming french-style dinner, set in a unique space adorned with antiques and inspired by french salons. On the menu: Basque-style chicken, ratatouille, gratin dauphinois, marinated shrimp and vegetables, quiche, pork rillettes, french cheese, gâteau au chocolate with crème anglais, and financiers. A true culinary journey that was met with great enthusiasm and offered guests a chance to connect more deeply with one another.

blocks.section: Health, Well-being, and Nutrition at the Morikawa Salon 2025
blocks.text: Between exchanges, new discoveries and delicious tastings, this evening at the Morikawa Salon offered in this busy daily life a needed break. A human-scale event, true to the spirit of the clinic: promoting health, listening and quality of life.

title: Congratulations to Miyawaki Baisen’an for their 200 years!
description:
2 centuries of activity, it is something. In France as well as in Japan, a traditional craft’s longevity is something we value deeply. Craftsmanship rooted in decades of practice, in history and tradition, it is what produces a unique touch.
Our member Miyawaki Baisen’an of Kyoto is one of those guardians and makers of an ancient art, and at a time when the annoying insect-like whirr of small electric plastic personal ventilators are buzzing our ears all summer, Baisen’an prefers to promote the majestic flap of a wooden fan’s wing. Flowers, plants, birds, fishes and other geometrical shapes are common designs, and those are drawn individually by the hand of a master, making each piece a unique work of art.
One of those masters is the talented Ayuko Sadaie, who's floral designs will be displayed exclusively from May 19 to May 30, 2023 at Baisen'an's Kyoto main shop, with the support of local CCIFJ Ambassador Seishirō Hayashi, as a celebration for its 200th anniversary. 200 years of perseverance, dedication and transmission of rare skills.
If you come by Kyoto, make sure to visit their shop.

blocks.section: Higher starting salaries in Japan
blocks.text: As prices continue to rise in Japan, many companies are increasing their starting salaries to recruit new graduates .

blocks.section: Higher starting salaries in Japan
blocks.text: 50% of member companies of the Japan Chamber of Commerce and Industry reported that they had increased their salaries . Salary increases are being implemented across a wide range of sectors, from airlines and retail, including Lawson.

title: HORIBA acquires South Korea’s EtaMax to strengthen semiconductor business
description:
HORIBA Group, through its subsidiary HORIBA STEC Korea, has completed the acquisition of South Korean company EtaMax, based in Suwon. EtaMax specializes in wafer inspection systems for the compound semiconductor market.
The company develops equipment using photoluminescence technology to detect microscopic defects and assess wafer uniformity — a key process in the production of next-generation power semiconductors, widely used in electric vehicles and data centers.
With this acquisition, HORIBA aims to integrate its own spectroscopic technologies, such as Raman spectroscopy and ellipsometry, with EtaMax’s software expertise to offer more advanced inspection solutions. The goal is to improve production yields and strengthen quality control for compound semiconductors.
This strategic move aligns with HORIBA’s MLMAP 2028 management plan, which targets ¥235 billion in sales by 2028 in the advanced materials and semiconductor field.

description: HORIBA Medical et le CEA-Leti poursuivent leur partenariat pour développer le diagnostic de demain, au lit du patient.

blocks.text: Companies news

blocks.section: HORIBA Medical and CEA-Leti Strengthen Their Partnership to Develop Tomorrow’s Diagnostics at the Point of Care
blocks.text: HORIBA Medical and CEA-Leti Strengthen Their Partnership to Develop Tomorrow’s Diagnostics at the Point of Care

blocks.section: HORIBA Medical and CEA-Leti Strengthen Their Partnership to Develop Tomorrow’s Diagnostics at the Point of Care
blocks.text: HORIBA Medical et le CEA-Leti poursuivent leur partenariat pour développer le diagnostic de demain, au lit du patient.

blocks.section: HORIBA Medical and CEA-Leti Strengthen Their Partnership to Develop Tomorrow’s Diagnostics at the Point of Care
blocks.text: HORIBA Medical, a subsidiary of Japan-based HORIBA Group, the global leader for measurement and analysis systems, has been designing, manufacturing and marketing high performance analyzers for laboratories and hospitals for over 30 years. This expertise that has made the company one of the world leaders in Hematology and a key player in the Hemostasis and Clinical Chemistry activity.

blocks.section: HORIBA Medical and CEA-Leti Strengthen Their Partnership to Develop Tomorrow’s Diagnostics at the Point of Care
blocks.text: Today, patient care and treatment practices are evolving quickly. HORIBA Medical is designing solutions to anticipate patient-centered needs by developing new POCT (Point of Care Testing) systems.

blocks.section: HORIBA Medical and CEA-Leti Strengthen Their Partnership to Develop Tomorrow’s Diagnostics at the Point of Care
blocks.text: In parallel, for the past six years HORIBA Medical has been working with one of the most innovative organizations in the field of new technologies, CEA-Leti, the technology research laboratory of CEA Tech, federating their respective skills in a Joint Laboratory called HEMACOUNT.

blocks.section: HORIBA Medical and CEA-Leti Strengthen Their Partnership to Develop Tomorrow’s Diagnostics at the Point of Care
blocks.text: “We focused on two disruptive technologies: a microfluidic cartridge and a new, lens-free imaging device (LensFree), which will enable development of more compact, easier-to-use POCT-type devices,” says Damien Isebe, who heads up this highly innovative project at HORIBA Medical. “Twelve families of patents have been filed since the start of the project, and the latest one has been the subject of several scientific papers”.

blocks.section: HORIBA Medical and CEA-Leti Strengthen Their Partnership to Develop Tomorrow’s Diagnostics at the Point of Care
blocks.text: “Flow cytometry is the main analytical technology in hematology, but it requires large and complex hardware systems. Conversely, lens-free imaging combined with a sample prepared as a microfluidic cartridge paves the way to a simple and compact disruptive architecture. This imaging technique provides a wide field of view (≈30mm²) resulting in a counting statistic (a few thousand cells) in one single acquisition consistent with required hematological performance,” explains Sophie Morales, laboratory head at CEA-Leti.

blocks.section: HORIBA Medical and CEA-Leti Strengthen Their Partnership to Develop Tomorrow’s Diagnostics at the Point of Care
blocks.text: The latest publications and presentations to date: for LensFree, one publication in the Journal of Biomedical Optics and two oral presentations at ECBO (European Conferences on Biomedical Optics), held in Munich in late June 2019; and for the work on microfluidics, presentation of a scientific poster at µTAS (International Conference on Miniaturized Systems for Chemistry and Life Sciences) in Basel, Switzerland, in October 2019.

title: Hotel prices in Japan to rise by 25% between 2022 and 2023
description: The end of health restrictions and the upturn in tourism have had an impact on accommodation prices.

blocks.text: Foresight

blocks.section: Hotel prices in Japan to rise by 25% between 2022 and 2023
blocks.text: Hotel prices in Japan to rise by 25% between 2022 and 2023

blocks.section: Hotel prices in Japan to rise by 25% between 2022 and 2023
blocks.text: The end of health restrictions and the upturn in tourism have had an impact on accommodation prices.

blocks.section: Hotel prices in Japan to rise by 25% between 2022 and 2023
blocks.text: The price of hotel rooms in Japan in 2023 rose by more than 25% compared with 2022 , according to the latest Consumer Price Index report published by the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications. This increase is attributed to the lifting of health restrictions and the low yen rates that have led to a strong recovery in tourism since 2023.

blocks.section: Hotel prices in Japan to rise by 25% between 2022 and 2023
blocks.text: According to Takuto Yasuda, researcher at the Nissay Research Institute : “With the end of the Corona and the significant upturn in demand, there is a shortage of staff. Wages have had to be increased in order to acquire labor, and prices are being passed on to hotel bills. There is also a tendency to pass on increased costs due to higher prices to hotel bills .”

blocks.section: Hotel prices in Japan to rise by 25% between 2022 and 2023
blocks.text: The end of the pandemic, the significant upturn in demand and the shortage of manpower in Japan are also having an impact on hotels, which are having to spend money on renovations.

blocks.section: Hotel prices in Japan to rise by 25% between 2022 and 2023
blocks.text: Japan-wide, the impact is also being felt on “business travel.” Many companies are having to increase their flat-rate accommodation costs for employee travel.

title: Hotel Toranomon Hills debuts as Tokyo’s first hotel within the unbound collection by Hyatt Portfolio
description:
Situated at the heart of the dynamic Toranomon Hills global business hub, the hotel serves as an urban launchpad offering bleisure travelers comfort, convenience and cosmopolitan cuisine.
Hyatt Hotels Corporation (NYSE: H) announced today the opening of Hotel Toranomon Hills as the first property in Tokyo under The Unbound Collection by Hyatt brand. Situated in the heart of Tokyo, the hotel is located within the new Toranomon Hills Station Tower in Toranomon Hills, the ever-evolving integrated development and global business hub by Mori Building Co., Ltd. Hotel Toranomon Hills is poised to become an urban launchpad for cosmopolitan professionals and travelers with its comfortable and purposefully designed spaces for seamless transitions between rest, work and socializing.
“We are honored to join hands once again with Mori Building Co., Ltd. and Mori Hospitality Corporation to launch a new brand – this time The Unbound Collection by Hyatt – in Tokyo. We are grateful for their trust and collaboration to be included in the transformative Toranomon Hills project from the beginning, starting with our Andaz brand nearly 10 years ago, and coming full circle with the highly anticipated opening of Hotel Toranomon Hills,” said David Udell, group president, Asia Pacific, Hyatt. “The Unbound Collection by Hyatt portfolio is a compilation of one-of-a-kind hotels that inspire stories worth collecting. We are excited to have these hotels at the center of all that Toranomon Hills has to offer as they set the stage for our guests to discover energizing experiences, including immersive culinary moments at Le Pristine Tokyo.”
“Over the years, Mori Building has collaborated with Hyatt on Grand Hyatt Tokyo, Andaz Tokyo Toranomon Hills, and Park Hyatt Shanghai. Through these joint projects aimed at delivering top-quality hospitality, Mori Building and Hyatt have formed a relationship of deep trust. We are now delighted to announce the opening of Hotel Toranomon Hills, featuring unique character and one-of-a-kind charm as the second hotel in Toranomon Hills. With this opening, the Toranomon Hills complex will continue to expand and evolve as an international hub and global business center, further contributing to Tokyo's international competitiveness,” said Shingo Tsuji, President and Representative Director of Mori Building Co., Ltd.
At the crossroads of Japan’s full-fledged international hub and global business center and conveniently located in central Tokyo with easy access to shopping and entertainment hubs such as Ginza and Roppongi, the hotel caters to the growing trend of “bleisure travel” where business travel is combined with leisure. The hotel is within walking distance of the iconic Imperial Palace, around 30 minutes by car from Haneda International Airport, and connected directly to Toranomon Hills subway station on the Hibiya Line via Toranomon Hills Station
Tower. Toranomon Hills Station Tower is home to TOKYO NODE, which includes a presentation/performance hall, art galleries and other facilities on the top floors, and a commercial facility with approximately 70 stores and restaurants on the lower floors.
Comfort-first, minimalist spaces with purposeful design 
Hotel Toranomon Hills marks the Japan debut of Space Copenhagen, a leading Danish design studio. The timeless, minimalist interiors draw inspiration from Danish and Japanese aesthetics to create relaxing spaces where guests can readily unwind, work and socialize.
Hotel Toranomon Hills offers 205 stylish rooms and suites from which guests can enjoy views of the city or the famed Tokyo Tower. All guestrooms feature NEMOHAMO-brand organic bath amenities and a built-in purified-water hydration station. The hotel’s 30 suites also come with a Japanese-style hot tub for a relaxing soak after a day of meetings or exploration. The two spacious “Toranomon Suite” duplexes, each measuring 1,722 sq. ft. (160 sq. m.), can be used for intimate meetings and private events as well as overnight stays – with a flexible area for meeting, dining and entertaining; a living room; a kitchen on the lower level; and a convertible bedroom and bathroom on the upper level.
Guests staying at the hotel – including those who arrive too early to check in or have late flights to catch – can enjoy exclusive access to The Lounge, a multi-functional space with a lofty six-meter ceiling and dramatic views of Tokyo’s cityscape centered on Tokyo Tower and Toranomon Hills. The Lounge offers flexible spaces for in-person meetings, online business and co-working, as well as practical facilities such as showers, private relaxation areas and complementary refreshments.
Le Pristine Tokyo: Groundbreaking collaboration with Michelin-starred chef 
The immersive casual fine dining restaurant and café, helmed by Sergio Herman, will mark the Asian debut of the acclaimed Dutch chef-entrepreneur as part of a groundbreaking collaboration between Hyatt and the Sergio Herman Group.
Located on the street level of Toranomon Hills Station Tower and leading to the hotel’s reception area, Le Pristine Tokyo will serve contemporary European cuisine with a cosmopolitan flair, using thoughtfully sourced produce from Zeeland in the Netherlands and seasonal Japanese ingredients. Signature dishes such as Salad ‘Le Pristine’ pumpkin, grapefruit, taleggio, endive, hazelnut and Orecchiette Zeelandaise will be prepared with care and panache in the restaurant's open kitchen. The café features a rectangular bar where guests can enjoy tasty temptations such as fresh Japanese seafoods, seasonal pastas and the signature tiramisu, as well as delightful cocktails such as Le Pristine Spritz.
Diners can expect a sophisticated and creative fusion of food, fashion, design, art and music, as well as a laidback vibe on the café’s outdoor terrace during warmer months. The interior, designed by Space Copenhagen, will feature striking art and objets d’art by Dutch and Belgian artists such as Maarten Baas, Rinus van de Velde and Rotganzen.
Sergio Herman will oversee all food and beverage offerings at the hotel including breakfast.

We are excited to have these hotels at the center of all that Toranomon Hills has to offer as they set the stage for our guests to discover energizing experiences, including immersive culinary moments at Le Pristine Tokyo.”

blocks.section: Hotel Toranomon Hills debuts as Tokyo’s first hotel within the unbound collection by Hyatt Portfolio
blocks.text: “Over the years, Mori Building has collaborated with Hyatt on Grand Hyatt Tokyo, Andaz Tokyo Toranomon Hills, and Park Hyatt Shanghai. Through these joint projects aimed at delivering top-quality hospitality, Mori Building and Hyatt have formed a relationship of deep trust. We are now delighted to announce the opening of Hotel Toranomon Hills, featuring unique character and one-of-a-kind charm as the second hotel in Toranomon Hills. With this opening, the Toranomon Hills complex will continue to expand and evolve as an international hub and global business center, further contributing to Tokyo's international competitiveness,” said Shingo Tsuji, President and Representative Director of Mori Building Co., Ltd.

blocks.section: Hotel Toranomon Hills debuts as Tokyo’s first hotel within the unbound collection by Hyatt Portfolio
blocks.text: At the crossroads of Japan’s full-fledged international hub and global business center and conveniently located in central Tokyo with easy access to shopping and entertainment hubs such as Ginza and Roppongi, the hotel caters to the growing trend of “bleisure travel” where business travel is combined with leisure. The hotel is within walking distance of the iconic Imperial Palace, around 30 minutes by car from Haneda International Airport, and connected directly to Toranomon Hills subway station on the Hibiya Line via Toranomon Hills Station

blocks.section: Hotel Toranomon Hills debuts as Tokyo’s first hotel within the unbound collection by Hyatt Portfolio
blocks.text: Hotel Toranomon Hills marks the Japan debut of Space Copenhagen, a leading Danish design studio. The timeless, minimalist interiors draw inspiration from Danish and Japanese aesthetics to create relaxing spaces where guests can readily unwind, work and socialize.

blocks.section: Hotel Toranomon Hills debuts as Tokyo’s first hotel within the unbound collection by Hyatt Portfolio
blocks.text: Hotel Toranomon Hills offers 205 stylish rooms and suites from which guests can enjoy views of the city or the famed Tokyo Tower. All guestrooms feature NEMOHAMO-brand organic bath amenities and a built-in purified-water hydration station. The hotel’s 30 suites also come with a Japanese-style hot tub for a relaxing soak after a day of meetings or exploration. The two spacious “Toranomon Suite” duplexes, each measuring 1,722 sq. ft. (160 sq. m.), can be used for intimate meetings and private events as well as overnight stays – with a flexible area for meeting, dining and entertaining; a living room; a kitchen on the lower level; and a convertible bedroom and bathroom on the upper level.

blocks.text: Guests staying at the hotel – including those who arrive too early to check in or have late flights to catch – can enjoy exclusive access to The Lounge, a multi-functional space with a lofty six-meter ceiling and dramatic views of Tokyo’s cityscape centered on Tokyo Tower and Toranomon Hills. The Lounge offers flexible spaces for in-person meetings, online business and co-working, as well as practical facilities such as showers, private relaxation areas and complementary refreshments.

The café features a rectangular bar where guests can enjoy tasty temptations such as fresh Japanese seafoods, seasonal pastas and the signature tiramisu, as well as delightful cocktails such as Le Pristine Spritz .

title: Hummingbag : reusable bags in the land of disposable packaging
description:
Hummingbag designs and manufactures reusable bags made from recyclable materials, tailored to its clients’ needs. The company, based in Hong Kong, decided to enter the Japanese market after a first trip to Tokyo in 2011 : “We were told that it would be difficult to sell bags in Japan, that our product did not offer enough added value. When we arrived, we immediately noticed the following : bags are mostly intended for single use and are not aesthetic at all. We therefore decided to take our chance.”
In 2012, Hummingbag took part in the Tokyo International Gift Show. There, Cécile Chaigneau, Head of Sales, met the Seijo Ishi group, with whom Hummingbag signed its first sale four months later. Building on this experience, Hummingbag turned to CCI France Japan to structure its development project: “We found a few clients through our website, but our direct prospecting, without a real command of Japanese and above all without being introduced, led to nothing. We then heard that CCI France Japan could help us save a great deal of time.”
In 2014, after two months of preparation, the team from the Business Support Service of CCI France Japan organized a series of meetings for Hummingbag with fifteen Japanese companies, including major agri food distributors and firms specialized in events and communication. “I realize how important it is to come and meet your counterparts in Japan. We are not the only ones manufacturing this type of bag, but we arrived at the right time and met the right people. Without CCI France Japan, we probably would not have been able to move forward so quickly”, explains Cécile Chaigneau.
The connection was particularly strong with CGC. This group, a cooperative serving gourmet grocery chains and Japanese supermarkets, has outlets in nearly 4,000 stores. “They had only one reusable bag, and it was not very attractive. It took us a long time to agree on a design and colors. In the end, they trusted us and placed an initial order for 400 retail outlets.” Hummingbag also carried out a communication campaign with Mart magazine, which they met during the mission. For its 10th anniversary, the magazine offered two “grocery shopping bags” designed by Hummingbag to its readers.
Since entering the Japanese market, Hummingbag has sold 800,000 bags. “It is a good start, and we are in a very positive dynamic”, says Cécile Chaigneau. “Our partners trust us, and the brand managers we work with, CGC, Lawson, and Kitano, are highly motivated. We are now waiting for the reaction of the real jury: the consumer”.

title: Hurry and visit Miss Dior before she escapes!
description:
"Miss Dior spotted in Tokyo": it could be the title of a dispatch, a musical fugue or a novel. The iconic perfume is the subject of Miss Dior, Stories of a Miss, an exhibition at the Roppongi Museum until July 16, in the heart of a Japan that has made the timeless Miss Dior its adopted daughter, so to speak.   Miss Dior is Christian's child prodigy. After the war, the French designer left his (pink) mark on fashion history with his creations. But even in his unique world, this fragrance remains singular. The first women's fragrance, in which the designer wanted to combine love and freedom, it has accompanied the House of Dior since its first fashion show in 1947. With stubbornness: Miss Dior is now the world's leading prestige fragrance, according to consultant NPD. It is always in the zeitgeist. And it's got a lot to live up to: it was composed as a tribute to Christian Dior's own sister, Catherine, an early World War II Resistance fighter deported to Ravensbrück.   The exhibition showcases Dior treasures never before on public display, such as the typewriter of the great Christian Dior's little sister, original ready-to-wear ensembles from the 60s and famous Haute Couture gowns from the past. It also includes original creations. In particular, the Japanese architect Shohei Shigematsu has created a vertiginous path in the shape of an untied pink ribbon, already used by Dior's contemporary muses: Natalie Portman, Jisoo (Blackpink), Yuko Araki...,    Miss Dior, Stories of a Miss manages to capture the elusive Miss Dior. But not for long: the very essence of perfume is to escape. Run to the Roppongi Museum before she takes to the air on July 16.
Duration: Until July 16. 10:00-21:00
Location: Roppongi Museum (5-6-20 Roppongi, Minato-city, Tokyo)

title: « Ibaraki Prefecture: EU-Japan Regional & Clusters Cooperation Webinars
description:
« Ibaraki Prefecture: EU-Japan Regional & Clusters Cooperation Webinars "Innovations in Food Biotechnology – Immune System" (March 7th) »
Ibaraki Prefecture will conduct the 4th session of the ‘EU-Japan Regional & Clusters Cooperation Webinars’ scheduled for March 7, 2024, from 9:00 to 11:00 (CET) and organized by the EU-Japan Regional & Clusters Cooperation Helpdesk. This event, focused on “Food Biotechnology – Immune System”, will not only introduce advanced technologies from Japan and EU countries but also provide an opportunity to connect with stakeholders in the biotechnology industry from both regions. We look forward to the active participation of those interested/with interests in the biotech clusters or research and educational institutions in the EU and Japan.

１：Date　Thursday 7th March 2024 9:00-11:00 (CET) / (17:00-19:00 JST) - Webinar: 9:00-10:00 / Matchmaking: 10:00-11:00 (20min x 3)
２：Place　B2Match
３：Topic　Food Biotechnology – Immune System What happens in the body when consuming nutritious foods? In addition to be digested by digestive enzymes and absorbed as a source of nutrients, nutritious foods also undergo the influence of gut bacteria. This interaction leads to the production of various metabolites, which, in turn, interact with the intestinal tract, exerting various effects on the body. In this webinar, we will introduce innovative techniques assessing the impact of food components on the body as well as technologies for the efficient development and production of beneficial food components.
４：Language　Japanese/English
５：Fees　Free of charge

title: Increase in consumer price index for 2023
description: The Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications has published its latest report on the average consumer price index.

blocks.text: Foresight

blocks.section: Increase in consumer price index for 2023
blocks.text: Increase in consumer price index for 2023

blocks.section: Increase in consumer price index for 2023
blocks.text: The Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications has published its latest report on the average consumer price index.

blocks.section: Increase in consumer price index for 2023
blocks.text: The latest report on the consumer price index (inflation measure) for the year 2023 has been published by the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications.

blocks.section: Increase in consumer price index for 2023
blocks.text: On average, the consumer price index in Japan rose by 2.8% year-on-year (excluding unprocessed fresh food).

blocks.section: Increase in consumer price index for 2023
blocks.text: This was 0.2 percentage points less than the previous year's increase of 3.0% - the highest level in 41 years, since 1981.

blocks.section: Increase in consumer price index for 2023
blocks.text: The index for food products (excluding unprocessed fresh foods) rose by 7.5% on the previous year. Among products, the index for eggs rose by 24.5%, for ice cream by 11.6% and for minced steaks in restaurants by 9.2%.

blocks.section: Increase in consumer price index for 2023
blocks.text: Due to the recovery in tourist demand, prices for accommodation, including hotels, rose by 25.5%.

blocks.section: Increase in consumer price index for 2023
blocks.text: However, prices for electricity and city gas bills fell by more than 10% respectively.

blocks.section: Increase in consumer price index for 2023
blocks.text: The Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications said: “In the catering sector, measures have been taken to increase prices due to rising labor costs. We would like to confirm whether the current depreciation of the yen will affect the prices of food and other products .”

title: Increase in Japanese automobile exports in February
description: Automobile exports rose by 11.8% in February 2024 compared with February 2023.

blocks.text: Foresight

blocks.section: Increase in Japanese automobile exports in February
blocks.text: Increase in Japanese automobile exports in February

blocks.section: Increase in Japanese automobile exports in February
blocks.text: Automobile exports rose by 11.8% in February 2024 compared with February 2023.

blocks.section: Increase in Japanese automobile exports in February
blocks.text: The weakening yen is said to be behind the rise in automobile exports in February 2024 . This is the conclusion of a report published on March 29 by the Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association. This is the 13th consecutive month of growth.

blocks.section: Increase in Japanese automobile exports in February
blocks.text: By vehicle type, cars grew by +17% in February 2024 compared with February 2023, while trucks and buses recorded negative growth (-25.1% and -49.4% respectively).

blocks.section: Increase in Japanese automobile exports in February
blocks.text: By region, exports increased to Europe, North America and Oceania (+44.9%, +18.7% and +7.2% respectively). However, exports to Asia, the Middle East and Africa were lower than the previous period.

blocks.section: Increase in Japanese automobile exports in February
blocks.text: In January, domestic production had fallen by 7%, the first decline in 13 months.

title: Increase in the number of foreign tourists in hotels
description: Hotel stays by foreigners rose by 68% in Japan, reaching a record high in March.

blocks.text: Foresight

blocks.section: Increase in the number of foreign tourists in hotels
blocks.text: Increase in the number of foreign tourists in hotels

blocks.section: Increase in the number of foreign tourists in hotels
blocks.text: Hotel stays by foreigners rose by 68% in Japan, reaching a record high in March.

blocks.section: Increase in the number of foreign tourists in hotels
blocks.text: Overnight stays by foreigners in Japanese hotels rose by 68.2% year-on-year to around 12.7 million.

blocks.section: Increase in the number of foreign tourists in hotels
blocks.text: This was the highest monthly figure ever , due in part to the weak yen.

blocks.section: Increase in the number of foreign tourists in hotels
blocks.text: According to the Japan Tourism Association, this latest figure exceeded the previous record of around 12.3 million set in December 2023.

blocks.section: Increase in the number of foreign tourists in hotels
blocks.text: Overnight stays by all travelers (including foreign travelers) were also up 8.2% year-on-year, reaching around 55 million in the reference month.

blocks.section: Increase in the number of foreign tourists in hotels
blocks.text: Tourism in Japan has been on the rebound since the government lifted border controls imposed in the wake of the pandemic, but also thanks to the low level of the yen.

blocks.section: Information for Foreigners Working in Companies
blocks.text: Source : Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare

blocks.section: Information for Foreigners Working in Companies
blocks.text: 1. Company must pay a leave allowance to Japanese as well as foreign workers when they are forced to take days off from work by the company. 2. When you take days off from work because your children's schools are closed, you can use paid vacation days just like Japanese workers. 3. The subsidy the national government pays companies to protect worker employment can be used for Japanese as well as foreign workers. 4. Companies cannot freely fire you at will. When a company wants to fire a foreign worker, the same rules as Japanese workers must be followed. If you need help, please consult your local labour bureau, labour standards supervision office or public employment security office (Hello Work).

description:

We extend our heartfelt gratitude to AGS Four Winds for their invaluable support in making this event possible.
