blocks.section: Evolutions macroéconomiques
blocks.text: Un rapport du Ministère de l’Economie, du Commerce et de l’Industrie (METI) publié le 31 mars illustre l’impact croissant de l’épidémie de Covid-19 s ur les chiffres du commerce de détail et du commerc e de gros au Japon .

blocks.section: Evolutions macroéconomiques
blocks.text: Les ventes de détail ont augmenté au total de 1,7% en février 2020 par rapport à février 2019. Les ventes en supermarchés ont augmenté de 6% en rythme annuel alors que les ventes dans les grands magasins ( departement stores ) ont enregistré une baisse record de -11,8%. Ces chiffres s’expliquent par les achats de masse de produits de première nécessité dans la perspective d’un éventuel confinement de certaines préfectures de l’archipel. La baisse des flux touristiques a également eu un impact négatif sur les ventes dans les grands magasins de Fukuoka (-19,8%), Osaka (-19%) et de la préfecture d’Hokkaido en état d’urgence depuis la fin du mois de février (-22%). Les commerces qui affichent des performances positives sont les pharmacies (+19%, dont +46,5% sur les masques et gels désinfectants) et les grands magasins d'électroménager, fournisseurs d’équipements destinés à améliorer le confort à la maison en période de télétravail. Le commerce de gros, à l’inverse, perd -6,2% par rapport au même mois de l’année précédente, notamment dans le secteur de ventes d’équipements et de machines, en baisse significative de -16%. METI

blocks.section: Evolutions macroéconomiques
blocks.text: Le baromètre de confiance des grandes entreprises japonaises s’effondre en mars 2020 et tombe au plus bas depuis 2013. Pour rappel, les indices de l’enquête Tankan (publiée trimestriellement par la Banque du Japon) sont calculés en soustrayant le nombre de réponses négatives au nombre de réponses positives, permettant d’évaluer le niveau d’optimisme ou de pessimisme des chefs d’entreprises sur la conjoncture économique. L’indice de confiance du secteur manufacturier a ainsi chuté de 0 en décembre 2019 à -8 en mars 2020 tandis que l’indice non manufacturier s’est replié de +20 à +8. Les chefs d’entreprise sont particulièrement pessimistes dans les secteurs de la construction navale/machinerie lourde (solde d’opinion à -29 points), métallurgie (solde à -19 points), automobile (solde à -17 points), textile (solde à -17 points) et équipements de production (solde à -11 points). Le secteur non manufacturier semble autant affecté, voire davantage pour ce qui est de l’hôtellerie/restauration (solde d’opinion à -59). Banque du Japon ; Asian Nikkei Review ; Zone Bourse

blocks.section: Evolutions macroéconomiques
blocks.text: Les marchés financiers japonais ont subi de fortes tensions et de la volatilité à l’approche de la clôture fiscale le 31/03/2020 .

blocks.section: Evolutions macroéconomiques
blocks.text: L’indice Nikkei a clôturé à 18 919 points le 31 mars, en repli de -12% depuis le 1 er avril 2019 et de -20% sur le dernier trimestre. Face à l’extension de la crise du Covid-19, les investisseurs japonais ont été nombreux à vendre leurs actifs risqués et réduire leur exposition au marché actions, en particulier sur les secteurs financier, automobile, sidérurgique, aérien, minier et pétrolier. Le rendement de l’obligation souveraine à 10 ans ( Japanese Government Bond ) a clôturé l’exercice fiscal à 0,02% (versus -0,08% le 1 er avril 2019 et -0,01% le 1 er janvier 2020), signe d’une rare absence de performance sur le marché des obligations alors même que les marchés boursiers dévissaient. C’est un fait nouveau car il illustre la vente par les investisseurs de produits considérés jusqu’ici comme sûrs. Les investisseurs semblent avoir délaissé le marché obligataire pour privilégier le marché monétaire, sur fond d’anticipation de la hausse de l’endettement public et de dégradation de la liquidité. Les tensions apparues sur la liquidité en dollar se sont toutefois apaisées après les mesures conjointes prises par les banques centrales. Business standard ; Asia Nikkei ; Asia Nikkei

blocks.section: Evolutions macroéconomiques
blocks.text: Les consommateurs japonais reviennent à la consommation à domicile ; les chaînes alimentaires doivent se réorganiser : l’augmentation de 4,5% de la fréquentation des restaurants en février 2020 aura été éphémère car, depuis mi-mars, les recommandations de la Gouverneure de Tokyo et de ses homologues des préfectures voisines incitent à limiter très fortement les sorties. Après la fermeture des cantines scolaires le 2 mars, les incitations croissantes au télétravail tout au long du mois écoulé puis la déclaration de l’état d’urgence le 8 avril dans 7 préfectures dont Tokyo, la tendance à la consommation à domicile ne fait que se renforcer avec des conséquences sensibles sur de nombreuses productions agricoles :

blocks.section: Evolutions macroéconomiques
blocks.text: - baisse des prix des produits haut de gamme comme la viande wagyu et certains fruits comme le melon (jusqu’à -70% de baisse) qui ne trouvent plus preneurs du fait de la baisse de la demande des restaurants au Japon et en Asie (-6% et -11% d’exportations agroalimentaires aux mois de janvier et février 2020 par rapport à 2019) ;

blocks.section: Evolutions macroéconomiques
blocks.text: - tensions sur le riz du fait de la forte hausse des achats de détails. JA estime qu’en mars, les ventes ont augmenté de 10 à 20% par rapport à la même période l'année précédente.

blocks.section: Evolutions macroéconomiques
blocks.text: SoftBank Group abandonne l'offre publique de rachat, pour 3 Mds USD, de titres détenus par les grands actionnaires de WeWork qui avait été convenue l'année dernière avec ses actionnaires. Cette décision risque de déclencher une action en justice et d'intensifier les tensions avec le co-fondateur Adam Neumann, le fonds Benchmark, ainsi que d’autres investisseurs institutionnels de la start-up américaine d’espaces de travail partagés, qui auraient dû bénéficier de la moitié de ces 3 Mds USD. SoftBank Group avait annoncé son offre publique d'achat en octobre dernier, dans le cadre d'un plan de sauvetage de 9,5 Mds USD de WeWork. Le retrait de SoftBank intervient alors que le groupe tente difficilement de regagner la confiance de ses investisseurs dans un contexte de tourmente des marchés liée notamment à l’épidémie de COVID-19. Ainsi, le groupe a annoncé le 2 avril la fusion entre son opérateur de téléphonie mobile américain Sprint et son concurrent T-Mobile, qui doit lui permettre de dégager des bénéfices. L'action de SoftBank a cependant baissé de -1,2% à la suite de cette annonce. Le groupe avait déjà tenté en mars de rassurer ses investisseurs en annonçant une importante opération de cession d’actifs (41 Mds USD) pour financer un rachat d’actions et réduire son endettement, ce qui lui avait valu une dégradation de deux crans de sa note par l’agence Moody’s. Nikkei Asian Review

blocks.text: Publication de la deuxième NDC japonaise : la température augmente mais l'ambition climatique ne suit pas. Le 30 mars, le Japon a publié sa deuxième contribution déterminée au niveau national ( NDC – Nationally Determined Contribution ). Publié par le Japon une première fois en 2016, ce document décrit les efforts déployés par chaque pays pour réduire ses émissions de gaz à effet de serre (GES) nationales et s’adapter aux effets du changement climatique. Cette publication s’accompagne de l’annonce d’une révision à venir du plan national de lutte contre le changement climatique, adopté en 2016 et d’un rappel du lien étroit entre NDC et mix énergétique, lequel sera également revu en 2021. Le Japon s’engage ainsi à revenir vers l’ONU avant la prochaine échéance de cinq ans pour fournir des informations complémentaires sur sa contribution pour le climat. Cette publication est qualifiée de décevante et nettement insuffisante par de nombreux acteurs et observateurs japonais et internationaux. La nouvelle NDC est en réalité identique aux engagements pris en 2016, avec une cible 2030 de -26 % de gaz à effet de serre par rapport à 2013. Selon le consortium Climate Action Tracker, un tel niveau d’ambition à l’échelle internationale mènerait à une hausse inévitable des températures d’au moins +3°C par rapport aux niveaux préindustriels d’ici 2100. Le lendemain de cette publication, la Secrétaire exécutive de la Convention-cadre des Nations unies sur le changement climatique, a critiqué une NDC japonaise ne montrant aucune ambition réelle d’accroître les efforts actuels. Le World Resource Institute a qualifié la situation d’« occasion manquée » pour l'archipel, soulignant que les alternatives à faible émissions sont désormais plus accessibles que jamais et souvent moins onéreuses que les solutions traditionnelles. Troisième économie mondiale et cinquième émetteur de gaz à effet de serre, le Japon est l’un des seuls pays du G7 à encore construire de nouvelles centrales électriques au charbon. The Guardian , 30 mars ; The Mainichi , 31 mars; Japan Today , 1er avril.

title: Jean Todt Presents the Global “Make A Safety Statement” Campaign at CCI France Japon
description:
On September 16, 2025, the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCI France Japon) had the honor of welcoming Jean Todt, United Nations Secretary-General’s Special Envoy for Road Safety, for a CEO Breakfast Conference held in Tokyo.
A former iconic leader of the Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA), Jean Todt now works alongside the United Nations to raise awareness among the public and policymakers on a global issue: road safety. Every year, road accidents cause nearly 1.3 million deaths worldwide.
A Global Campaign in Partnership with JCDecaux
During his presentation at CCI France Japon, Jean Todt introduced the new global campaign #MakeASafetyStatement, launched by the United Nations in partnership with JCDecaux.
The campaign was unveiled on September 12 at Expo 2025 Osaka, alongside Japanese Olympic skateboarding champion Cocona Hiraki, before being displayed at the United Nations Pavilion (September 12-15). It is also being rolled out across 10 cities and airports in Japan: Fukuoka, Hiroshima, Kawasaki, Kobe, Sendai, Nagoya, Osaka, Sapporo, Tokyo, and Yokohama.
The goal is clear: to engage citizens on the importance of simple, responsible actions while driving, riding a motorcycle or bicycle, or walking, and to remind everyone that each of us can contribute to saving lives.
Renowned Ambassadors
The campaign features internationally recognized faces to amplify this universal message. Among them is Academy Award-winning actress Michelle Yeoh, also Jean Todt’s spouse, who lends her image to the initiative to enhance its impact with the public.

blocks.section: JFTC released 'State of Japan Trade 2022'
blocks.text: “Foreign Trade 2022” marks the 47th edition of this publication since it was first released in 1976. Using latest trade statistics, “Foreign Trade 2022” features Japan’s foreign trade, by area and by commodity. It is abundant with graphs and charts, and concise comments so readers can quickly grasp the basic trend of Japan’s trade. Items such as Nonferrous Metals, Power Generating Machine and Semicon Machinery etc. are added to Chapter 2. Trade by Major Commodity and Data Chapter was also improved this year.

title: Join a free Monitor Tour in Kobuchizawa, Yamanashi Prefecture
description:
Tricolage is a sustainable travel and events consultancy in Japan. From luxury getaways for individuals to incentive trips for corporations, they specialize in crafting journeys that are conscious to the communities and the environment that we visit.
Calling all professionals working in foreign businesses based in Japan! Are you interested in experiencing the serenity of nature and local culture near Tokyo and discovering how it can enhance your business travels?  Tricolage invites you to join our exclusive 3-day program from November 19th to 21st. Explore the potential of incorporating nature retreats into your corporate travel plans, offering your clients or staffs unique experiences and benefiting local communities. This is a FREE trip, with the only cost being transportation to and from Yamanashi.
​Interested applicants will be carefully reviewed and selected for this opportunity.   
REGISTER TO THIS MONITOR TOUR

Purpose of the Monitor Tour
This monitor tour is designed to promote the use of Yamanashi Prefecture's unique natural and cultural resources for incentive trips aimed at overseas companies. The tour serves as a model for retreats that can enhance employee productivity and satisfaction.
Target Audience
Executives and high-performing employees from companies primarily overseas
Why Attend This Tour?
In the era of COVID-19, the importance of meaningful experiences beyond incentive trips and meetings is growing for employee retention. This tour offers physical refreshment, mental stability, leadership development, and team cohesion, all contributing to improved employee productivity and satisfaction.
Overview of the 3-Day Program
Dates : November 19-21, 2023 Location : Yamanashi Prefecture, Kobuchizawa Accommodation: Atelier Lodge  Itinerary summary (tentative):
● Day 1: Arrival and Japanese spiritual experience, followed by exploration of Kiyosato and welcome dinner party
● Day 2: Morning refreshment at Izumi Spring, mushroom foraging, and optional activities.
● Day 3: Horse trekking and community engagement through renovation volunteering.
Host: Tricolage, Inc.
Note:
● All costs for activities, meals, and accommodations are covered, except for transportation to and from Kobuchizawa.
● English-speaking guide will be accompanied throughout the trip
● The entire 3-day tour will be recorded for promotional purposes. A short movie will be created from the footage and used for future marketing and promotional activities.

blocks.text: The Business Forum France Cambodia 2024 is a premier event designed to explore the vast potential of the Cambodian market and will be held in Phnom Penh from July 8 to 10, 2024.

blocks.section: Join the Business Forum France Cambodia 2024
blocks.text: The CCI France Cambodge is pleased to invite you to the France-Cambodia Business Forum 2024 from 8th to 10th July . This forum is a leading event aimed at exploring the vast potential of the Cambodian market. This event directly follows the visit of Prime Minister of the Kingdom, Hun Manet, to France on January 18th and 19th, 2024. On this occasion, seven protocols of agreements were signed, particularly in the energy, infrastructure, and distribution sectors, marking a new dynamic in the Franco-Cambodian relations. These agreements also reflect the Cambodian government's commitment to promoting private sector development. The Forum is therefore a unique opportunity for French companies to leverage this potential for growth and economic development and connect with potential partners, policymakers, and local experts.

title: Join the “Summer Soirée” of FocusCore Japan
description:
FocusCore Japan organizes a summer in-person event, the “Summer Soirée”, on Thursday, August 3.
This event promises to be an exciting gathering of like-minded professionals, featuring esteemed panelists and a range of thought-provoking discussions. Mark your calendars for August 3rd, and get ready to expand your horizons in the world of accounting and finance.
The event boasts a stellar lineup of panelists, each bringing their unique insights and experiences to the table:
 	Tatsuhiko Miyamoto, Director at NEC 	Shinya Konishi, Finance Director at Johnson & Johnson 	Dr. Chie Ikegawa, Representative Director at Strat Consulting 	Zen-Ichiro Ishibashi, President of IMA 
Together, they will share their knowledge and engage in a compelling discussion on the current trends and opportunities in the Japan accounting and finance market.
Highlights of the Summer Soirée Networking Party include:
*A panel discussion to discuss the current Japan accounting and finance market. *Benefits of certification as a Certified Management Accountant (CMA) and how it can benefit an organization.
*Valuable tools and development resources available from the IMA. *Networking: Engage with professionals from diverse industries and backgrounds, fostering connections that can lead to new partnerships, collaborations, and business opportunities.
*Drinks and Light Buffet: Enjoy a delightful selection of drinks, including alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages, as well as a delectable light buffet featuring an array of mouthwatering dishes.

Date: August 3rd, Thursday, from 18:30 to 21:00 Location: L'Espace CCIFJ venue in Nihonbashi-honcho.

blocks.section: Joint Statement on Cooperation in the fields of Cybersecurity, Aircraft industry and Energy transition
blocks.text: On April 1st, 2026, following the Business Forum held during the French President's official visit to Japan, A Letter of Intent was signed in Tokyo between the representatives of MEDEF INTERNATIONAL, Mr. Frédéric Sanchez, of Business France, Mr. Louis Margueritte, of JETRO, Mr. Susumu Kataoka, aiming to deepen cooperation between France and Japan in the fields of cybersecurity, aeronautics and energy transition.

blocks.section: Joint Statement on Cooperation in the fields of Cybersecurity, Aircraft industry and Energy transition
blocks.text: This was counter-signed by Mr. Jérôme Chouchan, President of the CCI France Japon and Mr. Norbert Leuret, President of CCEF Japon. This Letter of Intent aims at creating a dynamic between French and Japanese companies to deepen cooperation in these three industries that are critical to achieve our goals in economic , security , sustainability and technological sovereignty , shared by both France and Japan in the current uncertain global environment. This Letter of Intent will contribute to structure the follow-up of the Economic Forum entitled “FRANCE-JAPAN PARTNERSHIPS : FOR A SOVEREIGN, SHARED AND SUSTAINABLE INNOVATION”, that was organized on the same day at Tokyo Innovation Base .

blocks.section: Joint Statement on Cooperation in the fields of Cybersecurity, Aircraft industry and Energy transition
blocks.text: Business France and the CCI France Japon will offer their services and networks to support French companies in their development projects in Japan, particularly in the strategic fields highlighted in this Letter of Intent.

title: Joint Statement on the Entry Restrictions in Japan
description:
On November 12, the CCI France Japon, together with the American, British, Canadian, German and Italian Chambers of Commerce in Japan and the European European Business Council, issued a joint statement on the entry restrictions in Japan.
The American Chamber of Commerce in Japan (ACCJ), British Chamber of Commerce in Japan (BCCJ), Canadian Chamber of Commerce in Japan (CCCJ), German Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (AHK Japan), French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCI France Japon), Italian Chamber, and the European Business Council in Japan (EBC), welcome the change to the Government of Japan’s inbound travel policy that took effect on November 8, 2021. Permitting business travelers and students to once again enter Japan is a critical step toward Japan’s post-COVID-19 economic recovery. It will help to ensure that international businesses operating in Japan can continue serving their clients and customers in country and is a necessary precondition to attracting new investment and talent from overseas to meet Japan’s economic goals.
We also welcome the reduction from 10 to three days for the quarantine period required of vaccinated business travelers permitted to enter Japan as well as the proposed new measure to allow pre-approved movements after the third day.
However, we note with concern that even with the aforementioned changes, new reporting requirements imposed on sponsoring companies and organizations, as well as other regulatory requirements, mean that Japan will remain more difficult to enter than most of its major economic partners, including other G7 countries.
Further, the continuing requirement for business travelers to obtain a visa (up to 3 months’ stay) leads to a significant increase in administrative burden for Japanese and international companies, while limits on the number of businesspeople entering the country adds further uncertainty and complications.
In light of the aforementioned issues and recognizing that the safe resumption of international travel is vital to Japan’s economy, we request:
● Simplification of, and greater transparency for, the decision-making process for obtaining visas for business travelers. ● The Government of Japan to move as rapidly as possible to eliminate quarantines and to simplify and eventually eliminate sponsorship procedures for vaccinated travelers. ● The Government of Japan to consider increasing the limits on the number of business people entering the country in the near future.  We have appreciated the Government of Japan’s efforts to limit the spread of COVID-19 in Japan and to accelerate vaccination of the population, including all foreign residents.
Further, we applaud the Japanese government’s willingness to recognize digital vaccination systems implemented in many major partner countries, such as the SMART system used widely in the United States and across Europe.  ● To further facilitate the smooth resumption of international travel, we request that Japan enhance its procedures by recognizing the validity of all vaccines accredited by the World Health Organization for entry into Japan.  We commend the Government of Japan for re-opening its borders to international students. International education is critically important as an industry itself and more broadly as a vital incubator of the talent on which business depends. Unfortunately, the new procedures required of students seeking to study in Japan are costly, time-consuming, and onerous. These procedures and the resulting delays constitute a barrier to international education and will deter, rather than facilitate, international students from studying in Japan.  ● In this context, we strongly encourage the Government of Japan to take immediate steps to simplify, expedite, and lower costs for entry of students into Japan.  Finally, we request that the entry process at Japan’s airports, which can currently take many hours, be streamlined. Fuller utilization of digital documentation could substantially reduce entry waiting times, reduce costs, and help prepare for eventual expansion of visitor numbers as public health conditions permit.  We look forward to having the opportunity to discuss these recommendations, and to continuing to support Japan’s economic recovery and growth.
PRESS RELEASE
------------------------------------  French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCI France Japon) www.ccifj.or.jp American Chamber of Commerce in Japan (ACCJ) www.accj.or.jp British Chamber of Commerce in Japan (BCCJ) www.bccjapan.com Canadian Chamber of Commerce in Japan (CCCJ) www.cccj.or.jp European Business Council in Japan (EBC) www.ebc-jp.com German Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (AHK Japan) www.japan.ahk.de/en/ Italian Chamber of Commerce in Japan (ICCJ) www.iccj.or.jp

blocks.text: The American Chamber of Commerce in Japan (ACCJ), British Chamber of Commerce in Japan (BCCJ), Canadian Chamber of Commerce in Japan (CCCJ), German Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (AHK Japan), French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCI France Japon), Italian Chamber, and the European Business Council in Japan (EBC), welcome the change to the Government of Japan’s inbound travel policy that took effect on November 8, 2021. It will help to ensure that international businesses operating in Japan can continue serving their clients and customers in country and is a necessary precondition to attracting new investment and talent from overseas to meet Japan’s economic goals.

blocks.section: Joint Statement on the Entry Restrictions in Japan

blocks.section: Joint Statement on the Entry Restrictions in Japan

blocks.section: Joint Statement on the Entry Restrictions in Japan
blocks.text: In light of the aforementioned issues and recognizing that the safe resumption of international travel is vital to Japan’s economy, we request:

blocks.section: Joint Statement on the Entry Restrictions in Japan
blocks.text: ● Simplification of, and greater transparency for, the decision-making process for obtaining visas for business travelers. ● The Government of Japan to move as rapidly as possible to eliminate quarantines and to simplify and eventually eliminate sponsorship procedures for vaccinated travelers. ● The Government of Japan to consider increasing the limits on the number of business people entering the country in the near future. We have appreciated the Government of Japan’s efforts to limit the spread of COVID-19 in Japan and to accelerate vaccination of the population, including all foreign residents.

blocks.section: Joint Statement on the Entry Restrictions in Japan
blocks.text: Further, we applaud the Japanese government’s willingness to recognize digital vaccination systems implemented in many major partner countries, such as the SMART system used widely in the United States and across Europe. ● To further facilitate the smooth resumption of international travel, we request that Japan enhance its procedures by recognizing the validity of all vaccines accredited by the World Health Organization for entry into Japan. We commend the Government of Japan for re-opening its borders to international students. description: The French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCIFJ) is pleased to announce the arrival of Justine Bailly as the Manager of the Gunma Office.

blocks.text: Justine Bailly: A New Manager for the CCIFJ Gunma Office

blocks.section: Justine Bailly: A New Manager for the CCIFJ Gunma Office
blocks.text: The French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCIFJ) is pleased to announce the arrival of Justine Bailly as the Manager of the Gunma Office.

blocks.section: Justine Bailly: A New Manager for the CCIFJ Gunma Office
blocks.text: I am delighted and honored to join the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan as part of my final-year internship. After completing a master’s degree in International Relations at Sciences Po Bordeaux and a university exchange at the University of Tsukuba, I am highly motivated to promote Franco-Japanese relations through business development between the two countries. I hope to actively contribute, in my own way, to strengthening CCIFJ's presence in Gunma Prefecture through this new regional branch.

blocks.section: Justine Bailly: A New Manager for the CCIFJ Gunma Office
blocks.text: As part of its commitment to strengthening economic ties between France and Japan, the CCIFJ has established a branch in Gunma, a dynamic region located about 100 km from Tokyo. This area plays a key role in industries such as automotive and metallurgy and is home to major companies like Michelin, Subaru, and Danone.

blocks.section: Justine Bailly: A New Manager for the CCIFJ Gunma Office
blocks.text: The branch aims to enhance economic partnerships, support local businesses, and assist French companies in expanding into the Japanese market.

title: Kansai Desk Networking with the Monaco Economic Board at The Osaka Expo
description: On June 30, as part of the Osaka World Expo, the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCI France Japon) had the pleasure of hosting a networking event between a delegation of 30 Monegasque companies led by the Monaco Economic Board (MEB) and a selection of Japanese companies.

blocks.text: Kansai Event report

blocks.section: Kansai Desk Networking with the Monaco Economic Board at The Osaka Expo
blocks.text: Kansai Desk Networking with the Monaco Economic Board at The Osaka Expo

blocks.section: Kansai Desk Networking with the Monaco Economic Board at The Osaka Expo
blocks.text: On June 30, as part of the Osaka World Expo , the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCI France Japon) had the pleasure of hosting a networking event between a delegation of 30 Monegasque companies led by the Monaco Economic Board (MEB) and a selection of Japanese companies.

blocks.section: Kansai Desk Networking with the Monaco Economic Board at The Osaka Expo
blocks.text: The event was initially held at the Australian Pavilion due to space availability and began at 11:00 AM with an inspiring and insightful talk by Mr. Jiri Mestecky , Registered Foreign Attorney at Kitahama Partners, a member of the Chamber. Mr. Mestecky highlighted the economic vitality and attractiveness of the Kansai region: a hub of Japanese industry, strategically located at the center backbone, extremely well-connected to the rest of Japan and the world through two major ports and three airports. He emphasized the region's highly skilled and well-educated workforce, thanks to its rich academic ecosystem, combined with significantly lower wage costs and a cost of living that is 15% lower than in the capital. Mr. Mestecky also pointed out the region’s unparalleled cultural appeal, as it represents the historical heart of Japan.

blocks.section: Kansai Desk Networking with the Monaco Economic Board at The Osaka Expo
blocks.text: This made for a perfect introduction for the companies from the Principality of Monaco seeking to expand their activities in Japan.

blocks.section: Kansai Desk Networking with the Monaco Economic Board at The Osaka Expo
blocks.text: Jean-François Rauch, Regional Director of CCI France Japon, then introduced the Chamber’s mission and activities in the region. This was followed by a joint presentation from MEB representatives Guillaume Rose (CEO) and Justin Highman (Deputy CEO), who highlighted Monaco’s strengths as a destination for international business development and investment. A roundtable session allowed each Monegasque company to briefly introduce itself, paving the way for targeted and meaningful networking opportunities.

blocks.section: Kansai Desk Networking with the Monaco Economic Board at The Osaka Expo
blocks.text: At 12:30 PM, the exchanges continued in a friendly atmosphere over a networking cocktail held at the Monaco Pavilion, in the presence of distinguished guests, including:

blocks.section: Kansai Desk Networking with the Monaco Economic Board at The Osaka Expo
blocks.text: Stéphan Bruno , Director of Economic Development for the Prince's Government of Monaco

blocks.section: Kansai Desk Networking with the Monaco Economic Board at The Osaka Expo
blocks.text: Thierry Boutsen , Former Formula 1 pilot, founder and CEO of Boutsen Classic Cars and Boutsen Aviation

blocks.section: Kansai Desk Networking with the Monaco Economic Board at The Osaka Expo
blocks.text: Guillaume Rose , CEO of the Monaco Economic Board

blocks.section: Kansai Desk Networking with the Monaco Economic Board at The Osaka Expo
blocks.text: Justin Highman , Deputy CEO of the Monaco Economic Board

blocks.section: Kansai Desk Networking with the Monaco Economic Board at The Osaka Expo
blocks.text: Emmanuel Marchat , Board Member of the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCIFJ) and Managing Director of Stahl Japan

blocks.section: Kansai Desk Networking with the Monaco Economic Board at The Osaka Expo
blocks.text: Jiri Mestecky , Registered Foreign Attorney at Kitahama Partners

blocks.section: Kansai Desk Networking with the Monaco Economic Board at The Osaka Expo
blocks.text: This event perfectly illustrates the Principality of Monaco's commitment to strengthening its economic ties with Japan, building on the unique local presence of our Chamber. It reflects a strong and lasting dedication to international economic cooperation, particularly within the strategic framework provided by Expo 2025.

blocks.section: Kansai Desk Networking with the Monaco Economic Board at The Osaka Expo
blocks.text: The involvement of Monegasque companies highlights the growing interest of foreign businesses in the Kansai region. Likewise, the strong participation from Japanese companies demonstrates an increasing openness to international collaboration. Often underestimated despite having a GDP comparable to the one of Singapore or the Netherlands, Kansai holds tremendous potential that deserves to be recognized and promoted. The region’s economic future looks promising, and the momentum generated on June 30 is a clear example of that.

blocks.section: Kansai Desk Networking with the Monaco Economic Board at The Osaka Expo
blocks.text: We extend our sincere thanks to all the participants and partners who contributed to the success of this event. Thank you for your presence, your energy, and your trust. We look forward to seeing you again very soon at our upcoming events.

Every year since 2013, the Kansai Gala Party celebrates gastronomy, culture and French art de vivre in Kansai area. This year will be organized in partnership with Paris Region.
We are pleased to welcome three chefs from Paris this year. Nicolas Beauman from the two-Michelin-starred restaurant "Maison Rostang," Matthias Marc from the one-Michelin-starred restaurant "Substance," and Tom Meyer from "Granite," who has earned one Michelin star and received the MOF (Meilleur Ouvrier de France) title. Coordinated by Eclore group, the three chefs will collaborate to create a special menu exclusively for this onenight event.
We look forward to seeing you on November 7th, 2023!

blocks.section: KDDI finalizes acquisition of Lawson
blocks.text: KDDI, the Japanese telecommunications company, has finalized its takeover bid for Lawson .

blocks.section: KDDI finalizes acquisition of Lawson
blocks.text: Announced last February, this 490-billion-yen takeover bid will enable Lawson to adopt a common management structure with its parent company, Mitsubishi, and telecommunications giant KDDI. The procedure was completed on April 26, with KDDI buying back over 38% of Lawson's shares.

blocks.text: This joint operation not only speeds up decision-making in a highly competitive sector , but also develops collaboration between the convenience store network and the cell phone business.

title: Kreston Global Ranked 10th Biggest Accounting Network in Japan
description:
Kreston Global has been ranked as the 10th biggest accounting network in Japan in terms of revenue by the International Accounting Bulletin (IAB), moving up one spot from the previous year.
The IAB is the leading trusted source for the latest news, analysis and insight for Accountancy firms, networks, and associations. It is a monthly accountancy trade magazine that covers the global accounting business.
They are proud to be a part of Kreston Global and believe that their membership in this network gives them a competitive edge in the Japanese market, as they can offer their clients access to a global network of expertise and resources. This ranking is a testament to their hard work and dedication, and they are excited to continue to grow their business in Japan.
About the IAB
The IAB is one of a network of 40+ proprietary B2B websites, with an unrivalled global audience of active decision-makers, influencers, and opinion leaders across the world, with a combined readership of 55 million industry professionals each year.
As part of GlobalData, they have access to over 1 billion data points, including companies, deals, projects and forecasts, and trends. Leading data informs and supports their industry-leading content. With expertise spanning more than 80 markets globally and driven by 800+ award-winning journalists, researchers, and analysts, they connect users with the information that makes and breaks businesses daily.

title: The French brand Millet opens a new flagship store in Shibuya
description:
The mountain equipment brand Millet is strengthening its presence in Japan with the opening of its new flagship store, MILLET BRAND STORE TOKYO SHIBUYA, inaugurated on Saturday, March 7, 2026, in the heart of Tokyo.
Founded in 1921, Millet is one of the historic brands in alpine sports equipment. Now recognized worldwide for its technical expertise and strong alpine heritage, the company continues to expand its development in Japan.
A store inspired by a French Alps mountain refuge
Located in the dynamic Shibuya district, the new store was designed around an original concept: a mountain refuge from the French Alps. Visitors can discover the brand’s universe through a complete range of products dedicated to mountain and outdoor activities, from mountaineering and hiking to trail running.
The first floor of the store is inspired by the rocky ridges of Chamonix, the historic birthplace of the brand. The space has been designed not only as a retail store but also as a meeting place for the outdoor community. Visitors will find books and photographs dedicated to mountaineering and mountain culture.
Millet also plans to host various events with its ambassadors and partners, including mountain guides, athletes, and photographers from the outdoor world.
Celebrating the opening with customers
To celebrate the opening of the MILLET BRAND STORE TOKYO SHIBUYA, the brand will offer special edition Millet items to customers who make a purchase in store, while stocks last and on a first-come, first-served basis.
Practical information
Location: Jingumae Green Terrace, 6-16-12 Jingumae, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo 150-0001Opening hours: 11:00 AM – 7:00 PM
Phone: +81-3-6433-5022

title: The Ambassador of France to Japan Visits CL by C. Lemaire in Kyoto
description:
On January 27, 2026, Her Excellency Ms. Béatrice Le Fraper du Hellen, Ambassador of France to Japan, visited CL Fashion & Café in Kyoto, the concept store of the Japanese brand CL by C. Lemaire. The visit highlights the growing interest in initiatives that promote cultural ties between France and Japan through fashion, craftsmanship, and equestrian culture.
The Ambassador was welcomed by Christophe Lemaire, internationally renowned French jockey and co-founder of the brand, together with Chinami Hiraoka, President and CEO of CL by C. Lemaire. Ms. Sandrine Mouchet, Consul General of France in Kyoto, was also present.
During the visit, the Ambassador discovered the world of CL by C. Lemaire, built on the meeting of Japanese craftsmanship and horse racing culture. The brand seeks to redefine horse racing as a cultural and aesthetic expression, offering fashion pieces inspired by the jockey’s world and entirely made in Japan.
Based in Japan for over ten years, Christophe Lemaire is now one of the leading figures in Japanese horse racing. Holder of a permanent JRA license, he was named Jockey of the Year in 2025 and continues to compete at the highest level.
Through its collections and concept store, CL by C. Lemaire positions itself as a bridge between French and Japanese cultures, while also embracing a social and sustainable approach, notably by supporting organizations dedicated to retired racehorses.

title: Launch of the 2025 France Japan Foundation Young Leaders Seminar
description:
The France Japan Foundation is proud to announce the first edition of its Young Leaders seminar, to be held in France—between Paris and Strasbourg—from May 8 to 11, 2025. This program will bring together 27 promising French and Japanese young leaders from diverse sectors to strengthen bilateral relations and foster new forms of cooperation.
Established under the aegis of the France Asia Foundation, the France Japan Foundation is dedicated to reinforcing ties between France and Japan. It builds upon more than a decade of work carried out by its sister organizations, the France China Foundation and the France India Foundation. Its mission is to generate synergies between emerging leaders from both countries and promote initiatives that deepen mutual understanding.  At the heart of this mission is the Young Leaders Program, designed to build a dynamic community of influential decision-makers committed to long-term Franco-Japanese cooperation in key areas such as economy, diplomacy, innovation, and culture. The 2025 Young Leaders seminar will take place in two phases:
 	In Paris (May 8–9), the delegation will attend conferences, engage in high-level meetings, and visit key institutions. 	In Strasbourg (May 10–11), participants will immerse themselves in the workings of the 
European Parliament, engage in international policy discussions, and explore the shared culinary traditions of France and Japan. The program will feature strategic discussions, emblematic site visits, and curated networking sessions to cultivate enduring connections among participants.

The list of candidates will be announced soon!

blocks.section: Le chômage partiel comme réponse sociale au CORONAVIRUS
blocks.text: Si la situation sanitaire engendrée par le COVID-19 donne l’apparence d’être contenue au Japon, un certain nombre d’entreprises n’en est pas moins confronté à de sérieuses difficultés résultant de problèmes dans les chaines d’approvisionnement, de chute de fréquentation ou plus généralement de trésorerie. Tout comme ANA qui a annoncé mettre 5.000 de ses employés en chômage partiel (1) , il est plus que probable que les filiales de groupes français présents au Japon et les entrepreneurs établis dans l’archipel devront recourir à de semblables mesures pour préserver l’emploi dans l’attente de la reprise. Nous vous proposons donc ci-dessous un rappel des grandes lignes applicable au chômage partiel au Japon.

blocks.section: 1. La suspension des contrats de travail pour motif économique
blocks.text: 1. La suspension des contrats de travail pour motif économique

blocks.section: 1. La suspension des contrats de travail pour motif économique
blocks.text: Confrontés à des difficultés économiques, les employeurs ont, comme en France, la possibilité de suspendre les contrats de leurs salariés sous réserve de conclure un accord collectif d’ajustement de l’emploi (1.1.). Mais cette suspension des contrats de travail n’exonère pas les employeurs de toute obligation vis-à-vis des salariés dont les contrats ont été suspendus : ils doivent en effet leur verser une indemnité de suspension de contrat (kyûgyôteate ou 休業手当 en japonais) (1.2).

blocks.section: 1. La suspension des contrats de travail pour motif économique
blocks.text: 1.1. La conclusion d’un accord d’ajustement de l’emploi

blocks.section: 1. La suspension des contrats de travail pour motif économique
blocks.text: Pour mettre en place une activité partielle au sein de leur établissement, les employeurs doivent conclure par écrit et avant toute mise en oeuvre un accord collectif (rôshikyotei ou 労使協定 en japonais)avec un syndicat représentant plus de la moitié des salariés ou, à defaut, un représentant de plus de la moitié des salariés.

blocks.section: 1. La suspension des contrats de travail pour motif économique
blocks.text: Cet accord doit au minimum préciser la durée prévisionnelle du recours à l’activité partielle (2) , son nombre de jours, le nombre d’heures concernées, les catégories et le nombre de salariés concernés et les modalités de calcul de l’indemnité de suspension de contrat versée par l’employeur.

blocks.section: 1. La suspension des contrats de travail pour motif économique
blocks.text: 1.2. Le versement d’une indemnité de suspension de contrat

blocks.section: 1. La suspension des contrats de travail pour motif économique
blocks.text: Quand bien même leurs contrats de travail sont suspendus, les employeurs n’en sont pas moins tenus de verser aux salariés concernés une indemnité de suspension de contrat partielle dont le montant doit au minimum correspondre à 60% du salaire moyen versé au cours des trois derniers mois. Des dispositions contractuelles ou conventionnelles peuvent parfois prévoir un pourcentage plus élevé.

blocks.section: 1. La suspension des contrats de travail pour motif économique
blocks.text: Aux termes de l’article 26 de la loi sur les conditions de travail, le versement d’une telle indemnité incombe à l’employeur dès lors que la raison de la suspension du contrat de travail lui est imputable, ce qui est généralement considéré être le cas lorsque la suspension des contrats de travail provient de difficultés économiques affectant l’employeur.

blocks.section: 2. Les possibilités de versement d’une indemnité par l’agence de l’emploi (Hello Work) (3)

blocks.section: 2. Les possibilités de versement d’une indemnité par l’agence de l’emploi (Hello Work) (3)
blocks.text: L’agence pour l’emploi peut être amenée à verser une subvention aux entreprises qui en font la demande. Les conditions générales de versement de cette subvention sont assez strictes (2.1), mais il a été décidé par les autorités publiques japonaises de les assouplir pour préserver la situation de l’emploi dans le contexte de la crise sanitaire (2.2).

blocks.section: 2. Les possibilités de versement d’une indemnité par l’agence de l’emploi (Hello Work) (3)

blocks.section: 2. Les possibilités de versement d’une indemnité par l’agence de l’emploi (Hello Work) (3)
blocks.text: Les employeurs qui font face à des difficultés économiques suite notamment à des modifications de l’environnement économique ou des mutations de la structure industrielle et qui sont amenés à réduire leur activité et par voie de conséquence à mettre en place un plan d’activité partielle peuvent déposer une demande de subvention auprès de l’agence pour l’emploi dont ils dépendent. Le montant de cette subvention couvre les 2/3 pour les PME ou la moitié dans les grandes sociétés de l’indemnité de suspension de contrat versée aux salariés concernés, et ce dans la limite d’un plafond journalier par salarié. Des conditions de production et d’emploi très strictes doivent être remplies par les entreprises qui sollicitent cette subvention (4) .

blocks.section: 2. Les possibilités de versement d’une indemnité par l’agence de l’emploi (Hello Work) (3)
blocks.text: Cette subvention n’est accordée que pour une certaine durée et ne peut être sollicitée de nouveau avant l’expiration d’un intervalle d’un an.

blocks.section: 2. Les possibilités de versement d’une indemnité par l’agence de l’emploi (Hello Work) (3)
blocks.text: Lors de l’examen de la demande de subvention, l’agence de l’emploi s’assure de la réalité des conditions de difficultés économiques et de réduction de l’activité qui justifient son versement.

blocks.text: Afin d’aider les entreprises maintenir l’emploi, les pouvoirs publics japonais ont annoncé des mesures d’assouplissement des conditions de versement des subventions d’ajustement de l’emploi.

blocks.text: Difficultés économiques

blocks.section: 2. Les possibilités de versement d’une indemnité par l’agence de l’emploi (Hello Work) (3)
blocks.text: Les conditions économiques auxquelles les employeurs sont confrontés peuvent être une baisse de plus de 10% de l’indice de production (le CA ou la volume de production) le dernier mois (et non les trois derniers mois) par rapport à la même période de l’année précédente. Dans le contexte de la crise liée au coronavirus, il est également admis que les difficultés économiques pourront être les suivantes : Nécessité de réduire les activités suite à une baisse des commandes en provenance de partenaires commerciaux dont l’activité est réduite en raison de l’influence du coronavirus, Nécessité de réduire les activités en raison de la fermeture d’un établissement décidée par l’employeur suite à la découverte d’un salarié infecté, Nécessité de réduire les activités suite à la fermeture d’un établissement décidée par l’autorité administrative sans qu’aucun salarié ne soit infecté, Arrêt des activités suite à des difficultés affectant le maintien de la production notamment liées aux absences pour congés pour une longue durée de plus de la moitié des salariés en raison de la fermeture des écoles primaires et secondaires.

blocks.text: La durée maximale de versement de cette subvention est 100 jours par an. La règle d’intervalle est écartée. Indépendamment du nombre de jours pour lesquels un employeur a déjà bénéficié de la subvention, il peut de nouveau en bénéficier pour la période maximale prévue.

title: Japan’s Expansion into France and Europe: Is your Intellectual Property keeping pace?
description:
€45 billion: this is the amount of SoftBank’s investments announced at the Choose France 2026 Summit, making Japan the leading Asian investor in France.
This figure is no coincidence: nearly 490 subsidiaries of Japanese companies are currently established in France, employing approximately 74,000 people. Toyota, for example, has invested more than €1.5 billion in its plant in the Hauts-de-France region and, since 2022, has become the country’s leading car manufacturer.
Murata, for its part, has made its Caen site — acquired through the takeover of French start-up IPDia — one of its main operations in Europe, investing €60 million in its expansion.
And the economic opportunities extend well beyond France’s borders. France is a strategic gateway to the European Single Market, its 27 Member States and 450 million consumers. In this context, market entry must be strategically planned from the outset, particularly when it comes to protecting intangible assets.

Are your innovations and know-how as well protected in Europe as the capital you invest there?
Japan currently ranks third worldwide in terms of patent filings, with more than 419,000 applications filed in 2024. This exceptional capacity for innovation represents a considerable economic asset when entering the European market — provided, however, that these innovations are also protected in Europe.
A trademark protected only in Japan, a patent that has not been extended to Europe, or know-how shared without a solid contractual framework when establishing a subsidiary: these are all vulnerabilities that can prove costly for a company, whether it is a major industrial group or an SME expanding into Europe.
Contrary to a common misconception, securing intellectual property rights in Europe is not reserved for large corporations. Protection costs can be optimised by filing applications with the EUIPO for trademarks and designs and/or the EPO for patents, making it possible to secure protection across multiple European markets through centralised procedures.
However, proceeding without the support of a French Patent & Trademark Attorney (Conseil en propriété industrielle – CPI) would be unwise. As a recognised intellectual property expert, a CPI is a key partner for companies seeking to secure their innovations in Europe.

The French Patent & Trademark Attorney: your partner in securing your IP in Europe
A French Patent & Trademark Attorney (CPI) is an independent professional specialising in advice and strategic assistance in intellectual property matters, both in France and across Europe.
The profession includes engineers, scientists and lawyers who have undergone rigorous professional training and qualification. Their core role is to guide companies in the protection, defence, and promotion of their intellectual property rights, including trademarks, patents, designs, software and know-how.
In practical terms, a French Patent & Trademark Attorney can assist you in three essential areas:
Strategy and filing: defining the best approach to protecting and promoting your intangible assets, even before establishing your business in Europe;Contracts and disputes: drafting assignment or licensing agreements, preventing disputes and advising you in cases of infringement;Optimisation and value creation: auditing and assessing your intellectual property, particularly in connection with growth transactions or fundraising.
All CPIs, or French Patent & Trademark Attorneys, are members of the CNCPI (Compagnie Nationale des Conseils en Propriété Industrielle), the only legally established organisation representing all French Patent & Trademark Attorneys.
The profession was created under French law in 1990. French Patent & Trademark Attorneys provide companies with specialised expertise in the protection, defence and promotion of their intellectual property rights.
Working with a French Patent & Trademark Attorney therefore means being advised by a qualified professional bound by professional obligations and with in-depth knowledge of the French and European intellectual property systems.

Franco-Japanese cooperation already in action
Close ties between France and Japan in the field of intellectual property are nothing new. For several years, the CNCPI has maintained strong relationships with the JPAA (Japan Patent Attorneys Association) and the JIPA (Japan Intellectual Property Association).
More recently, another important step was taken. In 2025, a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed between the CNCPI and the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCI France Japon), focusing on economic cooperation, innovation and industrial property.
The two organisations have since established a joint action plan through 2028. This includes jointly organising webinars and seminars for French and Japanese companies on topical issues such as artificial intelligence, luxury goods and semiconductors, as well as strengthening connections between their respective ecosystems.
This initiative is part of the broader role played by CCI France Japon, the leading European chamber of commerce in Japan, with more than 750 member companies, which actively supports French and Japanese businesses in their development.

Intellectual property protection as strong as your European ambitions
Investing in France or elsewhere in Europe, particularly to establish a subsidiary or develop commercial partnerships, is a major strategic decision. Legally securing this ambition is a logical prerequisite — and often the best guarantee of its long-term success.
French Patent & Trademark Attorneys and CCI France Japon are available to assist companies established in Japan in securing their intellectual property and know-how in Europe.
Whether you are considering filing a trademark or design, extending a patent, or simply reviewing your current protection strategy, French Patent & Trademark Attorneys can be trusted partners in helping you enter the European Single Market with confidence and security.

title: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School
description: The CCIFJ organized a week-long Learning Expedition for students of ESCP Business School’s Executive Master in Managing Projects and Transformation.

blocks.text: Sectors & markets

blocks.section: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School
blocks.text: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School

blocks.section: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School
blocks.text: The CCIFJ organized a week-long Learning Expedition for students of ESCP Business School’s Executive Master in Managing Projects and Transformation.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School
blocks.text: The French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan developed an immersive program for a cohort of students from ESCP’s Executive Master in Managing Projects and Transformation. Scheduled at the end of their program, this journey offered participants a unique opportunity to explore Japan’s business ecosystem through direct engagement with leading corporations, institutions, and innovators.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School
blocks.text: Structured as an intensive, week-long experience, the Learning Expedition combined strategic insights, on-site visits, and high-level discussions, showcasing how Japan effectively integrates innovation, digital transformation, and operational excellence across diverse sectors.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School
blocks.text: Day 1 – Foundations: Economic Outlook, Business Culture, and Transformation

blocks.section: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School
blocks.text: The program began with an introductory seminar designed to provide participants with essential insights into the Japanese business environment.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School
blocks.text: Arthur Sogno-Pèes, from the Regional Economic Service of the French Embassy in Japan, offered a comprehensive overview of Japan’s economic landscape.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School
blocks.text: Emilie Teruel-Esclattier, Head of Business Development at the French Chamber of Commerce in Japan, led an interactive session on intercultural communication, highlighting the practical realities of doing business in Japan.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School
blocks.text: Axel Loiseau, APAC Chief Resources Officer at Capgemini, shared valuable perspectives on digital transformation in Japan.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School
blocks.text: This foundational session set the tone for the week, emphasizing the importance of understanding Japan not merely as a market but as a complex ecosystem shaped by culture, long-term vision, and continuous improvement.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School
blocks.text: In the afternoon, the group visited Exotec , a French logistics robotics company that rapidly expanded in the Japanese market after forming a partnership with retail giant Uniqlo, which now uses Exotec robots in its warehouses. Participants met with Pierre Perdiguier, Exotec’s Vice President for Japan, and explored how a high-growth technology company successfully entered and scaled in Japan by meeting the country’s exacting standards for quality, reliability, and performance. The visit highlighted the strategic importance of partnerships, particularly with major Japanese clients, in supporting international expansion.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School
blocks.text: The day concluded at Marubeni Corporation , one of Japan’s leading sogo shosha (trading companies). Konosuke Okura, head of the Digital Innovation Department, presented how the group is leveraging data analytics and generative AI to accelerate internal digital transformation, foster innovation across business units, and cultivate new digital talent within the organization.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School
blocks.text: Day 2 – Innovation Policy and the Startup Ecosystem

blocks.section: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School
blocks.text: The second day was dedicated to innovation policy and entrepreneurship, offering insights into how public and private stakeholders collaborate to support innovation in Japan.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School
blocks.text: In the morning, the group visited Tokyo Innovation Base (TiB) , the global startup hub established by the Tokyo Metropolitan Government. There, participants met with Pierre Bugel, who works jointly with Expertise France, part of the French Development Agency, and Japan’s Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI). He shared insights into Japan’s startup landscape as well as France Japan cooperation in startup policy. The session was followed by a tour of TiB, showcasing the infrastructure and support systems put in place to help Japanese startups grow and scale.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School
blocks.text: In the afternoon, the group visited the DMM.com Group , highlighting another dimension of innovation through the application of digital transformation to regional revitalization and public services. Participants were welcomed by Takeru Takayama, Head of the Regional Revitalization Business Division, and learned how DMM partners with Japanese prefectures and municipalities to digitize administrative processes and enhance citizen services through practical and scalable solutions.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School
blocks.text: Day 3 — Corporate Transformation Across Industries

blocks.section: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School
blocks.text: The third day focused on corporate transformation across industries, offering participants a comparative perspective on how organizations operating in Japan navigate strategic change and long-term value creation.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School
blocks.text: Bernard Delmas, Lead Independent Director of Nissan Motor Corporation , shared insights into the company’s Re:Nissan turnaround plan. His presentation addressed key priorities such as electrification, organizational transformation, and sustainability, outlining a long-term strategy aimed at significant cost reduction and the redefinition of strategic partnerships.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School
blocks.text: The day continued with a session with MCDecaux Japan , a joint venture between JCDecaux and Mitsubishi Corporation. Malik Roumane, CEO for Japan and Mongolia, together with Marco Martinez Del Pino, Digital Transformation Manager, discussed the deployment of digital urban furniture, IoT sensors, and AI-powered digital-out-of-home (DOOH) campaigns in Japanese cities. The session illustrated how data-driven innovation and smart infrastructure are reshaping urban communication within Japan’s specific regulatory and cultural context.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School
blocks.text: Participants then met with Milleporte / Matsuya Ginza , where CEO Armel Cahierre presented the transformation of an iconic department store through the redesign of its e-commerce platform. This case highlighted the evolution of retail in Japan, showcasing how heritage brands adapt through omnichannel strategies, digital tools, and enhanced customer experience.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School
blocks.text: Overall, the sessions underscored that corporate transformation in Japan is often incremental, pragmatic, and data-driven, with a strong emphasis on customer experience, operational excellence, and long-term vision.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School
blocks.text: Day 4 — Smart Cities, BeautyTech, and Digital Healthcare

blocks.section: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School
blocks.text: The final day of the program focused on how digital transformation is reshaping everyday life in Japan, from urban development to consumer engagement and innovation in the beauty sector.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School
blocks.text: The day began with a visit to Mori Building Co., Ltd. and its flagship Azabudai Hills project. Participants explored how smart technologies and data platforms are embedded into large-scale urban developments to enhance living, working, and shopping experiences. Discussions highlighted the role of digital transformation in urban planning, sustainability, and the creation of integrated, people-centric city environments.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School
blocks.text: The group then traveled to Yokohama to visit the Shiseido Global Innovation Center . During exchanges with Omer Iqbal, Senior Vice President for Digital/Technology & Head of Beauty Tech Labs, participants gained insights into Shiseido’s approach to digital customer personalization and the growing influence of technology in the beauty industry. The visit showcased how AI, data, and BeautyTech solutions are redefining customer engagement while maintaining a strong balance between technological innovation and human expertise.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School
blocks.text: Together, these sessions illustrated how Japan leverages digital transformation not only to improve efficiency and services, but also to enhance quality of life and consumer experience across industries.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School
blocks.text: Day 5 – Healthcare innovation and Beauty Tech

blocks.section: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School
blocks.text: The Learning Expedition concluded with a focus on healthcare and consumer innovation, highlighting how digital technologies are reshaping both care services and global organizations operating in Japan. Participants first met with AS Partners , a Japanese company specializing in the development and operation of senior care facilities. The discussions centered on how IoT, AI, and integrated digital solutions are being deployed to transform elderly care environments, enhance operational efficiency, and improve the quality of care. The session provided concrete insights into how technology can help address the challenges of Japan’s aging society through data-driven and human-centered approaches.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School
blocks.text: The program then continued with a session at L’Oréal Japan , led by Japan President Jean-Pierre Charriton . Participants explored the company’s strategic vision for BeautyTech and its broader digital transformation initiatives within a global organization. The discussion highlighted how innovation, technology, and personalization are embedded across L’Oréal’s operations, illustrating how global leaders adapt digital strategies to local markets while maintaining a strong brand identity and long-term vision.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition: A Week Exploring Business Transformation in Japan with ESCP Business School
blocks.text: This Learning Expedition provided an in-depth look at Japan’s approach to business transformation and its distinctive management practices. The French Chamber of Commerce in Japan is proud to serve as a bridge between France and Japan, connecting executive education programs with innovative companies and business leaders.

title: Learning Expedition H2-BATT: Five days of meetings dedicated to clean mobility
description:
Organised by the CCIFJ in partnership with the Pôle Véhicule du Futur

Japan, an essential destination
If there is one country that has brought all modes of transportation, rail, automotive, aviation and more, to the highest level of sophistication, it is Japan. To fully understand the future of mobility, both in terms of vehicles and usage, it is essential to immerse oneself in this ecosystem today.
This conviction led the Pôle Mobilités du Futur, a network of around 500 French industrial players from industry, education and research working on mobility issues, to prepare a mission to Japan. The organisation of this mission was entrusted to the Business Support Division of the CCI France Japan, a natural choice given its experienced Franco Japanese, trilingual and bicultural team, capable of adapting to all types of clients, and reflecting the very diversity of the Chamber itself.
Monday 15 January 2024 marked the beginning of a week long study tour focused on hydrogen and battery technologies, for a delegation of 15 French companies. Over five days, participants were accompanied across Japan to meet six Japanese companies and three laboratories, renowned for their strong commitment to clean mobility and carbon neutrality. Our objective was to ensure that participants were in the best possible conditions to fully benefit from this unique opportunity.
From Kobe to Fukushima, via Tokyo, the French companies were able to discover the many developments underway in Japan, including fuel cells, hydrogen technologies, H2 ecosystems, and their multiple potential applications.
Weekly Program :
Monday, January 15, 2024 
Morning – visit to Kobelco
Kobelco, a key player in steel manufacturing in Japan, is also a major producer and distributor of hydrogen. The company is particularly specialized in the manufacturing of components for hydrogen refueling stations and works closely with Toyota on its Mirai model, which is powered by a fuel cell.
Afternoon – Kawasaki Heavy Industries
Kawasaki Heavy Industries, one of the three giants of heavy industry manufacturing in Japan, is also deeply involved in the hydrogen market. The company is notably known for having designed the world’s largest liquid hydrogen carrier, the Suiso Frontier, with a storage capacity of 1,250 cubic meters, as well as large liquid hydrogen storage tanks installed directly at the Port of Kobe.
Evening – Networking at the Ana Crowne Hotel Plaza Kobe
This event brought together the fifteen participating companies and the largest hydrogen cluster in the Hyōgo region. The evening was marked by presentations from local companies active in the hydrogen sector, a panel discussion on the topic “Liquid hydrogen and internal combustion engines, perspectives and needs ?”, and a networking cocktail.
Tuesday, January 16, 2024 
Morning – Yamaha Motor Company
Well known for its strong position in the mobility market, the teams at Yamaha Motor Company are currently involved in several programs aimed at achieving decarbonized mobility through the use of hydrogen. In 2022, in partnership with Toyota, the company launched the development of hydrogen engines and, in 2023, introduced its first marine engine powered by liquid hydrogen.
Afternoon – FC-Cubic
The FC Cubic laboratory was created through a collaboration between five private companies, six universities and AIST, the National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology. This laboratory is known for its work on the development of polymer electrolyte fuel cell systems, particularly focusing on the development of single cell fuel cells. Until now, the technology had been limited to dual cell systems, making this a major technological breakthrough.
Wednesday, January 17, 2024 
Morning - National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST)
AIST is currently working on the development of innovative solutions for the storage of new energy sources such as hydrogen. In particular, the institute is developing a system designed to increase battery overcapacity in order to enhance its storage potential.
Afternoon - Fukushima Hydrogen Energy Research field (FH2R)
This research site, operated by NEDO, the New Energy and Industrial Technology Development Organization, hosts a laboratory specialized in battery research, hydrogen energy applications and fuel cell technologies. The site also plans to produce 1,200 cubic normal meters of decarbonized green hydrogen per hour, operating 24 hours a day. This production could continuously supply up to 150 households and 560 fuel cell equipped vehicles.
Thursday, January 18, 2024 
Morning – IHI
IHI, a major engineering player in Japan, known for its vision of creating a world where nature and technology work in harmony, is investing significant resources and efforts in the development of zero carbon mobility technologies. Its Yokohama center, which the delegation had the opportunity to visit, specializes in the production of ammonia using hydrogen, with the objective of decarbonizing its emissions.
Afternoon – University of Tokyo
The delegation also visited a research laboratory led by Tatsuoki Kono, Professor in the Hydrogen and Energy Unit of the Research Center for Advanced Science and Technology, which specializes in hydrogen studies. The University of Tokyo, the most prestigious university in the country, conducts extensive research on the development of cutting edge technologies, particularly on the use of hydrogen as an energy source. In partnership with the University of Miyazaki, its researchers were the first to produce hydrogen using solar energy in a cost effective and stable manner.
Evening – Seminar and Networking at the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan
The evening began with a seminar led by Mr. Takashi Yatabe, General Manager of the Hydrogen Department at TEPCO, on the topic “Development of hydrogen utilization technologies toward carbon neutrality, promoting indirect electrification”, followed by a networking cocktail bringing together more than fifty participants.
Friday, January 19, 2024 
Morning - Nissan
The day began with a visit to Nissan’s All Solid State Battery research center in Yokosuka. Known for its leading position in the automotive industry, Nissan envisions the development of electric vehicles powered by solid electrolyte batteries. The Yokosuka laboratory is specifically dedicated to this innovation. According to Nissan’s projections, the first models equipped with this technology are expected to be launched around 2028.
Afternoon – Embassy of France in Japan
The week concluded with an insightful seminar focusing on the Japanese economy and energy trends. The seminar was structured around four presentations. The first, delivered by Christophe Grignon and Rémy Cardinet from the Regional Economic Service of the French Embassy in Tokyo, outlined government strategies, with a strong emphasis on hydrogen. The second presentation, by Professor Tatsuoki Kono from the University of Tokyo, explored hydrogen based energy systems powered by renewable energies in Japan. The third, presented by Professor Stéphane Heim from Kyoto University, shed light on global developments in the automotive industry in the context of electrification. Finally, Hirotaka Yasuzumi from Air Liquide Japan concluded the seminar by presenting the company’s activities in Japan. These presentations focused on the Japanese economy, its rapidly expanding hydrogen market and the Japanese government’s strategy regarding renewable energies.
This opportunity, entrusted to us by the French mobility cluster Pôle Véhicule du Futur, enabled the CCIFJ to establish new contacts while developing new expertise. We would like to extend our sincere thanks to Mr. Bruno Jamet for offering us this valuable opportunity to connect Japanese and French know how.

blocks.text: Japan, an essential destination

blocks.section: Learning Expedition H2-BATT: Five days of meetings dedicated to clean mobility
blocks.text: If there is one country that has brought all modes of transportation, rail, automotive, aviation and more, to the highest level of sophistication, it is Japan. To fully understand the future of mobility, both in terms of vehicles and usage, it is essential to immerse oneself in this ecosystem today.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition H2-BATT: Five days of meetings dedicated to clean mobility
blocks.text: This conviction led the Pôle Mobilités du Futur, a network of around 500 French industrial players from industry, education and research working on mobility issues, to prepare a mission to Japan. The organisation of this mission was entrusted to the Business Support Division of the CCI France Japan, a natural choice given its experienced Franco Japanese, trilingual and bicultural team, capable of adapting to all types of clients, and reflecting the very diversity of the Chamber itself.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition H2-BATT: Five days of meetings dedicated to clean mobility
blocks.text: Monday 15 January 2024 marked the beginning of a week long study tour focused on hydrogen and battery technologies, for a delegation of 15 French companies. Over five days, participants were accompanied across Japan to meet six Japanese companies and three laboratories, renowned for their strong commitment to clean mobility and carbon neutrality. Our objective was to ensure that participants were in the best possible conditions to fully benefit from this unique opportunity.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition H2-BATT: Five days of meetings dedicated to clean mobility
blocks.text: From Kobe to Fukushima, via Tokyo, the French companies were able to discover the many developments underway in Japan, including fuel cells, hydrogen technologies, H2 ecosystems, and their multiple potential applications.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition H2-BATT: Five days of meetings dedicated to clean mobility
blocks.text: Kobelco, a key player in steel manufacturing in Japan, is also a major producer and distributor of hydrogen. blocks.section: Learning Expedition H2-BATT: Five days of meetings dedicated to clean mobility
blocks.text: Kawasaki Heavy Industries, one of the three giants of heavy industry manufacturing in Japan, is also deeply involved in the hydrogen market. blocks.text: Well known for its strong position in the mobility market, the teams at Yamaha Motor Company are currently involved in several programs aimed at achieving decarbonized mobility through the use of hydrogen. blocks.section: Learning Expedition H2-BATT: Five days of meetings dedicated to clean mobility

This laboratory is known for its work on the development of polymer electrolyte fuel cell systems, particularly focusing on the development of single cell fuel cells.
