title: Learning Expedition in Japan: Exploring the Japanese Ecosystem for 8 Occitanie Companies
description:
In April 2025, the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan, in collaboration with Business France and the Occitanie Chamber of Commerce, organized a Learning Expedition for a delegation of 8 Occitanie companies. The mission aimed to explore the Japanese market, understand its specificities, and establish strategic partnerships.

Day 1 – Introduction to the Japanese Market The delegation began their trip with a welcome seminar at the French Chamber of Commerce in Japan, which provided an overview of the Japanese economic landscape and key sectoral trends, presented by Emilie Teruel, Director of the Business Development Services at French Chamber of Commerce in Japan, and Nicolas Sestier, Deputy Director for Northeast Asia at Business France.
In the afternoon, a seminar at Crédit Agricole CIB allowed participants to learn about the bank’s operations in Japan. Three speakers enriched the discussions: Pierre Mustière (Bouygues Asia) shared his experience of the Japanese market and best practices in business development; Albert Bazin (Rakuten) discussed current challenges and the future of artificial intelligence in the Japanese context; and Yann Rousseau, correspondent for Les Échos in Tokyo, spoke about the major societal issues currently facing Japan.

Day 2 – At the Heart of Innovation, Robotics, and Research in Japan On the second day of the Learning Expedition in Tokyo, the delegation had the opportunity to discover key players in Japanese technological innovation. The morning began with a visit to Exotec, a unicorn specialized in automated robotic storage systems. Through its innovative solutions, Exotec is transforming logistics and e-commerce globally. The visit also highlighted the company's growing presence in the Japanese market, particularly through its strategic partnership with UNIQLO, a symbol of successful industrial collaboration between France and Japan.
 In the afternoon, the delegation visited the Tokyo University of Technology. Welcomed at the Digital Twin Center, they explored research on digital modeling, advanced engineering, and simulation technologies. These innovations play a crucial role in designing the infrastructure of tomorrow, developing smart cities, and creating sustainable mobility solutions.

Day 3 – Strategic Meetings and Partnerships On the third day, the delegation had the opportunity to meet with Nissan and visit their showroom in Yokohama, one of the leaders in the Japanese automotive industry. During this visit, the delegation was able to discover the company’s latest innovations, including its strategies for electrification, the development of next-generation vehicles, and advanced technologies shaping the future of mobility. This exchange provided concrete insights into the major technological directions in the automotive sector in Japan and how companies like Nissan are anticipating global market transformations.
 The day concluded with a series of one-on-one meetings organized by the Business France teams. These personalized exchanges allowed the participating companies to receive tailored advice on their market entry or development strategy in Japan. Accompanied by Business France sector leaders, the executives addressed concrete issues related to their business activities, explored the specifics of the Japanese market, and identified the first steps to consider for a successful market entry.

title: Learning Expedition in Japan : Vitagora & the Bourgogne-Franche-Comté Region
description:
As part of the Osaka 2025 World Expo, the Vitagora competitiveness cluster traveled to Japan for a one-week mission, accompanied by the Regional Economic Agency of Bourgogne-Franche-Comté and Dijon Métropole.
The mission began with an introductory seminar held at the French Embassy in Japan, offering participants a strategic overview of the Japanese market. This inaugural session laid the foundation for a better understanding of the country's economic, cultural, and legal landscape, thanks to the insights of several key experts:
 	Nicolas Sestier, Deputy Director for Northeast Asia at Business France, provided an overview of the Japanese market, highlighting its key features, current trends, and the main opportunities and challenges for foreign companies. 	Emilie Teruel, Director of the Business Development Department at the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCI France-Japon), spoke about Japanese business manners and cultural codes, essential for successful professional interactions in Japan. 	Philippe Thirouard, President of Savencia Japan, shared the story of the group's development in Japan, offering real-world insights into the steps, strategies, and adaptations needed for long-term success in the market. 	Lastly, Lionel Vincent, lawyer at Lefèvre Pelletier & Associés in Tokyo, provided legal insights, giving practical advice for companies looking to establish or grow their operations in Japan. 

Later on, the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan organized a group visit to Megmilk Snow Brand, one of the leading players in Japan's dairy industry. The delegation visited their Noda plant, located in the Tokyo suburbs, where they explored the full range of Megmilk’s products, took part in a tasting session, and gained insights into their innovative technologies—including a unique process that prevents residue from forming on yogurt cup lids, a detail highly appreciated by Japanese consumers.

The French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan also arranged several B2B meetings on behalf of two French companies, Naturalim and Groupe St-Aubin, as well as the investment promotion agency Dijon Bourgogne Invest. These meetings enabled the delegation to identify potential Japanese business partners, assess the market’s interest in high-value French products, and explore opportunities for technological collaboration in the agri-food sector.

At the same time, the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan provided crucial logistical and operational support for Vitagora’s mission. This assistance allowed the delegation to focus on strategic meetings and site visits while benefiting from experienced local coordination, translation, and seamless organization of their activities.

The French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan is proud to have helped to strengthen ties between the French and Japanese agri-food ecosystems, initiate new economic exchanges, and support the active participation of Bourgogne-Franche-Comté stakeholders in Expo 2025 in Osaka.

title: Learning Expedition to Japan: Leroy Merlin's Strategic Exploration into Customer Relationships and the Circular Economy
description:
As part of its Vision 2035 strategy, the French company Leroy Merlin embarked on a 3-day Learning Expedition to Japan, organized by the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCIFJ). The mission was designed to provide key insights into two themes: customer service and circular economy, with participants divided into two groups.
The 22 senior managers participating in this mission were engaged in a strategic initiative to redefine the company’s core missions and CSR commitments. By studying the Japanese approach to the circular economy and customer experience, Leroy Merlin aimed to gather valuable insights that will inform their ongoing strategic transformation.
Therefore, over the course of three days, we had the pleasure of assisting Leroy Merlin in their pursuit of discovering and learning the Japanese approach to circular economy and customer service. To achieve this, we organized 3 seminars in our conference room, arranged 8 company visits, and scheduled a meeting with the Tokyo Metropolitan Government's Environmental Bureau. Throughout this study trip, our goal was also to ensure that our participants were in the best possible conditions to make the most of this opportunity. We would like to thank Leroy Merlin for their trust!
The program for the week:
 	Monday 27th of January 
Morning: welcome seminar and introduction to Japan, with key insights on customer service and circular economy.
The Learning Expedition kicked off with an engaging seminar at CCIFJ’s conference room l’Espace, where several key experts shared their insights:
 	Christophe Grignon, Deputy Head of the Japan-South Korea Regional Economic Service at the French Embassy in Tokyo, provided an in-depth analysis of the Japanese economy. 	Mehdi Matagne and Ophélie Dujat, export advisors at the CCIFJ introduced the Japanese market and its business practices. 	Benjamin Costa, Director of La Maison du Chocolat Japan, discussed the evolving customer experience in Japan. 	Guillaume Dourdin, CEO of Veolia Japan & India, explored the circular economy in Japan. 
Afternoon : Panasonic Showroom, the Try-Ie Lab at Daiwa House, Matsuya Ginza & Milleporte.com
Following the seminar, the first group visited the Panasonic Showroom to explore their customer service strategies, and later attended a roundtable with Armel Cahierre, CEO of Matsuyaginza.com and Milleporte.com, focusing on Japan’s luxury e-commerce market. Meanwhile, the second group visited Try-Ie Lab at Daiwa House Industry to explore sustainable technologies for custom-built homes.
 	Tuesday 28th of January 
Group 1 (customer service) : Grand Prince Hotel Shin-Takanawa and Kohnan Shoji
The group focusing on customer experience kicked off the day with a visit to the Grand Prince Hotel Shin-Takanawa, where they delved into the hotel’s customer satisfaction initiatives and learned about the strategies behind creating memorable guest experiences. Next, the team visited Kohnan Shoji, Japan’s third-largest DIY chain, where they gained valuable insights into how innovative retail practices can enhance customer engagement and elevate the shopping experience.
Group 2 (circular economy) : Circular Economy Association and Tokyo Metropolitan Government’s Environmental Bureau
Meanwhile, the group focused on the circular economy met with the Circular Economy Association (CEA), discovering emerging sustainable economic practices that are shaping the future of business. The group also had the opportunity to visit the Tokyo Metropolitan Government’s Environmental Bureau, where they participated in a site inspection of a waste treatment facility. They were presented with an in-depth overview of Tokyo’s advanced waste management efforts, showcasing the city’s commitment to sustainability.
 	Wednesday 29th of February 
Group 1 (customer services) : Sohgo Security Services (ALSOK) and DCM
The first group began their day with a visit to Sohgo Security Services (ALSOK), one of Japan’s leading security companies, where they explored cutting-edge security solutions and customer service strategies. Then, they visited DCM, Japan’s second-largest DIY and home center chain, and engaged with key figures who shared DCM’s customer-centric approach.
Group 2 (circular economy) : Panasonic Eco Technology Center Kanto and Digglue Inc.
Meanwhile, the second group explored Panasonic Eco Technology Center Kanto, where they learned about the company’s innovative recycling and sustainability initiatives. Then, they attended a conference hosted by Digglue Inc., a startup focusing on digital platforms for the circular economy, presented at the Chamber's conference room
We would like to thank Leroy Merlin for trusting us on this enriching journey. It was a true pleasure to accompany them in exploring new perspectives and forward-thinking practices !

title: Learning Expedition with the Financial Services Authority of Indonesia : A Journey Through Japan’s Financial Ecosystem
description: The French Chamber of Commerce in Japan organized a 3-day Learning Expedition for the Financial Services Authority of Indonesia (OJK).

blocks.text: Sectors & markets

blocks.section: Learning Expedition with the Financial Services Authority of Indonesia : A Journey Through Japan’s Financial Ecosystem
blocks.text: Learning Expedition with the Financial Services Authority of Indonesia : A Journey Through Japan’s Financial Ecosystem

blocks.section: Learning Expedition with the Financial Services Authority of Indonesia : A Journey Through Japan’s Financial Ecosystem
blocks.text: The French Chamber of Commerce in Japan organized a 3-day Learning Expedition for the Financial Services Authority of Indonesia (OJK).

blocks.section: Learning Expedition with the Financial Services Authority of Indonesia : A Journey Through Japan’s Financial Ecosystem
blocks.text: In November, the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan welcomed ten Regional Heads from the Financial Services Authority of Indonesia (OJK), for a three-day Learning Expedition designed in partnership with Cegos.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition with the Financial Services Authority of Indonesia : A Journey Through Japan’s Financial Ecosystem
blocks.text: Grounded in the objective of exploring how financial regulators can become catalysts for regional economic development. The program combined expert exchanges with in-depth meetings with regulators, local government officials, regional banks, and companies benefiting from regional economic support, providing firsthand insight into Japan’s unique approach to local revitalization.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition with the Financial Services Authority of Indonesia : A Journey Through Japan’s Financial Ecosystem
blocks.text: Across Tokyo and Ibaraki, the participants discovered an ecosystem where regulators, financial institutions, local governments, and industry players cooperate closely to sustain regional industries and foster long-term innovation in a dynamic international financial hub.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition with the Financial Services Authority of Indonesia : A Journey Through Japan’s Financial Ecosystem
blocks.text: Day 1 — Tokyo: Entering Japan’s Financial Core

blocks.section: Learning Expedition with the Financial Services Authority of Indonesia : A Journey Through Japan’s Financial Ecosystem
blocks.text: The Learning Expedition began with a meeting with the Japanese regulator: the Financial Services Agency (JFSA) . The discussions centered on regional financing, regulatory challenges, and the role of the Regional Financial Support Unit in strengthening local administrations.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition with the Financial Services Authority of Indonesia : A Journey Through Japan’s Financial Ecosystem
blocks.text: The group then proceeded to a meeting at the Bank of Japan , where they learned how the central bank supports regional economies through supervision, data analysis, and capacity building for local financial institutions. The meeting provided a concrete example of how macro policy translates into local impact.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition with the Financial Services Authority of Indonesia : A Journey Through Japan’s Financial Ecosystem
blocks.text: The day concluded at Norinchukin Bank , one of Japan’s most important institutions supporting agriculture, fisheries, and forestry. The session highlighted the cooperative based model that underpins Japan’s primary sector and the bank’s commitment to sustainable management.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition with the Financial Services Authority of Indonesia : A Journey Through Japan’s Financial Ecosystem
blocks.text: By the end of the first day, participants had traced the journey of financial regulation from the center to the regions, gaining a clearer understanding of how national policy frameworks translate into regional development strategies.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition with the Financial Services Authority of Indonesia : A Journey Through Japan’s Financial Ecosystem
blocks.text: Day 2 — From Tokyo to Ibaraki: Where Government and Regional Finance Meet

blocks.section: Learning Expedition with the Financial Services Authority of Indonesia : A Journey Through Japan’s Financial Ecosystem
blocks.text: The second day opened with an in-depth exchange with the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Bureau of Industrial and Labor Affairs . The discussion focused on Tokyo’s local government Global Financial Strategy, its support mechanisms for SMEs and startups, and the FinCity.Tokyo initiative designed to strengthen Tokyo’s international financial competitiveness.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition with the Financial Services Authority of Indonesia : A Journey Through Japan’s Financial Ecosystem
blocks.text: In the afternoon, the group traveled to Ibaraki for a meeting with Joyo Bank , a major regional bank with a network spanning over 180 branches in Japan and several overseas offices. Joyo Bank’s leadership shared their approach to supporting local businesses, managing regional risks, and contributing to community development, providing a benchmark for how regional banks can drive economic vitality.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition with the Financial Services Authority of Indonesia : A Journey Through Japan’s Financial Ecosystem
blocks.text: Through these exchanges, the participants deepened their understanding of how both metropolitan and regional institutions articulate their development priorities and the role regulators play in enabling growth.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition with the Financial Services Authority of Indonesia : A Journey Through Japan’s Financial Ecosystem
blocks.text: Day 3 — Ibaraki: Agriculture, Cooperatives, and Local Revitalization

blocks.section: Learning Expedition with the Financial Services Authority of Indonesia : A Journey Through Japan’s Financial Ecosystem
blocks.text: The final day centered on Japan’s cooperative model and agricultural innovation.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition with the Financial Services Authority of Indonesia : A Journey Through Japan’s Financial Ecosystem
blocks.text: The delegation first visited JA Bank Ibaraki and the Ibaraki Prefectural JA Central Union , part of JA (Japan Agricultural Cooperatives), discovering how financial services, cooperative management, and agricultural support centers work hand in hand. Presentations highlighted farmer financing, regional credit networks, and the evolving role of JA in strengthening local economic resilience.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition with the Financial Services Authority of Indonesia : A Journey Through Japan’s Financial Ecosystem
blocks.text: The day ended at Lapoppo Namegata Farmers Village , an inspiring example of regional revitalization, a former elementary school transformed into a sweet potato agricultural theme park through collaboration between the Shirohato Group, JA, and the local government. With its integrated production system, experiential tourism, and community partnerships, Lappopo Namegata Farmers Village demonstrated how agriculture can be reimagined as a driver of innovation and local pride.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition with the Financial Services Authority of Indonesia : A Journey Through Japan’s Financial Ecosystem
blocks.text: A Story of Collaboration, Innovation, and Shared Purpose

blocks.section: Learning Expedition with the Financial Services Authority of Indonesia : A Journey Through Japan’s Financial Ecosystem
blocks.text: Beyond the institutional visits, what marked this Learning Expedition was the collective recognition that regional development thrives when ecosystems work together .

blocks.section: Learning Expedition with the Financial Services Authority of Indonesia : A Journey Through Japan’s Financial Ecosystem
blocks.text: Japan’s financial and administrative architecture offers valuable lessons for emerging and established regulators alike:

blocks.section: Learning Expedition with the Financial Services Authority of Indonesia : A Journey Through Japan’s Financial Ecosystem
blocks.text: collaboration over silos ,

blocks.section: Learning Expedition with the Financial Services Authority of Indonesia : A Journey Through Japan’s Financial Ecosystem
blocks.text: enablement over compliance alone ,

blocks.section: Learning Expedition with the Financial Services Authority of Indonesia : A Journey Through Japan’s Financial Ecosystem
blocks.text: innovation aligned with local needs ,

blocks.section: Learning Expedition with the Financial Services Authority of Indonesia : A Journey Through Japan’s Financial Ecosystem
blocks.text: and long-term thinking as a foundation for economic resilience .

blocks.section: Learning Expedition with the Financial Services Authority of Indonesia : A Journey Through Japan’s Financial Ecosystem
blocks.text: For OJK’s regional leaders, the journey provided not only technical insights but also inspiration, revealing new ways regulators can influence regional prosperity while balancing stability, inclusion, and innovation.

blocks.section: Learning Expedition with the Financial Services Authority of Indonesia : A Journey Through Japan’s Financial Ecosystem
blocks.text: We look forward to continuing this collaboration and to supporting future learning programs that build bridges between Japan and the world on key economic and regulatory topics.

title: "Learning From The Failures Of Successful Women": an event by Sasuga Communications
description:
In Japanese, we say, “Shippai wa seiko no moto” (we learn from our mistakes). 
 Our failures often come with embarrassment, shame, or pain that most of us would prefer to avoid, right? Well, what if you could learn valuable lessons for women in business without those unpleasant feelings? What if you could gain insights and inspiration just from listening to other women’s setbacks?
Sasuga Communications K. K. is hosting the third event of The #LessEffortMoreImpact for Women In Business " at l’Espace on Saturday, September 30 for women in business in the Tokyo area.
"Learning From The Failures Of Successful Women" is a Roundtable where three fabulous women will courageously reveal how they messed up in their careers including
⭐️ “I thought I would never recover (but I did)”
⭐️ “It turned out to be a good thing”
⭐️“Now I look back, it’s hilarious”
You can ask questions, share your stories, and enjoy small-group conversations with other women in the room, so that everyone can be involved and feel inspired.

title: Advice from an importer of agri food products in Japan
description: A specialist in the import of French agri food products in Japan answers our questions

blocks.section: Advice from an importer of agri food products in Japan
blocks.text: Advice from an importer of agri food products in Japan

blocks.section: Advice from an importer of agri food products in Japan
blocks.text: A specialist in the import of French agri food products in Japan answers our questions

blocks.section: Advice from an importer of agri food products in Japan
blocks.text: On June 21, 2023, we had the pleasure of interviewing Mr. François Xavier COLAS, Managing Director of the Japanese branch of Classic Fine Foods , known as French F&B Japan , a company importing high end agri food products, present in Japan for 40 years.

blocks.section: Advice from an importer of agri food products in Japan
blocks.text: 80% of the products imported by Classic Fine Foods Japan are European, of which 70% are French. The company imports and distributes high quality ingredients dedicated to cooking and pastry, as well as dry grocery products. Its clients are luxury hotels, fine dining restaurants, reception venues, airline caterers, as well as wholesalers supplying pastry shops.

blocks.section: Discover the advice of an expert on developing on the Japanese market and certain practices of importers.
blocks.text: Discover the advice of an expert on developing on the Japanese market and certain practices of importers.

blocks.section: Discover the advice of an expert on developing on the Japanese market and certain practices of importers.
blocks.text: His analysis of distribution channels in Japan :

blocks.section: Discover the advice of an expert on developing on the Japanese market and certain practices of importers.
blocks.text: In Japan, agri food products can be distributed through several types of stores, each playing a different role and corresponding to a different strategy:

blocks.section: Discover the advice of an expert on developing on the Japanese market and certain practices of importers.
blocks.text: Department stores make it possible to enhance the image of the brand and the product and to sell at higher prices, however the volumes purchased are limited. Department stores only pay for what they have sold and return the rest to the importer. Indeed, using an importer is essential to work with department stores, as responsibilities are borne by the importer. In particular, the importer is responsible for providing a salesperson.

blocks.section: Discover the advice of an expert on developing on the Japanese market and certain practices of importers.
blocks.text: High end supermarkets such as Seijo Ishii, Kaldi, Kinokuniya, Meidi ya, Meidi ya, Nissin, National Azabu are importer distributors. They import directly and allow larger volumes to be sold and better margins compared to department stores. They pay for everything they purchase and take the risk of stocking the goods. Within this channel, products are renewed every three years to meet customers’ expectations for novelty.

blocks.section: Discover the advice of an expert on developing on the Japanese market and certain practices of importers.
blocks.text: Finally, large supermarkets and convenience stores (Japanese convenience shops open 24/7) are the ones that purchase the largest volumes from foreign exporters. They are managed by Japanese trading houses such as Mitsui Bussan, Mitsubishi, which act as importers and distributors. These contracts are very significant and more difficult to obtain.

blocks.section: Discover the advice of an expert on developing on the Japanese market and certain practices of importers.
blocks.text: These three channels are organized like a pyramid, from top to bottom, from department stores to supermarkets and convenience stores.

blocks.section: Discover the advice of an expert on developing on the Japanese market and certain practices of importers.
blocks.text: Sales volumes will be lower at the department store level but the product will gain visibility, while supermarkets and convenience stores can allow large volumes to be sold but do not build the brand image of the product.

blocks.section: Discover the advice of an expert on developing on the Japanese market and certain practices of importers.
blocks.text: It is possible to change distribution channels in order to evolve one’s strategy, however this can only be done from top to bottom .

blocks.section: Discover the advice of an expert on developing on the Japanese market and certain practices of importers.
blocks.text: For example, the brand La Mère Poulard gained its reputation in department stores and was later able to develop its sales through other distribution channels.

blocks.section: Discover the advice of an expert on developing on the Japanese market and certain practices of importers.
blocks.text: How do importers work ?

blocks.section: Discover the advice of an expert on developing on the Japanese market and certain practices of importers.
blocks.text: A local importer will be your key and indispensable partner to develop on the Japanese market. Importers of agri food products handle product registration with customs, shipment to Japan, and the storage of your goods in their dedicated warehouses before distributing them.

blocks.section: Discover the advice of an expert on developing on the Japanese market and certain practices of importers.
blocks.text: Japanese importers favor exclusive contracts . If this is essential for your Japanese partner, try to associate them with performance related objectives (turnover communication, points of sale, development strategy, marketing tools, etc.) which will help foster a transparent relationship.

blocks.section: Discover the advice of an expert on developing on the Japanese market and certain practices of importers.
blocks.text: For example, Classic Fine Foods sends commercial reports every three months detailing the evolution of its overall turnover and the revenue generated by different products, product by product performance, as well as distribution locations.

blocks.section: Discover the advice of an expert on developing on the Japanese market and certain practices of importers.
blocks.text: His advice on best practices to adopt :

blocks.section: Discover the advice of an expert on developing on the Japanese market and certain practices of importers.
blocks.text: To export to Japan, product quality alone is not sufficient; it is also necessary to be flexible regarding packaging, conditioning, and the quantities per package (stricter weight constraints and different eating habits in Japan).

blocks.section: Discover the advice of an expert on developing on the Japanese market and certain practices of importers.
blocks.text: It is advisable to come to Japan to understand the market, to test the potential of one’s product in order to determine whether it is sufficiently adapted, and to identify what interests local consumers the most. When you are a small company, one of the best ways to enter the Japanese market is to participate in trade shows in order to present your products to potential partners and consumers.

blocks.section: Discover the advice of an expert on developing on the Japanese market and certain practices of importers.
blocks.text: On the other hand, Japanese companies do not favor direct calls from foreign companies. Being introduced through a local intermediary is a good way to establish initial contact. There are various consulting organizations. CCI France Japan, thanks to its 100 years of presence in the country, has acquired a certain reputation that allows it to open doors for French companies.

blocks.section: Discover the advice of an expert on developing on the Japanese market and certain practices of importers.
blocks.text: To support the work of an importing partner, it is beneficial to have a local representative who masters the language and Japanese business culture . This person can support the importer in its commercial strategy in order to find new clients. It is important to note that Japanese people do not primarily have a sales driven mindset; they above all have a strong sense of service . Relationships with existing distributors and logistics are very well managed, but promotion and sales may require external support. According to Mr. Colas: “ delegation without control is abandonment ”.

blocks.section: Discover the advice of an expert on developing on the Japanese market and certain practices of importers.
blocks.text: To conclude, once distributed in Japan, it is essential to keep in mind that product quality must remain flawless ; otherwise, it could mean the end of exports to Japan.

blocks.section: Discover the advice of an expert on developing on the Japanese market and certain practices of importers.
blocks.text: Regulations to keep in mind :

blocks.section: Discover the advice of an expert on developing on the Japanese market and certain practices of importers.
blocks.text: In the agri food sector, the most sensitive products to export are fresh products. Large scale retailers only accept products when more than 50% of their use by date remains . It is therefore necessary to take this rule into account, as well as shipping time (46 days by sea from Europe, for example) and customs clearance (2 weeks).

blocks.section: Discover the advice of an expert on developing on the Japanese market and certain practices of importers.
blocks.text: Mascarpone, for example, is difficult to import due to its 150 day shelf life.

blocks.section: Discover the advice of an expert on developing on the Japanese market and certain practices of importers.
blocks.text: New trends among its clients :

blocks.section: Discover the advice of an expert on developing on the Japanese market and certain practices of importers.
blocks.text: Within the activity of Classic Fine Foods, pastry ingredients are currently booming. Sugars, in particular “technical” sugars, and butter are increasingly in demand by Japanese clients.

blocks.section: Discover the advice of an expert on developing on the Japanese market and certain practices of importers.
blocks.text: French know how is highlighted both by pastry manufacturers wishing to differentiate themselves and by consumers who are concerned about product quality.

blocks.section: Conclusion
blocks.text: Conclusion

blocks.section: Conclusion
blocks.text: To sum up, Mr. François Xavier Colas has today allowed us to share with you some important aspects of the agri food sector in Japan.

blocks.section: Conclusion
blocks.text: It is a market that offers many opportunities for French companies, provided they adapt their positioning and meet local requirements.

blocks.section: Conclusion
blocks.text: Because each company and each product has its own specificities, our “Business Services” team supports you in order to help identify the best strategy and find the local partner that suits you.

blocks.section: Conclusion
blocks.text: Do not hesitate to contact us to receive advice. You can rely on our network and our knowledge of the market to define the steps to follow to develop in Japan.

blocks.section: Conclusion
blocks.text: We remain at your disposal : business@ccifj.or.jp

title: Looking back at "Cybersecurity in Japan Today: Risks, Regulation and Practical Incident Response"
description:
On July 2nd, the CCI France Japon hosted an evening dedicated to one of the most pressing challenges facing businesses operating in Japan today: cybersecurity.
The session brought together legal and security professionals who walked participants through the current threat landscape in Japan, the evolving regulatory framework, and the practical steps organisations should take in the event of a cyber incident. The presentations sparked rich discussions and gave attendees concrete takeaways to bring back to their organisations.
We extend our sincere thanks to our speakers — Carlo Geraci and Sean King from PwC, and Kentaro Toda from TMI Associates — for sharing their expertise and delivering such an informative and engaging session.
We also thank all participants for their active involvement, and look forward to welcoming you at our next IT Committee event.

title: Looking back at "Decoding the Gaishikei Finance Function”
description:
The French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan organized “Decoding the Gaishikei Finance Function,” an event exploring the evolving role of finance teams in foreign-affiliated companies in Japan, from the impact of AI to talent management and strategic business partnering.
Following a presentation of survey findings conducted by FocusCore Group, our three speakers, Makiko Goshi (Senior Officer, Financial Management at Prudential Holdings of Japan), Tsutomu Miura (Finance Business Partner, Japan & Korea at Barry Callebaut), and Taisuke Yoshida (East Asia Industrial Automation Business Finance Leader at Schneider Electric), shared their insights and experiences on the challenges and opportunities shaping finance functions today. The discussion highlighted key priorities for finance leaders, including succession planning or talent development.
We sincerely thank our three speakers for sharing their perspectives on finance and its future in Japan, as well as FocusCore Group for their contribution to the event.

description:
The French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan organized a seminar entitled “Economic Intelligence: A Strategic Tool to Protect, Anticipate and Decide, in an Era of Geopolitical and Trade Instability.” The event explored the growing importance of economic intelligence in helping companies navigate an increasingly uncertain geopolitical and trade environment, anticipate risks, and identify new business opportunities.
Our speaker, Jacques Beltran, Deputy CEO of ADIT, delivered an insightful presentation on how economic intelligence can support businesses, followed by a lively and extensive Q&A session. The numerous questions raised by participants led to dynamic exchanges on the challenges and opportunities facing companies in today’s geopolitical and economic landscape.
We sincerely thank Jacques Beltran for sharing his valuable insights and expertise, as well as all participants for their active engagement and questions which contributed to such a stimulating discussion!

title: Digital Transformation: Time Saving
description: For this 2nd edition of the Sectoral Meetings, Marion Baillat gives us a practical case to study the Digital Transformation, applied to time saving.

blocks.text: Kansai Event report

blocks.section: Digital Transformation: Time Saving
blocks.text: Digital Transformation: Time Saving

blocks.section: Digital Transformation: Time Saving
blocks.text: For this 2nd edition of the Sectoral Meetings, Marion Baillat gives us a practical case to study the Digital Transformation, applied to time saving.

blocks.section: Digital Transformation: Time Saving
blocks.text: Here we are, inaugurating the second episode of our Kansai Sectoral Gatherings, 2023. Our guest speaker this time is Marion Baillat, head of production at 42 Interactive , and her specialty is time saving through digital transformation . As she brilliantly demonstrated through a practical case (to manage a complex real estate), digital transformation is a long and complex but crucial and worthy process , which helps businesses make the transition from an heterogeneous analog system to an organized and efficient digital system . Efficiency is the key, but because the digital transformation fundamentally changes the way a business operates to deliver a higher value of service, one of the key issues that was debated during the speech was onboarding : if you want the change to take roots, there is a necessity that everybody in the company (and its partners) feels involved in the change and takes it up willingly. Thus, there is not only a technical issue , but there is also a really deep people issue . In fact, the process of digital transformation requires a deep understanding of the structure’s functioning, which is a challenge in itself. For the digital transformation to be relevant and involve the people it will benefit on the ground, there is a critical need to put yourself in their shoes and deeply understand what is at stake in what they do to make their life easier and simpler . If the solution is just forced from above, failure is nearly certain. The bottom line is, digital transformation is a patient and painstaking work that requires a lot of consideration. Wherever it takes place, it will not happen overnight, let alone be dropped brutally on a given organization. But if it is such a delicate process, how to make the need for digital transformation be felt, when it is so easy to leave things be and stay in your comfort zone? Efficiency is the key. The amount of money and time saved through a streamlined digital workflow , as opposed to paper processing, can save 4 times the time , and the cost of it in money can amount to millions of dollars for big structures. Teamwork and the employee’s quality of life are also strongly impacted, as well as security and internal access to information/documentation, while the quality of the service delivered to customers is increased. Obviously, Japan is THE country where the question of getting everybody on board for change, transitions and innovation is a tough challenge , and there is a growing concern, not only among foreigners in Japan but also among Japanese players themselves, that the Japanese economy and society is slowly falling behind due to an increasingly worrying lack of innovation , or motivation thereof (see the N°172 December 2022 issue of France Japon Eco on that subject). In that regard, Marion’s input and expertise are very welcome assets to the Japanese market, and we do hope that her presentation will help our participants to solve issues they might have in their respective departments and companies. We are actually very happy that Marion, although being French, speaks flawless English, which allowed both French and Japanese participants to attend the event and follow her presentation. The next session of our Kansai Sectoral Meetings will be hosted by Damien Vitry at Arkema ’s KTC (Kyoto Technical Center) on Tuesday, March 28 . Damien will not only deliver an insight on Bio-based performance materials , he will also offer us an exclusive guided tour of the R&D lab , so put on your goggles and join us for an exceptional immersion in the world of sustainable polymers!

title: Looking back at the event : "How the Japanese Society Shaped the Retail" with Davide Sesia, Sogo & Seibu Co.Ltd.
description:
CCI France Japon was delighted to host a special event with Mr. Davide Sesia, Executive Director and Vice President of Sogo & Seibu Co., Ltd., who shared valuable insights into the evolving dynamics of Japan's middile class in the post-Covid economy.
The discussion explored the impact of inflation, stagnant wages, and structural social shifts on consumption patterns, highlighting the challenges and opportunities facing the distribution sector and department stores.
Thank you to Mr. Sesia for his insightful presentation, to our moderator, Mr. Yann Rousseau, for expertly guiding the discussion, and to all attendees for contributing to a lively and successful event.We look forward to welcoming you again on another occation!

title: Looking back at the Gala Fukuoka 2025
description:
On Monday, 19 May 2025, we were pleased to host the Fukuoka Gala Dinner 2025 at the Solaria Nishitetsu Hotel Fukuoka. The event, held in collaboration with the city of Bordeaux and the Conseil Interprofessionnel du Vin de Bordeaux (CIVB), welcomed 191 guests for an evening of food, culture, and connection.
We were honored to welcome Ms Akie Omagari, deputy governor of the prefecture of Fukuoka, Mr Eiichi Nakamura, deputy mayor of the city of Fukuoka. We also thank Ms Sandrine Mouchet, consul general of France in Kyoto, Mr Yoshiaki Matsuo, mayor of the city of Arita, and Mr Christophe Chateau, communication director of CIVB for attending.
The dinner featured a special menu created by the Michelin-starred Chef Mathieu Martin from “Saint James” in Bordeaux, and the entertainment was provided by two former actresses of the Takarazuka Revue, Yu Hodaka and Yukino Kojyo. The evening concluded with a tombola, where 56 prizes were awarded to lucky winners.
We thank the companies who contributed prizes and all who helped make the evening a success. A special thank you once again to the city of Bordeaux and the Conseil Interprofessionnel du Vin de Bordeaux, and to our generous supporters.

title: Looking back at the Gala Kansai 2024
description:
On Thursday, November 28th, we had the pleasure to hold our second gala of the week, this time in Kansai at the Portopia Hotel, which has been very professional and very helpful. In partnership with Région Hauts-de-France, the event was attended by over 250 guests.

Our heartfelt thanks go to François Decoster, Vice president of the region, together with the entire delegation from Hauts-de-France, and Nord France Invest for their gracious presence. We also extend our gratitude to the Consule Générale de France à Kyoto, Ms Sandrine Mouchet, for her support in this event.
We had the privilege of hosting Chef Christophe Dufossé again, an esteemed culinary master awarded with Two MICHELIN Stars and a Green Star at Château de Beaulieu Hôtel-Restaurant-Spa. In collaboration with Jocelyn Deumie from Rougie Japan for this segment in Kansai, he curated a splendid menu that delighted all attendees, perfectly complemented by the finest wines and Champagne Telmont. 
The evening was further elevated by a special performance from the renowned Julien Clerc, who performed solo at the piano – a rare treat as he usually performs with musicians, offering us a warm and memorable connection. A huge thank you to Florent Dabadie for offering us this opportunity.
The night concluded with a lively tombola filled with excitement and joy. We are deeply grateful to the companies that contributed to the 125 splendid prizes. 

A heartfelt thank you to all the guests, hosts, and supporters who made this event a remarkable success!
Special thanks to our partner: Région Hauts-de-France, Nord France Invest
To our sponsors: Horiba, Crédit Agricole CIB, Morikawa Clinic
And for their invaluable support: Sébastien Phal, Airstar Japan, LIFE.14, Jean Charles Rochoux Valrhona

description:

title: Looking back at the Gala Nagoya 2025
description:
On Wednesday, 16 April, we were pleased to host the Nagoya Gala Dinner 2025 at Courtyard by Marriott Nagoya. The event, held in collaboration with our partner, the Bourgogne-Franche-Comté Region, welcomed 120 guests for an evening of food, culture, and connection.

We thank the companies who contributed prizes and all who helped make the evening a success. A special thank you once again to our partner, the Bourgogne-Franche-Comté Region, and to our generous supporters.

title: Looking back at the Gala Tokyo 2024
description:
On Tuesday, November 26th, the Cerulean Tower Tokyu Hotel in Tokyo was the venue for an unforgettable night as we celebrated Gala Tokyo 2024 in partnership with Région Hauts-de-France. Over 750 distinguished guests graced the event with their presence, making it a night to remember.

A special thanks goes to Xavier Bertrand, President of the Regional Council of Hauts-de-France, along with his team and delegation, for their invaluable support in organizing this remarkable event. Our heartfelt gratitude extends to the Ambassade de France au Japon, especially Mr. Philippe Setton, French Ambassador to Japan, for his inspiring opening remarks, and Mr. Raphaël Keller, French Minister Counsellor for Economic Affairs.
We were truly privileged to have Chef Christophe Dufossé, an acclaimed culinary artist recognized with Two MICHELIN Stars and a Green Star at Château de Beaulieu Hôtel-Restaurant-Spa, who curated an exquisite menu that delighted all attendees from start to finish. Special recognition goes to the Cerulean Tower Tokyu Hotel staff and Nobuhiko Fukuda for their dedicated assistance in making the night exceptional.
The evening reached new heights with a captivating performance by the renowned Julien Clerc, marking his first appearance in Japan in 50 years.
Ms. Clara Bodin skillfully directed the evening's events with remarkable poise and expertise, ensuring that every aspect of the proceedings unfolded elegantly.
The night concluded with a thrilling tombola lottery, filling the atmosphere with excitement and joy. We extend our deepest gratitude to the companies that contributed to the 320 splendid prizes, making this a night to remember.

A heartfelt thank you to all the guests, hosts, and supporters who made this event a remarkable success!
Special thanks to our sponsors: Région Hauts-de-France, Air France, BNP Paribas, Crédit Agricole CIB, Exotec, LVMH, Natixis Corporate & Investment Banking, Société Générale, Hermès, and Richemont.
And for their invaluable support: Andaz Tokyo - A Concept By Hyatt, Sébastien Phal, Airstar Japan Boomachine K.K., CLARINS K.K, LIFE.14, La Maison du Chocolat, Shanu Agarwal, Veuve Clicquot, CCI Hauts-de-France, and Florent Dabadie.

title: Looking back at the Joint Chamber event "Energy Transition in the Post-FIT Era: Shift Toward PPAs and Emission Trading"
description:
The CCI France Japon was pleased to organise a joint chamber event together with the Danish Chamber of Commerce in Japan (DCCJ) and Japan Energy Hub.
The roundtable discussion brought together industry experts to share insights on how Japan's energy market is evolving beyond the Feed-in Tariff (FIT) era. It was a successful and meaningful evening, with engaging discussions and valuable exchanges among participants.
We would like to extend our sincere thanks to our panellists, who made the discussion particularly lively and insightful:

title: Crêpe party in Kansai!
description: Candlemas is originally a religious holiday, but nowadays it is mostly the occasion to eat crêpes and... make new acquaintances!

blocks.text: Kansai Event report

blocks.section: Crêpe party in Kansai!
blocks.text: Crêpe party in Kansai!

blocks.section: Crêpe party in Kansai!
blocks.text: Candlemas is originally a religious holiday, but nowadays it is mostly the occasion to eat crêpes and... make new acquaintances!

blocks.section: Crêpe party in Kansai!
blocks.text: Being a crêpe enthusiast, it would have been a shame to miss such an opportunity to make and eat some!

blocks.section: Crêpe party in Kansai!
blocks.text: Considering how fast our 10 guests made the hundred crêpes ? prepared by yours truly disappear, they shared that belief. This dinner, which was meant to be relaxed and informal, was originally intended to animate our Osaka Business Center . Our goal is indeed to increase conviviality between all the representatives of our resident companies, which are renting the office space provided by the CCIFJ inside our walls.

blocks.section: Crêpe party in Kansai!
blocks.text: Our friends from Air France KLM did answer the call, but they were not alone to join us. Eventually many distinguished guests surrendered to the crêpes' perfume and came to Avanza to sit around the meeting table with us. The conference room had been turned into a dining room of sort for the occasion. Honey, chocolate, sugar, jam, ham & eggs: there was something for every taste. A few bottles, some of them graciously offered by Morikawa Clinic from Kobe, helped loosen the tongues and warm the atmosphere.

blocks.section: Crêpe party in Kansai!
blocks.text: Mr. Seiichirō Hayashi , our Ambassador of the Chamber in Kyoto and undisputed life of the party, amused everybody with his witticism, which would belong in a French salon. Always kind and quick, he offered that everyone attending the party would say a few words before leaving, so as to alleviate the melancholy of ending the evening. A news, an announcement, anything that would be worth sharing with the assistance. Everybody complied, and not only did it allow us to know each other better, but it also gave everyone a good chance to give some information regarding an upcoming event, a flagship product or a commercial campaign.

blocks.section: Crêpe party in Kansai!
blocks.text: After this final salutation, we all went our way, with a light heart and a heavy stomach.

blocks.section: Crêpe party in Kansai!
blocks.text: This might become a new tradition in Osaka!...

title: Looking Back at the Kansai Christmas Dinner 2022
description:
On Wednesday 7, we held our CCIFJ Kansai Christmas dinner at FAUCHON L'HOTEL KYOTO. Mr. Jules Irrmann, Consul General of France and Dr. Felix Moesner, Consul of Switzerland were kind enough to attend and delivered empowering and supportive speeches about positive local dynamics and international cooperation to come in the region, with the 2025 Universal Exhibition in focus.
Among nearly 30 guests, our local Ambassador of the Chamber in Kyoto, Max Hayashi, was able to get us Mr. Kodai Kuriyama, national Champion of Taekwondo and official member of the Japanese National Team.  The amazing 6 courses meal was prepared by Executive Chef Kohei Ichikawa, a friendly and energetic character trained by MOF Guy Lassausaie in Lyon. His dishes delighted all participants.  As Christmas presents, L'Auberge du Tanuki Noir provided a "Tour de France" of traditional candies from all regions, Morikawa Clinics gave therapeutic masks and Fauchon delivered their famous macarons. This was the perfect end to a somewhat busy year, with a warm and convivial Kansai gathering.  For those who could not come, see you next time! Many heartful thanks to all those who came, and of course Happy Holidays to all!?

title: Looking back at the Kansai International Meishi Exchange
description:
Conrad Osaka, May 28, 2025
On May 28, 2025, the Kansai International Meishi Exchange (KIME) was held at the Conrad Osaka and proved to be a great success, bringing together over 220 participants, including 30 members from the French Chamber. This event is part of a now-unmissable series that has grown significantly over the years, reflecting an impressive rise in scale and impact. What began as a modest initiative involving the American Chamber (ACCJ), the Kobe Chamber (KCCI), and the French Chamber (CCIFJ) has recently evolved into a major international gathering thanks in large part to the momentum generated by the Osaka Kansai World Expo. It is now supported by many chambers of commerce that have joined over the years, a momentum that was particularly reinforced since last October's G7 of Chambers of Commerce and Industry.
The evening was opened by Simone Thomsen, ACCJ Kansai Governor and President of Eli Lilly Japan, followed by remarks from Benoît Rulleau, our Kansai Board Member. A group photo captured this high-level gathering, bringing together, notably:
 	Vittorio Falconeri, Italien Chamber of Commerce Tokyo Counselor  	Benoit Rulleau, Representative Director and co-CEO of Kansai Airports, French Chamber Kansai Ambassador  	Keizo Yamada, Director - Kansai of the American Chamber of Commerce in Japan  	Jiro Kawakami, vice-président de l’ACCJ, 	Simone Thomsen, Group Vice President, President Eli Lilly Japan K.K. 	Kimiko Itō, Vice Chairperson of the Kobe Chamber of Commerce and Industry / Representative Director of Tashima & Co., Ltd. 	Paramjit Chadha, Honorary President of the Indian Chamber of Commerce, Japan  	Yavorska Kateryna, President of the Ukrainian Chamber of Commerce in Japan  	Yoshihiko Okabe, Honorary Consul of the Honorary Consulate of Ukraine in Kobe 	Brittany Banta, Principal Commercial Consul of the U.S. Consulate General Osaka-Kobe  	Mike Blyth, Consul-General of the British Consulate-General Osaka  	Jean-François Rauch, Directeur des antennes régionales de la CCI France Japon 
The Kampai was ultimately led by Mike Blyth, the British Consul General.

title: Looking back at the Networking Cocktail at the Heart of the France Pavilion

On Thursday, June 19, under a radiant sky, nearly 100 guests gathered at the heart of Osaka Expo 2025 for a unique event marked by networking opportunities, inspiring speeches from several renowned business leaders, and immersive visits to leading international pavilions.
The day began in the morning with the Chamber's monthly Board of Directors meeting, held behind closed doors, exceptionally taking place inside the France Pavilion itself to mark the occasion. The vitality of the French regions was acknowledged and praised by the board members in attendance.

It is also the result of several years of effort, coordination, and determination, led by the Chamber and its partners, to highlight our presence in this key region of Japan.

title: Looking back at the Private Preview of the exhibition "Woodcity QUINTESSENCE"
description:
On Tuesday, May 26th, CCI France Japon was thrilled to host a private preview of "Woodcity QUINTESSENCE", the first solo exhibition in Japan by French artist Laurent Minguet, presented by IKONO ART at Gallery Concept 21.
With Laurent Minguet himself on hand to welcome guests, the evening offered a rare opportunity to discover his remarkable WOODCITY series up close — hyperrealistic urban landscapes of New York, Paris, and Tokyo, painted directly onto fine timber. A truly unique artistic vision where material, gesture, and subject come together in a striking conversation.
It was a pleasure to share such an intimate and inspiring moment with our community. A special thank you to IKONO ART for making this exclusive preview possible. We look forward to welcoming you at our upcoming events!
The exhibition runs from May 26th to June 4th at Gallery Concept 21.

blocks.text: L'Oréal, France’s top 1 in gender equality

blocks.section: L'Oréal, France’s top 1 in gender equality
blocks.text: L’Oréal was ranked ninth in the world in terms of gender equality.

blocks.section: L'Oréal, France’s top 1 in gender equality
blocks.text: “We are very proud to once again be recognized for our long-standing commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion” (DE&I) said L'Oréal’s Chief Executive Officer.

blocks.section: L'Oréal, France’s top 1 in gender equality
blocks.text: At the beginning of March, L’Oréal was ranked ninth in the world according to the NGO Equilap's 2024 Global Gender Equality Ranking . The world’s largest cosmetics company was also named France’s best company for gender equality.

blocks.section: L'Oréal, France’s top 1 in gender equality
blocks.text: “The fact that we have made it into the top ten globally this year is testament to the hard work of everyone in our company ,” said Nicolas Ieronymus, general manager of L’Oréal, following the publication of the study.

blocks.section: L'Oréal, France’s top 1 in gender equality
blocks.text: The study by Dutch NGO Equilap evaluates companies in terms of gender equality on the basis of various criteriai ncluding: gender balance among senior managers and employees, the gender pay gap, parental leave, sexual harassment and supply chain policies.

blocks.section: L'Oréal, France’s top 1 in gender equality
blocks.text: The L’Oréal Foundation is also committed to gender equality through programs such as Inclusive Sourcing and For Women in Science, in partnership with UNESCO, to support women scientists.

blocks.section: L'Oréal, France’s top 1 in gender equality
blocks.text: At L’Oréal, women make up half the board of directors, 32% of the executive committee and 62% of international brand managers. In Japan, 54% of management positions are held by women.

title: LVMH - Explore the LOEWE x My Neighbor Totoro collaboration
description:
Inspired by Hayao Miyazaki’s film masterpiece My Neighbor Totoro, the latest capsule collection from Loewe celebrates the love of craft shared by the celebrated Spanish luxury house and Studio Ghibli. 
The result, LOEWE x My Neighbor Totoro, transports the protagonists of the movie onto a range of clothing, leather bags and accessories. The collection celebrates the poetry and immediacy of these characters’ iconography – qualities have made My Neighbor Totoro a true cultural landmark.
Studio Ghibli was a natural choice for Loewe’s latest collaboration given their mutual love of artisanal techniques.
The characters and images in the film have become timeless icons marked by poetic animation, fantastical adventures, environmental message and magnificent soundtracks. For Loewe Creative Director Jonathan Anderson, My Neighbor Totoro is the ultimate in heartwarming entertainment. The designer finds the friendship of the young heroines with the king of the forest, the magical Totoro and his mischievous susuwatari dust bunnies who can’t be seen by adults especially touching.
Characters from the animated film come to life on leather accessories such as wallets and pouches, plus the iconic LOEWE Puzzle, Balloon and Hammock bags. Tote bags are embellished with a tapestry technique, drawing on meticulous craftsmanship to recreate the world of My Neighbor Totoro. Studio Ghibli’s original drawings are interpreted for this collaboration with Loewe as prints, leather marquetry and jacquard intarsia, giving the collection a timeless and mythic feel.
“The message is one of dreamy serenity and hands-on creativity – of being at one with nature and with one’s own inner child,” says Jonathan Anderson. “This is especially important right now and, I think, always will be,” adds the designer. The LOEWE x My Neighbor Totoro collection is available in a limited edition at Loewe points of sale worldwide, including Le Bon Marché in Paris.

title: Madoka no Mori in Gōra, Hakone: a sustainable stay that awakens both the mind and the senses
description:
Located conveniently close to Tokyo, Gora in Hakone is nestled within lush natural surroundings. Here, you’ll find a traditional Japanese inn advocating a new concept of "Green Luxury"—this is Madoka no Mori. This inn upholds a philosophy of harmony with nature and contribution to a sustainable future. A stay here promises a one-of-a-kind experience that stimulates intellectual curiosity and deeply soothes the body and mind.
The Spirit and Philosophy Behind Madoka no Mori
Since its opening in 2014, Madoka no Mori has prioritized building meaningful "connections" with its guests—a value reflected in its very name. Hospitality infused with a "round heart" (a play on the word “Madoka,” meaning round or harmonious) provides each visitor with a warm, attentive, and sincere experience.
Madoka no Mori is more than just a place to stay; it embodies a philosophy of connecting people with nature and the future—a place where new value is born.
Living in Harmony with Nature: The Origin
The inn’s deep commitment to the environment was catalyzed by a major natural disaster in 2019. As a result of this disaster, the historic Sounkaku, which had been in operation since 1925, was forced to close. However, this event became a turning point that deepened the recognition of nature’s power, blessings, and preciousness.
Since then, Madoka no Mori has pursued a vision of a sustainable inn that lives in gratitude and harmony with the natural world.
A Culinary Experience that Opens the Future: Innovative Hydrogen Cooking
The cuisine at Madoka no Mori combines environmental consciousness with supreme flavor through an innovative method—hydrogen cooking. At the in-house restaurant Kappo Mugen, this CO₂-free cooking technique enhances the natural umami of seasonal ingredients.
The head chef and proprietress handpick ingredients from across Japan, transforming them into dishes that are crispy on the outside and incredibly juicy inside, thanks to hydrogen heat and expert technique. It’s a gastronomic experience that stimulates both intellect and the senses, while also being kind to the planet.
Commitment to Sustainability: Responsibility to Future Generations
Madoka no Mori is strengthening its sustainability efforts through various initiatives:
Moving away from combustion-based energy: In addition to hydrogen cooking, the inn uses bio-technology-based food waste processors to actively reduce waste.Transitioning away from plastic: By rethinking materials for drink bottles and amenities, the inn is reducing single-use plastics and minimizing environmental impact.
Madoka no Mori not only offers guests enriching moments, but also presents a new style of travel that contributes to the future of our planet.
Experience refined “Green Luxury” at Madoka no Mori:https://madokanomori.gorahanaougi.com/

blocks.text: Maison Duculty : a successful export story

blocks.section: Maison Duculty : a successful export story
blocks.text: Renowned for its outstanding charcuterie, Maison Duculty turned to the Business Support service of CCI France Japan to enter the Japanese market.

blocks.section: Maison Duculty : a successful export story
blocks.text: Charcutiers for several generations, Maison Duculty has been producing high quality charcuterie in the Lyon region for many years.

blocks.section: Maison Duculty : a successful export story
blocks.text: Having long held a personal interest in Japan, Gaëtan Duculty, Managing Director of the company, turned his attention to this market with the aim of sharing his products in Japan. Quickly faced with the difficulties of importing such products and it should be recalled that Japanese regulations are very strict when it comes to charcuterie he decided to call on the Business Support service of CCI France Japan to assist him in his efforts.

blocks.section: A prospecting mission tailored to his sector
blocks.text: A prospecting mission tailored to his sector

blocks.section: A prospecting mission tailored to his sector
blocks.text: Thanks to his region’s Go Export program, he was able to quickly identify his needs. CCI France Japan then organized business meetings for him during the France Week event, which brings together French product exporters at the renowned Isetan department store in Tokyo.

blocks.section: A prospecting mission tailored to his sector
blocks.text: “ CCI prepared eight highly qualified business meetings for me. This allowed me to very precisely identify the work that needed to be done in order to import my products. It was also an opportunity to establish contacts with importers, an essential gateway to selling my products in Japan ”, Gaëtan Duculty tells us.

blocks.section: A prospecting mission tailored to his sector
blocks.text: Upon his return, he wasted no time and complied with the country’s requirements. He quickly implemented the expected standards along the production chain and prepared an application for approval.

blocks.section: A prospecting mission tailored to his sector
blocks.text: Exports are still exclusive and limited to the hotel and restaurant sector, but Gaëtan Duculty hopes to soon be able to distribute his products to the Japanese general public. He was also present at the French Week organized at Isetan, where his charcuterie products enjoyed real success with Japanese consumers.

blocks.text: He also leads the Philosophy for Responsible Innovation program at the Institut Catholique de Paris. blocks.section: Mathieu Martin - CCIFJ Fukui Ambassador
blocks.text: CCIFJ ambassador for Fukui prefecture, Mathieu Martin is responsible for French, German, and American markets at Hironen Co., Ltd.

blocks.section: Mathieu Martin - CCIFJ Fukui Ambassador
blocks.text: Mathieu Martin, a 40-year-old native of Vendée, France, has been living in Japan for 17 years and serves as the CCIFJ Ambassador for the Fukui region. A graduate of a textile engineering school, he first established ties with Fukui during a university exchange. He later began his career there after completing his final-year internship in the area.

blocks.section: Mathieu Martin - CCIFJ Fukui Ambassador
blocks.text: For more than eight years, he has worked as a Technical Sales Representative at Hironen Co., LTD., a textile company where he manages the French, German, and American markets. One of his most significant achievements was seeing a product he developed displayed in a storefront on Madison Avenue in New York City.

blocks.section: Mathieu Martin - CCIFJ Fukui Ambassador
blocks.text: Becoming an ambassador was a stroke of luck, according to him, and he has seized the opportunity to leverage his experience and network to benefit the Chamber. His goal is to increase the CCIFJ's visibility among Fukui's textile companies and to strengthen ties with the local Franco-Japanese association, thereby bringing France and the region even closer together.

title: Mazars appoints Jean Francois Salzmann as the new Managing Partner for Japan
description:
Mazars Japan announced that Jean Francois Salzmann has been elected as the new Managing Partner of Mazars in Japan succeeding Emmanuel Thierry, who will take a new leadership role at Mazars France, covering Sustainability Audit services in Europe. With three decades of fervent experience in professional service industry, Jean François will ensure that Mazars in Japan continues to deliver top-quality services to clients and drive the growth of Mazars in Japan managing day-to-day business operations as well as its planned strategic expansion in Japan and the APAC region.
Jean Francois joined Mazars in 1998 and has been a renowned and seasoned leader in various Mazars country offices which include France, Germany as well as setting up office in Czech Republic and Slovakia and before he became the monitor of Mazars Central Europe activities. Having successfully organised his succession, he became managing partner in Mainland China in 2010 driving the practice to over 5,000 professionals. He is a member of the Mazars APAC board responsible among other for Financial Advisory services, Northern Asia, as well as for ERP global roll out.
With his current appointment, he said: “I have immense respect for what Emmanuel and Mazars in Japan have been able to build and achieve thus far, and I am looking forward to working with the team to expand the business even further. What drew me to this role is the ability to apply all of my previous experiences to building on Mazars in Japan’s outstanding commitment to its people and clients.  
PRESS RELEASE
MAZARS JAPAN

title: ME.LAND : French shoes brand
description:
CCI France Japan and Business France had the pleasure of organizing a mission in October 2023 on behalf of the French Federation of Footwear. The purpose of this mission was to prospect for a delegation of 7 companies and to arrange qualitative meetings for them. A showroom presenting French brands to Japanese prospects was also set up, making good use of l’Espace at the CCI France Japan.

It was during this mission that ME.LAND, one of the French brands, was able to establish connections with certain Japanese prospects. These connections quickly led to an order and discussions with new partners. It is noteworthy here the particular speed with which the contract was concluded, unusual for the Japanese market. This illustrates that when supply and demand complement each other perfectly, discussions can progress rapidly.

As a result, since April 2024, the French brand ME.LAND has been present in around ten stores of its Japanese distributor.

Here are some feedbacks from Frédéric Robert, Designer, Director of Operations, and Co-founder of the brand:
"This mission was a great opportunity, and we are very pleased with it. Japan is a strategic country for advancing our distribution in Asia. In addition to the current partnership, we have other ongoing exchanges with potential partners that could lead to new orders. The teams of Business France and CCIFJ have done a really good job. Thanks to them for understanding our expectations and needs so well."

"What struck me the most during this mission was the professionalism and market knowledge of the Business France and CCIFJ teams. They have a privileged relationship with local distributors or agents and are truly valuable for brand development. Once again, I want to thank them for the extraordinary work done on-site in such a short time."

Frédéric ROBERT
Designer, Director of Operations, and Co-founder

title: Message from the President of the CCI France Japon
description:
The CCI France Japan is deeply saddened by the news of the death, in tragic circumstances, of former Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe.
Few Japanese leaders have meant as much to France as Shinzo Abe. The former Prime Minister saw the country as an anchor in Europe, but also as a bridge to Africa and a vital voice at the United Nations. He had a sincere familiarity with his French interlocutors, from all walks of life, which greatly benefited diplomatic, commercial and simply human exchanges between our two countries.
Fighting against the protectionist forces at work in his opposition and even in his own inner circle, Shinzo Abe used much of his political capital to impose the historic JEFTA (Japan-EU Free Trade Agreement) between his country and the European Union, which came into force in 2019, with French companies among the beneficiaries. "The signing of the economic partnership agreement has so far had a positive impact on France's foreign trade with Japan (significant increase in wine and dairy exports), even if its full implementation remains an issue (residual presence of non-tariff barriers). During the first ten months following its entry into force, French exports to Japan (+18%) outperformed European exports, which were almost stable (6%).  Trade has increased in both directions and the effects of the agreement are perceived positively on the Japanese side," notes the Senate in an April 2021 report.
As an enthusiastic supporter of the triennial TICAD conference, which brings together Japan and dozens of African countries, he understood the decisive role of France on this continent.
Wishing to raise Japan's role at the UN by obtaining a seat as a permanent member of its Security Council, Shinzo Abe had found support in France. He also recognized in France, the only European power with a large military presence in the Indo-Pacific, an important partner in maintaining security in "his" region of the world.
The sheer number of times that Shinzo Abe visited France attests to the importance that he attached to that country. "It had been seven years since a Japanese head of government had visited France. Seven years ago, his name was already Shinzo Abe," said François Hollande when he received him in Paris in 2014, referring to his first stint as prime minister in 2007. Until 2019, Shinzo Abe visited Paris at least once a year to meet his French counterpart.
But it was on the economic and cultural level that the relationship was richest. Shinzo Abe saw France, the world's leading tourist destination, as a "gateway" that would place his country at the top of the list of "destinations". Thus, he had initiated, and richly endowed, a year of Japanese cultural events in France in 2018, under the title "Japonismes". Other popular world events are also taking place, in France and Japan consecutively: the Rugby World Cup, in Japan in 2019 and then in France in 2023; the Olympic and Paralympic Games in Japan in 2021, then in France in 2024.
This was the meaning of the renewal in 2013 of the "exceptional partnership" between France and Japan, a document that frames and encourages Franco-Japanese relations and whose three axes are, in order: economy, security, culture. Its "roadmap" is due to be renewed in 2023.
In Japan, his voluntarist policy known as "Abenomics" revived economic activity and benefited the member companies of the CCI France Japon.
In the hope of the future fruits of this work, we send our most sincere condolences, in these tragic circumstances, to the family and friends of Shinzo Abe.  
Jérôme Chouchan, president of the CCI France Japon

blocks.text: Supporting companies in financing (loans and guarantees)

blocks.section: Supporting companies in financing (loans and guarantees)
blocks.text: METI will provide financing support for businesses affected by the expansion of the novel coronavirus disease.

blocks.section: Supporting companies in financing (loans and guarantees)
blocks.text: No.4 and No.5 Safety Nets for Financing Guarantee

blocks.section: Supporting companies in financing (loans and guarantees)
blocks.text: No. 4: If an SME is runs a business in a designated area in which a wide variety of industries are affected by the disease and it faces a decline in sales of 20% or more from the previous year, it is eligible to make use of a financing guarantee for the full loan amount under a framework of up to 280 million yen, which is separate from a general financing guarantee.

blocks.section: Supporting companies in financing (loans and guarantees)
blocks.text: On March 2 (Mon.), METI designated all prefectures across Japan as target areas subject to the No.4 Safety Net for Financing Guarantee (February 28).

blocks.section: Supporting companies in financing (loans and guarantees)
blocks.text: No.5: If an SME is a business in an industry particularly severely affected by the disease and it faces a decline in sales of 5% or more from the previous year, it is eligible to make use of a financing guarantee of 80% of the loan amount under a framework of up to 280 million yen, which is separate from a general financing guarantee.

blocks.section: Supporting companies in financing (loans and guarantees)
blocks.text: On March 3 (Tue.), METI decided to designate an additional 40 industries as eligible for the financing program, including accommodations and hotels, eateries, restaurants and fitness centers (March 3).

blocks.section: Supporting companies in financing (loans and guarantees)
blocks.text: On March 11 (Wed.), METI decided to designate an additional 316 industries as eligible for the financing program, such as dairy product manufacturers and hair-dressing and beauty salons (March 11).

blocks.section: Supporting companies in financing (loans and guarantees)
blocks.text: Guarantee Related to Emergencies: If an SME in any industry across Japan* faces a decline in sales of 15% or more from the previous year, it is eligible to make use of a financing guarantee of the full loan amount under a framework of up to 280 million yen, which is separate from a general financing guarantee.

blocks.section: Supporting companies in financing (loans and guarantees)
blocks.text: *Note: These industries must fall under the industries subject to the Credit Guarantee System.

blocks.section: Supporting companies in financing (loans and guarantees)
blocks.text: METI decided to implement the Guarantee Related to Emergencies in addition to the Safety Nets for Financing Guarantee (March 11).
