title: Microsoft to invest nearly $3 billion in Japan to improve its AI data centers
description: This is the American company's largest-ever investment in an Asian country.

blocks.text: Foresight

blocks.section: Microsoft to invest nearly $3 billion in Japan to improve its AI data centers
blocks.text: Microsoft to invest nearly $3 billion in Japan to improve its AI data centers

blocks.section: Microsoft to invest nearly $3 billion in Japan to improve its AI data centers
blocks.text: This is the American company's largest-ever investment in an Asian country.

blocks.section: Microsoft to invest nearly $3 billion in Japan to improve its AI data centers
blocks.text: American IT giant Microsoft is set to invest nearly $3 billion (440 billion yen; almost 2.7 billion euros) over two years to expand its data centers in Japan.

blocks.section: Microsoft to invest nearly $3 billion in Japan to improve its AI data centers
blocks.text: The announcement was made during Fumio Kishida's official visit to the United States . This is the first visit by a Japanese leader in nine years, as the two countries deepen their relationship against the backdrop of China's growing assertiveness in the Indo-Pacific region.

blocks.section: Microsoft to invest nearly $3 billion in Japan to improve its AI data centers
blocks.text: This is not only Microsoft's biggest investment in Japan, but also its biggest investment in an Asian country.

blocks.section: Microsoft to invest nearly $3 billion in Japan to improve its AI data centers
blocks.text: In an exclusive interview with NHK , Microsoft's Chairman emphasized the importance of AI-related investments in Japan: “Japan has a huge technology base, but the population is shrinking due to the aging population. It is essential for Japan to harness the power of AI [...] I believe this is an indispensable investment for Japan's future ” has he declared.

blocks.section: Microsoft to invest nearly $3 billion in Japan to improve its AI data centers
blocks.text: The data centers will incorporate state-of-the-art semiconductors and other equipment suited to the development and operation of artificial intelligence, capable of processing large amounts of computation.

blocks.section: Microsoft to invest nearly $3 billion in Japan to improve its AI data centers
blocks.text: Microsoft will also expand its digital training program to train just over three million people in AI over the next three years.

blocks.section: Microsoft to invest nearly $3 billion in Japan to improve its AI data centers
blocks.text: According to forecasts by the Japan Federation of Electronics and Information Technology Industries (JEITA), the demand for AI-related services generated in Japan is set to increase by around 15 times year-on-year, reaching almost 1,770 billion yen by 2030.

blocks.section: Monaco & Japan: A Partnership for the Future
blocks.text: During our interview, Pierre-André Chiappori, Monaco’s Minister of Economy and Finance, honored us by sharing his vision for the Principality’s economic future. He emphasized Monaco’s strong ambition to enhance its international appeal by building close ties with countries at the forefront of technology, culture, and innovation — starting with Japan. Promising projects are underway, including a tax treaty to avoid double taxation between the two countries, which could be finalized by the end of the year. Mr. Chiappori also highlighted Monaco’s many advantages: a strategic location in Europe, exceptional safety, high quality of life, and a responsive administration dedicated to supporting development.

title: Montblanc: the centenary of the Meisterstück collection
description: Montblanc’s iconic Meisterstück celebrates its 100th anniversary this year.

blocks.text: Companies news

blocks.section: Montblanc: the centenary of the Meisterstück collection
blocks.text: Montblanc: the centenary of the Meisterstück collection

blocks.section: Montblanc: the centenary of the Meisterstück collection
blocks.text: Montblanc’s iconic Meisterstück celebrates its 100th anniversary this year.

blocks.section: Montblanc: the centenary of the Meisterstück collection
blocks.text: Richemont Japan K.K. This year, Montblanc celebrates the centenary of the Meisterstück, a veritable jewel in the culture of writing.

blocks.section: Montblanc: the centenary of the Meisterstück collection
blocks.text: The origins of Montblanc

blocks.section: Montblanc: the centenary of the Meisterstück collection
blocks.text: Contrary to what the Montblanc brand name might suggest, the company was founded in Germany at the beginning of the 20th century.

blocks.section: Montblanc: the centenary of the Meisterstück collection
blocks.text: Three friends from Hamburg (Alfred Nehemias, August Eberstein and Claus Voss) met regularly to exchange ideas. It was during these discussions that they came up with the idea of creating a pen with its own ink reservoir .

blocks.section: Montblanc: the centenary of the Meisterstück collection
blocks.text: The first “fountain pen” model was born after three years of intense research, with the launch of the “Rouge et Noir” collection, echoing the game of roulette. The project was a rapid success, leading the three friends to register their own trademark: the Montblanc brand was born.

blocks.section: Montblanc: the centenary of the Meisterstück collection
blocks.text: The name Montblanc was chosen because the brand would be, in the words of its creators, “the pinnacle of writing instruments.” The visual identity and logo reinforce this ambition, with a white six-pointed star referring to the six glaciers of the mountain range.

blocks.section: Montblanc: the centenary of the Meisterstück collection
blocks.text: The fountain pen, a luxury object

blocks.section: Montblanc: the centenary of the Meisterstück collection
blocks.text: Montblanc breaks the codes of luxury, making the fountain pen an object in its own right. The number of models multiplied, culminating in the launch of its emblematic Meisterstück collection - word in German for “masterpiece.” The brand broke new luxury codes by making the fountain pen an object in its own right.

blocks.section: Montblanc: the centenary of the Meisterstück collection
blocks.text: The Meisterstück aesthetic is characterized by its 18-carat gold nib: the pen is no longer just an everyday object, but a sign of distinction.

blocks.section: Montblanc: the centenary of the Meisterstück collection
blocks.text: The Meisterstück collection, a true objet d'art

blocks.section: Montblanc: the centenary of the Meisterstück collection
blocks.text: You've probably come across this Meisterstück fountain pen somewhere. Since its creation, the emblematic Mesiterstück collection has been used by many celebrities: J.F. Kennedy, Nelson Mandela, Yoko Ono…

blocks.section: Montblanc: the centenary of the Meisterstück collection
blocks.text: Since its inception, limited editions have multiplied in number, some reaching prices in excess of €10,000. Over the years, the German house has created even rarer pieces, including a limited edition with ten Taj Mahal pieces (sold for almost €2 million) or a pen covered with precious stones, gold and black diamonds, sold at auction for eight million dollars.

blocks.section: Montblanc: the centenary of the Meisterstück collection
blocks.text: To celebrate the collection's centenary, a limited edition “The Origin Collection” has been launched. Each nib is specially designed with the insignia “100”; “1924”; “2024” and the cap ring features a special sign.

title: Morgan Chaudeler – CCIFJ Ambassador for Chubu
description:
Morgan Chaudeler serves as the CCIFJ Ambassador for the Chubu region and is the President & Representative Director of Aichi International Convention & Exhibition venue in Japan. 
Morgan Chaudeler serves as the CCIFJ Ambassador for the Chubu region and is the President & Representative Director of Aichi International Convention & Exhibition Center Co., Ltd. (Aichi Sky Expo), the 4th largest exhibition venue in Japan.
Based in Japan for over 25 years, he graduated from Paris Dauphine University and INALCO. His career spans auditing and consulting (Andersen, Ernst & Young), the luxury industry (LVMH, Hermès, Petit Bateau), and the management of concessions and public-private partnerships (Vinci Airports, GL events). These experiences have provided him with a unique expertise in the governance of complex organizations, combining strong Japanese language skills with deep intercultural understanding.
After contributing to the privatization of Kansai, Itami, and Kobe airports, he launched Aichi Sky Expo in 2019, Japan’s first concession-based exhibition center, where he built a team of 27 people within one year in close cooperation with Aichi Prefecture.
As CCIFJ Ambassador, he works to strengthen ties between France and the Chubu region, a strategic hub of the Japanese economy. In 2024, he contributed to the launch of the Smart Manufacturing Summit and is already preparing for the 2026.

title: MORPHEE+: a real-time fall detection system serving patients and healthcare facilities
description:
Morphée+, founded on May 3, 2018 in Dijon, develops and markets the electromagnetic device of the same name: a real-time monitoring and fall detection system that enhances the safety and well-being of residents in nursing homes (EHPAD – Residential Care Facilities for Dependent Elderly People) as well as patients living at home.
In 2014, Bruno Duperrier, Chief Executive Officer of the company CERIG and an expert in the field of senior care, came up with the idea of confronting the current and future needs of elderly people with the technologies available at the time. Thus, the innovative Morphée+ project was born. It is the only fall detection system that protects the privacy of elderly individuals and the confidentiality of care procedures—thanks to the absence of image capture—while also addressing the issue of forgetting or rejecting wearable sensors, which are often invasive for patients.
Beyond instantly alerting caregivers or healthcare professionals to falls and worrying health parameters, the Morphée+ device helps reduce healthcare-related costs by anticipating the onset or worsening of illnesses and by automating part of data recording and monitoring.
Winner of the 2017 OCS Innovation Award (connected objects and health applications) in Dijon and the 2018 Jury’s Special Prize from the French Society of Telemedicine, SNITEM, and the Medicen competitiveness cluster—to name just a few—selected for the “innovation village serving living systems” at the 2017 Supélec TEDx conference, and chosen in February 2019 to join the X-UP accelerator at École Polytechnique, Morphée+ has a promising future ahead, both nationally and internationally.
A Franco-Japanese collaboration with a promising future
In November 2018, Morphée+ traveled to Tokyo—alongside other companies led by the Bourgogne–Franche-Comté delegation—to take part in the “100 SMEs” mission organized by CCI France Japan. It was during this mission that the Dijon-based company met its future partner, Z-Works, a Japanese firm specializing in IoT solutions, particularly for the medical and social care sectors. Subsequent exchanges allowed the two companies to build trust, identify strong complementarities, and naturally led to a shared desire to collaborate.
This partnership between Morphée+ and Z-Works is expected to result in even more reliable, innovative, and integrated solutions—a true “win-win” for both companies, but also “creating significant added value for patients, healthcare facilities, and various organizations in the medical and social sectors (mutual insurers, insurance companies, etc.),” according to Bruno Duperrier. “Without the ‘100 SMEs’ mission organized by CCI France Japan, there would have been no partnership in the Japanese archipelago,” the business leader told us, expressing his satisfaction with the services and support provided by the CCI France Japan teams. He emphasizes the “relevance and suitability” of the business meetings scheduled for his company during the event.
Bruno Duperrier extends particular thanks to Z-Works CEO Tatsuya Takahashi and his team for their trust, as well as to Pierre-Olivier Ghintran (Director of CCI International Bourgogne–Franche-Comté) for introducing him to the subtleties of the Japanese market and inspiring him to develop Morphée+’s activities in the Land of the Rising Sun.
The “100 SMEs” initiative, along with other events, made it possible to celebrate 2018 with distinction and professionalism—a year that marked the centenary of CCI France Japan (1918–2018) and the 160th anniversary of Franco-Japanese diplomatic and commercial relations.

title: Itinéraires singuliers – Cyril Coppini: From a Passion for Kanji to the Stage of the Olympia, 25 Years of Performance and Translation in Japan
description:
Cyril Coppini could have become a Japanese language teacher in France. Instead, the life of the southern French native took an unexpected turn when he discovered rakugo, the traditional Japanese storytelling art that originated during the Edo period, in which a lone performer kneels on a cushion to tell humorous or dramatic stories.
Today, as a renowned manga translator, including the famous Detective Conan, and the only French rakugo performer based in Japan, he embodies a unique cultural bridge between France and Japan.
“Whatever choices we make, we will always face obstacles. So we might as well devote our energy to what truly matters to us.”
Falling in Love with the Japanese Language
Cyril Coppini discovered Japanese as a teenager, almost by chance, after choosing it as an elective subject at school. From his very first lesson, he was captivated by the beauty and complexity of Japanese writing.
Soon afterwards, he visited Japan for the first time through a school exchange program. There, he experienced firsthand the gap between the Japanese taught in classrooms and the language spoken in everyday life, while discovering the country's remarkable cultural and linguistic richness.
He went on to pursue advanced studies in Japanese before returning to live in Japan. Despite his strong academic background, he came to realize that true language mastery is acquired above all through daily life and direct interaction with local people.
Rakugo: From Osaka to the Olympia
Cyril Coppini first discovered rakugo on television. In 2009, he began studying the art in Osaka while continuing his professional career. Two years later, he gave his first public performance. As he did not follow the traditional apprenticeship required of professional Japanese rakugo storytellers, he describes himself as a "rakugo performer" rather than a master, a position that gives him greater creative freedom when introducing the art abroad.
His work as a translator, where rendering Japanese humour and wordplay presents constant challenges, has led him to reject literal translation in favour of thoughtful cultural adaptation. This experience has also enabled him to tailor his performances to audiences in multiple languages.
From 2016 onwards, he began adapting and translating his stories for non-Japanese-speaking audiences. Their enthusiastic reception demonstrated that rakugo's distinctive humour and storytelling tradition can resonate with audiences around the world.
He notably delivered a memorable performance at the Olympia in Paris, a venue comparable in prestige to Japan's National Theatre stages. In 2025, he also performed at the France Pavilion during Expo 2025 Osaka, bringing his stories to life before a predominantly Japanese audience.
25 Years in Japan and Looking Ahead
After more than 25 years in Japan, Cyril Coppini has witnessed the country's gradual internationalisation. Today, he also performs in English to meet the growing interest of international audiences eager to discover rakugo. His ambition is to keep the art alive beyond its traditional settings, which can sometimes feel inaccessible to younger generations, notably by developing masterclasses.
For Cyril Coppini, the most important thing is to pursue what one truly loves while accepting that the journey will inevitably be filled with challenges. In his view, the pursuit of absolute stability is an illusion. After all, the stories of mistakes and failures often become the funniest ones to tell, provided that we continue moving forward with our goals firmly in sight.
He concludes:
“Deep down, nobody really knows what stability is. That's precisely why it's better to follow the path that genuinely draws you. That doesn't mean wandering aimlessly for years, though. It's important to have a clear direction, a core conviction that guides your decisions.”
HACHETTE COLLECTIONS JAPAN KK
Hachette Collections Japan K.K., part of the Hachette Livre group, publishes partwork series that spark curiosity and invite people to discover, create, and learn. Available through retail and subscription channels, its range includes model kits, handicraft series, and collectible items, offering a hands-on experience through assembling, creating, and learning.
This year, the group celebrates its bicentenary, sharing the richness of time through knowledge, creativity, and the joy of discovery creativity, and the joy of discovery.

title: Nailmatic : a young, innovative cosmetics company 100% made in France
description:
Company overview
Nailmatic is a young, innovative cosmetics company 100% made in France, founded in Paris in November 2012. This Paris based company quickly stood out from its competitors thanks to the unprecedented creation of a vending machine used to sell its nail polishes. But that is not all. Beyond this original distribution concept, the company also offers ethical and eco responsible products.
Shortly after the launch of its first vending machine at the Citadium Paris store in 2012, Nailmatic’s “color vending machine” began to find its place in major Parisian department stores such as Printemps Haussmann, BHV Le Marais, and Galeries Lafayette. In 2014, Nailmatic was awarded by the Paris Dauphine Commercial Innovation Observatory, receiving the prize for best customer strategy. That same year, the company decided to launch a new product range specifically designed for children, featuring responsible and bio sourced formulas.
What about Japan?
“We began to take an interest in exporting in 2015. As Japan is the reference country when it comes to vending machines, exporting our products there seemed like an obvious choice,” explains Stéphane Philip, Export Manager at Nailmatic.
Aware of the complexity of the Japanese market, Nailmatic turned directly to CCI France Japan in its search for a new partner to distribute its women’s product range in Japan. Following its request, CCI France Japan proposed an individual mission in February 2016, which led to several meetings with three different prospects, including National Vending Co LTD. Since that initial meeting, Nailmatic has built strong ties and maintained a solid relationship of trust with this partner, notably through multiple meetings in France and in Japan. “We would not have been able to build these relationships so easily without the help of our on site translator and interpreter,” Stéphane Philip emphasizes.
At the beginning of the partnership, only 20 vending machines were sold, but everything accelerated in 2019. That year, National Vending Co LTD decided to purchase 60,000 euros worth of vending machines and 50,000 euros worth of products from the women’s range, for a total turnover of 110,000 euros. At the same time, the Japanese partner decided to hire two people to manage this business segment. “It is a real pleasure to work with the Japanese, and we are very happy with our partnership with National Vending Co LTD,” says Nailmatic’s Export Manager, adding that “orders are becoming increasingly regular, and we estimate the value of upcoming orders at 100,000 euros excluding vending machines.”
Nailmatic returned to Japan for nine days, from June 22 to 30, 2019, for the exceptional opening of a pop up shop in one of Tokyo’s trendiest districts, Omotesando. The event welcomed many visitors, journalists, and influencers, providing yet another opportunity to shine a spotlight on Nailmatic’s well known products and vending machines in the capital of the Land of the Rising Sun.

title: Nara International Film Festival 2020, to be held in September
description:
As film and other cultural projects around the world have been greatly impacted by COVID-19, the Nara International Film Festival (now in its tenth year) will establish a new kind of film festival with a strong emphasis on safety, and is planning to hold the festival this September 18th (Friday) through the 22nd (Tuesday).
Screening films from young, up-and-coming directors of not only Japan, but also France, India, Korea, Catalunya, Malaysia, Russia, and many other countries, this festival is a chance to see many films would not normally be released to the public, all in their original language with Japanese subtitles and centered around the World Heritage sites of Nara. Become a Red Carpet Club member, and after walking this year’s red carpet at Todai-ji Temple’s Great Buddha Hall (Daibutsuden), you’ll have unlimited access to the monthly film screenings of Nara Cinematheque in Nara City by showing your membership card.
About the Nara International Film Festival
Marking 1,300 years since the capital of Japan was moved to Nara, the Nara International Film Festival began in 2010 with film director Naomi Kawase as its executive director. Based around the four pillars of sharing the beauty and culture of film, discovering young creators, developing the film people of the future, and intercultural exchange through film, our mission is to connect Nara with the rest of the world through film.

blocks.section: Naomi Kawase, Executive Director, Nara International Film Festival
blocks.text: Naomi Kawase, Executive Director, Nara International Film Festival

blocks.section: Naomi Kawase, Executive Director, Nara International Film Festival
blocks.text: Nara is god’s nursery, with deer and humans happily living together in this town of so much world heritage. In this town, we are cultivating four nurseries through film. The first is the actual festival, a sacred time. The second is Nara Cinematheque, a regular “ordinary” event. The third is the NARAtive project, which connects the sacred with the “ordinary”. The fourth is the Youth Cinema Project, a time for a time that is yet to come. We have all of those ideas in this nursery, and it has a door to the world. In 2020, people all around the world have felt the threat of this small virus. However, it is because this is such a difficult time that we decided to sow our seeds in our nursery again this year. It is because now, more than ever, is the time to open the doors from this nursery to the rest of the world, and realize these connections that literally cross borders. It is also because I would like to reaffirm my pride in Japan. We are all passengers riding on the same ship known as Earth. The radiance of art rests in the hearts of all 7.8 billion people, and I wish for that radiance to brighten the world. I hope we can all cultivate this nursery together.

blocks.section: Satoko Nakano, President, Nara International Film Festival
blocks.text: Satoko Nakano, President, Nara International Film Festival

blocks.section: Satoko Nakano, President, Nara International Film Festival
blocks.text: I would sincerely like to thank you for all of the kind words you have offered the Nara International Film Festival. It is thanks to you that 12 years have passed since we started this organization, and 10 years since we held our first film festival. In that time, we have had so many new encounters that have crossed both oceans and generations, all through film. I have been able to witness new works being created as well. It has been a path full of both thrills and miracles. Though there were some tough moments, being able to hold this festival has brought me such a deep happiness every time, and I am very grateful for all of your support that has allowed us to continue to move forward with our high goals. As we approach our 6th biennial festival, the world has been put into an unprecedented situation. With talk of a new normal, we have had plenty of time to stop and think deeply about all of this. As Nara is a place where the divine, natural, and people live in harmony, a film festival that reaches from Nara out to the rest of the world is needed now more than ever. That is the thought that I arrived at. With all of our experiences so far, I feel very strongly about delivering a “new” Nara International Film Festival to the world now. Thank you for all of your understanding and cooperation.

title: Nearly 40% of payments in Japan are now cashless
description: Cashless payments have increased by 3 percentage points compared to 2022.

blocks.text: Foresight

blocks.section: Nearly 40% of payments in Japan are now cashless
blocks.text: Nearly 40% of payments in Japan are now cashless

blocks.section: Nearly 40% of payments in Japan are now cashless
blocks.text: Cashless payments have increased by 3 percentage points compared to 2022.

blocks.section: Nearly 40% of payments in Japan are now cashless
blocks.text: Cashless payment methods (credit cards, transport cards, QR codes, debit cards) are on the rise in Japan.

blocks.section: Nearly 40% of payments in Japan are now cashless
blocks.text: According to a survey published on March 29 by the Japan Credit Association, cashless payment methods increased year-on-year, involving payments of 126,000 billion yen (around 771 billion euros).

blocks.section: Nearly 40% of payments in Japan are now cashless
blocks.text: These payment methods were popularized during the Covid pandemic . Today, they are up 12 percentage points in 2019 (28.8% of transactions).

blocks.section: Nearly 40% of payments in Japan are now cashless
blocks.text: The acceleration of cashless payments is a matter of public policy in Japan, with a stated government target of 40% of total transactions by 2025 .

blocks.section: Nearly 40% of payments in Japan are now cashless
blocks.text: There are many challenges to the adoption of cashless payments . The use of digital payment methods frees up labor in a country where it is in short supply.

blocks.section: Nearly 40% of payments in Japan are now cashless
blocks.text: The evolution of payment infrastructures has also helped to popularize this practice: a large number of payment methods can now be managed by a single machine, as can the choice of payment methods in stores.

blocks.section: Nearly 40% of payments in Japan are now cashless
blocks.text: However, the increase in cashless payment methods also means an increase in fraud, which will amount to 54 billion yen (nearly 330 million euros) in 2023 alone.

blocks.section: Nearly 40% of payments in Japan are now cashless
blocks.text: Japan still lags behind its neighbors : 80% of payments are cashless in China and 90% in Korea. In the United States and the United Kingdom, the figure is also over 50%.

title: New domestic travel subsidy program - SHARE YOUR OFFER
description:
Japan launched its new domestic travel subsidy program from Oct. 11 to late December as part of efforts to spur domestic tourism and revive the coronavirus-hit economy.
The "National Travel Discount" offers a 40% discount on travel costs, up to a maximum of 8,000 yen/person per night for a trip using public transportation (train/subway, bus, airplane, etc.) and 5,000 yen for a trip other than that (without using public transport or accommodation only), with local coupons that can be used at restaurants, souvenir shops, etc. worth 3,000 yen on weekdays and 1,000 yen on weekends.
The National Travel Discount program, which is available to Japan residents only, comes in the wake of the "Go To Travel" subsidy program and expands on similar existing programs operating at the prefectural level.
For the occasion, the CCI France Japon offers its members a way to communicate on their special offer or on their establishment with many attractive and affordable options!

title: New members honored at a welcome evening cocktail at KPMG (KPMG Tokyo Ignition)
description:
The French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan was pleased to organize the semi-annual welcome evening for its new members on July 23rd to welcome them to our business community and bring them together. They first had the opportunity to present their activities to all the participants, followed by a networking session.
We would like to express our gratitude to our member KPMG for allowing us to hold this event at their premises (KPMG Tokyo Ignition) and for their contribution to the smooth running of the evening.
A big thank you also to the participants: Bambuser Japan, Biesse Japan KK, Bull Co. Ltd, CarpeDiem Co. Ltd, CL by C. Lemaire, Cuvée J2 Hotel Osaka, Doki Doki Travel K.K., Hotel Heidi Co., Ltd. Hotel de l'Alpage, Naskeo Kankyo Co., Ltd, Nissin Corporation, Noppui, Platanus Inc., Tomei Diamond Co., Ltd, Mr. Keita Kawamura, Ms. Takizawa Nagisa, and Mr. Noriyasu Shimoyama.
To join the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan and participate in the next event for our new members, please contact membership(@)ccifj.or.jp. title: New partnership in our "France Japon Eco, Weekly with Kreab
description:
We are pleased to announce a new collaboration with Kreab*, a leading name in Public Relations (PR) consulting. This partnership will bring exciting new content to our "France Japon Eco, Weekly" readers, thus increasing the value of our weekly publication.
As part of this collaboration, KREAB will now contribute regular articles to our weekly editions. Rather than sticking to our usual descriptions of Japanese newspapers, Kreab will provide in-depth analysis on key issues, offering fresh insights and expert commentary.  This new partnership is in line with our ongoing commitment to bring innovative, engaging and informative content to our audience. 
The first publication after the summer will explore the unprecedented LDP presidential election.  READ FRANCE JAPON ECO, WEEKLY 912

Kreab is a world-class global affairs and PR consulting firm founded in Stockholm, Sweden. Kreab Tokyo is the firm’s Asia hub, supporting clients’ business activities with a focus on three business areas: public relations, government relations, and global risk management.

title: New Year with the MOF in Nagoya
description: New Year in Nagoya ＠MOF MUSEUM

blocks.text: Chubu Event report

blocks.section: New Year with the MOF in Nagoya
blocks.text: New Year with the MOF in Nagoya

blocks.section: New Year with the MOF in Nagoya
blocks.text: New Year in Nagoya ＠MOF MUSEUM

blocks.section: New Year with the MOF in Nagoya
blocks.text: On January 26, 2024 (Thursday), starting at 6 p.m., a New Year's reception was held at the MOF MUSEUM (Musée des Meilleurs Ouvriers de France), located in the Mizuho-ku district of Nagoya. We had the pleasure of welcoming more than 40 participants to this event.

blocks.section: New Year with the MOF in Nagoya
blocks.text: This event was co-organized by our company and the sponsor MOF (Meilleurs Ouvriers de France). The term MOF refers to the prestigious title of Meilleur Ouvrier de France, honoring artisans with exceptional skills to perpetuate French culture. On this occasion, we had the pleasure of enjoying a delicious buffet surrounded by works of artisans distinguished by this title. We were able to admire their attention to detail and expertise up close through items such as bags, scissors, antiques, and many others.

blocks.section: New Year with the MOF in Nagoya
blocks.text: Additionally, the buffet was accompanied by a superb selection of cheeses imported directly from France by Mr. Eri Hisada , who owns a cheese factory in Paris. They were perfectly matched with the champaigns and wines selected by sommelier Seika Hosokawa , who works in France. We also had the pleasure of tasting delicious French breads prepared by Mr. Masahiro Suzuki , a baker distinguished by the title of MOF.

blocks.section: New Year with the MOF in Nagoya
blocks.text: In addition to this, we had the opportunity to taste a variety of traditional French dishes, as well as Japanese onigiri and tonjiru (pork soup) prepared by a tofu shop, providing a culinary experience combining Japanese and French cultures.

blocks.section: New Year with the MOF in Nagoya
blocks.text: This gathering of the Franco-Japanese community after a long period allowed lively exchanges between people working in various sectors of activity.

blocks.section: New Year with the MOF in Nagoya
blocks.text: To conclude, we had the pleasure of tasting the Galette des Rois together, awarded this year by the French Embassy and created by the talented pastry chef Shota Nakayama of the Nagoya Tokyu Hotel . This tasting successfully marked the end of our 2024 New Year's reception, which proved to be a dynamic opportunity to strengthen ties between France and Japan. We intend to continue to organize meetings in order to deepen the Franco-Japanese network in the future. We would like to express our sincere gratitude to the MOF sponsors and all the participants who helped make this event unforgettable. We look forward to welcoming you at our 2025 New Year's Eve reception in Nagoya!

title: New Year's networking with the American Chamber of Commerce
description: On Friday January 31, we were delighted to host our traditional New Year's networking evening with ACCJ and BCCJ!

blocks.text: Kansai Event report

blocks.section: New Year's networking with the American Chamber of Commerce
blocks.text: New Year's networking with the American Chamber of Commerce

blocks.section: New Year's networking with the American Chamber of Commerce
blocks.text: On Friday January 31, we were delighted to host our traditional New Year's networking evening with ACCJ and BCCJ!

blocks.section: New Year's networking with the American Chamber of Commerce
blocks.text: It was a convivial evening that brought together our local business community in the luxurious surroundings of the prestigious InterContinental Osaka hotel!

blocks.section: New Year's networking with the American Chamber of Commerce
blocks.text: The evening began with words of welcome from the Vice-President of the American Chamber, Mr. Jiro Kawakami, followed by speeches from Ms. Simone Thomsen, Governor of the American Chamber in Japan. Two representatives of the Food Bank association, Ms Nakashima and Mr Ueno, also took the floor to underline the charity aspect of the event, in aid of their organization. The association transfers surplus food to children in need.

blocks.section: New Year's networking with the American Chamber of Commerce
blocks.text: The Consul General of the United States in Osaka and Kobe, Mr. Jason Cubas, then took the stage to conclude the series of speeches and toast the event. The traditional Kagami Biraki ceremony then took place, marked by the symbolic opening of a barrel of Japanese sake, a moment particularly appreciated by our guests.

blocks.section: New Year's networking with the American Chamber of Commerce
blocks.text: The buffet was particularly appreciated, with participants enjoying a mix of Japanese and Western dishes.

blocks.section: New Year's networking with the American Chamber of Commerce
blocks.text: To celebrate the start of the new year, a tombola was organized with magnificent prizes donated by our generous sponsors. The French Chamber of Commerce was pleased to present a bottle of Westland whisky offered by our member Rémy Cointreau.

blocks.section: New Year's networking with the American Chamber of Commerce
blocks.text: The evening not only celebrated the arrival of the New Year, but also strengthened the bonds of friendship and collaboration between the French, Japanese, American and British business communities.

blocks.section: New Year's networking with the American Chamber of Commerce
blocks.text: Many thanks to all our guests, partners and sponsors for contributing to the success of the evening!

title: Nihonshu Tasting at the Hilton Osaka with Shimizu Seizaburō

blocks.text: Kansai Event report

blocks.section: Nihonshu Tasting at the Hilton Osaka with Shimizu Seizaburō
blocks.text: Nihonshu Tasting at the Hilton Osaka with Shimizu Seizaburō

blocks.section: Nihonshu Tasting at the Hilton Osaka with Shimizu Seizaburō
blocks.text: On Tuesday,October 3 , we held our very first sake tasting dinner at the Centrum in Hilton Osaka, located in Umeda. It was the result of a special collaboration with one of our benefactor members, Shimizu Seizaburō Shōten , a brewery based in the prefecture of Mie and known for the famous award-winning “Zaku” brand, and another member from Kansai: the Hilton Osaka itself.

blocks.section: Nihonshu Tasting at the Hilton Osaka with Shimizu Seizaburō
blocks.text: Founded in 1869, Shimizu Seizaburo Shoten is located in Suzuka, also known as Umasake Suzuka no Kuni (味酒鈴鹿国), ‘Suzuka, the land of good sake’. On the road to their recognition on the French market, they won the famous Prix du Président at the Kura Master 2020 concours in Paris.

blocks.section: Nihonshu Tasting at the Hilton Osaka with Shimizu Seizaburō
blocks.text: For the occasion, Shimizu seizaburo made a special selection of Nihonshu: Zaku Kizui (Junmai Daiginjo), Zaku Naguwashi (Junmai Daiginjo), Zaku Monad (Junmai Ginjo), Zaku Concentration (Liqueur).

blocks.section: Nihonshu Tasting at the Hilton Osaka with Shimizu Seizaburō
blocks.text: While Shimizu Seizaburō was providing the high quality sake, the Hilton Osaka gave us the benefit of a befitting private room at the prestigious restaurant Centrum, as well as an original 4 course menu conceived by their French culinary director Philippe Egalon: duck confit, Jérusalem artichoke velouté, Japanese sea bass meunier or Wagyu beef pot au feu, and finally a Normandie apple tart. Cherry on top, a professional French sommelier specialized in Japanese sake, Kévin Lemonnier , was especially hired from Tokyo to comment on the sake during the tasting.

blocks.section: Nihonshu Tasting at the Hilton Osaka with Shimizu Seizaburō
blocks.text: The event started early with a private introductory meeting between the Hilton’s team, the sommelier and both Shimizu, husband and wife, who jointly direct their company. Then the event started for earnest with the arrival of our guests, who could enjoy the food, the intimacy and warmth of the private room, the alcohol, the conversation, and even an improvised acapella version of famous Edith Piaf song “ Non, je ne regrette rien ”, performed on the spot by our guest Matsumoto Kazuko (松本 和子)

blocks.section: Nihonshu Tasting at the Hilton Osaka with Shimizu Seizaburō
blocks.text: Overall, we are very proud that our local members in the regions are able to collaborate in order to help us put together such a complete and high-quality event, which also brought two of our offices together. Variety of talents, skills, knowledge and expertise, brought together into the CCIFJ’s community by growing friendships is what we are striving for. We provide the stage where you can play.

blocks.section: Nihonshu Tasting at the Hilton Osaka with Shimizu Seizaburō
blocks.text: If you are cursing your fate because somehow you missed the event, put your mind at ease: we have in mind to replicate it next year (most probably in September this time). Please also know that our end game is to actually take you all to Mie one day to visit the actual brewery and enjoy this sake at its birthplace, straight from the source. So keep an eye out for further notice!

blocks.section: Nissan announces production of next-generation batteries by 2029
blocks.text: Nissan announced on Tuesday the production of electric vehicles powered by next-generation batteries by 2029.

blocks.section: Nissan announces production of next-generation batteries by 2029
blocks.text: In the emerging electric car sector, Japanese automakers are lagging behind their American and Chinese competitors.

blocks.section: Nissan announces production of next-generation batteries by 2029
blocks.text: However, Nissan has announced the production of next-generation batteries to power electric vehicles , on the heels of a media tour of an unfinished pilot plant. “Nissan engineers are all working hard to create this new world,” said Hideyuki Sakamoto, the company's executive vice-president.

blocks.section: Nissan announces production of next-generation batteries by 2029
blocks.text: A real promise of a quantum leap : a powerful battery that's cheaper, safer and quicker to charge than today's lithium-ion batteries.

blocks.section: Nissan announces production of next-generation batteries by 2029
blocks.text: However, considerable challenges remain before the technology can reach commercial mass production. Nissan officials remain tight-lipped about many aspects of the technology, as well as the total investment.

blocks.section: Nissan announces production of next-generation batteries by 2029
blocks.text: Competitors such as Volkswagen and Toyota have also announced efforts to produce vehicles with low environmental impact, with Toyota setting a date of 2027-2028 to start bringing them to market.

blocks.text: Some traditions transcend time without ever losing their brilliance. The French Art de Vivre is undoubtedly one of them. Blending elegance, creativity, gastronomy, craftsmanship, and culture, it embodies the spirit of sharing and the richness of French savoir-faire.

blocks.section: New BONJOUR FRANCE Event: Vive l’Art de Vivre!
blocks.text: Whether you are passionate about French culture, a gastronomy enthusiast, a design lover, or simply curious to enjoy a unique experience, this event promises to be one of BONJOUR FRANCE's highlights of 2026.

blocks.section: New BONJOUR FRANCE Event: Vive l’Art de Vivre!

title: “OECD Education2030 Project Infinity": international collaboration for tomorrow's schools
description: ​​​​​​​Après le succès du “Tohoku Appeal Event” en 2024, c’est au tour de la “OECD Education2030 Project Infinity” !

blocks.text: Also

blocks.section: “OECD Education2030 Project Infinity": international collaboration for tomorrow's schools
blocks.text: “OECD Education2030 Project Infinity": international collaboration for tomorrow's schools

blocks.section: “OECD Education2030 Project Infinity": international collaboration for tomorrow's schools
blocks.text: ​​​​​​​Après le succès du “Tohoku Appeal Event” en 2024, c’est au tour de la “OECD Education2030 Project Infinity” !

blocks.section: “OECD Education2030 Project Infinity": international collaboration for tomorrow's schools
blocks.text: After the success of the “Tohoku Appeal Event” in 2024, it's the turn of the “OECD Education2030 Project Infinity”!

blocks.section: “OECD Education2030 Project Infinity": international collaboration for tomorrow's schools
blocks.text: Following the earthquake on March 11, 2011, in Japan and the ensuing nuclear accident, Fukushima University, the Japanese Ministry of Education, Science and Technology and the OECD decided to create the “Tohoku School” , days dedicated to sharing and bringing students together.

blocks.section: “OECD Education2030 Project Infinity": international collaboration for tomorrow's schools
blocks.text: Above all, these events enabled children who had lived through the disaster to make new friends, to rebuild the school as a place to live, to rediscover the essential values of life, and to build a new world based on the use of renewable energies.

blocks.section: “OECD Education2030 Project Infinity": international collaboration for tomorrow's schools
blocks.text: The project culminated in an event in August 2014 - the Tohoku Appeal Event in Paris - which took place on the Champs de Mars in Paris. Students from all over the world mobilized for the occasion. The event was introduced by a speech from the city of Paris,the Japanese Ambassador to France as well as representatives from the OECD. The days were punctuated by animations, dances, cultural events (Tachibana)...

blocks.section: “OECD Education2030 Project Infinity": international collaboration for tomorrow's schools
blocks.text: 10 years on, the OECD has decided to carry out a new project for education: “OECD Education2030 Project Infinity.” The project was led by students from Japan and Canada. Its aim is to enable students from different countries to create collaborative products, which could help improve well-being at school and within communities.

blocks.section: “OECD Education2030 Project Infinity": international collaboration for tomorrow's schools
blocks.text: The project currently involves 112 schools in 24 countries, with 30 Japanese schools taking part . A Summit for the project will be held this December at the OECD offices , to present the products created in collaboration and discuss future education with actors from around the world, based on the real experiences of students and teachers through “Project Infinity.”

blocks.section: “OECD Education2030 Project Infinity": international collaboration for tomorrow's schools
blocks.text: The “OECD Education2030 Project Infinity” is an extremely important milestone: this year marks the 60th anniversary of Japan's membership of the OECD , and the Japanese committee wishes to remember achievements such as the “Tohoku School” and also show its solidarity for people in crisis situations , such as in Noto after the earthquake or in Ukraine, in Paris.

blocks.section: “OECD Education2030 Project Infinity": international collaboration for tomorrow's schools
“OECD Education2030 Project Infinity": international collaboration for tomorrow's schools
blocks.text: Would you like to support the project, or enter into a partnership?

blocks.section: “OECD Education2030 Project Infinity": international collaboration for tomorrow's schools

title: ONIS : A sucessfull prospecting mission that turns into a V.I.E
description: A testimonial by Adriana Saikali, VIE at ONIS, a company specializing in manufacturing equipment for industrial piping operations.

blocks.text: Testimonials

blocks.section: ONIS : A sucessfull prospecting mission that turns into a V.I.E
blocks.text: ONIS : A sucessfull prospecting mission that turns into a V.I.E

blocks.section: ONIS : A sucessfull prospecting mission that turns into a V.I.E
blocks.text: A testimonial by Adriana Saikali, VIE at ONIS, a company specializing in manufacturing equipment for industrial piping operations.

blocks.section: ONIS : A sucessfull prospecting mission that turns into a V.I.E
blocks.text: Founded in 1979 , ONIS is a company specializing in the design and manufacture of equipment dedicated to industrial piping operations. For more than forty years , the company has been developing solutions that enable fast , safe , and repeatable interventions, carried out by a single operator and requiring no tools. With over 12,000 devices deployed worldwide , ONIS has built a strong reputation for reliability, supported by an international network of engineers committed to continuously improving the safety, performance, and profitability of industrial assets.

blocks.section: ONIS : A sucessfull prospecting mission that turns into a V.I.E
blocks.text: The company’s flagship product, the Quick Action Line Blind (QLB), is designed to replace spectacle blinds and figure-eight blinds. The QLB ensures absolute isolation between upstream and downstream, without the use of bolts or nuts. It therefore guarantees optimal sealing while significantly reducing downtime during line blinding operations.

blocks.section: ONIS : A sucessfull prospecting mission that turns into a V.I.E
blocks.text: Designed for critical applications, ONIS solutions primarily serve the oil and gas sector , including refineries, compression units, and pipeline management systems. They are capable of operating under extreme conditions , ranging from –120°C to 650°C and up to 420 bar (6,000 PSI).

blocks.section: ONIS : A sucessfull prospecting mission that turns into a V.I.E
blocks.text: As part of its international development strategy, ONIS naturally turned to Japan , a market renowned for its stringent standards in industrial safety and performance. In 2021 , despite a particularly challenging health and economic context, the company took part in an initial prospecting mission organized with the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCIFJ) . This initiative made it possible to identify a local partner and lay the foundations for a gradual market entry, which materialized in 2024 with the recruitment of a VIE in Japan to sustainably support business development and strengthen local relationships.

blocks.section: ONIS : A sucessfull prospecting mission that turns into a V.I.E
blocks.text: Adriana Saikali Sales Engineer, ONIS

blocks.section: ONIS : A sucessfull prospecting mission that turns into a V.I.E
blocks.text: Following the mission carried out with the CCIFJ in 2021, we identified a local partner and continued our outreach to Japanese companies. Building on the success of this mission, I was recruited as a VIE for ONIS in Japan in September 2024. We were also very satisfied with the support provided by the CCIFJ during this initial market entry mission, especially given the particularly challenging context at the time. After one year of a VIE assignment in Japan, we have identified strong potential in the Japanese market. The philosophy of continuous improvement and the priority given to industrial process safety—deeply rooted in Japanese culture—are perfectly aligned with the values and benefits of ONIS solutions. We are confident that our equipment, fully compliant with Japanese standards, meets the most stringent market requirements. Building on this first phase, ONIS now aims to strengthen its presence in Japan by increasing brand awareness and continuing to adapt its offerings to the specific needs of local industries. »

title: Osaka comes to Tokyo with the Zakka Rendez-vous
description:
On September 2, the CCI France Japon welcomed the Osaka Zakka Rendez-vous, organized by the City of Osaka and the Osaka Business Development Agency, alongside the Tokyo International Gift Show.
For one evening, several SMEs from Osaka came to Tokyo to showcase their products, expertise and unique worlds to an audience of professionals and members of the international community.
The evening featured company presentations, product demonstrations and hands-on discoveries, giving participants the opportunity to meet the businesses directly and learn more about the stories, ideas and know-how behind their products.
The event continued over a cocktail, creating a relaxed setting for conversations, new connections and potential business opportunities.
More than a product showcase, the Osaka Zakka Rendez-vous was a chance to bring Osaka and Tokyo closer together, while connecting local businesses with an international audience and celebrating creativity, craftsmanship and new ideas.
A great evening to discover what Osaka’s businesses have to offer and to see how far a good idea can travel.

blocks.text: CCIFJ's Osaka BC is growing!

blocks.section: CCIFJ's Osaka BC is growing!
blocks.text: The Osaka Business Center of the CCI France Japon is proud to announce the creation this month of 3 new desks! Another 2 FLEX desks are under study.

blocks.section: CCIFJ's Osaka BC is growing!
blocks.text: There are now about 25 residents in our Osaka Business Center , belonging to half a dozen companies , both major and modest. Most of them are members of the French Chamber of Commerce in Japan, but we are not narrow-minded: everybody looking for a base camp to work in the Kansai Region is welcome in our facility.

blocks.section: CCIFJ's Osaka BC is growing!
blocks.text: In anticipation of the Expo 2025 Osaka Kansai , we have decided to expand our capacity in order to be able to accommodate more people. We offer a variety of packages (including a meeting room), usually highly customizable, at competitive prices, right at the heart of Osaka's business district .

blocks.section: CCIFJ's Osaka BC is growing!
blocks.text: The building itself, Dōjima Avanza , is actually a well-known landmark in the region, the name alone usually drawing appreciative "Oooohs" and "Aaaahs" from your partners.

blocks.section: CCIFJ's Osaka BC is growing!
blocks.text: It is less than 10 minutes from Osaka-Umeda station by foot, and you can even do the whole walk underground when it rains. From there, it is a 30 minutes trip to Kyoto, 20 minutes to Kobe (Sannomiya), and just one small stop to Shin-Osaka where you can catch your Shinkansen to Nagoya (50'), Tokyo (2:30') or Hakata, Fukuoka (2:30'). The whole area being packed with small restaurants, bars and cafés, you have a wide range of options for your more unformal business meetings or for a place to have a break and relax.

blocks.section: CCIFJ's Osaka BC is growing!
blocks.text: Being hosted at the CCIFJ also entails exclusive perks, such as being physically part of the tight community of resident members , more opportunities to make relevant connexions and the chance to share new information first hand about what is going on in the local business scene. You also have an immediate access to CCIFJ services when you need them Every month or every other month, we have a small office party for everyone to have a chance to get to know their fellow residents, and to keep a lively spirit up inside the office.

blocks.section: CCIFJ's Osaka BC is growing!

title: Over 3 million tourists visited Japan in March, an all-time record
description: This is the highest number achieved for a single month, surpassing the 2,991,100 visitors in July 2019.

blocks.text: Foresight

blocks.section: Over 3 million tourists visited Japan in March, an all-time record
blocks.text: Over 3 million tourists visited Japan in March, an all-time record

blocks.section: Over 3 million tourists visited Japan in March, an all-time record
blocks.text: This is the highest number achieved for a single month, surpassing the 2,991,100 visitors in July 2019.

blocks.section: Over 3 million tourists visited Japan in March, an all-time record
blocks.text: According to a survey conducted by the National Tourism Organization, the number of Japanese tourists was 3.08 million in March , the highest number ever recorded for a single month, surpassing the 2,991,100 visitors who visited Japan in July 2019.

blocks.section: Over 3 million tourists visited Japan in March, an all-time record
blocks.text: Tourists from South Korea were the most numerous, followed by visitors from Taiwan, China and the USA.

blocks.section: Over 3 million tourists visited Japan in March, an all-time record
blocks.text: “Of the 23 countries and regions surveyed, 17 recorded a record number of visitors in March. We are closely monitoring the number of tourists from China, which remains at around 70% of its pre-pandemic level,” said the Japan National Tourism Organization.

blocks.section: Over 3 million tourists visited Japan in March, an all-time record
blocks.text: The cherry blossom season and the depreciation of the yen are said to have been the main reasons for the increase in tourists.

blocks.section: Over 3 million tourists visited Japan in March, an all-time record
blocks.text: In addition, tourist spending per traveler is around 209,000 yen, more than 60,000 yen higher than the same period in 2019. The Japan Tourism Agency attributes these figures to the impact of the weak yen, as well as to an increase in the number of days spent in Japan.

blocks.text: Chubu Event report

blocks.section: Panel Discussion about Diversity and Inclusion in Japanese companies, from the point of view of 3 Women leaders in the Air Transport industry

blocks.section: Panel Discussion about Diversity and Inclusion in Japanese companies, from the point of view of 3 Women leaders in the Air Transport industry
blocks.text: Panel Discussion about Diversity and Inclusion in Japanese companies, from the point of view of 3 Women leaders in the Air Transport industry.

blocks.section: Panel Discussion about Diversity and Inclusion in Japanese companies, from the point of view of 3 Women leaders in the Air Transport industry
blocks.text: "We had never considered that French women faced challenges in reaching managerial positions similar to those in Japan. We thought we were the only ones dealing with such issues."

blocks.section: Panel Discussion about Diversity and Inclusion in Japanese companies, from the point of view of 3 Women leaders in the Air Transport industry
blocks.text: On December 5th, 2023, a significant event unfolded at the Nagoya Innovators' Garage , located in Nadya Park. The gathering, which brought together professionals and individuals, focused on empowering women and promoting leadership roles. The event featured 3 prestigious speakers: Ms Béatrice Delpuech , Director Japan/Korea for Air France Cargo , Ms. Mayumi Ejima , General Manager of ANA ’s Nagoya Branch, and Ms. Junko Sakihara , General Manager of JAL ’s Chubu Branch Office.

blocks.section: Panel Discussion about Diversity and Inclusion in Japanese companies, from the point of view of 3 Women leaders in the Air Transport industry
blocks.text: The event kicked off with Béatrice Delpuech’s speech. She outlined her background with insights into her remarkable achievements with Sodexi , Air France and Air France Cargo .

blocks.section: Panel Discussion about Diversity and Inclusion in Japanese companies, from the point of view of 3 Women leaders in the Air Transport industry
blocks.text: She went on sharing her views on maintaining a work-life balance, addressing the differences between the working environments for women in France, Amsterdam ( KLM ), and Japan, and exposing AF methods to increase the representation of women in male-dominated sectors, such as logistics.

blocks.section: Panel Discussion about Diversity and Inclusion in Japanese companies, from the point of view of 3 Women leaders in the Air Transport industry
blocks.text: A talk session between the three guest speakers followed the seminar.

blocks.section: Panel Discussion about Diversity and Inclusion in Japanese companies, from the point of view of 3 Women leaders in the Air Transport industry
blocks.text: After being invited to reflect on the impactful points of Béatrice's presentation, the other two speakers Junko Sakihara and Mayumi Ejima shared their own thoughts on the question, offering understanding into the promotion of female leadership at JAL and ANA, respectively. The talk session took an unexpected turn as the speakers shared their surprise at the revelation that France, perceived by many as progressive, is still grappling with issues of gender inclusivity. The realization sparked a dynamic conversation, and shed light on the need for continuous efforts to address gender disparities in various professional spheres, even in seemingly advanced societies. The event ended with a networking session, where everyone could share their thoughts with the speakers.

blocks.section: Panel Discussion about Diversity and Inclusion in Japanese companies, from the point of view of 3 Women leaders in the Air Transport industry
blocks.text: If we could pinpoint one key moment, it would undoubtedly be when Béatrice Delpuech made an observation regarding the self-imposed barriers that women often place on their professional aspirations. She noted that, due to fear and a lack of self-confidence, many women hesitate to accept well-deserved positions, driven by the enduring belief that aspects like marriage or pregnancy might hinder their professional success.

blocks.section: Panel Discussion about Diversity and Inclusion in Japanese companies, from the point of view of 3 Women leaders in the Air Transport industry
blocks.text: In conclusion, our heartfelt gratitude extends to the Central Japan Economic Federation for their steadfast support. A special appreciation is due as well to Haruka Mizuta from IBA for her live translation, and finally we also thank sincerely the MOF (Meilleur Ouvriers de France) organization for their sponsorship, allowing participants to enjoy Nespresso coffee during the event. Each of them was also able to take home a delightful treat—a bag of bread from Gifu's delectable bakery, ' Guruman Vital '.

title: Paris Saint-Germain brings “ICI C’EST PARIS LA MAISON” to Tokyo
description:
Paris Saint-Germain announces the launch of its immersive pop-up experience, “ICI C’EST PARIS LA MAISON,” to be held in Shibuya, Tokyo, from May 2 to 5, 2026, following successful editions in Los Angeles and London. This initiative underscores the Club’s commitment to strengthening its presence and engagement in the Japanese market.
Designed as a multi-dimensional experience, the event extends beyond football to encompass fashion, music, art, and gastronomy, reflecting the cultural dialogue between Paris and Tokyo. The three-floor venue will offer a wide range of activations, including football-related experiences, gaming zones, wellness programs, a café, exclusive merchandise, and a bistro inspired by French and Japanese culinary influences.
This initiative forms part of Paris Saint-Germain’s broader strategy to establish itself as a leading lifestyle brand. By integrating local cultural elements into its global projects, the Club aims to deliver meaningful and engaging experiences to its international audience. Japan remains a key strategic market, and this event further reinforces Paris Saint-Germain’s long-term commitment to the country.
For more information, please visit:Paris Saint-Germain brings “ICI C’EST PARIS LA MAISON” to Tokyo for a new international chapter

blocks.text: The Park Hyatt, the famous hotel in the heart of Tokyo, closed its doors on May 7 , to be reopened next autumn.

blocks.section: Park Hyatt hotel to be closed for renovation
blocks.text: The renovation coincides with the hotel's thirtieth anniversary, having opened its doors in 1994. The 52-storey building features over 200 accommodations, including 177 rooms and 23 suites, as well as 8 restaurants.

blocks.text: The hotel is one of Tokyo's best-known hotels, having played a central role in Sofia Coppola's film "Lost in Translation" (2003).

blocks.text: It also hosts the annual general meeting of the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan.

title: Park Hyatt Tokyo Announces Hotel Upgrades to Begin in 2024
description:
TOKYO (April 26, 2023) – Park Hyatt Tokyo today announces plans for a property-wide renewal of its guestrooms and facilities starting in spring 2024. The hotel will suspend operations from May 7, 2024 and is slated to reopen in the 2nd quarter of 2025. The planned enhancements coincide with the hotel’s 30th anniversary, ushering in a new chapter for the hotel, aimed at elevating the guest experience and revitalizing its iconic ambiance. Locals and worldly travelers alike have cherished the hotel as a sophisticated home-away-from-home since its opening in 1994, and the forthcoming updates will bring a fresh, modern feel to the already-renowned property.  To continue meeting the needs of today’s discerning travelers while preserving the hotel's distinct and timeless design concept, acclaimed design agency Jouin Manku has been chosen to lead the transformation respecting the beloved design philosophy of the hotel’s notable original interior designer, John Morford.  In a joint statement, Mr. Patrick Jouin and Mr. Sanjit Manku, co-founders and CEOs of Jouin Manku share, “We are sincerely grateful that our studio has been given the rare opportunity to renovate Park Hyatt Tokyo and set the stage for this prestigious hotel’s much-anticipated future. We are excited to work with the hotel team to create a uniquely elegant design experience for guests, all in keeping with John Morford's original vision. We thank the Park Hyatt Tokyo team for the trust they have placed in us."  "As Park Hyatt Tokyo approaches its 30th anniversary next year, we are delighted to work with the wonderful team at Jouin Manku and our hotel’s associates to make this renewal a success," said Fredrik Harfors, general manager of Park Hyatt Tokyo. "We are grateful for everyone’s patience and understanding as we embark on a journey to enhance the guest experience at our hotel. Drawing inspiration from the trailblazing legacy of Park Hyatt Tokyo, we are committed to creating an elevated atmosphere that will continue to shine as a beacon of understated luxury for decades to come."  More information about the planned upgrades and construction schedule will be announced closer to the project's start date.

title: PARSYS : Telemedecal solution
description:
In 2023, as part of a collective mission organized by CCI France Japon and Business France, in partnership with the Ile de France Region, the telemedicine company Parsys, along with other companies from the Île-de-France region, benefited from a prospecting mission in Japan.

This was the second mission for Parsys, the first having taken place in 2021. This mission provided an opportunity for Parsys to meet new prospects and establish new partnerships. Following this mission, and after several years of operation, Parsys finally concluded a partnership with Sharemedical, a Japanese company in the telehealth and medical devices sector.

"Penetrating the Japanese market proves challenging for French companies due to significant barriers such as language and cultural differences. Faced with these challenges, many hesitate to engage in it. Moreover, to succeed in this market, it is crucial to offer an innovative solution. If a similar solution already exists, Japanese companies generally prefer a local option due to ease of communication, local support, and absence of time zone differences. My personal experience perfectly illustrates these obstacles.
Upon my arrival in Japan, I attempted to contact Japanese prospects without success. I then sought assistance from CCIFJ for an initial prospecting mission, which allowed me to secure several meetings, including one with a company to which I had previously sent multiple unanswered messages. It was during this meeting that I made my first contact with Sharemedical. Subsequently, we remained in contact with Sharemedical's president, but without finalizing a collaboration project. Last November's mission was decisive. Thanks to the work and support of my project leader, Ms. Takahara, and my translator, Ms. Miki, we were able to overcome the final obstacles and finalize a partnership agreement between our two companies."

M. Julien FOURTANE
Business Developer

title: Past Event: Code your first website in 2hours
description:
On 12 April, CCIFJ hosted a young professionals committee event for 17 participants on designing a landing page using HTML/CSS. The workshop aimed to provide attendees with a comprehensive understanding of HTML/CSS core notions, graphical tips and tools, and the importance of creating responsive websites for different devices.
The workshop began with an introduction to HTML/CSS, followed by a discussion of various graphical tips and tools, including FontAwesome, Google Fonts, and coolors. Participants were encouraged to code and design their own landing pages throughout the workshop, with opportunities to receive feedback from their peers and the instructor.
By the end of the workshop, participants had gained practical skills and knowledge that they could apply to their future projects. The event was successful in fostering a community of designers and developers who are passionate about creating beautiful and functional websites.
Overall, the workshop was a well-organized and informative event that contributed to the professional development of attendees in the field of web design and development.



<SPEAKER>
Yann KLEIN
Bootcamp Manager, LE WAGON TOKYO  
I am a software developer and bootcamp manager at Le Wagon Tokyo. I'm a maker by essence and I love to develop applications and push the limits of fields like VR, AR or recently AI (I guess it's not the right place to talk about my leathercraft addiction? ?).
I'm also a people person, changing the life of our coding bootcamp students is the reason why I wake up every morning ❤️.

blocks.text: Gabrielle Chanel overturned the codes of haute couture when she invented the 2.55 handbag. “I was tired of carrying bags in my hand and losing them, so I added a strap so I could carry them over my shoulder,” she was quoted as saying at the time.

blocks.text: Chanel’s latest advertising campaign features this iconic handbag with a nod to French cinema. It was first shown in Deauville during the presentation of the Fall/Winter 2024-25 ready-to-wear collection last March.

blocks.text: Deauville is not only the place where Gabrielle Chanel opened her first boutique, but also the setting for Claude Lelouch's film “Un homme et une femme” (1966). In a scene from the film, lead actress Anouk Aimée also wears a Chanel handbag.

blocks.section: Penélope Cruz and Brad Pitt in “Un homme et une femme” for Chanel
blocks.text: Those who have seen "Un homme et une femme" may notice that the ad is almost identical to the original, both in the images and in the conversation between Penelope Cruz and Brad Pitt.

title: People Analytics: Big Data is HR’s next frontier
description:
The second HR Committee of 2019 on 18th July dealt with the subject of big data and its applications in human resources. 30 participants from a wide range of companies listened as Peter Romero, People Analytics Lead at the Cambridge Psychometrics Centre of the University of Cambridge, UK, talked them through why and how HR needed to become “quantitative”. By using numerous examples and documented thought-provoking figures (e.g. 82% of managers are misplaced, 13% of employees are engaged), Peter explained in particular how People Analytics can help organizations make better leader selections and raise any alarm bells early on as to which profiles might be unfit for the role. Peter also gave tips as to how even smaller companies can kick-start People Analytics using off-the-shelf tools.
Adding to the many applications of People Analytics, Fabien Roudier, Senior Manager at Institution for a Global Society Corporation (IGS), explained how its application GROW360 uses data analysis and machine learning in optimizing recruitment processes. Again, using the example of a large Japanese corporation, Fabien showed how to remove selection bias and make sure the best candidates are selected based on their soft skills assessment and on continuously improving predictive models of who will be a top-performer.
The CCI France Japon wishes to thank the speakers, participants and president of the HR Committee, Grégory Dancs, for a successful and very informative session.

This transaction is the latest in a series of successful deals illustrating the Group’s active portfolio management, part of its “Transform & Accelerate” strategic plan

blocks.section: Pernod Ricard invests in Japenese Gin brand
blocks.text: The partnership with KI NO BI, the fast-growing ultra-premium Japanese gin brand, strengthens Pernod Ricard’s extensive gin portfolio. This transaction is the latest in a series of successful deals illustrating the Group’s active portfolio management, part of its “Transform & Accelerate” strategic plan

blocks.section: Pernod Ricard invests in Japenese Gin brand
blocks.text: Pernod Ricard announced the signing of an agreement for a significant investment in KI NO BI Kyoto Dry Gin. The investment will be used primarily to build a new, state-of-the-art, distillery to meet the growing demand for KI NO BI ultra-premium gin.

blocks.section: Pernod Ricard invests in Japenese Gin brand
blocks.text: KI NO BI is a small-batch, artisanal gin with a Japanese heart. Distilled at Japan’s first dedicated gin distillery, built in Kyoto in 2014, it is made with obsessive attention to detail, care and precision, from a high-quality rice spirit and Japanese botanicals such as yuzu, lemon, sansho pepper, ginger and gyokuro tea. KI NO BI has been carefully crafted to ensure perfect harmony between its various botanicals and its Kyoto origins. KI NO BI has a recognisable dry gin flavour with a Japanese accent: pure, perfectly balanced with distinctive aromas and a lingering finish of light ginger.

blocks.section: Pernod Ricard invests in Japenese Gin brand
blocks.text: For Alexandre Ricard, Chairman & Chief Executive Officer of Pernod Ricard: “ We are thrilled to welcome this one-of-a-kind brand to our portfolio. KI NO BI’s unique origins and taste profile make it a perfect complement to The Gin Hub’s extensive stable of brands. I am excited for Pernod Ricard to be part of its ongoing development. ”

blocks.section: Pernod Ricard invests in Japenese Gin brand
blocks.text: Driven by the rise of mixology, the ultra-premium gin category has been experiencing uninterrupted dynamism. KI NO BI will immediately join The Pernod Ricard Gin Hub and reinforce its prestigious stable of international brands such as Beefeater, Plymouth, Malfy and Monkey 47. Together with Monkey 47, KI NO BI will form a powerful repertoire to optimise the growth opportunity in ultra-premium gin.

blocks.section: Pernod Ricard invests in Japenese Gin brand
blocks.text: With this partnership, Pernod Ricard further expands its portfolio of specialty and prestige brands, composed of small brands with unique and comprehensive value propositions, selected distribution and significant growth potential. Thanks to Pernod Ricard’s extensive distribution network, this strategy is yielding positive results as sales of the Group’s specialty brands have been growing at a double-digit rate, well above the industry average.

title: PMC Japan celebrates 50 years of expertise supporting European Businesses in Japan
description:
PMC Japan has celebrated its 50th anniversary, marking half a century of expertise in assisting European companies in Japan. Since its founding in 1974 by Pierre Martin, PMC has become an essential partner for businesses aiming to succeed in the Japanese market.
With a strong network across various private and public sectors, PMC helps its clients navigate the complexities of the Japanese market. Its services cover a wide range, from market entry strategies to administrative and HR support, ensuring effective establishment and growth for foreign companies in Japan.
Today, with over 250 clients, PMC is a key player in international business development in Japan. Its trilingual team, well-versed in the cultural and commercial nuances of the country, plays a vital role in the success of its clients.
As PMC looks ahead to the next 50 years, it continues to innovate, helping businesses seize opportunities and face the challenges of Japan’s ever-evolving market.
Happy anniversary!

title: Podcast Itinéraires Singuliers – From Strasbourg to Tokyo: The Journey of Jérôme Guth, Head Coach of Japan's Olympic Sabre Fencing Teams
description:
A French fencing enthusiast falls in love with Japan and leads the national team to a historic Olympic medal in Paris. The podcast Itinéraires Singuliers opens its first episode with the story of Jérôme Guth – Head Coach of Japan's Men's and Women's Olympic Sabre Fencing Teams – and what it reveals about the business of sport in Japan.
Born in Strasbourg, he discovered fencing at the age of six and met a fencing master who would mark his entire life. This charismatic, demanding, and caring mentor passed on his love for the sabre – a passion that would stay with Jérôme forever. After serious studies and an early career as a high-level referee, Jérôme moved to the United States at 25, first to complete his studies, then to open his own club. America taught him entrepreneurship, freedom, and the power of believing in his dreams – even if the “all-business” logic eventually made him crave something else.
It was then that Japan entered his story. After several brief but deeply impactful trips, he accepted the role of head coach for the Japanese national sabre team. Arriving during the Covid period, he had to wait before settling in, but once there, he transformed the team’s dynamic. With caring management, Olympic-level rigor, and profound respect for local culture, he restored confidence in his athletes and achieved historic results.
The pinnacle: the 2024 Paris Olympic Games. In a packed Grand Palais, his fencers accomplished the extraordinary by winning a bronze medal against France, the world number one team. Immense joy, shared without restraint, became a turning point for Japanese sabre.
But Jérôme didn’t stop there. With the medal in hand, he was already looking ahead to Los Angeles 2028. His mission: continue growing the team, develop young talent through the Elite Academy, and firmly establish Japan among the world’s leading fencing nations.
This story is not just about a coach. It is the story of a man who proves that you can stay true to yourself, even on the other side of the world, and create an alchemy between cultures to achieve excellence.
If you love stories where passion meets rigor, where a “French way” of working thrives in Japan and transforms a team from within, this episode is for you. Tune in to discover how Jérôme Guth turned a group toward excellence – and what this journey tells us about sport, mobility, and opportunities in Japan.

title: Pole Véhicule du Futur : A Learning Expedition to Japan to Explore the Future of Mobility
description:
In January 2024, the CCIFJ, in partnership with the Pôle Véhicule du Futur (Future Vehicle Cluster) organized a study week in Japan for a delegation of 15 French companies, focused on the themes of hydrogen and batteries.
Over five days, participants had the opportunity to meet with six key companies in the mobility and energy sectors (such as Kawasaki Heavy Industries, Yamaha Motor Company, Nissan…), as well as three renowned Japanese laboratories conducting research in these fields (such as the University of Tokyo). Two networking events, one in Osaka and one in Tokyo, including one hosted by Mr. Takashi Yatabe, director of the hydrogen department at TEPCO, which further enriched these discussions. Finally, the mission concluded with a seminar at the French Embassy in Japan, dedicated to the Japanese economy and the country's energy trends.
This trip provided participating companies with valuable insights into the current dynamics of the Japanese energy and mobility markets and allowed them to connect with key industry players.
We would like to thank the Pôle Véhicule du Futur for their trust!
