blocks.section: Pole Véhicule du Futur : A Learning Expedition to Japan to Explore the Future of Mobility
blocks.text: The Pôle Véhicule du Futur (Future Vehicle Cluster) organized a Hydrogen & Batteries mission to Japan, in the format of a Learning Expedition, in January 2024. Having a local partner is essential: the CCIFJ was the ideal choice. A preliminary program was developed in advance, along with a commercialization phase to secure the business model (minimum number of participants to confirm the 'GO'). This entire process was built with transparency and collaboration. Once the mission was secured, appointments with companies and laboratories were arranged: the CCIFJ's network of contacts opened many doors! We ended up with an intense, comprehensive program that fully satisfied the 15 participants from all over France. From Kobe to the Yamanashi region, then Tokyo, and finally up to the Ibaraki region and Fukushima-Namie for the FH2R project... everything was very well prepared by the CCIFJ teams, including our contact Mehdi Matagne. The delegation was also highly engaged, which energized our hosts, who were very open to discussion and led to the establishment of Franco-Japanese collaborative relationships! In detail, the mission was mainly focused on hydrogen (70%), with a supplementary focus on batteries. Upon arrival in Kobe-Osaka, we were able to visit Kawasaki Heavy Industries and their flagship hydrogen-related projects, followed by Kobelco, and then a networking evening with numerous Japanese companies, including some members of the Hydrogen Cluster. On the second day, we visited the leading fuel cell and component laboratory, as well as Yamaha, whose technological pragmatism is inspiring in an era dominated by single-technology preaching. On Wednesday, we delved into research with AIST, then visited the iconic FH2R site near Fukushima. Thursday and Friday continued along this path with IHI, Nissan, Tokyo University, another very rich networking session with many Japanese participants, and concluded with an exchange with the French Embassy in Japan. A competent and well-established local service provider is essential for organizing an effective international mission, and the CCIFJ met these expectations: a HUGE THANK YOU! »

title: Post-Pandemic Retreats in Northern Okinawa
description:
Sponsored content
As we carefully plan our post-pandemic travels, personal health and safety remain among our top priorities. Okinawa’s subtropical climate makes it an ideal place at any time of year to take a peacefully insular workcation. Stay focused and relax with family in a secluded villa, then enjoy socially distanced outdoor activities such as trekking through the forest, exploring ancient castle ruins, or cycling along quiet coastal roads in northern Okinawa.

blocks.section: Post-Pandemic Retreats in Northern Okinawa
blocks.text: As we carefully plan our post-pandemic travels, personal health and safety remain among our top priorities. Okinawa’s subtropical climate makes it an ideal place at any time of year to take a peacefully insular workcation. Stay focused and relax with family in a secluded villa, then enjoy socially distanced outdoor activities such as trekking through the forest, exploring ancient castle ruins, or cycling along quiet coastal roads in northern Okinawa.

blocks.section: — Spend a Peaceful Workcation in a Private Villa
blocks.text: — Spend a Peaceful Workcation in a Private Villa

blocks.section: — Spend a Peaceful Workcation in a Private Villa
blocks.text: For a safe and productive working retreat, Okinawa has a wide range of private accommodations in secluded locations where you can set up office, while remaining close to nature. On the Motobu Peninsula, you can rent an entire villa in its own private garden surrounded by trees from Shinminka Villa. Each villa is fully furnished with a deluxe kitchen and even an outdoor barbecue, so you can shop for fresh produce at local food markets and enjoy slow-life within the local village community. The newly built wooden buildings are modeled after traditional Okinawan minka folk houses, but redesigned with contemporary architecture—the outer walls are completely transparent to give you a 360-degree view of your immediate surroundings, and by extension an intimate connection with the natural environment.

blocks.section: — Explore Deep Ryukyu Culture in Nakijin
blocks.text: — Explore Deep Ryukyu Culture in Nakijin

blocks.section: — Explore Deep Ryukyu Culture in Nakijin
blocks.text: The site of the late 13th century Nakijin Castle is one of the nine Gusuku Sites and Related Properties of the Kingdom of Ryukyu, which are collectively designated as a World Cultural Heritage Site, representing five hundred years of Ryukyuan culture and history. The sprawling fortress of Nakijin Castle is a prime example of Nozura-zumi, an ancient construction technique that piles rocks according to their natural shape in order to build strong walls. You can easily spend a half a day exploring the ruins, walking across the undulating walls as you admire sweeping views of the surrounding forest and sea beyond, while reflecting upon the deep history of Ryukyu culture.

blocks.section: — Hike through the primitive forests of Yanbaru
blocks.text: — Hike through the primitive forests of Yanbaru

blocks.section: — Hike through the primitive forests of Yanbaru
blocks.text: Yanbaru is northern Okinawa’s mountainous region of primeval forests and rare endemic wildlife. Among its native subtropical flora are epiphytic ferns and orchids, living fossil cycads, giant banyans, evergreen Itajii, and the famous towering Okinawa Urajirogashi tree on Mt. Ibudake. Endemic species of fauna include the iconic Yanbaru kuina (Okinawa Rail), Noguchi gera (Okinawa Woodpecker), Ryukyu yamagame (Ryukyu Black Breasted Leaf Turtle). Hike up to cloud forests on Mt. Yonahadake, admire spectacular views from limestone cliffs overlooking Shioya Bay, or follow a scenic trail leading to the 26-meter drop of Hiji Otaki Falls.

blocks.section: — Discover the Romance of Kouri Island
blocks.text: — Discover the Romance of Kouri Island

blocks.section: — Discover the Romance of Kouri Island
blocks.text: If limiting interaction with others while slow traveling remains a concern, consider renting a bicycle in Nago and going for a refreshing ride along Kouri Island - it’s a highly charismatic destination for lovers, featuring the timeless attraction of a coralline rock formation in the shape of a heart, which is also the setting of Okinawa’s own Adam and Eve legend. From Nago, turn off Route 58 onto Yagaji Island, then continue across to Kouri Bridge, savoring each scenic minute of its 1,960-meter span over clear turquoise water. On the other side, enjoy touring the coastline with more luscious sea views around Kouri Island’s 8-kilometer circumference.

blocks.section: — Discover the Romance of Kouri Island
blocks.text: Wherever and however you choose to travel through the islands, keep in mind that the less populated, more wild region of northern Okinawa offers a variety of secluded retreats and safe activities for both a socially distanced workspace and a splendid vacation.

blocks.section: Price rises for nearly 3,000 food products in Japan
blocks.text: Starting in April, the price of around 2,800 food will increase this month.

blocks.section: Price rises for nearly 3,000 food products in Japan
blocks.text: This is the first time in 6 months that more than 2,000 food items will see their prices increased.

blocks.section: Price rises for nearly 3,000 food products in Japan
blocks.text: According to Teikoku Databank, the average price increase is around 23%. Among the items, processed foods - such as ham and sausages - will see the biggest increase.

blocks.section: Price rises for nearly 3,000 food products in Japan
blocks.text: In the future, higher import costs due to the weak yen and higher labor costs due to rising wages are likely to have an impact on selling prices .

title: From Biogas to Popcorn: An unexpected encounter that embodies the spirit of CCI France Japon
description:
At first glance, there is little to connect a company specializing in agricultural biogas production with a company promoting French gastronomy in Japan. Yet a chance encounter during a pilgrimage to Notre-Dame d'Akita led to a friendship and, eventually, a natural collaboration.
Today, NASKEO has chosen to sponsor Marc&Co's membership in CCI France Japon, perfectly illustrating the purpose of our sponsorship programme: to create lasting connections between companies that share common values and a desire to contribute to the development of Franco-Japanese relations.
An unexpected encounter that became a true friendship
It all began during a pilgrimage to Notre-Dame d'Akita. It was there that Félix Portier, CEO of NASKEO, and Marc Glaisse, founder of Marc&Co, first met. Despite operating in very different industries, they immediately connected.
"Our relationship started with a chance encounter that gradually turned into a genuine friendship," they explain.
They quickly discovered that they shared many values: a passion for entrepreneurship, an appetite for new projects and a strong commitment to fostering exchanges between France and Japan. A relationship built on trust developed and, a few years later, naturally led them to work together.
Two different worlds, one shared commitment
On one side, NASKEO Environnement develops innovative renewable energy solutions. Based in Sapporo, Hokkaido, the company is the exclusive distributor in Japan of agricultural biogas units designed by Biolectric. It supports Japanese dairy farms by transforming manure management into renewable energy and fertilizer.
On the other side, Marc&Co, founded in 2013 in Ashiya, showcases various aspects of French gastronomy in Japan through original concepts accessible to the general public. The company has developed several brands, including Glamourdise, dedicated to the world of Parisian macarons; Wafla, built around waffle croissants; and, more recently, Maïs Doré, a premium popcorn brand made from 100% French corn.
At first glance, biogas and popcorn have nothing in common. Yet their leaders share the same philosophy.
"Ultimately, we belong to the same world and help each other grow, demonstrating that there are French, or French-inspired, companies in Japan that truly deliver on their promises of quality," explains Félix.
When the best collaborations grow out of human connections
The opportunity to work together arose through a project linked to the French Embassy. This experience confirmed what they had already sensed: the strongest collaborations are often built on sincere relationships developed over time.
"Looking back, we would probably never have imagined that a simple encounter would lead us to work together a few years later," says Marc.
One anecdote perfectly illustrates this mindset. During the pilgrimage to Notre-Dame d'Akita, Marc took the initiative to prepare a buffet for all the participants and personally served each guest himself.
"The atmosphere he created that day encouraged people who had never spoken to each other to finally start conversations. Seeing him being both generous and humble left a strong impression on me. I immediately thought he was someone I would like to work with. Before business, this is the kind of spirit I look for: dedication, generosity and a genuine willingness to reach out to others."
Joining the CCIFJ Community
For Marc&Co, joining CCIFJ was an obvious choice. As a Japanese company deeply attached to its French roots, it aims to expand its professional network, meet other entrepreneurs and contribute to strengthening economic ties between France and Japan.
"CCIFJ seems to us to be the ideal environment for sharing experiences, developing partnerships and creating new opportunities for collaboration," says Marc.
For its part, NASKEO highlights the many benefits it has gained from being a member.
"Our business is highly specialized, and CCIFJ gives us access to a network of business leaders we would not otherwise meet. The sense of community among members is genuine and welcoming."
The company also emphasizes the value of CCIFJ's support services, particularly in recruitment, which provide meaningful assistance to French-minded organizations operating in Japan.
The story of NASKEO and Marc&Co is a great example of what the CCIFJ community can create. More than a simple recommendation, these kinds of relationships are what make our network so valuable: connections between companies from very different backgrounds, exchanges that transcend industries and collaborations that emerge where they are least expected.
Because beyond being a professional network, CCIFJ is above all a community that fosters meaningful encounters, encourages the sharing of experiences and creates lasting opportunities for collaboration between France and Japan.
NASKEO
MARC&CO

blocks.text: "The atmosphere he created that day encouraged people who had never spoken to each other to finally start conversations. Seeing him being both generous and humble left a strong impression on me. I immediately thought he was someone I would like to work with. Before business, this is the kind of spirit I look for: dedication, generosity and a genuine willingness to reach out to others."

blocks.section: Joining the CCIFJ Community
blocks.text: Joining the CCIFJ Community

blocks.section: Joining the CCIFJ Community
blocks.text: For Marc&Co, joining CCIFJ was an obvious choice. As a Japanese company deeply attached to its French roots, it aims to expand its professional network, meet other entrepreneurs and contribute to strengthening economic ties between France and Japan.

blocks.section: Joining the CCIFJ Community
blocks.text: "CCIFJ seems to us to be the ideal environment for sharing experiences, developing partnerships and creating new opportunities for collaboration," says Marc.

blocks.section: Joining the CCIFJ Community
blocks.text: For its part, NASKEO highlights the many benefits it has gained from being a member.

blocks.section: Joining the CCIFJ Community
blocks.text: "Our business is highly specialized, and CCIFJ gives us access to a network of business leaders we would not otherwise meet. The sense of community among members is genuine and welcoming."

blocks.section: Joining the CCIFJ Community
blocks.text: The company also emphasizes the value of CCIFJ's support services, particularly in recruitment, which provide meaningful assistance to French-minded organizations operating in Japan.

blocks.section: Joining the CCIFJ Community
blocks.text: The story of NASKEO and Marc&Co is a great example of what the CCIFJ community can create. More than a simple recommendation, these kinds of relationships are what make our network so valuable: connections between companies from very different backgrounds, exchanges that transcend industries and collaborations that emerge where they are least expected.

blocks.section: Joining the CCIFJ Community
blocks.text: Because beyond being a professional network, CCIFJ is above all a community that fosters meaningful encounters, encourages the sharing of experiences and creates lasting opportunities for collaboration between France and Japan.

blocks.text: Quick Guidance for Employment Adjustment Subsidy

blocks.section: Quick Guidance for Employment Adjustment Subsidy
blocks.text: Source : Miyuki Tsuboi - Certified Social Insurance & Labor Specialist at HR Advisory Services

blocks.section: Quick Guidance for Employment Adjustment Subsidy
blocks.text: An Employment Adjustment Subsidy ("Koyouchousei-jyoseikin") is provided for an employer, who has been forced to reduce business activities due to the effects of Covid-19 and temporarily suspended work, or who has trained or dispatched employees in order to maintain their employment, for some of the leave allowance paid to employees.

blocks.section: Quick Guidance for Employment Adjustment Subsidy
blocks.text: The term “to reduce business activities" means that the production index for the latest month has decreased by more than 5% compared to the same period last year. Details can be obtained through consultation via the Subsidy window at a local office of Ministry of Health, Labor, and Welfare (MHLW).

blocks.section: Event report: AEON France Fair – BONJOUR FRANCE 2026
blocks.text: From April 24 to 30, the new edition of “AEON France Fair - BONJOUR FRANCE 2026” was held in more than 5,000 AEON stores across Japan. Organized under the patronage of the French Embassy in Japan by BONJOUR FRANCE, the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCI France Japon), and the AEON Group, this nationwide event showcased French products, gastronomy, and the French Art de Vivre.

blocks.section: Event report: AEON France Fair – BONJOUR FRANCE 2026
blocks.text: The 2026 edition notably highlighted the Occitanie region, in southern France, which was chosen as the featured theme. It also strengthened collaboration with the regional offices of the CCI France Japon, particularly in the Kyushu, Nagoya, and Kansai regions. Also, on April 23, a special opening for the press and media was held at AEON Himonya.

blocks.section: Event report: AEON France Fair – BONJOUR FRANCE 2026
blocks.text: AEON Lake Town, in Koshigaya (Saitama), hosted the official opening ceremony of the event in the presence of several French and Japanese institutional and business representatives. Speeches were delivered by:

blocks.section: Event report: AEON France Fair – BONJOUR FRANCE 2026

blocks.section: Event report: AEON France Fair – BONJOUR FRANCE 2026

blocks.section: Event report: AEON France Fair – BONJOUR FRANCE 2026
blocks.text: Mitsuko TSUCHIYA, Board Director, Executive Vice President and Executive Officer, Merchandising and Logistics, AEON Co., Ltd

blocks.section: Event report: AEON France Fair – BONJOUR FRANCE 2026
blocks.text: The Kagami-biraki ceremony was then held alongside Yasuyuki FURUSAWA, President of AEON RETAIL Co., and Fabrice SOMMIER, MOF, President of the Union de la Sommellerie Française and founder of the Wine School.

blocks.section: Event report: AEON France Fair – BONJOUR FRANCE 2026
blocks.text: Throughout the week, numerous activities were offered to the public in several AEON Malls across the country, including Talk-Shows, Cooking-Shows, concerts, and live performances. AEON Lake Town notably served as the main operations hub. Various guests took part in these events, including Bebechan, Patric PACHON, and Fanny FERNANDES.

blocks.section: Event report: AEON France Fair – BONJOUR FRANCE 2026
blocks.text: The venue also hosted “Le Marché BONJOUR FRANCE,” where our exponents presented a selection of exceptional products, including Maison Brémond 1830, CLUIZEL, Le Comptoir, Le Jardin Gaulois, Porte Bonheur, Tokyo Gourmande, and GP Create.

blocks.section: Event report: AEON France Fair – BONJOUR FRANCE 2026
blocks.text: The success of this event once again demonstrated the dynamism of Franco-Japanese relations and the shared commitment to strengthening cultural exchanges between the two countries.

blocks.section: Event report: AEON France Fair – BONJOUR FRANCE 2026
blocks.text: We would like to thank all the distinguished guests who attended the opening ceremony, our exhibitors, and everyone who participated in the various events. We look forward to seeing you again next year!

title: Real wages fall for 23rd consecutive month in Japan
description: Wage increases have failed to keep pace with inflation: this is the longest decline on record.

blocks.text: Foresight

blocks.section: Real wages fall for 23rd consecutive month in Japan
blocks.text: Real wages fall for 23rd consecutive month in Japan

blocks.section: Real wages fall for 23rd consecutive month in Japan
blocks.text: Wage increases have failed to keep pace with inflation: this is the longest decline on record.

blocks.section: Real wages fall for 23rd consecutive month in Japan
blocks.text: According to government data released on Monday, real wages in Japan fell for the 23rd consecutive month .

blocks.section: Real wages fall for 23rd consecutive month in Japan
blocks.text: With Prime Minister Fumio Kishida calling on business leaders to raise wages at a rate below inflation, the country equaled its longest period of real wage decline since 1991, with a 1.3% drop in February.

blocks.section: Real wages fall for 23rd consecutive month in Japan
blocks.text: The last such decline occurred between 2007 and 2009 , during the global financial crisis.

blocks.section: Real wages fall for 23rd consecutive month in Japan
blocks.text: However, real wages have lagged behind price rises, essential to overcoming the deflationary stagnation that has prevailed since the 90s. Households’ purchasing power is declining, while the price of everyday consumer goods continues to rise due to rising raw material costs and the weak yen.

blocks.section: Real wages fall for 23rd consecutive month in Japan
blocks.text: The impact of higher starting salaries at major Japanese companies will be reflected in the future.

blocks.section: Recap of the Celebration Reception of the 10th Anniversary of BONJOUR FRANCE 2025
blocks.text: Recap of the Celebration Reception of the 10th Anniversary of BONJOUR FRANCE 2025

blocks.section: Recap of the Celebration Reception of the 10th Anniversary of BONJOUR FRANCE 2025
blocks.text: Let’s relive together the Celebration Reception of the 10th Anniversary of BONJOUR FRANCE 2025!

blocks.section: Recap of the Celebration Reception of the 10th Anniversary of BONJOUR FRANCE 2025
blocks.text: On November 12th, a limited number of 250 guests, including participants, invitees, sponsors, partners, members of the press, and VIPs, gathered at the Residence of the French Ambassador to Japan for the Reception celebrating the 10th Anniversary of BONJOUR FRANCE 2025.

blocks.section: Recap of the Celebration Reception of the 10th Anniversary of BONJOUR FRANCE 2025
blocks.text: The soirée was highlighted by the presence of special guests:

blocks.section: Recap of the Celebration Reception of the 10th Anniversary of BONJOUR FRANCE 2025
blocks.text: - Mizuka UENO, who has been a leading figure in the Japanese ballet world for over 20 years and is a world-renowned ballerina sought after by dancers around the world for collaborations.

blocks.section: Recap of the Celebration Reception of the 10th Anniversary of BONJOUR FRANCE 2025
blocks.text: - Laurent GHNASSINA, artistic director of LA BOITE TOKYO. He created the logo and visuals for the launch of BONJOUR FRANCE.

blocks.section: Recap of the Celebration Reception of the 10th Anniversary of BONJOUR FRANCE 2025
blocks.text: - Klara BLANC, a business leader and influencer based in Tokyo, where she has more than 900,000 followers on social media.

blocks.section: Recap of the Celebration Reception of the 10th Anniversary of BONJOUR FRANCE 2025
blocks.text: - Charles-Henry DEBOURG: after gaining experience in Michelin-starred kitchens around the world, he opened the modern French café “Charles-Henry” in Daikanyama, Tokyo, in April 2024.

blocks.section: Recap of the Celebration Reception of the 10th Anniversary of BONJOUR FRANCE 2025
blocks.text: - Bebechan, a well-known YouTuber in Japan whose YouTube channel “Bebechan – Français au Japon” has over 783k subscribers. On social media he even has over 1 million of followers.

blocks.section: Recap of the Celebration Reception of the 10th Anniversary of BONJOUR FRANCE 2025
blocks.text: - Florent DABADIE, interpreter and sports news presenter, who hosted the entire soirée as the MC.

blocks.section: Recap of the Celebration Reception of the 10th Anniversary of BONJOUR FRANCE 2025
blocks.text: The soirée began with speeches by Mr. Gilles BORDES, Minister Counselor for Economic Affairs at the French Embassy in Japan, and Mr. Jérôme CHOUCHAN, President of the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan, who came to celebrate the 10th anniversary of BONJOUR FRANCE.

blocks.section: Recap of the Celebration Reception of the 10th Anniversary of BONJOUR FRANCE 2025
blocks.text: The ceremony was hosted by Florent DABADIE, interpreter and sports commentator. It continued with the screening of a commemorative video retracing the 10 years of effort, evolution, and influence of BONJOUR FRANCE since its creation in 2015, followed by a breathtaking performance by the famous Japanese ballerina Mizuka UENO.

blocks.section: Recap of the Celebration Reception of the 10th Anniversary of BONJOUR FRANCE 2025
blocks.text: This was followed by a toast led by Laurent GHNASSIA, Artistic Director of LA BOITE TOKYO, accompanied by a glass of Champagne Lanson, the event’s main sponsor. This kanpai also marked the moment to enjoy a magnificent buffet specially prepared for the occasion by the executive Chef of the French Ambassador in Japan.

blocks.section: Recap of the Celebration Reception of the 10th Anniversary of BONJOUR FRANCE 2025
blocks.text: Several exhibitors also offered you the opportunity to taste and discover true French craftsmanship.

blocks.section: Recap of the Celebration Reception of the 10th Anniversary of BONJOUR FRANCE 2025
blocks.text: A special entertainment was offered during a first talk session featuring Klara BLANC, Florent DABADIE, and Laurent GHNASSIA. To create an unforgettable festive moment, a champagne sabrage was performed by the Confrérie du Sabre d'Or.

blocks.section: Recap of the Celebration Reception of the 10th Anniversary of BONJOUR FRANCE 2025
blocks.text: Some lucky participants also had the chance to take home gifts provided by our sponsors through a tombola held during the event. With a total of seven prizes, including bottles of Champagne Lanson and BONJOUR FRANCE tote bags, many guests left with their hands full!

blocks.section: Recap of the Celebration Reception of the 10th Anniversary of BONJOUR FRANCE 2025
blocks.text: To continue the soirée, a second talk session was held featuring Mizuka UENO and Florent DABADIE, an inspiring discussion full of exciting perspectives. Finally, to conclude the evening on a sweet note, a surprise dessert was prepared by Charles-Henry LEBOURG and Bebechan, offering the last French delicacy of the night. Before leaving, each participant received a tote bag and Tory Burch notebooks, accompanied by a bottle of Champagne Lanson as a gift, allowing everyone to fully enjoy French culture, both in terms of gastronomy and lifestyle.

blocks.section: Recap of the Celebration Reception of the 10th Anniversary of BONJOUR FRANCE 2025
blocks.text: The Reception, highly appreciated by visitors, celebrated the many events organized by BONJOUR FRANCE and concluded on an optimistic note for the year ahead. We would like to thank the French Embassy in Japan, as well as all the sponsors and partners who helped make this evening a success, with special thanks to Champagne Lanson, and Mottox Co., Ltd..

title: Recap of the France–Japan Import-Export Seminar in Gunma
description: On Monday, June 30, CCIFJ Gunma held its very first event at the Gunma Prefectural Government Building since opening in January 2025.

blocks.text: Gunma Event report

blocks.section: Recap of the France–Japan Import-Export Seminar in Gunma
blocks.text: Recap of the France–Japan Import-Export Seminar in Gunma

blocks.section: Recap of the France–Japan Import-Export Seminar in Gunma
blocks.text: On Monday, June 30, CCIFJ Gunma held its very first event at the Gunma Prefectural Government Building since opening in January 2025.

blocks.section: Recap of the France–Japan Import-Export Seminar in Gunma
blocks.text: Focused on the theme of import-export between France and Gunma, this inaugural event was a great success, bringing together over 35 participants.

blocks.section: Recap of the France–Japan Import-Export Seminar in Gunma
blocks.text: The first part of the event, held in the form of a seminar, took place at Netsugen Seminar Space , located on the 32nd floor of the prefectural building. Offering a panoramic view of the surrounding Maebashi mountains, this modern coworking space also features a seminar room that can accommodate around fifty people.

blocks.section: Recap of the France–Japan Import-Export Seminar in Gunma
blocks.text: The seminar opened with a speech by Takashi SOMEYA , Director of the Future Investment and Digital Industry Division at the prefecture, who highlighted Gunma’s strong commitment to supporting the development of the CCIFJ office and strengthening Franco-Japanese economic relations. We would like to take this opportunity to sincerely thank the Gunma Prefecture for its valuable financial and logistical support as the event’s official sponsor.

blocks.section: Recap of the France–Japan Import-Export Seminar in Gunma
blocks.text: As an introduction, Justine BAILLY, Manager of the Gunma Desk, and Louna WANG, Project Manager of Start in France , presented the activities of the CCIFJ and the latest news from the Gunma office, emphasizing the Chamber’s growing interest in expanding its initiatives beyond Tokyo.

blocks.section: Recap of the France–Japan Import-Export Seminar in Gunma
blocks.text: The main part of the seminar featured two CCIFJ member companies based in Gunma:

blocks.section: Recap of the France–Japan Import-Export Seminar in Gunma
blocks.text: Kōki YUASA , Director of Aritaya , a soy sauce producer exporting notably to France, spoke about the international development of his business. He shared his experience in seeking French partners and participating in trade shows in France. He also stressed the importance of preserving the artisanal production of natural soy sauce and maintaining the rich culinary heritage of Japan, even abroad.

blocks.section: Recap of the France–Japan Import-Export Seminar in Gunma
blocks.text: Kurumi TADOKORO , Director of NAC , an importer and distributor of Guérande salt in Japan, introduced the unique qualities of this emblematic product, illustrated with photos from her recent trip to France, where she visited salt marshes and met local producers. She also addressed the challenges her company faces in the current uncertain global economic climate, which has had an impact on their activities in Japan.

blocks.section: Recap of the France–Japan Import-Export Seminar in Gunma
blocks.text: In the second part of the event, participants gathered for a friendly French-style aperitif in the Gingham kitchen area, located on the 31st floor, an ideal setting for informal receptions. The guests, mostly Japanese, enjoyed French wines and typical aperitif delicacies. Aritaya and NAC also offered tastings of their products: natural soy sauce and Guérande salt .

blocks.section: Recap of the France–Japan Import-Export Seminar in Gunma
blocks.text: This reception was made possible thanks to the support of Netsugen , whose coordinators we warmly thank for their valuable assistance, which greatly contributed to the success of this convivial gathering.

blocks.section: Recap of the France–Japan Import-Export Seminar in Gunma
blocks.text: We look forward to welcoming you again very soon for upcoming events in Gunma!

blocks.text: Le gouvernement japonais a diffusé des consignes (voir ci-dessous) et pris un ensemble de mesures :

blocks.section: Mesures de portée générale :
blocks.text: surveillance médicale interne accrue depuis le 28 janvier. Conformément à la législation en vigueur, les autorités locales peuvent décider d’hospitaliser et de soumettre à des examens médicaux les personnes susceptibles d’être infectées, avec une prise en charge par l’État japonais ;

blocks.section: Mesures de portée générale :
blocks.text: possibilité de mise en quarantaine des personnes exposées ou ayant développé des symptômes ;

blocks.section: Mesures de portée générale :
blocks.text: fermeture, à compter du 2 mars, de tous les établissements primaires et secondaires du pays jusqu’à la fin des vacances de printemps et vraisemblablement au-delà dans certains départements ;

blocks.section: Mesures de portée générale :
blocks.text: incitation au report ou à l’annulation des événements de grande ampleur prévus dans des lieux confinés.

blocks.section: Mesures de portée générale :
blocks.text: Le gouvernement japonais a décrété l’état d’urgence dans sept préfectures (Tokyo, Kanagawa, Chiba, Saitama, Osaka, Hyogo et Fukuoka) le 7 avril, avant de décider de l’étendre à tout le territoire japonais le 16 avril. Il doit durer jusqu’au 31 mai. Sur cette base, les gouverneurs des préfectures peuvent adopter les mesures qu’ils jugent nécessaires pour freiner la propagation du Covid-19 au sein de leur territoire : demande de confinement à domicile, fermetures d’établissements tels que les écoles et certains commerces non essentiels, annulations d’événements et réquisitions à des fins sanitaires. Tous les Français actuellement au Japon sont invités à se tenir informés, notamment en consultant les sites internet mis en place par les autorités préfectorales, et à respecter rigoureusement l’ensemble des consignes et recommandations. Pour plus d’informations sur l’état d’urgence .

blocks.section: Mesures de portée générale :
blocks.text: Le panel d’experts du gouvernement recommande par ailleurs à l’ensemble de la population depuis le 22 avril d’appliquer les dix mesures suivantes :

blocks.section: Mesures de portée générale :
blocks.text: Maintenir le contact avec ses proches par appel téléphonique ou vidéo tout en évitant les rencontres physiques (Ce point concerne particulièrement les personnes dont les parents ou proches sont âgés et résident dans un lieu différent) ;

blocks.section: Mesures de portée générale :
blocks.text: Faire ses courses seul et éviter les heures d’affluences dans les supermarchés ;

blocks.section: Mesures de portée générale :
blocks.text: Faire son jogging seul ou en petit groupe et aux heures où les parcs sont les moins peuplés ;

blocks.section: Mesures de portée générale :
blocks.text: Réaliser les achats les moins urgents en ligne ;

blocks.section: Mesures de portée générale :
blocks.text: Garder le contact avec ses amis en ligne plutôt que de sortir en ville ;

blocks.section: Mesures de portée générale :
blocks.text: Consulter son médecin par internet, notamment pour les consultations de routine ;

blocks.section: Mesures de portée générale :
blocks.text: Faire du sport chez soi ;

blocks.section: Mesures de portée générale :
blocks.text: Préférer les plats à emporter ou la livraison à domicile plutôt que le restaurant ;

blocks.section: Mesures de portée générale :
blocks.text: Privilégier le télétravail ;

blocks.section: Mesures de portée générale :
blocks.text: Porter un masque , notamment pour parler.

blocks.section: Conseils des autorités japonaises – mesures individuelles :
blocks.text: Conseils des autorités japonaises – mesures individuelles :

blocks.section: Conseils des autorités japonaises – mesures individuelles :
blocks.text: Pour les personnes présentants des symptômes, le panel d’experts du gouvernement a formulé les recommandations suivantes :

blocks.section: Conseils des autorités japonaises – mesures individuelles :
blocks.text: Les personnes qui ont une fièvre supérieure à 37,5°C pendant plus de 4 jours ou qui ressentent une fatigue intense et des difficultés respiratoires sont invitées à contacter leur service départemental de consultation téléphonique ( voir liste - informations en japonais ). En cas de symptômes de rhume et de fièvre, ce conseil concerne également les personnes qui suivent un traitement antipyrétique (pour le traitement de la fièvre).

blocks.section: Conseils des autorités japonaises – mesures individuelles :
blocks.text: Pour les personnes âgées, diabétiques, souffrant d’insuffisance cardiaque ou respiratoire, sous dialyse, ou sous traitement anticancéreux ou immunosuppresseur et qui sont susceptibles de présenter des symptômes graves en cas de contamination, les recommandations ci-dessus sont valables dès le deuxième jour après l’apparition des symptômes.

blocks.section: Conseils des autorités japonaises – mesures individuelles :
blocks.text: Les femmes enceintes sont également invitées à consulter le plus rapidement possible en cas de symptômes.

blocks.section: Conseils des autorités japonaises – mesures individuelles :
blocks.text: À ce stade, les enfants ne sont pas considérés comme des personnes susceptibles de souffrir de symptômes graves et peuvent donc suivre les recommandations valables pour la population générale.

blocks.section: Conseils des autorités japonaises – mesures individuelles :
blocks.text: Si vous présentez l’un de ces symptômes (fièvre, symptômes du rhume) :

blocks.section: Conseils des autorités japonaises – mesures individuelles :
blocks.text: limiter les sorties, ne pas se rendre au travail ou à l’école et prendre quotidiennement sa température.

blocks.section: Conseils des autorités japonaises – mesures individuelles :
blocks.text: porter un masque

blocks.section: Conseils des autorités japonaises – mesures individuelles :
blocks.text: prévenir à l’avance l’établissement médical avant de s’y rendre pour faire des examens

blocks.section: Conseils des autorités japonaises – mesures individuelles :
blocks.text: structures médicales et hotline pouvant être contactées : À Tokyo : Tokyo Novel Coronavirus General Consultation Call Center (tél : 0570-550571 /anglophone), de 9:00 à 21:00 tous les jours ; En-dehors de Tokyo : ligne anglophone d’assistance générale « Japan HELPLINE » (tél : 0570 000 911), pour une orientation vers un établissement médical en cas d’urgence ; Le ministère japonais de la santé invite les étrangers à contacter la Japan visitor Hotline qui répond également à vos questions pour une assistance y compris pour le coronavirus (tél : 050-3816-2787 /anglophone, 24/7) ; Dans le Kansai (PDF) ; contacts utiles dans l’Ouest du Japon (PDF)

blocks.section: Conseils des autorités japonaises – mesures individuelles :
blocks.text: Certaines préfectures japonaises ont également mis en place des services de consultation en langues étrangères pour les ressortissants étrangers.

blocks.section: Conseils des autorités japonaises – mesures individuelles :
blocks.text: D’une manière générale, le gouvernement recommande à l’ensemble de la population d’éviter les rassemblements publics, et particulièrement les lieux mal ventilés. Plusieurs collectivités locales ont pris des mesures spécifiques selon leur situation. Les départements de la région du Kantō recommandent ainsi depuis le 26 mars d’éviter autant que possible les déplacements non-nécessaires et de privilégier le télétravail lorsque c’est possible.

title: Record number of foreign passengers at Kansai airport
description: This is the second highest number of foreign passengers ever recorded at Kansai Airport.

blocks.text: Companies news

blocks.section: Record number of foreign passengers at Kansai airport
blocks.text: Record number of foreign passengers at Kansai airport

blocks.section: Record number of foreign passengers at Kansai airport
blocks.text: This is the second highest number of foreign passengers ever recorded at Kansai Airport.

blocks.section: Record number of foreign passengers at Kansai airport
blocks.text: The number of foreign passengers taking international flights to Kansai Airport was 15 million between April 2023 and March this year , according to the latest data from Kansai Airport, the operator of Kansai Airport.

blocks.section: Record number of foreign passengers at Kansai airport
blocks.text: This is the second highest number of foreign passengers ever recorded after a record 15.5 million achieved in fiscal 2018, also signaling Japan's tourism recovery from the Covid pandemic.

blocks.section: Record number of foreign passengers at Kansai airport
blocks.text: On the other hand, the number of Japanese passengers using international flights was 3.94 million this year. Despite the weak yen, Kansai Airport said it expected an increase next year.

title: Record sales for distribution giant Æon
description: The company expects record sales of 10,000 billion yen for the coming year.

blocks.text: Companies news

blocks.section: Record sales for distribution giant Æon
blocks.text: Record sales for distribution giant Æon

blocks.section: Record sales for distribution giant Æon
blocks.text: The company expects record sales of 10,000 billion yen for the coming year.

blocks.section: Record sales for distribution giant Æon
blocks.text: Japanese distribution giant Æon has announced record sales and operating profit for the year just ended .

blocks.section: Record sales for distribution giant Æon
blocks.text: At a press conference, Æon President Akio Yoshida stated that he wanted to “respond [to household needs] by taking the situation into account.” Faced with a situation of rising food prices , households in Japan are in fact facing an increase in the Engel coefficient, i.e. the share of consumption allocated to food expenditure.

blocks.section: Record sales for distribution giant Æon
blocks.text: Between February 2023 and February 2024, the Group has announced a level of sales almost 5% higher than the previous year, i.e. nearly 9,500 billion yen (almost 57 billion euros).

blocks.section: Record sales for distribution giant Æon
blocks.text: The company also announced that it expected sales to reach 10,000 billion yen in the current fiscal year (equivalent to 60 billion euros), just behind Seven & i Holdings.

blocks.section: Record sales for distribution giant Æon
blocks.text: This result is linked to the improved performance of supermarkets in general, and a significant increase in the profits of small supermarkets such as Maibasuketto.

blocks.section: Record sales for distribution giant Æon
blocks.text: In addition to an increase in distribution prices due to higher food prices, the company also expects higher labor costs due to rising wages in Japan .

title: Record tax-free sales in supermarkets
description: Tax-free sales in supermarkets were 2.4 times higher than in the same month last year.

blocks.text: Foresight

blocks.section: Record tax-free sales in supermarkets
blocks.text: Record tax-free sales in supermarkets

blocks.section: Record tax-free sales in supermarkets
blocks.text: Tax-free sales in supermarkets were 2.4 times higher than in the same month last year.

blocks.section: Record tax-free sales in supermarkets
blocks.text: Sales of tax-free products in supermarkets increased by a factor of 2.4 in March 2024 compared with the same period last year . This record figure is attributable to the weakening yen and the upturn in tourism,

blocks.section: Record tax-free sales in supermarkets
blocks.text: According to a report published by the Japan Superstore Association, sales amounted to 510.9 billion yen last month, an increase of around 1% on the same month of the previous year. This was the 25th consecutive month of growth.

blocks.section: Record tax-free sales in supermarkets
blocks.text: Among the sales of large stores, tax-free sales amounted to 49.5 billion yen, 2.4 times higher than in the same month last year. This is the highest record since 2014, when the surveys began.

blocks.section: Record tax-free sales in supermarkets
blocks.text: “The weak yen is very beneficial for foreign customers,” said Japan Superstore Association CEO Yoko Yasuda . However, she remains cautious: “if the yen weakens further, Japanese customers could enter a phase where it [will be] difficult to buy.”

description: The French Chamber of Commerce and Industries in Japan had the pleasure of hosting this year’s European Joint Chambers Networking Party.

blocks.section: Reflecting on the European Joint Chambers Networking Party 2022
blocks.text: Reflecting on the European Joint Chambers Networking Party 2022

blocks.section: Reflecting on the European Joint Chambers Networking Party 2022
blocks.text: The French Chamber of Commerce and Industries in Japan had the pleasure of hosting this year’s European Joint Chambers Networking Party.

blocks.section: Reflecting on the European Joint Chambers Networking Party 2022
blocks.text: On Tuesday, October 18 at The Tokyo EDITION, Toranomon, we welcomed more than 220 guests with the collaboration of 14 chambers: Austrian Business Council, British Center of Commerce, Belgian-Luxembourg Chamber of Commerce, Danish Chamber of Commerce, Finnish Chamber of Commerce, German Chamber of Commerce, South Africa Chamber of Commerce, Spanish Chamber of Commerce, Netherlands Chamber of Commerce, Greek Chamber of Commerce, Norwegian Chamber of Commerce, Swedish Chamber of Commerce, and the Swiss Chamber of Commerce – with the support of the European Business Council.

blocks.section: Reflecting on the European Joint Chambers Networking Party 2022
blocks.text: This year’s party was especially memorable, as it celebrated the 50 th anniversary of the European Business Council, and a birthday cake was brought to the stage to commemorate a half-century of operations in Japan.

blocks.section: Reflecting on the European Joint Chambers Networking Party 2022
blocks.text: The party finished off with the traditional raffle, in which the luckiest of attendees were gifted 6 premium gifts. The first prize was a bottle of Mouton Cadet Cuvee Heritage with a dinner for two at the Tokyo EDITION, Toranomon.

blocks.section: Reflecting on the European Joint Chambers Networking Party 2022
blocks.text: With free-flowing drinks provided by Baron Philippe de Rothschild, Reserve Royale, Bière des Amis, Monin, Perrier, and food from Jewels Farm and Godiva, guests enjoyed not only a night of business opportunities and development but also one of cultural sharing and exchange.

blocks.section: Reflecting on the European Joint Chambers Networking Party 2022
blocks.text: We hope to see you all again next year at our European Joint Chambers Networking Party 2023!

title: Comité Fiscalité et Réglementation
description:
Ce jeudi 12 décembre 2024, la Chambre de commerce et d'industrie française au Japon a eu l'honneur d'accueillir Maitre Ayano Kanezuka, avocate aux Barreaux de Paris et de Tokyo-Daini, du cabinet LPA Tokyo, pour un événement du Comité Fiscalité et Réglementation.
Cet événement a été l'occasion d'approfondir nos connaissances sur l'entrée en vigueur de la nouvelle réforme de la loi sur la protection des données personnelles, prévue pour juin 2025. Maitre Kanezuka a également abordé les différences entre la protection des données en France et au Japon, en soulignant les impacts significatifs de cette réforme sur les entreprises responsables de la protection des données.
La séance s'est conclue par une session de questions-réponses approfondie, où Maitre Kanezuka a répondu aux préoccupations et interrogations des participants concernant la protection des données personnelles dans des domaines tels que la médecine, l'intelligence artificielle et les données personnelles.

title: Regards Croisés – BEL Japan: 20 Years of Cheese Innovation in the Heart of Tokyo
description:
In this new episode of our series Business: Regards Croisés, we meet BEL Japan, a subsidiary of the BEL Group, which this year celebrates its 20th anniversary in Japan. Having entered the archipelago in 1983 with the Kiri brand, the group has succeeded in transforming a product once seen as exotic into an everyday favorite for millions of Japanese consumers.
“It has become part of Japanese daily consumption throughout the day. They see it as a ‘Me Moment,’ something they can enjoy peacefully during the day to take a small break,” says Aytekin Yildiz, President and CEO of Bel Japan.
A cultural challenge successfully met
When BEL first entered Japan, cheese consumption remained marginal. The initial challenge was to introduce a new product while respecting local eating habits. Kiri found its place by focusing on a positioning centered around personal well-being: “Be kind to yourself.” Today, Kiri’s individual portions have become a daily ritual, particularly appreciated by Japanese women who see it as a moment of sweetness and comfort.
A laboratory of innovation for the BEL Group
The Japanese market quickly established itself as a key testing ground for BEL. Japan saw the launch of unique products such as Kiri Sweet Cheese, the brand’s first sweet version, combining cream cheese with fruit. The country also witnessed the creation of Kiri Cafés, in partnership with Bagel & Bagel - BEL’s first permanent food service experience. These local initiatives often became models and sources of inspiration for other international markets, making Japan a true innovation hub for the group.
A company committed to empowering women
Beyond its commercial success, BEL Japan stands out for its strong social commitment. With a team that is 60% women, the subsidiary has launched a female empowerment program as part of Kiri’s “Brand Social Role.” The goal: to strengthen women’s confidence and position in Japanese society, well beyond product consumption.
A market with sustainable growth
Although cheese consumption in Japan remains lower than in Europe, it continues to grow steadily. Japan is now BEL’s largest market in Asia, thanks in particular to its portion-based products, perfectly suited to local snacking habits and the pursuit of a balanced diet. In the medium term, growth is expected to continue, driven by the increasing recognition of cheese as both a healthy and indulgent food.

title: Regards croisés – Ceysson & Bénétière: The international ambition of a French gallery
description:
In this new episode of our Business: Regards croisés series, we meet Loïc Bénétière, partner and founder of Ceysson & Bénétière Art Gallery. Founded in Saint-Étienne, the gallery celebrates its twentieth anniversary this year and continues to follow a distinctive path: that of a major player in contemporary art, now present in France, across Europe, in the United States, and more recently in Japan, with the opening of a new space in Tokyo.
“Having artworks is not so difficult. But once they are there, they profoundly change your life: they bring you an added dimension of soul.”

The gallery’s origins and an international vision
Founded in 2006 in Saint-Étienne, Galerie Ceysson & Bénétière rapidly expanded internationally, establishing locations in Europe, the United States, and most recently Tokyo. Championing abstraction and the French avant-garde of the 1970s while also representing major American artists, the gallery has brought to life a long-standing ambition in Tokyo: establishing a presence in Asia.This opening was made possible in particular thanks to Leslie You, an art specialist and now Director of the Tokyo gallery.
In a profession where recognition is built over time, the opening nonetheless received strong international media attention, and the gallery now welcomes an average of around thirty visitors per day.

A gallery conceived as an ideal space for works between luxury and history
Designed as an ideal gallery space, the Tokyo location is the result of a significant investment, carried out within the Japanese context of strict regulations, high costs, and tightly structured timelines. Conceived as an exceptional venue, it aims to provide a setting worthy of the artists exhibited and to establish a lasting presence within Tokyo’s cultural landscape.
Positioned at the intersection of art and luxury, the gallery presents internationally renowned artists and addresses discerning collectors with a deep sensitivity to art history. Ceysson & Bénétière thus attracts an audience in search of singular works, while maintaining an approach firmly rooted in a demanding and coherent reading of art.

Building a sustainable artistic dialogue in Tokyo
The relationship to art differs significantly across cultures. In Japan, very large-scale works, common in Europe, are less frequent, and relationships with collectors tend to unfold over time, grounded in explanation, contextualization, and the gradual construction of trust. This slower process requires pedagogy and consistency, but it also fosters a deeper dialogue, notes Loïc Bénétière.
In this spirit, the gallery pursues a dual ambition: introducing French and American artists to Japanese audiences, while also identifying and supporting Japanese artists to later exhibit them on the European scene. While Japanese art already enjoys strong recognition in Europe, and many French artists maintain historical ties with Japanese movements of the 1970s, the gallery’s image can sometimes appear intimidating. To overcome this perception, Ceysson & Bénétière has developed off-site formats, collaborating on pop-up exhibitions and alternative venues to make art more accessible. In Tokyo, this dynamic is led by Leslie You, whose on-the-ground work with collectors strengthens the project’s local roots.Web site

title: Regards Croisés – Intellectual Property and Artificial Intelligence: what does the law say?
description:
In this new episode of our Business : Regards Croisés series, Emmanuel Podevin, President of the French National Company of Industrial Property Attorneys, shares his analysis of major trends in intellectual property law in France and Japan.
And his conclusion is clear:
"Artificial intelligence today raises real challenges when it comes to copyright law."
Throughout the discussion, he sheds light with precision on current legal issues and emerging challenges tied to innovation:
The structural differences between the French and Japanese systems of protecting inventionsThe central role of patents in a well-managed innovation strategyThe new legal issues raised by AI, particularly concerning ownership of generated creationsThe evolving role of industrial property attorneys, now expected to act as strategic partnersAnd the best practices to adopt in order to secure intangible assets in an international context
An essential conversation for companies focused on innovation, seeking to understand how the law can support - and anticipate - technological transformations.

description:
In this new episode (in English) of our series Business regards croisés, Akihito Uesada, mayor of Matsue, reflects on the relationship between Matsue and France, as well as the key role played by the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCIFJ) in strengthening cultural and economic ties between the two countries.
Throughout this conversation, Akihito Uesada explores the unique history of Matsue and analyzes the cultural and economic dynamics that connect the city to France:
 	 	The international prominence of Matsue, a city of living art and culture where traditions -nfrom matcha tea to Yakumonuri lacquer - remain an integral part of daily life 	 	 	The central role of the CCIFJ in fostering cultural and economic exchanges between Matsue and France 	 	 	The importance of local craftsmanship and the transmission of traditional skills as a driver of cooperation and tourist appeal 	 	 	The symbolic link between Matsue and Paris, illustrated by the peony, Matsue’s emblematic flower also present at the Bois de Vincennes 	 	 	The ambition to further strengthen economic, industrial, and tourism collaborations in a sustainable and people-centered way 	 
An inspiring interview highlighting the vision of a Japanese city proud of its heritage and fully committed to cultural dialogue and future-oriented development.

title: Regards Croisés – La French Tech Tokyo: A Bridge Between French and Japanese Ecosystems
description:
In this second episode of our Business: Cross Perspectives series, we give the floor to Aude Moras, Head of Product at Tripla and President of French Tech Tokyo.
WATCH THE FULL INTERVIEW 
Ten years ago, France launched the French Tech initiative with a clear ambition: to unite an emerging ecosystem in order to accelerate innovation and support startups. Since then, the movement has become a true benchmark, with more than 50 French Tech capitals in France and 70 communities worldwide, including Tokyo.
"Japan will not welcome you with open arms. Even if you have achieved great success in France or Europe, you will need to prove yourself again and start from scratch in the Japanese market."
French Tech Tokyo’s mission is threefold:
 	 	Support French entrepreneurs seeking to establish themselves in Japan. 	 	 	Help Japanese investors and entrepreneurs expand into France. 	 	 	Actively contribute to the growth of the Tokyo startup ecosystem. 	 
With 600 members, a board of 8 volunteers, and a very active community, French Tech Tokyo fosters a network where networking events, panel discussions, and collaborations with Japanese tech players intersect.
A bilateral platform of opportunities The initiative serves as a unique lever to encourage exchanges and partnerships around innovation. On the French side, an entrepreneur who starts a company in France and wants to expand internationally can rely on French Tech. On the Japanese side, there are also opportunities to invest, collaborate, and set up operations in France.
The Japanese challenge: starting from scratch with humility Establishing a presence in Japan requires a particular mindset: even when a startup has already proven itself in France, it must accept the need to rebuild its legitimacy locally, with patience and humility. Another major challenge remains visibility - raising awareness of the French Tech ecosystem among Japanese stakeholders.
A future of strong growth French Tech Tokyo envisions itself as a long-term, ever-growing movement. Thanks to the energy of its members and the support of its partners, the community aims to further strengthen the bridges between France and Japan, in a spirit of cooperation and shared innovation.
An inspiring testimony for all startups and investors who dream of venturing between Paris and Tokyo: French Tech demonstrates that with a network mindset and a global vision, opportunities are limitless.  
WATCH THE FULL INTERVIEW

title: Regards Croisés – La Maison du Chocolat in Japan: French Excellence and Japanese Finesse
description:
In this first episode of our Business: Cross Perspectives series, we give the floor to Benjamin Costa, CEO of La Maison du Chocolat, a jewel of French craftsmanship that has become a true benchmark for premium chocolate in Japan.
Watch the full interview
As the brand’s second-largest market after France, Japan perfectly illustrates the successful encounter between French artisanal know-how and cultural refinement.  And the observation is clear:
“The Japanese have an immediate connection with excellence and craftsmanship: they ask questions, taste with finesse, and value chocolate as an exceptional product.”
Throughout the conversation, Benjamin Costa sheds light on the specificities of this demanding market and shares his strategic vision for the future:
Adapting to the Japanese market:
 	 	Special attention to packaging – two-piece boxes, delicate separators, kawaii touches – to match Japan’s gift culture and aesthetic sensibility. 	 	 	A product offering designed both for personal enjoyment and the art of gifting, at the heart of local customs. 	 
Strategic choice of locations:
 	 	Recent openings of two remarkable venues in Takanawa and Seibu. 	 	 	A new boutique-salon concept offering an all-day menu (lunch, after-five, small plates), enabling customers to experience French excellence in everyday life. 	 
Balancing French and Japanese influences:
 	 	A luxury identity defined by excellence rather than price: each chocolate is handmade, a reflection of the artistry of its recipes and the quality of its ingredients. 	 	 	A proud presence within the Comité Colbert, embodying the global influence of French luxury and art de vivre. 	 
An inspiring testimony for any French company looking to establish itself in Japan: it demonstrates how heritage, innovation, and cultural sensitivity can elevate a product into a true art of living.

blocks.section: Regards Croisés – Les Langues du Monde: Decoding Japanese-Style Leadership
blocks.text: In this new episode of our Business: Crossed Perspectives series, we welcome Ana Escobedo , founder and director of Les Langues du Monde , a pioneering company in intercultural training and global leadership development in Japan.

blocks.section: Regards Croisés – Les Langues du Monde: Decoding Japanese-Style Leadership
blocks.text: « Being a good leader in Japan isn’t about being more friendly; it’s about knowing how to inspire respect within a hierarchical framework. »

blocks.section: Regards Croisés – Les Langues du Monde: Decoding Japanese-Style Leadership
blocks.text: Navigating the Codes of Japanese Management

blocks.section: Regards Croisés – Les Langues du Monde: Decoding Japanese-Style Leadership
blocks.text: When a foreign executive arrives in Japan, they quickly discover that the usual management benchmarks do not apply in the same way. The country values hierarchy, restraint, and often in contrast with the more direct Western approaches. The teams at Les Langues du Monde support these leaders by helping them establish their legitimacy in an environment where politeness and discretion prevail over confrontation.

blocks.section: Regards Croisés – Les Langues du Monde: Decoding Japanese-Style Leadership
blocks.text: Understanding a Unique Decision-Making Process

blocks.section: Regards Croisés – Les Langues du Monde: Decoding Japanese-Style Leadership
blocks.text: The corporate decision-making process particularly illustrates this cultural gap. Whereas Western organizations favor speed and debate, Japanese companies rely on thorough preparation and upstream consultation. An approach sometimes perceived as slow, but one that ensures smooth and harmonious implementation once the decision has been made.

blocks.section: Regards Croisés – Les Langues du Monde: Decoding Japanese-Style Leadership
blocks.text: Comprehensive and Tailored Support

blocks.section: Regards Croisés – Les Langues du Monde: Decoding Japanese-Style Leadership
blocks.text: The support offered by Les Langues du Monde goes far beyond language training. Each program is custom-designed, blending language learning, leadership development, and a deep understanding of Japan’s implicit cultural codes. Executives receive personalized follow-ups, practical exercises, and simulations inspired by real-life situations to learn to communicate with clarity, confidence, and intercultural sensitivity.

blocks.section: Regards Croisés – Les Langues du Monde: Decoding Japanese-Style Leadership
blocks.text: Training Leaders Who Can Bridge Cultures

blocks.section: Regards Croisés – Les Langues du Monde: Decoding Japanese-Style Leadership
blocks.text: By sharing its expertise, Les Langues du Monde helps foster a new generation of leaders capable of navigating across cultures, building trust, and strengthening international cooperation, an invaluable skill in a world where intercultural understanding has become a true driver of success.

title: Regards Croisés – Luxury Hospitality in Japan: What Evolutions, What Challenges?
description:
In this new episode of our series Business: Cross Perspectives, David Collas, General Manager of the Mandarin Oriental Tokyo, shares his insights on the profound transformations taking place in Japan’s luxury hospitality sector.
And his observation is clear:
“Guest expectations are evolving: luxury is no longer limited to comfort or refinement, it now lies in experience and personalization.”
 
Throughout this exchange, he offers a nuanced analysis of the sector’s contemporary challenges and the specific issues of the Japanese market:
 	The expectations of an increasingly diverse and connected international clientele 	The rise of post-COVID luxury tourism, driven by visitors from Asia, Europe, and North America 	The growing importance of a tailor-made guest experience, going beyond the traditional hotel product 	The cultural specificities of Japan in service, hospitality, and team management 	The integration of sustainability and well-being into the strategy of high-end establishments 
A must-read interview for tourism professionals, premium brands, and anyone interested in the evolution of luxury in Asia, at the crossroads of tradition, innovation, and operational excellence.

title: Regards croisés - Repositioning a watchmaking house in Japan: The Breitling example
description:
In this new episode of our Business: Regards Croisés series, we meet Jérôme Schmutz, President and Representative Director of Breitling Japan. Drawing on his international background and deep experience of the Japanese market, he shares the key levers behind the transformation of a historic watchmaking house, as well as the factors for success in a demanding and constantly evolving cultural environment.
“Watches are part of your personality. In the end, it’s like a companion.”
Jérôme Schmutz’s career Path
Founded in Switzerland in 1884, Breitling was successively owned by the Schneider family before being acquired by the investment fund CVC Capital Partners just over seven years ago. It was at this turning point that Jérôme Schmutz joined the brand, drawn by the challenge ahead. He began as Asia-Pacific Manager based in Switzerland, then became Market Head in Australia. Three years ago, he arrived in Japan for a mission initially planned to last one year, in a post-Covid context where the brand needed to regain momentum.
The objective was clear: reposition Breitling as a major contemporary brand. In 2017, it ranked 19th in the Swiss watchmaking industry; today, it stands in the Top 10.
After one year, Jérôme Schmutz hesitated between a new assignment in Miami and continuing his journey in Japan. He chose Japan, driven by curiosity and the unique learning opportunity it represents. 
Breitling: Between Technological Heritage and Lifestyle Evolution
Breitling is deeply connected to the history of aviation and horological precision. The brand played a major role in the development of the modern chronograph and launched the Navitimer in 1952, designed to meet the needs of aerial navigation. It also made its mark in the automotive world with models featuring tachymeter scales capable of measuring average speed.
Today, while remaining true to this heritage, Breitling is evolving toward a more accessible, lifestyle-oriented positioning. This strong legacy provides a foundation of trust to support a long-term vision in a market where the watch remains an essential product. 
Japan: A Demanding and Highly Structured Market
The Japanese market places particular importance on technical expertise and precision. While Breitling enjoys a positive image, its global strategy must be adapted to local expectations. The purchasing journey is long and highly structured, sometimes involving up to fifteen touchpoints before the final decision, fostering a lasting relationship with the brand.
Breitling notably relies on the Breitling Club, accessible with the purchase of a watch, which offers events, services, and dedicated communication. Limited editions and the adaptation of colors or materials to local tastes also play a key role.
From a digital perspective, Japan favors an Online-to-Offline approach. While online purchases do exist, physical boutiques and human interaction remain central.
For a European company, succeeding in Japan requires patience and a long-term vision: staying true to one’s identity while speaking the language of the Japanese consumer is the key to sustainable differentiation.

title: Regards Croisés: Vanda Japon and the Transmission of French Floral Art in Japan
description:
In this new episode of our Business: Regards Croisés series, we meet Vanda Japon, represented by its director Yuko Morimoto, florist and Ikebana master. Established in Japan since June, the school’s mission is to promote French floral art in a country where this tradition is still not widely known.
« Our goal is to preserve French floral tradition and culture, and to create new floral events here in Japan. »
A Cultural Challenge Successfully Met
When launching in Japan, Vanda Japon had to adapt to a market where flowers are not part of daily life, as opposed to France, where they are purchased spontaneously. In Japan, people have fewer opportunities to give flowers as gifts, and their higher cost further limits their use. To facilitate this cultural shift, Vanda began with small seasonal workshops, especially for Christmas, offering the Japanese public a first concrete experience of French floral aesthetics and laying the foundations for a new floral culture. 
A Bridge Between Ikebana and French Floral Art
With twenty years of experience in Ikebana and formal training in French floral art, Yuko Morimoto brings a unique http://www.vanda-formation.frperspective on the two traditions. However, she refuses to mix them: “I can teach both styles, but I cannot fuse them.” For her, each art form has its own philosophy. Vanda Japan thus becomes a meeting point between two powerful aesthetics, where French tradition is transmitted faithfully while respecting Japanese sensibilities.

A Japanese Floral Market of Exceptional Richness
Tokyo’s flower market one of the most diverse in the world, offers Vanda Japon extraordinary raw materials. Japan even surpasses the Netherlands in variety of available flowers, thanks to local producers who constantly innovate in textures, shapes, and colors. This abundance allows Vanda to teach French floral art with flowers of remarkable quality, appreciated by both professionals and hobbyists.

Training Open to All
Vanda Japon offers a wide range of courses: professional training programs, workshops for amateurs, and in-depth French floral art classes. At a time when traveling from Japan to France for training has become increasingly difficult, the school provides access to rare and sought-after instruction. Vanda aims to become Japan’s leading reference for French floral education.

title: Remote work after Covid-19: Robert Walters Japan announced the results of its last survey
description:
Specialist professional recruitment firm Robert Walters Japan announced the results of a survey conducted among 173 companies in Japan on workplace practices they have adopted in the new normal.
With the vaccine rollout in Japan underway, they surveyed companies on growing expectations and anxieties surrounding coming back to work in the post-pandemic era.
Remote work after Covid-19: most companies allow remote work 3-4 days a week, over half expect more than 50% of employees to continue Of the 173 foreign-affiliated and Japanese global companies that responded to their survey, 86% said they would continue to offer remote work even after Covid-19. The survey also revealed that in terms of how often remote work would be allowed, three to four days a week (42%) was the most common response followed by every day (28%). When asked what percentage of the company’s workforce they predict would continue to work from home beyond the pandemic, the most common response was “51-75%” of employees (33%), followed by “76-100%” of employees (29%).
Rush to prepare for hybrid workforces: increasing investment in IT infrastructure and employee development
As the hybrid workstyle (a combination of working in the office and remote work) is expected to become the norm in the future, IT infrastructure such as Wi-Fi and cloud tools (42%), and general training/upskilling for employees (40%) were cited as the top areas that companies plan to increase investment in beyond Covid-19. 30% of companies also plan to invest in training for managers to help them maintain productivity among hybrid teams.
The role of the office: creating a workplace that encourages collaboration
Of the 173 companies that responded to the survey, 34% are planning to downsize or renovate their offices. According to the survey results, 61% of companies plan to redesign their office spaces to allow hot desking (free seating), 59% will reduce the number of individual desks and increase common and meeting spaces, and 55% will reduce their total office space. 
Speaking on the results of the survey, Managing Director at Robert Walters Japan Jeremy Sampson commented: “During the pandemic, most work could be accomplished remotely thanks to the acceleration of digitisation and improvements in efficiency such as the spread of electronic signatures and online meetings. That being said, remote work still poses some challenges, such as difficulties in communicating with colleagues, feelings of social isolation, and lack of inspiration sharing. On the other hand, many companies are seeing an improvement in work-life balance among employees, such as effective use of time that used to be devoted to commuting. As we move toward the end of the pandemic, the purpose of coming to the workplace will be re-evaluated based on these advantages and disadvantages, and we will see rapid progress in creating workplaces that focus on promoting collaboration and increasing a sense of belonging.”

title: Remote work on the decline in Japan
description: The results of a survey conducted by the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism were published on March 31.

blocks.text: Foresight

blocks.section: Remote work on the decline in Japan
blocks.text: Remote work on the decline in Japan

blocks.section: Remote work on the decline in Japan
blocks.text: The results of a survey conducted by the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism were published on March 31.

blocks.section: Remote work on the decline in Japan
blocks.text: Remote work practices, made widespread by the Covid-19 pandemic, are on the decline in Japan . These are the findings of an online survey conducted by the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism between November and December 2023 on a sample of 40,000 people.

blocks.section: Remote work on the decline in Japan
blocks.text: In the course of 2023, 26.1% of respondents indicated that they teleworked, a decrease of 0.9 percentage points compared to 2022. This proportion varies by region. For example, almost 40% of respondents working in Tokyo telework, compared with 17.5% in the regions.

blocks.section: Remote work on the decline in Japan
blocks.text: However, it seems that work patterns combining telecommuting and presence in the workplace are on the increase .

blocks.section: Remote work on the decline in Japan
blocks.text: The frequency of employed teleworkers intending to continue working is high. The main reasons are “efficient use of time” (around 40% of respondents) and “reduced commuting time” (around 33% of respondents).

title: Remy Cointreau: Terroir, People and Time
description:
The Rémy Cointreau Group, whose Charentaise origins date back to 1724, is the result of the 1990 merger of holding companies owned by the Hériard Dubreuil and Cointreau families, which controlled E. Rémy Martin & Cie SA and Cointreau & Cie SA, respectively.
The Group is also the result of successive partnerships with other companies active in the same wines and spirits business lines.
Backed up by a portfolio of striking, high-end brands, the group's aim is to establish itself as the world leader in exceptional spirits.
Since 2011, Remy Cointreau Japan KK is importing, distributing and building the brands for the Remy Cointreau Group premium spirits and liqueurs portfolio in Japan.
Starting with the luxury iconic brand LOUIS XIII created in 1874, Remy Martin “Fine Champagne Cognac” and the premium orange liqueur “Cointreau” created in 1875, Remy Cointreau French brands have a long history in Japan dating back to first imports in the 19th century. We proud ourselves with a strong value to deliver to the connoisseurs of high quality liquors to be appreciated in various lifestyle occasions, from neat to mixology.

A love of our terroirs and the mastery of time have always been at the heart of our expertise. It is up to each and every one of us to allow this link between the land, people and time to coexist harmoniously side by side.
In line with this philosophy, Remy Cointreau has acquired and the developed brands that share the same values:  Remy Cointreau Japan builds their story with our Japanese clients from day to day.
-             The Islay Single Malts Bruichladdich distillery created in 1881 was acquired in 2012, Remy Cointreau Japan started distribution right after in 2013. The brands embody the value of terroir and transparency with Bruichladdich Unpeated Malts, Port Charlotte heavily peated and the super heavily peated Octomore series. The Progressive Hebridean Distillers also gave birth to the hand-crafted gin The Botanist made from core 22 botanicals foraged in the wild on the island.
-             Westland is the youngest acquisition in 2017 – the American Single Malt embodies the American North-Pacific West Coast pioneering spirit and paves the way to a new category in world of American spirits – a Single Malts strongly anchored in the History and specificities of its terroir.
-             Mount Gay Rum is an icon of premium Rum. In the Barbados and since 1703, the most complex blends have come to life in ancestral ageing cellars.
-             In a joint venture with Lucas-Bols, Remy Cointreau also distributes the premium Passion Fruit Liqueur Passoa in the Japan market.

blocks.section: Results Survey on the “Reaction Of The European Business Community In Japan To COVID-19 Crisis And Impact On Its Operations”
blocks.text: In February 2020, the European Union and Japan celebrated the first anniversary of the entry into force of the EU-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA). According to a European Commission Press Release, “in the first ten months following the implementation of the agreement, EU exports to Japan went up by 6.6% compared to the same period the year before.”

blocks.section: Results Survey on the “Reaction Of The European Business Community In Japan To COVID-19 Crisis And Impact On Its Operations”
blocks.text: In this context of increased exchanges between the EU and Japan, the objective of this survey is to better understand the current situation at European companies operating in Japan confronted to the COVID-19 crisis and to highlight its direct impact on their economic activity.

blocks.section: Results Survey on the “Reaction Of The European Business Community In Japan To COVID-19 Crisis And Impact On Its Operations”
blocks.text: SUMMARY

blocks.section: Results Survey on the “Reaction Of The European Business Community In Japan To COVID-19 Crisis And Impact On Its Operations”
blocks.text: 260 companies from 16 EU countries answered the survey. 82% of them introduced changes to their working style to protect their employees by implementing specific measures such as restrictions on business trips (76%) and public events (55%). Telework is an interesting option for most of them (70%).

blocks.section: Results Survey on the “Reaction Of The European Business Community In Japan To COVID-19 Crisis And Impact On Its Operations”
blocks.text: The impact on turnover for the first semester 2020 is generally revised downwards: 35% of the respondents expect a 20% decline, but 38% stress their lack of visibility.
