blocks.section: Welcome to the world of ballet, the magic of the stage told by Mizuka Ueno, a co-organized event by BONJOUR FRANCE
blocks.text: In a privileged setting bringing together 100 participants, Mizuka UENO presented her art through various video excerpts, including Swan Lake , notably a version filmed in the industrial heart of Kanagawa, Luna , and Bolero . Many other topics were discussed, such as the importance of makeup in ballet performance, which plays an integral role as part of the costume. During a Q&A session with the audience, she also revealed that one of her favorite manga from childhood was Arabesque , a manga centered on ballet. She also shared that her very first trip abroad was to France. They also discussed which male roles she might have enjoyed performing, one of which could have been the Basil from « Don Quichotte ».

title: Recap of the Galette des Rois with ACCJ, TJCS and MOF
description:
On February 10th, the France–Japan Chamber of Commerce and Industry (CCIFJ), Chubu Desk, co-hosted a Galette des Rois celebration at Restaurant Vollon in Nagoya.
For the first time in the Chubu region, the CCIFJ joined forces with the American Chamber of Commerce in Japan (ACCJ), the Tokai Canada Japan Association, and the MOF Museum Nagoya to co-host this event. This traditional Galette des Rois celebration brought together four business communities in a warm and friendly atmosphere, fostering new connections and strengthening existing relationships.
Following the great success of last year’s edition, which welcomed over 70 guests, this year’s event exceeded expectations with more than 100 participants. Each organization reached full capacity several days in advance. This strong attendance created valuable opportunities for networking, with many participants exchanging business cards and engaging in meaningful discussions.

blocks.text: The CCI France Japan welcomed, on October 4, 2025, at its Tokyo offices, a morning session dedicated to 50 French entrepreneurs from the CPME.

blocks.section: A morning dedicated to French entrepreneurs
blocks.text: A morning dedicated to French entrepreneurs

blocks.section: A morning dedicated to French entrepreneurs
blocks.text: On October 4, 2025 , the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCIFJ) had the pleasure of welcoming, at its Tokyo offices, a delegation of 50 French entrepreneurs and SME executives led by Amir Reza Tofighi , President of CPME International .

blocks.section: A morning dedicated to French entrepreneurs
blocks.text: Organized in collaboration with the French Foreign Trade Advisors (CCEF) , this event was part of the CPME Mission to Japan , a collective program designed to help French companies better understand the economic and cultural specificities of the Japanese market.

blocks.section: Understanding the Japanese market and its business culture
blocks.text: Understanding the Japanese market and its business culture

blocks.section: Understanding the Japanese market and its business culture
blocks.text: The opening session, led by Norbert Leuret , President of the CCEF and President of LVMH Japan , and Nicolas Bonnardel , General Manager of the CCIFJ , introduced key trends in the Japanese market and the opportunities available to French SMEs.

blocks.section: Understanding the Japanese market and its business culture
blocks.text: The intercultural presentation delivered by Émilie Teruel , Head of Business Development and Managing Director at the CCIFJ , highlighted the core values of doing business in Japan such as patience , high standards , trust , credibility , and long term cooperation , as well as differences in communication styles and decision making processes that shape Franco Japanese professional relationships.

blocks.section: Understanding the Japanese market and its business culture
blocks.text: The program then focused on several key themes :

blocks.section: Understanding the Japanese market and its business culture
blocks.text: Quality standards , presented by Norbert Leuret (LVMH Japan);

blocks.section: Understanding the Japanese market and its business culture
blocks.text: Food supply chain and distribution , with Philippe Thirouard (Savencia Japan) and François Xavier Colas (Classic Fine Foods Japan);

blocks.section: Understanding the Japanese market and its business culture
blocks.text: The legal business environment in Japan , by Laurent Dubois (TMI Associates);

blocks.section: Understanding the Japanese market and its business culture
blocks.text: The role of Japanese trading companies (Sogo Shosha), with Robert Verdier (Midi Pyrénées KK) and Mr Inoue ;

blocks.section: Understanding the Japanese market and its business culture
blocks.text: A testimonial from La Maison du Chocolat , presented by Benjamin Costa , on the successful development of a French brand in the Japanese market.

blocks.section: Understanding the Japanese market and its business culture
blocks.text: The day concluded with a visit to the Ginza Six shopping center , a symbol of craftsmanship, innovation, and cooperation between French and Japanese brands.

blocks.section: A strong commitment from the CCIFJ to French SMEs
blocks.text: A strong commitment from the CCIFJ to French SMEs

blocks.section: A strong commitment from the CCIFJ to French SMEs
blocks.text: Through this event, the CCIFJ reaffirmed its role as a key player in supporting the development of French companies in Japan. Each year, the Chamber supports numerous SMEs in their projects through :

blocks.section: A strong commitment from the CCIFJ to French SMEs
blocks.text: market studies and market entry strategies ,

blocks.section: A strong commitment from the CCIFJ to French SMEs
blocks.text: intercultural training ,

blocks.section: A strong commitment from the CCIFJ to French SMEs
blocks.text: export support programs ,

blocks.section: A strong commitment from the CCIFJ to French SMEs
blocks.text: and a unique network of local partners .

blocks.section: A strong commitment from the CCIFJ to French SMEs
blocks.text: This morning event illustrated the shared commitment of the CCIFJ , the CCEF and the CPME to strengthening Franco Japanese economic ties by fostering a better understanding of local realities and encouraging the creation of long term, sustainable synergies between the two countries.

blocks.text: Acknowledgements

blocks.section: A strong commitment from the CCIFJ to French SMEs
blocks.text: The CCIFJ would like to extend its sincere thanks to Amir Reza-Tofighi , President of CPME International, for leading the delegation; to Philippe Thirouard and Norbert Leuret for their valuable contributions to the organization and discussions; and to the CCEF and MyComm for their invaluable collaboration.

title: A look back at the signing of the Letter of Intent for friendship and cooperation between Osaka City and the French Embassy in Japan
description:
On the occasion of President Emmanuel Macron’s visit to Japan, and in the wake of the Osaka-Kansai World Expo 2025, Osaka City and the French Embassy in Japan signed, on March 31, a Letter of Intent aimed at establishing a partnership of friendship and cooperation to strengthen economic, cultural, and international exchanges.
Held at the Ambassador’s residence following a cocktail reception, the ceremony marks a significant new step in reinforcing ties between the two parties. It took place in the presence of leading figures involved in Franco-Japanese relations in Kansai and across Japan.

blocks.section: A look back at the signing of the Letter of Intent for friendship and cooperation between Osaka City and the French Embassy in Japan
blocks.text: Held at the Ambassador’s residence following a cocktail reception, the ceremony marks a significant new step in reinforcing ties between the two parties. It took place in the presence of leading figures involved in Franco-Japanese relations in Kansai and across Japan.

blocks.section: A look back at the signing of the Letter of Intent for friendship and cooperation between Osaka City and the French Embassy in Japan
blocks.text: Representing Mayor Hideyuki Yokoyama , Mihoko Arai, Director of International Relations at the Economic Strategy Bureau of Osaka City, and Béatrice Le Fraper du Hellen , Ambassador of France to Japan , reaffirmed their commitment to continuing dialogue and developing concrete joint projects.

blocks.section: A look back at the signing of the Letter of Intent for friendship and cooperation between Osaka City and the French Embassy in Japan
blocks.text: This commitment will notably result in increased support from the Embassy for the development of French businesses and the promotion of French culture in Osaka . In return, Osaka City has committed to contributing to the improvement of the living environment for the French and francophone community , notably by supporting the establishment of a branch of the French Lycée; originally founded by APEK in Kyoto, thereby facilitating access to education accredited by the AEFE network.

title: Recap of the New Year's Networking Evening with the ACCJ
description: On Friday, January 23, the New Year’s Networking Evening, marking the first event of the year for the CCIFJ Osaka desk, was held at the splendid W Osaka Hotel, located in the heart of Shinsaibashi. Organised in collaboration with the American and British Chambers of Commerce, our team was ready to welcome guests from 6:00 pm onward. The event brought together more than 120 participants, with approximately one third registering via our website, representing a significant increase compared to last year.

blocks.text: Kansai Event report

blocks.section: Recap of the New Year's Networking Evening with the ACCJ
blocks.text: Recap of the New Year's Networking Evening with the ACCJ

blocks.section: Recap of the New Year's Networking Evening with the ACCJ
blocks.text: On Friday, January 23 , the New Year’s Networking Evening, marking the first event of the year for the CCIFJ Osaka desk , was held at the splendid W Osaka Hotel , located in the heart of Shinsaibashi . Organised in collaboration with the American and British Chambers of Commerce , our team was ready to welcome guests from 6:00 pm onward. The event brought together more than 120 participants , with approximately one third registering via our website , representing a significant increase compared to last year.

blocks.section: Recap of the New Year's Networking Evening with the ACCJ
blocks.text: The evening opened with welcoming remarks made by Mr. Jiro Kawakami , Vice President of the ACCJ in the Kansai region and Senior Vice President of MGM Resorts Japan LLC, followed by Mr. Richard N. Larsen , newly-appointed Consul General of the United States in Osaka-Kobe. Laura Younger , ACCJ Executive Director of the ACCJ also took part of the event. These opening addresses were followed by the traditional Kagami Biraki ceremony. This japanese tradition, performed at important events, involves breaking open the lid of a sake barrel with wooden mallets and sharing the sake with guests, symbolising harmony and good fortune .

blocks.section: Recap of the New Year's Networking Evening with the ACCJ
blocks.text: The Kampai said by Eric John , President of the ACCJ , marked the beginning of a valuable networking session . Throughout the evening, participants had the opportunity to interact and exchange in the three languages of the event, English, French and Japanese . A raffle was held toward the end of the evening, allowing one lucky winner to receive a VIP overnight stay at the W Osaka Hotel .

blocks.section: Recap of the New Year's Networking Evening with the ACCJ
blocks.text: The dinner prepared by the W Osaka Hotel was also highly appreciated by the guests.

blocks.section: Recap of the New Year's Networking Evening with the ACCJ
blocks.text: Although the event officially concluded at 8:30 pm, conversations and exchanges continued in the hotel lobby well past 9:30 pm, reflecting the strong engagement and enthusiasm of the participants .

blocks.section: Recap of the New Year's Networking Evening with the ACCJ
blocks.text: This event also provided an opportunity to remind our guests of the upcoming events organised by the Chamber, in particular the annual Nagoya Gala , which will take place on the 14th of April at the Nagoya Tokyu Hotel , located in the city center.

blocks.section: Recap of the New Year's Networking Evening with the ACCJ
blocks.text: We are delighted to see this event grow in scale and impact each year, further strengthening the ties between the various international business communities . Our sincere thanks go to the ACCJ and the BCCJ for their collaboration, as well as to all the participants for their positive feedback. We look forward to welcoming you again at our future events .

blocks.section: Recap of the New Year's Networking Evening with the ACCJ
blocks.text: Further information regarding our next event , once again organised in cooperation with the ACCJ , as well as the MOFs (Meilleurs Ouvriers de France) and the TJCA , is available on our website. This upcoming gathering in Nagoya will offer an opportunity for business communities to come together over a high-quality meal, followed by the traditional Galette des Rois.

blocks.text: On September 10, the CCIFJ Kansai Desk hosted its After Summer Party at Café de Paris in Kobe.

blocks.section: Event Recap: Kansai After Summer Party at Café de Paris
blocks.text: The After Summer Party is an annual opportunity for CCIFJ members and partners to reconnect in a relaxed and friendly setting, while also making new connections. This year, the event was held at Café de Paris , bringing together 30 participants from the Franco-Japanese business community for an enjoyable evening in a distinctly French atmosphere.

blocks.section: Event Recap: Kansai After Summer Party at Café de Paris
blocks.text: The evening began with a welcome address and a toast from Jean-François Rauch, Head of the CCIFJ Kansai Desk, setting the tone for an evening of lively conversations and new encounters. Guests were then invited to enjoy a generous French buffet specially prepared by the Café de Paris team.

blocks.section: Event Recap: Kansai After Summer Party at Café de Paris
blocks.text: The buffet featured a wide selection of cheeses, meats, and side dishes, including quail legs, roast pork, roasted potatoes, ratatouille, and much more. Champagne, wine, and other drinks complemented the meal, allowing guests to enjoy a taste of French cuisine while catching up and making new connections.

blocks.section: Event Recap: Kansai After Summer Party at Café de Paris
blocks.text: Throughout the evening, conversations continued over dinner in the warm and welcoming setting of Café de Paris. Guests had the opportunity to reconnect with members of the CCIFJ network, meet new contacts, and expand their professional networks. The relaxed atmosphere of the restaurant and the friendly spirit of the evening made for an enjoyable and engaging gathering.

blocks.section: Event Recap: Kansai After Summer Party at Café de Paris
blocks.text: The enthusiastic response to this first edition in Kobe highlights the value of bringing more CCIFJ events to the city. We look forward to continuing to organize events in Kobe and creating more opportunities for the Franco-Japanese business community to connect and grow together.

blocks.section: Event Recap: Kansai After Summer Party at Café de Paris
blocks.text: A big thank you to the chefs and the entire team at Café de Paris for their warm welcome and for helping make the evening a success, as well as to all our participants for joining us and contributing to the wonderful atmosphere.

blocks.section: Event Recap: Kansai After Summer Party at Café de Paris
blocks.text: We look forward to seeing you again at our upcoming events in Kobe!

description: A unprecedented collaboration between the CCIFJ’s Kansai desk and the Cercle France Kansai to celebrate France's National Day.

blocks.section: A look back at our France's National Day Dinner
blocks.text: A look back at our France's National Day Dinner

blocks.section: A look back at our France's National Day Dinner
blocks.text: A unprecedented collaboration between the CCIFJ’s Kansai desk and the Cercle France Kansai to celebrate France's National Day.

blocks.section: A look back at our France's National Day Dinner
blocks.text: For the first time, the Kansai desk of the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCIFJ) partnered with Cercle France Kansai (CFK) , a long-standing local partner, to bring the spirit of France’s National Day to life in Japan. Historically, the Cercle France Kansai had already been bringing together the local Franco-Japanese community on a monthly basis for years before the CCIFJ office opened in Osaka. For this reason, this collaboration was a logical step .

blocks.section: A look back at our France's National Day Dinner
blocks.text: Held on Tuesday, July 21, to celebrate France’s National Day, this event took place at the Hilton Osaka , a member of the Chamber, which provided us with high-quality service befitting the importance of the gathering. Members of the French community and Japanese Francophiles in Kansai were able to gather in an elegant setting, decorated in the colors of France, to enjoy a meal thoughtfully prepared by the hotel’s culinary teams .

blocks.section: A look back at our France's National Day Dinner
blocks.text: The evening began with remarks by Mr. Tadashi Nakajima, the current president of Cercle France Kansai, who took this opportunity to reaffirm the importance of the cooperative relationship between our two organizations.

blocks.section: A look back at our France's National Day Dinner
blocks.text: In a spirit of conviviality and sharing, the evening brought participants together for a gourmet French dinner , featuring a pâté en croûte, mushroom vichyssoise, sea bass with Véronique sauce, Provençal-style chicken, and, to conclude the meal, peach Melba, honouring the iconic flavours of French cuisine. To accompany these dishes, a selection of wines specially selected by our partner AOC France was matched to each course.

blocks.section: A look back at our France's National Day Dinner
blocks.text: With a majority of French and Japanese guests attending, this evening provided an ideal setting for networking, making new connections, and fostering future collaborations, all in a warm and festive atmosphere.

blocks.section: A look back at our France's National Day Dinner
blocks.text: We would like to express our sincere thanks to our co-organizer, the Cercle France Kansai, as well as to our partners, the Hilton Osaka and AOC France Co., Ltd., whose precious support contributed greatly to the success of this event .

blocks.section: A look back at our France's National Day Dinner
blocks.text: We have therefore agreed to make this an annual event , to be held every year whenever possible. We look forward to welcoming you again next year!

blocks.text: On July 15, 2026, BONJOUR FRANCE and CCI France Japon had the pleasure of hosting the Dîner Gourmand Prestige at Chez Olivier in Tokyo, in collaboration with Mottox Inc..

blocks.section: A Look Back at the Dîner Gourmand Prestige 2026
blocks.text: This exclusive gastronomic evening brought together 21 participants for a unique experience featuring Mathilde BOULACHIN , President & CEO of Maison Chavin and creator of Pierre Zéro , the leading de-alcoholized wine brand in the Japanese market*. The event offered guests the opportunity to discover the full potential of de-alcoholized wines through a refined food and wine pairing experience.

blocks.section: A Look Back at the Dîner Gourmand Prestige 2026
blocks.text: Mayu HANDA , Director of BONJOUR FRANCE, served as Master of Ceremonies all along the soirée. The event opened with welcoming remarks from Charles KOKORIAN , Managing Director & Head of Member Services at CCI France Japon, followed by speeches from Mathilde BOULACHIN and Olivier ODDOS , chef-owner of “Chez Olivier”.

blocks.section: A Look Back at the Dîner Gourmand Prestige 2026
blocks.text: Guests then enjoyed an exceptional dinner created by Chef Olivier ODDOS. Each course was carefully paired with one of the six Pierre Zéro selections: Pierre Zéro Signature, Blanc de Blancs, Chardonnay, Rosé, Merlot, and Muscat Sparkling, highlighting the diversity, elegance, and gastronomic pairing possibilities offered by de-alcoholized wines.

blocks.section: A Look Back at the Dîner Gourmand Prestige 2026
blocks.text: Throughout the evening, participants experienced a true culinary journey combining French gastronomy, innovation, and the French Art de Vivre. Beyond the gastronomic experience, the Dîner Gourmand Prestige also provided a valuable opportunity for professionals and gastronomy enthusiasts to connect and exchange ideas in a warm and chic setting.

blocks.section: A Look Back at the Dîner Gourmand Prestige 2026
blocks.text: BONJOUR FRANCE and CCI France Japon would like to warmly thank all partners for their contribution to the success of this event, as well as all guests who helped make this evening a memorable success.

title: Looking Back at Gala Fukuoka 2026
description:
The French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan celebrated a truly unforgettable edition of its Fukuoka Gala Dinner, held on May 18, 2026, at the Solaria Nishitetsu Hotel Fukuoka. More than 130 guests enjoyed an exceptional evening dedicated to fine gastronomy, art, and emotion.
We had the honor of welcoming distinguished guests, including the Consul General of France in Kyoto, the Vice Governor of Fukuoka Prefecture, and the Vice Mayor of Fukuoka City, representing both France and Fukuoka.
Chef Masafumi Hamano, who has built a long and distinguished career in France and was the chef-owner of the restaurant Au 14 Février Saint-Amour-Bellevue, awarded two Michelin stars from 2018 to 2023, created an exclusive menu especially for this unique occasion. Guests enjoyed exceptional cuisine paired with prestigious Bordeaux wines, generously provided by the Bordeaux Wine Council (CIVB).
The evening was also highlighted by a concert performed by pianist Ayako Hayashi and flutist Genta Usui, creating an elegant French atmosphere.
This 2026 edition brilliantly celebrated Franco-Japanese friendship through gastronomy, culture, and meaningful exchanges. We look forward to welcoming you again at our next edition.

Our heartfelt thanks to our partners:
Airstar Japan, Bordeaux Wine Council (CIVB), Life14, Naos Japan, Godiva

blocks.section: A look back at the Kansai International Meishi Exchange 2026
blocks.text: Last Friday marked the 2026 edition of the Kansai International Meishi Exchange, a networking event bringing together members of many Japanese and foreign chambers of commerce in Osaka . Organized jointly by the American Chamber of Commerce in Japan (ACCJ), the British Chamber of Commerce (BCCJ), the Canadian Chamber of Commerce (CCCJ), the German Chamber of Commerce (AHK Japan), the Indian Chamber of Commerce (ICCJ), the Kobe Chamber of Commerce (KCCI), the Korean Chamber of Commerce (KCCJ), the Osaka Chamber of Commerce (OCCI), and the French Chamber of Commerce (CCIFJ), this edition brought together nearly 400 professionals from all backgrounds who came to expand their networks, meet new people, and reconnect with old acquaintances.

blocks.section: A look back at the Kansai International Meishi Exchange 2026
blocks.text: Among them, the number of members from the Osaka Chamber of Commerce and Industry was particularly significant this year, exceeding 100, marking a turning point in local businesses’ interest in other international actors present in the local economic community . The French Chamber of Commerce and Industry In Japan was the third-largest contributor to the event in terms of the number of participants, demonstrating the strength of its regional presence through its local branches .

blocks.section: A look back at the Kansai International Meishi Exchange 2026
blocks.text: Held in the elegant venue of the Waldorf Astoria Osaka , the reception began with an opening address by the city’s mayor, Hideyuki Yokoyama, whose presence demonstrated the growing importance of this event in the regional economic scene and the recognition it now receives from local governments. It is indeed the largest international event held since the end of the 2025 World Expo in Osaka.

They stood alongside more traditional industries, such as firms specializing in supporting the establishment of international companies, as well as numerous local institutional organizations.

title: A look back at our Dinner Seminar at the Morikawa Salon:
description:
This Thursday, July 16, we held an event that has been organized in years past with the Morikawa Clinic: a dinner seminar, this year themed around “The Art de Vivre.”
Participants gathered for a convivial evening at the Morikawa Lounge in Amagasaki, whose decor is inspired by the French elegance of the Marie Antoinette era. The event began with a presentation on the Art de Vivre, exploring various themes that highlighted the connections and influences between French and Japanese cultures.
During this presentation, the benefits of roses were highlighted: by using all of our senses, we can enjoy their many virtues, such as relaxation, improved circulation, and stress relief, among others. We can experience these blessings through a wide variety of products: beverages, jams, oils, and other rose-based preparations. Guests also had the opportunity to try several of these products during dinner.
The seminar then continued with a focus on the health benefits of tea. Ms. Morikawa shared her expertise as a Kampō Tea Master (herbal teas derived from traditional Chinese medicine). She highlighted the properties of various plants and how they can be used to promote everyday well-being.
In the spirit of this philosophy, Salon Morikawa will soon open its doors as a tea lounge. It will feature a space dedicated to exploring tea and rose-based products, in keeping with the "art de vivre" philosophy presented during the seminar.

title: A look back at our seminar Craftsmanship: Cross Perspectives France × Japan :
description: Three panel discussions, each exploring one of the major issues; seven inspiring and inspired speakers; a lively networking buffet; and nearly 100 delighted participants who traveled specifically from Tokyo, Ishikawa, and Fukuoka: here is a glimpse into the success of this first collaboration in Kyoto between the Institut Français du Kansai and the Kansai Office of the CCI France Japon, focusing on the important topic of traditional crafts and their future in the current socio-economic context.

blocks.text: Kansai Event report

blocks.section: A look back at our seminar Craftsmanship: Cross Perspectives France × Japan :
blocks.text: A look back at our seminar Craftsmanship: Cross Perspectives France × Japan :

blocks.section: A look back at our seminar Craftsmanship: Cross Perspectives France × Japan :
blocks.text: Three panel discussions , each exploring one of the major issues ; seven inspiring and inspired speakers ; a lively networking buffet ; and nearly 100 delighted participants who traveled specifically from Tokyo, Ishikawa, and Fukuoka: here is a glimpse into the success of this first collaboration in Kyoto between the Institut Français du Kansai and the Kansai Office of the CCI France Japon, focusing on the important topic of traditional crafts and their future in the current socio-economic context .

blocks.section: A look back at our seminar Craftsmanship: Cross Perspectives France × Japan :
blocks.text: On June 18, 2026, the Institut Français du Kansai hosted the first event dedicated to the evolution of craftsmanship practices between France and Japan . The first session focused on the numerous opportunities for modernization offered by the digital transformation of businesses . We explored two key areas in particular: internal management systems , on the one hand, and methods for distributing craft products —particularly logistics—on the other.

blocks.section: A look back at our seminar Craftsmanship: Cross Perspectives France × Japan :
blocks.text: We were able to learn from the systems introduced and implemented by Pierre Vauvy to rationalize the internal operations of the family-owned business , Okayama Kōgei , particularly in order management (more than 500 fabrics tracked in real time), the indexing of design patterns (more than 20,000 references), and customer relations (real-time color-matching tests for patterns via video conferencing).

blocks.section: A look back at our seminar Craftsmanship: Cross Perspectives France × Japan :
blocks.text: Meanwhile, Thomas Bertrand has worked with Ship&Co over the past two decades to develop highly effective logistics solutions for large-scale international shipping . He has also shared his insights with us regarding online visibility and the importance of a combined physical presence. The time savings generated by these solutions allow artisans to spend more time focusing on the creative process .

blocks.section: A look back at our seminar Craftsmanship: Cross Perspectives France × Japan :
blocks.text: International outreach was also at the heart of the discussion between Kōtarō Nishibori and Ema Okamoto during the second roundtable, which focused on opening up artisanal excellence to the international market . In addition to efforts to introduce foreign customers to traditional Japanese craftsmanship,this process of renewal first began within Japan through interactions with other creative fields. The curiosity of both speakers led them to rethink Japanese design and cultural norms , paving the way for new collaborations with foreign artists and breaking into new markets that were previously considered saturated.

blocks.section: A look back at our seminar Craftsmanship: Cross Perspectives France × Japan :
blocks.text: Finally, the seminar ended with a remarkable presentation by Toma Yamazoe , Mayuko Sano , and Emina Morioka on the process of transcreation of cultural resources: the challenge of transforming heritage into new value . Drawing on their respective roles in the political, academic, and private sectors, these three speakers demonstrated how the implementation of innovations and initiatives on a global scale is driven by the commitment and engagement of both private and government stakeholders.

blocks.section: A look back at our seminar Craftsmanship: Cross Perspectives France × Japan :
blocks.text: Following the final panel discussion, Ms. Sandrine Mouchet , Consul General of France in Kyoto and Director of the Institut Français du Kansai, concluded the seminar by highlighting the essential role of traditional crafts in strengthening the ties between France and Japan.

blocks.section: A look back at our seminar Craftsmanship: Cross Perspectives France × Japan :
blocks.text: Each of these actors plays a significant role in fostering trends that are well suited to the economic landscape, with the key players being the local residents and artisans , without whom a healthy ecosystem that benefits everyone cannot exist.

blocks.section: A look back at our seminar Craftsmanship: Cross Perspectives France × Japan :
blocks.text: Following these roundtable discussions, the French and Japanese participants continued their discussions throughout the evening, with the generous support of our sponsors Mouton Cadet and Veuve Clicquot , over an exceptional French buffet showcasing the tastes of France.

blocks.section: A look back at our seminar Craftsmanship: Cross Perspectives France × Japan :
blocks.text: Thank you all for your enthusiastic participation in this seminar , which proves that the far too often neglected topic of traditional craftsmanship deserves renewed attention. We look forward to your continued involvement, ideas, and future efforts to help develop it further!

blocks.section: A look back at our seminar Craftsmanship: Cross Perspectives France × Japan :
blocks.text: Many thanks to CoeFont for providing its live translation system.

blocks.text: Après une présentation de l’évolution du marché de l’agroalimentaire au Japon par Régis Arnaud, rédacteur en chef du magazine France Japon Eco, Francois-Xavier Colas, directeur général de la société Classic Fine Foods Japan a exposé ses enjeux actuels en tant qu’importateur distributeur au Japon. Il a ensuite répondu aux questions posées par les entrepreneurs français désireux d’accéder au marché japonais. Pour clôturer ce webinaire la CCI France Japon a présenté ses solutions d’accompagnement virtuel.

title: Retour sur le Webinar: COVID-19 and related Japanese tax considerations
description:
The French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan held a webinar on Monday, April 20, 2020 where Hans-Peter Musahl, tax partner and Balazs Nagy, associate partner at EY, shared their opinion about related Japanese tax considerations facing the COVID-19 crisis.
Philippe Dalpayrat, international lawyer and manager of Dalpayrat Foreign Law Office ensured the flow of webinar as moderator.
This webcast first explained about the COVID-19 related tax reform proposal and its expected impact on tax payers.  Thay also discussed additional potential tax considerations which are relevant in the current disruptive business environment.

description:
On April 3rd, the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry held its fourth webinar on COVID-19.

title: Retour sur le Women in Business Committee Webinar: Power of Parity: a Japan perspective
description:
The French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan held a Women in Business Committee webinar on Tuesday, July 21, 2020.
Speakers:
Naomi Yamakawa and Maya Horii, both Partner, McKinsey & Company’s Tokyo on our webinar 
Advancing women’s equality in Japan could add $325 billlion USD to their collective annual GDP by 2025, a 6 percent increase over the business-as-usual trajectory. Already a powerful engine of global growth, pursuing the goal of gender parity can lift many more women out of poverty and unleash the economic potential of many others.

blocks.section: Looking Back at The French Brand Design Seminar, Fukui Desk
blocks.text: On June 16, the CCIFJ Fukui Desk organized a seminar dedicated to brand concept creation.

blocks.section: Looking Back at The French Brand Design Seminar, Fukui Desk
blocks.text: After a brief presentation of the Chamber’s activities by our Regional Offices Director, we had the honor of welcoming Ms. Virginie Lefevre, CCIFJ Ambassador in Fukui, who shared her vision of how a brand can stand out through its craftsmanship and know-how.

blocks.section: Looking Back at The French Brand Design Seminar, Fukui Desk
blocks.text: Designer and entrepreneur, Ms. Lefevre is the founder of the brand Viruxiny. She began her career as a designer for major international fashion houses in Paris, London, Canada, and the United States. Twenty-five years ago, she moved to Japan to teach fashion at ESMOD Tokyo, before eventually settling there permanently.

blocks.section: Looking Back at The French Brand Design Seminar, Fukui Desk
blocks.text: Based in Fukui for the past 19 years, she founded her own company and has developed a brand that is entirely locally produced. Her creations are now distributed in major department stores such as Isetan, Hankyu, and Mitsukoshi through pop-up sales across Japan. She also works as a freelancer with several local companies and is actively involved in the region’s cultural and media scene, including campaigns such as the Pink Ribbon initiative on Fukui TV, interviews with NHK, and various local publications.

blocks.section: Looking Back at The French Brand Design Seminar, Fukui Desk
blocks.text: Fukui is a particularly attractive region where traditional craftsmanship coexists with innovative companies that are oriented toward international markets.

blocks.section: Looking Back at The French Brand Design Seminar, Fukui Desk
blocks.text: The conference was followed by a Q&A session, allowing participants to further explore the topics discussed and ask questions to the speakers.

blocks.section: Looking Back at The French Brand Design Seminar, Fukui Desk
blocks.text: These exchanges were greatly appreciated and continued in a friendly atmosphere during the networking session that concluded the event.

blocks.section: Looking Back at The French Brand Design Seminar, Fukui Desk
blocks.text: We would like to take this opportunity to express our sincere thanks to Fukui Prefecture for its support in organizing this event.

title: Recap of the Chandeleur Celebration at the Kansai Office
description:
On February 3, 2026, our traditional Chandeleur buffet was held at the Dōjima Avanza office, bringing together 32 participants, a record attendance for this event. In a warm and friendly atmosphere, the evening continued well beyond the scheduled time, reflecting the strong enthusiasm of the participants.
A wide variety of crêpes was prepared by the Kansai office team for the great enjoyment of the guests.

blocks.text: Kansai Event report

blocks.section: Recap of the Chandeleur Celebration at the Kansai Office
blocks.text: On February 3, 2026, our traditional Chandeleur buffet was held at the Dōjima Avanza office , bringing together 32 participants , a record attendance for this event. In a warm and friendly atmosphere, the evening continued well beyond the scheduled time, reflecting the strong enthusiasm of the participants .

blocks.section: Recap of the Chandeleur Celebration at the Kansai Office
blocks.text: A wide variety of crêpes was prepared by the Kansai office team for the great enjoyment of the guests.

blocks.section: Recap of the Chandeleur Celebration at the Kansai Office
blocks.text: The menu featured savory crêpes with ham and pickles, ham and cheese, and salmon with white sauce and dill, as well as sweet crêpes with chocolate, sugar, and strawberry jam. As is tradition, the dishes were accompanied by a selection of brut and sweet cider , along with several non-alcoholic beverages.

blocks.section: Recap of the Chandeleur Celebration at the Kansai Office
blocks.text: The evening unfolded in a cheerful and relaxed atmosphere , marked by business card exchanges and informal conversations. The last guests stayed late into the evening to finish the dishes and continue their discussions, highlighting the strong sense of camaraderie within the Kansai business community.

blocks.section: Recap of the Chandeleur Celebration at the Kansai Office
blocks.text: We would like to extend our sincere thanks to our sponsors for their valuable contributions to the success of the evening, in particular Ms. Morikawa for the rose jelly, rose syrup , and non-alcoholic crémant ; Mr. Shinko of Yuasa Shōyu for the shoyu–cacao spread; and the Tanuki Noir Inn for the delicious traditional French confections.

blocks.section: Recap of the Chandeleur Celebration at the Kansai Office
blocks.text: Further information regarding our next event , to be held at the Holiday Inn Kyoto Hotel for a special cocktail evening , is available on our website.

blocks.section: Recap of the Fukui Industries in Europe Event
blocks.text: This Wednesday, February 25, marked the very first event organized by the CCIFJ Fukui Desk since its opening in October 2024.

blocks.section: Recap of the Fukui Industries in Europe Event
blocks.text: This first event, dedicated to international expansion, brought together more than 20 participants. The first part, held in the form of a seminar, took place at Koshino Valley , a coworking space featuring a seminar room that can accommodate around sixty people.

blocks.section: Recap of the Fukui Industries in Europe Event
blocks.text: During the seminar, Mr. Mathieu MARTIN, Ambassador of CCIFJ in Fukui, presented the key points to consider for a successful expansion to Europe.

blocks.section: Recap of the Fukui Industries in Europe Event
blocks.text: During his presentation, Mr. MARTIN highlighted several challenges that Japanese companies may face. He also emphasized the importance of relying on a local agent or partner to facilitate entry into the European market.

blocks.section: Recap of the Fukui Industries in Europe Event
blocks.text: Subsequently, Wejden Ben Hmiden, Manager of the Fukui Desk, presented the Chamber’s activities as well as its international business development support services.

blocks.section: Recap of the Fukui Industries in Europe Event
blocks.text: The seminar was followed by a networking session during which participants enjoyed delicious galettes des rois , accompanied by drinks.

blocks.section: Recap of the Fukui Industries in Europe Event
blocks.text: We would like to extend our sincere thanks to Pâtisserie Olivière for its valuable support as an event sponsor, as well as to the Fukui Prefectural Government for its logistical support in organizing this event.

Organized in collaboration with J'imagine Japan, the event featured students from Martinique, Réunion and other regions currently undertaking internships in Japan through the organization's program.

blocks.text: On June 25, 2026, CCIFJ members gathered at the CCI France Japon office in Osaka for a convivial evening dedicated to discovering rums from France's overseas territories. Organized in collaboration with J'imagine Japan, the event featured students from Martinique, Réunion and other regions currently undertaking internships in Japan through the organization's program.

blocks.section: Highlights from our tasting evening featuring rums from France’s overseas territories.
blocks.text: Through their presentations, these young talents offered participants an immersion into the world of sugar cane, from the origins of rum in France’s overseas territories to the diversity of French rum traditions. By sharing their knowledge and personal experience, they helped participants gain a deeper understanding of the expertise, history, and cultural richness that shape these spirits.

blocks.section: Highlights from our tasting evening featuring rums from France’s overseas territories.
blocks.text: Guiding guests through a tasting of 12 rums from Martinique and Réunion, the students explained the distinctive characteristics of each spirit, from terroirs and production methods to tasting notes and serving recommendations. The experience was complemented by a selection of specialties from the French overseas territories, including fresh tropical fruits and accras, offering participants a true culinary journey.

title: Seminar Recap: Exporting Wagashi to France
description: Artisan perspectives, market insights, regulatory challenges, innovation in the use of kanten, and support for companies expanding internationally.

blocks.text: Chubu Event report

blocks.section: Seminar Recap: Exporting Wagashi to France
blocks.text: Seminar Recap: Exporting Wagashi to France

blocks.section: Seminar Recap: Exporting Wagashi to France
blocks.text: Artisan perspectives, market insights, regulatory challenges, innovation in the use of kanten, and support for companies expanding internationally.

blocks.section: Seminar Recap: Exporting Wagashi to France
blocks.text: We were pleased to welcome nearly 60 participants , including around 15 who joined online . Among them were professionals connecting from Tokyo, as well as students from the French National Institute for Oriental Languages and Civilizations ( Inalco ) , who were able to follow the seminar via a live stream with automatically generated subtitles.

blocks.section: Seminar Recap: Exporting Wagashi to France
blocks.text: The seminar opened with a presentation on the growing interest in Japanese culture among French audiences. Highlighting nearly 170 years of diplomatic relations between France and Japan, our master of ceremonies, Ms. MIZUTA Haruka , reflected on several milestones that have strengthened ties between the two countries, including Japonismes 2018 , French President Macron's visit to Japan last April, and the recent sumo tournament held in Paris .

blocks.section: Seminar Recap: Exporting Wagashi to France
blocks.text: Ms. MIZUTA also noted the steady increase in the number of French visitors traveling to Japan each year, as well as the growing presence of Japanese grocery stores and specialty wagashi shops across France. She then introduced the seminar's speakers, who shared their expertise and experiences with the audience.

blocks.section: Two wagashi artisans share their experience
blocks.text: Two wagashi artisans share their experience

blocks.section: Two wagashi artisans share their experience
blocks.text: We were honored to welcome Mr. OKAMOTO Nobuharu , owner of the Kotoyo wagashi shop in Yokkaichi. We were also delighted to welcome Mr. MURATA Takanori , a Nagoya-born wagashi artisan now based in Paris, who joined the seminar online.

blocks.section: Two wagashi artisans share their experience
blocks.text: Drawing on their respective experiences, both speakers shared valuable insights into their craftsmanship and the challenges and opportunities of expanding their businesses internationally. Their firsthand perspectives provided participants with practical advice and inspiration for bringing traditional Japanese confectionery to overseas markets.

blocks.section: Kanten: A promising ingredient for the European market
blocks.text: Kanten: A promising ingredient for the European market

blocks.section: Kanten: A promising ingredient for the European market
blocks.text: Expanding into international markets presents both opportunities and challenges. With this in mind, we were honored to welcome Ina Food Industry Co., Ltd. , a leading manufacturer of plant-based gelling agents derived from seaweed, better known as kanten .

blocks.section: Kanten: A promising ingredient for the European market
blocks.text: Rich in dietary fiber, vegan, and naturally gluten-free, kanten offers an attractive alternative to animal-based gelatin for a growing number of health-conscious consumers across Europe. Throughout the seminar, Mr. IKEZAKI Norio , Sales Director, shared his expertise and extensive experience in international markets, providing participants with valuable insights into the opportunities for promoting kanten and Japanese food products overseas.

blocks.section: Supporting companies expanding into France
blocks.text: Supporting companies expanding into France

blocks.section: Supporting companies expanding into France
blocks.text: Our Regional Director, Mr. RAUCH Jean-François , then introduced the services offered by the CCIFJ to support companies in their business development in France. He also announced our upcoming event dedicated to the export of Japanese food products: an online seminar conducted in Japanese by Ms. GOKURA Nathalie , Head of the Start in France service at the CCIFJ.

blocks.section: Supporting companies expanding into France
blocks.text: Scheduled for October 6th 2026 , this seminar will focus on the regulations applicable to the European Union market. We invite all companies and professionals interested in expanding their international activities to register via this link .

blocks.section: Supporting companies expanding into France
blocks.text: Participants also had the opportunity to learn about an upcoming product selection competition aimed at identifying Japanese products with potential for import and commercialization in France. Further details will be announced at a later date.

blocks.section: A friendly networking moment around wagashi
blocks.text: A friendly networking moment around wagashi

blocks.section: A friendly networking moment around wagashi
blocks.text: The networking session continued in a warm and convivial atmosphere with a tasting experience pairing wagashi and wine. Mr. OKAMOTO generously offered participants dorayaki filled with chestnut cream, accompanied by an Oloroso-style Spanish wine selected by Ms. HOSOKAWA Seika , a Nagoya-born sommelier now based in Paris. The wine’s subtle nutty notes complemented the delicate flavors of the dorayaki beautifully.

blocks.section: A friendly networking moment around wagashi
blocks.text: A candidate for the title of Meilleur Ouvrier de France (MOF) , Ms. HOSOKAWA was introduced to us by the Nagoya Museum of Meilleurs Ouvriers de France , which also kindly supported the distribution of beverages during the event. We would also like to extend our sincere thanks to Nichifutsu Bōeki , a long-established importer of French food products in Japan, for generously providing Perrier beverages for the participants.

blocks.section: A friendly networking moment around wagashi
blocks.text: Finally, Mr. OKAMOTO presented several of his original creations inspired by famous Japanese animation characters, as well as his remarkable trompe-l'œil confectionery pieces, which captivated and impressed the audience.

blocks.section: A friendly networking moment around wagashi
blocks.text: The CCIFJ Chūbu Regional Office would like to express its sincere gratitude to all participants and speakers for their presence, enthusiasm, and valuable contributions. We were honored to welcome representatives from the cities of Nagoya , Yokkaichi , Nishio , Ōgaki , and Tsu , as well as the Director of the Tokyo Pastry School , the Head of Content Programming at NHK , representatives from Imuraya , renowned for its azuki bean ice cream, several wagashi artisans, and many professionals eager to better understand the challenges and opportunities involved in exporting Japanese products to France.

blocks.section: A friendly networking moment around wagashi
blocks.text: On the occasion of this event, Ms. MARTINS Yumiko and her intern SCHOTT Hélène , who will conclude their assignments on July 31st 2026 , would also like to express their heartfelt appreciation to everyone they have had the pleasure of meeting and supporting over the past several months.

blocks.section: A friendly networking moment around wagashi
blocks.text: Finally, we would like to extend our special thanks to Haruka, Pierre-Thibault, Mattyas, and Théo . Their continued support and dedication played a key role in the success of this seminar!

title: A Memorable Evening at Monsieur Dior by Anne-Sophie Pic in Osaka
description: A look back at a special evening of wine, cocktails and creations by Anne-Sophie Pic at Monsieur Dior by Anne-Sophie Pic in Osaka.

blocks.text: Kansai Event report

blocks.section: A Memorable Evening at Monsieur Dior by Anne-Sophie Pic in Osaka
blocks.text: A Memorable Evening at Monsieur Dior by Anne-Sophie Pic in Osaka

blocks.section: A Memorable Evening at Monsieur Dior by Anne-Sophie Pic in Osaka
blocks.text: A look back at a special evening of wine, cocktails and creations by Anne-Sophie Pic at Monsieur Dior by Anne-Sophie Pic in Osaka.

blocks.section: A Memorable Evening at Monsieur Dior by Anne-Sophie Pic in Osaka
blocks.text: On September 17, the CCIFJ Kansai Desk had the pleasure of hosting an exclusive apéritif at Monsieur Dior by Anne-Sophie Pic . The 16 participants enjoyed a tasting of three exceptional wines and three cocktails, accompanied by canapés created by three-Michelin-starred chef Anne-Sophie Pic.

blocks.section: A Memorable Evening at Monsieur Dior by Anne-Sophie Pic in Osaka
blocks.text: The evening began at 6:30 p.m. with a few words of welcome from Mr. Jean-François Rauch, Head of the CCIFJ Kansai Desk, before moving on to the tastings.

blocks.section: A Memorable Evening at Monsieur Dior by Anne-Sophie Pic in Osaka
blocks.text: The first group of guests was invited to discover three exceptional wines in the intimate setting of Monsieur Dior's wine cellar:

blocks.section: A Memorable Evening at Monsieur Dior by Anne-Sophie Pic in Osaka
blocks.text: ☆ Saint-Péray, Pic & Chapoutier 2022 ☆ Yamagata Bailey A 2020 ☆ Saint-Émilion, Jean Faure 2010

blocks.section: A Memorable Evening at Monsieur Dior by Anne-Sophie Pic in Osaka
blocks.text: The restaurant's head sommelier, Mr. Koji Ikeda, guided the participants through the tasting, introducing each wine and sharing his expertise. In the elegant and intimate setting of the cellar, the tasting provided a warm atmosphere for conversation and discovery.

blocks.section: A Memorable Evening at Monsieur Dior by Anne-Sophie Pic in Osaka
blocks.text: Meanwhile, the second group enjoyed a selection of cocktails prepared in front of the guests, accompanied by the chef's explanations. Among the creations were the Monsieur Dior Negroni and the Amber , a refined cocktail combining umeshu and sparkling wine. Beautifully decorated with flowers, the cocktails were served alongside three canapés created by three-Michelin-starred chef Anne-Sophie Pic, bringing together gastronomy, creativity and the French art of living.

blocks.section: A Memorable Evening at Monsieur Dior by Anne-Sophie Pic in Osaka
blocks.text: Between the two tasting sessions, participants had the opportunity to explore the Dior boutique, with the restaurant located on the fourth floor of the House of Dior Shinsaibashi . The visit included a closer look at Dior's tableware collection, extending the experience offered by Monsieur Dior by Anne-Sophie Pic.

blocks.section: A Memorable Evening at Monsieur Dior by Anne-Sophie Pic in Osaka
blocks.text: The groups then switched places, allowing those who had started with cocktails to discover the wines presented by Mr. Koji Ikeda, while the first group had the chance to enjoy the cocktails and learn more about their preparation.

blocks.section: A Memorable Evening at Monsieur Dior by Anne-Sophie Pic in Osaka
blocks.text: Throughout the evening, participants exchanged ideas and enjoyed meeting one another in a relaxed and convivial atmosphere, both during the tastings and between sessions. These moments provided an opportunity to make new connections and share a common interest in gastronomy, wine and the world of Monsieur Dior by Anne-Sophie Pic.

blocks.section: A Memorable Evening at Monsieur Dior by Anne-Sophie Pic in Osaka
blocks.text: The evening was a wonderful opportunity to discover the elegant setting of Monsieur Dior by Anne-Sophie Pic while celebrating the French art of living and encouraging connections among participants.

blocks.section: A Memorable Evening at Monsieur Dior by Anne-Sophie Pic in Osaka
blocks.text: We would like to warmly thank Monsieur Dior by Anne-Sophie Pic, the restaurant team and all the participants for this memorable evening, and we look forward to future opportunities to collaborate with Monsieur Dior by Anne-Sophie Pic.

title: A look back at our guided tour, exploring Hakata-ori and the landscapes of Itoshima
description:
On Friday, July 3, the CCIFJ Kyushu Office was pleased to organize a day dedicated to exploring the artisanal heritage and iconic landscapes of Fukuoka Prefecture. The six participants had the privilege of enjoying a beautiful sunny day, which provided ideal conditions for this cultural immersion in the heart of Itoshima.
We were delighted to welcome the participants alongside Mr. Kuroki at Kuroki Orimono, where they began the day with a presentation on this family-run business and its craftsmanship, passed down through several generations. They learned about the history of Hakata-ori, its weaving techniques, and the symbolism behind its traditional patterns.

blocks.text: Kyushu Event report

blocks.text: A look back at our guided tour, exploring Hakata-ori and the landscapes of Itoshima

blocks.section: A look back at our guided tour, exploring Hakata-ori and the landscapes of Itoshima
blocks.text: On Friday, July 3, the CCIFJ Kyushu Office was pleased to organize a day dedicated to exploring the artisanal heritage and iconic landscapes of Fukuoka Prefecture. The six participants had the privilege of enjoying a beautiful sunny day, which provided ideal conditions for this cultural immersion in the heart of Itoshima.

blocks.section: A look back at our guided tour, exploring Hakata-ori and the landscapes of Itoshima
blocks.text: We were delighted to welcome the participants alongside Mr. Kuroki at Kuroki Orimono , where they began the day with a presentation on this family-run business and its craftsmanship, passed down through several generations. They learned about the history of Hakata-ori, its weaving techniques, and the symbolism behind its traditional patterns.

blocks.section: A look back at our guided tour, exploring Hakata-ori and the landscapes of Itoshima
blocks.text: During the workshop tour, participants were able to explore the entire obi-making process, from the creation of the weaving yarn to the final product. This behind-the-scenes look at the workshop highlighted the precision, technical skill, and passion that drive the artisans at Kuroki Orimono. Participants then took part in a weaving workshop, creating a sample obi that they were able to keep as a memento of the experience an activity that generated great enthusiasm. The visit concluded with a friendly get-together, followed by a tour of the workshop’s boutique, offering the opportunity to discover and purchase original Hakata-ori creations.

blocks.section: A look back at our guided tour, exploring Hakata-ori and the landscapes of Itoshima
blocks.text: The group then gathered for a convivial lunch overlooking the magnificent Itoshima Bay, where they enjoyed a generous buffet featuring seafood specialties, sashimi, and tempura, all while taking in the stunning scenery. The afternoon continued in the heart of Itoshima with a tour of several local artisan shops offering souvenirs, clothing, and regional products, before wrapping up with a break at a local café featuring traditional Japanese architecture.

blocks.section: A look back at our guided tour, exploring Hakata-ori and the landscapes of Itoshima
blocks.text: From learning about ancestral craftsmanship to meeting artisans, sampling local cuisine, and exploring Itoshima’s heritage, the day offered participants a rich and enjoyable cultural experience that was greatly appreciated by the entire group.

blocks.section: A look back at our guided tour, exploring Hakata-ori and the landscapes of Itoshima
blocks.text: We extend our warmest thanks to Kuroki Orimono for their warm welcome, their time, and for sharing their expertise, all of which greatly contributed to the success of this day of discovery. Our sincere thanks also go to the participants, the City of Fukuoka , and Two Blooms for their contributions to this wonderful day of exchange and discovery.

title: Looking back on the « Launch party for PARIS mag by BONJOUR FRANCE »
description: Let’s take a look back at the “Launch party for PARIS mag by BONJOUR FRANCE”, which marked the official inauguration of PARIS mag by BONJOUR FRANCE.

blocks.text: Event report

blocks.section: Looking back on the « Launch party for PARIS mag by BONJOUR FRANCE »
blocks.text: Looking back on the « Launch party for PARIS mag by BONJOUR FRANCE »

blocks.section: Looking back on the « Launch party for PARIS mag by BONJOUR FRANCE »
blocks.text: Let’s take a look back at the “Launch party for PARIS mag by BONJOUR FRANCE”, which marked the official inauguration of PARIS mag by BONJOUR FRANCE.

blocks.section: Looking back on the « Launch party for PARIS mag by BONJOUR FRANCE »
blocks.text: BONJOUR FRANCE organized two exceptional soirées to celebrate the recent launch of PARIS mag on April 3 and 10, held at the CCI France Japon premises, at L’Espace@CCIFJ.

blocks.section: Looking back on the « Launch party for PARIS mag by BONJOUR FRANCE »
blocks.text: In total, 212 participants attended the two events, with 103 guests on April 3 and 109 on April 10. Media representatives, influencers, and France enthusiasts gathered to share a unique experience celebrating French culture. All guests also followed the dress code, incorporating a touch of blue, white, or red into their outfits, each with their own personal style.

blocks.section: Looking back on the « Launch party for PARIS mag by BONJOUR FRANCE »
blocks.text: The event began with opening speeches from representatives of the CCI France Japon. On April 3, the general manager Nicolas BONNARDEL opened the evening, followed on April 10 by the administrator Bernard DELMAS, who also delivered a speech.

blocks.section: Looking back on the « Launch party for PARIS mag by BONJOUR FRANCE »
blocks.text: Next, Mayu HANDA, Director of BONJOUR FRANCE, presented BONJOUR FRANCE’s 2026 event and unveiled “PARIS mag by BONJOUR FRANCE,” introducing three key pillars designed to bring new momentum to the project. First, to highlight the richness of France’s regions and recent local information through articles published in the digital magazine. Second, to organize future events at L’Espace@CCIFJ, such as Talk-Shows or food and wine or champagne pairing tastings. Finally, to launch a “Select Shop PARIS mag” at upcoming markets and BONJOUR FRANCE events.

blocks.section: Looking back on the « Launch party for PARIS mag by BONJOUR FRANCE »
blocks.text: In addition, the Talk-Show by Françoise MORÉCHAND, a French lifestyle consultant and essayist, was a highlight of the soirées. It offered a refined glimpse into the French “Art de Vivre” and captivated all attendees.

blocks.section: Looking back on the « Launch party for PARIS mag by BONJOUR FRANCE »
blocks.text: During the cocktail, a selection of breads, wines, and chocolates generously provided by our sponsors was offered to guests, who greatly appreciated these delightful treats. At the end of the evenings, a raffle was held, featuring various prizes, including Assemplage items and BONJOUR FRANCE tote bags, generating great excitement among the guests.

blocks.section: Looking back on the « Launch party for PARIS mag by BONJOUR FRANCE »
blocks.text: We would also like to express our heartfelt gratitude to our sponsors for contributing to the success of these evenings. We hope these events allowed you to discover, or rediscover, the French Art de Vivre through PARIS mag and BONJOUR FRANCE.

blocks.text: Let’s look back at the Talk-Show featuring the renowned actor Jean RENO!

blocks.section: Looking back on the « A rendez-vous with Jean RENO : Presented by BONJOUR FRANCE»
blocks.text: On April 20 , BONJOUR FRANCE organized an exceptional Talk-Show at L’Espace@CCIFJ centered around the play “ Rakuda ,” performed solo in Japan by Jean RENO , an iconic figure in French and international cinema.

blocks.section: Looking back on the « A rendez-vous with Jean RENO : Presented by BONJOUR FRANCE»
blocks.text: The evening began with a warm welcome speech by Jérôme CHOUCHAN , President, CCI France Japon, and was smoothly hosted throughout by Mayu HANDA , Director BONJOUR FRANCE, CCI France Japon, serving as Master of Ceremonies.

blocks.section: Looking back on the « A rendez-vous with Jean RENO : Presented by BONJOUR FRANCE»
blocks.text: During the Talk-Show, the play’s director, Ladislas CHOLLAT , also took part in the discussion, while presenter, journalist, and sports commentator Florent DABADIE moderated the exchange.

blocks.section: Looking back on the « A rendez-vous with Jean RENO : Presented by BONJOUR FRANCE»
blocks.text: Jean RENO spoke about how he gradually and consistently built his acting career, as well as his deep attachment to Japan. He also reflected on his family and the many landmark films in which he has appeared. Throughout the discussion, he explained how the idea of performing the solo play “Rakuda” in Japan came about, as well as the reasons behind choosing such an unusual title.

blocks.section: Looking back on the « A rendez-vous with Jean RENO : Presented by BONJOUR FRANCE»

title: Return on Event : Presentation J'imagine Japan
description:
On December 10, the Chūbu Office of the CCIFJ had the pleasure to organize in collaboration with the association J’imagine Japan, a seminar held at Nagoya University of Foreign Studies. The event brought together around twenty students and faculty members, with the aim of raising awareness among students about international mobility and its key challenges.
Until now, J’imagine Japan had focused primarily on promoting mobility opportunities for French-speaking students in Japan. During this seminar, the association presented and promoted its new program, which takes the opposite approach by offering internship opportunities in France to Japanese students.

blocks.text: Chubu

blocks.section: Return on Event : Presentation J'imagine Japan
blocks.text: Return on Event : Presentation J'imagine Japan

blocks.section: Return on Event : Presentation J'imagine Japan
blocks.text: On December 10 , the Chūbu Office of the CCIFJ had the pleasure to organize in collaboration with the association J’imagine Japan , a seminar held at Nagoya University of Foreign Studies . The event brought together around twenty students and faculty members , with the aim of raising awareness among students about international mobility and its key challenges.

blocks.section: Return on Event : Presentation J'imagine Japan
blocks.text: Until now, J’imagine Japan had focused primarily on promoting mobility opportunities for French-speaking students in Japan. During this seminar, the association presented and promoted its new program, which takes the opposite approach by offering internship opportunities in France to Japanese students .

blocks.section: Return on Event : Presentation J'imagine Japan
blocks.text: Well established in the Kansai region, J’imagine Japan has for many years been actively strengthening ties between France and Japan in various ways. In particular, the association has provided French students with internship opportunities within Japanese companies, as well as immersive internships centered on Japanese culture, including courses at Japanese language schools .

blocks.section: Return on Event : Presentation J'imagine Japan
blocks.text: The French model of long-term internships (lasting several months) remains largely unfamiliar in Japan, which explains why corporate internship opportunities for foreign students are relatively rare. This issue had already been addressed last year during a dedicated seminar . In addition to supporting French students, J’imagine Japan is now tackling the issue from the other direction by raising awareness among Japanese students , starting at the university level, of the benefits of the French internship model and by offering them the opportunity to experience it firsthand. We hope that this long-term effort to promote immersive, extended internships will ultimately help bring about a shift in mindset on this issue within Japanese society.

blocks.section: Return on Event : Presentation J'imagine Japan
blocks.text: The students showed strong interest in the internship opportunities , which would allow them to stand out in their academic paths, even though such experiences remain uncommon in Japan.

blocks.section: Return on Event : Presentation J'imagine Japan
blocks.text: This unique opportunity to gain international professional experience was met with great curiosity from the students, who asked numerous questions not only about the internships themselves, but also about Martinique , the home island of François Régina, a representative of J’imagine Japan, which remains largely unfamiliar to them.

blocks.section: Return on Event : Presentation J'imagine Japan
blocks.text: Personal feedback and experiences were also shared, notably through testimonials from French students who had come to Japan for a language exchange or to undertake internships within Japanese organizations. These testimonials took the form of videos in which they described their individual paths. The testimony of a Japanese student from Kyoto University who had completed an internship in Martinique was also particularly impactful, especially due to the sense of closeness it created with the students present in the room.

blocks.section: Return on Event : Presentation J'imagine Japan
blocks.text: Finally, the last part of the session consisted of a presentation on the cultural differences between France and Japan in the professional environment , followed by the sharing of a personal internship experience in France. This oral presentation aimed to provide as clear and concrete an understanding as possible of how an internship in France would unfold.

blocks.section: Return on Event : Presentation J'imagine Japan
blocks.text: The presentation concluded in a friendly and warm atmosphere.

blocks.section: Return on Event : Presentation J'imagine Japan
blocks.text: We would like to express our sincere thanks to J’imagine Japan for its participation in the event, as well as to Nagoya University of Foreign Studies for hosting the seminar.

blocks.text: Over 4,800 professionals globally share their work style preferences

blocks.section: Ideal number of days to work in the office: twice per week
blocks.text: Ideal number of days to work in the office: twice per week

blocks.section: Ideal number of days to work in the office: twice per week
blocks.text: Specialist recruitment consultancy Robert Walters surveyed more than 4,800 professionals globally, including 334 in Japan, to understanding their work style preferences and career plans for 2021. Among professionals in Japan, twice per week is the most ideal number of days to work in the office, followed by three days per week. Globally, twice a week was also the most popular response (30%).

blocks.section: Ideal number of days to work in the office: twice per week
blocks.text: 19% of respondents in Japan said they prefer to continue working fully remote, slightly higher than the global average of 13%. Among Japanese professionals, 37% said they would reject a job offer if they had to work nearly 100% of the week in person at the office. Commuting (84%), flexible hours (60%), and flexibility on where to live (52%) are the main reasons why professionals are willing to give up the office day-to-day.

blocks.section: Popularity of remote work: only 5% willing to go back to going to the office every day
blocks.text: Popularity of remote work: only 5% willing to go back to going to the office every day

blocks.section: Popularity of remote work: only 5% willing to go back to going to the office every day
blocks.text: Only 5% of Japanese professionals affirm that they would like to go back to the old normal of going to the office five times a week. Remote work has been positively accepted, with only 3% saying that they would refuse a job offer that was 100% remote. The top three reasons preventing them from accepting a fully remote role include: having the option to come to the office when you feel like it (54%), feeling more productive in the office (36%), and face-to-face meetings and social interaction with colleagues (25%). Meanwhile, globally, 10% of professionals said they would decline a role that was fully remote.

blocks.section: Over 1 in 5 professionals in Japan concerned about skills relevance, but more than 50% plan to change careers or companies in 2021
blocks.text: Over 1 in 5 professionals in Japan concerned about skills relevance, but more than 50% plan to change careers or companies in 2021

blocks.section: Over 1 in 5 professionals in Japan concerned about skills relevance, but more than 50% plan to change careers or companies in 2021
blocks.text: With remote work having been an option for most professionals for over a year now, many of them have used this momentum in a positive way and decided to leverage their skills. Globally, professionals in Japan are the least confident about their current skill set, with more than 1 in 5 fearing that their current skills will not be relevant to the labour market in 5 years-time. In comparison, professionals in Africa are the most optimistic—58% responded that they are “very confident” about their current skill sets.

blocks.section: Over 1 in 5 professionals in Japan concerned about skills relevance, but more than 50% plan to change careers or companies in 2021
blocks.text: To stay employable in the future, 93% of respondents in Japan are willing to retrain or learn a new skill. For those who want to upskill but have not yet done so, the main reasons are the financial cost (43%), not having the assurance that this investment will result in higher compensation (17%), and no guarantee that this will strengthen job security or progression (33%).

blocks.section: Over 1 in 5 professionals in Japan concerned about skills relevance, but more than 50% plan to change careers or companies in 2021
blocks.text: Despite concerns about skills relevance, professionals in Japan have expressed intentions to switch professions in 2021 (23%) or stay in the same profession but change employers (29%). Less than one-third plan to stay in the same role with the same company.

title: Robert Walters Japan announced the latest hiring trends for digital talent
description:
Rapid growth in e-commerce and progress in DX accelerates demand for digital talent. Shortage of data security specialists leads to increased training efforts
Retail companies rush to recruit digital talent amidst rapid e-commerce growth Due to Covid-19, physical retail shops and restaurants have been heavily impacted by dwindling foot traffic and inbound tourism. On the other hand, more consumers are turning to e-commerce sites as well as online services as they spend an increasing amount of time at home. As changing consumer habits push more companies to drive omnichannel strategies with greater emphasis on the digital side, demand for digital talent within the retail industry is growing rapidly.
While hiring for most retail positions paused in 2020, e-commerce and digital related roles remained highly active. Nevertheless, the talent pool for English-speaking candidates with digital retail experience in Japan is extremely small since the domestic e-commerce market is still relatively new. The competition for talent is intensifying particularly for professionals with skills in digital marketing, strategic marketing, CRM, mobile advertising, search engine marketing, and analytics.
Traditionally, salaries offered in retail companies have not been as competitive as they have heavily relied on strong branding to secure talent. However, as demand for digital talent grows across multiple industries such as fintech, retail companies are no longer competing just among themselves. To attract professionals with digital skills, companies will need to prominently highlight career paths and attractive salaries as part of their employee value proposition.
Hiring in tech: intensifying competition for security and DX talent It used to be that technology was considered an additional cost for companies, but nowadays, no company can operate successfully without it. Companies that have been agile in adopting digital transformation have benefitted from better business performance overall as well as increased productivity through mobilized and engaged workforces. They are also more 2 competitive in securing talent given that more professionals prioritise organisations where technology is valued. As digital transformation and cybersecurity will continue to be big trends in 2021, there is great demand for tech talent with change management skills who can effectively engage with business stakeholders in ways that non-technical users can understand and get value from. As data governance requirements in highly regulated industries become stricter, candidates with experience in data and cybersecurity will be highly sought after. However, the talent pool of professionals with experience in DX is still limited as it is relatively new in Japan.
Shortage of specialists in data security: growing trend in training Director of Tech & Transformation at Robert Walters Japan Tomokazu Betzold commented: “With more day-to-day business operations being completed online, companies are placing greater emphasis on data governance and cybersecurity. Although the volume of such positions is notably less than the most in-demand tech positions in the job market, there is a serious shortage of professionals with practical experience in these areas. To address this, more companies are taking measures such as utilising experienced professionals from their overseas offices and teaming them with a less experienced but more readily available hire in Japan, who can leverage the team’s expertise while they develop and grow into the job. Companies will also support local employees to gain the required experience and certifications with the aim of securing talent in Japan for the long term. We can expect this trend of internal development to spread to various industries over the next one to two years. Covid-19 has pushed many companies to shift to cloud computing, which has led to increased hiring needs for cloud engineers. As demand for server engineers and other traditional IT infrastructure-related roles declines, there is a growing trend to compensate for the talent shortage over the long term by combining in-house training with reskilling of traditional system engineers to acquire skills in cloud engineering.”
