title: Robert Walters Japan announced the results of survey findings on childcare leave among female company employees in Japan

blocks.text: Companies news

blocks.section: Robert Walters Japan announced the results of survey findings on childcare leave among female company employees in Japan
blocks.text: Robert Walters Japan announced the results of survey findings on childcare leave among female company employees in Japan

blocks.section: Robert Walters Japan announced the results of survey findings on childcare leave among female company employees in Japan
blocks.text: On 17 March, specialist professional recruitment firm Robert Walters Japan announced the results of a survey regarding childcare leave conducted among female company employees working in Japanese and foreign-affiliated companies in Japan.

blocks.section: Robert Walters Japan announced the results of survey findings on childcare leave among female company employees in Japan
blocks.text: Childcare leave usage among female employees: 72% in foreign companies, 66% in Japanese companies

blocks.section: Robert Walters Japan announced the results of survey findings on childcare leave among female company employees in Japan
blocks.text: Among female professionals with children that we surveyed, 72% of those working for foreign-affiliated companies and 66% of those working for Japanese companies said they have continued to work after pregnancy and have taken childcare leave. Conversely, when female employees who did not take childcare leave were asked why they did not, the most common response was “I resigned from my job” (41%), followed by “I did not qualify since I recently changed jobs” (36%). The results indicate that many women have resigned for various reasons due to pregnancy or childbirth.

blocks.section: Robert Walters Japan announced the results of survey findings on childcare leave among female company employees in Japan
blocks.text: Returning from maternity leave: 15% experienced change in responsibilities, 40% “satisfied”

blocks.section: Robert Walters Japan announced the results of survey findings on childcare leave among female company employees in Japan
blocks.text: Regarding changes in responsibilities and workload after returning from maternity leave, 60% reported experiencing no changes while 21% said they changed jobs. Fifteen percent of female employees said their responsibilities and workload changed unintentionally after returning to work. In terms of satisfaction with job duties and workload after returning from maternity leave, 41% answered that their work was “flexible and well-balanced” or “rewarding and generally satisfying.” Thirty-one percent responded that they found their work rewarding but the heavy workload made it difficult to balance work and family, while 13% said they were able to use their time flexibly but found their work not very rewarding.

blocks.section: Robert Walters Japan announced the results of survey findings on childcare leave among female company employees in Japan
blocks.text: Balancing work & childcare: female employees generally satisfied with support system

blocks.section: Robert Walters Japan announced the results of survey findings on childcare leave among female company employees in Japan
blocks.text: When asked about the level of satisfaction with their employer’s support system for balancing work and childcare, around 70% of those who took childcare leave answered that they were “satisfied” or “somewhat satisfied.” On the other hand, only 50% of female employees who did not take childcare leave but are currently working answered that they were “satisfied” or “somewhat satisfied.” This suggests that, among female employees, whether maternity leave is offered by an employer impacts satisfaction of the support system.

blocks.section: Robert Walters Japan announced the results of survey findings on childcare leave among female company employees in Japan
blocks.text: Based on the survey findings, there is room for improvement for companies to create a workplace environment where all employees can play an active role and have equal opportunities for success even while raising children.

title: Robert Walters Japan conducted a survey among professionals who changed jobs during Covid-19 regarding their remote onboarding experience
description:
82% of new hires during Covid-19 satisfied with onboarding experience. More than 50% of foreign and Japanese global companies implement remote onboarding 
On March 11, specialist professional recruitment firm Robert Walters Japan announced the results of a survey conducted among professionals who changed jobs during Covid-19 regarding their remote onboarding experience.
More than 50% of new hires undergo onboarding remotely. 82% of job changers satisfied with the overall onboarding experience during Covid-19
Among professionals who changed jobs after March 2020, 53% responded that their employers had digitised their onboarding procedures such as submitting paperwork. While many employees who moved to a different organisation during the pandemic experienced a combination of remote and on-site onboarding, 78% of respondents felt that they were able to clearly understand their own job responsibilities and expectations from the company. 72% of respondents also said that they were able to deepen their understanding of their company's culture through the onboarding process. Overall, the onboarding experience during Covid-19 has been a positive one, with 82% of respondents expressing satisfaction with the general onboarding process and 76% expressing satisfaction with the quality of communication with superiors and colleagues.
Top remote onboarding challenges: “fewer chances to learn by observing on the job” and “finding and accessing company files/data”
While the level of satisfaction for the overall onboarding experience was high, 1 out of 3 respondents were dissatisfied with the initial job-related training, which normally includes an introduction to the company's strategy and guide to using internal systems. 32% of respondents also felt that they were not sufficiently equipped with all the tools and resources to perform their job successfully when they joined. In addition, “fewer chances to learn by observing on the job” (35%) and “finding and accessing internal files/data” (34%) were the top challenges encountered during the onboarding period.
Many employees found it difficult to learn by observing how their colleagues complete daily tasks or struggled to access company data during remote onboarding and sought solutions in the form of training provided by the company. In fact, 87% of company employees felt the need for personal development during the onboarding period, and 69% spared time outside working hours to do so. In terms of relationships with co-workers immediately after joining the company, only 9% reported having trouble seeking support from their supervisor or co-workers, indicating that most respondents had successfully built relationships where they could approach their teams for support. On the other hand, 30% found it challenging that they had fewer opportunities to connect with colleagues, suggesting that this may have led to feelings of loneliness and lack of inspiration during onboarding.
Speaking on the results of the survey, Managing Director at Robert Walters Japan Jeremy Sampson commented: “Onboarding is an essential process for ensuring that employees are equipped with the necessary knowledge and tools to perform at high levels early on in their careers. The survey results suggest that onboarding combined with online training conducted during Covid-19 has not been less effective in achieving this aim. However, new working styles brought on by the pandemic have presented challenges such as fewer chances to learn by observing at the workplace.  For an enhanced remote onboarding experience, there is an urgent need for companies to provide new joiners with more digitised training materials and opportunities to interact with their teams online.”
(Survey period: February 19 to February 26, 2021, Target: Bilingual professionals who moved to a foreign-affiliated or Japanese global company after March 2020  n=161)

title: Robert Walters Japan introduces new employee benefit: Social security benefits for same-sex partners
description: Robert Walters Japan announced the introduction of social security benefits for employees with same-sex partners on 1 June 2024.

blocks.text: Companies news

blocks.section: Robert Walters Japan introduces new employee benefit: Social security benefits for same-sex partners
blocks.text: Robert Walters Japan introduces new employee benefit: Social security benefits for same-sex partners

blocks.section: Robert Walters Japan introduces new employee benefit: Social security benefits for same-sex partners
blocks.text: Robert Walters Japan announced the introduction of social security benefits for employees with same-sex partners on 1 June 2024.

blocks.section: Robert Walters Japan introduces new employee benefit: Social security benefits for same-sex partners
blocks.text: Current status of same-sex marriage in Japan

blocks.section: Robert Walters Japan introduces new employee benefit: Social security benefits for same-sex partners
blocks.text: Unfortunately, same-sex marriage has still not been legalized in Japan, meaning same-sex partners often miss out on the social security premium coverage their married counterparts receive. Even if a person with a same-sex partner meets the financial requirements to be a dependent, they cannot receive coverage under their partner’s Employees’ Health Insurance and Employees’ Pension Insurance – they must pay for the National Health Insurance and National Pension by themselves through the ward office.

blocks.section: Robert Walters Japan introduces new employee benefit: Social security benefits for same-sex partners
blocks.text: Our new employee benefit for same-sex partners

blocks.section: Robert Walters Japan introduces new employee benefit: Social security benefits for same-sex partners
blocks.text: Robert Walters Japan is now offering a financial benefit to employees who have a same-sex partner and whose partner meets the conditions for coverage stipulated by the Health Insurance Society. The benefit covers an amount equivalent to the partner's National Health Insurance and National Pension premium.

blocks.section: Robert Walters Japan introduces new employee benefit: Social security benefits for same-sex partners
blocks.text: As part of our efforts to foster a workplace that ensures equity and inclusion for all employees, Robert Walters Japan has introduced various benefits treating same-sex partners as spouses since 2020, including marriage leave and parental leave. The new benefit is an expansion of our existing benefits program, aiming to provide the same level of support as married employees for our employees with same-sex partners who are currently not legally acknowledged as dependents.

blocks.section: Robert Walters Japan introduces new employee benefit: Social security benefits for same-sex partners
blocks.text: We hope that our change will inspire other organizations in Japan to move forward with similar initiatives, and we will continue to push for marriage equality.

blocks.section: Robert Walters Japan introduces new employee benefit: Social security benefits for same-sex partners
blocks.text: Equity, diversity & inclusion at Robert Walters Japan

blocks.section: Robert Walters Japan introduces new employee benefit: Social security benefits for same-sex partners
blocks.text: At Robert Walters Japan, diversity is more than just a policy—it’s who we are at our core. We believe in the power of a diverse workforce that champions the right for people to be their true, authentic selves, and we are committed to helping people and organizations to fulfil their unique potential by continuing to leverage our rich array of backgrounds and perspectives.

title: Saint-Gobain's Architecture Student Contest: Designing a Sustainable Tomorrow
description:
The Architecture Student Contest, initiated by Saint-Gobain Isover in Serbia in 2004, has evolved into a prestigious international competition since its inception in 2005. Rooted in Saint-Gobain's vision of sustainable buildings, this contest serves as a unique platform for aspiring architects to delve into the realm of sustainable construction. With over 1,300 students participating from 30 countries, it has become a global stage where creativity and innovation converge to shape the future of architecture.
Unveiling the Opportunity:
Participating in the Architecture Student Contest is not just a chance to showcase design prowess but also an opportunity to garner international exposure. The allure of a substantial €11,500 prize further sweetens the deal. This competition is not merely about winning; it's about gaining invaluable professional experience and contributing to the paradigm shift towards sustainable architecture.
A Focus on Sustainability:
At the heart of the Architecture Student Contest lies the core objective of promoting sustainability. Participants are tasked with developing projects that prioritize the well-being of both people and the planet. The emphasis is on creating buildings that are highly energy-efficient, low-carbon, and provide a comfortable environment for occupants. This focus on sustainability aligns with modern construction practices that seek to reduce carbon emissions, energy consumption, and resource utilization.
Ready to Take the Challenge?
► The registration deadline is set for March 29th, 2024

title: Sake Tasting and Konishi Brewery Visit in Itami
description: Mr. KONISHI Shinuemon (15th generation sake brewer) was kind enough to organize an exclusive tour of his 474 years old brewery.

blocks.text: Kansai Event report

blocks.section: Sake Tasting and Konishi Brewery Visit in Itami
blocks.text: Sake Tasting and Konishi Brewery Visit in Itami

blocks.section: Sake Tasting and Konishi Brewery Visit in Itami
blocks.text: Mr. KONISHI Shinuemon (15th generation sake brewer) was kind enough to organize an exclusive tour of his 474 years old brewery.

blocks.section: Sake Tasting and Konishi Brewery Visit in Itami
blocks.text: Mr. KONISHI Shinuemon (15th generation sake brewer) was kind enough to organize an exclusive tour of his 474 years old brewery , followed by a comparative tasting of rare sake from his collection.

blocks.section: Sake Tasting and Konishi Brewery Visit in Itami
blocks.text: After putting on the necessary (and highly fashionable) sanitary outfit to prevent any unauthorized bacterias from infiltrating the tanks and interfering with the delicate operation, we were allowed to enter the sanctum.

blocks.section: Sake Tasting and Konishi Brewery Visit in Itami
blocks.text: The whole process was very well explained, with detailed panels and samples of rice to visually catch in a glance the meaning of the different degrees of refinery . The guide was obviously a veteran brewer , and could give us many detailed explanations about the complex process.

blocks.section: Sake Tasting and Konishi Brewery Visit in Itami
blocks.text: Humidity is another important factor though, which is why part of the process happens inside wooden rooms, built inside the brewery. Some modern brewer do this in stainless steel rooms, but the Konishi brewery believes in the importance of the traditional wood to regulate the humidity properly. In this case in particular, sugi (pine).

blocks.section: Sake Tasting and Konishi Brewery Visit in Itami
blocks.text: Once the visit was finished, Mr. Konishi Shinuemon himself welcomed us at the nearby restaurant run by his company, the Chojukura , which doubles as a museum on the history of Sake brewing . He gave us a personal lecture on that history, giving us an educated insight on the difference between old sake and modern sake.

blocks.section: Sake Tasting and Konishi Brewery Visit in Itami
blocks.text: We were not all ears though, because tongs and palates played an essential part in this lecture. To better demonstrate, Mr. Konishi had actually taste different samples of sake, some of them new, some of them recreating original recipes from hundreds of years ago. Some were made the traditional way, while some were brought up in pine casks, or whiskey casks; all of them had very unique flavors and were very distinguishable , even to the neophyte.

blocks.section: Sake Tasting and Konishi Brewery Visit in Itami
blocks.text: To finish on a joyful tone, we finally all left the classroom to move to the table floor, where we were served a very good menu full of tasty meats, vegetables and seafood. Bottles of sake were available, of course, all throughout the meal, and we were even presented with a fine selection of belgian beers.

blocks.section: Sake Tasting and Konishi Brewery Visit in Itami
blocks.text: The Konishi company is indeed a privilege importer of a whole selection of famous belgian beers such as Chouffe, Vedett or Duvel.

blocks.section: Sake Tasting and Konishi Brewery Visit in Itami
blocks.text: It was definitely a precious evening, all the participants being able to bond over this delicious experience.

title: Sales of dietary supplements in Japan fell by 8%
description: The dietary supplements market has shrunk by 8% since the hospitalization scare linked to Kobayashi Pharmaceutical Co. pills.

blocks.text: Foresight

blocks.section: Sales of dietary supplements in Japan fell by 8%
blocks.text: Sales of dietary supplements in Japan fell by 8%

blocks.section: Sales of dietary supplements in Japan fell by 8%
blocks.text: The dietary supplements market has shrunk by 8% since the hospitalization scare linked to Kobayashi Pharmaceutical Co. pills.

blocks.section: Sales of dietary supplements in Japan fell by 8%
blocks.text: According to the latest data published by market research company Intage, sales of dietary supplements have contracted by 8% year-on-year , as consumers face growing concerns about these products.

blocks.section: Sales of dietary supplements in Japan fell by 8%
blocks.text: Indeed, Kobayashi Pharmaceutical Co. reported on March 22 that some people had developed health problems after taking dietary supplements designed to reduce cholesterol levels . The brand subsequently announced the deaths of five people who had taken the product.

blocks.section: Sales of dietary supplements in Japan fell by 8%
blocks.text: Declining sales have been observed for products claiming to reduce cholesterol levels.

blocks.section: Sales of dietary supplements in Japan fell by 8%
blocks.text: However, this decline comes after a period of expansion due to growing consumer interest in health issues, following the Covid-19 pandemic. In 2023, sales rose by 16% year-on-year to 49.1 billion yen.

description: First CCIFJ ambassador Seiichiro Max Hayashi was appointed to this role thanks to Michel Théoval, former vice-president of the CCIFJ.

blocks.text: Kansai The Chamber

blocks.section: Seiichiro Max Hayashi – Kansai Ambassador of the CCIFJ
blocks.text: Seiichiro Max Hayashi – Kansai Ambassador of the CCIFJ

blocks.section: Seiichiro Max Hayashi – Kansai Ambassador of the CCIFJ
blocks.text: First CCIFJ ambassador Seiichiro Max Hayashi was appointed to this role thanks to Michel Théoval, former vice-president of the CCIFJ.

blocks.section: Seiichiro Max Hayashi – Kansai Ambassador of the CCIFJ
blocks.text: Seiichiro Max Hayashi is the first Ambassador of the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCIFJ). His appointment to this role was made possible through his encounter with his mentor, the late Michel Théoval, former Vice President of the CCIFJ. Recognizing Hayashi’s potential, Théoval entrusted him with the opportunity to serve Franco-Japanese relations.

blocks.section: Seiichiro Max Hayashi – Kansai Ambassador of the CCIFJ
blocks.text: Currently, the President of Kawasaki Machine Industry Co., Ltd., Mr. Hayashi has followed an unconventional career path. A graduate of California State University, he began his career in the United States, where he took part in initiatives to combat gang violence, applying the spirit of bushidō. This ideal of blending culture with martial discipline continues to guide him today.

blocks.section: Seiichiro Max Hayashi – Kansai Ambassador of the CCIFJ
blocks.text: Deeply affected by the September 11 attacks, he returned to Japan a year later. His commitment as Ambassador is rooted in his desire to support bilateral economic development and enhance social well-being. After more than ten years of experience, he has fully devoted himself to this role, drawing inspiration from the prestigious brands represented by the Chamber’s members.

blocks.section: Seiichiro Max Hayashi – Kansai Ambassador of the CCIFJ
blocks.text: Alongside his ambassadorial duties, Seiichiro Max Hayashi is driven by a strong passion for supporting “craftsmanship and manufacturing.” To this end, he created a Club House, a space for professionals from various fields to meet and exchange ideas through seminars. His upcoming event, scheduled for Friday, November 14, 2025, will focus on bamboo, exploring its potential from a planetary to a space-scale perspective.

title: Short Past Event Report:Localize Your Marketing and Product: Key Strategies for Success in Japan’s Dynamic Market
description:
On Friday, March 1st, 2024, Millet Mountain Group Japan hosted a seminar featuring its president and marketing/product director. The event aimed to delve into the localization trends within the Japanese market, leveraging the significant growth the company has experienced, with sales doubling since 2020.
The seminar provided attendees with valuable insights into the strategies Millet is actively employing to ensure success in Japan. With a strong consumer-focused perspective, participants gained refined strategies and practical takeaways.
The event took place from 12:15 pm to 2:00 pm, offering attendees a comprehensive discussion on localization trends and strategies within the Japanese market, drawing from the profound experience of Millet's leadership team.

title: Signing of a Franco-Japanese strategic partnership for the development of the biogas sector
description:
Signing of a Franco-Japanese strategic partnership for the development of the biogas sector
On March 5, an official ceremony was held at the French Embassy in Japan to mark the signing of a strategic partnership dedicated to the development of agricultural biogas in Japan.
On this occasion, NASKEO Kankyo K.K., a company committed to developing environmental and energy solutions for the Japanese agricultural sector, formalized a partnership with the French company Naskeo Environnement SARL, as well as with two major companies based in Hokkaido: Sanesu Denki Tsushin Co., Ltd. and Ueda Gumi Co., Ltd.This agreement is part of a share transfer and capital increase within NASKEO Kankyo K.K.

title: Smart Manufacturing Summit by Global Industrie: Visitor Registration in now open
description:
From Wednesday 13 to Friday 15 March 2024, “Smart Manufacturing Summit by Global Industrie” will be held at Aichi Sky Expo (Aichi International Exhibition Centre).
The Smart Manufacturing Summit by Global Industrie offers a unique format based on :
 	Classic exhibition and demonstration areas around 6 industry categories, 	C-level speakers leading panel discussions, keynote sessions and pitches at the Business Summit, 	A Startup and Innovation corner, connecting the most promising industry startups with industry leaders, corporates, innovation ecosystems and institutional partners 	Factory tours, allowing you to deep dive into the Japanese manufacturing 

Explore the 5 main areas of interest of the event and register now!
①： Business Summit
Lectures by world-leading companies and governments on smart manufacturing, including case studies and initiatives to realise smart manufacturing.
②：Innovation Showcase
Startups with cutting-edge technologies essential for the realisation of smart manufacturing will showcase product demonstrations and case studies.
③：Smart Manufacturing Expo
Various products and solutions for achieving smart manufacturing will be showcased in booths.
④：Smart Factory Demonstration
Various demonstrations for achieving smart manufacturing will be displayed.
⑤：Smart Factory Tour
Factory tours of smart manufacturing companies in Aichi Prefecture.


You can register as a visitor in advance via the QR code below. We are looking forward to your visit!

https://sms-gi.com/register/

Benefits of participation
 	Share your vision of smart manufacturing with business and government stakeholders from Europe and Japan. 
 	Understand the Japanese market and take the first steps to entering it. 
 	Benefit from our matchmaking solution MySMSAichi open to all participants to meet potential business partners and develop your network. 
 	Support innovation development and also deepen your knowledge of Industry 5.0. 

Smart Manufacturing Expo
More than 150 exhibitors, including:
 	Toyota Motor Corporation 	Kowa Optronics 	Dassault Systèmes 	Exotec 	Staubli 	Brother Industries 	Yamazaki Mazak Corporation 	DMG MORI 	Airbus (as a visitor) 

Latest conference schedule
https://sms-gi.com/english/summit/ 
Have a first overview of the topics and speakers on the stage of Business Summit and Innovation Showcase:

[Business Summit - Main Stage]
“How to Reinforce Collaboration between Japan and Europe on Smart Manufacturing?” (Panel Discussion)
Speakers:
 	Manuel HUBERT (EU-Japan Centre for Industrial Cooperation, EU-side Managing Director) 
 	Susumu KATAOKA (JETRO, President) 	Naohiko YOKOSHIMA (NEDO, President) 
Date and time: Wednesday 13th, 10:50 - 11:35

“Converging virtual and real worlds by Virtual Twin Experiences”
Speakers:
 	Philippe GODBOUT (Dassault Systèmes, Japan managing director) 	Daisuke MATSUO (Yutaka Electronics Industry, SI Engineering Department, Machining Technology Development Office and Aerospace PJ Main staff) 
Date and time: Wednesday 13th, 11:50 - 12:35

“What universities and industries should do for preparing profiles required in new era- from education, recurrent learning to re-skilling” (Panel Discussion)
Speakers:
 	Akihiro SASOU Ph.D. (Nagoya University, Vice President in charge of Academic Research & Industry-Academia-Government Collaboration and Professor, Education and Research Center for Flight Engineering, Graduate School of Engineering Tokai National Higher Education and Research System, Chancellor’s Adviser) 	Masaaki TERANO Ph.D. (Nagoya University, Tokai National University Organization, Director and Specially Appointed Professor, Open Innovation Promotion Office, Future Society Creation Organisation, Executive Officer, Tokai Innovation Institute Inc.) 	Osamu TABATA Ph.D. (Kyoto University of Advanced Science, Vice President, Dean of Faculty of Engineering) 
Date and time: Thursday 14th, 14:00 - 14:45

“New Innovation: Co-creation (industry-academia-government collaboration) to trigger future innovations (TBC)” (Keynote Speech)
Speaker:
 	Hiroaki MIYATA (Co-Innovation University Presidential Candidate (to be determined by the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology in October 2024)) 
Date and time: Friday 15th, 10:15 - 10:45

“Smart Logistics to empower industries” (Keynote Speech)
Speaker:

“German Japanese Business and Technology Seminar: Advanced and Innovative Solutions in Smart Manufacturing, Robotics and AI”
Organizer: NRW.Global Business GmbH (German NRW State Trade and Investment Promotion Agency) / NRW.Global Business Japan
Speakers:

title: SMBC Trust Bank -PRESTIA- Offering comprehensive English support for international residents in Japan
description:
SMBC Trust Bank -PRESTIA- has been highly rated by international residents in Japan for its customer-friendly services.
Banking in Japan may sound intricating for international residents in Japan. It is crucial but frustrating because of the complicated language, processes and documentation or limited business hours. For those who start living in Japan, or have been struggling with your Japanese bank, SMBC Trust Bank is here to help.
We have enhanced our capabilities of having financial discussions in English, so that our foreign customers are able to feel comfortable in going through all banking process from daily transactions - i.e. debit services or cross border transactions-, to asset management such as loans or investments.

Why choose PRESTIA?
We offer ultimate English services through various channels, focusing on comfortable and safe banking. Most major transactions can be simply done through our secured Online Banking.
PRESTIA Phone Banking is also available for 24h/365d in English, in which you can directly ask for any inquiries and get assistance for transactions from all around the world without any anxiety of time difference.
We are also welcoming our customers to visit our Global Branches, flagship branches specialized for English speaking customers, located in Hiroo and Akasaka. You can choose your favorite channel which most suits your situation.

Products and services highly rated by foreign customers:
Global Pass
- a cash card with Visa debit service that can be paid in 18 currencies
Loan Products
- available to foreign national customers without any special add-fee
PRESTIA GOLD Service
- special service for special customers, offering preferential fees for some transactions and preferred interest rate for some deposits and loan products

Some Customer Feedbacks
We have carefully listened to customer feedbacks to improve functionality and efficiency.
Here are some feedbacks we have received:
“Good online service, and cash card is accepted everywhere and easy to use. ”
“Amazing service—smooth, friendly and efficient. A banking pleasure. ”
“PRESTIA Gold account is highly recommended for the ease of both domestic and overseas transfers. ”
“Staff was very professional and explained everything concisely in fluent English. ”
“Very happy with the entire team that handled mortgage even for a foreigner without permanent residence. ”
If you have any difficulties with your banking in Japan, please feel free to speak to our bank staffs.

MORE INFORMATION

blocks.section: Societe Generale has launched its first incubator programme dedicated to market solutions in Asia Pacific
blocks.text: A unique vertical incubation platform fully dedicated to financial markets.

blocks.section: Societe Generale has launched its first incubator programme dedicated to market solutions in Asia Pacific
blocks.text: After the success of the Global Markets Incubator launched in Europe in 2018, Societe Generale opens the doors of its trading floors in Asia Pacific and has launched its first incubator programme dedicated to market solutions in Asia Pacific. Global Markets Incubator is an open framework that benefits from world class experts to build tailored and valuable collaborations. ​

blocks.section: Societe Generale has launched its first incubator programme dedicated to market solutions in Asia Pacific
blocks.text: Selected applicants will be entitled to a 6-month incubation period, gaining access to dedicated resources from Societe Generale to define and develop their proposed solutions. Market experts from any of the 12 locations in Asia Pacific, including financial engineers, traders, sales, middle and back office teams, as well as data and proprietary platforms will allow early-stage entrepreneurs to benefit from the required ecosystem and resources to turn their start-up into a valuable business proposition.

blocks.section: Societe Generale has launched its first incubator programme dedicated to market solutions in Asia Pacific
blocks.text: Within Societe Generale, one of the leading European financial services group, the market activities are integrated into a multi-asset class, multi-product platform focusing on delivering high quality investment, financing and risk management solutions to: asset managers, pension funds, private banks, banks, insurance companies, hedge funds, corporates, family offices, sovereign funds and retail network distributors around the world.

blocks.text: Companies news

blocks.section: Societe Generale: Worldwide Partner of the 2023 Rugby World Cup in France
blocks.text: Societe Generale: Worldwide Partner of the 2023 Rugby World Cup in France

blocks.section: Societe Generale: Worldwide Partner of the 2023 Rugby World Cup in France
blocks.text: The journey for the 'Official Bank of Rugby' began when Societe Generale partnered with the French rugby union in 1987. Since then, and for more than 30 years, the Group have cemented a bond between its own values and the core values of rugby.

blocks.section: Societe Generale: Worldwide Partner of the 2023 Rugby World Cup in France
blocks.text: Today, Societe Generale supports rugby from its grassroots to professional pinnacles , encouraging the practice of rugby by women and younger generations, especially as a channel for social inclusion, and making sure that the historic journey with rugby embodies the Group’s mission – contributing to positive transformations in society .

blocks.section: Societe Generale: Worldwide Partner of the 2023 Rugby World Cup in France
blocks.text: In line with this mission, Societe Generale partners with rugby institutions all around the world : in Europe, Africa, America (with recently Rugby Quebec in Canada), Asia Pacific (namely Hong Kong Valley rugby club, Sydney Easts rugby club and India rugby union) and last but not least, Rugby World Cup, for the seventh time.

blocks.section: Societe Generale: Worldwide Partner of the 2023 Rugby World Cup in France
blocks.text: As Worldwide Partner and Official bank of Rugby World Cup 2023, Societe Generale will offer again unique opportunities to share with our clients, staff and all our stakeholders rugby’s values and spirit, to bring more people to this amazing sport and contribute to its expansion.

blocks.section: Societe Generale: Worldwide Partner of the 2023 Rugby World Cup in France
blocks.text: After sharing together the passion and emotions of Rugby World Cup 2019, Societe Generale invites you to join a new exciting journey towards Rugby World Cup 2023!

title: Solid interest in our seminar about French internships in Osaka
description: This seminar aimed to popularize the concept of French internships among Japanese companies and to highlight its merits.

blocks.text: Kansai Event report

blocks.section: Solid interest in our seminar about French internships in Osaka
blocks.text: Solid interest in our seminar about French internships in Osaka

blocks.section: Solid interest in our seminar about French internships in Osaka
blocks.text: This seminar aimed to popularize the concept of French internships among Japanese companies and to highlight its merits.

blocks.section: Solid interest in our seminar about French internships in Osaka
blocks.text: Altogether, around thirty people gathered on Thursday, May 9th, at the premises of our member and co-organizer Kitahama Partners to attend this seminar, which addressed the topic of internships from three perspectives: that of universities and students, represented by Ms. Fumiko SUGIE of Centrale Lille ; that of companies hosting interns, presented by Mr. Damien VITRY of Arkema ; and finally, the legal aspects and procedures, presented by Attorneys Jiri MESTECKY and Claude KANEDA of Kitahama Partners.

blocks.section: Solid interest in our seminar about French internships in Osaka
blocks.text: To start, Ms. Fumiko SUGIE, a Japanese teacher at Centrale Lille in France , opened the seminar with a general presentation on the concept of internships in France. She highlighted how internships have become essential in a student's academic journey in France and the significant role they play in preparing students for the professional world. Internships are now a common step to smooth the way from academia to the professional sphere, allowing for a more gradual acclimatization to corporate life for those who benefit from.

blocks.section: Solid interest in our seminar about French internships in Osaka
blocks.text: Conversely, this practice remains rare in Japan, where internships are generally shorter, conducted outside the academic framework, and sometimes even require the intern to pay for the experience. However, following the democratization of international internships within the European area , for example, the number of foreign students eager to embark on an adventure in Japan has been increasing, as they regard internships as an excellent entry point into the otherwise quite closed Japanese job market. This is particularly relevant because in Japan, professional codes are very specific and require a certain practice.

blocks.section: Solid interest in our seminar about French internships in Osaka
blocks.text: Yet, Japan still severely lacks young employees capable of speaking foreign languages , while many French students are ready to come and gain their first experience in Japan to improve their Japanese language skills .

blocks.section: Solid interest in our seminar about French internships in Osaka
blocks.text: On the other hand, employing foreign interns could bring significant benefits to Japanese companies with international ambitions . Although this workforce is inexperienced, they are generally very open-minded, eager, and highly adaptable. Hiring foreign interns in Japanese companies would gradually create a pool of young employees capable, not only of opening doors for Japanese businesses in foreign markets, but also of being comfortable with the language and unique codes of the Japanese business world.

blocks.section: Solid interest in our seminar about French internships in Osaka
blocks.text: Thus, Damien VITRY, General Manager at Arkema, along with one of his former interns, Miki LAUNOIS , explained the advantages of using interns from the company’s perspective: identifying young talents , providing concrete on-the-job training , offering junior staff their first management experience , acquiring an additional, creative, and motivated workforce without long-term commitments, introducing fresh ideas , and gaining flexibility . These are all benefits that companies can achieve by employing interns.

blocks.section: Solid interest in our seminar about French internships in Osaka
blocks.text: To conclude, the administrative formalities related to internships can seem complex and raise concerns among companies. For instance, the duration of an internship, typically 2 to 6 months , often exceeds that permitted by a tourist visa in Japan. What are the alternative solutions ? What are the different formats of internships? What types of visas are admissible for these internships? What information should be included in an internship agreement? What about the salary ? The employment contract? And the protection of company data ? These crucial questions were clarified by the expertise of Attorneys Claude KANEDA and Jiri MESTECKY of Kitahama Partners, who also provided many concrete details during the question-and-answer session at the end of the event.

blocks.section: Solid interest in our seminar about French internships in Osaka
blocks.text: The questions were numerous and the exchanges lively, demonstrating the participants' interest . The evening concluded with a vibrant networking session , where conversations continued enthusiastically, building on the previous presentations. One thing is certain: this topic is timely and deserves further exploration in Japan.

blocks.text: Jean RENO in Tokyo? A must-see Talk-Show centered around his play “Rakuda”!

blocks.section: Special Event! A rendez-vous with Jean RENO : Presented by BONJOUR FRANCE
blocks.text: BONJOUR FRANCE is pleased to announce an exceptional event that will delight lovers of cinema and the performing arts. On Monday, April 20, from 6:00 PM, L’Espace@CCIFJ will host an exclusive Talk-Show in the presence of the iconic actor Jean RENO, a major figure in both French and international cinema.

blocks.section: Special Event! A rendez-vous with Jean RENO : Presented by BONJOUR FRANCE
blocks.text: This special moment will offer the audience a unique insight into the actor’s latest artistic project, “Rakuda”, a solo performance he is presenting in Japan. Through this work, Jean RENO will revisit the origins of this singular production, somewhere between theatre and personal storytelling. The discussion will be led by journalist Florent DABADIE, bringing his perspective to this exceptional conversation.

blocks.section: Special Event! A rendez-vous with Jean RENO : Presented by BONJOUR FRANCE
blocks.text: “Rakuda” is unveiled as a world premiere. On stage, Jean RENO is joined by director Ladislas CHOLLAT and pianist Pablo LANTY to bring to life a narrative blending music, imagery, and memories. During this soirée, Ladislas CHOLLAT will also be present to provide an overall perspective on the project.

blocks.section: Special Event! A rendez-vous with Jean RENO : Presented by BONJOUR FRANCE
blocks.text: The evening will continue with a cocktail dinner accompanied by DASSAI sake and a special menu created in tribute to Jean RENO for this unique occasion, offering guests the opportunity to extend together the magic of this artistic encounter. In addition, attendance at the Talk-Show includes access to the play “Rakuda”, performed on several dates in May, offering a complete experience.

blocks.section: Special Event! A rendez-vous with Jean RENO : Presented by BONJOUR FRANCE
blocks.text: Limited to 100 participants, this event promises a rare opportunity to get up close to a true legend of cinema in an intimate and artistic atmosphere.

title: Success for the 1st edition of the Smart Manufacturing Summit
description:
Supported by Global Industrie, the largest industrial trade fair in France, GL events Venues orchestrated the very first gathering dedicated to smart manufacturing in Japan, with the theme of Industry 5.0.
The Smart Manufacturing Summit, whose 1st edition took place at the Aichi International Exhibition Center on March 13, 14, and 15, was the international meeting point for professionals in the future industry and brought together a total of over 10,000 visitors.
The event attracted a total of 246 exhibitors and 95 speakers from 40 different countries, including Japan and various European countries.
« We set out to create a unique event - the Smart Manufacturing Summit - to bring together industry exhibitors, start-ups and government representatives. We have also offered content focused on conferences, innovation, and the opportunity for everyone to take a solid step towards an innovative and sustainable industry, Industry 5.0. », said Christophe Cizeron, Chairman and CEO of GL events and organizer of the event.
He also expressed his enthusiasm for the next edition of the event, scheduled in Aichi, Japan, in June 2025, building on the momentum created by this edition.

Event Recap:  
1. Business Summit
Nearly 25 programs were held on the main stage bringing together a total of 71 people towards « Industry 5.0. » These were conducted based on case studies of European companies at the forefront of « Industry 5.0 », the sharing of know-how and discussions on the « international agora » (visions and strategic directions) by government bodies.
2. Exhibition on intelligent manufacturing
189 companies came together to present their products and solutions for achieving Industry 5.0.
3. Innovation showcase
57 Industry 5.0 start-ups exhibited their products and made business pitches with the aim of raising funds and collaborating with other companies.
4. Product demonstration: smart factory and logistics
Business pitch and product presentation from three companies working in Industry 5.0 (Juken Kogyo Co.,Ltd., Exotec Nihon Corporation and SPACE Monkey) and Aichi Prefecture (« Aichi Digital Island Project »).
5. Visit to an intelligent factory
CKD Corporation (head office in Aichi) organized a visit to its new showroom and factory on Wednesday 13 March.

For more information, please visit the official event website.

title: Summer in Hida Takayama
description:
Hida Takayama was awarded 3 stars in the French Michelin Travel Guide as a must-see destination. Located in the center of the Japan, Hida Takayama offers historic townscapes, beautiful nature, and local cuisine. One of World Heritage Sites, Shirakawa-go is located about an hour from Hida Takayama, and you can enjoy its unspoilt Japanese landscape. 
Their local Wagyu beef is called “Hida-gyu”. It’s very tender, finely marbled, and melt-in-your-mouth. You can taste this Hida-gyu as Yakiniku,(barbecue), in Sukiyaki or even as Sushi.
 [Example of itinerary]
 	Day 1：To Shirakawa-go→ Stay at Hida Takayama 	Day 2：Visit Hida Takayama : Jinya, morning market, old town streets→Norikura Plateau→ Stay at Hida Takayama 	Day 3：Hirayu Hot Springs→Shin Hotaka Ropeway→Kamikochi→Matsumoto 

Hotel We recommend "Takayama Green Hotel" for lodging for sightseeing based in Hida Takayama. At Takayama Green Hotel has a good quality of natural hot spring. There is a large bath covered by glass window and also an open-air garden bath, which relieve your travel fatigue.

Transportation Express buses are more convenient and economical than airplanes or Shinkansen trains from Tokyo to Hida Takayama. The highway bus, which takes about 5 hours and 30 minutes with no transfers. "Three-Star Alps Shinjuku Ticket," is convenient to visit each of the sightseeing spots listed in the " Example of itinerary " from Tokyo (Shinjuku).
Enjoy history, culture, and nature in Hida Takayama this summer!

For more information about sightseeing in Hida Takayama and highway buses, please click the link here. http://www.keioinfoplaza.jp/en_hida/

title: Symposium: Employment and Work in the Age of AI: France-Japan Perspectives
description:
On September 29, 2026, in Tokyo, with the support of the French Chamber in Commerce in Tokyo, AOTS will host an international symposium focusing on how artificial intelligence is transforming the world of work. The event will explore the impact of AI on employment, quality of work, human resource management and worker protection, as well as recent developments in legal frameworks.
The symposium will highlight the French experience with Professor Pascal Lokiec, Professor of Labour Law at Université Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne, who will discuss recent developments in France regarding the impact of AI on employment and work. Professor Ryo Hosokawa of Aoyama Gakuin University will provide insights into current debates and emerging challenges in Japan.
A panel discussion will then bring together French and Japanese experts around the theme “Human-Centered Work and the Future of Employment in the Age of AI,” offering an opportunity to reflect on the future of work and the lessons Japan can draw from the French experience.
The symposium will take place from 2:00 to 5:00 p.m. at Bellesalle Kanda in Tokyo and will also be available online, with simultaneous Japanese-French interpretation. 
Admission is free, with registration open until September 28, 2026: employers-bb@aots.jp

title: Tasting of Shimizu Seizaburo's Sakes at the Hilton Osaka
description: Exclusive guided tasting of "Zaku" sake from Shimizu Seizaburo during a gastronomic dinner at the Hilton Osaka.

blocks.text: Kansai Event report

blocks.section: Tasting of Shimizu Seizaburo's Sakes at the Hilton Osaka
blocks.text: Tasting of Shimizu Seizaburo's Sakes at the Hilton Osaka

blocks.section: Tasting of Shimizu Seizaburo's Sakes at the Hilton Osaka
blocks.text: Exclusive guided tasting of "Zaku" sake from Shimizu Seizaburo during a gastronomic dinner at the Hilton Osaka.

blocks.section: Tasting of Shimizu Seizaburo's Sakes at the Hilton Osaka
blocks.text: This unique experience was complemented by a gourmet dinner specially crafted by Hilton Osaka and prepared by the chefs of the "Centrum" restaurant, located on the second floor of the hotel. Participants enjoyed a selection of refined sakes , each offering distinct notes that harmonized beautifully with the accompanying dishes.

blocks.section: Tasting of Shimizu Seizaburo's Sakes at the Hilton Osaka
blocks.text: Alexandre Luciani, a sommelier specializing in Japanese sake, guided us through the tasting, sharing his expertise on the selection of the day and helping the guests appreciate the different aromas and characteristics of each sake. He also provided insights on the pairing with the dishes and offered general recommendations for how to best enjoy each product.

blocks.section: Tasting of Shimizu Seizaburo's Sakes at the Hilton Osaka
blocks.text: Indeed, Japanese sake lends itself well to food pairings, in the same manner as French wine. Its aromas are indeed quite similar to those of white wines. This opens up a whole avenue for cultural adaptation, allowing Japanese sake to find its place in French gastronomy. This is what Mr. and Mrs. Shimizu have been working on for many years, striving to introduce their sake to France. As such, they have already won numerous prestigious awards, including the Kuramaster.

blocks.section: Tasting of Shimizu Seizaburo's Sakes at the Hilton Osaka
blocks.text: Mr. and Mrs. Shimizu also shared with us the production process of their sakes, which has been brewed for 150 years in Suzuka , located in the Mie Prefecture, often referred to as "Suzuka, the Land of Good Sake" ('Umasake Suzuka no Kuni').

blocks.section: Tasting of Shimizu Seizaburo's Sakes at the Hilton Osaka
blocks.text: Everyone had the opportunity to appreciate not only the diversity of the presented sakes, but also the passion and craftsmanship of its producers. This form of seminar, delivered in small segments, allows participants to learn throughout the meal without overwhelming them with a lengthy, didactic monologue.

blocks.section: Tasting of Shimizu Seizaburo's Sakes at the Hilton Osaka
blocks.text: Beyond the tasting experience , this event provided a unique opportunity for learning and sharing , fostering lively discussions on the traditions and subtleties of Japanese sake, which became even more animated as the guests savored the drinks available to them.

title: The 55th Paris Air Show (SIAE) will bring together players from all over the world at Paris Le Bourget
description:
The next edition of the Paris Air Show (Salon International de l'Aéronautique et de l'Espace), to be held at the Parc des Expositions de Paris-Le Bourget from 16 to 22 June 2025, will bring together all the key players in the global industry to showcase the latest innovations. The first 4 days of the show are reserved for professionals, followed by 3 days for the general public.
 With 2,500 exhibitors from 48 countries, 130,000 trade visitors and 322 official delegations from all over the world, the Paris Air Show, organised by SIAE, a subsidiary of GIFAS (Groupement des Industries Françaises Aéronautiques et Spatiales), is the world's biggest event for the aerospace industry. For over a century, the SIAE has embodied the excellence, innovation and international cooperation of the entire industry: civil aviation, the defence sector and space. It is undeniably a high point in the economic life of the sector, with many orders being placed at the time of the show.
 Stand sales for the SIAE 2025 exhibition are almost complete, and many of the world's top 100 companies have already signed up to take part. The SIAE also plays host to a large number of start-ups in the aerospace industry, on exhibitors' stands and in the regional and international pavilions. The Start Me Up programme offers them a unique platform to present their innovations to customers, partners and investors, and to benefit from support throughout the show.
 For international trade visitors, the Paris Air Show is the ideal event for discovering the latest market trends, meeting manufacturers, equipment suppliers and systems suppliers all in one place, and developing their network. A wide range of services are on offer, including pre-programmed business meetings (Aerospace Meetings Paris) to enable them to meet manufacturers and do business. Ticketing for trade visitors will open in March 2025.

title: “The Arc”: Nissan's new strategic plan
description: Nissan Motor Corporation announced on Monday its new strategic plan for the next three years.

blocks.text: Companies news

blocks.section: “The Arc”: Nissan's new strategic plan
blocks.text: “The Arc”: Nissan's new strategic plan

blocks.section: “The Arc”: Nissan's new strategic plan
blocks.text: Nissan Motor Corporation announced on Monday its new strategic plan for the next three years.

blocks.section: “The Arc”: Nissan's new strategic plan
blocks.text: “We cannot succeed if we keep doing the things the same way as before,” said Nissan CEO Makoto Uchida at a press conference on Monday.

blocks.section: “The Arc”: Nissan's new strategic plan
blocks.text: Facing intense competition in China as well as an acceleration of the energy transition, Nissan has announced the launch of its new strategic plan called for the next three years, “The Arc.”

blocks.section: “The Arc”: Nissan's new strategic plan
blocks.text: The new strategic plan aims first to increase Nissan’s sales volume. Japan’s third-largest automaker plans to increase its sales by a further million units and its operating margin by 6% by fiscal 2026. 30 new models, including 16 electric vehicles, will be launched by 2026.

blocks.section: “The Arc”: Nissan's new strategic plan
blocks.text: Nissan is also seeking to improve its profitability. In China, where competition is intensifying, 73% of Nissan brand cars will be renewed by 2026. The automotive giant is banking on the strategy of energy competitiveness, with the introduction of 8 new electric vehicles locally.

blocks.section: “The Arc”: Nissan's new strategic plan
blocks.text: Nissan has also announced that it is extending its strategic alliances with other companies to improve its competitiveness. It has signed an agreement with Honda and is already considering collaboration in the field of electrification and vehicle intelligence.

blocks.section: “The Arc”: Nissan's new strategic plan
blocks.text: The strategic plan also includes the reduction of electric car costs by 30%, as well as a total return target of 30% for shareholders through dividends and share purchases.

blocks.section: “The Arc”: Nissan's new strategic plan
blocks.text: Potential sales of 2.5 trillion yen are expected by fiscal 2030. “The Arc represents Nissan's path to the future,” promises Makoto Uchida at the press conference.

title: The “C-19 Chronicles Life & Business in Vietnam” by Indochina Legal
description:
In their first edition “From Success to Hardship” of their series of publications “C-19 Chronicles Life & Business in Vietnam”, Indochina Legal depicted the hardships Vietnam has been facing since late May 2021 as a result of a fast-spreading outbreak of COVID-19 cases in the country.
This second edition “Living with the Virus – Preserving the Economy” provides further insights into the impact of the pandemic by focusing on the country’s key economic sectors: the industrial and export sectors.
This follows their "From Success to Hardship" inaugural article, which depicted the hardships Vietnam has been facing since late May 2021 as a result of a fast-spreading outbreak of COVID-19 cases in the country.  
Download the full publication here
 Indochina Legal is a multi-cultural Vietnam based law firm providing client advocacy of international standards in diversified transactional and litigation work. Founded in 2007, the firm integrates legal practice of over 15 years in Vietnam. Indochina Legal acts as a correspondent firm for a number of international and regional law firms and is a member of Legalink, an international network of independent law firms.

title: The difficult transition to reduced overtime for truckers
description: Overtime regulations came into force on April 1, 2024.

blocks.text: Foresight

blocks.section: The difficult transition to reduced overtime for truckers
blocks.text: The difficult transition to reduced overtime for truckers

blocks.section: The difficult transition to reduced overtime for truckers
blocks.text: Overtime regulations came into force on April 1, 2024.

blocks.section: The difficult transition to reduced overtime for truckers
blocks.text: Legislation governing overtime for truck drivers came into force at the beginning of April . Companies are gradually adapting to this new law.

blocks.section: The difficult transition to reduced overtime for truckers
blocks.text: For example, a subsidiary of supermarket giant Aeon has implemented an AI tool and high-tech robots to manage orders and define delivery routes.

blocks.section: The difficult transition to reduced overtime for truckers
blocks.text: Also, the reduction in overtime work has led delivery services to increase their costs, notably at Yamato Transport or Sagawa Express.

blocks.section: The difficult transition to reduced overtime for truckers
blocks.text: Mos Food Service (the delivery service of fast-food chain Mos Burger) has decided to bring its Tokyo deliveries forward to 4 a.m. to avoid traffic jams.

blocks.section: The difficult transition to reduced overtime for truckers
blocks.text: There is also a shared-transport program involving Asahi Group Japan, which has reduced labor by almost 40%.

blocks.section: The difficult transition to reduced overtime for truckers
blocks.text: However, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) are reacting slowly. According to the Japan Chamber of Commerce and Industry (JCCCI), less than half of SMEs have adapted to the new legislation .

title: The European Business Council urges Japan to relax travel restrictions
description: Source ; Japan Times

blocks.text: COVID-19

blocks.section: The European Business Council urges Japan to relax travel restrictions
blocks.text: The European Business Council urges Japan to relax travel restrictions

blocks.section: The European Business Council urges Japan to relax travel restrictions
blocks.text: Source ; Japan Times

blocks.section: The European Business Council urges Japan to relax travel restrictions
blocks.text: The EBC (European Business Council) urged the Japanese government to revise its coronavirus-triggered entry restrictions imposed on foreign nationals, warning that the ban threatens to leave a lasting negative impact on operations of European and Japanese businesses alike.

blocks.section: The European Business Council urges Japan to relax travel restrictions
blocks.text: The entry restrictions were imposed about a year after a trade pact between Japan and the European Union came into effect on Feb. 1, 2019. The deal was meant to increase exports from the European Union and direct investment from Europe. Within a year, the agreement boosted exports from the EU by 6.6 percent.

blocks.section: The European Business Council urges Japan to relax travel restrictions
blocks.text: “Now … (the agreement) is losing momentum because of the travel ban,” said Michael Mroczek, President of the European Business Council in Japan, during a news conference in Tokyo. He suggested that in easing the restrictions, Japan should prioritize permanent residents and long-term residents — noting that those groups include a large number of people who either run their own businesses or are employed in Japan — followed by business travelers.

blocks.section: The European Business Council urges Japan to relax travel restrictions
blocks.text: To prevent further fallout, “a possible solution could be that permanent and long-term residents should be immediately let out and back again into Japan; in the second step the restriction could be lifted on business travelers and later … tourists.”; he added.

description: Or why proper cups of coffee, great IT, and mask-to-mask meetings still matter when it comes to office life

blocks.text: Companies news

blocks.section: The Executive Centre launches the “Welcome Back to The Office” campaign
blocks.text: The Executive Centre launches the “Welcome Back to The Office” campaign

blocks.section: The Executive Centre launches the “Welcome Back to The Office” campaign
blocks.text: Or why proper cups of coffee, great IT, and mask-to-mask meetings still matter when it comes to office life

blocks.section: The Executive Centre launches the “Welcome Back to The Office” campaign
blocks.text: The COVID-19 outbreak has led to businesses and employees re-evaluating what the workplace means to them. Today, The Executive Centre (TEC), the leading premium flexible workspace provider across Asia Pacific and the Middle East, launches the “Welcome Back to The Office” video campaign, where characters find ways to adapt to the new working environment.

blocks.section: The Executive Centre launches the “Welcome Back to The Office” campaign
blocks.text: The campaign is a take on the work-from-home phenomenon, and while the characters in the videos are fictional, their triumphs and struggles are drawn from real experiences of TEC’s 1000+ global team.

blocks.section: The Executive Centre launches the “Welcome Back to The Office” campaign
blocks.text: What’s clear is that while homeworking arrangements are becoming normalised and people are enjoying less commuting, not having to dress to impress and spending more time with their families; on the flip side, there are also irreplaceable benefits of working in an office such as proper coffee in a proper coffee cup, chatting to colleagues and collaborating on projects, IT that works, comfortable ergonomic furniture, admin support, and a highly-productive environment that boosts concentration and minimises distractions.

blocks.section: The Executive Centre launches the “Welcome Back to The Office” campaign
blocks.text: “After an extended period of time working from home, we are inspired to explore how the typical workday has changed, and is continuing to change,” said Paul Salnikow, TEC Founder and CEO. “We believe the future of the workplace hinges on its relationship with the people who truly make it work. As the pandemic has accelerated the shift to flexible workspaces, we are certain that the office, rather than becoming obsolete, will become an increasingly valuable asset facilitating collaboration and driving business growth. Our clients are telling us that their offices of the future will need solutions that are tailored to their success, limit current challenges, give their staff maximum flexibility and provide the best office environment that they can find.”

blocks.text: Welcome Back to the Office – Good to leave, even better to come back.

title: The French Business Awards 2022 showcase and reward the efforts and successes of French companies in Japan
description:
The CCI France Japon held the 11th edition of its French Business Award on Tuesday, the 8th of March 2022 at Grand Hyatt Tokyo.
This year, 14 companies of various industries and sectors were in competition for 3 awards, which showcase and reward the efforts and successes of companies in Japan.
The CCI France Japon is pleased to announce the results of this competition. 

The 2022 laureates are: 
AC MEDIA / Ki-oon  - “Company of the Year” Award
Imperial Hotel, Ltd. - “Product or Service of the Year” Award
Kisui TECH Co. LTD  - “French Tech Tokyo” Award 
PEEL Lab  - “Sustainable Development Award”
UnaBiz Japan Co., ltd  - “Special Jury Award”

The jury was composed of the Chairman of the CCI France Japon, and French and Japanese business leaders.
They selected among the nominees the most dynamic, innovative and performing companies with grounded success on the Japanese market.
All 14 companies were a testimony of the diversity, the strength and the polyvalence of French and Japanese businesses.
Highly diverse industries were showcased this year.

description: The French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan is pleased to announce that its new antenna, the Chubu office, opened on the 27th of January, 2020. Our delegate, Faustine Peyceré, is operating it from her desk in Nagoya, hosted in one of Aero Inc.’s offices. Her main goal will be to reinforce and promote the French-Japanese business community in the Chubu prefecture.

blocks.text: The French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan is pleased to announce that its new antenna, the Chubu office, opened on the 27th of January, 2020. Our delegate, Faustine Peyceré, is operating it from her desk in Nagoya, hosted in one of Aero Inc.’s offices. Her main goal will be to reinforce and promote the French-Japanese business community in the Chubu prefecture.

blocks.section: An international hub on the forefront of manufacturing industries
blocks.text: An international hub on the forefront of manufacturing industries

blocks.section: An international hub on the forefront of manufacturing industries
blocks.text: Nagoya is renowned for its great economic potential, ranking first in Japan since 1977 in terms of industrial production.

blocks.section: An international hub on the forefront of manufacturing industries
blocks.text: As the capital city of the Aichi prefecture, Nagoya is a hub of the industry and of the maritime shipping of the central Japanese island of Honshu. Thanks to its location, but also to its land, sea and air infrastructures, Nagoya is easy to access for most neighboring countries.

blocks.section: An international hub on the forefront of manufacturing industries
blocks.text: The region is host to the greatest concentration of industries in Japan, in regard to the automobile, aerospace, among other high technlogy industries.

blocks.section: An international hub on the forefront of manufacturing industries
blocks.text: This new office is tasked with contributing more efficiently to the development of the French-Japanese activities in the region, where some French companies have already settled.

blocks.text: After getting two bachelor degrees, Japanese culture and language and International relations, at Inalco (National Institute for Oriental Languages and Civilizations), Faustine Peyceré graduated with a Master in technical translation. She then handled several projects, for a Unesco delegation among others, before joining the new Chubu desk to develop it. This new network is counting on her linguistic skills and her passion for Japan and its culture!

title: The Independents Groups acquires Bureau Betak
description:
Bureau Betak, the global events and production company founded by Alexandre de Betak in Paris in 1990, has sold a majority stake to The Independents group (joining K2, Karla Otto, The Qode and Lefty), according to representatives from both firms.
Over the last 30 years, Bureau Betak has built a name for producing some of fashion’s most opulent and extravagant shows and generated more than $100 million in revenue in 2019. It was responsible for Miu Miu’s first runway show in 1994 and Fendi’s glass labyrinth to mark creative director Kim Jones’ January couture debut.
The Independents has reached a new milestone, as it continues to position itself as a key player in fashion and luxury. The move cements The Independents Group and Bureau Betak’s status as industry trailblazers, collectively enabling an integrated approach to comprehensive client services. The group is a global leader in communications and digital marketing (Karla Otto/The Qode), experience and content (K2) and influence and data (Lefty). 
This is a major milestone of the group’s development as a strategic and ROI-driven partner of our clients globally. Alexandre de Betak understood earlier than most the importance of culture and content for brands. His vision will help push the ball even further, making us a highly relevant strategic communications partner and giving us the ability to advise clients on campaigns that build on their cultural DNA.", said Isabelle Chouvet, chief executive of The Independents Group.
ABOUT K2 (Member of the CCI France Japon)
Experiential agency K2 is the trusted partner for luxury, fashion, beauty and lifestyle brands, specializing in event concept, design and production with a unique craft in storytelling and interactivity – from fashion shows, exhibitions and conferences to popups, product launches and immersive brand experiences. Founded in 2002, the agency has developed leadership positions in Japan, Greater China, and Korea.

title: Brands Forum - The Japan Master Collection Project, Modernization of Japanese Craftsmanship
description:
We are delighted to announce the outstanding success of our recent Brands Forum event, “The Japan Master Collection Project: Modernizing Japanese Craftsmanship.”
With over 30 participants, the event was graced by Mr. Hiroshi Onishi, President of Haneda Future Research Institute Incorporated, as our distinguished speaker. His insights into the modernization of Japanese craftsmanship were truly inspiring, and his sage words will remain with us. The event also included an incredible Q&A session, which sparked lively discussions and insightful questions.
Following the formal presentation, attendees had the opportunity to engage in vibrant networking sessions, exchanging ideas and forging new connections in a relaxed atmosphere. This interaction facilitated dynamic conversations and the sharing of valuable experiences among professionals.
We would also like to extend our gratitude to Richemont Japan and Miki Hitoshi for co-hosting this event and contributing to its success.
Thank you to all who attended and participated. We look forward to seeing you at our future events!

blocks.section: The Osaka 2025 World Expo : France unveils its pavilion
blocks.text: Here is the translated and summarized text:

blocks.section: The Osaka 2025 World Expo : France unveils its pavilion
blocks.text: **Unveiling a Powerful Pavilion and a Strong Project**

blocks.section: The Osaka 2025 World Expo : France unveils its pavilion
blocks.text: The France Pavilion for the Osaka 2025 World Expo was revealed on January 9 at the French Foreign Ministry in Paris, under the patronage of the French President. The Expo, themed "Designing Tomorrow’s Society, Imagining Our Lives in the Future," will take place from April 13 to October 13, 2025.

blocks.section: The Osaka 2025 World Expo : France unveils its pavilion
blocks.text: Olivier Becht, French Minister of State for Foreign Trade, Attractiveness, and French People Overseas, and Jacques Maire, Commissioner General for France Osaka 2025, introduced the pavilion's architecture and central theme, "A Hymn to Love," to over 250 French and Japanese dignitaries.

blocks.section: The Osaka 2025 World Expo : France unveils its pavilion
blocks.text: **The France Pavilion: A Hymn to Love**

blocks.section: The Osaka 2025 World Expo : France unveils its pavilion
blocks.text: Designed by Coldefy & Associés Architectes Urbanistes and CRA-Carlo Ratti Associati, the France Pavilion embodies "A Hymn to Love" in its architecture, exhibition spaces, and programming. It offers an immersive experience showcasing French innovation. The sustainable pavilion's structure is recyclable, featuring a modern facade resembling an open theater.

blocks.section: The Osaka 2025 World Expo : France unveils its pavilion
blocks.text: The visitor experience includes a multisensory journey, starting from the entrance porch and leading to a chic French-style hall. The permanent exhibition explores three aspects of love: self-love, love for others, and love for nature. The pavilion's programming, based on "A Hymn to Love," includes six temporary exhibitions and twelve themed fortnights aligned with the UN's Sustainable Development Goals.

blocks.section: The Osaka 2025 World Expo : France unveils its pavilion
blocks.text: **The France Pavilion: A Tool for Outreach, Development, and Attractiveness**

blocks.section: The Osaka 2025 World Expo : France unveils its pavilion
blocks.text: The France Pavilion aims to highlight France's economic momentum, energy independence, low-carbon reindustrialization, and leadership in the lifestyle sector. It seeks to inspire individual and collective commitment with a vision guided by the meaning of life and love.

blocks.section: The Osaka 2025 World Expo : France unveils its pavilion
blocks.text: For collaborating businesses, the Osaka 2025 Expo provides a showcase for expertise and innovations across various sectors. The pavilion targets the Japanese market, emphasizing the "France 2030 plan" for reindustrialization and seeking partnerships with Japan's "New Capitalism" project.

blocks.section: The Osaka 2025 World Expo : France unveils its pavilion
blocks.text: Universal exhibitions have historically contributed solutions to global challenges. The Osaka 2025 Expo, covering 155 hectares on Yumeshima Island, aims to be an international laboratory for innovation and expertise, aligning with the UN's Sustainable Development Goals. Over 160 countries are represented, with 28 million visitors expected.

blocks.section: The Osaka 2025 World Expo : France unveils its pavilion
blocks.text: The France Pavilion strategically positioned in the "Empowering Lives" zone ensures exceptional visibility and a high number of visitors, being located facing the main entrance and opposite the Japan Pavilion.

blocks.section: The Osaka 2025 World Expo : France unveils its pavilion
blocks.text: For more information, visit www.franceosaka2025.fr

title: The Park Hyatt Tokyo rewarded as the #1 Best Hotel in Tokyo
description:
The Park Hyatt Tokyo has been selected as the #1 Best Hotel in Tokyo in the Travel+Leisure 2021 World’s Best Awards. Congratulations to our member!
This year's World's Best Awards survey was open for voting January 11 through May 10, 2021, as destinations around the world were lifting COVID-19 restrictions. Survey rules have always allowed readers to reflect on their travel experiences over a three-year period.
Every year for the World's Best Awards survey, Travel+Leisure asks readers to weigh in on travel experiences around the globe — to share their opinions on the top hotels, resorts, cities, islands, cruise ships, spas, airlines, and more. Hotels were rated on their facilities, location, service, food, and overall value. Properties were classified as city or resort based on their locations and amenities.
Congratulations to our member, which has been selected as the #1 Best Hotel in Tokyo.
This Shinjuku mainstay earned the top spot with perennially popular features. Its sky-high location, which stretches from the 39th to 52nd floors of a high-rise, provides fantastic views of Tokyo's urban sprawl; the top-floor New York Bar, made famous in the Sofia Coppola film Lost in Translation, is a big draw, and the swimming pool on the 47th floor, with its sweeping floor-to-ceiling city and Mount Fuji views.

title: The second tapestry of the series "Hayao Miyazaki's imagination captured in Aubusson tapestry" will be unveiled to the public
description:
The Cité internationale de la tapisserie in Aubusson, France, has signed an agreement with Japanese Studio Ghibli for the creation of five Aubusson tapestries based on images from the animated films of director Hayao Miyazaki.
After 12 months of weaving at the Manufacture Robert Four in Aubusson, the second tapestry of the series "Hayao Miyazaki's imagination captured in Aubusson tapestry" will be unveiled to the public on 20th January 2023 in the auditorium of the Cité internationale de la tapisserie.
This tapestry, based on an image from the film "Spirited away", will be 3 metres high and 7.5 metres long.
You can follow this event live on their YouTube channel from 3:30 pm French time (or in replay) thanks to the following link: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T6KXU7mh-rE

To re-live the cutting off and unveiling of the first tapestry of the series, "Ashitaka and Yakul in the forest" (based on an image from the film "Princess Mononoke"), which took place on 25 March 2022 : CLICK HERE

title: Three Leaders in Beauty and Fragrance arrive in Japan distributed by Assemplage
description:
Assemplage, a key player in promoting French cosmetic and olfactory culture in Japan, has signed an exclusive distribution agreement with three renowned cosmetic brands from Southern France: Eau de Menton, Lao Care, and Vinésime. Through this unique collaboration, these brands are beginning their expansion into the Japanese market, aiming to share the know-how and cosmetic culture of regions such as Grasse and Burgundy.
Eau de Menton – Authentic Perfume from Grasse
 	Founded in 1947 in Menton, Eau de Menton has established itself as a leader in Côte d’Azur perfumery by creating scents that capture the refreshing zest of lemons from Grasse. 	Japan Launch: Home diffusers (August 1, 2025), perfumes (September 2025, online & in-store). 	 Instagram: @eaudementon_japon 
Lao Care – Innovative, 100% Natural Haircare  Lao Care has emerged in France as a new cosmetic leader with its patented reconstructive shampoo (the first European patent in this field), capable of reinforcing and rebuilding the hair’s protein bonds with natural ingredients.
 	Japan Launch: Late August 2025 	Key Products: Shampoo, treatments, hair cream 	Distribution: Hair salons, department stores, concept stores 	 Instagram: @lao.care.jp | Website: https://lao-care.com/ 
Vinésime – The Heritage of Burgundy Vineyards  In collaboration with the University of Burgundy, Vinésime offers an anti-aging skincare line developed from grape marc extracts and vine stem cells, delivering elasticity, radiance, and firmness to the skin.
 	Japan Launch: September 2025 via official website 	Key Products: Lotions, creams, serums, makeup removers, body oils, eye contour treatments 	Distribution: Spas, hotels, department stores, duty-free, selective distribution 	Instagram: @vinesime.jp | Website: https://vinesime.jp/ 

About Assemplage Founded in 2015, this Japanese company actively contributes to spreading French olfactory culture, notably through Bleu d’Argens. With this new collaboration, Assemplage is committed to conveying the history, culture, and philosophy of the French cosmetic terroir.
