title: TotalEnergies celebrates its 100th anniversary
description: The French company celebrated its centenary last March.

blocks.text: Companies news

blocks.section: TotalEnergies celebrates its 100th anniversary
blocks.text: TotalEnergies celebrates its 100th anniversary

blocks.section: TotalEnergies celebrates its 100th anniversary
blocks.text: The French company celebrated its centenary last March.

blocks.section: TotalEnergies celebrates its 100th anniversary
blocks.text: TotalEnergies celebrated its 100th birthday last March .

blocks.section: TotalEnergies celebrates its 100th anniversary
blocks.text: The Compagnie Française des Pétroles

blocks.section: TotalEnergies celebrates its 100th anniversary
blocks.text: It all began in 1924, when Compagnie Française des Pétroles was created to supply France with oil: a daring gamble, given that the country had no black gold.

blocks.section: TotalEnergies celebrates its 100th anniversary
blocks.text: The company then set off to the four corners of the globe in a race for energy.

blocks.section: TotalEnergies celebrates its 100th anniversary
blocks.text: Nowadays

blocks.section: TotalEnergies celebrates its 100th anniversary
blocks.text: This energy race gave rise to the energy giant TotalEnergies as we know it today. The company produces and supplies a variety of energy sources, including oil and biofuels, natural and green gas, renewables and electricity.

blocks.section: TotalEnergies celebrates its 100th anniversary
blocks.text: A global energy giant, TotalEnergies is present in nearly 130 countries, including Japan , and employs over 100,000 people.

blocks.section: TotalEnergies celebrates its 100th anniversary
blocks.text: The company is also diversifying its activities, turning to motor sport sponsorship. Fans recognize the company as a sponsor of Red Bull and Renault in Formula 1, or Peugeot at Le Mans. TotalEnergies is also a partner of car makers Peugeot and Citroën, using its products as greases and oils.

blocks.section: TotalEnergies celebrates its 100th anniversary
blocks.text: TotalEnergies into the future

blocks.section: TotalEnergies celebrates its 100th anniversary
blocks.text: The world-class company is currently focusing on the energy transition, including hydrocarbons or LNG (liquefied natural gas) and electricity from 2020. The company has made a long-term commitment to ensuring a secure energy supply for the future.

title: Toulouse, European Capital of Aerospace
description:
Toulouse, a global economic giant, stands as the central hub for the future of European aeronautical and aerospace industries. A nexus of innovation nestled in an exceptional living environment; the "Pink City" attracts companies of all sizes.
Toulouse, the fourth largest city in France, stands as the central hub for the future of European aeronautical and aerospace industries. A nexus of innovation nestled in an exceptional living environment; the "Pink City" attracts companies of all sizes.
When a company looks up to the sky or, more modestly, to the world, it looks at Toulouse. The metropolis is a thriving economic region (around 3% annual growth) that attracts tourists, students and decision-makers from all over the world. Why? Behind Toulouse's charming living environment lies a powerful industrial dynamism, particularly in the European aerospace industry, with CNES (the French equivalent of the JAXA space agency), Airbus Defence & Space and Thales Alenia Space being some of the most prestigious companies. Toulouse relies on a vast network of SMEs, ETIs and large companies, as well as multinationals and start-ups, and gets its workforce from research centres, laboratories, universities and world-renowned schools (a quarter of the local population is made up of students). Remarkably well-connected (the local airport serves 82 destinations, including 72 international ones), Toulouse is an ideal anchor point for moving throughout Europe. That's why, in less than a year and a half, around ten foreign players in the NewSpace sector have set up in Toulouse. Astroscale chose Toulouse with the support of Invest in Toulouse, the Economic Development Department from the Agence d'Attractivité de Toulouse Metropole. As a leader in orbit services, the Japanese space company is establishing its technical center for orbit cleaning and space debris capture in the city. An obvious choice: when aiming for the stars or seeking international business expansion, it's wise to make a stop in Toulouse.

For more information on Invest in Toulouse, the Economic Development Department from the Agence d'Attractivité de Toulouse Metropole, visit the website.
Contact the Aerospace and Space Sector Manager, Charlotte Voisin, on Linkedin.

description: Trade shows & business travel in France: CCIFJ and CCI France International help you recover your corporate VAT with zero financial risk.

blocks.text: The Chamber • Services

blocks.section: Trade Shows and Business Travel in France: How to Recover French VAT on Your Business Expenses
blocks.text: Trade Shows and Business Travel in France: How to Recover French VAT on Your Business Expenses

blocks.section: Trade Shows and Business Travel in France: How to Recover French VAT on Your Business Expenses
blocks.text: Trade shows & business travel in France: CCIFJ and CCI France International help you recover your corporate VAT with zero financial risk.

blocks.section: Trade Shows and Business Travel in France: How to Recover French VAT on Your Business Expenses
blocks.text: Every year, numerous companies based outside the European Union make substantial investments to exhibit at trade shows, explore new markets, or conduct business missions in France. Yet, due to the intricacies of local tax regulations, significant amounts of VAT are never reclaimed. To turn these expenses into direct cost savings, the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCIFJ) is rolling out a dedicated service to assist with French VAT recovery, in direct partnership with the CCI France International network.

blocks.section: A Major, Often Untapped Financial Opportunity
blocks.text: A Major, Often Untapped Financial Opportunity

blocks.section: A Major, Often Untapped Financial Opportunity
blocks.text: Whether participating in major international trade events (Maison&Objet, VivaTech, SIAL, JEC World, or the Paris Air Show) or organizing regular business travel during Paris Fashion Weeks, services invoiced in France generally include a standard VAT rate of 20%. Under European tax regulations (13th Directive), non-EU companies that do not carry out taxable operations in France are legally entitled to a refund of this tax on their business expenses. On a €50,000 budget for booth rental, logistics, and corporate hospitality, the recoverable amount can approach €10,000—providing a direct cash injection that significantly lowers international business costs.

blocks.section: Administrative Hurdles: The Main Barrier for Businesses
blocks.text: Administrative Hurdles: The Main Barrier for Businesses

blocks.section: Administrative Hurdles: The Main Barrier for Businesses
blocks.text: While the right to a refund is guaranteed by law, operational complexities frequently deter corporate finance departments:

blocks.section: Administrative Hurdles: The Main Barrier for Businesses
blocks.text: Strict documentation standards: The French tax authorities require strictly compliant invoices (mandatory legal notices, explicit VAT breakdown, and the full identity of the foreign buyer). A single formal omission will result in the rejection of the expense.

blocks.section: Administrative Hurdles: The Main Barrier for Businesses
blocks.text: Procedural complexity: Refund applications must follow strict digital filing procedures within rigorous statutory deadlines.

blocks.section: Administrative Hurdles: The Main Barrier for Businesses
blocks.text: Language barrier and administrative follow-up: Handling inquiries, supplemental document requests, and formal follow-ups with the non-resident tax division requires local representatives experienced in French administrative practices.

blocks.section: Administrative Hurdles: The Main Barrier for Businesses
blocks.text: Confronted with these challenges, many Japanese and international companies ultimately forfeit their refund claims.

blocks.section: A Turnkey Service, from Tokyo to Paris
blocks.text: A Turnkey Service, from Tokyo to Paris

blocks.section: A Turnkey Service, from Tokyo to Paris
blocks.text: To overcome these barriers, CCIFJ now offers end-to-end management of your claim, combining local proximity in Japan with direct representation before the French tax authorities through CCI France International:

blocks.section: A Turnkey Service, from Tokyo to Paris
blocks.text: Preliminary eligibility audit: Upfront screening of invoices and validation of supporting documentation to secure your claim.

blocks.section: A Turnkey Service, from Tokyo to Paris
blocks.text: Formal application and filing: Rigorous preparation of tax schedules and official submission to the French Directorate General of Public Finances (DGFiP).

blocks.section: A Turnkey Service, from Tokyo to Paris
blocks.text: Active representation and follow-up: Comprehensive management of all exchanges with tax inspectors through to the final disbursement of funds into your corporate bank account.

blocks.section: A Turnkey Service, from Tokyo to Paris
blocks.text: CCIFJ's support operates on a transparent, result-oriented model ( success fee ): our fees are structured as a sliding scale commission (from 6% to 10%) deducted exclusively from the VAT amounts successfully recovered. If no refund is obtained, no fee is charged.

blocks.section: Optimize Your Upcoming Business Travel Now
blocks.text: Optimize Your Upcoming Business Travel Now

blocks.section: Optimize Your Upcoming Business Travel Now
blocks.text: Have you incurred business expenses in France over recent months, or are you preparing to take part in upcoming trade shows? Our teams are available to carry out a preliminary assessment of your eligible invoices.

blocks.section: Optimize Your Upcoming Business Travel Now
blocks.text: Note: In accordance with French tax law, hotel accommodation and passenger transport expenses remain excluded from this refund scheme.

title: [Translate to Anglais:] Le Gala de Fukuoka 2019 : illustration de l'amitié entre Bordeaux et Fukuoka
description:
La 6ème édition du Gala Fukuoka de la CCI France Japon se déroulait cette année le lundi 20 mai à l’hôtel New Otani Hakata de Fukuoka. Pour la quatrième année, Bordeaux et Fukuoka fêtaient leur amitié lors de cette soirée exceptionnelle en présence d’une délégation bordelaise et de représentants officiels locaux tels Didier Cazabonne, adjoint au maire de Bordeaux chargé des relations internationales, et Eiichi Nakamura, vice maire de Fukuoka.
Consacré à la fois Bocuse d’Or et meilleur ouvrier de France, le chef étoilé François Adamski, un favori et habitué du Gala Fukuoka, a ravi pour la quatrième année consécutive les papilles des convives avec un menu spécialement préparé pour l’occasion honorant la haute gastronomie bordelaise.
Yuri Shinohara, talentueuse pianiste de Fukuoka et invitée d’un commun accord par les deux villes jumelées, a proposé des classiques de la musique française et européenne.
Enfin, la traditionnelle grande tombola a conclu l’événement au cours de laquelle il était possible de gagner, parmi plus de 70 lots, un superbe séjour en resort à Bali offert par le Club Med.

title: [Translate to Anglais:] Le Gala Kansai 2017 célèbre la France à Osaka
description:
Pour sa cinquième édition, le Gala Kansai, rendez-vous d’ores et déjà traditionnel de la CCI France Japon, s’est tenu cette année dans la ville d’Osaka. Près de 300 invités de prestige se sont réunis le 10 mars dernier à l’hôtel Imperial pour une soirée gastronomique d’exception célébrant l’amitié franco-japonaise. 
En 2016, la Chambre a été très active dans le Kansai avec en septembre, le Gala Kansai et le Forum Economique à Kyoto en partenariat avec la ville de Kobe, et en décembre, le Grand Forum franco-japonais de l’Innovation. Dans cette continuité, il était significatif pour les relations franco-japonaises que la CCI France Japon s’associe aux grands magasins Hankyu et soit tenu pendant la « French Fair », rendez-vous incontournable du magasin Hankyu Umeda. 
« Nous avions célébré les 95 ans de la Chambre en lançant le Gala Kansai. C’était il y a 4 ans : nous fêtons donc cette année nos 99 ans et aurons le plaisir l’année prochaine de célébrer avec vous notre Centenaire » a dit Hisataka Nobumoto, premier vice-président de la CCI France Japon, pour déclarer la cérémonie ouverte.
Jean-Matthieu Bonnel, Consul général de France à Kyoto, a souhaité évoquer le Grand Forum franco-japonais de l’Innovation organisé à Grand Front par l’Ambassade et la CCI France Japon, avec le concours de Knowledge Capital et l’aide de la Ville et de la Préfecture d’Osaka : « par l’importance de la participation des entreprises et de collectivités locales françaises et japonaises, et par la qualité des discussions auxquelles il a donné lieu, cet événement a contribué à nouer des contacts fructueux pour les échanges franco-japonais ».
Le chef Philippe Bodier, ayant fait ses armes dans les plus grands restaurants étoilés en France, a élaboré un menu spécialement pour le Gala et notamment un filet de bœuf japonais en croûte de l’Auberge (en rappel à son restaurant l’Auberge de la Roche à Saint-Jean-de-Linières) qui a fait sensation.
Cette année, les invités ont pu apprécier deux spectacles : le premier avec Fredy Leseck qui les a fait voyager dans les rues de Paris au son de son accordéon, et le deuxième avec la soprano lyrique Anne Rodier qui a enchanté le public avec son interprétation magistrale des grands airs du répertoire français.
En souvenir de ce Gala, les invités sont repartis les mains remplies : de nombreux cadeaux (dont des boîtes de chocolats Godiva spéciales célébrant le « White Day » pour les participants venus en couple), ainsi que des somptueux lots pour soixante heureux gagnants tirés au sort. Cette année, les prix incluaient un voyage en France comprenant un aller-retour Osaka-Paris sur Air France et un pass Eurail « select » pour traverser l'Europe en TGV 1ère classe, des sacs à main ou des montres de luxe. 
La CCI France Japon remercie ses partenaires, les entreprises donatrices qui ont gracieusement offert les lots de la tombola et les sponsors qui ont permis d’organiser ce majestueux événement :
BNP ParibasDanone JapanFlexisGodiva JapanHankyu Hanshin Departments Stores, Inc.J-SonyMHD Moët Hennessy DiageoNAOS JapanValrhona Japon

blocks.section: [Translate to Anglais:] L'Occitanie à l'honneur du Gala Kansai 2018 de la CCI France Japon
blocks.text: [Translate to Anglais:] L'Occitanie à l'honneur du Gala Kansai 2018 de la CCI France Japon

blocks.section: [Translate to Anglais:] L'Occitanie à l'honneur du Gala Kansai 2018 de la CCI France Japon
blocks.text: Le mercredi 30 mai, la CCI France Japon organisait la sixième édition de son désormais traditionnel Gala du Kansai à l’hôtel Hyatt Regency Kyoto, durant laquelle près de 300 invités se sont réunis pour une soirée gastronomique exceptionnelle aux couleurs de la région Occitanie / Pyrénées-Méditerranée en amont de la visite de la présidente de la Région, Carole Delga.

blocks.section: [Translate to Anglais:] L'Occitanie à l'honneur du Gala Kansai 2018 de la CCI France Japon
blocks.text: La Région Occitanie était représentée par sa vice-présidente du Conseil Régional, Nadia Pellefigue, et la préfecture de Kyoto par son gouverneur, Takatoshi Nishiwaki. Le maire de Kyoto, Daisaku Kadokawa, était également de la fête pour une soirée mettant à l’honneur l’amitié entre les deux régions. Car comme l’a rappelé Emmanuel Menanteau, administrateur hors Kanto de la CCI France Japon , en ouverture de soirée, Kyoto et l’Occitanie n’en sont pas à leur premier rapprochement, « puisque la préfecture de Kyoto et l’[ancienne région] Languedoc-Roussillon ont signé, en 2015, un vaste accord d’amitié et de coopération […]. Ces deux grands territoires se rapprochent plus vite que les continents ! ».

blocks.section: [Translate to Anglais:] L'Occitanie à l'honneur du Gala Kansai 2018 de la CCI France Japon
blocks.text: Cette année, les invités ont pu goûter un menu mettant à l’honneur la gastronomie occitane, spécialement créé et réalisé par le chef étoilé Michel Sarran , connu pour sa chaleureuse cuisine familiale et sa participation en tant que juge de l’émission de télévision « Top Chef ». Un concert du talentueux Rémi Panossian, pianiste de jazz présenté par le festival Piano aux Jacobins a enchanté l’audience avec des reprises de grands morceaux de la culture populaire internationale.

blocks.section: [Translate to Anglais:] L'Occitanie à l'honneur du Gala Kansai 2018 de la CCI France Japon
blocks.text: Il était possible de gagner des bouteilles de vin d’Occitanie lors d’un grand quiz testant les connaissances de tous à propos de la région Occitanie, de Kyoto et de la CCI France Japon. De nombreux cadeaux ont été aussi offerts aux invités lors de la grande tombola qui concluait la soirée. Le très convoité premier lot incluait un billet aller-retour pour la France offert par Air France, un pass Eurail offert par Rail Europe Japan et un séjour de 2 nuits à Toulouse et Nîmes avec visites guidées, offert par la Région Occitanie.

title: [Translate to Anglais:] Retour sur le Gala de Tokyo 2020
description:
Pour l’édition 2020 de son gala, la CCI France japon avait l’honneur d’accueillir comme partenaire Monaco. Les raisons ne manquent pas de se rendre à Monaco : une convention internationale, une soirée à l’Opéra, une nuit au palace, une promenade dans ses rues… ou les quatre à la suite. Mais pour un soir unique, le 4 novembre, Monaco s’est rendu au Japon.
Pour l’occasion le chef Christian Garcia avait concocté un menu laissé aux bons soins des cuisiniers de l’hôtel Cerulean : Mont-blanc salé, Loup braisé à la Méditerranée, Agneau en habit vert en croute d’herbes, Citron des Princes de Monaco… Les 530 convives, triés sur le volet et dûment passés par les fourches sanitaires mises en place pendant l’épidémie de COVID-19, se sont régalés. L’audience était digne des grands soirs de la Principauté. On y reconnaissait l’ambassadeur Patrick Médecin, ambassadeur de Monaco au Japon ; Ratna Sari Dewi Sukarno, veuve du premier Président d’Indonésie et habituée des plateaux télévisés nippons ; la cinéaste Naomi Kawase, régulièrement en compétition officielle au festival de Cannes. Ou encore la mythique créatrice de mode Junko Koshino. Le monde du sport était, en ce prélude aux Jeux Olympiques, bien représenté par Yuki Ota, président de la fédération japonaise d’escrime et Xavier Dorfman, entraîneur de l’équipe nationale d’aviron du Japon ainsi que son épouse Bénédicte Dorfman-Luzuy, elle-même championne d’aviron. Ce monde s’est emballé, comme chaque année, pour les 354 lots de la tombola !
À l’année prochaine !
CCI France JAPON

title: Two Michelin Stars, One Shared Vision at InterContinental Osaka
description:
From 23 to 26 July 2026, InterContinental Osaka will host an exceptional four-day culinary collaboration celebrating excellence, sustainability and French gastronomy.
To mark the 10th consecutive year that its Specialty Restaurant Pierre has been awarded one Michelin star in the Michelin Guide Kyoto-Osaka 2026, the hotel will welcome acclaimed French chef Julien Dumas for an exclusive event entitled "Two Stars, One Vision."
Chef Julien Dumas, who leads the Parisian restaurant Zostera in the 16th arrondissement of Paris, recently earned his own Michelin star in the Michelin Guide France 2026. Renowned for his expertise in seafood cuisine, he is also a strong advocate of sustainable gastronomy, promoting responsible sourcing and zero-waste practices in his daily work.
Having trained under renowned chefs such as Jean-François Piège at Hôtel Plaza Athénée and Jacques Maximin at Rech, Julien Dumas has established himself as one of the rising figures of contemporary French cuisine. In 2024, he was also awarded the prestigious Gault & Millau d'Or in recognition of his outstanding career achievements.
The event will open on 23 July with a gala dinner held at HINOKI, featuring a six-course menu paired with wines.From 24 to 26 July, guests will be able to experience a unique culinary collaboration at Specialty Restaurant Pierre through specially curated lunch and dinner menus.
By bringing together two Michelin-starred chefs around a shared commitment to culinary excellence and sustainability, "Two Stars, One Vision" promises to offer guests an unforgettable gastronomic journey between France and Japan.

title: UnaBiz appointed as new owner of Sigfox SA and Sigfox France SAS
description:
The Commercial Court of Toulouse announced the appointment of UnaBiz, massive IoT service provider and Sigfox Operator for Singapore and Taiwan, as the new owner of Sigfox.
The results of the receivership proceeding for Sigfox and its subsidiary Sigfox France SAS were unanimous, with UnaBiz endorsed as the best offer among nine initial bidders by the Jury, Administrators, the Public Prosecutor, Sigfox SA, Sigfox France SAS and Sigfox Employee Representatives.
Over the next few weeks, the Administrators, Sigfox Management and the Employee Representatives will work alongside UnaBiz to ensure a smooth transition of ownership to Sigfox’s existing commercial activities.
Business continuity is a top priority for the new management team. Upon handover, UnaBiz will safeguard 110 existing employees on a total of 174 and make financial and operational assessments to protect the firm’s assets, books, and most importantly, mission-critical network and backend systems, to address customers concerns. 
“I want to thank the entire Sigfox community for supporting us, and the French government for authorising our investment. While the transition of ownership marks a new beginning for Sigfox, UnaBiz will definitely guarantee the French sovereignty of Sigfox,” says Henri Bong, Co-Founder and Co-CEO of UnaBiz. 
As the world’s leading provider of IoT communication services and the pioneer of the 0G network in 75 countries worldwide, Sigfox is in a unique position to champion massive IoT adoption. “On top of securing the sales pipeline for Sigfox in the next 12 months as global markets emerge from the pandemic, UnaBiz and Sigfox will strive towards the convergence of LPWAN. The new Sigfox will reinvent itself and collaborate with other IoT communication technologies to seize new market opportunities,” Henri added.
To establish a more durable and collaborative global ecosystem, new strategies and governance will be put in place to facilitate engagements with Sigfox’ existing partners, customers, and Sigfox Operators to align stakeholders’ interests and support the company’s long-term development in its new chapter.

title: Understanding the future of work – emlyon x Malakoff Humanis
description:
How are careers, skills, and work environments evolving in the face of social, economic, and technological transformations?
At emlyon business school, we are committed to producing research that helps companies and institutions navigate these changes. In partnership with Malakoff Humanis, we have launched a dedicated Research Chair to study the key transitions shaping the world of work.
This initiative explores emerging forms of employment, career reorientation, and the societal impact of new work models with a strong focus on inclusion, wellbeing, and adaptability.
We invite you to explore the objectives, focus areas, and key themes of this Chair, as well as its contributions to shaping a more sustainable and human-centered future of work.

title: Understanding the Japan-EU Economic Partnership Agreement : Balancing Cost Savings and Managing Risks
description: The CCI France Japon was enchanted to host our Tax and Regulations Committee event "Understanding the Japan-EU Economic Partnership Agreement : Balancing Cost Savings and Managing Risks", on the evening of September 13th 2023. This event was mainly about the Japan-EU Economic Partnership Agreement (JEEPA), an agreement between the EU and Japan that reduces or eliminates the duty for imports of products between the two, and provides duty saving opportunities to the importing businesses in those countries. Our speaker, Robert Olson, Partner of PricewaterhouseCoopers WMS, having over 25 years of experience in customs and global trade, provided our guests with an overview of how to use the JEEPA to reduce their duty expense into Japan, and also with strategies to organize and prepare their records for inevitable audits by Japan Customs.

title: Sustainability Committee - Recap Event
description:
On March 6th, the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan, in collaboration with the German and American Chambers of Commerce in Japan, brought together visionaries for an inspiring Sustainability Committee event. The session, titled "Unlocking a Low Carbon Future: Turning Ideas into Reality - Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS)," showcased the expertise of Allan Baker, Managing Director and Global Head of Power Advisory & Project Finance, and Michael De Witte, Director of Energy Finance & Advisory, from Société Générale.
The event's highlight was the visionaries behind the world’s first gas-fired power station equipped with Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS). They offered profound insights into the challenges they encountered, the innovative solutions they implemented, and the significant milestones they reached in this pioneering project.

title: Valrhona Japan Hosts the Third Edition of É-Cothèque
description:
Valrhona Japan will host the third edition of É-Cothèque on 21 July 2026 in Tokyo, bringing together leading experts from the worlds of pastry, gastronomy and food science for an afternoon dedicated to innovation, creativity and knowledge sharing.
Created by L’École Valrhona Tokyo, É-Cothèque aims to move beyond the traditional demonstration format by offering an immersive learning experience where professionals can explore the latest trends, techniques and products shaping the future of cuisine and pastry. Alongside live talks by industry specialists, participants will enjoy around twenty tastings of pastries, desserts, ice creams and beverages prepared using products from the Valrhona Selection range.
This year’s edition, entitled “Science and Pastry in Reaction – When Knowledge Opens the Door to Creativity,” will feature renowned pastry chef Jordi Bordas, winner of the 2011 Coupe du Monde de la Pâtisserie and creator of the innovative “B·Concept” methodology, alongside Dr. Takashi Mikogami, a life sciences specialist and expert in nutrition and functional dairy ingredients at the Savencia Group.
Together, they will explore the “chemical reaction” between science and pastry, examining topics such as texture, ingredient interactions, the role of proteins in recipes and the relationship between food and the human body. Their dialogue will highlight how scientific understanding can enrich culinary creativity and open new possibilities for chefs and food professionals.
Following the talks, guests will be invited to discover a wide range of creations prepared with Valrhona Selection products. In addition to the chefs of L’École Valrhona Tokyo, this year’s event will welcome distinguished guest chefs Yusaku Shibata and Moe Takahashi, winners of the 2023 Coupe du Monde de la Pâtisserie, as well as Yusuke Aoki, who is active both in Japan and internationally. Together, they will present an exclusive tasting experience, offering participants a rare opportunity to discover not only exceptional creations but also the inspirations, techniques and ingredient philosophies behind them.
Event Details
Date: Tuesday, July 21, 2026Time: 1:30 p.m. – 5:00 p.m. (Reception opens at 12:30 p.m.)Venue: WITH HARAJUKU HALL, TokyoFee: JPY 8,000 (tax included)Capacity: 220 participants

title: Valrhona Japon launches a charity event “INFLUENCES”, a chocolate art exhibition.
description:
Valrhona believes in creating a more sustainable world of chocolate by sharing its experiences and showing how its social and environmental commitments make a vital contribution to the quality of Valrhona’s products.
Valrhona has been carrying out numerous initiatives to foster more responsible gastronomy. But in order to better connect the world of cocoa and gastronomy, Valrhona will visualize its initiatives through the statement, “TOGETHER, GOOD BECOMES BETTER.”
Ending child labor and educating children in cocoa-producing countries is one of the essential values to Valrhona.
As for Valrhona Japon, a charity event “INFLUENCES” will be launched as the first initiative. This event was held in 2014 and 2017 in France, and Tokyo will be the third exhibition. Valrhona will donate portion of sales of the chocolate sold at the event to bring smiles and excitements to hospitalized children through Japan Hospital Clowns Association.

title: Veolia : A player in Japan's energy transition
description:
As Japan struggles to reduce its plastic consumption, the French company Veolia has inaugurated a PET bottle recycling plant with its partners Mitsui&Co and Seven&i.
JAPAN: WORLD RECORD FOR PER CAPITA CONSUMPTION OF PET BOTTLES  23 billion: the number of PET bottles consumed by the Japanese each year, or 183 per person per year. By comparison, a European consumes 145 bottles a year. However, the country manages to collect 93% of these containers for recycling. A goldmine that Veolia has decided to exploit.    RECYCLING PET BOTTLES: VEOLIA'S PROJECT  " In an increasingly circular economy, it is essential to be able to recycle this waste more effectively," explains Guillaume Dourdin, CEO of Veolia Japan. Veolia has long experience in the recycling of plastics: 175,000 tonnes are recycled each year, 45,000 tonnes in Asia alone. Together with its Japanese partners - Mitsui&Co and Seven&i - Veolia inaugurated a new recycling plant in eastern Japan in mid-March.
DEVELOPING A CIRCULAR ECONOMY IN JAPAN  The new site will be able to create 25,000 tons of PET resin from recycled plastic, the equivalent of 1.5 billion PET plastic bottles. It will also reduce CO2 emissions by 27,500 tonnes per year. In the words of Toru Matsui, one of Mitsui's directors, the plant is a solution to creating a "true circular economy": "For us, this plant is just the beginning. "

title: Vinexpo Asia Returns to Singapore in 2025 with a Powerful Line-Up
description:
Following its successful debut in 2023, Vinexpo Asia 2025 is set to return to Singapore from 27 to 29 May, reaffirming the city’s strategic position as the gateway to the Asia-Pacific market. Held at Marina Bay Sands, the event will welcome 1,100 exhibitors from over 20 countries and 11,000 visitors from 70 nations, offering three days of intense networking and business.
Rodolphe Lameyse, CEO of Vinexposium, states: “With global consumption declining, Southeast Asia—anchored by Singapore—is a key growth engine for the wine and spirits industry.”
This edition will draw participants from established markets like Japan, South Korea, and China, while opening doors to emerging ones such as Vietnam, Thailand, and Malaysia. According to IWSR, the region holds promising prospects, with Singapore showing steady growth and premium product demand on the rise.
A Dynamic Programme for a Fast-Evolving Market
Vinexpo Asia 2025 promises a rich and diverse programme featuring top producers from France, Italy, Australia, Spain, South Africa, Japan, and more. The show will spotlight organic and biodynamic wines through the “WOW! – Welcome to the Organic World” area and host the Asia debut of the Wines Unearthed collective, highlighting boutique producers seeking regional distributors.
Spirits will also take center stage, with strong representation from Japan, Ireland, the UK, and China. The Vinexpo Academy will return with premium masterclasses, tastings, and conferences led by renowned sommeliers and experts, offering a deep dive into industry trends and challenges.

title: Virginie Lefevre – Ambassadrice CCIFJ pour la région de Fukui
description:
Ambassadrice de la Chambre de Commerce et d’Industrie Française du Japon (CCIFJ) pour la région de Fukui, Virginie Lefevre est la fondatrice et directrice de la marque de mode Viruxiny et du select shop 7amour, tous deux installés au cœur de la ville de Fukui.
Après des études de Droit, d’Art et de Mode, elle a d’abord travaillé comme designer pour de grandes marques internationales à Paris, Londres, au Canada et aux États-Unis. Arrivée au Japon il y a 25 ans pour enseigner la mode à Esmod Tokyo, elle s’y est définitivement installée.  Installée à Fukui depuis 19 ans, elle y a fondé sa propre entreprise et développé sa marque 100 % fabriquée localement, aujourd’hui distribuée dans de nombreux grands magasins japonais (Isetan, Hankyu, Mitsukoshi, etc.) sous forme de pop-ups. Parallèlement, elle collabore en freelance avec plusieurs sociétés locales et participe activement à la vie artistique et médiatique de la région (campagne télévisée Pink Ribbon de Fukui TV, interviews NHK, presse régionale).  Reconnue pour sa connaissance du terrain et son engagement pour le rayonnement du savoir-faire local, Virginie œuvre, en tant qu’Ambassadrice de la CCIFJ, à renforcer les ponts économiques et culturels entre la France et la région de Fukui, territoire riche d’artisanats et d’entreprises innovantes en pleine ouverture internationale.

title: Visit of the 55th edition of the Mode in France trade show in Tokyo
description:
On July 27, 2023, our team visited the Mode in France trade show in Tokyo in order to exchange with the participating companies and learn more about their journeys in Japan, their successes and their difficulties. We were thus able to collect valuable information to better support fashion companies as part of our services.

Presentation of the trade show : 
Mode in France Tokyo
The 55th edition of the biannual event of French fashion in Japan, the Mode in France trade show, took place on July 25, 26 and 27, 2023 in the heart of Tokyo, in the Ebisu district. This trade show is organized by the Fédération Française du Prêt à Porter Féminin, DEFI and the Promas office.
Since 1996, this event has brought together every year many French ready to wear and fashion accessories brands, allowing them to meet BtoB partners to export their products to Japan and to strengthen their existing business ties.
This edition brought together 26 companies, whereas before the Covid crisis, the event generally welcomed around sixty brands. At the request of Japanese participants, the event was maintained during the pandemic so that they could discover new collections and place orders.
Since the reopening of borders in October 2022, the trade show has returned to normal, with a participation rate gradually increasing.

Feedback from the companies : 
Some brands that have been distributed on the Japanese market for several years are experiencing a decline in their turnover, explained by a mature and highly competitive market, as well as by border closures, decreased consumption during the pandemic, and the weakness of the yen (as of August 4, 2023, 1 euro equals 156 Japanese yen).
The increase in logistics and transport costs and the current exchange rate make imported products more expensive for Japanese consumers, and business relations with local partners more complex.
On the other hand, several exhibitors explained that they have a network of a few Japanese retailers who regularly purchase a certain number of pieces from them. They do not necessarily need to work with exclusive import partners in the early stages of their development, but several of them now see an interest in doing so in order to increase their sales.
Several companies told us about the mutual importance for them and their clients of participating in Mode in France every year in order to maintain the relationship and present their new collections in person.

Interest in participating :
The trade show is mainly aimed at SMEs and mid sized companies in the ready to wear sector that wish to develop on the Japanese market and benefit from the long standing trusted partnerships established by the organizers.
However, not all brands match the target of Mode in France, which is why they are advised in advance on the interest of participating in the trade show. Do not hesitate to visit the contact page of the event’s website in order to discuss the relevance of your participation.
Unlike other major international trade shows held in Japan, this one highlights only French brands, which are appreciated for their elegance and their know how.

Our strategic recommendations : 
In a mature market such as Japan, where competition is intense and consumers are demanding, any company wishing to develop there must clearly differentiate itself.
In the fashion industry, where visuals and brand image are a priority, French brands approaching the Japanese market must have a strong DNA, a well defined universe and impactful storytelling.
It is important to be aware that this is a market highly driven by trends, to know how to constantly reinvent oneself, as well as to understand and adapt to Japanese style.
For example, one brand told us that its design did not sufficiently match the concern for discretion of Japanese female consumers (necklines that are too revealing, sleeves that do not provide enough protection from the sun, etc.).

As a result, participating in a trade show such as Mode in France Tokyo is one of the components of the development of a French ready to wear brand in Japan.
Please also note that CCI France Japan can offer additional support in the form of a prospecting mission to contact qualified players and strengthen your sales.
Contact us to discuss your project : business@ccifj.or.jp

title: Florent Petit, Musée du Louvre
description:
Il y a plus d’un an aujourd’hui, la CCI France Japon a été contacté par le service mécénat du musée du Louvre qui entretient des relations de longue date avec de grands groupes japonais. Afin de poursuivre le développement de sa stratégie de prospection à l’international, le musée du Louvre a pu bénéficier de l’appui de la CCIFJ dans sa recherche de nouveaux mécènes au Japon.
La CCIFJ a ainsi pu organiser quatre rendez-vous avec des entreprises japonaises ayant un engagement avéré pour le secteur de l’Art. Cinq mois plus tard, Le Louvre poursuit ses échanges et une délégation du musée a pu être reçue par un grand groupe lors de son séjour au Japon à l’automne dernier.
Nous avons également eu le plaisir d’accueillir le musée du Louvre au sein des membres de la CCIFJ, afin qu’il puisse utiliser ce réseau comme relais auprès de partenaires éventuels.
Nous remercions Florent PETIT, coordinateur de projets, et le service mécénat du musée du Louvre pour leur confiance et leur engagement à nos côtés pour renforcer les relations franco-japonaises.

title: Webinar: Harnessing Renewable Energy in the Food & Beverage Industry
description:
Join an insightful webinar on Wednesday, September 18, 2024, from 3:00 PM to 4:00 PM SGT, to learn how renewable energy can transform the Food & Beverage (F&B) industry by reducing emissions, cutting costs, and promoting sustainability across the supply chain. TotalEnergies, a global energy leader, is at the forefront of this transition, offering innovative, no-CAPEX solar solutions that help businesses in Asia-Pacific lower their carbon footprint through long-term Power Purchase Agreements (PPA).
In 2022, TotalEnergies formed a 50/50 joint venture with Japan’s ENEOS Corporation to develop 2 GW of solar distributed generation in the region over five years. Present in 11 countries with HQ in Singapore, TotalEnergies Renewables DG operates over 300 MW of solar capacity. Their tailor-made photovoltaic systems—installed on rooftops, carports, water spaces, or vacant land—enable businesses to only pay for the energy they generate, delivering immediate savings.
This webinar is designed to provide F&B and Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG) companies with actionable insights into reducing their environmental impact by adopting renewable energy. Industry experts will present case studies, discuss successful projects in the region, and engage in interactive discussions on the future of sustainability in the sector.
Why Attend?
- Learn how renewable energy can help reduce emissions in the F&B industry. - Discover long-term benefits of green electricity for your business. - Explore TotalEnergies' expertise across the energy value chain.
Speakers:
- Elodie Renaud, Managing Director, TotalEnergies Renewables Distributed Generation Asia Pacific - Sharon Goh, Regional Innovation & Business Partnerships Manager, TotalEnergies Asia Pacific and Middle East - Rachel Toh, Key Account Director, TotalEnergies Renewables Distributed Generation Asia Pacific - Raditya Pramudiantoro, Senior Sustainability Manager, Danone

description:
The French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCIFJ) is pleased to announce the appointment of Wejden Ben Hmiden as Head of the Fukui Desk.
“I am delighted to join the CCIFJ Fukui Desk. After studying optics and eyewear in Tunisia, I decided to pursue Japanese language and international business studies in France. I also had the opportunity to take part in two university exchange programs in Japan, at Keio University and Saitama University. I hope to contribute to the development of Franco-Japanese economic exchanges by strengthening the presence of the Fukui Chamber of Commerce and promoting the Fukui region internationally.”
The Fukui Desk is part of the CCIFJ’s ongoing effort to strengthen economic cooperation between French and Japanese regions. Located in the heart of the Hokuriku area, Fukui Prefecture is renowned for its industrial expertise, particularly in textiles, optics, and precision manufacturing.
The office’s mission is to support local companies in their business exchanges with France, promote investment opportunities, and showcase Fukui’s economic and cultural vitality on the international stage.
Contact Wejden Ben Hmiden: fukui-desk(@)ccifj.or.jp

title: Welcome to Kreston ProWorks Corp., the experts in Business Support
description:
Kreston ProWorks Corp., is an international market entry, accounting & business support firm operating in Japan as a member of Kreston Global. With over 750+ member offices and experts in 110 countries, Japan experience and qualified all bi-lingual professional team we hold strong position among the top in-bound market leaders in Japan. 
They have been assisting foreign companies and investors in Japan since 2007. 
Their expertise includes Japan market entry, visa, accounting & payroll, HR, EOR, individual and corporate tax returns and advisory, M&A and other personal and business matters.

Their activities:
Company Formation and Immigration Services
 	setting up your business presence, including entity incorporation 	license and visa applications 	employment 	systems selection and set up 
Accounting and Tax
 	ongoing bookkeeping, accounting and reporting support 	corporate income taxation 	wage tax and personal income tax support for seconded employees 	advice on how to structure acquisitions, mergers, or other restructurings 
HR, Payroll & Benefits
 	payroll processing 	benefits 	HR-related administrative work 
On-Demand Professionals
 	dispatch of staff from an extensive network of professionals 
Legal & Transactional
 	obtaining business licenses and visas 	company secretarial matters 	controlling bank accounts and making payments on behalf of our clients 
Business Consulting
 	business strategy consulting for profit and agility 	review and update of systems and processes 	organizational and HR transformation consulting 	assistance in charting a course through changes related to systems, processes, people, and costs 
They have supported many French-owned companies throughout the years.
“When I set up Kreston ProWorks it was out of frustration particularly as I saw that many companies had problems related to Japan (understanding of business and social environment). I wanted to provide true service to companies entering and operating in Japan. I had worked in Japan in business support with various certified professionals long enough to understand what is lacking and that we need to make communication our number one priority and I felt it was important to create a bridge and be able to assist clients in situations where they feel blind, and be able to understand what the clients are trying to achieve and help them solve their problems / improve their results and experience in Japan.”, said Marek Lehocky, CEO of Kreston Proworks.

title: HEC Paris - Partners Event
description:
On January 20, 2025, the French Chamber of Commerce, in collaboration with HEC Paris for their alumnies, hosted an event featuring HEC Professor Alberto Alemanno. The talk, "What's Next for Europe," explored future challenges and opportunities for the European Union.
Professor Alemanno provided an overview of the EU's new administration, guiding Europe until 2029. He highlighted challenges such as environmental crises and Europe's global position. The event included an engaging Q&A session covering topics like European industry transformation, funding solutions, and future budget needs.

title: Why the yen is falling despite rising interest rates
description: In a historic move, Japan raised interest rates for the first time in 17 years. Yet the yen continues to fall.

blocks.text: Foresight

blocks.section: Why the yen is falling despite rising interest rates
blocks.text: Why the yen is falling despite rising interest rates

blocks.section: Why the yen is falling despite rising interest rates
blocks.text: In a historic move, Japan raised interest rates for the first time in 17 years. Yet the yen continues to fall.

blocks.section: Why the yen is falling despite rising interest rates
blocks.text: A weak currency is a boon to exporters’ profits, but by driving up import costs, it can weigh on Japanese households. According to a Reuters survey , here are the reasons why the currency is falling despite rising interest rates.

blocks.section: Why the yen is falling despite rising interest rates
blocks.text: Speculative effect of the interest rate hike announcement

blocks.section: Why the yen is falling despite rising interest rates
blocks.text: The historic announcement of the Bank of Japan's exit from negative interest rates led to rapid market anticipation. As a result, the yen fell by over 1% on the day of the announcement.

blocks.section: Why the yen is falling despite rising interest rates
blocks.text: Yes is the lowest-yielding currency in the G10

blocks.section: Why the yen is falling despite rising interest rates
blocks.text: The yen's low yields make it ideal for carry trades, in which an investor decides to borrow in a low-interest currency and then invest the proceeds in a higher-yielding currency.

blocks.section: Why the yen is falling despite rising interest rates
blocks.text: Investors are now betting on the fact that Japanese interest rates will not rise rapidly, thus promoting carry trades in the yen.

blocks.section: Why the yen is falling despite rising interest rates
blocks.text: Cash of major Japanese investors

blocks.section: Why the yen is falling despite rising interest rates
blocks.text: The yen is deprived of the support of repatriation flows. Indeed, low interest rates are remunerative enough for large Japanese investors, who prefer to stay abroad. Foreign investors hold around $3,000 billion in foreign bonds and yen.

blocks.section: Why the yen is falling despite rising interest rates
blocks.text: Among the largest financial companies, Japan Post Bank and Japan Post Insurance have declared that they will not change radically in response to the change in monetary policy.

blocks.section: Why the yen is falling despite rising interest rates
blocks.text: Uncertainty surrounding public intervention

blocks.section: Why the yen is falling despite rising interest rates
blocks.text: Currently at 151.27 to the dollar, the yen appears very close to the 151.94 level that triggered intervention in 2022. The risk would therefore be that the Japanese Ministry of Finance would intervene to support the yen, with limited success. The markets therefore seem to fear this new public intervention.

title: Women In Business 2026 @ Nagoya: Crossing sights between France and Japan
description:
On January 23, 2026, the Chūbu Office of the CCIFJ had the pleasure of organizing the Women in Business @ Nagoya event, bringing together four outstanding guest speakers. For the first time, this event was held in Nagoya, having previously taken place in Tokyo, at the OKB Harmony Plaza, a prestigious venue ideally located near Nagoya Station.
About 40 participants attended the event, which represents one of the few opportunities in Nagoya to highlight major societal issues related to the role of women in the workplace in Japan, while fostering dialogue among professionals from a wide range of sectors. Due to strong interest, the event quickly reached full capacity, reflecting the keen engagement of regional economic and institutional stakeholders with the topics addressed.

blocks.text: Chubu Event report

blocks.section: Women In Business 2026 @ Nagoya: Crossing sights between France and Japan
blocks.text: Women In Business 2026 @ Nagoya: Crossing sights between France and Japan

blocks.section: Women In Business 2026 @ Nagoya: Crossing sights between France and Japan
blocks.text: On January 23, 2026, the Chūbu Office of the CCIFJ had the pleasure of organizing the Women in Business @ Nagoya event, bringing together four outstanding guest speakers. For the first time, this event was held in Nagoya, having previously taken place in Tokyo , at the OKB Harmony Plaza , a prestigious venue ideally located near Nagoya Station.

blocks.section: Women In Business 2026 @ Nagoya: Crossing sights between France and Japan
blocks.text: About 40 participants attended the event, which represents one of the few opportunities in Nagoya to highlight major societal issues related to the role of women in the workplace in Japan , while fostering dialogue among professionals from a wide range of sectors. Due to strong interest, the event quickly reached full capacity , reflecting the keen engagement of regional economic and institutional stakeholders with the topics addressed.

blocks.section: Women In Business 2026 @ Nagoya: Crossing sights between France and Japan
blocks.text: The evening opened with a keynote presentation by Aya Yamanouchi from LVMH Moët Hennessy Louis Vuitton Japan , who introduced the various initiatives implemented by the group to promote women’s access to leadership positions. Programs such as EllesVMH and Shero enable female employees to connect with senior leaders from different business units and benefit from a structured mentoring system, supporting professional development and career progression.

blocks.section: Women In Business 2026 @ Nagoya: Crossing sights between France and Japan
blocks.text: This presentation was followed by a panel discussion featuring four distinguished speakers: Makiko Tauchi ( Denso ), Atsuko Morita ( St. Louis International ), Misako Arai ( Nagoya University ), and Aya Yamanouchi . The discussion was moderated by Motoyuki Suzuki from CEVA Logistics .

blocks.section: Women In Business 2026 @ Nagoya: Crossing sights between France and Japan
blocks.text: Each speaker shared her professional experience, as well as the challenges she currently faces or has faced in the past. Ms. Tauchi spoke about the difficulties of being a woman in a predominantly male industrial environment. Ms. Morita, a specialist in Femcare , addressed health-related issues such as menstruation, maternity, and menopause, and their impact on professional life. Ms. Yamanouchi highlighted the many barriers women continue to face when aspiring to leadership positions, while Professor Arai provided an academic perspective, comparing Japan with other developed countries and pointing out how far Japan still lags behind on women’s participation in the workforce.

blocks.section: Women In Business 2026 @ Nagoya: Crossing sights between France and Japan
blocks.text: The panel concluded with a highly dynamic Q&A session , fostering rich and constructive exchanges between the audience and the speakers. Participants were able to further explore several topics discussed during the panel while also expressing their appreciation for the speakers’ openness in sharing their personal and professional experiences.

blocks.section: Women In Business 2026 @ Nagoya: Crossing sights between France and Japan
blocks.text: Many questions focused on mindset and the desire to challenge and move beyond traditional frameworks that remain deeply rooted in Japan . This topic, which is still relatively new in the Japanese context, generated in-depth discussion among both the panelists and the audience. Additional questions addressed mentorship programs at LVMH , as well as the role of corporate internationalization as a long-term driver of change in mindsets and management practices within organizations.

blocks.section: Women In Business 2026 @ Nagoya: Crossing sights between France and Japan
blocks.text: The evening concluded with a networking cocktail , prepared by MOF Museum Nagoya and Nichifutsu Boeki . Guests enjoyed mulled wine, cocktails, toasts, and freshly prepared fondue, providing an ideal opportunity to continue discussions in a warm and convivial atmosphere.

blocks.section: Women In Business 2026 @ Nagoya: Crossing sights between France and Japan
blocks.text: The event successfully strengthened professional connections while contributing to an essential dialogue on the role of women in business in Japan.

blocks.section: Women In Business 2026 @ Nagoya: Crossing sights between France and Japan
blocks.text: Thanks to our sponsors MOF Museum Nagoya , Nichifutsu Boeki and OKB Harmony Plaza for allowing us to host this wonderful event.

title: Women in Leadership: A Dynamic Workshop in Nagoya
description: Two inspiring women led engaging seminars and workshops on management and leadership in Nagoya

blocks.text: Chubu Event report

blocks.section: Women in Leadership: A Dynamic Workshop in Nagoya
blocks.text: Women in Leadership: A Dynamic Workshop in Nagoya

blocks.section: Women in Leadership: A Dynamic Workshop in Nagoya
blocks.text: Two inspiring women led engaging seminars and workshops on management and leadership in Nagoya

blocks.section: Women in Leadership: A Dynamic Workshop in Nagoya
blocks.text: On April 16, 2025, in collaboration with our partner, the Central Japan Economic Federation, the CCIFJ organized a special event featuring seminars and interactive workshops led by two exceptional speakers: Béatrice Delpuech , Area Director for Japan and Korea at AF-KLM Cargo, and Helen IWATA , President and bilingual coach at Sasuga Communications .

blocks.section: Women in Leadership: A Dynamic Workshop in Nagoya
blocks.text: Members, partners, and friends of the Chamber gathered at the Nagoya Innovators Garage , right in the heart of the city. The event began with a seminar by Béatrice Delpuech, who shared insights from her 36 years of experience in team management and outlined what it truly takes to be an effective leader.

blocks.section: Women in Leadership: A Dynamic Workshop in Nagoya
blocks.text: The second seminar was led by Helen IWATA, who, as a professional coach, explained the keys to building trust in the workplace. Drawing on the trust equation and the three main causes of workplace conflict, she guided participants through a hands-on reflection to apply these concepts to their own situations and explore practical conflict resolution approaches.

blocks.section: Women in Leadership: A Dynamic Workshop in Nagoya
blocks.text: After the two dynamic seminars, the event transitioned into small-group workshops: one led by Béatrice, the other by Helen. In a relaxed and open atmosphere, participants shared the real-life challenges they face and received personalized advice from the facilitators.

blocks.section: Women in Leadership: A Dynamic Workshop in Nagoya
blocks.text: The event concluded with a networking session. One of our valued partners, the MOF Museum Nagoya , kindly provided delicious sandwiches and coffee (special thanks also to Arcane and Takanashi Milk ). Participants enjoyed the refreshments while engaging in lively conversations. The CCI France Japon hopes that events like this will help foster a more positive and inclusive working environment throughout the Chubu region.

title: Yen falls to lowest since 1990
description: Yen reached its lowest point since July 1990.

blocks.text: Foresight

blocks.section: Yen falls to lowest since 1990
blocks.text: Yen falls to lowest since 1990

blocks.section: Yen falls to lowest since 1990
blocks.text: Yen reached its lowest point since July 1990.

blocks.section: Yen falls to lowest since 1990
blocks.text: Yen continues to weaken after the Bank of Japan announced the end of its 17-year policy of negative interest rates.

blocks.section: Yen falls to lowest since 1990
blocks.text: A rise in interest rates generally implies an increase in currency purchases. The exact opposite occurred in Japan: yen selling became widespread, and the yen weakened against the US dollar.

blocks.section: Yen falls to lowest since 1990
blocks.text: “We will take decisive action against any excessive movement [in the markets] without ruling out any option”, said Finance Minister Suzuki on March 27.

blocks.section: Yen falls to lowest since 1990
blocks.text: “The exchange rate is a factor that has a significant impact on the economy and prices. The Bank of Japan will continue to closely monitor developments in the foreign exchange market and their impact on the economy and prices, in close cooperation with the government” said Bank of Japan Governor Ueda about the yen's first depreciation in 33 years.

blocks.section: Yen falls to lowest since 1990
blocks.text: How does the fall in the yen rate affect the Japanese economy?

blocks.section: Yen falls to lowest since 1990
blocks.text: A weakened yen is an advantage for companies exporting abroad . They can sell their products abroad at lower prices, making them more competitive.

blocks.section: Yen falls to lowest since 1990
blocks.text: The low yen is also a boon for the tourism sector . According to the Japan National Tourism Organization, the number of tourists was nearly 3 million last month, a figure that is set to rise in the coming months.

blocks.section: Yen falls to lowest since 1990
blocks.text: However, a low yen also means higher import costs , particularly for raw materials such as oil, energy and cereals.

blocks.section: Yen falls to lowest since 1990
blocks.text: This rise in commodity prices could have an impact on households if prices rise faster than wages.

title: Yoshiki Tsurumaki Joins LPA Tokyo as Head Partner of Japanese Law Practice
description:
LPA Registered Foreign Law Corporation - LPA Law Office in Tokyo continues to significantly strengthen its capabilities in Japan in response to growing market demand.
We are pleased to announce that Yoshiki Tsurumaki has joined the firm as Head Partner of the Japanese Law Practice.
With more than 23 years of experience in Japanese and international legal practice, Yoshiki has advised Japanese and international clients across a broad range of areas, including domestic and cross-border M&A, finance, capital markets, ESG investment, real estate, data centres, technology, data, cybersecurity, general corporate matters and dispute resolution.
Through this appointment, LPA Tokyo further strengthens its capability to support both domestic Japanese matters and cross-border transactions, assisting Japanese companies in their overseas expansion as well as foreign companies and investors entering and expanding in the Japanese market.
Yoshiki will lead the Japanese law practice in Tokyo while also enhancing collaboration with LPA Law’s offices across Europe and Asia. LPA Tokyo aims to provide practical legal services that deeply reflect Japanese corporate perspectives and decision-making processes, while also responding to the evolving international business environment.
Yoshiki’s arrival marks an important step in further strengthening LPA Tokyo’s Japanese law practice and Japan-related cross-border capabilities.
As a unique European-Japanese law firm platform with offices across more than 15 jurisdictions, LPA Law will continue to strengthen its platform and aim to become an increasingly important legal partner for domestic and international clients.

blocks.text: Today, this partnership continues, and seeing the soy sauce embraced by the French people, with some even calling it the best in the world, is a source of immense pride. It is a testament to the power of cultural exchange and shared passion.

title: Zugmeyer : its Franciscains spark a sensation in Tokyo
description:
Audrey Besson, co managing director of the chocolatier and confectioner Zugmeyer, can hardly believe it. The Franciscain, the flagship cake of this legendary Grenoble based house, topped the popularity rankings at the Matsuzakaya department store in Nagoya during its chocolate fair. This small family run company from the Rhône Alpes region found itself ahead of veterans Pierre Hermé and La Maison du Chocolat at the end of the event. A first attempt, a masterstroke. “Incredible!” she exclaims. “Valentine’s Day in Japan is unique in that women give chocolates only to their loved ones and to people they appreciate,” she explains, amazed by the enthusiasm for her products. But Audrey Besson is on all fronts. “In Nagoya, we had to limit the number of boxes per person. In Kyoto, we sold out. Here, it’s madness.” On that day, she is standing in front of the Zugmeyer booth at the annual chocolate fair of the Odakyu department store in Shinjuku. Once again, her Franciscain causes a sensation.
Immediate successSucceeding in Japan does not necessarily take time. By the end of its second trip to the Archipelago, Zugmeyer had already become a reference. Audrey Besson recalls the circumstances of her first stay last May: “We had received an award for a business trip through Air France to a destination of our choice. We chose to go far.” That destination was Tokyo. “We immediately attracted the interest of many importers. One of them was particularly enthusiastic. He was very precise in his requests, asked a lot of questions… That gave us confidence.” A contract was signed in October, and the first chocolates were delivered as early as December. After this first successful Valentine’s Day, Zugmeyer is now considering having its own corner in a department store. “We are very proud to be distributed in Japan. It is wonderful to begin our export journey here!” says Audrey Besson. The key to success? “The Chamber of Commerce’s business support team. They helped us tremendously,” Audrey Besson reveals.

blocks.section: Summary
blocks.text: To celebrate this centenary, the CCI France Japon published a book called “1918-2018: un siècle d’histoires d’entreprises au Japon”. The author, Christian Polak, is a specialist in French-Japanese relations. He retraces the evolutions of the activities of the Chamber since 1918, through the History of its members. This bilingual book (French-Japanese) is widely illustrated with exceptional period documents (posters, letters, old photographs, newspapers …) provided by companies.

blocks.section: Author: Christian Polak
blocks.text: Author: Christian Polak

blocks.section: Author: Christian Polak
blocks.text: A 1971 graduate from the Japanese study department of the National Institute of Oriental Language and Civilisation (INALCO), Christian Polak enters the Language study Institute of Waseda University the same year. In 1973, he joins the Law faculty of the national university Hitotsubashi, in the department of Diplomatic History. In 1980, he presents his thesis on French-Japanese relations from 1914 to 1925. He becomes resident at the Maison Franco-Japonaise in 1980 and the year after, creates the Seric, a counselling firm specialized in metallurgy, automotive, aeronautics and the environment. At the same time, he continues his academic work and research at the University Hitotsubashi, and then at Meiji University. He frequently publishes books and articles on the History of French-Japanese relations, and organizes exhibitions on this subject in France and Japan.

blocks.text: Part 1 – Working in harmony in the company ・Your colleagues are partners, not friends ・Your manager also has a manager ・Pull your subordinates upwards ・Respect is the foundation of harmony ・Weddings and funerals Part 2 – Deal with the client ・Business Meetings ・The first impression is what matters ・Welcoming visitors : make them feel important ・Business cards, etc. Part 3 – Negotiation skills ・A bit of psychology ・The nemawashi, at the core of management ・How to build a network ・How to refuse something without hurting people, etc. Part 4 – Public relations ・The company and its reputation ・Internal events ・Receptions ・Strangers, etc.

blocks.section: Summary
blocks.text: Fit in Japanese companies

blocks.section: Summary
blocks.text: Fit in a Japanese company can be hard if you don’t know Japanese habits and customs. Cultural differences can confuse French investors, willing to sustainably handle their exchanges with Japanese people and companies. What are the Japanese labour codes? What are the mistakes to be avoided? How to start negotiating with a Japanese company and its top managers? Business Otsukiai answered to those questions by gathering all the codes used in Japan. This guide has been created by Japanese people and for Japanese people, gathering interviews with thousands of Japanese business men. From the booking of the appointment to the negotiation, through the act of sharing your business card, you will learn all the codes to succeed in Japan.

blocks.section: Summary
blocks.text: Nemawashi is essential in day-to-day work, even for minor tasks. Succeeding doing that means to ban some expressions from your vocabulary like “It’s the first time that I hear about this” or “I wish someone told me this sooner”.

title: EPISODE #27 - John Blagys | CCI France Japon
description: Japan is the best place to ski! The Hakuba Hotel Group is the most committed group in the area. This one-of-a-kind hospitality company has mixed its Japanese and foreign elements to carve the best stay offers around.

blocks.section: John Blagys
blocks.text: John Blagys

blocks.section: John Blagys
blocks.text: Japan is the best place to ski - East of the French Alps! The best way to realize this is in the stunning domain of Hakuba.

blocks.section: John Blagys
blocks.text: A few hours away from Tokyo, this natural gem combines the best-powdered snow on Earth, a vibrant local culture, great ski, and hospitality infrastructures. Not to mention its "green" season, fresh, colorful, and calm. The Hakuba Hotel Group is the most committed group in the area. This one-of-a-kind hospitality company has mixed its Japanese and foreign elements to carve the best stay offers around. It is also an astute real estate investor, aware of the inner value, both aesthetic and financial, of the place. On Hakuba, on ski, on tourism - and on the challenges and opportunities of the Covid-19 era -, there was no better person to listen to than John Blagys, the young head of sales and marketing at Hakuba Hotel Group.

title: EPISODE #37 - Jacques Babaud, Nihon Michelin Tire | CCI France Japon
description: Additive manufacturing is becoming a key part of industrial processes. It allows its users to imagine and manufacture components with the sole limit of human imagination. Jacques Babaud from Michelin explains the technology.

blocks.section: Jacques Babaud
blocks.text: Jacques Babaud

blocks.section: Jacques Babaud
blocks.text: AM, or additive manufacturing: this groundbreaking technology is often mentioned but rarely explained.

blocks.section: Jacques Babaud
blocks.text: Yet additive manufacturing is becoming a key part of industrial processes. It allows its users to imagine and manufacture components with the sole limit of human imagination. Manufacturing giant Michelin, one of its early adopters, believes that Japan is one of the key areas for its usage. It has set up an AM platform in the industrial basin of Gunma prefecture. Jacques Babaud explains the technology, Michelin’s involvement, and its relevance for Japan’s industry.

blocks.text: With the kind support of Michelin Nihon Tire

blocks.section: With the kind support of Michelin Nihon Tire
blocks.text: Michelin contributes to the future of monozukuri in Japan through metal 3D printing

blocks.section: With the kind support of Michelin Nihon Tire
blocks.text: Japan is still at an early stage of adoption of metal 3D printing or metal Additive Manufacturing (AM). Education of a new generation of talented engineers will facilitate the spread of this disruptive innovation. People development through Application is part of the mission of the “Gunma AM Platform” (GAM) consortium.

blocks.section: With the kind support of Michelin Nihon Tire
blocks.text: Michelin has been using metal 3D printing technology for tire mold manufacturing for 10+ years. Michelin established in 2016 the “AddUp” joint venture producing 3D metal printers one side, and operating those printers to print parts for final customer on the other. In Japan, many potential users need a deeper understanding of the technology—notably its possibilities and limitations— before making the leap from conventional production means. The public-private-academic consortium “GAM” wants to contribute to this revolution.

title: Work in Japan
description: The Japanese labour market is conservative and hard to access for foreigners. This is why it is very important to think carefully about your career plan before moving to Japan. To inform you, CCI France Japon has created a complete guide to Working in Japan.

blocks.section: Work in Japan
blocks.text: Work in Japan

blocks.section: Guide: Working in Japan
blocks.text: Guide: Working in Japan

blocks.section: Guide: Working in Japan
blocks.text: You will find useful information on the labour market, research channels, and advice about practical life.

blocks.section: Guide: Working in Japan
blocks.text: Globally, the Japanese labour market is conservative and hard to access for foreigners. Very good command of the Japanese language is often a prerequisite to find a job. This applies both to reaching Japanese companies and foreign companies that have settled in Japan and now employ primarily Japanese workers.

blocks.section: Guide: Working in Japan
blocks.text: This is why it is very important to think carefully about your career plan before moving to Japan. To inform you, CCI France Japon has created a complete guide: Working in Japan .

blocks.section: Guide: Working in Japan
blocks.text: You will find useful information on the labour market, search channels, and advice about practical life (accommodation, language schools…)

blocks.section: Guide: Working in Japan
blocks.text: You can also sign-up to our Job platform , where you will find the job offers of the CCI France Japon members.

blocks.section: Guide: Working in Japan
blocks.text: Below, you will find a Q&A that we encourage you to read before contacting us .

blocks.section: Labour market
blocks.text: Labour market

blocks.section: Labour market
blocks.text: The labour market is conservative, with a low turn-over rate. This is a market that is known for being tough to penetrate for foreigners, where European people are still under-represented. With a very low unemployment rate (close to 2%), this market is very close to reaching full employment. However, we need to beware of this employment rate as 35% of the active population have precarious jobs (2/3 of this group are women).

blocks.section: Labour market
blocks.text: In 2017, the French Embassy in Japan identified more than 9000 French people in Japan. Counting foreign nationals that are not registered to the Embassy, we can estimate French population in Japan at more or less 10 000 people.

blocks.section: Labour market
blocks.text: There is no standard profile and it mostly depends on the needs of the companies. However, we can detect a principal trend. For local contracts, companies are looking for applicants that have completed graduate or postgraduate education, that have a practical knowledge of Japanese language and that have an expertise in an industry or position. Knowing the language is not enough, it needs to be completed with valuable experience alongside companies.

blocks.section: Labour market
blocks.text: Professions in IT, research & development, recruitment firm, education, catering are the sections that are the most likely to be fulfilled by foreigners. Some Japanese companies can also recruit Japanese-speaking foreigners for business development positions abroad.

blocks.section: Labour market
blocks.text: Even if it is hard, it is not impossible to find a job in Japan without speaking Japanese. Some positions require a technical expertise that sometimes prevails on Japanese language. It concerns mostly IT engineers, R&D researchers or some positions in Finance. Globally, it mainly regroups jobs that focus on back office, where the Japanese language is secondary. Recruiting firms can also be good alternatives for foreigners that do not find a job in their core business. Japanese market being mostly closed to foreigners, it is crucial to develop and leverage a network there (mainly through associations), in order to hear about opportunities via word of mouth.

blocks.section: Labour market
blocks.text: It depends on multiple variables: work experience, Japanese proficiency, research intensity, distance, network strength… After beginning an active search for a job in Japan, it can seem appropriate to make a brief account after the first six months. It will help you understand your strengths, weaknesses and to potentially re-evaluate your position in the job market.

blocks.section: Labour market
blocks.text: Every year, recruitment firms (Robert Walters, Michael Page) publish a document that compiles salary data for different positions. For reference only, an assistant will earn 3-4 million of yens, a manager will earn 6-8 million of yens, a branch representative managing at least 5-10 people will expect 10 million of yens or more. This information can be taken into account for foreign professionals for whom the salary system is based on competency and not seniority. In Japan, it is possible that an assistant earns 5-6 million of yens, including bonus, if he reaches 20 years of experience.

blocks.section: Visa
blocks.text: Visa

blocks.section: Visa
blocks.text: There are a lot of visas that will allow you to work in Japan. The most famous one is the working visa, which actually groups several visas depending on the situation of the applicant (Specialist in Humanities, Skilled Labour…). It is the role of the company to sponsor the applicant to help him/her obtain a visa. The “Student Visa” and the “Dependent Visa” also allow you to engage in a paid activity for at most 28 hours a week, if you obtain a derogation from the Immigration Office. The Student Visa is sponsored by a school (university or language school) and the Dependent Visa can be granted to the legal spouse of a person that works in Japan. The working-holiday visa, non-renewable, can be granted to people under 30 years of age, for 1 year, to work in Japan (as a support job to pay the expenses there).

blocks.section: Visa
blocks.text: The website of the French Embassy in Japan lists the different visas you can obtain, and the requirements.

blocks.section: Visa
blocks.text: It is strictly prohibited to work with a temporary visa (tourist visa) of 90 days. However, it is possible to participate in professional meetings or interviews. When the visa expires, the government discourages people from leaving the country for a few days and then re-entering for another 3 months. Immigration inspectors can find frequent back and forth trips suspicious.

blocks.section: Visa
blocks.text: To get a working visa, it is necessary to obtain an employment contract with a company because it is its role to start the procedures with the Immigration Office. The company will obtain an Eligibility Certificate for a period of 2-3 months, document (often mandatory) that will allow you to apply for a visa that you will obtain in a couple of days, from the Immigration Office if you are in Japan, or the Japanese consulate in France. Thus, you will need approximately 3 months to obtain a working visa.

blocks.section: Visa
blocks.text: The immigration office reviews on a case-by-case basis and there are no specific or strict rules to follow. However, we can observe that the contract must not be precarious (no part-time or one-off work), the applicant must at least possess a bachelor degree, the salary must be sufficient to maintain an adequate standard of living in Japan (minimum 200 000 yen) and the training or experience of the applicant must match with the position for which he is applying for a visa.

blocks.section: Visa
blocks.text: It is hard to obtain a visa for manual work in Japan. Without a bachelor degree, 3 to 10 years of core-business experience are required to obtain a “Skilled Labour” visa. Moreover, it is important to understand that French degrees are almost not recognized in Japan and that performing your manual work in Japan will probably require local qualifications.

blocks.section: Visa
blocks.text: Several Immigration Offices exist in Japan. In Tokyo, the closest underground station is “Shinagawa”. You will then need to take a bus that will bring you directly to the Office.
